act49side.tagline: Ch'en follows her missing uncle into an emptied capital, and comes to stand where a 120-year game over one erased name comes to its end. Whose blood was it that had to be spilled?

chars.name: Ch'en
chars.desc: Former Senior Superintendent of the Lungmen Guard Department, who follows her missing uncle Wei Yenwu into the capital, Baizao · Operator Ch'en the Dawnstreak

chars.name: Wei Yenwu
chars.desc: Ch'en's uncle on her mother's side and Governor of Lungmen. He rarely lets anyone see what he is thinking.

chars.name: Wang
chars.desc: Second of the Twelve, born from Sui's shattered consciousness. A master who has played the same game of weiqi for a thousand years · Operator Wang

chars.name: Jie
chars.desc: Fifth of the Twelve. A proxy who loved writing and history, and helped compile the histories of Yan.

chars.name: Zuo Le
chars.desc: A Candleholder of Yan's Sui Regulator. An earnest young man caught up in the Token he brought back from the Garden of Grotesqueries · Operator Zuo Le

chars.name: Mo Yi
chars.desc: A girl of the Shanhaizhong. She claims to know more about Feranmuts than any Candleholder.

chars.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
chars.desc: Magistrate of Water at the Sky Mirror Pavilion. The last one left of the Ch'en, a family of historians.

chars.name: Chongyue
chars.desc: Eldest of the Twelve. A martial arts grandmaster who remembers everything and keeps it all to heart · Operator Chongyue

chars.name: Jun
chars.desc: Fourth of the Twelve. A musician versed in the laws of Yan, and the fairest, most selfless of them all.

chars.name: Ling
chars.desc: Eldest sister of the Twelve. A poet who loves wine and verse · Operator Ling

chars.name: Nian
chars.desc: Ninth of the Twelve. A spirited smith who loves fireworks and films · Operator Nian

chars.name: Shu
chars.desc: Sixth of the Twelve. One who quietly foresees what is to come · Operator Shu

chars.name: Dusk
chars.desc: The sleepyhead of the Twelve, in charge of painting · Operator Dusk

chars.name: Yu
chars.desc: Youngest of the Twelve. A cook who keeps Savors at Yu's · Operator Yu

chars.name: Ya
chars.desc: A Feranmut who has nursed a grudge against Sui and Yan since the days of the Great Hunt.

chars.name: Ju
chars.desc: The ancient Feranmut Ju. An artisan living in a body made in human likeness · Operator Ju

chars.name: Hou
chars.desc: The ancient Feranmut Hou. A fisherman who drifts through the world wherever the wind takes him.

chars.name: Grand Commandant
chars.desc: One of the Three Excellencies of Yan, who has spent his whole life on the battlefield. He argues for war with Sui.

chars.name: Zuo Xuanliao
chars.desc: General of Yumen and Lord Exorcist. Zuo Le's father.

terms.name: Yan
terms.desc: A great nation in the far east of Terra, ruled for a thousand years by its sovereign, the 'True Lung.'

terms.name: True Lung
terms.desc: The sovereign of Yan. Bound by blood to the first Originium, so that for a thousand years all power has rested in one person alone.

terms.name: Baizao
terms.desc: The capital of Yan. A nomadic city built atop the Tomb of Sui.

terms.name: Sui
terms.desc: An ancient Feranmut sleeping in the 'Tomb of Sui' beneath Baizao. In its dreams it evolves without end, seeking to swallow the whole world.

terms.name: the Twelve
terms.desc: Twelve proxies born from Sui's shattered consciousness. Siblings who each found their own answer to 'who am I' in the human world, and live as themselves.

terms.name: Sui Regulator
terms.desc: An organization founded on the old battlefields of the Great Hunt. For a thousand years its only duty has been 'the best choice for Yan in matters of Feranmuts.'

terms.name: Candleholder
terms.desc: An agent of the Sui Regulator who stays close to a proxy, watching over them and serving as liaison.

terms.name: Garden of Grotesqueries
terms.desc: A garden kept by Yi, the eighth sibling. Site of the Placation, and part of the force that holds Sui down.

terms.name: Token
terms.desc: The mark a Candleholder receives after completing the Placation. This time it takes the form of a small doll, not a jade rule.

terms.name: Shanhaizhong
terms.desc: A group descended from the teachings of a carpenter a thousand years ago. Yan treats them as bandits.

terms.name: Geist
terms.desc: The power some Feranmuts have to breathe life into inanimate things. 'Scriptgeists,' born from written characters, appear in Baizao.

terms.name: Sky Mirror Pavilion
terms.desc: The first library of Yan, in Baizao. Its top floor is a restricted area sealed off by the Sui Regulator.

terms.name: Writing Knife
terms.desc: An ordinary knife once used to scrape characters off bamboo slips. Steeped in the power of Jie, the fifth sibling, it came to erase or alter characters, names, and even history itself.

terms.name: Bu Fan
terms.desc: 'No return.' An Originium enchantment the True Lung of the Great Hunt completed at the cost of his own life. Later True Lungs can use its power only by paying with their own lives.

terms.name: Yumen
terms.desc: A military nomadic city guarding the northwest of Yan. It is now stationed near the Tomb of Sui.

blocks.x: Beneath Baizao, the capital of Yan, sleeps the ancient Feranmut **Sui**. Born from its shattered consciousness, the Twelve have lived for centuries under human names.
The day after Mid-Autumn, one of the Twelve entered the Tomb of Sui, and half a month later there is still no word. Five Feranmuts lurk around Yan, and the court wants war.

blocks.cap: The True Lung at the Grand Commandant's sickbed. The time left runs until the next full moon.

blocks.x: Around then, when the bedridden Grand Commandant presses the True Lung to set a deadline, the True Lung answers that he will wait only until the next full moon. After that comes war.
At the same time, in an inn near Baizao, Ch'en hears an old voice as if in a dream. “Hui-chieh, grow up soon. When you grow up, you'll be able to change everything.”
1. A Voice No One Else Hears

**Ch'en**, former Senior Superintendent of the Lungmen Guard Department, is staying at that inn with her uncle **Wei Yenwu**. Wei Yenwu tells her to go back to Lungmen. Ch'en says that this time, she is not leaving.

blocks.cap: The inn near Baizao. Outside the window, the autumn rain falls without pause.

blocks.x: Why had her mother followed her uncle all the way to Lungmen? Ch'en wanted to find that answer with her own eyes, not hear it from her uncle's mouth.
That night, the Grand Tutor of Yan comes to the inn in person to warn that the True Lung may open 'Bu Fan,' and that Lord Wei should have his own trump card ready.
Because Bu Fan is a power that can be used only at the cost of the True Lung's life, Wei Yenwu, the True Lung's elder brother, raises his voice. “He must never be the one to pay that price.”

In that room, only Ch'en hears another voice. If the True Lung is gone, it says, another must be raised, and if there is no one else, even this girl will have to do. But neither the Grand Tutor nor Wei Yenwu heard a thing.
After the Grand Tutor leaves, her uncle asks after Talulah. Ch'en lashes out at him and walks out. Not long after, Wei Yenwu disappears without leaving so much as a note.
The Shadow Guard tell her he likely went to the capital, summoned by a letter in the True Lung's own hand. Ch'en's answer is short. This time, she will find him.

Around the same time, **Zuo Le**, a Candleholder of the Sui Regulator, finishes the Placation in the Garden of Grotesqueries and steps outside, but he cannot shake the feeling that he has done all of this many times before.

What is more, the Token in his pocket turns out to be not the usual jade rule but a small doll, and 'Old Tianshi' of the Tianshi Bureau tells him to ask no questions and take it to the Sui Regulator, sending him off to Baizao.
2. An Army Drawn in Ink, the Last of the Ch'en Family

By the time Zuo Le reaches Baizao, evacuation orders have already been issued, and near a checkpoint he runs into a masked Candleholder. The masked Candleholder produces a document in the Supervisor's own hand and demands the Token, and when Zuo Le refuses, orders the Patrol Battalion soldiers to arrest him.

The one who gets him out with a smoke bomb is **Mo Yi**, a girl of the Shanhaizhong. She snatches Zuo Le's doll and chants an incantation calling on Jie, fifth of the Twelve, but when nothing happens, she vanishes with the doll.

blocks.cap: On a night when dark clouds hide the moon, a silent procession flows through the streets.

blocks.x: That night, an army appears in the streets. Without commands or footsteps, soldiers in bloodstained armor from a thousand years ago march on, and an Imperial Guard drillmaster calls them Geists.

The same night, Ch'en shows her ID to enter the city and saves a woman from the creatures. The woman recognizes her at once as a descendant of the Yan bloodline and asks what the difference is between one person's will bending ten thousand and one person's wisdom awakening ten thousand.

When day breaks, it turns out the Geists all poured out of one place: the Sky Mirror Pavilion, the first library of Yan. That dawn, only the Magistrate of Water, **Ch'en Chao-ch'ien**, remains inside.

blocks.cap: “Ch'en Hui-chieh? What are you doing here?”

blocks.x: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien's face hardens when she sees Ch'en's ID. Ch'en's mother, Princess Yanjing, had remarried into the Ch'en, a family of historians, and Ch'en's father was Ch'en Chao-ch'ien's elder cousin.
After the princess died of illness in Lungmen, the Ch'en family, who had never even had the power to refuse the match, were branded as having mistreated her, and fell to ruin.

Ch'en says it is the first time she has heard so much about where she comes from, and that she had thought she was the only one left. The two look at each other in silence, as if into a clouded mirror.

Then Geists spill from between the bookshelves, and Zuo Le and Mo Yi cross blades over the doll. The one who settles the commotion is Liang Xun, once an advisor of Yumen and now a transcriber at the Sky Mirror Pavilion.

According to the Sui Regulator's records, which Zuo Le now reveals, sealed at the top of the Sky Mirror Pavilion is the **Writing Knife**, left by the proxy Jie, who died 120 years ago. It is a blade that can erase or alter names, existence, even history.

Breaking the seal takes two keys, one held by the Sui Regulator's Supervisor and one by Jun, the fourth proxy. And when she hears that the Ministry of War has lately been searching the Pavilion for no stated reason, Ch'en draws a line between the Grand Commandant, the Writing Knife, and her missing uncle Wei Yenwu.

Meanwhile, at Savors at Yu's, a restaurant on an emptied street, the youngest, **Yu**, waits for customers. When Ya, a Feranmut with a thousand-year grudge, arrives and draws her sword, a voice like a court of law freezes the room. It is the woman Ch'en saved at the checkpoint: **Jun**, fourth of the Twelve.

blocks.cap: “The dining table is no place for swords and bloodshed.”

blocks.x: 3. A Game Lost for a Thousand Years

Meanwhile, the 'criminal' who entered the tomb is the second of the Twelve, the weiqi player **Wang**, and he is now trapped in Sui's dream. Sui builds a prison out of his memories and replays, one by one, the games he has lost over a thousand years.
The dream brings back an evening 500 years ago. Jie is copying text from bamboo slips onto newly invented paper, and Yu is splitting old slips his sister gave him to grill skewers.

blocks.cap: Copied bamboo slips become skewers. An evening of Jie and Yu, 500 years ago.

blocks.x: That day, Jie said someone had written 'Sui' over every character of the Jijiuzhang she had copied. If she scraped characters with the Writing Knife, steeped in her own power, she felt they might vanish from people's memories too. Someday, she said, she might be able to erase 'Sui' from every script in the world.
As long as we don't forget who we are, of course.

blocks.cap: “The ones who create characters helped me think of one to use as a name. Could you read this for me, brother?”

blocks.x: And now, when he opens that book again in the dream, Jie's writing is gone, the pages packed instead with red 'Sui.' Wang scrapes them away one by one with the Writing Knife, and with every character erased, lightning, fire, and bitter cold sweep through the room.
Only after he erases the 1,394th character does the room return to normal. On the back of a game record tucked into the back cover was a letter from Jie, but even that is buried under a darker 'Sui.'
The last ink stain flickers through twelve names and stops at 'Wang,' and Wang, having scraped that name away, collapses in his own blood and dies.
Then he stands up again, unharmed. The body that fell has shattered into three black stones. He gave up three stones and killed one fragment of Sui's memory.
...I will continue the game. Until neither of us can ever rise again.
4. A Split Board, a Shadow in the Mirror
The dream moves on to another memory. On the day the Feranmut Ju, the last threat of the Great Hunt, was subdued, Wang secretly let him go.

The eldest brother, **Chongyue**, then called Shuo, wanted to break free of Sui the honest way. Wang countered that there was no time. Shuo's palm came down, and Wang's weiqi board split an inch deep.

blocks.cap: The board, split at the end of the brothers' quarrel.

blocks.x: Their eldest sister, **Ling**, who arrived late and made peace between the two, said she wanted to leave a dream behind. A dream Sui could not disturb even if it woke, with all twelve of them in it.
Around then, Wang went to see Ju, who had fashioned himself a new body and meant to die in the Shanhaizhong's place, and told him that only if he left would the Shanhaizhong survive.
Ju promised to repay the debt without fail, and told Wang that one tree does not make a forest; he should ask his siblings for help as well.

Back before Ling, Wang revealed the clue he had gotten from Hou: nothing says I must be in its dream, nor that it must be in mine. He promised not to act rashly, drained the cup of wine Ling handed him, and entered Sui's dream.

blocks.cap: Sui's dream, entered by way of a single cup of wine. A landscape never seen in chaos or in the mortal world.

blocks.x: There, Hou showed him a shadow that had filled the empty space in Sui's nightmare. It wore Wang's face. It was Sui's puppet, formed from all the strange incidents that had surrounded his siblings.
The Wang of that day left it behind and departed the dream. The Wang of today sends a single stone outside and plunges alone into the shapes of the Yan army from a thousand years ago.
Sui then shows him visions of Ling and his younger siblings perishing, but Wang does not waver. The verse in her mouth was one Ling would never compose, not even in the face of death.
5. A Ginkgo of Twenty Years, Soundless Voices

Over a hundred years ago, a seventeen-year-old True Lung opens the door to a room in Yan that only the True Lung may enter, and comes face to face with **Bu Fan**. The True Lung of the Great Hunt completed this enchantment at the cost of his life, and later True Lungs can use its power only by paying with their own.

blocks.cap: Beyond the door the young True Lung opened, the deepest secret of Yan.

blocks.x: Some time later, the young sovereign summons Wang and declares that he will make Baizao a nomadic city and do away with Sui. When Wang answers that he might perhaps be able to take Sui's place, the True Lung points to a ginkgo sapling planted that spring and gives him twenty years.

Around then, a new Candleholder comes to Jie: **Chun**, a long-lived Elf of Yaan. To Chun, who says the records of the Great Hunt describe her kind as vicious, Jie says she cannot lend out the Writing Knife, but promises to help correct the records the proper way.
Before long, the Sui Regulator and the justice ministry acknowledge the Elves' innocence.
One day the Minister of Works comes calling and asks her to change the more than three thousand dead of the Chidao project in Danyan to around a hundred. Jie refuses.
History has never been decided by one person. It is the combined soundless voices of millions.
Then Jie's Writing Knife disappears. Fearing her hot-tempered brother would lose his head, Jie asks Jun not to tell Wang, of all people.
Jie talks about a future she saw in a dream. A future in which everyone lives as their true selves, and which felt nothing like a dream.
The Writing Knife turned up, of all places, on the True Lung's desk. When he used it to scrape away a 'Wang' character that bothered him in his own handwriting, the paper went blank.

blocks.cap: The True Lung's palace. The missing Writing Knife was here.

blocks.x: At the same time, construction supplies bound for Baizao have ground to a halt one after another, and the True Lung recognizes this as a move by Jie's brother. He leaves the numbers as Jie wanted, and returns the Writing Knife.

Meanwhile, the Sui Regulator's Supervisor of the time summons Chun and tells her to alter a document Jie had reviewed. Tear the paper or paint over the ink, and the characters return as they were. Jie's power was growing along with the history of Yan, the Supervisor says, and one day it would become more terrifying than Sui.
6. Who Must Die
Twenty years pass. Wang has shut himself in a temple, doing nothing but playing weiqi. Someone leaves a single ginkgo nut at the very center of his board.
Around then, an anonymous letter listing Wang's crimes reaches the Sui Regulator. Framing officials, secret meetings, arson, hiding a Feranmut. The Supervisor submits it to the True Lung.
From that day on, faceless voices circle in Chun's ears. Eliminate the great evil first, then remove the culprit. Jie will become something more terrifying than Sui, and only you can help her.

The day after his teacher, the Grand Preceptor, passes away, the True Lung asks a young official, another of the Grand Preceptor's students, whether he is at fault, and she passes on her teacher's words: the affairs of the world are fickle, so one must always hold fast to one's conscience.
That day, a petition of impeachment from the Sui Regulator lay on the True Lung's desk, and the True Lung musters his army and opens the Tomb of Sui.
Then Wang, entering the tomb alone, plays weiqi with a half-awake Sui. He wins by half a point, but that game was only one corner of a board hundreds of lines wide.

Meanwhile, at the Sky Mirror Pavilion, Jie asks Chun how she felt when her mother died. If the death of family is only a small sorrow in a long life, Jie can die in his stead. If it is unbearable pain, she can survive and shoulder that pain herself.
Chun answers that she felt nothing in particular, that she stopped crying soon after, and that now she is happy, here with you. In truth, it felt as if her heart would tear apart.
Jie thanks her and tells her she really is a responsible Candleholder. With those words, a hole opens in Chun's chest that the wind blows through.

blocks.cap: The Writing Knife, passing from Jie's hand to Jun's.

blocks.x: And to Jun, who comes running, Jie entrusts the Writing Knife, saying she wants it kept by the fairest, most selfless person there is. Someone will come back, she says.

blocks.cap: “The sunlight... How warm.”

blocks.x: Jie does not step toward the sunlight; she leaves the room as she is and walks into the tomb, where darkness waits.

Back in the present, Wang in the dream sees how it ended. As he lay pierced by white stones, about to breathe his last, a golden light embraced him. A sight he has not forgotten for a single moment in 120 years.
...I'm sorry. Wait for me... until I come back. Until... you come back.
Jie smiles faintly, nods, and vanishes into a torrent of light.
7. A Door That Opens Without a Key
Back to the top of the Sky Mirror Pavilion in the present. The Sui Regulator's Supervisor, waiting for the group before the sealed room, is Chun. Jie's last Candleholder, 120 years ago.

Mo Yi lays bare the Grand Commandant's scheme. The truth of the night the emperor was assassinated forty years ago survives in no ministry's records, so if that night is rewritten with the Writing Knife to make Wei Yenwu 'the reigning True Lung,' the life Bu Fan takes will be his.

Chun says this is not treason but for the good of the realm, and that Jie dying in Wang's place was likewise the soundest decision once gains and losses were weighed. Left alone, Jie would have become more terrifying than Sui.
Ch'en Chao-ch'ien pushes back. What of the historians who never put down their brushes even in prison? What of the elders of her own family, who froze to death on the snowfields guarding the truth?
Chun's answer is a single word. Writers.
Ch'en says she has met people like Chun before. People who abandon their friends, then pray to see them in their dreams. Not hoping for a reunion, but for forgiveness.

When the fighting ends, the doll falls to the floor. It was a Geist. Wang had dug Sui's imagination out of the Garden of Grotesqueries to make a shell, then poured in his siblings' memories to shape it.
A translucent figure wakes and walks toward the room that has been shut for a hundred years, and the door opens without a key. The owner needed no key to enter her own room.

It reaches for a crumbling book, opens the window, and is about to look out at the osmanthus tree outside when it stops. The figure disperses like ink dropped into clear water, and only the small doll remains on the floor.

blocks.cap: Jie's study, shut for a hundred years. The room is exactly as it was at the start.

blocks.x: Chun keeps repeating that it is not her. Jie was taller, her hair darker.
Jun, now standing beside her, asks. “Who else could it be?”
Chun leaves the study without a word. Jun entrusts the doll to Zuo Le and Mo Yi, and asks Ch'en what justice is.
Ch'en answers. That Wei Yenwu not die a pointless death. That the events of forty years ago be judged in full. That the sacrifice of the proxy who died for Yan not be in vain.

blocks.cap: Ch'en's hand taking the Writing Knife; Jun's hand letting it go.

blocks.x: The history of Great Yan should be written by the Yanese people.
8. The Sword That Cuts Regret

On the eve of the full moon, the Grand Commandant, realizing that the True Lung means to use Bu Fan with his own body, cites the precedent of Ursus and cries out that only war with Sui can restore discipline to Yan.
The True Lung asks in return whether he remembers what happened to Gaul, and then, leaving the palace, says:
If Great Yan must truly spill blood... then that blood... should be the True Lung's, first of all.
Left alone in the empty palace, the Grand Commandant orders Yumen to move.
Around the same time, before the Forbidden City, Ch'en finds Wei Yenwu. He had not been abducted; he had taken the Writing Knife and meant to go before Bu Fan and end it all with his own life.
When Ch'en will not hand over the Writing Knife, Wei Yenwu draws on Heaven's Eye, the pinnacle of the Chi Xiao sword arts. A sword that severs when it must, and swings without regret.

blocks.cap: Chi Xiao in her left hand, the Writing Knife in her right.

blocks.x: Ch'en thrusts the Writing Knife forward like a sigh, and the keen sword-intent scatters like a fleeting dream. Wei Yenwu's Heaven's Eye carried the scent of regret.
Apologies from the dead are meaningless. If there are people you want to apologize to, then tell them you're sorry while you're still alive.
If he asks whether Talulah is well, Ch'en says, her answer is that she is not. Even so, she is still willing to talk about Talulah with him.
When Ch'en asks him to name the sword she just used, Wei Yenwu answers: Heaven's Plaint. This time, he will do something he won't regret.
Meanwhile, Mo Yi hands Ya a map marking where Bu Fan lies. Blocking Ya's path are two old ones, the ancient Feranmuts **Hou** and **Ju**. Theirs were the voices Ch'en had heard as if in a dream.
Hou asks whether, at the end of a thousand-year journey, she still means to settle scores with Sui. Ya, who scorns the word 'kin,' vanishes, leaving the two elders behind in her own world.

blocks.cap: Ya's world. The two elders are left behind on a river that has not thawed in ten thousand years.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, as Yumen's marching horns sound, Zuo Le scales the walls with his lightness skill to find his father, **Zuo Xuanliao**. The general, all but held captive by the Grand Commandant's envoys, hears his son out and refuses the bogus military orders.

Taihe of the Department of Discipline and Supervision, who happens to be there, offers himself as a witness, and the Ministry of War's envoys freeze. Zuo Xuanliao says only a few words to his son. You did very well today.
9. The Siblings Outside the Dream

At that hour, deep in the tomb, Wang grasps a fragment of the letter Jie left. Her brother tried to calculate human hearts, it says, and she tried to measure them through history; their paths differed, but they would arrive at the same place.
Sui sneers. Has Jie's choice robbed him even of the will to act?
Wang admits that it weighs on him, and says that this is the human heart, which a beast like you will never understand.

Wang has already torn himself into 181 pieces and scattered them throughout Yan and beyond, and while Sui poured its mind into the endless game, it had been growing weaker. At last, Wang faces himself in the mirror: the one holding White.
At the very moment the puppet is about to swallow Wang, Sui realizes that it is still inside the dream.

blocks.cap: Ling's cup of wine, poured not to the heavens but to the earth.

blocks.x: Outside the dream, Ling recites verse and Jun plays the strings. Jun does not sing. Jie has not come back yet.
The dream woven from the two sounds drags the Feranmut back into a long sleep.

Then Sui thrashes, the tomb collapses, and Geists pour out. Ji, the seventh, and Yi, the eighth, hold Mangshan Town; **Nian**, **Dusk**, **Shu**, and Yu hold the wastes outside the tomb. Fang, the tenth, who never shows himself, stands alone before an ancient colossus and asks it to turn back.
Then, as Yumen draws near, Ch'en steps forward.

blocks.cap: The sword of Heaven's Plaint. A golden sandstorm sweeps toward Yumen.

blocks.x: As golden sand settles like snowflakes, the soldiers of Yumen remember a poet who raised her cup and sang in the face of disaster, and count the drums of departure. At the eighteenth beat, Yumen comes to a halt.
In that opening, Zuo Le runs for the last of the cannons. Yu scoops up a handful of golden sand and thinks of the sister he has not seen in over a hundred years.

Meanwhile, the doll Mo Yi carried to the tomb has ended up in Chongyue's hands, and holding it close, he tears through the boundary of the dream and stands before his younger brother. He wanted to show him Jie, he says.

blocks.cap: The eldest brother, tearing through the boundary between dream and reality.

blocks.x: Live. ...Live, and come back to us.
Wang promises nothing. His brother's fading voice carries to the very end. Then I will look for you. I always will.
10. The Sui That Killed Sui
As Wang's blade falls, primeval memories pour out and wash Sui's consciousness away. All that remains is a will that is forgetting even who it is.
To that will, Wang says: you were an arrogant dreamer, and in the end you died by my hand.
Then Wang turns his last stone into a blade and drives it into Sui's eye. Sui closes its eyes as a galaxy of black stones draws near, gazing at a future that exists only in dreams.
...May you dream well.
The shadows of proxy and Feranmut merge into one, and a new 'Sui' is born. In that instant, the Geists sweeping through Baizao vanish without a trace.

blocks.cap: A vast shadow, blocking out the light of Bu Fan.

blocks.x: At the same moment, before Bu Fan, a vast shadow appears in front of the True Lung, who grips the jade seal, and says that Sui is dead, but its thousand years of rage still burn.
The True Lung says that if it is a new Sui, he will end it together with his own life, and if it is Wang, he will pardon his past crimes. Then Ya arrives.
Ya raises her sword but cannot swing it. The enemy she hunted is already dead; what stands before her is a Sui that is not Sui.
It leaves the choice to Ya. Carve eternal torment into this body with this stone, or simply leave.

blocks.cap: Laughter, bursting out where a thousand years of hatred let go.

blocks.x: Ya throws back her head and laughs, then cuts away the Originium of Bu Fan together with the space it occupies and drives it deep into Sui's body. Atone for Sui's sins for all eternity, she says, and if you ever become like Sui, I will come back and kill you.
Cutting through time with a body already near death comes at a heavy price, and Ya's body crumbles away in the wind.
Around then, in Mangshan, Old Tianshi gazes toward the tomb and murmurs. No one can touch you now, but you will suffer forever. Weiqi player, this game is yours.

Only then, in the secret chamber, does the True Lung see Wang's final move. At the price of near-eternal suffering, Wang took Sui's place and accepted Ya's vengeance, and Bu Fan, on which Yan had leaned for a thousand years, was lodged in the Feranmut's deepest core.
As the secret chamber collapses, the True Lung thinks that dying here would not be so bad. The one who grabs him by the shoulder is Wei Yenwu.

When the quake subsides, Chun informs the court officials that the scourge of Sui has been removed, and listens to the Feranmut's heartbeat. Mixed in with the rage is the sound of forgiveness, gathered from somewhere in Baizao.
He did it, Chun murmurs to herself. He removed Sui, and he found you.
As the Sui Regulator's report is announced, the Grand Commandant dies beside the empty Dragon Throne. His words, that the old man who started the rebellion awaits judgment here, never reach anyone.
And before the siblings gathered in the wasteland, Chongyue walks out alone and desperately swallows a sigh, as if about to declare something.
Epilogue. A Record Without Omissions

After it is all over, Ch'en offers to use the Writing Knife to correct the family history Ch'en Chao-ch'ien wrote. Ch'en Chao-ch'ien declines again and again, then says she will open the book to the places that need correcting, if Ch'en will hold the knife.
What I want most right now is the courage to write history responsibly, even knowing there are unsolved questions in this world that will never have answers.

Where the Writing Knife passed, no trace was left, and Ch'en says that, used properly, it is nothing more than a very good eraser. Ch'en Chao-ch'ien soon moves to a research post at the Imperial Historical Cabinet.

Meanwhile, there are empty seats around the hot pot Yu has made. Fang only sent word through a disciple, and Dusk has gone to sleep, leaving a talisman that says not to wake her until brother Wang comes back. Yu believes the day will come when everyone sits around this table.

blocks.cap: Brothers, with one thin curtain between them.

blocks.x: And in a quiet study, the True Lung and Yan Wu sit on either side of a curtain. The True Lung says that once, his dream was to spend his whole life inside the Sky Mirror Pavilion.
When the True Lung admits he truly hated his brother, his brother answers that he once thought he would die someday by his younger brother's hand.
When the True Lung confesses that he has always been waiting for someone to judge his mistakes, his brother answers.
Yan Li... You can set them aside now.

Around then, while searching for records from forty years ago, Ch'en found a neat stack of books, as if someone had pulled them out ahead of her, and there in the library she meets a girl of about ten, with dragon horns and red hair. The girl says she is studying to become the True Lung.

blocks.cap: Walking the girl from the library back home.

blocks.x: Ch'en tells the girl that laying so much power on one person is itself wrong. It is unfair to that one person, too.
Once you grow up, maybe you can make a change... So... grow up quick.
Meanwhile, Chun has admitted her wrongdoing and stepped down as Supervisor, and Wang, having killed Sui, has sunk back into something close to sleep, one with the Originium.

Meanwhile, Zuo Le goes to Mo Yi as she is about to leave and tries to return the wooden lock she said was her mother's keepsake. Mo Yi pulls an identical lock from inside her coat and tells him to keep it. How to make one, at least, she really did learn from her mother.
Mo Yi says she believes Zuo Le will never look at the Twelve with eyes that divide people from beasts, and then leaves into the sandstorm.
Around the same time, Chongyue asks Hou and Ju to keep him informed about Wang, and sets out on the road. The next time Wang needs help, he will never leave him alone.

The year turns, and as the snow begins to melt, Chongyue, on the road, notices a street wager game of weiqi. A boy whose father lost the family fortune at the board, and whose little sister is sick, has been pushed to the brink of defeat.
A faint voice reaches the boy's ears. 4-7, shoulder hit. Inside the boy's collar, a charm of black jade catches the winter sun and glows softly.
The words young Ch'en once heard were 'grow up soon.' Now Ch'en passes the same words to a child studying to become the True Lung. This time, she also tells her what needs to change.

act48side.tagline: A seasick Sargonian ambassador gets saddled with a Minoan temple construction project, only to discover that the national treasure she brought to return is a fake. And a lyre that, with blood on its strings, rings for the first time in a hundred years.

chars.name: Titi
chars.desc: Ambassador of the Sargonian delegation · museum curator · seasick

chars.name: Mio
chars.desc: Feranmut traveling with Titi · in charge of haughty comfort

chars.name: Xanthos
chars.desc: Ferryman of the Delphi Canal · dockmaster · Operator Varkáris

chars.name: Pallas
chars.desc: Proposer of the First Temple reconstruction · lover of drink

chars.name: Cassandra
chars.desc: Dream-reading priestess of the Temple of Endymion

chars.name: Lydia
chars.desc: Astynomos of Athenius · shrewd operator

chars.name: Lena
chars.desc: Rhodes Island doctor · Lydia's older sister · Operator Perfumer the Distilled

chars.name: Hekademos
chars.desc: Clerk to the Astynomos · the embodiment of leaving on the dot

chars.name: Lykeion
chars.desc: Xanthos's apprentice · nicknamed 'the Orating Pebble'

chars.name: Venui
chars.desc: Deputy ambassador of the Sargonian delegation · from the prestigious Ensifa family

chars.name: Periandros
chars.desc: Corinia's merchant-minded priest

chars.name: Siniska
chars.desc: Priest of Lakedaímōn · fingers that double as weapons

terms.name: Lyre
terms.desc: The instrument of the founding hero Kereseira. "It rings only for the tales of heroes." It vanished after old Athenius fell.

terms.name: Minos
terms.desc: A land of hero legends and theater where many city-states coexist. It fought Sargon for a long time before a ceasefire five years ago.

terms.name: Athenius
terms.desc: Minos's first city-state, the 'Mountain-Rimmed Garden.' It was rebuilt as a nomadic city during the Sargonian occupation.

terms.name: Sargon
terms.desc: The neighboring great power that once occupied Minos. Its regions are ruled by Padishahs. This time, it has sent a 'cultural exchange' delegation.

terms.name: Padishah
terms.desc: The title of the rulers who govern Sargon's regions. Above them all stands the King of Kings in the City of Gold.

terms.name: Kereseira
terms.desc: Minos's founding hero and the bard of its epic. Owner of the First Temple and the Lyre. Her statue stands in the plaza.

terms.name: First Temple
terms.desc: The first temple of Minos, built by Kereseira and refugees. Destroyed in the war, it is now being rebuilt by citizen volunteers.

terms.name: Oracle
terms.desc: A hero's revelation that arrives through dreams and visions. Interpreted by the priests of the Temple of Endymion.

terms.name: Ithakos
terms.desc: Xanthos's old friend. Nine years ago, he received an Oracle and left his hometown of Athenius.

terms.name: Ostracon
terms.desc: A pottery shard inscribed with yes or no and dropped into a ballot box. Minos's age-old way of voting.

terms.name: Burdenbeast
terms.desc: A large livestock animal of Minos, raised with a hood over its head.

terms.name: Delphi Canal
terms.desc: A canal built along the Delphi River, which flows down from Mt. Hymnoi. Ferries bound for Athenius travel its waters.

terms.name: Corinia
terms.desc: One of Minos's three great cities, famous for its business-savvy merchants.

terms.name: Lakedaímōn
terms.desc: One of Minos's three great cities, a city of martial arts famed for its fighting contests.

blocks.x: In Kerespereia, the epic of Minos, the founding hero **Kereseira** stands before outlanders who have trampled the land and commanded all things to sing for them. She hangs her lyre on the tip of a laurel branch and grips a dagger.
My lyre rings only for the tales of heroes!

Long, long after that, the war with **Sargon**, the neighboring great power that once occupied Minos, ended five years ago, and this year the two nations formally established diplomatic relations. Sargon will return Kereseira's **Lyre**, and in exchange it gets back the technical records it left behind when it built the three great cities during the occupation.

The one who hauled that Lyre all the way here is the delegation's ambassador, **Titi** (real name: Medjehtiqedti Nasutu Mashayer). A museum curator head over heels for Minoan legends, she broke away from the main party to walk in Kereseira's footsteps and promptly got herself lost. **Mio**, the haughty Feranmut who had to help drag along 50 kg of luggage, is absolutely fuming.
But at the end of the mountain path, both of them fall silent at the same moment.

blocks.cap: "Wow..." "Wow..." The 'Mountain-Rimmed Garden,' the nomadic city of Athenius.

blocks.x: 1. A Seasick Ambassador, and a Ferryman Who Welcomes Everyone but Sargonians

Meanwhile, at an auxiliary dock on the Delphi Canal, the giant ferryman **Xanthos** is getting an earful from his apprentice **Lykeion** for showing up ten minutes late. He still keeps going back over the day seven years ago when he ferried his friend **Ithakos** across on his way to the front. But when Ithakos said that day, "Minos's winter is especially cold this year," he can't recall what he said back.

At the same moment, in the Astynomos' Office, deputy ambassador **Venui** is pressing Astynomos **Lydia** about when the exchange ceremony will be. Lydia, swamped with the temple reconstruction and apple harvest season, promises a grand ceremony and a 'surprise,' and assigns her clerk **Hekademos** as their guide. The self-proclaimed 'Runaway Megaphone' opens with: "I'll do my very best... within working hours, of course."
Meanwhile, Titi's party turns up at the auxiliary dock and boards Xanthos's boat. As he rows, he explains that the Delphi Canal is kind to every good passenger, and then adds: "Except Sargonians."

Bringing up Padishah Mala, the 'Queen from Beyond' who burned the cities of Minos and banned their plays, Xanthos snaps that this delegation might just be another band of conquerors. Titi opens her mouth to argue back, but...

blocks.cap: The rebuttal will have to wait. The Sargonian ambassador surrenders to the canal first.

blocks.x: Still, clutching the apple Xanthos handed her, Titi finally opens her eyes and looks at the river. "This river, this city... they're so beautiful." The ferryman still has no idea his passenger is the Sargonian ambassador.
2. Civic Affairs by Arm-Wrestling, and a Proposer in an Apple Crate

That afternoon, after sleeping like the dead for three hours at the hotel, Titi follows Hekademos to the **First Temple** reconstruction site. But when she asks who proposed the reconstruction, he says, "Give me three seconds," and the moment the clock strikes 5 p.m. on the dot, he simply clocks out. Yes, really.

On top of that, the temple grounds are a battlefield between orchard farmers who need to haul out their apples and craftsmen who need to move stone, so the job of mediating falls to Titi, a tourist who just happened to be passing by.

blocks.cap: Black ears pop out from under the stone table. The two representatives' hands end up clasped before they know it.

blocks.x: Titi sets up an arm-wrestling match, hero-Heraces style, with one rule: only the winner gets to talk. Round after round, the shouting gives way, and each side starts to actually hear the other's situation. The solution is even bolder: shave down the peak that blocks the sun from the orchards, turn it into a quarry, and have the orchard farmers help with the quarrying too.

Meanwhile, at Ithakos's grave, **Cassandra**, the dream-reading priestess of the Temple of Endymion, comes to find Xanthos as he lays cyclamen on the headstone. Thinking of his friend, who left nine years ago after receiving a dream of 'a river stained with blood' as an **Oracle**, Xanthos asks her: if he told her he'd had the same dream, what reading would she give him this time?
Around then, back at the dock, Titi is searching for the reconstruction proposer, who vanished the night before, when she spots a single red flower swaying atop a pile of apples.

blocks.cap: "So this is the proposer with all that public support...?" A sleepyhead Forte, rolling out along with the apples.

blocks.x: Half-asleep, **Pallas** mumbles a solution that's exactly the same as Titi's, and Titi bursts out laughing. Right, this is Minos, not Sargon. Here, it isn't only mighty generals who get to be heroes.
3. A Banned Play, and One Blank Ostracon

Pouring cider she brewed herself, Pallas asks whether Sargon's conquest of Minos was ever necessary. Titi answers that dumping an empire's problems on its neighbors is nothing but incompetence, and the two become friends on the spot. Titi, for her part, gets thoroughly drunk on the drink Pallas swore was a cure for seasickness.

Around then, Rhodes Island doctor **Lena**, who is setting up a medical office for the Infected in her hometown of Athenius, meets her younger sister Lydia again, the girl she grew up with. Lydia calls her out to Lena's old garden, which was sold to the city and turned into a public garden, hoping to bring authority over Infected care under the Astynomos. Lena only tells her not to do anything dangerous.

Meanwhile, the Oripathy medicine Lykeion has been picking up actually belongs to his master Xanthos, who is hiding his infection. Hekademos, not knowing this, assumes his old classmate from the priests' academy is gravely ill and frets about it all by himself.

A few days later, beneath the finished statue of Kereseira, Titi learns why the classical play it's based on, Kereseira and the Outlander, vanished from the stage. After it was banned during the occupation, the outlander who gets executed came to mean a Sargonian, so these days nobody puts it on.

When Titi says she'd like to hold the exchange ceremony in this very plaza, Lydia suggests putting her in charge of finishing the temple outright, and **Periandros**, the priest of Corinia, chimes in: "Let's put it to a vote." Xanthos, overhearing them, confirms that the 'Columbian' who threw up on his boat was the Sargonian ambassador, and even guesses that her heavy 'cargo' is Kereseira's Lyre.

On the night of the vote, the craftsmen are already firmly on Titi's side, so much so that the craftsman Manos tells her, "I think of you as one of us." But in the line to cast the **Ostracon**, a man who once fought with the guerrillas speaks up.

blocks.cap: "Is it really the year 1100? I thought we'd gone back a hundred years."

blocks.x: Without so much as glancing at Titi, he tosses an Ostracon with nothing carved on it beside the ballot box and walks off. It meant she wasn't even worth a 'no' vote. The vote passes, but Titi can't bring herself to smile.

blocks.cap: The plaza after everyone has gone and the lights are out. Mio, beside a curled-up Titi.

blocks.x: Mio grumbles that she can wipe her tears on his fur, then immediately follows up with, "Scratch the tear-wiping. I hate getting damp." Thanks to that, Titi gets back on her feet and makes herself a promise: she'll finish the temple as fast as she can and return to Kereseira what should have been returned long ago.
4. Operation Lyre Heist (Culprit: The Kind Ferryman)

Some time later, on the day the Lyre is to be moved to the temple, the hotel shakes with a thud. Lykeion's boat, delivering groceries, took the request to pull up as close to the kitchen as possible a little too faithfully: it raised its sail and rammed straight into the kitchen.

While Hekademos rushes over and, convinced his friend's eyesight is finally done for, offers up his entire wallet as compensation, Titi escapes the smoke and bumps into a familiar giant in the crowd. With a bad feeling, she heads back to her room, and there's Xanthos, the crate pried open, holding the Lyre.

"You never should have made friends with a Sargonian." With those words to Pallas, he leaps out the fourth-floor window onto the haystack in the boat lodged in the kitchen. That boat was both a smokescreen and his ride out.

With Pallas's help, Titi jumps out the window too and gives chase. Cheered on by the craftsmen, she races across the streets until the two of them square off over the Lyre aboard a ferry hidden beneath the pier.

blocks.cap: Two hands reach out at once. The thousand-year-old Lyre goes flying.

blocks.x: In the brief moment the Lyre falls, the daughter of a fallen noble house who grew up with her father's study for company, and the ferryman who believed there was nowhere to bury himself but the battlefield Ithakos had gone to, wear the very same pale face.
The Lyre survives with a crack in its stand, and Titi covers for the arrested Xanthos and Lykeion, insisting that what got broken was her own personal property.
5. But That Lyre Is a Fake

But on the night she repairs the Lyre, Titi finds traces of a distinctly Sargonian anti-drying treatment in the wood grain along the crack. The lab identifies it as Sargonian resin from more than a hundred years ago. The delegation's Lyre was an elaborate replica, carved from Minoan wood by a Sargonian craftsman of old.
When Titi says the exchange ceremony has to be stopped, Venui scoffs.
What matters at a cultural artifact exchange ceremony isn't the 'artifact,' it's the 'ceremony.' So what if the artifact's a fake? It still makes a sound, doesn't it?

He even mocks Titi's late father as a useless man, declares that he is the real ambassador now, and goes straight to Lydia to blow the Lyre's theft up into a diplomatic incident. Cornered by the pressure, Lydia ends up charging Xanthos and Lykeion with treason and sending them to death row before any verdict is handed down.

blocks.cap: Death row. The price of trying to take back the Lyre.

blocks.x: Locked up in that prison, Xanthos opens up to his apprentice for the first time. When Ithakos was troubled by his dream of a red river, Xanthos brushed it off as iron dust from upstream, but in the end the one he had been deceiving all along was himself. A wandering old man in the same prison sneers at the two of them: since the invasion, is there anything left that they can truly call their own?

Meanwhile, Lydia informs Cassandra that she has chosen the popular classic King Perteus for the opening performance, and that Cassandra need only attend. Since Cassandra never once asked to see the Lyre, Lydia remarks, Sargon's Lyre must not be the relic she knows. Cassandra cannot find a word to say.
6. Is There No Hero Who Runs Off with the Lyre?

The day before the exchange ceremony, Titi tells Pallas everything and lays out her plan. If she runs off with the fake Lyre tomorrow, on the surface it will look as though the Sargonian envoy stole a national treasure. But as long as she keeps running, the powers that be in both nations will not be able to bury the truth.
That night, leaning back in the audience seats and gazing up at the stars, Titi wonders. Among all the hero stories her father told her, was there not one about a hero who runs away with a lyre?

At the same moment, at Hekademos's house, a jailbreak is being plotted, with Lena and even Cassandra joining in. And in the prison, when the wandering old man speaks of his son, who left nine years ago after dreaming of 'a river stained with blood,' Xanthos asks, his face rigid: "You... could you be Ithakos's father?"

Meanwhile, Mio, hearing the plan, explodes: even hauling the Lyre down the old road alone to avoid Venui's gang was a way of doing things where she was the only one who lost out. Titi smiles as she answers. What happened to Xanthos and Lykeion can still be remembered as a hero's tale, and even if her protagonist can do nothing but run, she wants to write a story of her own.
Hearing this, Cassandra takes Titi to a **Burdenbeast** pasture and clears away the fodder by a fence. The battered old instrument beneath, covered in teeth marks, is **the real Lyre of Kereseira**.

Cassandra says the Lyre, which has not sounded since the day old Athenius fell, is Titi's to take if she can make it ring. But no matter how she plucks it, it gives only a dull thud. When Mio suggests stealing the fake and running, Titi shakes her head: the heroes in her father's stories never ran away.

The father Titi remembers was a frail man who did nothing but collect old Minoan books, mocked by the nobles even at his own funeral. Even so, the voice that read hero stories to her was always strong.

blocks.cap: The pasture beneath the twin moons. In a dream, her father turns a page.

blocks.x: In the dream, her father straightens the back that was always bent, and speaks.
Every one of us is given the chance to become a hero. When there is a responsibility we must shoulder, all we have to do is accept it with courage, Titi.

Seeing tears on the sleeping Titi's face, Mio starts to snap a photo as evidence, then thinks better of it. He stands before the big Burdenbeast and mutters: she needs a 'miracle'? That's easy enough.
And the next morning, every last Burdenbeast in the pasture has vanished.
7. Countryman, Just Point Me in the Right Direction

This is the story Xanthos told Ithakos's father in prison. A year after Ithakos left for the front, Xanthos left the marsh village too. Ithakos had promised to come home when the war was over, and if he was already dead, Xanthos meant to avenge him.

The first thing he found was the armor he had made for Ithakos. The guerrilla wearing it said he had received it from another comrade as that comrade lay dying. Xanthos did not take the armor back. He said:
Countryman, just point me in the right direction.

And so the ferryman, who had never held anything but an oar and farm tools, joined the guerrillas. One by one, he found worn-out boots, a shield carved with initials, and a left-handed Arts unit. Each time, he left the item with the countryman who was using it now. A year later, he had become the most renowned guerrilla in the highlands.

Then, in a forest, a Sargonian officer tied to a tree confessed that two years earlier, his unit had wiped out the guerrilla band escorting the wounded. "I have found Ithakos." Xanthos told him that the name was their devotion and their love, and the Sargonians' crime and punishment, and he raised his oar.

blocks.cap: The silent fir forests of Minos. Somewhere among them, or everywhere within them, Ithakos lost his life.

blocks.x: When Ithakos's father, having heard it all, asks whether he got his revenge, Xanthos says no. Just as he was about to bring the oar down, a countryman with a broken leg caught hold of his hand, and the horns sounded: Minos had won the last battle before the ceasefire.

What filled that countryman's eyes was fear of Xanthos, a man who might shatter a peace they had only barely won. That day, Xanthos says, he realized the war had not ended. It went on inside his body.

Then Ithakos's father shares something unexpected. During the occupation, his grandfather, an engineer, was taken away and put to work building the nomadic city, and the Sargonians carried off every one of the engineers' notebooks recording the names of the Minoan laborers conscripted by force. Today's accepted history says that 'Padishah Mala did not use Minoans for forced labor.'
**What Sargon wants in exchange isn't technical records. It's the engineers' notebooks that record its own crimes.**
8. In the Wake of the Burdenbeast Stampede

On the day of the exchange ceremony, Ithakos's father tells them the escape route, even unlocks their shackles, and then says he will stay behind. "You haven't received your own Oracle yet. Until then, just stay alive."
As the two of them slip out of the prison with Hekademos, the bellowing of beasts comes surging toward them from somewhere.

blocks.cap: A herd of Burdenbeasts, loose from the pasture, sweeps through the streets of Athenius.

blocks.x: At the same moment, in the public garden, Lena is keeping Lydia talking to buy time. To her sister, who says that what she is protecting isn't the citizens' interests but her title of Astynomos, Lena replies, "I'm a doctor, Lydia."

Then the Burdenbeast herd tramples through the garden, and amid the scattered scent of flowers, Lydia opens up for the first time. Her sister left on a whim and dumped the plants tied to the inheritance on her, but Lydia never once hated that garden. It's just that her sister wants to take things back, and she herself won't look back.
"These ten-odd minutes I spent 'walking into your net of my own free will'? Think of them as my last gift to you. Sister Lena, I don't owe you anything anymore."

blocks.cap: The trampled garden. Her older sister's back, growing distant.

blocks.x: Lydia senses it. They will still cross paths for work, but this is the last time she will ever face the gentle 'Sister Lena.'

Meanwhile, hiding in an alley, Hekademos reveals that he has quit his job, and makes a long-overdue confession. Jealous of Lykeion's archery, he once sent an arrow flying far off, and when Lykeion went to retrieve it, he got hurt and became infected.

Their debates had stalled at 3 to 3, and on the final topic, 'Can the Infected be heroes?', Lykeion answers that what makes Oripathy frightening is that it puts an irreversible deadline on every dream. Hekademos then declares he will make Lykeion a hero of Minos and win the debate that way. The reply: "...You're insane."
And only then does Hekademos realize that the one in critical condition isn't Lykeion, but Xanthos, who left the prison saying he wanted to do something worthwhile while he still had the strength.
9. The Sargonian Who Volunteered to Play the Outlander
Around then, Xanthos goes to the temple theater to say goodbye to Cassandra, and asks the question he has carried for so long.

blocks.cap: "What exactly is an Oracle? Why can it drive people to their deaths?"

blocks.x: Cassandra answers that an Oracle is the true wish deep in one's heart given form, so nine years ago, even though she wanted to tell Ithakos not to go, she could not deny that wish. Then, for the first time, she reveals her own feelings: for five years she has watched over him, hoping that he, the last proof that Ithakos lived, would live in peace.

At the same moment, in front of the temple, **Siniska**, the priest of Lakedaímōn, brings the rampaging herd to a halt. A single finger placed on its head is all it takes for the lead Burdenbeast, which four or five grown men couldn't hold down, to drop to its knees, and the Lyre caught on the horns of the very last beast ends up in Cassandra's hands.

Then Titi, who came running after the Burdenbeasts, chooses Kereseira and the Outlander as the play for the ceremony and says she will play the outlander herself. When Pallas tries to stop her, she answers that this is the responsibility she must bear, here and now, as a Sargonian.

When the curtain rises, Pallas, as Kereseira, chants that the time has come to drive out the last outlander. Dragged onstage, Titi as the outlander repents of everything her father and her ancestors did, and cries out that she will pay the price without fail.

blocks.cap: The moment of execution. The tip of the dagger, which should be rubber, flashes in the sunlight.

blocks.x: But the soldier with the covered face seemed somehow unfamiliar, a shout of "Kill that wretch!" rose from the audience, and the tip of the dagger had the sheen of metal, not rubber. Titi chooses to trust her friend, and the heroic spirit of the Minoans, and closes her eyes.
At that moment, the man who steps out of the audience and kicks the soldier away is Xanthos, who should have already left Athenius.
Committing murder with a switched dagger and passing it off as an accident. When, and where, did we Minoans learn such a contemptible thing?

blocks.cap: Beneath the statue of Kereseira, an escaped prisoner with an oar puts his question to the whole plaza.

blocks.x: He asks why they set foot on land that was not theirs and why they came back as if nothing had happened, asks his countrymen how they can forget so quickly, and then exposes what the engineers' notebooks really are. And to an Athenius that imitates heroes through Oracles and plays, he cries out: where, then, is true heroic spirit?
In the silence, Titi takes one step forward.
Now, this is the battle I owe you as a Sargonian.
10. The Lyre Rings for the First Time in a Hundred Years

Bleeding in the fight, Xanthos hears the sound of a lyre from somewhere, and when he opens his eyes, an unfamiliar scene unfolds before him. A Minoan prisoner held in a Sargonian camp, and a young guard, 'Mashayer,' who sets the interrogation aside and keeps begging for hero stories.

Among the stories the prisoner made up off the cuff was one about Siopi, the Silent Hero, who kept a secret for thirty years. One night, the cell door was left slightly ajar, and the guard chasing after him tripped over armor that didn't fit and somehow couldn't get back up for quite a while.
"That's... my father." To Titi, standing in the same vision, Xanthos says, "He planted the seed of a hero in your heart."

The vision moves on to the audience chamber of Padishah Keri, who before her departure told her to trade the Lyre for 'a few blueprints,' and Titi now suspects she was chosen because she could be disposed of easily if anything went wrong. Even so, she came to Minos because she wanted to know the answer: what was the heroic spirit her father always spoke of?

Pallas, appearing next, shows them the day when, after years of getting by on drink to forget her hatred, she could not deny at Rhodes Island that the Blood Knight Dikaiopolis, an Infected Minoan, was a hero.
Heroes come from among us. That's why we, too, can define what a hero is and give it new meaning.
Only Minoans think of the hero Pheidippides when they see an olive branch, Pallas says, and no invader can ever take stories like that away. "Wherever we are, that is Minos."

And in the plaza of the real world, as the blood Xanthos has shed pours onto the strings of the old Lyre held by the statue of Kereseira, the Lyre, silent for a hundred years, creaks and begins to sound. As Xanthos, his strength spent, sinks down beside the pedestal, the Lyre's song rings on and on across the sky above the plaza, and the people realize they are witnessing a miracle.
Amid that sound, Xanthos finally remembers. That day, crossing the river, when Ithakos said this winter was especially cold, what he had said in reply.
Yeah, but it's all right. When spring comes, it'll be warmer than before.

blocks.cap: The riverbank that day, seeing Ithakos off. He smiled warmly at those words.

blocks.x: The pain of loss and an anger with nowhere to go had hidden even the face of Ithakos, smiling at those words.
Epilogue — The River of No Return

Afterward, Lydia withdraws the detention orders for Xanthos and Lykeion, and it turns out she had guessed the jailbreak plan long ago and quietly smoothed the way. Lykeion, leaving Athenius alongside Hekademos, still answers his demand to admit that Oripathy has nothing to do with heroic spirit with: "Don't make me laugh."

After seeing the two of them off, Lena finds pale blue boronia in the trampled garden. When they were little, she and Lydia promised that whoever got lost should come looking for this flower bed, and whoever found the way first would show the other the same way. Now that very flower had been planted all across the garden.
"Thank you, Lydia. I'm home."

Meanwhile, Pallas turns down Cassandra's offer to take charge of the First Temple; once the temple is finished, she plans to visit Lakedaímōn and Corinia. When Periandros proposes reviving the old league of city-states and their traditional festivals, Siniska answers briefly: "Lakedaímōn refuses no challenge."
And at the Delphi Canal, Xanthos ferries Titi across the river to see her off. When he says he still cannot accept Sargonians setting foot on Minoan soil, Titi tells him she understands.

blocks.cap: A dock on the Delphi Canal. The same ferryman, the same passenger, the opposite direction.

blocks.x: Titi says she will take every one of the engineers' notebooks and put them on display in her museum, so that every Sargonian can see that Sargon's history books are lies. Lydia has already arranged a special issue of a Columbian academic journal, and plans to award Titi an 'Honorary Minoan' decoration as well.

Told that Cassandra read Titi's vision as 'a revelation that she will become a Padishah,' Xanthos replies that if there had been a Padishah like her on the border, countless bloody tragedies might never have happened.

Then he goes back to face a citizens' vote on whether he will stay in this city or leave. Having told Cassandra that the river of his homeland in the vision was calm and unstained by blood, he is able to accept the result, whatever it may be, in peace.

Three months later in Sargon, Venui, sweating over the cleanup after Titi's special Minos exhibition, receives an envoy of the King of Kings. As he gets excited, sure the envoy has come for him, the envoy says, "You there, the noisy gentleman, you're not the one I'm here for," and summons Titi to the City of Gold. "...Yes!"

The hero of Kerespereia refused to play for the outlanders. A hundred years later, that Lyre rang again before a Sargonian who volunteered to play the outlander and a ferryman who bled. The Lyre rings only for the tales of heroes.

act47side.tagline: In a science paradise 600 meters up, a fake park guide, a smuggling Chief Executive, and a rule-reciting secretary stir up chaos until the whole paradise comes crashing down. And one tree, planted in the sky for a mother losing her memories.

chars.name: Nasti
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Engineering Section. A Banshee from Kazdel: few words, quick hands.

chars.name: Væla
chars.desc: An old Banshee who looked after the Banshees of the Convallis. Vanished from her hut after the forgetting began.

chars.name: Ferne
chars.desc: A one-woman tour guide who only goes where it's 'impossible.' Has been to the Bleached Wasteland three times · Operator Cairn

chars.name: Gordon
chars.desc: A Savra from ATAO who rose from Propeller Paradise's administrator to its Chief Executive. Can't stand rules · Operator Skybox

chars.name: Mercia
chars.desc: Gordon's secretary. Recites the 'Rules of Secretaries' in the face of any obstacle.

chars.name: Sky
chars.desc: A Rhine Lab assistant researcher who climbed up from the slums. Idolizes Kristen.

chars.name: Aspen
chars.desc: Head of 'Lucky Cystybeast,' who has bet everything he owns on the sky. A former grocer.

chars.name: Gustave
chars.desc: Former head of ATAO. Gordon's old boss.

chars.name: Oakley
chars.desc: The guide specially invited by Propeller Paradise. From Bunkerhill.

chars.name: Tin Man
chars.desc: A tin-armored veteran who came out of Kazdel's furnace alive. An old friend of Væla's.

chars.name: Laqeramaline
chars.desc: The 'Lord of the Banshees.' Built the Convallis together with Væla.

chars.name: Kristen
chars.desc: Rhine Lab's former Control, who split the sky over Trimounts two years ago.

chars.name: Muelsyse
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Ecological Section. An Elf who commands water clones.

chars.name: Saria
chars.desc: Rhine Lab's current Control. Sent Nasti to the park on a business trip.

chars.name: Jackson
chars.desc: Vice President of Columbia. Officially declared the push into the sky before Congress two years ago.

chars.name: Jara
chars.desc: Rhine Lab's former Director of HR. Now retired.

chars.name: Maryam
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Scientific Investigation Section. Out of contact for so long that rumors said Maryam had died in the wilderness.

terms.name: Propeller Paradise
terms.desc: Columbia's floating science park, hovering 600 meters up. The crystallization of 'sky fever.'

terms.name: Rhine Lab
terms.desc: The Columbian science company Kristen once led. The original proposer of this park.

terms.name: ATAO
terms.desc: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium. The Columbian agency that inspects Originium products and polices their import.

terms.name: Maylander
terms.desc: A Columbian foundation. Its Emergency Management Council takes over administrative authority in accidents and disasters.

terms.name: Convallis
terms.desc: A hidden refuge beyond Mist Lake, built by the Banshees 200 years ago. They dreamed of a life with songs and desserts.

terms.name: Roosting Tree
terms.desc: A great tree deep in the Convallis. Thought of as a Banshee's final resting place.

terms.name: Banshee
terms.desc: A Sarkaz people charged with funerals and guiding the dead. For them, 'forgetting' is itself a sign of death.

terms.name: bone pen
terms.desc: The tool Banshees use to inscribe incantations. Nasti runs the Vivarium with hers.

terms.name: Space Fin 054
terms.desc: A finbeast-shaped robot guarding Gordon's collection. Claims to be an 'extraterrestrial.'

terms.name: Ring Lab
terms.desc: Rhine Lab's experimental facility that lit up tens of millions of Columbians on that night in Trimounts two years ago. The Vivarium is built on the data it sent back.

blocks.x: Ever since a beam of light split the night sky over Trimounts two years ago, Columbia has been completely bewitched by one little word: 'sky.' Furniture sprouted propellers, and any company that slapped 'sky' onto its name watched its stock soar.
The crystallization of that fever is a floating science park hovering 600 meters up: **Propeller Paradise**. In seven days it will host Air Expo Columbia, broadcast live across the whole nation.

blocks.cap: In the high-altitude elevator, a cartoon guide gushes about the future of the sky.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, far, far away, the tin-armored veteran **Tin Man** arrives at the Banshees' **Convallis**, ringed by Mist Lake, only to find the hut beneath the Roosting Tree, where his old friend lived, standing empty.
For a Banshee, forgetting is a signal sent by death. **Væla**, an old Banshee who had been losing her 300 years of memories one by one, has vanished from the very spot where she sat waiting to die.
1. The Very Bottom of a Sky Paradise

Up in the park's sky restaurant, Cloud, administrator **Gordon Tannen** is busy sweet-talking investors. He's a Savra who used to frisk people at the border for ATAO, and he hustled his way all the way up here.

Then his old boss shows up: **Gustave**, former head of ATAO. Gustave lets Gordon know he's recommended him as the park's Chief Executive, but adds a sharp jab. Without Kristen Wright, all this talk of progress and the future would be nothing but sleep-talk.
And even as Chief Executive, there's exactly one power Gordon doesn't get. That one belongs to the park's original proposer: **Rhine Lab**.

Rhine Lab itself, though, is stuck way below the levitation layer, in the Vivarium down on the ground. **Nasti**, the Banshee Director of Engineering (few words, quick hands), has spent half a year raising saplings and tweaking floating botanical units.

Her assistant researcher **Sky** is losing his mind. The advance tour skipped Rhine Lab entirely, and it feels like Kristen's dream is about to end as one glorified 'botanical garden.' "How long has it been since we last looked up at the sky?"

blocks.cap: The sky, seen from beside a pit of dirt, crammed with every company's floating gadgets.

blocks.x: Instead of answering, Nasti just tugs the brim of her hard hat down a little.
2. Second Rule of Secretaries: Lunch Is a Brick
Around then, Gordon's secretary **Mercia** drops by the Vivarium. She answers absolutely everything with the 'Rules of Secretaries,' and the notebook of rules Gordon gave her is a whole 2 cm thick.
Nasti, who has turned down Gordon's emails sixteen times, skips the lunch invitation and instead digs a wad of foil out of her toolbox. Inside: a ration bar the size of a brick.

blocks.cap: "Is the lunch you mentioned... that brick?" "It's a ration bar."

blocks.x: Following the Second Rule, 'never decline an offer from your boss's guest,' Mercia chews the thing down and promptly starts coughing.

But Nasti has a rule of her own: 'no one lies in front of food.' So Mercia spills Gordon's actual request: please run the engineering inspections in the order Gordon drew up. Nasti knows there's a trick hidden in it, but takes the list anyway.

That same day, Sky slaps a failing grade on Lucky Cystybeast's floating revolving bar. The concept is 'you may spin, but your wine won't,' except the tester was busy spinning and throwing up. **Aspen**, the company's head and a former grocer, begs that he's bet everything he owns on it. No dice.

Sky has his reasons, too. He grew up in the slums and spent six years mopping the floors of an engineering college while eavesdropping on lectures. Then, on that night two years ago, while getting beaten up in a back alley, he saw a light shooting into the sky and chased after it in a daze.

blocks.cap: That night in Trimounts two years ago: a beam of light soaring into the sky.

blocks.x: When he asked the people he ran into who that great person was, the one who answered "Kristen Wright" was Nasti. That's why Sky can't stand the way nobody mourns Kristen anymore.

Meanwhile, at Cloud, Gordon is raising a toast after receiving the congratulatory telegram on his appointment as Chief Executive, when a man walks in and introduces himself as Oakley, the guide the park specially invited. Gordon sprays his whole mouthful of champagne.
3. The Fake Guide and the Missing Client

The 'Oakley' who'd been running the advance tour was actually **Ferne**, a one-woman tour guide who'd been posing as the park guide for a month after the real Oakley, drunk on heartbreak, more or less handed her his résumé. She borrowed his identity to ask how to cure her client, an old Banshee she met in the Bleached Wasteland whose memory was going hazy.
Gordon, who'd just been threatening to toss her 600 meters down, suddenly offers to help that client. "Columbia will do good by a good person."

Of course, Gordon's kindness always comes with a price tag. Deep inside the park, in a secret collection, he's been hoarding things banned under ATAO regulations: Sarkaz sorcery weapons, Leithanian Arts units, and plenty more.

Gordon has been secretly transplanting these into companies' exhibits as their 'hearts,' and Aspen, on the verge of elimination, gets called in too. At the door, visitors are greeted by **Space Fin 054**, a robot very proud of its laser cannon.

Meanwhile, Gordon assigns Ferne to Nasti as the Vivarium's guide. Ferne fires off a string of off-the-wall questions, like which horn-care brand Nasti recommends, then wanders off to tour the Vivarium.
Not long after, every plant in the Vivarium withers in an instant. 72 trees, 350 saplings, and about 1,000 freshly sprouted seeds.

blocks.cap: The Vivarium, dried to ash-gray in a matter of seconds.

blocks.x: As if he'd been waiting for it, Gordon calls in the guards and seals off the Vivarium. Nasti asks: "When did those guards show up outside the door?"

Meanwhile, the runaway Ferne is holding a pale rod she pulled out of a Vivarium tree: a Banshee's **bone pen**. She borrowed it thinking it might wake her client up, with no idea it was the key that ran the entire Vivarium.
But when she gets back to her lodgings, the client's room is empty. On the wide-open window frame, only a fragment of black feathered horn sways in the breeze.
4. A Guide Drops into the Collection: "We're Done For"

Gordon names Ferne as the culprit and puts out a warrant. His original plan was only to make her look like Nasti's accomplice and then expose her fake identity. The Vivarium disaster caught even him off guard.

Around then, Mercia finds an access port in the dead trees, tracks Ferne down, and sides with her instead of her own boss. If Ferne wants to find her client, she says, she should check the row of 'VIP rooms' outside Mr. Tannen's office.
But locked in the VIP room isn't the client. It's the real Oakley. On the spot, Ferne signs Oakley up for 'Ferne's Tours,' warns of "some loud noises," and knocks out the guard.

The chase spills up into the levitation layer. The two borrow a jump-board and leap onto the top of a pod, the guards open fire, and the hole they blast in the wall opens, of all places, into Gordon's secret collection.

blocks.cap: The Chief Executive and the guide, face to face from a meter apart. What they both blurt out at once: "We're done for."

blocks.x: That same day, Sky goes to see Gustave alone. He'd found nonstandard parts in Aspen's revolving bar, and figured out that the supplier was Gordon.
Gustave snatches the report and has his bodyguards drag Sky out. The very first rule he ever taught Gordon, apparently, was this: "We'll always be of one mind when we stand for Columbia."

When Sky is let go and returns to the Vivarium, the news waiting for him is that Nasti has apologized to Gustave and handed over control of the site along with Rhine Lab's place in the expo. Meanwhile, the testers who'd had nowhere to go have somehow ended up hired by Rhine Lab.
When Sky beats himself up for being nothing but a musbeast in the gutter, Nasti asks him: "Why do you think ordinary people are supposed to be left behind?"
5. A Director in a Flowerpot, a Tree Shooting into the Sky

Gordon decides to hurry the rest of his contraband out. The hauling goes to Ferne and Oakley, who wrecked his collection; the route is Rhine Lab's transport tunnel beneath the sealed-off Vivarium. Mercia volunteers to keep Nasti busy.
But Mercia has a secret. She's a special agent of **Maylander** posing as a secretary, and she's been quietly hiding the missing Banshee client. The client's name: Væla.

When Mercia runs an old slide projector, scenes seep out of Væla's memories: the chains of a Leithanian spire, a cathedral in Laterano, the Bleached Wasteland. At the end of it all, Væla murmurs that the trees here are withering too, and that she can sense that child here.
That same night, as Gordon's crew makes its way through the underground tunnel, 'Nasti' appears in front of them. Except this Nasti is weirdly bubbly, and keeps saluting.

blocks.cap: 'Nasti' rises up wreathed in streams of water. Gordon's crew freezes, clutching their crates of contraband.

blocks.x: It's actually a water clone that Nasti's colleague **Muelsyse** hid in the potted plant she gave her as a farewell gift. One line, "If you died here, how many people would even know?", and the three of them run for their lives.

Meanwhile, the real Nasti follows fragments of the bone pen bearing traces of a familiar incantation through the night streets, and remembers her childhood in the Convallis. When little Nasti angrily blew into a bone whistle that wouldn't make a sound, Væla taught her to play a leaf whistle instead.

blocks.cap: "One does not need a bone whistle to accompany a smile."

blocks.x: And in the shadows at the end of the street, an old Banshee is waiting for that child. But before she can call out the name, something begins rising into the sky.

The floor beneath the Vivarium has caved in, and a giant 'tree' of rotted wood and tangled metal is shooting up into the night sky. Hanging from its branches: Gordon, Ferne, and Oakley, contraband crates and all.
Watching the young Banshee run toward the tree, Væla never manages to call her name. "In the sky... is that the Roosting Tree...?"
6. The Hearing Is Delayed, and the Trial Begins
The next day the park is in an uproar, but what the company heads want to know isn't the truth. It's whether the expo is still happening.

In front of the tree, Sky, the researchers, and the testers form a human wall. "If Director Lunorey hadn't taken me in, I'd already be in prison by now." Just before it comes to blows with the guards, Maylander's Emergency Management Council shows up and takes over administrative control of the park.

blocks.cap: The floating platform at daybreak: a standoff in front of the 'tree.'

blocks.x: Locked in a cell once again, Ferne has a story of her own. She once refused to believe the adventure tales of her father, who was mocked as a braggart. When he died last year, she started a travel agency on her own, keeping his name on the staff roster.
'Impossible' is just an excuse for the lazy and the cowardly.

That's how Ferne became a guide who only goes where no one else will. Two months ago, in the Bleached Wasteland, she found a Banshee who had collapsed. The Banshee said she "still hadn't seen that child," and pointed toward D.C. with an incantation.
Nasti, who comes to the cell and hears the whole story out, says that what dragged a Banshee whose forgetting had already begun all this way must be the last obsession left in her mind.
"**Thank you for caring for my mother, Ferne.**" With those words, Nasti is taken into custody by the Council. "The hearing is delayed, but the trial has already begun."

At the same time, the 'scientific consultant' Gustave brought in turns out to be a hulking Kuranta. When the consultant points out that the drive mechanism inside the tree has empty slots for two 'keys,' Gustave reaches his conclusion: if a device is low-risk but invites speculation, you can define it however you like.
And Tin Man, the 'senior' Mercia had been waiting for, arrives at the park.
7. A Deal in the Cable Car
Nasti is taken not to a prison but to a ropeway station, where Tin Man invites her aboard a cable car to look around the park together.

Tin Man hides nothing. Over a hundred companies are tangled up in the smuggling ring, and digging it all up would kill the expo. For a hearing that is only a formality, nothing makes a better explanation than Rhine Lab.

Looking out the window, Nasti remembers the day she first met Kristen. Nasti had been recording the voices of the Banshees and listening to them thousands of times over, and Kristen asked her to take charge of Rhine Lab's Engineering Section.

blocks.cap: "I'm only looking for the power that will let us break through the sky."

blocks.x: If we're doing what no one has ever done before, we'll face doubt and loss more times than we can count... So we must never stop.

The deal Nasti offers is this. Two years ago, when Kristen diverted the Department of Defense's investment, the one undeniable accomplice was Nasti herself. So she alone will take responsibility, not the company.
Her conditions: leave everyone else at Rhine Lab alone, and let her assistant researcher take the tree's data. Just before getting off, she also tells Tin Man that Væla is in the park.
