Soon the park broadcast announces the outcome of the hearing. The suspect, Nasti Lunorey, has admitted to all charges and is in custody, and the expo will open as scheduled.

The broadcast drifts into the room where Væla is hiding as well. Asked what has happened to Nasti, Mercia lays her hand on the projector's dial, as she always does. Erasing memories with Originium Arts was Mercia's work as a Maylander agent.
But the hand turning the dial stops in midair. She cannot do this to an old woman with so few memories left.
"I'm sorry, my daughter. Because of me, you had no home to return to."

Near the end of her time in the Convallis, Væla had just seen off Demoi, a fellow Banshee whose memory emptied out over three months before she died. Every Banshee who died after they settled in the Convallis went through that same forgetting.

Afraid her clever child would see the truth, Væla deliberately kept Nasti away from the Roosting Tree and the funerals. **Laqeramaline** told her the child would only feel that her mother was pushing her away.

blocks.cap: The day she left the Convallis: a small boat gliding across Mist Lake.

blocks.x: And so Nasti left the Convallis. The answer she was looking for was not in Kazdel, she said, so she would go to Leithanien, or Laterano, or Columbia. After a long silence, this was all Væla said.
Take care of yourself, and make sure you eat well, my daughter.
Nasti did not look back. "Farewell... Mother."
8. By the Script, All the Way to the Fall
As the expo's live broadcast draws near, Mercia clouds the memory of the colleague sent to move Væla, buying her thirty minutes. "Go and fulfill your wish. You are free now."
At the same time, Gordon opens the opening-speech draft Gustave sent him. His joy at being given the podium lasts only a moment. It is a public apology announcing the cancellation of the expo.

And the ones who get Nasti out of her cell are Sky and, unexpectedly, Gordon. Gordon returns her confiscated bone pen and apologizes for his testimony at the hearing. "I'd rather stand in the dock with you than act out the script that man wrote for me."
Then, on the live broadcast screens, the floating pods begin to fall, and the falling pods stop in midair. As if someone were holding them tight.

What caught the 'accident' Maylander had staged was an incantation. Recognizing that its owner was a Banshee other than Nasti, Tin Man changes the plan: blow up a single engine and drop the entire levitation layer.

Meanwhile, Gustave lays his cards on the table for Gordon. Everything Gordon smuggled in was foreign military equipment that Gustave himself had picked out. Once the park blows, the sky fever will turn into Columbian rage against 'foreign spies,' and the park will become a testing base for armaments.

At the same time, in the surveillance room, Tin Man tells Mercia the same story. The passion for the sky has no force left in it this time, so its direction has to be 'turned.' He knows full well that the sacrifices of an arms race will not end with this one park.

blocks.cap: The long table in the surveillance room. Her senior called his own words 'nonsense.'

blocks.x: Mercia, don't forget... your family name is 'Selene.'

Meanwhile, instead of the sealed route, Nasti walks upward among the pods frozen in midair. With every step, a tile appears beneath her feet. The path is stitched together with the incantations the Banshees of the Convallis used, laid out for Nasti alone.
When Nasti lays her hand on the tree's roots, she feels warmth. She looks up, and a figure entangled in the roots calls to her. "Nasti, my dear daughter... you've come back."
9. A Rogue Outside the Rules, a Tour Group's Flag
Just before the opening speech, Gustave seats Gordon in the 'defendant's chair' in front of the cameras. Apologize as written, he says, and a position at the Department of Defense will be waiting.
The moment Gordon refuses, saying the chair is too uncomfortable, the live countdown ends, and Space Fin 054 pounces on Gustave.

blocks.cap: The former head of ATAO, pinned under 054, his face on every live broadcast screen in the park.

blocks.x: 054 was an old ATAO answering machine, the culmination of Gordon's seven years at the Bureau. Ever since the night he wrote his first self-reflection letter and caught the noise coming from that machine, Gordon had studied every device that passed through his hands, until he gave 054 the power to think for itself.
This 'Propeller Paradise' must never become a breeding ground for war.
Gordon's plan had a 10% chance of success: gather the contraband scattered through the exhibits, build a new power unit out of it, and make off with the entire park.

Ferne and the Rhine Lab staff signal to one another with the anti-collision lights on the floating botanical units as they recover the parts, and in the end everyone gathers before Maylander's cordon.

blocks.cap: A striped flag and a megaphone. The guide takes her place at the head of the 'tour group.'

blocks.x: Ferne raises the megaphone and calls out names one by one. A cobbler who wants to leave footprints on the twin moons. A hardware store owner who wants to tighten a screw on the second Ring Lab.

Then Aspen speaks for himself. To protect his family from creditors, he divorced and left home, and he promised his wife that he would put the name 'Lucky Cystybeast' on TV to show her he was doing all right.
Run! Jump! Fly!
The people charge the cordon, and the exhibits loaded with contraband take off into the sky. It was absurd. But it was free.

The one who hands Gordon the 34 parts is the scientific consultant, supposedly Gustave's trump card, who even helps assemble the power unit. Gripping the lever, Gordon says, "All right, Propeller Paradise. Say goodbye to D.C."

At the same time, in the surveillance room, Mercia pulls Tin Man and his three friends into a whirlpool of memories to hold them in place. Making people forget had always been her work, but this once, she wanted her senior not to forget: how many people's lives and dreams lay behind the price he was willing to pay.
As the plate drifts away from D.C., Maylander finally presses the detonator, and the entire levitation layer falls, engulfed in flames.

blocks.cap: Floating pods pouring down like pitch-black meteors.

blocks.x: In that sky, Ferne and Aspen hang from parachutes. Had the plate not changed course, the wreckage would have fallen squarely on the people in the park's lower levels.
"Aspen, you can go to Northville to see your wife now." Ferne fell along with 'Paradise,' and came back down to the world of people.
10. The Sky, a Land Promised to the Sarkaz
At the same time, inside the tree, Væla is half-swallowed by roots and bark. Seeing the path for her daughter's return crumbling, she merged with the tree herself to hold it together.

The tree shares Nasti's memories with her: her daughter staying up all night in the Lich's library, hiding her feathered horns in Laterano, sleeping on a steel shelf. Seeing it all, Væla cannot stop fussing over her.
Then Væla confesses the lie she has kept for 200 years. Of the Banshees who went through the war in Kazdel 200 years ago, fewer than a thousand survived, and half of those had lost their voices.

blocks.cap: Kazdel, 200 years ago. The coalition's steel fills the horizon.

blocks.x: The surviving Banshees settled in the Convallis and built lives with songs and desserts. But the 'tokens' announcing the deaths of their kin kept pouring in, and Væla intercepted them. If the Banshees set out to hold funerals, they would return to their old path.

The price was heavy. Souls left unguided could not return to the souls of the Sarkaz, and Banshees who went against their nature were consumed by a long, painful forgetting as death approached. Among the souls left unattended was Nasti's birth mother.
Nasti had known from the start, and that is why she left. And she gives that day's parting a name: not a regret she failed to make up for, but a conspiracy between the two of them.

Nasti reprograms the tree and undoes the fusion. The memories the tree shared, she says, were only temporary data for experiments, and the Roosting Tree of the Convallis was really just an ordinary phoebe tree that had reached the end of its life.
"Why did you make your tree look like the Roosting Tree?" "Because it reminds me of you."

On the day she left, Nasti lowered her head and looked at Væla's reflection in the water. That face, never free of tear stains, seemed to smile at the moment ripples crossed the windless surface. Above the sky reflected in the water.

blocks.cap: A small boat cutting across the sky reflected in the water. The mother's face, as her daughter remembers it.

blocks.x: After all, the sky, too, is a land promised to the Sarkaz.

This 'tree' can be more than a refuge for the living. It can be a place where Sarkaz souls return: a place that gathers the residues of information left after death in a server in the sky, and lets each one decide for itself what to leave behind in the end.

Asked what she wants to leave behind, Væla never finds an answer. Instead, she tells her daughter, "Don't stop here, either." If this tree can become a new resting place for Sarkaz souls, she will be its first resident.
Twenty-some years ago, I found you a home. Now, find one for me.

Every memory fades, and what remains at the very end is one brief scene: herself putting to sleep the child she had just brought to the Convallis, tired-faced, going on and on about nothing but how adorable that child was.
And so Væla vanished into the air. A single leaf came fluttering down.

blocks.cap: "To accompany a smile, there is no need for a bone whistle at all."

blocks.x: Nasti puts the leaf to her lips and blows. "Be at peace."
Epilogue. A Sky with Room for One Tree

That day, millions of D.C. citizens watched the fall in silence. The press soon cried out about a foreign 'premeditated act of terror,' and Vice President **Jackson** prepared a speech declaring that what they had destroyed was the dream of every Columbian.
But when the smoke cleared, the sky was not empty. A single floating facility had broken through the clouds and hung there.

blocks.cap: After everything else had fallen, the 'tree' alone remains above the clouds.

blocks.x: The Department of Defense immediately recommended opening fire, but **Jara**, Rhine Lab's former Director of HR, says it is just a tree. Fowlbeasts are already preening their feathers on it.
If that sky is the soil that will nurture a new era for Columbia... I see no reason it cannot make room for a single tree.
Afterward, Rhine Lab's Control, **Saria**, strikes a deal with Jackson. The park's 'escape' is treated as though it never happened, and the park is linked back up with D.C.

That night, Aspen says he wants to stay at the park and pay off his debts, and asks Ferne to deliver a letter to his wife. Gustave is led away in handcuffs, and Gordon says he will go back to ATAO and keep upgrading 054.
When Mercia visits the tree before leaving, Nasti tells her that every new leaf is Væla's epitaph. If Mercia remembers her, perhaps the wind will let a leaf or two fall.

Leaving the tree in Sky's care, Nasti returns to Rhine Lab headquarters in Trimounts. The last to enter the meeting room is a guest with loudly clattering hooves: **Maryam**, Director of Scientific Investigation, who had come to the park at Gustave's invitation.

blocks.cap: Rhine Lab's directors, together again. But first, the year-end party they had put off.

blocks.x: From deep in the Infy Icefield, Maryam has brought back fragments of a giant structure that Kristen called the 'Stargate.' Saria says that Nasti now holds the key that opens the door to a new field, and Rhine Lab must be the one to turn that key.
The sky was empty to begin with. The pods, the billboards, and the dreams that once filled it have all fallen, but now a single tree floats there, holding the things that forgetting cannot take away.

act46side.tagline: In a snowbound nation that has not known a Catastrophe for a thousand years, the first one falls. The Saintess sets out on a midwinter pilgrimage in search of a silent god, and her brother stands against a great power's fleet massed at the foot of the mountains.

chars.name: Enya
chars.desc: The Saintess of Kjerag. After the Catastrophe, she questions her god's silence and sets out on a pilgrimage into the blizzard · Operator Pramanix

chars.name: Enciodes
chars.desc: Head of the SilverAsh family and founder of Karlan Trade. An ambitious man set on reforming Kjerag through trade and industry · Operator SilverAsh

chars.name: Ensia
chars.desc: The youngest of the SilverAsh family, younger sister of Enciodes and Enya · Operator Cliffheart

chars.name: Joanna
chars.desc: A young hunter who lives alone in the snowy mountains. Daughter of a family that branched off from the Paleroches · Operator Snow Hunter

chars.name: Elena
chars.desc: A young researcher in Rhine Lab's Energy Department. She sets out to explain the Catastrophe through science · Operator Astgenne the Lightchaser

chars.name: Adso
chars.desc: An aged elder of the Vine-Bead Court who has spent half his life studying the scriptures in the Hall of Writings

chars.name: Arctosz
chars.desc: Head of the Paleroche family. A hot-tempered, blunt Ursus warrior

chars.name: Ratatos
chars.desc: Head of the Browntail family. Known for her calm, calculating way of dealing with others

chars.name: Sciurus
chars.desc: Ratatos's younger sister and heir to the Browntails. Frank and cheerful

chars.name: Degenbrecher
chars.desc: The Black Knight who travels with Enciodes. A bodyguard renowned for her skill

chars.name: Gnosis
chars.desc: A director of Karlan Trade and Enciodes's longtime associate

chars.name: Carolin
chars.desc: A researcher at the Rhine Lab observation station. She disappears with a bundle of documents just before the Catastrophe

chars.name: Monch
chars.desc: A Browntail warrior

chars.name: Duke of Caster
chars.desc: A great noble of Victoria. Enciodes's mother was his niece

chars.name: Alberta
chars.desc: A Victorian journalist who has come to report on Kjerag

chars.name: Sharp
chars.desc: An operator of Rhodes Island

terms.name: Kjeragandr
terms.desc: The god the people of Kjerag have served for a thousand years. Believed to rule the blizzards and the mountains and to keep the nation safe from Catastrophes

terms.name: Vine-Bead Court
terms.desc: The religious institution that serves Kjeragandr, and the spiritual center of Kjerag. The Great Elder and the clerics oversee matters of faith

terms.name: Three Clans
terms.desc: The collective name for the three families that make up Kjerag: SilverAsh, Paleroche and Browntail. They returned political power to the Vine-Bead Court and debate affairs in the Tri-Clan Council

terms.name: Karlan Trade
terms.desc: Kjerag's first international trading company, founded by Enciodes. In practice it handles Kjerag's foreign trade and diplomacy

terms.name: Rhine Lab
terms.desc: A Columbian scientific research company. Together with Karlan Trade, it built an observation station in Kjerag's snowy mountains

terms.name: Radsorn
terms.desc: The 'invisible monster' of Kjerag's bedtime tales. Passed down as a loanword whose original meaning has been lost

terms.name: Heart of Karlan
terms.desc: A name that appears in the scriptures' account of Kjerag's origins. Commonly thought to refer to Lake Silberneherze

terms.name: Lake Silberneherze
terms.desc: A lake in Kjerag. A statue of Kjeragandr stands there

terms.name: Silver Bell
terms.desc: A bell carried only by the Saintess. When rung, it is said to make a sound that calls Kjeragandr

terms.name: Feranmut
terms.desc: A legendary giant creature said to have been the size of a mountain range. With no reliable records, scholars dismiss it as fantasy

terms.name: Tschäggättä
terms.desc: The SilverAsh family's private army

terms.name: Trilby Asher
terms.desc: Victorian special agents in the service of the Duke of Caster

terms.name: Maylander Foundation
terms.desc: A foundation Carolin has been in contact with behind Victoria's back

blocks.x: Kjerag is a nation of faith among snow-covered mountains. No Catastrophe has struck this land in a thousand years, and its people believe that is the protection of their god, **Kjeragandr**.
Heed these commandments, and no calamity shall befall this land, and your home shall endure forever.

Over a decade earlier, at a banquet held by Victoria's Duke of Caster, the young **Enciodes** of the SilverAsh family declared that Kjerag would become a power impossible to ignore within thirty years. When the Duke asked on what grounds, he answered that Victoria had probably never considered what a nation united as one could do.

blocks.cap: The Duke of Caster's banquet hall, and a young relative from a foreign land.

blocks.x: Then, in December 1101, the first Catastrophe in a thousand years strikes Kjerag.
1. The Great Elder's Last Question

Before he dies, the Great Elder of the Vine-Bead Court summons **Enya**, the Saintess of Kjerag and Enciodes's younger sister, and makes a confession. Long ago, Kjeragandr's voice fell silent. He filled that void with his own will, and committed many wrongs.
Do you still... hear Kjeragandr's voice?

The old man thrashes, saying he saw Her abandon Kjerag, and at last asks her to read the final chapter of the scriptures. It is the chapter in which She tells the people they will walk the path ahead alone, and vanishes into the blizzard.

Meanwhile, at the train station, Rhine Lab researcher **Carolin** was fleeing with a bundle of documents held to her chest. When the Browntail warrior **Monch** caught her, she shouted that there was a bomb in the station, emptied it, and slipped away. When he caught up with her again on a mountain road, she asked him a question in return: how much longer did the people of Kjerag think they could last on the protection of a 'god'?

blocks.cap: The sleeping snow mountain awakens. For the first time in thousands of years, a Catastrophe has struck this land.

blocks.x: Black Originium fragments are found where the avalanche that buried the train station below the mountain began. When the Black Knight **Degenbrecher** reports that this was a Catastrophe, Enciodes orders the site sealed and the Infected concealed, straightens his clothes, and returns to the meeting room to resume the discussion where he left off.
2. She Never Promised

By then the Vine-Bead Court has split in two over whether this is a trial or a punishment. A cleric says She is angry because unbelievers were allowed to build on Mount Karlan. Enya, who granted that permission, asks him where in the scriptures She ever promised to protect Kjerag from Catastrophe forever.

Enya forbids talk of 'Kjeragandr's punishment,' announces that she will devote herself to interpreting the scriptures in the Hall of Writings, and entrusts the affairs of the Vine-Bead Court to the new Great Elder, **Adso**.
That night she returns to her room and calls for **Kjarr**, the head maid who has always been at her side. There is no answer.

blocks.cap: "...You promised. You said you would never just disappear."

blocks.x: In the room, where only the crackle of the fire remains, the Great Elder's last question echoes in her ears again.

Meanwhile, at the Rhine Lab observation station, Karlan Trade director **Gnosis** is searching for the missing researcher. When he, Enciodes's longtime associate, asks what caused the Catastrophe, Energy Department researcher **Elena** answers that there were no warning signs at all, and goes one step further.
Kjerag's long peace, and the attitude that takes that peace for granted — that is what's 'abnormal.'

But Elena soon finds that the readings from the early hours of December 7, the day before the Catastrophe, are identical to those taken at the same time three days earlier. Someone had swapped the data, and the person on observation duty that day was Carolin.

Then shouts ring out outside the station, demanding that outsiders leave Mount Karlan. An old woman in the crowd throws a snowball in Gnosis's face and tells him that he is the one driving Her away now.

Meanwhile, Columbia hints at pulling out its researchers, and Victoria presses aid on Kjerag that even includes 'peacekeeping squads.' Enciodes accepts it and tells Gnosis that if a Catastrophe has come after a thousand years, the customs of a thousand years must change as well.
3. A Midwinter Pilgrimage

Two days later, Enya has spent the night in the Hall of Writings, and Adso, who has kept to that hall for half his life, comes to see her. Together they read an old tale of a warrior who alone saw the monster 'Radsorn' on the ice, and Adso splits the word into 'an unseen place' and 'an unknown monster.' The place no human can look into is the heart.

Radsorn is the monster within the heart, Adso says. Since not even She can defeat it on the people's behalf, only the Saintess has the right to atone in their place. As the old man bows his head as if pleading, Enya asks in return, "A 'pilgrimage,' then."

As he withdraws, Enya asks whether he believes Kjeragandr does not exist. Adso answers that She surely does. If a god who granted whatever was asked appeared before one's eyes, he says, how could that be called faith?

Meanwhile, the heads of the Three Clans corner Enciodes. **Arctosz**, head of the Paleroches, throws down a Victorian supply crate and declares that he will not let Victorians onto his land, and even **Ratatos**, head of the Browntails, sides with him.

That evening, Enya summons her brother to the Vine-Bead Court. At the end of her rebuke that he treats everything only as words or cards to play, Enciodes speaks a name he has not called her in a long time: 'Enya.'

blocks.cap: The SilverAsh siblings, looking at the statue rather than at each other.

blocks.x: Enya announces that she will undertake a midwinter pilgrimage: three months on foot around Kjerag, with no attendants, no carriage and no rest. Some Saintesses have died on that road.
As Enya of the SilverAsh family, I have never forgiven the decision you made back then. But as the Saintess of Kjerag, I am simply grateful that there is still something I can do.

Even so, Enya urges him not to halt the changes. The factories, the railways and the observation station are cracks through which Kjerag can escape the prison of the heart, she says. Then she asks him to look after their youngest sibling, **Ensia**.

And so the pilgrimage begins. When villagers at the foot of the mountains, who have heard nothing from their families since the Catastrophe, ask whether She has truly abandoned them, Enya asks them to believe in Her goodness, and they choose to believe.
4. The Hunter of the Snow Mountains

Once the Saintess has left, the attacks begin. Arctosz, lured onto a mountain road by a false summons in the Vine-Bead Court's name, loses his car to a rockfall. Ensia, who set out with documents in her brother's place on the same summons, ends up hanging from a cliff after a staged collision, where Degenbrecher finds her.

Around the same time, in a snow-covered forest, an arrow pierces Enya's leg. As a second arrow aims for her heart, a young hunter, **Joanna**, carrying a crossbow bigger than she is, brings down the attackers and drags Enya away.

Joanna tends her wounds but makes no secret of her hatred for the SilverAshes. Karlan Trade's railways cut through the mountains and rivers and the animals died off, she says, and her family, who had lived devoutly for generations by hunting and carving holy statues, paid the price. Hearing this for the first time, Enya does not argue. When her cloak slips and reveals that she is the Saintess, Joanna begs forgiveness and asks to be punished.

Among the statues of Kjeragandr lying about the cabin's backyard, one crude figure reminds Enya of Kjarr — the head maid who used to insist that the statues looked nothing like Kjeragandr, and that the face should be slimmer.

blocks.cap: Joanna's backyard. Targets, a crossbow, and half-carved statues of Kjeragandr.

blocks.x: After sunset, when Enya calls her the most devout believer she has ever met, Joanna finally breaks down in tears. Her father, who carved statues every night to pay for her Oripathy medicine, was at that train station on the day of the Catastrophe.
Enya can find nothing to say and only strokes her back. If even the eternal Kjeragandr is silent, what can Her Saintess do?

Meanwhile, below the mountain, Enciodes sends Degenbrecher into the snowy mountains, suspecting that the real target may be Enya. When she tells him to prepare for the worst, he does not lay out his reasoning as he usually would. He says only that he trusts Enya.

That night the attackers surround the cabin again. The two throw them off with a statue of Kjeragandr propped behind a curtain and a set of traps, and at the end of a chase through the forest, Degenbrecher appears and slams the last of them into the frozen ground. They wore Paleroche armor, but their arrows had only two fletchings. Paleroche warriors use three. It was a Victorian disguise.
5. A Funeral Without a Body

Around then, below the mountain, the Browntails fall under suspicion for having escaped the attacks. When her younger sister **Sciurus** comes to her at night, Ratatos swears before Kjeragandr that she will protect her and the Browntails even at the cost of her own life.

Then she meets the Victorian Ambassador and joins hands with Victoria in exchange for a guarantee of safety for the Browntails and their people. The most urgent task is to deal with Arctosz, she says, so the following night she will have one last 'talk' with him at the family's old manor.

On the appointed night, Arctosz has the grounds of the old manor searched, and the Victorian spies hiding there are caught one after another. Before a Browntail guard can finish explaining that Ratatos meant to use herself as bait to draw them out, the manor explodes, and a single charred jacket drops from the flames.
At the funeral that follows, there is no body. The coffin holds only the clothes she wore in life and ashes gathered from the site.

blocks.cap: Snow piles on black umbrellas at the temple. A coffin without a body is placed upon the altar.

blocks.x: Sciurus, now head of the family, feels for the first time the weight of the mask her sister had to wear, and Arctosz says Ratatos died because of him and that he will not forget it. When the funeral ends, an envoy of the Vine-Bead Court announces that the Court will take custody of the captured spies, and warns Enciodes to abandon his delusions of monopolizing power.

Enciodes did not attend the funeral. In a car parked at a street corner, he says they must seize the opportunity Ratatos has bought them, and takes out a letter from the Duke of Caster. In exchange for aid and investment, it demands a share in Kjerag's mines, Originium included. It is little short of a declaration of war.

A few days later, while sorting through her sister's belongings, Sciurus finds that on every one of the family's business documents, her own name is written in the head of family's signature line. A communicator in the secret box the two of them shared holds a missed call from Karlan Trade. It was made yesterday.
6. What Fell from the Sky

Earlier, thirty-three hours before the Catastrophe, it is night at the observation station. When Carolin, Elena's senior, suggests that a Feranmut might be the reason Kjerag has gone a thousand years without a Catastrophe, Elena shakes her head and calls it unscientific.

blocks.cap: Beyond the observation station's transparent dome, a sky veiled by the blizzard.

blocks.x: That night, left alone, Carolin saw a strange light split the sky.

After the Catastrophe, Elena restores the damaged data from mechanical sounds picked up by a surveillance camera, and learns that at 3:19 a.m. on December 7, something fell onto Mount Karlan. The Catastrophe came thirty-two hours later.

Around then, Carolin has Monch, who survived the avalanche, tied up in a cabin. When he accuses her of being a spy, she tells him the story of a Victorian scholar seized by an intelligence agency and made to dig up Columbia's secrets, and says that she was simply bored with all of it.

Meanwhile, Enya, searching for Kjeragandr, slips back into the Vine-Bead Court's Hall of Writings and runs into Elena, who has also crept in. Elena's hypothesis is that an Originium vein inside Mount Karlan held off Catastrophes for a thousand years, until an 'extraterrestrial object' fell from the sky and broke the balance. Joanna, who came with Enya, objects, but Enya says she understands.
At that moment, Enya feels Kjarr's voice fading in her memory. Holding down her fear, she recalls a passage from the scriptures.
Her heart is the heart of Karlan, Her dwelling deep within the mountains.

The Heart of Karlan may not be Lake Silberneherze after all. The impact point Elena calculated lies in the joint Kjerag-Kazimierz mine, and the three set out together. On the way, Elena's detector displays 'Moderate Catastrophe Risk.'
7. The Swordsman's Victory

Meanwhile, Victoria's Duke of Caster suspects that the joint mine is really a Karlan Trade munitions factory. He buys up Kazimierz's stake and draws in clerics of the Vine-Bead Court. But when the Victorian Ambassador, with an envoy of the Vine-Bead Court at the front, opens the mine's secret warehouse, there is nothing inside but broken scrap.

The Vine-Bead Court then summons Enciodes on charges of colluding with Victoria. Enciodes arrives with ten years of trade records and his private army, the 'Tschäggättä,' declares that clerics have been in contact with Victorian spies, and lets no one leave the Vine-Bead Court.

Adso counters that if Enciodes cannot produce evidence before sunset, the SilverAsh name will vanish from Kjerag. As they argue over Kjerag's future, Adso brings up Enciodes's parents. Born a Browntail, he says the man who killed Enciodes's parents is standing before him, and holds out his bony hands, asking to be judged not for treason but for murder.
Enciodes closes his eyes, grips his cane, and answers. He has no intention of harming him. He will see that Adso receives a fair trial.

At the same moment, at the mine's exit, a Victorian agent's truck is stopped. An old cleric in the cargo bed sends Carolin, who was hiding with him, into the tunnel first, then lets himself be caught. Gnosis only watches through a telescope as she disappears into the dark.

When the cleric and the agent, now proof of collusion, are brought to the Vine-Bead Court, Enciodes has Adso and all the elders taken away. On his way out, Adso tells the apprentice clerics left behind to go on living, and to act according to their conscience no matter what happens.

blocks.cap: "The swordsman's victory lasts but a moment."

blocks.x: 8. A Vein of Iron, a Bell of Silver
By then Enya's party has reached the depths of the mine, and what lies there is not Originium but an ordinary Oriron vein. There is no trace of the extraterrestrial object either.

blocks.cap: Before the Oriron vein, Enya realizes the plan her brother has been hiding.

blocks.x: Enya says only that this place is not the Heart of Karlan but the 'bones' that hold up Kjerag's spine. As the other two lose heart, Joanna pleads with her to call on Her, and Enya rings the Saintess's Silver Bell.

The sound of the bell echoing through the cave stops Elena cold. Its frequency is nearly identical to the impact sound recorded at the observation station the day before the Catastrophe, and the Silver Bell was made by artisans in imitation of the sound the mountain makes.

If the mountain is a bell, there must be a vast hollow inside it. Enya recalls a refuge within Mount Karlan where clerics of old were said to have hidden with the scriptures, yet she cannot remember who used to bring her honeyed cystymilk when she worked on the scriptures late into the night.

Below the mountain, meanwhile, the board is overturned. Enciodes steps down from Karlan Trade, leaving behind a single letter of appointment, and Gnosis, who succeeds him as chairman, announces an end to all cooperation with Victoria and suspends every contract Enciodes signed.
Meanwhile, Sciurus follows an address Enciodes handed her as an 'invitation' and finds Monch tied up in a cabin.

Around then, Carolin makes it out of the tunnel, is abandoned by the Victorian agents who came to meet her, and is rescued by agents of the **Maylander Foundation**. She hands over only the 'extraterrestrial object' file, then throws the report meant for Victoria out of the car window into the blizzard, one page at a time.
And in prison, Adso moves one of the guards with the scriptural tale of 'Jürgen the Confessor,' then walks out between guards who stand aside for him and disappears into the snowy mountains.
9. There Is No God

And Ratatos, thought dead, is alive. Having handed the spies she caught behind her faked death over to Enciodes, she captures and questions the Victorian journalist **Alberta**, who pleads that what Kjerag needs is not Victoria's 'support' but real help.

Meanwhile, an open letter from the Duke of Caster listing Enciodes's 'crimes' floods Kjerag, and the Duke's special agents, the 'Trilby Ashers,' fall upon Ratatos's group. As they take refuge in the Vine-Bead Court under Degenbrecher's guard, a fleet led by the Duke himself sweeps toward the foot of the mountains.

blocks.cap: Under dark clouds, Victoria's steel Feranmuts trample the white ice field.

blocks.x: Watching the fleet, Enciodes tells Gnosis that since he chose this hard road himself, it is time to face where it ends.

Meanwhile, as Enya's party climbs Mount Karlan, they come upon Adso resting with the clerics who fled with him. He admits that urging the pilgrimage was itself a ploy to separate the Saintess from the Vine-Bead Court, and then says the opposite of what he told her on the day she set out: Kjeragandr does not exist.

In a lifetime spent searching the Hall of Writings for proof of Her, all Adso found were patched-together scriptures and the marks of past elders' revisions. People who needed comfort on the despairing snow mountains created 'Kjeragandr,' and to keep order, the lie had to be repeated generation after generation.
We did not build our country atop Her flesh and bones. We built Her country atop our own flesh and bones.

Asked whether she truly believes in Kjeragandr, Enya tries to remember Kjarr, but her face and voice are already gone. With an empty heart, she answers that she still believes. Adso offers to guide her if she helps him drive out Enciodes, and she sets one condition: if they witness Her existence, he must abandon every scheme against her brother.
10. The Unsheathed Blade

On reaching the foot of the mountain, the Duke gives Enciodes six hours. While the Victorian army blocks the roads at the base of Mount Karlan, the 'Trilby Ashers' storm the Vine-Bead Court to seize Ratatos, and Degenbrecher stands alone in their way.

blocks.cap: Covered in wounds, the Black Knight does not give ground.

blocks.x: When she staggers after facing seventeen of them, Rhodes Island's **Sharp** emerges from the smokescreen and holds her up. The Doctor sent him, he says. The hardest hour is already behind her.
At the same moment, Arctosz plants himself before the fleet and shouts that anyone who wants to set foot on Kjerag's soil will have to step over his corpse first.

And in the secret armory, Enciodes changes into formal wear and has a last conversation with Gnosis. A question from their youth, about making Kjerag a vast stage on which to use their talents to the full, has brought them to this day. Enciodes says he is glad to have had them, and trails off, saying they may manage what comes next better than he would.
Go and see the Kjerag of your dreams for yourself.

Around then, in a cave near the summit of Mount Karlan, Elena finds a vast hollow behind a thin rock wall and blasts it open. Adso had said that behind the legends of Saintesses awakening Her lay nothing but massacres and political compromise. Yet now that the wall is open, he refuses to go in.

It was he and the Vine-Bead Court, Adso says, who comforted the poor kneeling in the mud praying for salvation — no, for the end of their lives. He calls Her a tyrant for turning away from them and breaks down in tears. Enya says her faith will not waver whatever she sees, that she wants to look squarely at the path the people of Kjerag have walked, and goes deep into the cave.
11. The Heart of Karlan
The depths of the cave are pulsing. Stone veined like blood vessels glows in time with the sound, and the instruments pick up vital signs. They are inside the body of a living creature.
In the darkness stand rows of prostrate ice statues. They are Saintesses of the past who froze to death begging Her to return when She vanished, and all of them face the same direction.

blocks.cap: Where the frozen Saintesses gazed. Kjeragandr as the people of old saw Her.

blocks.x: When Enya's hand touches the colossal statue, visions pour over her. In a dream, Joanna's arm turns to stone from Oripathy as a beast mocks her, asking what good her faith has done her.

At the same moment, outside the cave, Adso comes face to face with himself decades ago, quietly ordering pine resin and firewood stacked in the secret room where the SilverAsh couple would be received, and he is swallowed by the flames of that day.

Enya sees a thousand years into the past. Three peoples are fighting over a lake that never freezes when someone appears before them, makes their crops grow, and ends the fighting. But when that someone leaves to rest, the people begin to suspect one another again.
Then a farm girl, chosen as the next Saintess, climbs the mountain and freezes in the blizzard calling for her mother, while someone cries out for her to stop, that she will die.
That voice calls to Enya. "So you saw." Enya looks up, and standing before her is **Kjarr**.
On a snowfield where the wind has died, in the middle of the lake that never freezes, Enya faces her. Asked whether she should call her Kjarr or Kjeragandr, she answers.
Kjeragandr is the name the people of the past gave me. But Kjarr? Kjarr will always be Enya's head maid.

She was not a god. Like her kin long ago called 'Feranmuts' and 'lords of the land,' she was just one life that had fallen onto this land without knowing why. She never made the commandments, and never wished for the Saintesses to die.

Living among humans, what she saw was the instinct of a small, frail species to survive by helping one another, and people called it 'virtue.' The form of Kjeragandr was made by humans, she says, but it is not a lie. They only borrowed that name to draw out the strength they already had.

Kjarr says she cannot stay by Enya's side this time, that her time has run out, and calls Enya the first Saintess ever to set out on the pilgrimage carrying resentment and bitterness. With her parting words, to clear away the last dark clouds and open a new tomorrow, the vision shatters, and in Enya's palm remains a single perfect snowflake that does not melt.
12. The Last Prayer

Joanna wakes and says that She told her in the dream that Oripathy is not a punishment. Elena, who saw nothing, falls silent before the one answer left: a Feranmut. Then the alarm rises another level. The probability of a second Catastrophe within three hours is 72 percent.

At the mouth of the cave, Adso says he saw Her footsteps, that the unforgivable unbeliever was himself, and collapses. Enya traces an arc on his forehead with her fingertip, tells him that while he did not know it, She was learning from him too, and in Her place absolves him of the sin of unbelief.

blocks.cap: The Saintess's fingertip traces an arc on the old man's forehead.

blocks.x: As the Duke's six hours are running out, a single silver-gray high-speed warship emerges from a snow-covered valley. Beside the fleet it looks paltry. Its commander, Enciodes, boards the Duke's flagship, the Gloriana, and declares that he has come to represent Kjerag as the only one who holds real power there.

blocks.cap: The flagship Gloriana. Two men face each other again after more than a decade.

blocks.x: He turns the Duke's contract on its head. Victoria may take part in the mining up to 80 percent, but no Victorian troops may enter, and sovereignty over the resources stays with Kjerag. Then a shell fired from the mountain shakes the fleet.

blocks.cap: Sciurus commands a battery hidden in the mountain. "Let's show them Kjeragandr's protection!"

blocks.x: 'D5, east, two hundred meters.' At Enciodes's word, a single shell lands precisely beside the flagship. The whole mountain is an impassable line of artillery, he says, and gives the Duke thirty minutes. This is the price of invading this land.

Meanwhile, Enya changes into her most formal attire and climbs the mountain path countless Saintesses have walked over a thousand years. For the first time, the path feels as near as the way to an old friend. Reaching the summit, she kneels.

blocks.cap: The summit of Mount Karlan. The Saintess's last prayer.

blocks.x: We will hold your goodness in our hearts. We will give thanks that you were with us. And we will leave your embrace...
The light scatters between the girl's palms, and the Catastrophe clouds that covered the sky part. The observation station's Catastrophe alarm stops almost as soon as it sounds.

At the same moment, as Adso is about to end his life at the edge of a cliff, a girl passing by holds him back. Telling him there is no proper time for repentance, she leaves a greeting for the absent Enya: when the time comes, she will visit again.

And before the Vine-Bead Court, clerics and artisans, herders and merchants form a silent wall in front of the army. Alberta steps out from among them and declares that she is the 'hostage,' and that the people of Kjerag never kidnapped her. A rainbow spans the sky, and the soldiers lower their weapons without meaning to.

Back on the deck of the Gloriana, the Duke asks whether this is the power of a nation united as one. Enciodes answers that what matters most is always 'people,' and that he put his trust in the people of faith in this land.
What stands in your way now, Your Grace, is 'Kjeragandr's might.'

blocks.cap: Light pours onto Mount Karlan through a gap in the clouds.

blocks.x: Acknowledging that the scales of victory have tipped, the Duke orders a withdrawal.
Epilogue — After the Descent

Enya has the clerics who followed Adso work the fields on the Three Clans' lands through the winter, and tells them to come back in spring. When a young cleric says Her miracle felt like a farewell, Enya answers that Her parting words are already written in the scriptures.
Heed these commandments, and no calamity in this land shall prevail over you, and your home shall endure forever.

Elena decides not to rush to publish her discovery of a Feranmut's traces. Carolin's guilt as a spy has been confirmed, but Elena still remembers the look in her senior's eyes when she talked about the universe.

And Enciodes receives Columbia's Vice President, Jackson. To the rumor that the Duke withdrew after witnessing a miracle, he replies that the Duke merely realized the price would be too high. Asked what he is now, he defers his answer.
I hope they will take this name as one of the countless foundation stones for Kjerag's next era.

And in a clearing deep in the mountains, Elena's power armor touches the object that fell from the sky. Thirty percent of its composition is nearly identical to the somatic cells of Terra's Elves. Seeing the shape of the infrasound the object gives off, Enya recalls the symbols of ancient Kjerag and writes out her translation in the snow.
Destruction... has come

The commandment once read as a promise that no calamity would befall them for a thousand years now reads that no calamity shall prevail over them. She has said her farewell, and Kjerag begins to walk the path beneath its own feet, as the final chapter of the scriptures said it would.

act45side.tagline: The leader of Ave Mujica, trapped in the Dream Castle, dives into the happy dreams of her four sleeping bandmates one by one to wake them up — and gets turned down by all four. No matter how wonderful a dream is, sooner or later it's time to wake up.

chars.name: Sakiko Togawa
chars.desc: Leader and keyboardist of the five-member band Ave Mujica. She often stays up all night writing new songs.

chars.name: Uika Misumi
chars.desc: Ave Mujica's vocalist and guitarist. Sakiko's childhood friend, and a popular idol.

chars.name: Mutsumi Wakaba
chars.desc: Ave Mujica's guitarist. A friend of Sakiko's since they were little, and a girl of few words.

chars.name: Umiri Yahata
chars.desc: Ave Mujica's bassist. Pro-level skills — and she handles the members' schedules on top of that.

chars.name: Nyamu Yūtenji
chars.desc: Ave Mujica's drummer. A popular figure who also livestreams, and who often butts heads with Sakiko.

chars.name: Vigna
chars.desc: A Vanguard operator at Rhodes Island. Sakiko's senior coworker and a kind-hearted nag.

chars.name: Iris
chars.desc: The mistress of the 'Dream Castle.' A fairy who gives children good dreams.

chars.name: Bena
chars.desc: Iris's partner. An all-purpose fairy who can fix and handle just about anything.

chars.name: Morpheus
chars.desc: A fairy of the Dream Castle. She prides herself on being the castle's true mistress and its finest 'Dream Weaver.'

chars.name: Wolff
chars.desc: A being who stays by Morpheus's side in the Dream Castle. Speaks with a stutter.

chars.name: Coretton
chars.desc: A pack of monsters in the Dream Castle who follow Morpheus. They can't speak.

chars.name: Eyjafjalla
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator who studies volcanoes.

chars.name: Croissant
chars.desc: A member of Penguin Logistics. This time she's on security duty at a TV studio.

chars.name: Francis
chars.desc: A member of a small family in Siracusa who drifted over from Columbia.

terms.name: Ave Mujica
terms.desc: The five-member band Sakiko formed. Its overwhelming 'doll'-themed stage concept has made it a hit.

terms.name: Masquerade
terms.desc: The name of Ave Mujica's shows — stages that promise to lead their guests into a dreamlike world.

terms.name: Dream Castle
terms.desc: A fairy-tale place said to lie in the forests of Victoria, where fairies show children beautiful dreams.

terms.name: Dream Weaver
terms.desc: A term for the rare fairies of the Dream Castle whose Arts let them create dreams themselves.

terms.name: Dreamless Border
terms.desc: An abyss where those whose dreams have shattered are said to fall and wander.

terms.name: Siracusa
terms.desc: A city that runs on a tangle of families and order, where mafia families vie for power.

blocks.x: The night after a Masquerade, the five members of the band **Ave Mujica** are waiting for the light at a crosswalk. Drummer **Nyamu Yūtenji** is excited about doing more fan service, while leader and keyboardist **Sakiko Togawa** lectures her about protecting the band's concept.
Then vocalist **Uika Misumi** speaks up. They've had their fights, but she's so glad the five of them are together again — everything's just like before, **like a dream**.

A dream. At that one word, the voices of old arguments ring in Sakiko's ears, and while her bandmates cross the street, she can't take a single step. The light turns red, the rain pours down, and Sakiko looks up at the sky and cries.

blocks.cap: Everyone crosses. Only Sakiko stands still.

blocks.x: 1. The Workaholic Rookie and the 'Fairies'

Then, amid a rattling, clattering sound, Sakiko opens her eyes. She's aboard the Rhodes Island landship, a rookie operator who joined only a few months ago. Her senior **Vigna**, who's come to wake her, offers to check whether she's still dreaming — and goes straight for a cheek pinch.

When Sakiko describes a dream full of scenery she's never seen, Vigna chalks it up to exhaustion. But workaholic Sakiko, who takes on late-night training and Medical Department support on top of everything, has no intention of resting — ever since losing her mother to illness, she's been set on helping people who suffer. In the end, she even tags along on a supply run Vigna is escorting.
Riding in the transport are two people introduced as 'fairies': **Iris** and **Bena**. The fairy-tale **Dream Castle** really exists, they say, and they're the very fairies who show children dreams.

Iris is in a hurry because of a girl who writes fairy tales, her pen pal for a whole year. The girl had sent stories about a father who rages that 'this is my real life' and a lonely little girl — and, saying she comes of age tomorrow, added one more line: **"This is my last letter."**
They have less than twelve hours left, and that's exactly when a tire blows. In the middle of the scorching wasteland, a long, long wait begins.

blocks.cap: A transport with a flat tire, under an indifferent sun.

blocks.x: 2. One Last Lullaby Before Growing Up

They reach the town a full four hours late, and it's already night. Splitting up to search, Sakiko asks for directions from an old flower-shop lady with poor eyesight and makes her way to 33 Garden Street.

Behind the creaking door, a drunken father is crying out for 'Anna.' His hand cut on a broken bottle, he crawls toward Sakiko, mistaking her for his daughter — and Sakiko leaves the room, gripped by a sadness and longing she can't explain.

Outside the house she runs into the girl, **An**, and the two of them go into a church. There An confesses that she wrote her fairy tales by turning the story of her home, which fell apart after her mom left, inside out. Several times today she stood at a high railing looking down at the ground, but she couldn't let go of Iris's letter in her pocket.

The clock hands on the wall are closing in on midnight, and Iris still isn't here. So at a moonlit piano, Sakiko gave An, moments away from becoming an 'adult,' the gift of a lullaby. When the bell tolled with the final note, An was asleep with a peaceful face.

blocks.cap: A church at midnight. The birthday present: one lullaby.

blocks.x: Arriving just after to give An a dream, Iris says dreams aren't meant for losing yourself in. All a fairy can do is plant a seed deep in a child's heart: the most precious moment or thing from their childhood.
Usually, it just rests quietly in the deepest part of the heart. But at a crucial moment — the moment a person is at their weakest — it gives them strength.
And in An's heart, she says, that seed had already been planted. Thanks to Sakiko.

Sakiko puts on the necklace Iris gives her, said to ward off nightmares — and when she turns around, no one's there. The corridors of Rhodes Island and a rainy intersection flash past one after another, and the last place she opens her eyes is inside a vast castle under two moons.
3. A Challenge from the (Self-Proclaimed) Mistress of the Dream Castle

Then, out of the darkness, to the click of high heels, a girl appears and introduces herself as **Morpheus**, mistress of this castle. Those days at Rhodes Island, trusted by everyone — that was a dream Morpheus had been making Sakiko dream.

In a castle with nobody but a pack of mute **Coretton** monsters and the stuttering **Wolff**, Morpheus says she's replayed the unfamiliar scenery in Sakiko's memories over and over. When Sakiko snaps that clinging to dreams and the past is weakness, a stage curtain slowly begins to rise.

blocks.cap: The curtain rises. In every chair, a familiar face sleeps.

blocks.x: Uika, Mutsumi, Nyamu, Umiri. All of them are sunk in Morpheus's 'top-grade' dreams and won't wake no matter how she calls — and then Sakiko's own arms and legs get bound up tight with strings.
Morpheus's game is simple. Go into the four girls' dreams and wake them all, and she'll send them home. Fail, and the four stay in this dream forever, and Sakiko goes back to sleep too.

Knowing Morpheus won't let her go even if she refuses, Sakiko declares the opposite. These are the finest members she hand-picked herself, and she won't leave until every last member of Ave Mujica is together.

After sending Sakiko into the dreams, Morpheus looks down at her sleeping form, vowing to figure out why she failed last time. After all, she's the finest **Dream Weaver** in this castle — or so she says.
4. Love — Lungmen's Star Doesn't Play the Drums

The first dream she steps into is the neon-drenched metropolis of **Lungmen**. Here, Nyamu is a movie star whose films and ads cover every screen in sight, and Sakiko is too busy getting shoved around by swarms of fans to do much else.

One night, filming grinds to a halt after the director and the screenwriter get into a fistfight and both end up in matching neck braces. On the phone from home, Nyamu's little brother excitedly tells her he's started practicing on the drums she used to play. Nyamu promises to practice with him tomorrow — then accepts a variety-show offer that comes in right after.
In front of a dusty electronic drum kit, unable to even remember where her sticks are, Nyamu murmurs that if you're going to live as a pro, sometimes you have to give something up.

On the day of the taping, Sakiko hands her entire savings to a shady man to sneak into the studio. But she sets off the brand-new intruder detector of **Croissant**, who's on security, and gets chased by a swarm of drones — while the man running beside her cackles and turns into Morpheus.

Meanwhile, in a studio at the end of an endless corridor, Nyamu overwhelms everyone with her performance as a 'doll' and says: surrounded by geniuses, an ordinary person like her has no choice but to work dozens of times harder.

For the final segment, Nyamu reenacts the famous scene from 'Drummer Girl,' shouting that she'll play the drums her whole life, that she'll be the greatest drummer in Terra — and at that moment, her true feelings overlap the line. **But I quit the drums.**
Just then comes a sound that should never be heard mid-shoot: shattering glass.

blocks.cap: Sakiko crashes through the window, grabs Nyamu, and falls.

blocks.x: Is this really your dream, Sakiko asks, having lost your drums, your bandmates, even yourself? Where did the Yūtenji who hated losing more than anyone go? And this time she calls her by name. "Nyamu, it's about time you woke up from your dream."
5. Fear — The 'Traitor' of Siracusa

The second dream is **Siracusa**, where the drizzle never stops. In this dream, Umiri Yahata is a lone-wolf bodyguard who drifts from one mafia family to the next, and she's just walked out of the prison gates with an instrument case on her back.
Cornering her in an alley are **Francis** and company. After Umiri left, they were attacked and lost their boss and their comrades, and they believe it's all the fault of Umiri, the 'traitor.'

Meanwhile, after hearing the story from Francis, Sakiko asks — what if someone deliberately drove the two of them apart? — and at that very moment, bodyguards burst out of the cabinets all around and seize her.

Around then, Umiri remembers something. Having a small family trust her had felt oddly nice, and on the night she turned down Francis's invitation to a family party, a feeling she'd never known before kept her awake.

Then, at dawn, after she'd made up her mind and packed her bags, her other employer — an old boss — sent her to prison to take the fall for his crimes. For half a year she longed to go back to that party night, but what awaited Umiri on her release was a ruined family. She had lost a 'home' all over again.
Now that same old boss offers to take Umiri into his family, with one final test: dispose of the captured Sakiko. And this time, he adds, no faking the scene with blood packs.

blocks.cap: The boss watches Umiri. Morpheus watches Sakiko.

blocks.x: Even so, Sakiko doesn't back down. It was the boss's own men who went after Francis's family, she says — is being used and thrown away over and over really the 'trust' you wanted? "Ms. Yahata, come back with me."
6. Sorrow — An Island for Two, a Missed Boat
In the next dream, Sakiko finds a single ferry ticket to a remote island in her hand. The boat leaves before sundown, and though the island has paved roads, there isn't a single car on it.
Watching Sakiko tumble down a slope, rickety borrowed bicycle and all, Morpheus cackles that this is the best thing ever.

Meanwhile, on the same island, Uika is spending time with **Eyjafjalla**, an operator who studies volcanoes. When Uika sings a song she can't remember learning, Eyjafjalla tells her she somehow looks sad.

The villa behind the volcano where they escape the heat is a house Uika looks after alone. Its owner, 'Saki,' was the first friend who ever truly saw her — but she left alone on a boat and never came back.

Meanwhile, in Uika's dream as Morpheus shows it, the two of them grew up together on this island from childhood and lived together. Uika has only one wish — 'I want to be with you' — but the dream always ends with Sakiko disappearing.

By now, having lived the same day over and over, Uika can barely recall Saki's face or even her name, and says she'll just wait here quietly. Eyjafjalla tells her that if she's crying, her heart is still holding on, and urges her to shout with everything she has.
Before she knew it, Uika was running. And by the time Sakiko reached the villa, Uika was aboard a boat leaving the island to find someone.

blocks.cap: She reaches the pier out of breath. The boat has already sailed.

blocks.x: Admitting she never expected Uika to leave, Morpheus calls it a draw. The boat will soon hit the edge of the dream and drop into the next one, she says, and with every repeat, Uika will forget a little more of Sakiko.

Then the seawater surges up wildly and drags Sakiko down to depths no light can reach. In the darkness, as her breath runs out, a familiar voice calls 'Saki' — and when she opens her eyes, there in the sandstorm is **Mutsumi Wakaba**.
7. Death — Letting Go in the Spring Light

The fourth dream she reaches is the land of sand, **Rim Billiton** — a small house deep in a narrow mine shaft. Mutsumi remembers everything the two of them have done together, and those words are what finally let Sakiko steady herself.
In this dream, Mutsumi sells cucumber juice, her mother mends clothes, and her father works at a construction site. They aren't well-off, but her mother holds Mutsumi close and smiles warmly.

That night, at a party where the neighbors have gathered, Mutsumi tells Sakiko that all of this is a lie, and that when she met Saki, she knew it was time to go back. She only asks for one last time — even if only in a dream — to sing freely, like everyone else.
Sitting on a cracked black chair, Mutsumi plays "Haruhikage" on a classical guitar. A melody that can never be forgotten, for as long as one lives.

blocks.cap: In a small house full of people, "Haruhikage" plays once more.

blocks.x: This was not the Mutsumi of old, who had struggled with her guitar. Her expression was as calm as ever, but she looked far happier than she had when it was just the two of them.
There were chances to take her away, again and again. But believing she had to let go for Mutsumi's happiness, Sakiko turns her back on the stage and flees into the dark of night.

Then 'Mutsumi' appears before her. This is a dream made by the shadows that live inside Mutsumi — by 'us,' she says. If Sakiko stays, this dream will become reality, and they will even give her a perfect Ave Mujica.

The real Mutsumi is still asleep in that cold castle, Sakiko says, and refuses: you are not Mutsumi. From somewhere, voices saying 'kill her' echo over one another, and 'Mutsumi' drives Sakiko to the edge of a cliff.

blocks.cap: "Mutsumi doesn't need Sakiko anymore. Goodbye, Sakiko."

blocks.x: 8. The Leader, Turned Down Four Times
As she falls without end, the four answers echo. Nyamu, who said she didn't care about Sakiko or the band. Umiri, who said she didn't need anyone to save her. And Uika, who gave no answer at all.

When she wakes again in the Dream Castle, Morpheus laughs to her heart's content. How does it feel, she asks, to have your dreams shattered and be trapped in the **Dreamless Border**? Before you went in, those girls had all but forgotten you and that trivial band.
Morpheus sneers that the 'contract' called Ave Mujica was, in the end, only about not wanting everyone to leave.

Laying a hand on the cheek of Sakiko, now robbed even of her voice, Morpheus whispers that this time she'll show her a dream she'll never want to wake from, even knowing it's a dream. "Good night, my noble, cunning, selfish little doll."
Then, opening her eyes to a rattling, clattering sound, Sakiko is back in the transport with Vigna, Iris, and Bena. But this time no one knows An, and the vehicle is taking Sakiko to her family home.

blocks.cap: The same transport, the same companions. But the dream has already changed.

blocks.x: 9. Oblivion — Mother at the Piano
The 'home' she arrives at in a rural Victorian village is a pure-white house with a well-kept garden, one she has no memory of.
Sakiko knows. Her real father is probably still wandering the streets with a can of beer, and this house is a prison meant to keep her here.

And yet the hand of 'Father' — who burned the dish he'd been practicing because his daughter loves it, and who strokes her hair, saying she's gotten so thin — is nothing like the limp hand she held the day she hauled her drunken father home. Before she knew it, Sakiko was smiling from the heart.
When she asks about the piano she hears upstairs, 'Father' answers that it's Mizuho, of course. The name of her late mother, who first taught Sakiko the piano.
She knows it's fake, but her feet climb the stairs on their own.

blocks.cap: In the light pouring through the window, her mother at the piano.

blocks.x: Later, walking a country path together, her mother lays their joined palms against each other and smiles: when you were born, your hand wasn't even half the size of mine, and now it's bigger.

Sakiko's mother died when Sakiko was in her third year of middle school. Sakiko asks her if she remembers a high school entrance ceremony that never happened. Back comes the beautiful answer she wanted to hear, even if it meant deceiving herself: the three of them took a photo in front of the school gate.
Meanwhile, Iris appears in the fields with a broken-down car. Someone who comes to believe a dream is reality, she says, wakes up with a young body and an old soul, having lost everything, all alone.
Just because things didn't go well in reality doesn't mean you can run away into dreams. With someone you were never meant to meet, you have to say a proper goodbye.

Still, Sakiko stays. In the piano room, telling 'Mother' about her bandmates, she confesses she's afraid that if she goes to find them, she'll be parted from her mother again — and at last it breaks out of her. "You were the one who left me behind, Mother!"

The day she first called her 'Mom.' The promise at the piano to always be together. The funeral that came far too soon. Her father, broken by drink. Sakiko had known all along. This was not her world. She had only wished that moment would come a little later.

'Mother' confesses first. She isn't really her mother; the Sakiko inside her stopped at middle school age, so she made up the story of the entrance ceremony. She's sorry she couldn't be there when Sakiko was struggling the most.
I want you to leave this place and find your real life. Go, Sakiko. Go back to your 'world.'

blocks.cap: The tears she held back pour out, and her mother strokes her back the way she used to.

blocks.x: To the teary 'Father' and 'Mother,' who tell her to be sure to eat properly, Sakiko says she's heading out. Side by side, the two of them answer. "Off you go."
10. When the Moonlight Pours Down

By then, the four dreams are wavering too. Nyamu finds her drumsticks in a corner of her bookshelf, and Umiri, offering the old boss a breach-of-contract fee so she can go back to the music party at Francis's family, ends up facing the barrel of a gun.
Uika's boat, as she looks back at the island feeling that someone called her, is swallowed by a fierce wave, and Mutsumi stands up to the 'Mutsumis,' saying Saki doesn't change her mind that easily.

And Sakiko runs to the departing transport, shouting that there's a necklace that wards off nightmares in a small box in Iris's pocket. Iris says this is the first she's heard of it — and then her fingertips touch cold metal.
At that same moment, on the stage of the Dream Castle, the sleeping doll rises. "Morpheus, this farce ends here."
In her pocket was the necklace that had crossed through countless dreams. Sakiko says her bandmates have had every wish granted, yet they are only wandering, still not happy.
My role is to show the way to dolls who have lost theirs. I will lead every one of you out of the dream — without fail.
And you, Morpheus, are one of them too, she says. This is our dream, so the masters of this dream are ourselves — and as Sakiko raises her arm, her costume begins to change.
When the moonlight pours down, the dolls are granted a fleeting life.

blocks.cap: Fingers gliding over the keys; the dolls' strings losing their hold.

blocks.x: As the piano rings out, the strings snap in every dream. Francis, falling from the sky, tells Umiri that they are beings born of her dream — which is why they trusted her from the very start — and sends her off. Nyamu, chased by police cars, starts a livestream high above Lungmen. "Nyamuchi is also Amoris, the drummer of Ave Mujica!"

The 'Mutsumis' closing in on Mutsumi collapse like puppets with cut strings at the sound of a voice from somewhere, and Uika, sinking into the sea, sees a light at the end of her fading memories. Saki, who draws everyone in and makes them shine.

Sakiko says she's sorry for hurting them so many times, but that she still wants to meet the real them. Ave Mujica is a community bound by fate, and she will protect it with her life. In the middle of the night, under twin moons, the dolls awaken.
Epilogue. Prelude to a New Fairy Tale

blocks.cap: "...We finally meet, Saki."

blocks.x: As the last note fades, Uika says they had passed each other in the same place again and again. Umiri, Nyamu, and Mutsumi are all there too, and Sakiko finally manages to speak. "Everyone... welcome back."

Morpheus tries to the very end to hold them with her net of dreams, and even Wolff, who stands in the way, is pierced by strings — and at that moment, a giant pair of scissors falls from the sky, tears the net apart, and the real Iris appears. Relieved, Sakiko collapses right onto the keys.

When Sakiko wakes a while later, Iris introduces herself for the first time. Sakiko was probably able to meet the Iris in her dreams thanks to the castle's previous mistress, Iris's grandmother, who is now convalescing.

Sakiko holds no grudge against Morpheus. Only by being turned down one by one did she realize she hadn't understood her bandmates' hearts. And Morpheus, who knows better than anyone that dreams are lies, must have had a reason for losing herself in them anyway.

Long ago, there was a young Morpheus who clung to Iris, begging her to say it wasn't true when others mocked her as a 'heartless monster.' For some reason, she can only live inside the castle, and after far too much pain, she could no longer believe in fairy tales.

Sakiko passes on the story of the seed she heard from the Iris in her dream. Perhaps Morpheus, too, is waiting for a real dream — one that will help her 'grow up.' The moon, she says, has already risen.

Still, they don't yet know how to return to their own world, so they plan to ask the Doctor of Rhodes Island for help. Once they go back, Iris says, their memories of this place will fade like a dream — but the courage to face hardship will never be forgotten.

Outside, meanwhile, Morpheus and the Corettons are building a new stage under Bena's direction. Beside the bandmates, who say they've had enough of dreams for a while, the grumbling Morpheus allows that she could listen to one song, at least.
Sakiko takes the hand her bandmate holds out and steps onto the stage. "Everyone, let's leave our sound upon this land!"

blocks.cap: In the heart of the Dream Castle, the five dolls' stage opens once more.

blocks.x: When the moonlight pours down, the dolls are granted a fleeting life. Carrying love, fear, sorrow, death, and oblivion, the five dolls have passed through a night that was 'just like a dream,' and now they sing, wide awake. Welcome to the world of Ave Mujica.

act44side.tagline: A police officer returns home after twenty years, is hunted as the killer from a local ghost story, and in the end cuts her ties with that home and leaves. The funeral a forged letter called for was held after all.

chars.name: Hoshiguma
chars.desc: An Oni woman returning to her hometown of Mitsukue after twenty years. An inspector with the Lungmen Guard Department.

chars.name: Momoka
chars.desc: An idol and actress famous for having ghost stories follow her around. She shot her debut film in Kajimachi. · Operator Haruka

chars.name: Tessai
chars.desc: Chairman of the Kinsekikai and Hoshiguma's adoptive father. Also a weaponsmith.

chars.name: Mifune
chars.desc: The real power in the Kinsekikai, in control of the Kinseki Group and its TV station. Before his rise he went by Kinbee.

chars.name: Mio
chars.desc: Mifune's taciturn secretary, assigned as Momoka's bodyguard.

chars.name: Moriuchi
chars.desc: Owner of an oden stall on Nita Street. Well versed in urban legends.

chars.name: Kichisei
chars.desc: A girl who minds a shop and a pachinko parlor in Kajimachi. A devoted Momoka fan.

chars.name: Tetsuya
chars.desc: Tessai's son, who always wears a mask. He hunts Northern Court spies under Mifune.

chars.name: Detective Koretou
chars.desc: The Mitsukue police detective who arrested and interrogated Hoshiguma.

chars.name: Fumizuki
chars.desc: Wife of Lungmen's Wei Yenwu. Like Hoshiguma, she comes from Higashi.

chars.name: Nosy Kami
chars.desc: A kami who rides a unicycle around Mitsukue, chasing its ghost stories.

chars.name: Sarasa
chars.desc: A hacker working undercover as a Kinseki Channel employee. She calls herself a 'cyber ninja.'

terms.name: Mitsukue
terms.desc: A major city of the Southern Court in Higashi. Hoshiguma's hometown.

terms.name: Nita Street
terms.desc: Mitsukue's entertainment district. Its main road leads to Kajimachi.

terms.name: Kajimachi
terms.desc: The old district where the Kinsekikai's people lived together. Caught up in a redevelopment plan, it is about to disappear.

terms.name: Kinsekikai
terms.desc: An old Mitsukue yakuza clan based in Kajimachi. Its chairman is Tessai.

terms.name: Hannya
terms.desc: A large triangular shield made by Tessai. Hoshiguma has carried it for twenty years.

terms.name: Ao-Oni
terms.desc: Hoshiguma's nickname twenty years ago. Today it circulates as the name of the killer in an urban legend.

terms.name: Wanyuudou
terms.desc: A Mitsukue ghost story about something invisible riding around on a unicycle. Often mentioned alongside the Ao-Oni tale.

terms.name: Kinseki Channel
terms.desc: Mitsukue's largest TV station, owned by Mifune. It airs the ghost-story programs Momoka appears on.

terms.name: Northern Court
terms.desc: The northern state of Higashi. It has long been at odds with the Southern Court to its south.

blocks.x: **Mitsukue**, a major city of the Southern Court in Higashi. For **Hoshiguma**, an inspector with the Lungmen Guard Department, it was the hometown she had not gone back to once in twenty years.

In late summer, a letter reached her under the name of her adoptive father, **Tessai**. **Kajimachi**, the neighborhood where she grew up, would soon vanish from the world, it said, and he meant to see it off with a funeral, however modest.
In the years since she left, a ghost story had grown up in Mitsukue with her at its center.
1. The One-Horned Oni on Stage

On Nita Street, Mitsukue's entertainment district, **Momoka**, an idol famous for having ghost stories follow her, was holding a concert. On stage she introduced the kaidan her debut film was based on: 'The Nameless Oni.'

In it, a one-horned oni mad with vengeance all but wipes out a yakuza clan and kills the Diet candidate she hates, then takes her own life and haunts the streets as a vengeful spirit. Listening from the audience, a one-horned Oni woman—Hoshiguma—reflected on how badly the story had been garbled.

Pursued by the police, she cut across the darkened stage and knocked down a man in her way, and at that exact moment the lights came on. Momoka saw the one-horned oni, screamed, and sank to the floor. The venue fell into chaos.
That night Hoshiguma was arrested without resistance at an oden stall in a back alley. Momoka, who had taken shelter there, watched blankly as 'Ghost-san' was taken away by the police.

blocks.cap: Fried meatchop and rice from home. Hoshiguma emptied the bowl without a word.

blocks.x: In the interrogation room before dawn, **Detective Koretou** called her 'the suspect from twenty years ago.' Hoshiguma answered that the statute of limitations had run out, and handed over the letter she had kept hidden. It was the letter that had led **Fumizuki**, wife of Lungmen's Wei Yenwu, to send her off, insisting that with a funeral to attend, she had to go home.

At daybreak, **Mifune**, a hulking Phidia, stormed into the station, browbeat the police, and walked out with her. He now owned Mitsukue's largest TV station, but Hoshiguma called him by the name he had gone by before his rise: Kinbee.
2. Home Greets Her With a Severed Finger

On the walk to Kajimachi, Mifune talked. Twenty years ago she had killed the Diet candidate and left carrying that burden alone, and that was why the Kinsekikai had survived. The seat at the chairman's left, he said, was still kept empty for her.

At the edge of the old neighborhood, Tessai came out to meet them. Then one of Mifune's men arrived and remarked that the old man did not have long to live. For breaking the chairman's prohibition, Mifune cut the man's throat on the spot, then cut off the little finger of his own left hand.
No one spoke.

Later, at his residence, Tessai said he had never sent any letter; Kinbee must have forged it. The Originium crystal business the old man had built, and the ventures that had grown into a TV station and a talent agency, had all passed into Mifune's hands. All that remained was Kajimachi, caught in a 'development plan.'

blocks.cap: Tessai's residence. The old man had become a toothless tiger.

blocks.x: The finger might be an act as well, the old man said, and either way it was nothing but an insult. He told her to go back to Lungmen at once. Hoshiguma shook her head.
Everything I regret... is from my time in Mitsukue.
The old man looked at the sheared-off corner of her shield, Hannya, and from the cut alone recognized the mark of Ch'en's sword, Chi Xiao. He took the shield in for repair.

Hoshiguma said she would first hold a memorial rite for her father. Her home, which had also been the clinic of her doctor father, had become a place of ill omen that people called the 'Haunted House,' and everyone who moved in after she left had come to a bad end.
3. The Stick From the Haunted House
That same day, Momoka was reprimanded at her agency. Her promise on stage to help Kajimachi had offended the agency's financial backer, the Kinseki Group, which was at odds with Kajimachi.

To make amends, she was handed a segment called 'Exploring the Haunted House of Kajimachi.' **Mio**, the secretary who had promised to come along, never showed up, claiming a cold, and Momoka went into the house alone with a camera strapped to her head.

blocks.cap: The darkened haunted house. The whole visit rested on a single flashlight.

blocks.x: The one she ran into there was Hoshiguma, who had come to clean the place. Momoka picked up a stick lying on the floor, tucked it into her clothes, and tried to flee, but the rotten floor gave way and she fell to the level below.

The footage soon swept Mitsukue's airwaves. Every channel branded Kajimachi the den of the 'returned vicious Oni.' Believing it was her fault, Momoka posted that Kajimachi was not a frightening place, and the head of her agency soon called her, swearing.

Meanwhile, in front of the haunted house, Hoshiguma came face to face with a masked young man, **Tetsuya**. He was the son of Tessai's second marriage, given the same name as the son Tessai had lost long ago. Hating his father, he worked under Mifune, hunting 'Northern Court spies.'

When she subdued him and his wooden sword with her bare hands, **Kichisei**, who had come to break up the fight, explained the situation. While Mifune's men drove residents out in the name of redevelopment, Kajimachi had survived only because Tessai held on to the land deeds.
4. "I'll Help You," Three Times

That night Hoshiguma woke to the sound of a bell. A small unicycle stood alone in the yard she had cleared, a helmet floating in the air above it. When she approached, the unicycle pedaled away. Thinking of the kaidan of the 'Wanyuudou,' she gave chase.

At the same hour, Momoka, unable to sleep, saw her TV go haywire, and Mifune and Mio appeared on the screen. Mifune said 'that girl' was out of control and should be quietly disposed of as before, or infected with Oripathy and forced to retire—all because she had happened to pick up 'that broken blade.'

The stick Momoka had carried out of the haunted house really was a broken blade. Soon after, Mio, who always knocked three times, came in without knocking and said only that Momoka should come with her for now.

blocks.cap: "...I'll help you, Momoka." The same expressionless words, repeated three times.

blocks.x: In an instant the familiar face became terrifying. Momoka opened the window and jumped from the second floor.

Meanwhile, having lost the unicycle, Hoshiguma arrived at the oden stall from the night before. Its owner, **Moriuchi**, said he was searching for a 'kami' resembling a maneki-neko that had helped him as a child and then vanished, and asked her to visit the shrine for him.
Then Momoka burst in, dragging a broken-down electric scooter. When Kinsekikai men came after her, Hoshiguma fixed the scooter, put her at the handlebars, and climbed on behind.

blocks.cap: Momoka steers through her tears. Behind her, Hoshiguma holds off the pursuit with her shield.

blocks.x: By then Mifune was on every TV in the streets, announcing that Momoka had gone missing and that 'the Ao-Oni of Kinsekikai' from the kaidan was involved.
5. The Kami Who Never Showed Itself

After riding through the night, the two reached the 'Shrine of Bonds' at dawn. On the grounds the unicycle appeared again and came after Momoka. Trembling at the kaidan that anyone who sees the Wanyuudou meets disaster, she threw herself forward instead of backing away.

blocks.cap: Only after they both fell into the pond did the Wanyuudou finally reveal itself.

blocks.x: What emerged, dripping wet, was the **Nosy Kami** in a unicycle helmet. Someone had been cleaning the haunted house and even sleeping there, it said, so it had simply gone to take a look.
