terms.desc: The red dragons' nest and the capital of independent Tara. It lies in the heart of the Dark Woods.

terms.name: Black Mist
terms.desc: The mist that hangs thick over the Dark Woods surrounding Na Saoirsí. It is said that those who enter without permission never come out.

terms.name: Flames of Death
terms.desc: A purple fire wielded by some red dragons. It makes the dead move, and when it spreads to the living, it slowly eats away at their lives.

terms.name: Samhain
terms.desc: Tara's festival marking the end of the autumn harvest and the coming of winter. It is said to be the day the worlds of the living and the dead connect.

terms.name: Fire-Returning Ceremony
terms.desc: Tara's traditional funeral rite of returning fire to the deceased. The Wakemen preside over it.

terms.name: Dublinn
terms.desc: The Taran independence faction led by Eblana. In Na Saoirsí, officers who fought the war together govern the city. It is also the sisters' family name.

terms.name: Wakemen
terms.desc: People who live in seclusion near ruins and preside over funerals. They do not involve themselves in the disputes of the living.

terms.name: Bealtaine
terms.desc: An old Taran festival held on the last day of spring, when every household puts out its fire and everyone gathers in one place to kindle it anew.

blocks.x: Tara, a nation newly freed from Victoria's long rule. In a shabby tavern in a remote village, a writer was drinking stale beer. Not one story in the collection he had published had an ending, and he threw his readers' letters into the stove unread.

A pale woman with her hood pulled low sat down across from him. Instead of pressing him for an ending, she offered him material for a story, and the writer assumed that she, too, had made it out of 'that city' alive last autumn.
So the two took turns telling the story. Of what happened in Na Saoirsí, the red dragons' nest, in the days before the Samhain festival.
1. A Specter Awakened After 600 Years

The woman's material began in the ruins of Tara's old capital, brought down by a Catastrophe. A red dragon lit a purple fire in a long-cold furnace and woke the specter of **Labhréathach**, a red dragon killed by his own blood 600 years ago. He was called 'the Exiled King.'

blocks.cap: The ruins of Tara's old capital. Purple fire rises in the long-cold furnace.

blocks.x: The red dragon said she had set fire to all of Tara to end Victoria's tyranny. Then she asked what it would take to withdraw the Flames of Death, the fire that made the dead walk and the living waste away.
The specter answered that those already tainted had been forsaken by life. Gather them in one place, he said, and then find another red dragon whose flames could warm life.

On her way back, the red dragon met an old man in a hut in the wilds. His son had come home wreathed in purple flame, he said, and even after being buried he would not stay in the ground, but wandered the wasteland.

When the son staggered toward her, the red dragon pinned him with the tip of her spear and turned him to ash. But when the old man closed his eyes and walked toward the spear, she stayed her hand. The specter seemed to be right, she said: life no longer tends to those tainted by the Flames of Death.
The writer drained another half glass of beer and began his own story.
2. A Feast in Name Only

The Black Mist hangs thick over the Dark Woods that surround Na Saoirsí. On the day the woods opened a path, **Loughshinny**, the younger of Tara's two red dragons, led a band of wanderers with nowhere else to go through the forest. She was hiding her identity under the name 'Reed.'

blocks.cap: The moment the Dark Woods opened their gate: the sight that spread before the wanderers.

blocks.x: On the forest path, **Moran**, who had once dreamed of becoming a bard, sang an old song of the Dark Woods.

I stepped into the dark woods one morn, calling to the mists of hoar. I trod upon the road, heading out to war. No pipes a-singing, nor battle drums a-roar. Only the bells behind me, through dew and fog their rings do soar.

Waiting to meet them was a close aide of her sister **Eblana**, who leads Tara: '**The Brigadier**.' When he said the wanderers could not be let into the city, **Nemos**, a Wakewoman who had left her people, took them to the Wakemen's settlement.

Then Loughshinny entered the city alone. **Culann**, the blacksmith they called a hero, was building a red dragon statue in time for Samhain, and residents crowded around him, offering their tableware, their axes, even their iron prosthetic legs as material.

Meanwhile, Culann's young apprentice **Theo** was shoved into a puddle simply for being Victorian. **Brigid**, a nomad, asked him to leave with her, but Theo stayed, saying he couldn't leave Culann alone.

That day, the residents threw a feast for 'Reed,' their countrywoman come home. Meat stew, grilled fins, oatmeal. The names were all different, but every dish was made of potatoes, and no one found that strange.
The statue was being made of tableware, the bonfire of the sun, the feast of potatoes.
3. The Flame Called a Blessing
That day, Loughshinny met her sister at the citadel. She had not come to take power, she said, but to watch. Yet the road her sister had walked had always been covered in corpses and blood.

Instead of answering, Eblana took her sister to the top of the citadel, and there Loughshinny saw what had stood between her and the residents. In the body of every person on the streets, purple Flames of Death were burning.

blocks.cap: Na Saoirsí seen from atop the citadel. Purple flames bloom all across the city.

blocks.x: Flames spread, Eblana said, and those people would gradually turn into something like zombies and soon vanish along with her. Then she offered a solution.
Kill me, Loughshinny.

If her sister's spear pierced her heart, everything tainted by the flames would vanish with her, and Loughshinny would become Tara's one and only Leader. Loughshinny refused. She would never again be her sister's shadow.
Later, when Loughshinny drew the purple out of one resident's hand, the resident screamed that the hand had lost all feeling. The people believed the flame was 'the Red Dragon's blessing.'

And at dusk, a shape like a mass of purple flame appeared before Loughshinny. The Exiled King told her that she and her sister shared his nature, a craving for power, struggle, and killing. Then he scattered on the wind.
4. Those Who Chased Treasure into the Woods

A few days later, food vanished from the city's shops. In truth, a **Dublinn** officer, 'The Bureaucrat,' had made the grain shop owner **Emma** smuggle it away, but when a rumor spread that Victorian spies had set fire to the farmland, the residents turned on one another and took up knives.
In the commotion, Theo, who had left home that morning, did not come back, and Nemos, Loughshinny, and Brigid searched the city for him.

At the same hour, Dublinn held a banquet at the citadel. Officers who had been heroes on the battlefield cornered Nemos, who had come with nothing but a flute instead of the sacred instruments, while in a corner people whispered about pinning the failed harvest on Victoria.
When Eblana finally appeared and told each of them to seize the treasure they wanted most, the treasures in the hall seemed to come alive and fled out the door, and the officers stampeded after them.

blocks.cap: A path glittering with treasure, born at the end of a dead-end alley.

blocks.x: Busy gathering treasure, no one looked at where the path led, and they ran straight into the gaping Dark Woods.

That night, The Brigadier and Nemos, whom Loughshinny ran into, wore dazed faces and kept repeating the same words: nothing happened tonight. After hearing about Emma and 'The Bureaucrat,' The Brigadier walked alone deep into the Dark Woods.
When day broke, the stolen food was back on the farmland as if by a miracle. But neither The Brigadier nor the officers from the banquet returned, and even speaking the word 'Dublinn' was forbidden.
5. The Hero Dragged the Statue to the Square

The morning Theo left home, he was hit by a burdenbeast cart. The resident who had meant to hand him over to Dublinn in exchange for potatoes heard there were potatoes left somewhere else, dumped him in an alley, and ran off.

The person the fallen Theo begged for help was Emma. Having starved under Victoria's blockade until she lost even the child in her womb, Emma ignored his plea to call Culann, and Theo died before her eyes.
And when Culann heard the news, the giant dragon, nearly finished, spoke to him in the empty workshop. What makes the likes of you a hero?

Culann realized he had fed this monster his people's tableware and fuel, and in the end Theo's life as well, to make it grow. He bound the statue in iron chains, meaning to drag it to the square, smash it, and give the people back their lives.
At dusk, in the square where people were making one another hold their hands to the fire to root out spies, the sound of something being dragged drew closer through the mist.

blocks.cap: The red dragon statue emerges from the mist. The chains were wrapped around the hero's shoulders.

blocks.x: Culann set the statue he had hauled on his bleeding shoulders down in the middle of the square and said the war was over. He asked what they wanted to do after Samhain. As for him, rather than carve names into a statue, he wanted to learn how to repair prosthetic legs.
No one needs to love their enemy. All I want is for you to love the living... to love yourselves.

When Culann aimed his hammer at the statue's head, an angry crowd surrounded him, and he confessed what he had kept hidden. The Victorian scouts he was said to have slain had been a caravan trampled by some army. He had saved just one child, then cut off the dead's heads and passed them off as scouts.

Amid cries of 'You're not Culann!', Culann, blood pouring from his mouth and nose, saw Theo's corpse in a corner of the square, wreathed in purple flame and watching him. With the last of his strength, he struck the dragon's head.
A sound like a death knell rang out, and the hero fell.

Soon purple flames swallowed the statue and Culann. When Culann rose within the fire, the statue too spread its wings and flew up onto its empty pedestal. Eblana came down from the citadel, said she was a step too late, and told everyone to go home. It was curfew.
6. The Dance She Always Avoided

When they were young, Eblana once handed her sister a book and asked her to dance. This was a sister who had never once danced, even when the family swayed to music, and Loughshinny let the book fall into the muddy water and shook off that cold hand.

And on the night the hero fell, in the empty square, Eblana asked again: did she think those people were still alive? Loughshinny answered that she believed the flames were a plague her sister had spread, that she would find a cure, and that she wanted it to heal her sister's wounds too.
Eblana said she was glad. Her sister was not planning how to run from her, but how to save her.

blocks.cap: "Come, dance with me, Loughshinny. The same dance I've always invited you to, the one you always ran from."

blocks.x: Told to pierce her heart with the spear before the final bar ended, Loughshinny said she would dance until one of them fell, but not the way her sister wanted. Then Eblana said that she was the one who could not wait.
Only then did Loughshinny see it. Beneath the cloak of purple flame, a sickly pallor was seeping out of her sister's skin.
Asked if she was all right, Eblana answered that she too had wanted to dance with her. Loughshinny said they would dance together once she found a way to cure her.

That night, Loughshinny laid Culann, whom she had failed to save, in a small box. And as Nemos stroked that box, the purple flame caught at last on her too, the last person in the city it had not touched.

The people she had relied on were a greedy pack, the Leader she had revered was an evil dragon, and her dearest friend had died for them. There was nothing left but revenge, Nemos said, and she swore to help Loughshinny's dance until the evil red dragon fell.
Nemos asked her to hold Culann's funeral, handed her the eulogy she had written, and stayed behind in the city with Brigid.
7. A Funeral That Returns the Fire

In the Dark Woods, where she had gone to seek help, the Black Mist did not attack Loughshinny. Its presence felt less like rejection than disappointment. When she lost her way, the Exiled King appeared again and led her out of the woods, and when they met Moran and the others coming to find her, he vanished like morning dew.

At the settlement, the Wakemen tried to send Loughshinny away, saying they did not take part in fights between red dragons, but when she said she had come to ask for a funeral, they opened their doors. The first person from Na Saoirsí to be given a funeral since independence had not even died in the war.

And so the Fire-Returning Ceremony began at the Wakemen's settlement. The old song of the Dark Woods they sang low reached Eblana in the citadel, Emma on her sickbed, and 'The Singer' of Dublinn, who had escaped the woods and reached the ruins of the old capital.

The eulogy Loughshinny read in Nemos's place was a letter to Culann. Culann had asked her to make him a hero, because once the war ended and there was no one left to blame, people would fall apart. She had accepted, it said, and now it was her turn to carry that burden.
Farewell, Culann. May you and I... meet again in the warm flames.

blocks.cap: Fire rises over the wooden coffin, and the people return their candles to the deceased.

blocks.x: Laying her candle by the fire, Moran called the departed a liar and a hero. And to Loughshinny, who said she had no right to mourn, she said they should return the fire so the dead could sleep holding our memories. Because we who live must go on living.
Only after everyone had gone did Loughshinny throw her candle into the flames.
8. A Red Dragon Never Forgives

The next day, as Loughshinny headed for the city, the Exiled King appeared before her again. When she said she wanted to hold the Fire-Returning Ceremony in Na Saoirsí, he took her to the altar in the ruins of the old capital.

The flame he raised was purple too. Putting her hand into it, Loughshinny saw the fates of those sacrificed on this land. An old sorrow, she said, had flared into hatred at her sister's touch, and in the end had consumed the people themselves.

Then the Exiled King showed her his own story. Weakened, he had come to the capital on the eve of Samhain to see his younger brother **Ailill** for the first time in twenty years, and had been dragged into this corridor.

blocks.cap: A corridor of the capital 600 years ago. Na Saoirsí was built as an exact copy of it.

blocks.x: He died with a guard's sword through his chest. He kept his eyes open until his last breath, but through the gap in the balcony door he never saw his brother's flame. Only one thing became clear: a red dragon never forgives.

When he died, purple flames rose on every ranch where he had lived. A week later the druids held a Fire-Returning Ceremony for him, and only then did the fire go out, but every life the fire had touched, beast or human, had turned to ash.

Your sister did not lie, he said. As long as she lived, the fire would keep spreading, so Loughshinny should run and seek help. When Loughshinny said she would go back anyway, the specter only sighed deeply.

Meanwhile, when a second body arrived from Na Saoirsí, one of the Wakemen confided in Moran. Their ancestors were the druids who had let Labhréathach into the capital, and the Wakemen began as an exile they imposed on themselves so as never to forget it. Moran answered that Reed was not Labhréathach.
Fates are often alike, but always differ where it matters most.

With that line, the writer in the tavern fell silent. From that point on, he said, everything he had seen, believed, and said had become tangled together. Then the woman said that this time she would tell him what she had seen and heard.
9. The Ending the Woman Wrote

In the woman's story, Loughshinny met her sister again in the long corridor of the citadel. Holding up her sister, who looked ready to collapse, she said they should go to the square together and let the people return the fire, and that if her sister grew weak, she would sit beside her and read her poetry.

Eblana called it the beautiful fantasy of a sister who had not lived through the snowy night their parents died. Wake from the dream, she said, kill me, and wear this crown. Then you will become me, and I will become you.
With her eyes closed, the younger sister raised the spear. It pierced her sister's body, and as she wrapped an arm around her waist, the elder sister fell. Like the final pose of a dance.

blocks.cap: Pierced by the spear, the elder sister falls into the younger one's arms.

blocks.x: But what burst from the wound was not blood but purple flame. The flames filled the corridor, spilled over the citadel, and spread across all of Na Saoirsí.

Nemos cried that it was a scheme Eblana had staged herself to burn the whole city before Samhain, but Loughshinny answered that her sister had deceived no one. Nemos decided to put the body in a coffin and tell the residents of the red dragon's death, while Loughshinny took up her spear to hold back the Black Mist pressing in on the city.

Having heard this much, the writer leapt to his feet and asked who she was. When he asked whether she had ever seen a red dragon kill another red dragon, the woman answered that it was only 'fiction,' the same as his having seen a hero drag a statue.
Scratching at a card with a dry fountain pen, the writer felt the urge to create that he had long forgotten. This had been your story from the start as well, he said, and took up the tale again.
10. An Elegy Sung While Dragging a Coffin

Around that time, as Brigid was leaving through the city gate, an unseen voice told her that this city would soon be covered in death, and that she should survive. Brigid said she would surely come back, and made a wager: if she won, he would go back to where he belonged.
The Exiled King accepted the wager and had Brigid carry a message to the Wakemen. It was 600 years ago now. He held no grudge against them, so they should do what they had to do.

blocks.cap: An unseen ancestor stands behind Brigid. A very little of his blood runs in her veins.

blocks.x: When the sun set, Nemos dragged the burning coffin into the streets under curfew. She stopped at every house, cast the purple light into its windows, and sang the Wakemen's elegy until her voice was hoarse, but no one opened a door.

As she sang the last song left, the old song of the Dark Woods, a door opened for the first time. Emma, who was said to be dying of illness, asked whether their red dragon truly lay in the coffin, and who had killed her. Behind every tightly shut door, bloodshot eyes like Emma's were waiting for revenge.

At the same time, Loughshinny was holding her ground before the Black Mist. Whatever her sister had promised, it would now have to collect from her. Until the people opened their doors and came out, it would take no one.
And before anyone knew it, everyone in Na Saoirsí had come out into the square. Like the purple flames in the lamps at their waists, they themselves were burning.
Say it was the Black Mist. Say it was the Victorians. Unable to push that thought down, Nemos looked up at the statue, remembered Culann, and shouted to the whole city.
The Red Dragon killed herself! To keep you from burning into cinders, the Red Dragon sacrificed her own life!
Revenge was refused in the most decisive way. Emma wailed: if she could not even take revenge, how was she supposed to live? She would rather go to meet her lover, Niels.
Then a song drew near. It was Brigid, and Moran, walking hand in hand with the Wakemen. For the first time, Moran added a new verse to the old song.
Again through the dark woods, parting the mists of hoar. Not to reunite, but to light the path you trod with fog and dew.

Moran told her to return the flame and go on living. When her hair turned white as snow, the two of them would meet again. As Emma took a candle, sobbing, people poured into the streets as if a dam had burst.

The Wakemen had the coffin placed beneath the statue, and the Exiled King, standing at a distance, muttered that they could call it a draw. When Nemos set down a lantern without calling the name of the deceased, the flames spread from the coffin to the statue.

blocks.cap: The statue burns as its fire is returned, and at last the people speak of what they have lost.

blocks.x: 11. The Red Dragon Who Returned from the Abyss of Death

With the words 'This is the path you chose,' the Black Mist lifted, and Loughshinny too went to the square and returned the fire to her sister. But the fire did not go out. The sky was still purple, and a giant burning dragon was looking at her with Eblana's eyes.
The dragon gradually took on Eblana's form. When Loughshinny asked what it had all been for, her sister answered that her own arrogance had been directed at the land, and her younger sister's at her.
Biting her lip, Loughshinny drove the spear in, and her sister said she had finally learned resolve. Death mocks everyone, she said, but she would mock death.
So bless me, Loughshinny. For I am finally about to embark on a grand adventure.
And in the last moment, as her form blurred, Eblana embraced her sister warmly. Farewell forever, until death brings us together again. I hope you like my parting gift.
In that moment, a small sun rose from the bottom of the funeral flames, and the purple vortex turned yellow from below.

blocks.cap: The vortex of flame scatters, and a red dragon walks out of its center.

blocks.x: Loughshinny walked out, stepping over the coffin turned to ash. There was no body in the coffin, only the spear the Leader had used. She could forgive everything else, she told herself, but never this parting gift.
I have returned. The Red Dragon who led you against Victoria and won independence and freedom... Loughshinny Dublinn has returned from the abyss of death.

She told them to take the flames of sorrow born of forced labor and humiliation and turn them into lamps that would warm themselves and light the road ahead. Then the color of the residents' lamps changed, and hands burned by the fire began to hurt again.
On the night before Samhain, it rained.

After everyone had gone home, the Exiled King, having lost the wager, drew the purple flame from the wound in his chest and returned it to the red dragon who walked the same path he had. When Loughshinny called his name and turned around, there was no one in the square.
Epilogue: The Last Page

Back in the tavern, the writer at last finished his ending. A mother who had lost her daughter wept all night before the funeral fire and said she still had people to protect, and the daughter rose again from the flames and embraced her. A happy ending.

As he glowed with excitement, the woman told him she hadn't thought he would have the courage to come back to Na Saoirsí after running away. The writer was 'The Singer' of Dublinn, who had made it out of the Dark Woods alive. He had dedicated this story to the woman, believing her to be Loughshinny, but the face under the hood was **Eblana**'s.

blocks.cap: "Had I known... I underestimated you far too much."

blocks.x: To his cry that she had died twice, once by the spear and again by the flames, she answered that for her, death had never been an eternal sleep. She then confirmed that what he had written as 'the Black Mist' was the Duke of Wellington's army blockading Na Saoirsí, and that the Dublinn officers led into the woods had been swallowed by that Black Mist. Literally.
Then martial law was lifted across Tara. Emma raised a glass in a tavern to the countrymen who had died for Tara, and The Brigadier came to Na Saoirsí to honor those he had fought beside.

At the end of spring, Bealtaine, the long-forgotten fire festival, was revived in Oak Grove County. As Tara's last Draco descendant, Loughshinny stepped up to the lighting ceremony and said that the history of humiliation was being recalled not for revenge, but for peace.
We remember so that we might provide the living the dignity of life, and the dead the promise of reunion... Throughout the cold night, we shall retain a warm flame.

After the ceremony, Nemos reported that Eblana's body still had not been found. The coffin Nemos dragged that night had been empty. It was Loughshinny who lit it with the last flame left on her sister's spear, Loughshinny who went to Wellington, laid out the plan, and got him to hold back his troops, and Loughshinny who walked out of the shining flames.

What her sister left behind was an ending in which someone had to die, and what saved it was a miracle the two of them made themselves. Still, Loughshinny said that without the Exiled King, Brigid, and Moran, there would have been no miracle. And now, giving herself to Tara, she would calmly await a judgment that could come at any time.

Meanwhile, in the tavern, Eblana said that giving up one doomed city in exchange for a stable Tara had been no loss. Only, the survival of Na Saoirsí's people had defied everyone's expectations, and it was something only Loughshinny as she is now could have done.

Crying that this was not how the story ended, the writer slashed at the paper and lost his voice. Eblana said the perfect story he had written was hers now, and left the tavern. Farewell, last Dublinner.
And on Rhodes Island, an operator who calls herself 'Necrass' sits across from the Doctor. Life is short, she says, and death is very long. She is only a very small shadow of Tara's Leader.
The writer who had only ever written stories without endings finally wrote one. But that ending was no longer his.

act40side.tagline: Chasing the taste of the tangerine cakes her father used to send her, Blaze arrives at the case of a Grand Preceptor branded a traitor forty years ago, and at the secret of her own birth. For the names the history books left out, a bowl of longevity noodles is set before the True Lung.

chars.name: Blaze
chars.desc: An Elite Operator of Rhodes Island. Raised in Victoria, she speaks fluent Yanese.

chars.name: Lin Qingyan
chars.desc: The Judicial Review Office Deputy Minister who brought Blaze to Baizao. A practitioner of Lei Fa, she does not back away from digging up the truth. · Operator Leizi

chars.name: Xingzhu
chars.desc: A gourmet who chronicles Baizao's hidden eateries under the pen name 'The Wandering Foodie.' Learned and courteous.

chars.name: Yu
chars.desc: The young chef of Savors at Yu's, a noodle shop across from the Judicial Review Office. Unusually proud of his own cooking.

chars.name: Wang
chars.desc: The man the court hunts as 'the convict.' A strategist likened to a black stone on a Go board, he has returned to Baizao after a hundred years.

chars.name: Gu Quan
chars.desc: A low-ranking official who spent over ten years in the Ministry of Rites as a ninth-rank ceremonial officer. He died ten years ago after joining a diplomatic mission to Victoria.

chars.name: Yu Cheng
chars.desc: A retired Deputy Minister of the Judicial Review Office. Lin Qingyan's senior and something of a mentor to her, he one day confesses to setting fire to the scrollery.

chars.name: Ning Shu
chars.desc: A retired former Minister of Rites. Having led the Ministry for decades, he is widely respected, and he is preparing to return to his hometown.

chars.name: Mo Bufu
chars.desc: Head chef of Ding Feng Lou. An old man at the summit of Baizao's culinary world, he rarely takes apprentices.

chars.name: Jie Zhen
chars.desc: A Censor of the Department of Discipline and Supervision. He sits in, as a formality, on Yu Cheng's interrogation, an internal Judicial Review Office matter.

chars.name: Chen Che
chars.desc: The Minister who heads the Judicial Review Office. She worked alongside Yu Cheng for many years.

chars.name: True Lung
chars.desc: The ruler of Yan. Every Mid-Autumn, at the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies, he discusses affairs of state with his officials.

terms.name: Baizao
terms.desc: The capital of Yan, built on top of an Originium vein to suppress its catastrophes. Its name comes from 'tending the kitchens of all under Heaven,' and eating itself is the city's pride.

terms.name: Feast of a Hundred Delicacies
terms.desc: A banquet held every Mid-Autumn, where the True Lung summons his officials to discuss affairs of state. It began with the story of an old official who offered a meager soup in a famine year as a frank remonstrance, and the dishes served that day are imitated across the city.

terms.name: Judicial Review Office
terms.desc: Yan's judicial authority. Its highest official is the Minister, and several Deputy Ministers beneath the Minister hear cases.

terms.name: Ding Feng Lou
terms.desc: Counted the foremost of Baizao's Four Great Restaurants. It prepares the dishes for the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies.

terms.name: Department of Discipline and Supervision
terms.desc: The Yan court's oversight body. Its officials are called Censors.

terms.name: Grand Preceptor
terms.desc: One of Yan's Three Grand Ministers. The one who held the post over forty years ago is recorded in the history books as having plotted treason and taken her own life.

terms.name: longevity noodles
terms.desc: Noodles eaten on birthdays as a wish for long life. At the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies, they are offered to the True Lung every year.

terms.name: tangerine cakes
terms.desc: A Baizao pastry baked with finely ground tangerine peel mixed into the dough. It was created by a scholar longing for home, and so it came to mean 'longing.'

terms.name: Sui
terms.desc: A colossal being asleep in a tomb beneath Baizao. For over a thousand years, Yan has agonized over what to do with it.

terms.name: Sui Regulator
terms.desc: The Yan court agency that monitors and tracks the beings split off from Sui. Its agents are called Candleholders.

blocks.x: In the spring forty years ago, the rain would not stop in **Baizao**, the capital of Yan. The previous True Lung had died, and twenty-eight members of the household of the **Grand Preceptor**, branded a traitor who had murdered the emperor, were thrown into prison. Only one infant, not yet a year old, who should have been on the list, was nowhere to be found.

Around then, a family racing through the downpour in a carriage lost their baby. And a man with blood on his hands entrusted a swaddled bundle to a taciturn old man, saying that whether it took thirty years or forty, the day the truth came to light would surely come.

Forty years later, as Mid-Autumn approached, Rhodes Island operator **Blaze** came to Baizao. She had been told there were questions about her father's death. At the bottom of those questions lay the names the history books never wrote down.
1. Five Plates of Tofu and the Tangerine Cakes

At **Savors at Yu's**, a small noodle shop across from the Judicial Review Office, the Office's officials were trading strange cases. A fire that could not be put out had broken out at **Ding Feng Lou**, the restaurant in charge of the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies. A thief who broke into the mansion of the retired former Minister of Rites had stolen nothing, only smearing honey on the mouth of a painted immortal. And an old man in prison clothes had reportedly thrown down his rice bowl at the Office's gate and shouted, "I'm the one who set the fire in the scrollery!"

A foreign tourist listening in from the next table joined the conversation in fluent Yanese. The woman who introduced herself as 'Huang' was Blaze, and **Lin Qingyan**, the Judicial Review Office Deputy Minister who had brought her, had warned her never to bring up her father.

The five dishes Blaze ordered that day had different names but were all tofu, and she shared them with the customers beside her. But when she tasted the dessert, **tangerine cakes**, she said they didn't seem authentic. They weren't the taste she remembered.

blocks.cap: The table at Savors at Yu's. Five plates with different names, all of them tofu.

blocks.x: The young chef burst out of the kitchen. The tangerine cakes Blaze remembered were the ones her family had sent her in Victoria more than ten years ago, far sweeter than these. The chef made a bet: search all of Baizao and bring back a tangerine cake better than his.
An elegant woman who had been watching the quarrel asked to come along. She was **Xingzhu**, a gourmet who chronicled Baizao's hidden eateries.
2. A Pine Branch in the Ashes

That same day, the Judicial Review Office's courtroom held the interrogation of **Yu Cheng**, a retired Deputy Minister who had confessed to setting the scrollery on fire. Already in prison when the fire broke out, he offered statements such as having sent a wounded fowlbeast off with burning straw in its beak. When the Minister, **Chen Che**, rebuked him, he said he had burned those documents because they were nothing but lies dressed up for show.

To Lin Qingyan, who served as clerk, Yu Cheng was a senior colleague who had been all but a teacher, and she was the one who had convicted him of tampering with evidence. As she left after the interrogation, Yu Cheng whispered behind her back. "It's almost time. ...Do not forget."

At the burned scrollery, where Lin Qingyan went straight afterward, Chen Che said the time and point of origin of the fire matched Yu Cheng's confession exactly. Most of what had burned were old cases Yu Cheng had handled. Just before retiring, Yu Cheng had tied two cases—the street murder of the Minister of Justice forty years ago, and the drowning ten years ago of **Gu Quan**, a member of a diplomatic mission bound for Victoria—to the Minister of Rites at the time, **Ning Shu**.

blocks.cap: The Judicial Review Office's scrollery, reduced to ash. Paper and ink left only faint traces.

blocks.x: Chen Che warned her to drop it, but Lin Qingyan found a green pine branch in the ashes. Long ago, Yu Cheng had shown her a pine he planted himself before being posted to Baizao, and asked her to make his coffin from it when he died. That day he had put a question to her.
Will you be able to handle the truth?

That night, Lin Qingyan asked Blaze to trust her a little longer. Blaze's father had worked for over ten years as a ninth-rank ceremonial officer in the Ministry of Rites before he died, and there was something suspicious about his death. The tangerine cakes at Savors at Yu's were the snack that father used to send to Victoria.
3. A Pastry Called Longing
Meanwhile, at the Ning manor, Ning Shu was preparing to return to his hometown. He was an old man who had led the Ministry of Rites for decades and was respected inside the court and out.

blocks.cap: The courtyard of the Ning manor. An old persimmon tree reaches its branches over the wall.

blocks.x: Visiting him, Lin Qingyan noticed a bare wall where a painting had been taken down, and then asked about Gu Quan. Two months before departure, the ninth-rank ceremonial officer had suddenly been made the mission's envoy of ceremonial rites, and the transfer order bore the signature of the Minister of Rites at the time, Ning Shu.

Ning Shu was calm. He said Gu Quan, ill and with little time left, had personally asked to spend his remaining days in Victoria, and that he had granted it out of fondness, having once entrusted the household children's calligraphy to him. He added that Gu Quan had no family, so all that remained was a cenotaph.

Meanwhile, Blaze spent a day with Xingzhu visiting five dessert shops but could not find the taste. Tangerine cakes had been created long ago by a scholar who came to the capital and missed the tangerines of his hometown, which is why they came to mean 'longing.' The authentic version, she learned, uses little sugar so the tangerine fragrance comes through.

For the first time, Blaze confided in Xingzhu. Her father was Yanese. After he returned to Yan for work, she did not see him for over ten years, and he died in a foreign land. Most of the places in her father's oil-stained letters were gone.
Xingzhu told her that Baizao had been built on top of an Originium vein to suppress its catastrophes. Asked what had become of the people who built the city, she had no answer.
4. The Student Missing from the Academy

Lin Qingyan's next stop was Baizao Academy. Posing as a teaching assistant, she got into the student records room, but there was no trace of Gu Quan, who according to the Judicial Review Office's records was an ethnic Yanese from Victoria who settled in Yan in 1074 and enrolled at the Academy in 1076.

What was more, the Shangshu Diner in front of the Academy's main gate, which Blaze's father had praised from his student days, had closed more than thirty years ago. Gu Quan had been in Baizao before 1074.

Tracing back through the enrollment records, Lin Qingyan found a name. **Gu Sheng**, born in Langyi in 1037, one of the first students admitted after the Academy's reform, top of his class in every subject. The last line of the record read, "Gu Sheng, along with his wife and daughter, disappeared in 1062." 1062 was also the year Blaze was born.

In the meantime, Blaze was learning to make **longevity noodles** from the young chef in the kitchen of Savors at Yu's. She meant to enter the cooks' competition Ding Feng Lou holds ahead of the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies, so she could ask its head chef, **Mo Bufu**, about the tangerine cakes.

blocks.cap: The young chef's longevity noodles. Ordinary ingredients, but the aroma was anything but ordinary.

blocks.x: In Blaze's hands, with her high body temperature, the dough kept drying out. After her twentieth failure, she talked about the night her Rhodes Island colleagues first celebrated her birthday in the canteen at midnight. The instant noodles she ate that night had been her 'longevity noodles.'

Xingzhu had never eaten longevity noodles. She had never seen her parents, and the lavish birthday banquets held at her home had only frightened her. That night, eating the longevity noodles Blaze made by boiling dried noodles, Xingzhu quietly wiped away tears.
5. The Three Trials of Ding Feng Lou

On the day of the competition, the first trial was to identify the ingredients in a cup of tea. Blaze named jasmine, chrysanthemum, green plum, and even Xiaohan wine. She owed it to what Xingzhu had told her about the plum grove that had appeared at some point on the mountain north of the city, as if in memory of the laborers who built it, and the wine steeped from its plums.

blocks.cap: The competition hall at Ding Feng Lou. The first trial was a single cup of tea.

blocks.x: In the second trial, the wooden placard Blaze drew read 'Medley of Whites.' It was the dish with which the Grand Preceptor, over fifty years ago, presented the True Lung with radishes that had spoiled on a long journey, stewed for hours, and urged that every student be given the chance to learn regardless of birth. When Blaze finished telling the story she had heard from her father, once a poor student himself, the audience fell silent.

In the final trial, Mo Bufu tasted the broth of Blaze's longevity noodles, recognized the hand of the owner of Savors at Yu's, and grew angry. Even after hearing her out, he would only say that putting sugar in tangerine cakes was a way of hiding clumsy technique.

At that moment the chandelier on the ceiling burst into flames. Blaze cut her palm and called up a blast of wind to put out the fire, and Lin Qingyan, who had followed her there, knocked the falling chandelier aside with lightning. The masked figure Lin Qingyan cornered vanished, leaving behind only a question: had they failed to see the truth, or were they looking away out of fear?

Owing them his life, Mo Bufu began to talk. Before he changed his name, he had been the cook who made last meals in the Ministry of Justice's death-row prison, and he remembered Gu Quan, the only condemned prisoner to walk out of there alive.

One year, at the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies, Gu Quan had offered 'Medley of Whites' together with a white steamed bun filled with red pickled tofu, and the True Lung was enraged by its meaning, a plea to clear a traitor's name. Two people visited him in prison. Yu Cheng, the Judicial Review Office Deputy Minister who brought him food, and Ning Shu, the Minister of Rites who took him out.

Only then did Blaze hear that forty years ago the Grand Preceptor had plotted to assassinate the previous True Lung and taken her own life, and that thousands had been implicated. When Lin Qingyan said that was what the history books recorded, Blaze shouted back. Just because something is written in the history books doesn't make it true.
6. Case Closed

Chen Che stormed onto the scene and took the two of them back to the Judicial Review Office, where she told Lin Qingyan that for some things, being forgotten forever is the best possible ending. Then she produced the record of a child declared dead on paper forty years ago and asked whether the woman Lin Qingyan had brought was really born in Victoria.

Only one person in all of Yan could answer for this case, she warned, and if Lin Qingyan kept digging, she could no longer protect either her or Blaze. When Blaze was released, Lin Qingyan read her the Office's closing document. Gu Quan had fallen into a river in a blizzard and died. There was nothing suspicious about it.

Around then, a letter from the True Lung reached Wei Yenwu in Lungmen, inviting him to view the moon together at the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies. Wei Yenwu, who calls the True Lung his younger brother, said it had been a full forty years since he left Baizao, and that he would go to settle old debts.

That same night, Mo Bufu came to Savors at Yu's and asked for longevity noodles made by the owner. The young chef had disappeared at some point, and the old man spoke of a winter thirty years ago. Refugees who had lost their homes to a catastrophe were about to clash with another group over food when, in front of a nearby temple, someone was boiling noodles.

blocks.cap: In front of a temple on the snowy wasteland, thirty years ago. People who had been about to fight quietly formed a line.

blocks.x: It was not a taste a human could make. Mo Bufu, who had spent thirty years searching for those noodles, found that taste again in Blaze's clumsy noodles, and he left behind her letter of acceptance.
That day, Xingzhu left Blaze a letter inviting her to her home. The address was the Ning manor.
7. The Manor's Transcriber

The next day, when Blaze visited the Ning manor, Xingzhu revealed her real name. **Ning Yin**. Adopted by Ning Shu as a child, she had grown up being introduced as a distant relative and had never once met her own blood kin.

blocks.cap: The pond at the Ning manor. The two walk past empty rooms where everything has been packed.

blocks.x: Ning Yin remembered her fifteenth birthday. Slipping away from the lavish banquet, she had come across a man in the blue robes of a low-ranking official in her grandfather's study. It was Gu Quan, the transcriber who copied the manor's letters. He knew her name and her birthday, and he gave her two copybooks he had copied by hand as a present.
When Ning Yin said that, unlike the rest of her family, she was ordinary, Gu Quan borrowed his teacher's words. Floods and tides are recorded, but without the streams there would be no waves.
The vast majority will never get to leave their names in the history annals, but they're not the empty space between the lines. They're the pages themselves.

A few years later, Ning Yin picked up a strong painkiller that a coughing Gu Quan had dropped, and that winter Gu Quan died on the way to Victoria. Ning Yin had kept the medicine bottle ever since. She did not ask Blaze to believe in her grandfather's innocence. She asked her to bring the truth to light, whatever it was.

Meanwhile, the **Department of Discipline and Supervision**'s Censor **Jie Zhen** came to see Lin Qingyan, who had shut herself in her office at the Judicial Review Office. He saw that she had stopped for fear that others would get hurt, and told her that if a thing could not be hidden, she might as well drag it out into the world. That day, only her official robes and a letter of resignation were left on her desk.

At the same hour, Ning Yin told her grandfather she would not go back to their hometown with him. Writing a history and chasing a person erased without a name, she had learned that history books are not vessels but sieves, and that she could not write a single certain line even about the grandfather she had lived with for decades. She waited a long time for his answer.

That night, Blaze and Lin Qingyan met again and decided to get into the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies and ask the True Lung directly. Meanwhile, a plan for war against **Sui** had been submitted to the palace, and the Grand Commandant said the True Lung had already made up his mind. All that remained was to announce it at the Feast.
8. Fire Under the Full Moon

Ten years earlier, when Gu Quan was released from death row, Yu Cheng had told him: who would believe you when you say your wife and daughter in Victoria are dead? Lend me your life, and I will uncover the truth you want.

On Mid-Autumn night, Blaze stood in the kitchen of the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies as a cook. Lin Qingyan asked what she would do if the truth turned out to be nothing like what they expected, and everything around her had been a lie. Blaze answered that if it was a lie, they would expose it.

It was Ning Yin who got Lin Qingyan into the banquet hall with a forged invitation. Under the full moon, as the True Lung's entrance was announced, Lin Qingyan stood up. "I have something to report, Your Majesty!"
At that moment, flames like beasts swept through the banquet hall.

blocks.cap: The Feast of a Hundred Delicacies on Mid-Autumn night. Fire of unknown origin engulfs the banquet hall.

blocks.x: Blaze fled the search, while Ning Yin swapped clothes with her and stayed behind to find Lin Qingyan. As Blaze headed for the south gate, the Junior Drillmaster of the Imperial Guard blocked her path and said the Imperial Guard had been hunting her for over forty years.
Forty years ago, only a single child was unaccounted for in the family of a treasonous mandarin.

Lin Qingyan ran up and planted herself in front of Blaze, and with a thunderbolt sent Blaze flying far beyond the Forbidden City. Lin Qingyan was captured by the Imperial Guard. Blaze closed her eyes.
9. One Street Corner

Blaze woke up at Savors at Yu's. The young chef, who had brought her in from where she lay collapsed in the street, said that when a tangerine seed blows from Jiangnan to Jiangbei, it isn't the land that grows it into a tangerine but decades of sun and rain. Then he set out a plate of tangerine cakes.
Too much sugar buried the tangerine fragrance, and too much oil kept them from being crisp. They were not good cakes. But they were, without a doubt, the taste she remembered.

Some years ago there had been a regular who bought tangerine cakes and wrapped them in layer after layer of letter paper, saying they were for his daughter abroad. Perhaps tangerine cakes that sweet had never been about flavor. That customer would come in before sunrise, order the cheapest breakfast, and sit by the window, waiting for someone.
At dawn, Blaze sat in that seat and saw it. The little restaurant and the great Ning manor were just one street corner apart.

blocks.cap: The regular at the window seat. Beyond the corner he watched lies the Ning manor.

blocks.x: Then Ning Yin opened the door and walked in. Waking in her grandfather's study the night before, she had found on the desk an unfamiliar history book holding the records of 1062.
10. Confession

That same morning, Ning Shu visited Yu Cheng in the Judicial Review Office's prison. Yu Cheng had been certain he would come. However dirty his hands had become, Ning Shu was a man who would want the two children to live with their heads held high.
Ning Shu admitted that he had had the Minister of Justice killed. The Grand Preceptor's treason had been a false charge from beginning to end.

In his final years, the previous True Lung, suffering from Oripathy, pursued lopsided policies. The prince tried to stop him, and the Grand Preceptor took the prince's side. On the night the prince entered the palace to remonstrate, the True Lung died and the prince vanished. Someone had to bear the blame, and the young new True Lung quickly brought the situation under control with a 'purge of traitors.'

Yu Cheng had pieced together the rest. On the day the Grand Preceptor's household was searched, a poor student from the Academy who had gone to pay his respects came out carrying a newborn girl of the Grand Preceptor's family. His own daughter had been born that same year.

Fleeing with his wife and the two children, he was caught by the Imperial Guard, who let him go in exchange for taking his own daughter. The one who took that child in was Ning Shu, once the Grand Preceptor's student, and Ning Shu did not deny it.

The student's name was Gu Sheng. In Victoria he raised the Grand Preceptor's child as his own daughter, then returned to Baizao under the name Gu Quan and became the transcriber at the Ning manor, where, copying the letters of high officials, he pieced the whole truth together. And from beyond the street corner, he watched over the daughter he had left behind.
Ning Shu said that seeing that child once more had fulfilled a long-held wish, and rose, saying he would now go to see His Majesty.

Earlier, before dawn, Jie Zhen had appeared before Lin Qingyan in her cell. The fires at the scrollery and Ding Feng Lou, and the painting at the Ning manor, had all been his doing, to lead her along the trail. It was also he who, after Gu Quan's death, had found Blaze, already Infected, in Victoria and placed her in the care of a medical institution. He asked whether she would reveal the truth to the world with him.

And at Savors at Yu's, Ning Yin asked what kind of man her father had been. Blaze said he was a fool. A man who spent his whole life lying to protect a child who was a complete stranger to him, and lost his own daughter and himself along the way.
Blaze's real name was **Gu Zhuhuang**. Ning Yin recited the meaning of the name, which Blaze had forgotten after going so long without hearing it.
A blazing candle to ward against the dark.

In a small town in western Victoria, the mother who raised Blaze, Ning Yin's birth mother, was still alive. Blaze said that once this was over, they would go see Mom together, and that from today on, Ning Yin was no longer alone.
11. Longevity Noodles for the True Lung

That night, the young chef left the shop in the care of Jiang, the assistant who had been with him for fifteen years. Jiang was a Candleholder of the **Sui Regulator**, which watches over Sui's proxies, and the chef was the youngest of the siblings split off from Sui, one who had long lived without remembering who he was. The young chef, **Yu**, set out to bring his brother a meal.
At the same hour, Blaze stood before the Junior Drillmaster once more. Kindling flames with the blood from her palm, she said she was on her way to offer longevity noodles to the True Lung.

blocks.cap: Before the Forbidden City once more. Blaze tells them to step aside.

blocks.x: Lin Qingyan, who had broken out of prison with Jie Zhen, held the drillmaster back, and a withdrawal signal sounded from the Forbidden City. No one stood in Blaze's way anymore.

In the great hall, the True Lung remembered forty years ago. He had sought out a legendary strategist, a black stone, and asked him to resolve the crisis for the sake of his elder brother and of Yan, promising to spare his life once in the future. With the Grand Preceptor's help, his brother entered the Forbidden City. Their father died, and his brother disappeared.

blocks.cap: The empty great hall. Blaze walks alone toward the dragon throne.

blocks.x: Blaze set the longevity noodles before the True Lung. His real birthday was the day after Mid-Autumn. The True Lung recognized her and said he had been looking for her for a long time.

Blaze asked about the teacher in her father's stories, her own family, who had given poor students the chance to learn. The True Lung answered that the Grand Preceptor had been his teacher too. Asked whether she had been falsely accused, he said no. He had sacrificed one person to steady the nation and the hearts of its people.
Blaze asked how the longevity noodles tasted. They say that a person in too much pain cannot swallow even good food. Did he regret it?

The True Lung thought of the 'price' he had come to understand only long afterward. The Grand Preceptor taking the blame, and a prince with a clean name, himself, inheriting the throne. That was the way out his brother and the Grand Preceptor had prepared in advance, and he had made the choice they wanted.

Blaze asked how a nation that held hundreds of millions of people could not make room for one good person. Yet she said her father had in the end accepted this outcome. Not as forgiveness, but only as recognition of what the True Lung and the Grand Preceptor had set out to achieve.
She wanted no compensation. No one could say whether an apology or a restoration of names would comfort the dead. Blaze asked for only one thing.
Don't forget them.
12. Snow at Mid-Autumn

That same night, in an old temple, Yu offered soup to his second brother, **Wang**, who had returned after a hundred years. In the temple, surrounded layer upon layer by the Imperial Guard, Yu said he had not come to stop his brother but to feed him.

blocks.cap: Two brothers at one table, face to face for the first time in a hundred years.

blocks.x: It was a soup he had kept simmering for the hundred years since his brother left. Yu said there is no perfect dish in the world and that every flavor comes from something lacking, and he talked about the day their scattered siblings would gather in Baizao to eat together.
Wang, my brother, I really... want you to come back alive...
Wang ate the soup and quietly set down the bowl. Then he rose, leaving behind his word that he would help them become human.

Meanwhile, the True Lung ordered that seven-tenths of all Baizao's energy be mobilized to open Sui's tomb. It came with a pardon: fulfill the thousand-year-old wish and no crime would be charged, but fail and wake Sui, and all of Yan's might would be brought down on him.

Believing that his own crime alone, framing a loyal minister, could not be pardoned, the True Lung resolved to wait for someone to judge it when the time came, and silently called to his brother. Yan Wu, it is time for you to return.
As the energy poles powered down one by one, snow fell on Baizao at Mid-Autumn.

blocks.cap: Unseasonable snow falls over Baizao as its lights dim.

blocks.x: Looking up at the snow with Lin Qingyan, Blaze said that the people who had passed, and their traces, would vanish like this snow in the end, but she hoped it would keep falling a little longer.

Under the same snow, Yu Cheng, being transferred, had the shackles put on him as the law required, then silently told Gu Quan that he had kept his promise. A snowflake fell on the draft history Ning Yin had opened and became its first stroke. Mo Bufu, back at Savors at Yu's, received a 'Greatest Under Heaven' placard laid in an empty bowl, and laughed freely for the first time in a long while.

As Wang's footsteps headed toward the tomb, the sleeping Sui roared, and Yu lit a fire that lulled the colossal being back to sleep. Wang sent back his little brother, who had wanted to come along. "What happens next is between us."

blocks.cap: Between rows of soldiers, Wang walks toward Sui's tomb.

blocks.x: Epilogue — The Pine on the Mountain

On the day he was sentenced to ten years, Yu Cheng left the Judicial Review Office. When Lin Qingyan urged him to petition for a retrial, he said the law is not a measure of morality, and that bringing the law closer to a justice everyone accepts is the work of those who come after.

Having taken off her official robes, Lin Qingyan said a single bolt of lightning could not settle all the rights and wrongs of the world, and that she would return to the Tianshi Bureau to train. Yu Cheng asked her, when the time came, to cut down that pine on the mountain and make his coffin from it.
Into the rice bowl Savors at Yu's had given him free of charge, Yu Cheng put a handful of unmelted snow from beneath a cypress, emptied it, and said, "Tasty."

Around then, Ch'en appeared before Wei Yenwu on his way to Baizao. And in the kitchen of Savors at Yu's, the young chef had a dream. In the darkness of the tomb, a small voice that had only just awakened was asking Sui what, exactly, a human was.

blocks.cap: The tomb in the dream. A small child sits before a colossal being.

blocks.x: Waking from the dream, the young chef tasted salt, soy sauce, and vinegar one by one and smiled. They tasted the same. Human or beast, it made no difference, he said, and he got up to open the shop first.

The history books left the Grand Preceptor as a single line, a traitor, and recorded neither Gu Sheng's name nor the names of the laborers who built the city. But as Gu Quan said, they were not the blanks in the history books but the pages themselves. Blaze asked the True Lung not to forget them, and the last chapter of Ning Yin's manuscript began with a single snowflake.

act39side.tagline: A wandering swordsman who insists he's no alchemist sets out to fix a pirate ship's compass, and ends up turning his own arm into one. And on a sea without water, he says out loud, for the first time, the one thing he wants.

chars.name: Isidro
chars.desc: An Ægir swordsman who came to Iberia's Salt Flat in search of a legendary sword technique. Rhodes Island affiliate · Operator Thorns

chars.name: Juana
chars.desc: Captain of the Salt Flat's pirate fleet. An Ægir who has lived for over a hundred years and dreams of returning to the sea.

chars.name: Pascuala
chars.desc: A self-proclaimed phantom thief girl on the run from the Inquisition. She drops in on the pirate fleet to do business · Operator Rose Salt

chars.name: Javier
chars.desc: The pirate fleet's chef. He was raised by Juana after losing his mother.

chars.name: Elysium
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island field operator. A friend who calls Thorns 'amigo'.

chars.name: Weedy
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island Engineering operator. She came with Elysium to look for Thorns.

chars.name: Anastasio
chars.desc: An Inquisition alguacil hunting the compass. He decorates his weapons with the bones of sinners.

chars.name: Silver
chars.desc: The calificador who leads the town of Aarón. Revered as the savior who rescued the town from disaster.

chars.name: Teach
chars.desc: A fleet veteran Juana calls her 'little perlita'. Her father was a sailor who roamed the seas alongside Juana.

chars.name: Rus
chars.desc: The fleet's boatswain. A realist who worries about how they'll make ends meet.

chars.name: Aulus
chars.desc: The alchemist who took in a young Isidro and taught him. A wanted criminal of the Inquisition.

chars.name: Nene
chars.desc: A small Saltfin Juana took in. Too frail to keep up, it fell behind its herd.

terms.name: Salt Flat
terms.desc: A land called the 'Pale Sea'. After the Profound Silence, the seawater receded and left nothing behind but white salt and bones.

terms.name: Saltfin
terms.desc: A kind of scaled beast that swims beneath the salt crust. There are dozens of species of every size, and their hides, bones, and meat are how the pirates make a living.

terms.name: Seaborn
terms.desc: Grotesque monsters that came from the sea. They ran rampant across the Salt Flat around the time the waters drained away.

terms.name: Corazonix
terms.desc: A mysterious fluid substance held inside the compass. Legend says it points toward whatever its bearer longs for most.

terms.name: Inquisition
terms.desc: The religious power that rules Iberia. It considers desire a sin and keeps it under strict control.

terms.name: Profound Silence
terms.desc: The great catastrophe that swept over Iberia. The sea swallowed the land and then pulled back, leaving behind what is now the Salt Flat.

terms.name: La Conquista
terms.desc: An old ship Juana seized on the open sea before the Profound Silence. These days it lumbers along behind the other salt ships.

terms.name: Aarón
terms.desc: A town on a mountaintop beyond the Salt Flat, governed by a calificador.

terms.name: Skeletal Reef
terms.desc: A canyon in the deepest part of the Salt Flat, where giant bones form a labyrinth. They say no one has ever come back alive, thanks to the steam that bursts from between the bones.

blocks.x: A young boy is feeling his way along the bottom of a cold lake, searching for a gold coin. His hands find nothing but waterweeds, and just as he's starting to lose hope, a gentle voice calls from the shore.
Don't look with your eyes. Let the water's flow tell you where to go.

That boy grew up to become the Ægir swordsman **Isidro**, and right now he's being held captive in a pirate fleet's tent on Iberia's Salt Flat. After spending a whole week digging a hole in the floor with stale bread, he finally breaks out — only for a giant ship's wheel to come flying out of nowhere and slam into the salt right at his feet.

The wheel belongs to **Juana**, an Ægir captain who has lived for more than a century. She wants just one thing from him — to fix her broken compass — and Isidro's answer never changes: 'I'm no alchemist!'
His reward for the escape attempt? Getting strung up upside down from the frame of a salt ship.

blocks.cap: Hanging upside down, Isidro still refuses to bend. "I won't surrender to you lot."

blocks.x: 1. The Pale Sea Has No Water

Two weeks earlier, Isidro — also known as Rhodes Island operator **Thorns** — was wandering Iberia in search of a pirate sword technique said to 'fight the wind and waves.' But when he reached the 'Pale Sea,' a place the map marked with nothing but a name, he found a sea with no water in it.

Since the Profound Silence, the place the sea drained from holds nothing but white salt and countless bones. The moment Isidro sets foot on this Salt Flat, a giant Saltfin bursts up from under the salt crust, rams him, and knocks him out cold.

blocks.cap: The 'Pale Sea,' filled with salt and bone instead of water.

blocks.x: The first to find him is a girl named **Pascuala**. Taking him for a corpse, she cheerfully strips him of his water and his money bag — 'your bad luck is my good fortune' — until her eyes light up at a gold coin engraved with a strange emblem.

Right then, **Anastasio** appears — an Inquisition alguacil whose weapons are decorated with the bones of sinners. He's the man Iberians don't even dare call by name, only whispering of him as 'the Alguacil.'

Isidro comes to and saves the girl almost on reflex, only to find his wallet has been lifted — and out of his own pocket comes stolen goods Pascuala secretly stuffed in there: a 'compass' holding Corazonix, swiped from the Inquisition.

'What relation have you with the wanted criminal Aulus?' The alguacil's rapier snaps Isidro's longsword in two, and what saves the fleeing pair is the Saltfin surging up once again. The alguacil goes flying through the air and comes down on a jagged bone.

With their sandboard wrecked, the two hitch a rope to the Saltfin's back instead and ride it to Aarón in half a day. Pascuala flashes an alguacil's badge she pinched, passes Isidro off as her 'slightly old-looking apprentice' — and then throws up from Saltfin-sickness.

Meanwhile, atop a pile of bones, a man with his body run straight through opens his eyes. 'Anastasio, you sinner. Since when was it your time to die?' Bleeding, he walks off into the depths of the Salt Flat.
2. A Salt Ship Beneath the Gallows
Back in Aarón, the townsfolk bolt their doors and windows the moment Isidro comes near — claiming they need to 'take in the laundry before it rains,' in the driest place in all of Iberia.

The only one willing to talk to him is a drunk old man humming a sea shanty. He says a man who learned that sword technique from pirates was buried along with his diary — so Isidro digs up the grave in the dead of night, gets caught by a Warrior Priest, and becomes a 'grave robber and cannibal.'

**Silver**, the calificador who leads the town, sentences him to hang. For some reason Pascuala is right there beside him — turns out she's in league with the pirate fleet and got caught tailing the calificador out of sheer habit.

Just as the sentence is about to be carried out, **Javier**, the pirate fleet's chef, comes storming in with his blade swinging. Following **Teach**, who'd been disguised as a townsperson, the group runs to the edge of a cliff and jumps right off — and Isidro leaps too, with Pascuala tucked under his arm screaming 'I'm not jumping!' What catches them is the sail of a salt ship waiting below.

Isidro, who says he can't raise his blade against the people who saved his life, is promptly knocked out by Pascuala's sleeping gas. The spoils she presents to the pirates: the compass — and an 'alchemist.'

Aarón, meanwhile, is left with nothing but wounds. The fire the pirates set burns down the granary, and an old doctor shoved aside in the chaos dies. A widow giving birth without a doctor passes away along with her baby.
That night, as Silver stands drenched in his townsfolk's blood, a man with a hole through his stomach calmly walks up to him. 'I am an alguacil, newly transferred. Might you require my assistance?'

blocks.cap: Aarón's streets at night, every window shut tight. Only a faint pink lamplight drifts by.

blocks.x: 3. I Told You, I'm No Alchemist

Back with the fleet, Juana is certain who Isidro really is. That gold coin engraved with salt and water is the token of a school of alchemy whose creed means 'look to the sea for life' — something a master gives only to their own disciple.

But for Isidro, his master **Aulus** is the stuff of nightmares. In his dreams, his master stands before the cold body of a fellow disciple and says that fusion is 'nothing more than erasing the barriers between' sea and land — and the corpse opens the eyes of some unknown creature and whispers: 'You are... the same... as me...'

Around this time, the fleet is in a tight spot. An Inquisition ambush has cut their salvage team in half, and with hands running short, Teach drags even Isidro out to work — 'around here, no work, no food.'

At the worksite, the boatswain **Rus** quietly asks him a favor: botch the alchemy on purpose so the captain will give up on the sea. He tells Isidro that the old captain, **Cruz**, and his crew all died hunting down the Seaborn while Juana alone came back alive — and even passes along the rumor that she made a deal with a sea monster.

Then the salt crust at the dig site caves in, and Cesc — one of Rus's men, assigned to keep an eye on Isidro — gets his leg pinned in a crack. Isidro starts to make a run for it, then turns back. He has Cesc bite down on a sword hilt, cuts off the leg, and keeps him alive.

At the same moment, Juana visits a cave in the desert alone. A Seaborn crawls out, dragging tentacles with blades lashed to them, and she offers it Saltfin meat, saying quietly: 'We will leave this place, this desert of salt. No matter the price.'

blocks.cap: A cave only Juana knows about. The trapped Seaborn watches her as it swallows the meat.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, **Elysium** and **Weedy** from Rhodes Island arrive in Aarón looking for the missing Thorns. Half their luggage being skincare products is one thing, but hearing that their friend stole a corpse and ran off with bandits? That's about as bad as news gets.

Outside town, pirates hanged by the alguacil sway from flagpoles, and an old man looking at the wanted poster clicks his tongue: 'In the prime of his youth...' Without waiting to hear the rest, Elysium leaves the communicator with Weedy and dashes out into the desert alone.
4. The Captain Does Not Fall

Around then, Juana confides the real reason she clings to the sea — to Javier alone. The underground rivers are drying up, the microorganisms are dwindling, and the Saltfins that feed on them are vanishing fast. **The Salt Flat is falling apart.**

So the fleet pushes its luck and goes after a giant Saltfin. The alpha-class Saltfin they thought was dead takes off with Juana clinging to the harpoon on its back, and disappears into the Skeletal Reef — a land of death no one has ever come back from.

When Javier insists he'll go alone if he has to, Isidro steps forward from the corner. 'I can help you get out of that canyon alive.' Setting off reagents to read the steam bursts before they happen, the group finds Juana sprawled atop the Saltfin's carcass — a ship's wheel lodged in its head.

blocks.cap: "Saltfin garum... What a shame. What I wouldn't do for some fine rum right about now."

blocks.x: Covered in blood, Juana coolly drains a canteen — then, of all people, asks Isidro to lend her a shoulder. Her ribs are broken. 'I can't let the crew see me weak.'

And on the way back, Silver and Anastasio lie in ambush. Juana throws herself into the fight, refusing to hand over her catch, until her wounds finally tear open and she collapses. Isidro carries her back to the ship.

That night, among the wounded, Isidro sits beside Cesc, whose liver has been pierced. When Isidro tells him he's drifted around with no home and no family, and that safe places only ever made him uneasy, Cesc gives a weak laugh.
You really are... a born pirate...
'...Maybe I was.' The meat stew cools in the night wind. In just a month, Isidro has grown used to its salty taste.
5. Cruz's Swordplay, Pelirrojito's Price

After that, Isidro has a change of heart and takes on the compass repair. Juana hands him the shipboard alchemy workshop that has sat empty for decades, and even dresses him in the old fleet alchemist's clothes.

Then she takes him to that cave. The Seaborn there has swallowed countless swordsmen who came to challenge it, and now, whenever it swings its tentacles, it mimics their techniques. The pirate swordplay Isidro was looking for is in there too.

**Because that Seaborn is the fleet's true captain, Cruz.** Having lured the last remaining Seaborn into the cave and gotten trapped there along with it, he handed the captaincy to Juana and asked her to take everyone back to the sea.
Even knowing he was a Seaborn, Juana couldn't bring herself to kill him. 'I love him, just as I love the time we spent sailing far and wide.'

Around the same time, a strange auction is held on the fleet. A young outsider hauled in from town shouts out his own price — 'Three years of saltfin garum!' — and the auctioneer fires back, 'Three days!' In the end, Pascuala buys him for three days' worth of garum and dubs him 'Pelirrojito.' Yes, it's Elysium.

When Pascuala shoves Pelirrojito into the workshop as the alchemist's assistant, the door opens and the two men throw their arms around each other, slapping each other on the back. Unable to get a word in, Pascuala quietly closes the door and leaves.

As Isidro examines the compass, golden light leaks out through the gaps in the workshop walls, and hungry sailors crowd around the windows. Over their faces, a street scene from long ago comes back to him.

blocks.cap: Young Isidro performing 'magic' in the street for a scrap of bread.

blocks.x: The boy had insisted he was only doing it to get something to eat — and the passerby who handed him a biscuit asked: 'Why do you have a smile on your face, then?'

Meanwhile, Silver dangles a pardon as bait: hand over the compass and the thief, and the pirates will be welcomed into the town. But Juana flatly says she'd rather die. After all, it was that very town — once reduced to eating its dead — that the pirates had protected from the Seaborn, and the moment the Inquisition arrived, it drove them out to the far corners of the desert.
6. Farewell, My Love
The repairs make little progress, and Teach warns Isidro never to breathe a word about what goes on in the workshop. Plenty of eyes are waiting for a single mistake that could drag the captain down.

On top of that, through Rus's scheming, the thick sinew needed for the repair is diverted to fixing the ship — and that sinew came not from a Saltfin, but from a Seaborn. Juana takes Isidro back to the cave. 'Cruz would have done the same.'

In the cave, Isidro crosses blades with the Seaborn. The rapier, greatsword, and dagger embedded in its tentacles come at him one after another, and finally a pirate's cutlass cleaves the air — with the very technique said to fight the wind and waves.
At the same time, outside the cave, Juana speaks to no one. Why wasn't it her who was devoured back then? Why did he leave this burden to her and go? 'Oh, how I've loathed you for this, Cruz.'

blocks.cap: The night sky over the Salt Flat. Juana's tears scatter on the wind before they can reach the ground.

blocks.x: Isidro comes back without dealing the final blow and hands her a blade engraved with Cruz's name. Juana goes into the cave and lays the Seaborn's head in her lap. As the light on its forehead fades, she remembers a night long ago, looking up from beneath the water — at a boy on a ragged sailing ship, holding a lantern and peering down into the sea.
'May we meet again on the boundless ocean. Farewell, my love.'
7. A Week at Swordpoint

Meanwhile, Javier and Rus stage a mutiny on the fleet. They tie up Pascuala and Elysium to hand them over to the Inquisition, but **Nene** slips away with Elysium's flag tied to its fin and races to Juana.

Searching the captain's cabin for the compass, Javier comes face to face with Juana on her return. To the woman who told him, after he lost his mother, that from now on she would be his family, he points his blade and says: you're nothing but a pitiful woman who turns her back on reality to chase the passions of days gone by.
The ocean is not our past. It's our future.
The mutinous sailors turn their blades, of all people, on Pascuala. If that thief hadn't stolen the compass, they say, the Inquisition would never have come after them.

blocks.cap: Facing a ring of blades all pointed at her, Pascuala speaks up.

blocks.x: Trembling, Pascuala shouts back anyway. Give it just one week. If the repair works, they can go to sea; if it fails, it won't be too late to hand her over then.
And she adds: Juana could have bought their lives with money, but she wanted them to live free. 'How can you call yourselves pirates when you've never even seen the sea?'
One by one, the sailors lower their weapons. Javier, who held out to the end, leaves the fleet that night with Rus, under orders not to return until their mission is complete.
8. An 87% Chance of Failure

A week later, the Arts field in the workshop collapses, and the compass parts turn into pitch-black sludge. 'I'm sorry, Juana. I failed.' Juana answers that this was her choice, and that she will bear all the responsibility.

Hearing the news, Javier goes to Silver. He'll hand over the pirates' hideouts, and even sailors to crew the salt ships — if only Juana is set free. But Anastasio pushes Silver aside and takes charge himself, declaring he'll burn the ships and their blueprints and eliminate the bandits.

That night, Juana sets Isidro and his companions free, and Isidro places the compass, perfectly intact, before her. What broke was a replica he'd secretly made. Tampering with the original without fully understanding its structure carried more than an 87% chance of failure — so he kept the original safe, leaving open the chance of finding another alchemist.
'Even if the odds of success were one in ten thousand, I would have staked everything on that one chance.' 'That's not experimentation. That's gambling.'
Tell me, is our life a gamble, or something closer to an experiment?
Unable to answer, Isidro says goodbye to Elysium and Pascuala and walks the desert alone through the night. He feels he has let a great many people down, but he cannot tell what he did wrong.
Meanwhile, guided by Javier, the Inquisition descends on the fleet. Javier seizes Juana, who had stayed behind alone, and Anastasio orders everything in sight burned.
Seeing flames rising in the distance, Isidro turns back without hesitation and runs, retracing his own footprints. Those footprints are no longer lonely.

blocks.cap: A long trail of footprints under the moonlight. Beyond the horizon, flames rise from where the fleet lies.

blocks.x: He isn't the only one who came back at the sight of the fire. So did Teach, Elysium and Pascuala, and Weedy, who had come to bring the two of them home. Together they rescue a drugged Juana and seize the old La Conquista, while Isidro, running into Anastasio in the workshop, blows up the entire workshop to shake him off.

At the edge of the canyon, the ship is caught in the steam and slides toward a giant bone — and Juana seizes the wildly spinning wheel. 'It's been so long, old friend!' The hundred-year-old ship catches the wind and slips out between the bones.
9. A Drawer of Withered Flowers
That night, La Conquista drifts with no destination. There is food for only two or three days, and everyone huddles together under a single blanket to endure the cold.

Pascuala, who always claimed the warmest spot first, mumbles in a fever. She wants to go home. She wants to live a good life without anyone kicking her around. She doesn't want to die. Teach, feverish too, has drifted back to her childhood, begging her father to take her to sea.

As the pot of simmering medicine makes a sound like small waves, Juana asks: 'Isidro, won't you come to the sea with us? You'd make a good captain.' Isidro never manages an answer, and back the way they fled, the lights of their pursuers flicker.

That same night in Aarón, Silver looks over the confiscated salt ship blueprints and dreams of building a few more ships to lead all the townsfolk out of this barren land. Of the alguacil he did not save from the explosion, he murmurs that the man never cared for this town anyway.
Then the match goes out, and in the darkness, a dead man's face appears.

blocks.cap: A face as pale as salt. Anastasio, returned alive from the explosion.

blocks.x: 'You were also corrupted by desire just like the others, no?' Silver sinks to the floor, clutching at a drawer, and petals pour out and cover him. They are flowers the townsfolk gave him as tokens of gratitude over decades — withered, rotted, and turned black.

Before those flowers, Anastasio recalls his childhood. After his father vanished, his mother went mad and forced meat down his throat; as he chewed it, weeping and begging to be killed, a cleric told him: 'You must live and atone for your sins. Perhaps one day, the purest flower will bloom at your touch.'
10. MY Compass

The next day, Javier comes into town but does not cook, not even in the kitchen Silver had fixed up. The people he always thought of while cooking are gone now. Anastasio calmly tells him that he killed Silver himself, then buys off the pirates and sends them after Juana's group.
