Dawn, who had come up beside them, burst out laughing. Others had realized before that this was the inside of a painting, she said, but it had been a long time since she'd heard anyone say it with such conviction: 'The mountains are but mountains, and the water is yet water.'

That instant, with a clap of thunder, someone furious came flying in with a sword, and Dawn called it 'a somewhat unusual send-off.' The sword split the painting, and the party landed on their behinds in an unfamiliar place that smelled of a lake, only to discover that everyone's mouths were pitch black. 'What have we been eating all this time!?'

Around then, in a certain room, **Dusk**, the owner of the ruined landscape painting, said, 'I don't need this painting anymore,' and when Dawn held out some hawthorn, she snapped, 'Don't need that either!'
6. A Seafood Platter on a Starving Shore (Guide: A Shady Priest)
Meanwhile, in a seaside cave in Iberia, the Abyssal Hunter Skadi struck down a monster once called the 'Bishop.'

And having lost all their luggage when the three went berserk in Sami, the party had arrived in the coastal town of Sal Viento. Watching the locals, who could barely speak, wolf down rotten clams, Senshi said he wanted to fill their bellies, and when Chilchuck remarked, 'You talk like you've been through it yourself,' he didn't answer.

Just then, a shady itinerant priest preaching 'the teachings of the sea' told them there was food in a cave to the south. Inside lay a dead, tower-sized, kraken-like monster, and Laios lamented, 'Whoever killed it must've gotten a way tastier meal than we will.'

Laios decided to lure out more monsters on purpose by setting the seaweed on fire, and Marcille let a spell rip with a quick 'Cover your ears.' Meanwhile, Chilchuck, left outside, caught on to the priest's scheme ('they shall soon become our brethren') and suggested they sit down and chat on a suspicious chest on the beach. The chest turned out to be a mimic, and the priest got swallowed whole.

Then Senshi lit a fire on the beach and prepped the monsters, curing the sashimi not with soy sauce and mustard but with an 'Emergency Sanity Potion' he'd picked up in a corner of the cave. Contains mustard powder extract; made in, of all places, Rhodes Island. And the mimic Chilchuck caught was handed over to Laios with a 'You're gonna want to taste it anyway.'

blocks.cap: Grilled seaweed, monster eggs, Sanity Potion-cured sashimi, and a mimic.

blocks.x: The priest came to, saw the sea-monster dishes, cried 'What blasphemy is this!', and fainted all over again. At the same moment, Anita at the tavern heard that some outsiders were cooking sea monsters and ran to the beach, but it was all over by the time she got there.

On a beach where nothing but long silence had lingered, people had gathered for the first time in ages, and off in the distance, four figures were wading into the sea with their hems rolled up, laughing.

blocks.cap: The sea breeze over Sal Viento feels especially striking today.

blocks.x: 7. When Drones Bomb, It Rains Popcorn

At the next stop, a frontier settlement in Columbia, a flying 'magic item' rained bombs on the party, and a bomb Marcille deflected blew up the village granary. The drones had actually gone haywire after the Catastrophe wrecked their relay station, but the pioneers took the party for supply thieves, and the party took the pioneers for raiders.

Rhodes Island field operator **Ryan**, who'd come to pick up Ceobe, shouted 'Let's talk first!' but nobody listened, and only after a horde of gloompincers swarmed in did everyone end up fighting on the same side. Once the fight was over, they went with Laios's proposal: 'On the count of three, everyone lowers their weapons, and it's a truce for tonight.'

That night, Laios woke Marcille up to go try the gloompincers, only to find the pioneers across the campfire already stuffing gloompincer legs into their mouths. After a long silence, the boss spoke: '...Want some?' Once everyone had shared the feast, the parting request was: 'Not a word about tonight to anyone!'

The remaining problem was the drones, still out of control. Senshi noticed they only target those who show hostility, and Marcille crafted a bait familiar out of gloompincer, fruit, flour, butter, and her own hair. Its model: Laios.

With Familiar Laios galloping on all fours, tongue lolling out, the pioneers scattered screaming, and Marcille dragged the drones out to the plains, wailing 'Why did I even think of doing this~~!!' Every last bomb came raining down there.
Except that was the pioneer boss's cornfield.

White popcorn drifted down like snow, and the one who came running at the smell and ended up munching even on Marcille's hair, buried in the popcorn mountain, was Ceobe. Senshi tossed the popcorn in butter and sugar, and made ice cream by mixing frozen fruit with 'the familiar, now a paste.'

blocks.cap: Popcorn and ice cream. As Chilchuck put it: "Best of all, no monster meat." (Let's pretend we didn't hear what the familiar was made of.)

blocks.x: Only after Ryan drove off with a full-bellied, sleeping Ceobe did the party realize he was from Rhodes Island. Apparently, Rhodes Island is currently parked just a few kilometers from here.
8. Rhodes Island at Last, but Something's Off with Ceobe
And at last, as the party stood at the edge of a cliff, a colossal steel ship cleaving across the land came into view. A city. A... dungeon. This was Rhodes Island.

blocks.cap: Bigger than any ship they've ever seen: a ship that sails on land.

blocks.x: Mudrock, who welcomed them aboard, filled them in on Big Bob. Anxious about whether his farm would ever work out, Big Bob gained huge confidence from watching the party eat so happily. He made money on beer, went to prison over taxes, got out by jailbreak or bail (nobody's quite sure which), and rumor has it the general store he opened in Sami is doing well these days. Senshi's take: 'Truly... a tenacious life.'

But after losing Mudrock at the elevator, the party ran into Arges, who said she had seen 'burning fire, a shock, and a fearsome beast.' In the training room she pointed them to was the High Priest, who told them to get in his mech if they wanted to see Ceobe, and the moment they climbed in, the mech exploded.

When **Eunectes** says 'This is pure revenge,' the High Priest replies: 'They boiled me, and I blew them up. So we're even.' Launched through the air, the party came down over the familiar P'o-shan Village and, with Dawn seeing them off with a 'See you again,' plunged into a bottomless well.
Where they ended up was Rhodes Island's kitchen. **Amiya** happened to be worrying about Ceobe, who'd grown quiet since coming back, when a loud crash rang out from Ceobe's room.

Inside was Ceobe, howling, transformed almost beyond recognition. Senshi threw popcorn to draw her attention, and while Laios, Senshi, and Matterhorn each pinned down a leg, Amiya whispered, 'Don't be afraid... This is your home...!'
Back to herself, Ceobe said she got so hungry in her dream that she sprouted a whole bunch of heads. When Laios asked, 'Do you know of a monster with three heads?', here's the answer he got.
Not three heads, it's got a thousand! I always wanna eat lots and lots, so even ten, a hundred, no, a thousand heads wouldn't be enough!

To the slack-jawed party, Amiya explained that getting them back to their own world would take time to look into, but that the Doctor and Dr. Kal'tsit would surely find a solution. And she welcomed them, asking them to stay on Rhodes Island for the time being.
Epilogue. Same Dish, Same Memories

Later, touring the ship, Laios made people back away by wondering aloud whether Liberi lay eggs, mistakenly asked the Doctor 'Do you lay eggs?', and got a good scolding for trying to touch Kal'tsit's Mon3tr. Senshi got yelled at for roasting chestnuts over Skyfire's flames, and Chilchuck was told by Hoshiguma at the bar, 'Children shouldn't be drinking.'

Then, that evening, Senshi recreated the dishes they'd eaten so far, using ingredients from the people they'd met on the road. When Marcille asked why he was making the same food again, Senshi brought up the scorpion hotpot and the basilisk from the Dungeon, and everyone's memories of those days came pouring out one after another.
Food is connected to memory. That's why, when you eat the same dish, the feelings from back then come back to you.
And the scene of this very moment, Senshi added, would also stay with them as a new memory of these dishes.

blocks.cap: The Rhodes Island cafeteria. From roast Originium Slugs to golden carrots, the flavors of the journey on one table.

blocks.x: Senshi lectured the Doctor, who reportedly skimps on meals, on 'A regular daily rhythm! A balanced diet!', while Laios murmured, 'I wish Falin were here too.'
Marcille said she'd learn these recipes and make sure Falin gets to taste them once they've saved her. She'd tell her that they met lots of good people, and made lots of wonderful memories.

Dropped onto an unfamiliar land, the gourmet party once again learned about the world by eating. Originium Slug stir-fry, High Priest stew, golden carrots, ink spirit jam, popcorn. Every bowl left behind one more memory of Terra, and the stories Marcille has to tell Falin grew by just as many.

act35side.tagline: An archaeologist chasing clues to a treasure trove slips a gem into a museum mummy and wakes a thousand-year-old guardian who copies her every move. Together they turn a city upside down on the eve of its festival, until the trail leads all the way to the bottom of the city. If something must not be forgotten, you remember it, even when it hurts.

chars.name: Pepe
chars.desc: Daughter of a Padishah and an archaeologist. A candidate to inherit her family's hereditary post as Historian.

chars.name: Titi
chars.desc: Vice curator of the museum. Longtime friend of Pepe and Anat · an incorrigible busybody.

chars.name: Anat
chars.desc: Acting curator of the museum. A by-the-book worrier · the Operator Papyrus.

chars.name: Zubayr
chars.desc: The nameless mummy at the heart of the museum's special exhibit. Believed to date from the Shah's era.

chars.name: Narantuya
chars.desc: A debt-ridden desert bandit boss. Self-proclaimed leader · has terrible luck with underlings.

chars.name: Aspasia
chars.desc: A tourist from Minos. Holder of ten silver medals · lives and dies by her principles.

chars.name: Lazvar
chars.desc: The young overseer of the Grand Bazaar's gem trading post. Weighs everything on his scales · the Operator Sand Reckoner.

chars.name: Mio
chars.desc: A cloudbeast kept by Lazvar. Has a temper, and something about it seems off.

chars.name: Woof
chars.desc: A black animal kept by Lazvar. Goes everywhere with Mio.

chars.name: Ajazi
chars.desc: One of Narantuya's underlings. Always paired up with Ajani.

chars.name: Ajani
chars.desc: One of Narantuya's underlings. Always paired up with Ajazi.

chars.name: Lugalszargus
chars.desc: The Shahanshah, King of Kings, of ancient Sargon. Known as the 'Shah of Past and Future.'

chars.name: Kharanduu Khagan
chars.desc: A leader of the Nightzmora of old. Remembered for a legendary battle against the Shah.

terms.name: Menat-Ha'mait
terms.desc: An old Sargonian city built along a river. So rich in gems that it's called the 'City of Radiance.'

terms.name: Flood Festival
terms.desc: A festival held in Menat-Ha'mait for a thousand years. When the river rises, people offer precious things to it and pray for good fortune.

terms.name: Historian
terms.desc: The post of recording Sargon's history at the Shahanshah's side. Once you enter the City of Gold, you can never leave for the rest of your life.

terms.name: City of Gold
terms.desc: The Sargonian city where the Shahanshah resides. Whoever becomes Historian enters it and never comes out again.

terms.name: Horakhet
terms.desc: The name Sargonians call the sun by. Used to greet the morning sun or in prayer.

terms.name: Nightzmora
terms.desc: A tribe of Kuranta warriors said to have marched day and night. On coming of age, each must undertake the 'Khaganquest' alone.

terms.name: Khaganquest
terms.desc: The Nightzmora coming-of-age rite. You travel alone to a land of trials, and it only ends when you make it home alive.

blocks.x: **Menat-Ha'mait** is a Sargonian city gearing up for the Flood Festival, a tradition a thousand years old. When the river swells, the people here offer their precious things to it and pray for a glimpse of the god's shadow walking along the banks.

Into this city comes **Pepe** — archaeologist, and daughter of a Padishah — carrying a gem left behind by the Shah. And from the day she sets that gem into the chest of a museum mummy, something that has waited a thousand years opens its eyes.
1. The friend she went to greet was in the river, catching a fin

**Titi** (Medjehtiqedti), the museum's vice curator, had people posted at every city gate to welcome her old friend. Pepe, meanwhile, was standing in the river, an hour and a half into trying to catch a pet fin some kid had lost.

Here's the plan Pepe lets them in on: use that gem as a clue to find the treasure trove the Shah supposedly promised the Nightzmora, then become the **Historian** — the one who writes down the Shahanshah's history in the City of Gold — in her little brother's place. In two months, an envoy is coming to take him away.

The last clue is the star of the special exhibit opening tomorrow: a mummy billed as 'a nameless general from the Shah's era.' When **Anat** — the third of the three friends, freshly appointed acting curator — says she can't lend it out until summer's over, Titi sighs and hands over her own access pass. If you get caught, she says, tell them you stole it.

blocks.cap: In front of a museum that has stood for centuries. "If only we could stop time for a moment."

blocks.x: Meanwhile, the red-haired desert bandit boss **Narantuya** overhears all this and runs the numbers: kidnap one Padishah's daughter, and her debts are paid off with change to spare.

And over at the museum ticket booth, Minoan tourist **Aspasia** is giving the ticket clerk a full history lecture on how poorly Minoan artifacts are being treated here. It ends with her buying one ticket.
2. Mid-speech, someone touched the curator's ear
That night, sneaking into the exhibition hall, Pepe recites the poem that serves as her clue. First, the heart. Second, the lungs. Third, the bowels. Fourth, the liver.

So she places the gem where the heart should be in the mummy's hollow chest. Nothing happens. And when she reaches in to take it back, her hand just paddles through empty air, as if groping around underwater. Just as a guard approaches, a cloudbeast named **Mio** turns up out of nowhere and meows, drawing his attention away.

The next morning, Titi shows up to work having poured an entire bottle of wine over herself, so it'll look like she was out drinking all night. Then, right before the opening ceremony, she rubs the ears of a trembling Anat. It's an old remedy only the three of them share — on the day of Anat's job interview, Titi and Pepe kept it up all day long.

But in the middle of her speech, a lost Aspasia stops to ask where an exhibit is, and Narantuya, on her way to an ambush with a syringe in hand, bumps into a guest and causes a scene. Thrown off her rhythm, Anat forgets what comes next.
That's when someone gently pinches Anat's ear. She's about to say thanks — and then she spots Titi in the crowd, staring this way with eyes as wide as saucers.

blocks.cap: The hand on her ear wasn't Titi's.

blocks.x: 3. A copycat mummy and a kidnapping plan gone sideways

At the scream of 'The mummy moved!', the hall descends into chaos and Anat faints. Pepe, calmly examining the mummy, realizes it copies her every movement — so she has it carry Anat and follow along, step for step, as she walks.
If she shortens her stride, the mummy trips on its robes. If Pepe falls, the mummy falls right along with her. And every single time, it's poor Anat who gets hurt.

blocks.cap: Not too long a stride, not too short. Anat's bruises keep adding up.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, Narantuya's underling **Ajazi**, disguised as staff, is evacuating visitors — but mixes up left and right, and ends up leading dozens of people into the dead-end Minos gallery. Where, as it happens, Aspasia is holding her family's golden goblet, plundered by Sargon a century ago, and vowing to 'take it home.'

When the lost visitors ask her the way out, she hoists a collapsed visitor onto her shoulder and leads everyone to the main entrance — only realizing after the shutters come down: "...Where's my goblet?"
Back in the curator's office, Anat comes to, hears the whole story from Pepe, and asks: if becoming the Historian means never leaving the City of Gold for the rest of your life, why go this far?
Thousands of years from now, someone I'll never meet will read those words and feel a connection to me and the Shah. I want the three of us to be linked like that.

In the end, Anat lends her the mummy — and throws in the museum's own second gem for good measure. Along with a request: that Pepe learn to accept that 'sometimes, no result is a result too.' But even with the second gem inside, the mummy doesn't budge.
4. His name is Zubayr, and his memory comes in five pieces

Then, while Anat steps out at the sound of Titi screaming, Narantuya climbs in through the window and creeps up behind Pepe, who's busy rifling through the bookshelves. The moment the syringe goes up, the mummy — motionless on the sofa until now — grabs her by the wrist.

blocks.cap: The needle turned back toward its owner's neck.

blocks.x: The mummy injects Narantuya with her own syringe and hauls her out the window. And who catches her as she falls from on high? Aspasia, who has been waiting outside for the museum doors to reopen.

And then the mummy speaks for the first time. He was a royal guard officer to **Lugalszargus**, the Shahanshah. Made undying, he has guarded His Majesty's trove, waiting for the return his king swore he would make. His name is **Zubayr**.
The catch: he can't remember where the trove is. He split those memories across five gems, and the army of ameers and padishahs that brought him to his knees made off with the rest of them.

As for Titi, the source of that scream: she'd been terrified by a metal **jewel construct** that smashed its way out of a display case. A little while later, she was playing fetch with it and calling it her 'cute little baby.'

That night, Pepe breaks the no-going-out order and takes Zubayr out on the town, where he casually reminisces about beheading the Padishah of Shahr-Cheshmeh, the City of Springs, in the springs themselves.
As dawn approaches, Pepe says it's time to head back, but Zubayr holds her there. He wants to see the one thing even time can't change.

blocks.cap: His first morning sun in centuries. "Greetings to you, Horakhet."

blocks.x: His golden body, asleep for centuries in the darkness beneath the sand, glitters in the morning light. Pepe tells him they can stay a little longer. Just a little, though.
5. Aiming for second place, accidentally winning first
A few days later, the third gem turns up somewhere unexpected: second prize at the Harvest Gathering, a pre-festival event, is 'a giant gem bearing traces of the Shah's era.'

In a contest where nobles and the wealthy flock in bearing family heirlooms, she needs to land in exactly second place. Gazing at the sunlight pouring through a skylight, Pepe points a finger at the sun.

blocks.cap: Praise be to you, Horakhet. And that round patch of light on the floor? Looks exactly like a golden slipper.

blocks.x: Her entry: a single golden slipper, handed down in her family for generations. Pepe quietly pulls a judge aside and asks for a score good enough for exactly second place.

Meanwhile, Narantuya wakes up in Aspasia's room and decides her lifesaver is a 'trusty underling' sent by fate. Aspasia, convinced Narantuya jumped as a bid for fame, tags along to help her find the will to live — and discovers that third prize at the Harvest Gathering is the 'other' goblet of her pair.

Aspasia's entry: ten silver medals from ten different events. Behind her back, Narantuya leans on the judges — 'the Minoan silver medals get third' — and one of them is so unusually terrified that he slumps to the floor muttering about the Padishah's gallows.

The results go exactly to plan: Pepe second by 0.05 points, Aspasia third. But then the first-place collector claims his hand slipped, smashes his own porcelain, and withdraws, declaring that no one should ever place above the Padishah's daughter.

Everyone moves up a spot. Pepe gets the first prize, a statue; Aspasia gets the gem Pepe was after; and the goblet goes to whoever came fourth. On top of that, tradition says winning entries are offered to the river — so the heirloom slipper and the ten silver medals sink side by side, to the sound of a choir.
Still, Aspasia is thrilled that Minoan culture got some recognition — so thrilled she nearly tosses the gem into the river too, before Narantuya grabs her. "Could I... borrow this gem for a while?"
6. The gem a cloudbeast coughed up, and an artifact that clocks in for work

Narantuya uses the gem as bait, rigs her room with traps, and sends Pepe an anonymous invitation. But while her underlings guard the door all night, Mio slips daintily past every trap and sits gazing at the gem on the table.
Around the same time, Titi and Anat have a fight at the museum. Titi wants to spin the whole incident as a 'living exhibit'; Anat says she worked too hard for this position to go stirring up trouble.

That night, Titi runs into Mio on the street and pours her heart out to it. Back in the day, Anat's voice was so quiet that everyone used to snicker — but even when the laughter drowned her out, she always kept talking to the end. So Titi hopes she won't give up on the special exhibit.

As she strokes Mio absentmindedly, her palm grows hot — and Mio spits out a gem. Titi offers it up in exchange for a promise from the other three, and the museum reopens with a new special exhibit: 'Meet the Shah-Era General Risen from the Dead.'

blocks.cap: The special exhibit reopens. This time, the exhibit clocks in himself.

blocks.x: Zubayr's days are exhausting. Endless rapid-fire photos, lucky coins flung right at the middle of his body, and twenty weddings a day that he goes through without the faintest idea why.
Meanwhile, Pepe deals with 73 visitors who've shown up claiming to have the very gem she's looking for — until Anat's head starts to look like a square pyramid.

That night, Zubayr wants to tell her all about his day, but the exhausted Pepe presses him to hurry up and get his memories back — and goes so far as to ask why else she would have woken him. "I told you already! I am not an exhibit!"
After Pepe apologizes and leaves, Zubayr, alone in the empty room, turns off the light — and a moment later, turns it back on.
7. Two people meet on the riverbank at night

Meanwhile, Aspasia — who spent three hours talking a collector into handing over the goblet — overhears, outside the door of their inn room, that Narantuya used that gem as bait in a plot to kidnap the Padishah's daughter.

Instead of explaining herself, Narantuya holds out 1,200 dinars to repay everything she owes. She asks whether Aspasia will grieve for her if an ameer catches and executes her someday. Of course, Aspasia answers. And with no debts left between them, the two part ways.
That night, Zubayr breaks a window and leaves the museum. And down by the river, next to Narantuya — sitting alone, insisting she's just seen a ghost — a dejected passerby sits down.

blocks.cap: The riverside street at night. Two people who each lost an argument sit side by side.

blocks.x: When the passerby confides about his day of twenty weddings, Narantuya answers that her old comrades sold their blades and are living in squalor, so as their boss, the debt is hers. Then she brings up what her mom told her when she left home: the Nightzmora are the masters of fear.
"You are a Nightzmora?" At that moment the streetlamp flickers on, revealing the passerby — and Narantuya's scream echoes down the street.

The next day, the two form a 'historic alliance' — and Narantuya sells Zubayr, coffin and all, to **Lazvar**, overseer of the gem trading post, for a gold bar. She winks and promises to come back for him once he finds the gem inside... and the second she's out the door, it's goodbye forever.

Left behind, Zubayr says that if she truly is a descendant of the Nightzmora, there will be a trove waiting for her. And then Mio and a black animal named **Woof** speak to Lazvar: "Well done, Lazvar."
8. Her brother's voice
Around then, Anat tells Pepe what she has been putting off. When she visited Pepe's father's estate two months ago, the envoy from the City of Gold had already come. Her brother was already gone.

Pepe's letter had twenty exclamation marks in it. Anat couldn't bring herself to tell her. She lent out the mummy, too, because she believed that in a city with gems beyond counting, Pepe would give up on her own.

Her brother didn't look happy, Anat says. He said they would never meet again in this life, and asked that his sister remember his voice. Most of his few belongings were things connected to her and to their father.
Only then does Pepe open up. Her brother was a restless boy who couldn't sit at a desk for even a second. He fought her for the post because he didn't want his sister left there alone.
I didn't want him stuck there by himself either.

At the same time, in the gem trading post, Lazvar brings a gem out of the vault. Three hundred years ago, an ameer's army searched for the trove by cutting off the villagers' hands. The one who finally led them there was a gem artisan who had already lost both of his.

In that battle, the guardian's chest was split open and every one of his gems was taken. The trading post founded by the artisan's child has been gathering gems into this city for generations, so that one day they could be returned to him.
When the sistrum touches Lazvar's chest, he sees the guardian walking alone across an endless desert, waiting for the sunrise.

blocks.cap: Walking the desert under the stars, the guardian turns his head. His eyes are sad.

blocks.x: ...It has been a long time indeed. You are all free now.

With the fourth gem, Zubayr recovers his post and his duty. He asks a favor of Mio and Woof: find out whether that Nightzmora truly descends from **Kharanduu Khagan**, and whether she is fit to be a companion who will wait with him for the Shah's return.
9. The city where the sand rises
That night, sitting at her desk, Pepe hears her brother's voice behind her, begging her to come and play. She turns around. No one is there.

The next morning, the radio carries breaking news: metal figures have been raiding homes for gems, and the tap water is coming out mixed with sand. Pepe rushes to the Grand Bazaar and sees it for herself. Every time the constructs raise their hands, a house crumbles into sand, and ancient pillars and walls rise in its place.
Then little Mio, sitting in the street, lets out a roar. When Pepe opens her eyes, a sand-colored beast is looming over her. It swallows her whole.

blocks.cap: A roar bursting from an animal smaller than her calf.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, Anat, chased by a swarm of constructs, calls out to Horakhet, asking to see tomorrow's sunrise — and the constructs stop and begin to pose riddles. Tell us the 'Name' he left to the world. Three minutes.

Anat opens Dr. Erikson's book, Terra: A Journey, and answers them one by one. The constructs fall quiet like an audience, and Anat remembers what Titi told her the first time she stood at a podium: "Just keep saying what you think is right, Anat."

Elsewhere, as Narantuya flees, the constructs in front of her all stop at once and gather around her like tamed burdenbeasts. Watching, Woof murmurs that she really is a descendant of Kharanduu Khagan.

blocks.cap: Narantuya, at the center of the halted metal figures.

blocks.x: Drawn into a dream, Narantuya realizes that the road she took when she left home alone with a single weapon was the **Khaganquest**, the Nightzmora coming-of-age rite — and wakes up shouting that she's scared. If the dream is going to end anyway, she asks, why not dream the best one possible? Aspasia bursts out laughing and holds out her hand.
10. Zubayr's memories
At the end of the darkness she took for the beast's belly, Pepe finds herself standing at a desert oasis. A boy pulls a golden fin from the lake and calls her 'sister.'

The boy says he will follow their father east on campaign, and asks his sister to come with him. The one who answers isn't Pepe, but a girl wearing a golden lotus ornament on her forehead. "I'll follow you and Father, Zubayr."

The boy grew up to command his father's guard, and his sister vowed to record the history of Sargon without leaving anything out. Only then does Pepe understand. The two of them were the Shah's children.

But their father, who had called on Kharanduu Khagan to face an unseen enemy in the south, vanished without a trace, and Zubayr was carried home burned black from head to toe. Still, his sister, now with child, did not put down her pen. She believed this history would become a bridge across time.

Zubayr tells his sister that she will honor their father through her records, and he will guard the trove their father left behind. He does not want to lie still forever, so he will place his consciousness into gems and take a new body.
Zubayr, I only wish for you to be happy, and nothing more. Promise me you'll remember these words forever.
The next moment, Pepe is lying on a stone table, wrapped in wet linen. A voice says the brain will now be removed. A blade touches the center of her forehead.

blocks.cap: Even as his consciousness was being drawn out, he was alive.

blocks.x: The voice in the dark goes on. He waited nearly a thousand years, but the descendants forgot the promise, and he came to hate himself for the choice he made. Even when he wanted to forget, the gems kept every memory vivid.
When the voice warns that there is a price, Pepe asks back: was there ever a single moment he wanted to forget his sister and his father? The answer is: "Never."
That's my answer. If something shouldn't be forgotten, we have to remember it, even if it brings us pain.

When she opens her eyes, she is back in the Grand Bazaar. Mio, the owner of that voice, protests furiously that she has failed. Historians have their tongues cut out, it says. Even Lugalszargus's youngest daughter, the first human it ever kept, had her tongue cut out by her own brother.

But Woof declares that Pepe has passed the test and drags Mio away by the scruff, and Pepe, hammer in hand, faces Zubayr. The trove lies beneath this very city, where his father's cenotaph stands. For centuries, treasure dug out of that tomb is what has kept the city alive.
Saying he will show her the deepest treasure, the one no one has yet touched, Zubayr turns the ground to quicksand with his sistrum.
11. What was in the trove

Around then, sand is pouring from every faucet in the museum. Even the gems used to purify the water have vanished, so the sand is flowing back up. If the underground waterways collapse, the whole city will sink into quicksand. Narantuya and Aspasia head down into the waterways to plug the leak.
Beneath the city, the lights come on in the trove, and countless illusions begin to walk the hall. Every one of them is the Shah.

blocks.cap: The Shah's words and image, preserved with ancient technology by the Historians of a thousand years ago.

blocks.x: These were records that Zubayr's sister, longing for their father, had asked to be preserved. Standing before them, Pepe sinks into emptiness: everything she has chased was only a passage from one illusion to another, and even her family's post might be an illusion too.

Zubayr tells her that her forehead ornament is identical to his sister's. The family's post as Historian began with one daughter who missed her father. It became hereditary when Zubayr's elder brother, having taken the throne, forced her to send one of her twin sons to the palace.
Zubayr offers her eternal life. Pepe shakes her head. She cannot take his sister's place. She has to go to the City of Gold to find her brother — but she cannot leave a crumbling city behind, either.
Zubayr says the vow is engraved into the gems, and he cannot stop himself. He tells her to come at him with everything she has, as the armies that once invaded this place did.

At the same time, in the underground waterways, a wall gives way and opens onto a darkness with no visible end. Aspasia tells Narantuya that her old underlings are doing fine — some opened restaurants, some write newspaper serials — so she owes them nothing. It is time for her to go home.

blocks.cap: Each trying to stop the other from jumping, the two draw their weapons at the same moment.

blocks.x: Narantuya laughs that this isn't a duty but her own choice — she just wants to see a mountain of gold with her own eyes. Then she blinds Aspasia with sand and illusions and jumps into the darkness first. "There. Another silver medal for you."

In the trove, Pepe is chasing Zubayr as he hides among the illusions. When she says that whatever she sets her mind to, she sees through, Zubayr answers that this is an illusion only someone who has lived a mere twenty-two years could hold. The greatest enemy of his life was time. He brings his staff down on her ankle.
Pepe closes her eyes. As a child, whenever she tried to catch her brother, quick as a fin, she would close her eyes and listen for his footsteps. "I'm all hidden, sister. You can come find me now."
Just as she did in that memory, Pepe turns and swings her hammer.
12. Let go
The sistrum stops just short of Pepe's throat. Her hammer rests against Zubayr's chest. A long, thin crack spreads across the gem there.

He always lost to his sister at hide-and-seek, Zubayr says, and now he has lost to Pepe as well. As her ancestor, he makes one last request. Inside the giant gem lies the final gem: the emotions he cut away so he could endure the long years alone. He asks her to place it in his chest. He wants to leave as a whole human being.
"You have always been human." Zubayr says there is something he wants to tell her about the City of Gold — then, in the end, leaves it unsaid.
Let go, Pepe. You must let me go...

blocks.cap: A white lotus drifts away across the golden waves.

blocks.x: Water pours into the collapsing trove and covers him, and the gem breaks apart in the current. Zubayr smiles with his eyes closed, and his body becomes golden water that slips away between Pepe's fingers.
"May you guide his soul to rest, Horakhet."

Meanwhile, having jumped into the darkness, Narantuya follows a red-haired apparition and sees, beyond a closed door, a mountain of gold and jewels. Beneath her feet, a vast fissure is sucking in the city's sand. She raises a black beast statue overhead and charges, shouting "Open up!" The door opens, and the toppling mountain of treasure pours into the fissure as a shining waterfall.

blocks.cap: Hanging from her blade fan, looking down on the waterfall of treasure, Narantuya laughs out loud.

blocks.x: All of this... is my own choice!
The sunken treasure seals the fissure and holds up the sand. And as Pepe, swept away by the current, begins to lose consciousness, someone grabs her hand.

blocks.cap: "Ha! Guess luck's on my side after all. At least I fished one thing out!"

blocks.x: They swim up and surface in the public gardens. The sand has stopped. The constructs no longer move.
Pepe starts to say something about Zubayr, glances once at the pond — and instead laughs that of course she looks pale, she nearly drowned, and splashes fountain water on the dust-covered Anat.

blocks.cap: "Isn't the sunlight just right today?"

blocks.x: Epilogue — At the crossroads, setting out again

Within two days, the city begins to return to itself. Anat steps down as acting curator, saying she will travel Terra like Dr. Erikson and write him letters along the way. Ajani and Ajazi are officially hired by the museum.

Pepe says she had dreamed of an adventure where someone comes after her gem, and it's a shame no one got in her way. Narantuya laughs awkwardly. Then she sets out alone on her Khaganquest. The road only ends when you return home alive, but she cannot go home — so she will call it finished when she meets her next underling.
On her way out, Narantuya presses a gift into the hands of Aspasia, who is heading back to Minos. It is the golden goblet from the museum's Minos gallery.

blocks.cap: "Just say 'thank you' and leave with it as fast as you can."

blocks.x: Aspasia asks nothing more and simply says thank you. Remembering that the goblet was the only treasure she gained in the whole month, Narantuya tells herself this, too, was her choice, and walks on.
And when Lazvar leaves the trading post, Woof stays behind in this city, which is still alive, while Mio, saying it wants to see the City of Gold, picks Titi as its new keeper.

Six months later, as her paper on Zubayr is drawing attention, an envoy of the Shahanshah comes to Pepe. His Majesty wishes to hear the story of Menat-Ha'mait in person, the envoy says. Prepare to leave for the City of Gold.

Perhaps the god's shadow said to walk the riverbank was the illusion of the Shah left in the trove beneath the city. The guardian who kept watch beside it for a thousand years has flowed away as golden water. And now the City of Gold is calling Pepe, who said she would remember, even if it hurts.

act34side.tagline: Five years after they left, the Hunters return to the sea of their homeland and fight to open a route linking sea and land, only to watch that path finally open through the bodies of the Seaborn. A story caught between surviving and having a reason to live.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: The physician who leads Rhodes Island. She travels to an Ægir city as Iberia's envoy.

chars.name: Skadi
chars.desc: An Abyssal Hunter from Ægir. She returns to the sea of her homeland after five years.

chars.name: Specter
chars.desc: An Abyssal Hunter. Her real name is Laurentina. Before becoming a Hunter, she dreamed of being a sculptor.

chars.name: Gladiia
chars.desc: The de facto leader of the Abyssal Hunters. Commander of Ægir's Honor Exercitus and a Chief Designer of Warfare.

chars.name: Ulpianus
chars.desc: An Abyssal Hunter who disappeared on his own. He keeps his distance even from his comrades and pursues a truth of his own.

chars.name: Secunda
chars.desc: Commander of the Milliarium Sea Patrol. Formerly a researcher in the Abyssal Hunter program. · Operator Underflow

chars.name: Irene
chars.desc: An envoy of the Iberian Inquisition. She has come to see for herself what is happening in the deep sea.

chars.name: Jordi Fontanarossa
chars.desc: An Inquisition clerk from Gran Faro. Ægir by blood, but he has never seen the sea his people come from.

chars.name: Clementia
chars.desc: A consul of Milliarium. Chief Designer of Warfare for the Waterway Program.

chars.name: Tullia
chars.desc: A data analyst for the Waterway Program. A quiet Ægir who tended endangered seaweed.

chars.name: Blandus
chars.desc: Weapons technology advisor to the Waterway Program. Formerly the technical advisor to the Abyssal Hunter program.

chars.name: Avitus
chars.desc: A scholar at the Institute of Prehistoric Studies, Academy of Science. He deciphers the texts left by the ancient civilization.

chars.name: Lucilla
chars.desc: An Ægir from Milliarium's Institute of Facility Management. She inspects the city's unit frameworks and surveys the currents.

chars.name: Horatia
chars.desc: A consul of Ægir's Institute of Scientific Development Planning. Gladiia's mother.

chars.name: Carmen
chars.desc: A Saint of the Iberian Inquisition. She watches the sea from the Eye of Iberia.

terms.name: Milliarium
terms.desc: Ægir's mobile undersea city and military fortress. It has come to the waters off the continent for the Waterway Program.

terms.name: Waterway Program
terms.desc: A plan to open a sea route linking the Ægir homeland and the continent. Beacons are planted in Seaborn nests, and weapons purge the waters.

terms.name: Class IV weapon
terms.desc: A biological weapon developed by the Academy of Technology for the Waterway Program. It kills off the Seaborn nests and their young in the target waters.

terms.name: Beacon Tower
terms.desc: The old beacon launcher at the heart of Milliarium. The product of a dream, three hundred years ago, of reaching out among the stars.

terms.name: Sophontheatrum
terms.desc: A public facility where Ægir gather to ask questions and debate. Knowledge is stored in a massive coral-shaped terminal.

terms.name: Auto-Adaptive Junction
terms.desc: A modification inside the bodies of the Abyssal Hunters. It keeps the Seaborn genes from taking control.

terms.name: Firstborn
terms.desc: A colossal entity at the root of a Seaborn swarm. Five years ago, the Hunters brought down one of them, Ishar'mla.

terms.name: We Many
terms.desc: The name the Seaborn use for themselves. It refers not to individuals but to a single, connected swarm.

terms.name: The Death of Life
terms.desc: A precursor's audio diary, deciphered and published by Avitus. It became a bestseller in Ægir as soon as it came out.

blocks.x: "A hunter returns by seacoast way. His journey ended, his home close at hand. Why do his feet disobey his command?"

In a small village on the road to the Eye of Iberia lighthouse, **Skadi** met the Doctor, then turned her head toward the sea. Through the troubled waves, an unfamiliar voice whispered: "Ishar-mla. I'm here."

blocks.cap: A forgotten seaside village. Within three months its residents had left, and the Penal Battalion had taken their place.

blocks.x: A week earlier, Ægir had informed Iberia that it would open a sea route between its homeland and the continent. Around then, **Gladiia** and **Specter** confirmed that the spot where the Stultifera Navis sank had become a Seaborn nest, and that the nearby seabed bore recent signs of battle that only a regular Ægir fleet could have left.
Cut off from their homeland since bringing down the Firstborn Ishar'mla five years ago, the Hunters decided to go home. **Kal'tsit** decided to go with them as Iberia's envoy.
1. A Greeting Descends on the Lighthouse

Meanwhile, **Saint Carmen** of the Iberian Inquisition and **Irene** had been watching the sea from the lighthouse for eight days. A formation of bionic drones crossed the sky toward them like a school of fish.

blocks.cap: The Saint's lantern and the drones' lights. The first official contact between two civilizations.

blocks.x: The voice behind the drones belonged to **Clementia**, a technology consul of Ægir. She said Ægir would clear the waters from its homeland to the continent so its main force could reach the coast, and invited the Iberian delegation to the city of Milliarium.

When the transmission ended, Carmen said only, "Arrogant. No doubt." The delegation would be Kal'tsit, Irene, and the Inquisition clerk **Jordi Fontanarossa**. Jordi was Ægir, yet had never seen that sea. Carmen told him that going home would be a trial as well.
Around then, **Ulpianus** swam alone into a Seaborn nest hidden at the deepest point of a trench.

blocks.cap: The Seaborn called the intruder "kin."

blocks.x: The Seaborn told him to shed his useless flesh and blood and return, and to leave the sea, for an era would soon awaken. Ulpianus asked one last question. "What connection is there between you and the affairs of the city?"
2. A Solitary Eye in the Ocean

The day after arriving in Milliarium, Jordi was thrown to the floor by a gravity adjustment while passersby calmly floated up into the air. He was the only one startled. He was afraid of how this place would see him: an Ægir who did not fit in Ægir.

Meanwhile, Specter took the Doctor's party to the beacon launcher at the center of the city. Three hundred years ago, Ægir had built the tower to set an undying beacon in the sea of stars beyond the barrier. Then the Seaborn appeared and cut that long dream short.
Hundreds of millions of nanomachines conceived inside the tower all died there when the energy was cut off. Now the tower served as a hub, gathering data from the beacons planted in the nests.

At the same time, Clementia received Gladiia in her Pensivarium and wrapped her in both arms. Ægir rarely greet one another with touch, and Gladiia could not remember whether her mother, **Horatia**, had ever held her like this.

blocks.cap: Clementia called the city a "solitary and luminous eye" in the ocean.

blocks.x: Clementia laid out the Waterway Program. She had brought Class IV weapons, biological weapons that kill off Seaborn nests and their young. Beacons would be planted in every nest to fix their positions. Once the weapons were activated, clear waters would open all the way to the homeland.

But over the past month, the Seaborn had evolved to shield one another even under bombardment. Clementia was unsure whether to believe Ulpianus's claim that there was more than one Firstborn, and said the Hunters' return would have to go through a tribunal.

Meanwhile, Sea Patrol commander **Secunda** was searching for **Tullia**, a data analyst for the Waterway Program. Tullia had been missing for thirty hours. Irene attached herself to the investigation despite being turned away.
3. A Hunter at Center Stage

In Tullia's room, Secunda and Irene found only empty hydroponic boxes hanging on the walls. She had cultivated endangered deep-sea algae at the Institute of Ecological Art. Two days before she vanished, she had downloaded data from the Beacon Tower's central control room and made a backup. The backup was nowhere to be found.

blocks.cap: Tullia's room. Books arranged by thickness, shells by size.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, a tribunal on the Hunters' return convened at the Sophontheatrum. A shadow approached the Doctor's seat in the back row without a sound.
"Not a sound." It was Ulpianus.

The Academy of Science asked whether the Hunters, assimilated by Seaborn genes, might one day become Ægir's enemies. **Blandus**, once technical advisor to the old Abyssal Hunter program, answered that as long as he maintained the Auto-Adaptive Junctions in their bodies, they would not become Seaborn.
Suspicion turned instead to the absent Ulpianus. His information that there were multiple Firstborn fit too well. It could be the truth, or an answer built to fit every question.
Ulpianus spoke only to the Doctor. There were signs that a new Firstborn was waking, and the great migration of the Seaborn and Ægir's Waterway Program were happening almost at the same time.
The tribunal recognized the innocence of the three Hunters and concluded that Ulpianus would be found and made to answer its questions.

blocks.cap: Gladiia, left alone at the center of the Sophontheatrum to take questions.

blocks.x: Gladiia had always sat in the highest, farthest seat in the theater. Watching her stand at center stage, Skadi said, "Only now does it really feel like we're back in Ægir."
4. Marine Snow
After the tribunal, an emergency distress signal came in. A Legion X fleet sent to plant a beacon at Nest 37 had been ambushed by the Seaborn.
Around then, Ulpianus appeared before the Doctor again and said the Waterway Program was going too smoothly. "If you truly care about the Hunters, keep a close eye on Skadi."

Hearing the alarm at the port, Gladiia deployed with only Specter and ordered Skadi to protect the Doctor. Left behind, Skadi confided in the Doctor. Five years ago, when their captain Ulpianus's signal went silent, she believed he was dead and struck the final blow against the Firstborn. She did not know why the captain still had not come back.

Meanwhile, at the port, Secunda told Irene about her past. As a researcher in the Abyssal Hunter program, she had applied to be modified herself and was rejected. She then joined the Sea Patrol, which fights alongside the Hunters and also keeps watch on them.

When Gladiia and Specter reached the coordinates, they found ship wreckage tangled with Seaborn corpses. Between them drifted fragments of tissue, Seaborn and human mixed, falling like snowflakes. People called it the snow of the sea: marine snow.

blocks.cap: The seabed where the fleet bound for Nest 37 went down.

blocks.x: Around then, Irene and Secunda found fragments of Tullia's tissue at the city's old mooring. The remains showed she had encountered the Seaborn, and the two concluded she could not have survived.

In the end, all Gladiia and Specter rescued was a single ship that had been covering the main fleet's retreat. The thousand or so they had come to protect fell into a larger ambush. The only survivors were the twenty-six aboard that ship.
"You survived. Lift your heads, Ægir."
5. The Death of Life
Meanwhile, at a terminal in the Sophontheatrum, Jordi looked up Breogan, the ship designer he had believed to be his ancestor. In the footage, he could find nothing of himself in the man.

blocks.cap: Jordi before the coral-shaped terminal of the Sophontheatrum.

blocks.x: "I finally followed its light and reached the foot of the lighthouse, and I couldn't see anything at all." **Avitus**, a prehistory researcher from the Academy of Science, told him that blood ties did not matter, but murmured to himself: what if history says the fall of our home and our civilization is inevitable?

The next day, Avitus visited his student Cassia. Her favorite book was The Death of Life, which he had deciphered and published: the audio diary of a man living through the collapse of the precursor civilization.
Cassia asked whether her teacher's despair had grown since his partner passed away. Then she said she still had work left to finish.

Meanwhile, in front of the Beacon Tower, Clementia said the Hunters would also have to take part in the final battle against Nest 37, which held the Waterway by the throat. When Kal'tsit asked about their safety, Gladiia answered for them. "The safety of the Abyssal Hunters is the Abyssal Hunters' own concern."
Clementia wanted to hold Gladiia one last time, as she had on the day of her return. She did not.

Then **Lucilla** of the Institute of Facility Management came to see Secunda. The day before the Institute of Ecological Art moved to another city, she said, Tullia had been saving every bit of seaweed she could from being thrown away.
These primitive seaweeds are some of the simplest, yet most tenacious lifeforms in the entire ocean.

Tullia had watched a breeding reserve be trampled by the Seaborn, and had said she could not stand by while these little ones withered. Secunda immediately had people search the city for a sealed space where the seaweed could be grown.
6. Her Journey Ended
Before the sortie, Blandus began surgery at the old institute to repair the Hunters' aging Auto-Adaptive Junctions. As he had five years ago, he lit a candle beside the sleeping Specter.

blocks.cap: The operating room of the old Abyssal Hunter institute.

blocks.x: Then cultists of the Church of the Deep, disguised as researchers, burst in, held a poisonous grass to Blandus's neck, and tried to stop the surgery. Gladiia, who had not been asleep, drove her spear through one of their chests. Skadi and Specter, also awake, subdued the rest.

The Hunters did not lower their weapons at Blandus either, who had tampered with the regenerative gel. He said he had wanted them to return to their old lives. Gladiia answered that the twenty-six they had rescued the day before had already volunteered for a new unit. "As long as the war does not end, no soldier can escape the battlefield."

Around then, Secunda met her old teacher Ulpianus in the shadows. He told her that Tullia had been an ordinary person who tried to report something and failed, and that it was Cassia who had muddied the investigation. Then he vanished.

Secunda and Irene found the old experimental field. Seaweed covered its walls. In front of it, a Seaborn drifted, coiled around a container of nutrient fluid, as if not yet used to its body. "Tul... li... a..."

Secunda pieced together what had happened. Tullia had told someone about an anomaly in the signal system, was driven by Church of the Deep cultists to a drain, and fell into the sea. With no equipment, she ate the flesh of another species to make it back to the city. Her mind had broken apart, and the only reason she came back was this seaweed.
The Seaborn suddenly screamed. It seemed to have seen its reflection in the glass of a hydroponic box.
Saying, "She is an Ægir," Secunda sent Irene back. She set up her shield between the Seaborn and the boxes, raised her weapon, and sang softly.
Her journey ended. Her home close at hand.
The shield kept the Seaborn's fluids from reaching the boxes. The seaweed only swayed, breathing quietly.
7. A Chronic Illness Called Fate

Meanwhile, Avitus told Jordi about his partner. When the Seaborn's encroachment outpaced creation, she gave up their plan to raise a child together. Five years ago, when the Hunters did not return, she fell ill and died. He sent their child to the Institute of Incubation.

At the same time, Blandus confessed to Secunda that he was the one who had rejected her application for modification. Ulpianus had agreed with him. "There should be no one in Ægir who wishes to become another."
Meanwhile, the Doctor stayed beside Blandus in the control room of Lab C-22 and reordered the surveillance feeds, mapping out a path for the infiltrating Ulpianus.

Blandus asked the Doctor what Oripathy felt like. When the Doctor answered that it was a fight against fate, he said that perhaps the chronic illness carved into the Hunters' blood was fate itself, and that he had never managed to free them from this cruel road of death.
Just before the sortie, Skadi asked Gladiia to destroy her on the spot if Ishar'mla really was inside her and she lost control. "My heart's right here. I trust you won't miss."

blocks.cap: The port before the sortie.

blocks.x: Then Ulpianus told the Doctor what he had found. Someone had altered the link between the beacons and the weapons. He had suspected Ægir from the start because, five years ago, he had seen an Ægir-made water flow meter inside Ishar'mla's body that had been there for at least two hundred years.
Ulpianus headed for the beacon launcher, and the Doctor for Clementia, who had sent the Hunters out.
8. Blandus's Bridge
Around then, deep within Nest 37, the Hunters passed Seaborn dividing into forms whose organs could not even be recognized, and drove a beacon into the rock wall.

Meanwhile, in the Pensivarium, Clementia heard the Doctor's warning and immediately ordered the Beacon Tower secured. She then admitted that the Abyssal Hunter program had continued in secret, and that its new test subjects had all degenerated into Seaborn the moment they awoke. She recited the maxim at the entrance of the Sophontheatrum.
There is no justice here, only the path ahead.
Blandus did not answer the call.

Five years ago, on the eve of the hunt for the Firstborn, Blandus had observed a strange phenomenon in Ulpianus's body. When the Auto-Adaptive Junction reduced the rejection response, the Seaborn genes also withdrew their attempt to control him.
Now, in the Beacon Tower's central control room, Ulpianus called him "Blandus, cultist of the Deep." The final beacon had already been activated, and the Class IV weapons had already been launched.

Blandus revealed that he had reproduced that surgical accident in the Hunters' bodies and modified the weapons on the same principle. If the Seaborn could see the Hunters as kin, We Many might come to see Ægir as neighbors. The Hunters would not be sacrificed; they would live and prove their worth.
Dying from experimenting on his own body, he asked Ulpianus to carry on the project. Ulpianus refused.
That is the same arrogance the Ægir once had when they were sure they could defeat the Seaborn. No, this is that a hundred times over.
"The only one who ever despaired was you, Blandus." Ulpianus delivered his final sentence as an Ægir.

The golden holochart rippled, too bright, and Blandus closed his eyes. Hearing his old friend's anchor scrape across the floor, he remembered, too late, that he had never once embraced the Hunters who had come home.

blocks.cap: The Beacon Tower's central control room. Blandus's last moments.

blocks.x: 9. The Nest That Became a Heart

Then Jordi entered the control room. Even after seeing Blandus collapsed, when he heard the Hunters were in danger he recalled Breogan's habits, bypassed the lockdown, and sent a warning signal to the beacon at Nest 37.

Ulpianus told him that Breogan had once lived in hiding in Gran Faro, and that the research notes of Jordi's parents were linked to him. "If all you shared with him was blood, then that would be something to be ashamed of."

At the same moment in the nest, the beacon's gravitational waves turned irregular, and the Seaborn swarmed in rapture. Rather than dying, the nest struck by the weapon multiplied explosively, and the Hunters sank into a drowsiness they had long forgotten.
And the Beacon Tower at the center of the city had turned into a giant stone pillar of layered Seaborn tissue.

blocks.cap: Beacon Tower Square, turned into a nest.

blocks.x: Following the beacon signals, the nests on the continental shelf joined into one and expanded, with Milliarium at their center. Kal'tsit asked, "Did Ægir drop weapons into the nests to drive the Seaborn out, or a mass of catalysts?"

In the control room, Ulpianus decided to detach and sink the city unit holding the Beacon Tower, the way an injured seabeast bites off a poisoned limb. But the linkage mechanism would not move, and Jordi remembered Avitus peering into an abandoned Little Handy from the Institute of Facility Management.
Ulpianus said he would stay in the control room to confirm the separation himself. When Secunda asked whether he would come back to Ægir, he cut her off: a meaningless question.
Secunda knew Ægir would not remember his sacrifice, just as it would not remember Tullia's. She accepted his choice anyway. "I will grant you a minimum of trust."

Around then, at the Sophontheatrum, a Seaborn appeared before Kal'tsit, the Doctor, and Clementia and recited the Sophontheatrum's maxim in halting Ægirian. It was Mártus, the architect of the Sophontheatrum, who had vanished in the mantle ruins some two hundred years earlier. The Seaborn called Kal'tsit "AMa-10."
10. The City That Cast Away Its Heart

Meanwhile, Avitus blocked Cassia's way at the broken linkage mechanism. Cassia said that life is reason enough to live, condemned him for knowing what she was and doing nothing but watch the ruin unfold, and fled.

Facing the remaining Seaborn, Jordi lit a lantern with trembling hands and swung it, and pressed Avitus, who lay on the floor. Was it really Ægir's future that had disappointed his partner, or was it him?

blocks.cap: Jordi lights a lantern with trembling hands.

blocks.x: Does the fall of a civilization really weigh more than the collapse of a city, a family, or a single person?
While Irene rushed in to hold off the Seaborn, Jordi repaired the mechanism, and Avitus at last got to his feet and offered to help.
Meanwhile, at another linkage mechanism, Cassia was forcing the safety valve. Lucilla, who had once fled from the domes to the surface, held the other side with the poisonous grass still at her neck.
"Because there's no going back for me." Lucilla did not let go, and Cassia was paralyzed by a poison that took effect late.
Meanwhile, inside the hardening shell of the nest, the Hunters were sinking into Ishar-mla's song. They were woken by the Last Knight, who appeared with the cry of Rocinante.

Meanwhile, Gladiia, the first to return, told Ulpianus in the control room, moments from sinking, that this was his last chance to come back. When he refused, Gladiia leveled her spear. As his anchor flew, the building sank, and seawater and Seaborn flooded in.
Gladiia saw her old comrade before the dark holochart, waiting for the waves to swallow him.

At the Sophontheatrum, Clementia at last ordered the entire city to withdraw toward land, reconfigure itself, and hold back the Seaborn with gravity fields. Soon after, as Carmen watched from the Eye of Iberia, the city that had cast away its heart rose above the surface.

blocks.cap: The city broke through the surface, and it and the raging waves tore at each other.

blocks.x: 11. Without Survival, How Can You Speak of Civilization?

Meanwhile, at the Sophontheatrum, Mártus told Kal'tsit what he had seen. Some two hundred years earlier, in the deepest part of the mantle ruins, he had met an enormous Feranmut sleeping behind a transparent bulkhead.

blocks.cap: The colossal thing sleeping in the depths of the ruins.

blocks.x: When he laid his hand on the bulkhead, the fall of an ancient civilization swallowed him, and beyond it, an endless darkness without life or meaning. Trapped in its dream, the thing repeated a single word. Survival.
Mártus woke it: Ishar-mla. The Church of the Deep was never an organization. It was only a few people who had spoken with him sincerely and opened a way for the Seaborn to live.

He chose that path because of one small life. A young Seaborn born from Ishar-mla's body was licking his ankle, unaware of the ruin that awaited it. Humans weigh possibilities and are always a step behind fate. A life that moved on instinct alone, he believed, could bear the mission of survival.
Kal'tsit answered that he had given up thinking as a human long before he ate the flesh of another species. The doubt, worry, and anguish he had discarded were the most precious things of all.
Without civilization, how can you speak of survival?
Without survival, how can you speak of civilization?

Mártus recognized the Doctor, saying that the Doctor and their companions had sown seeds in the depths of the sea. He vanished, leaving word that he would wake the sleeping Firstborn and lead his kind to the moon.
Around then in Iberia, the lighthouses along the coastline, silent for over half a century, lit up all at once.

Meanwhile, beside the sinking Beacon Tower, Ulpianus saw small lives breaking away from the tower. The microscopic nanomachines that had died two hundred years ago before they were ever born had been reborn from the Seaborn, and were swimming away under their protection.

blocks.cap: A web of light spread across the surface like the Milky Way.

blocks.x: Billions of lights stretched from Milliarium into the depths of the sea. The route linking sea and land had opened. Bound together with We Many.
12. Under Ægir's Leadership
Some time later, communication with the homeland was restored, and Horatia, consul of the Institute of Scientific Development Planning, appeared as a hologram in the Pensivarium.

blocks.cap: "Whyever do you look so fatigued, my little Gladiia?"

blocks.x: She explained that the bio-energy poured out by the Seaborn had nurtured the nanomachines, and that by riding that flow of information, fleets and cities could cross the ocean in an instant. Gladiia pointed out that this meant living in symbiosis with the Seaborn for a long time to come.

When Horatia said Ægir would send its technology to the nations of the land to end their wars and settle their disputes, Kal'tsit answered firmly. "Compared to the Seaborn, you would be the more direct threat."

Around then, Irene arrived leading Iberian ships. When Secunda said light could separate the nanomachines from the Seaborn, Irene suggested using the relit lighthouses. All of them were the work of Breogan, who had hoped for sea and land to join hands and died alone.

Meanwhile, once the two were alone, Horatia told Clementia that even if the purge of the waters failed, the Waterway Program would succeed. Clementia replied that she did not doubt the route would open even if not one of the city's hundred thousand soldiers and civilians survived. Asked whether she was hiding something, she never answered.

At the same moment, on the eastern streets, Mártus appeared before Skadi. He had eaten His flesh and blood, and He dwelt within Skadi, so the two of them were bound by blood, he said. He wrapped her in a glowing umbilical cord.

blocks.cap: "You are not nutrients to complete the cycle. You are its end."

blocks.x: The Doctor's voice cut through the confusion. Skadi severed the cord, and Mártus left, saying he would wait at the endpoint of evolution.
I'm Skadi. Abyssal Hunter Skadi. Rhodes Island Operator Skadi. Always have been.
Epilogue. Those Who Parted Ways, Those Who Walked Along
Then Ægir made a declaration to every civilization on land: set aside prejudice and hatred, and build a line of defense together under Ægir's leadership.

Milliarium had held out for a week. Keeping Skadi's and the Doctor's secrets from Horatia, Clementia agreed with Gladiia to take over Hunter research in the name of the Legions, and agreed to guide Kal'tsit, who meant to find the Ægir homeland.

Meanwhile, on a seaside cliff, Avitus said goodbye to Jordi. The tribunal had not deemed him corrupted, but he could not forget what his silence had caused. He would join the deep-sea expeditions about to resume and set out into the unknown.

The child Cassia left in the incubation chamber would, if the city held, be born safely and raised at the Institute of Incubation. Avitus asked Jordi to come with him. "We have no need to prove where we belong."
Later, at the lighthouse, Carmen told Jordi that whether he left or stayed was his choice. Asked how he had been sleeping lately, Jordi answered, "A rather peaceful night, all things considered."
And in the deep sea, Ulpianus was pursuing Mártus. Facing the founder of the Church of the Deep, he said he would get his answers at the price of corruption.

blocks.cap: "Only a shadow may merge with a shadow."

blocks.x: Mártus said that if Ulpianus became a true member of the kind, he would gain every truth, but he would neither be able nor want to bring it back to Ægir. As had been the case for Mártus himself.
The Seaborn swam into the depths of the nest. Ulpianus followed.

The hunter in the song hesitated with home close at hand. The Hunters who came home stood on the battlefield again, and one Hunter turned his back on that home and descended into deeper sea, along a path no one will remember.

act33side.tagline: Theresa, King of Sarkaz, dreamed of 'Babel,' a tower that would rise above race and nation. This is the story of how she parted ways with her twin, Theresis, and how she died in the end, betrayed by someone she trusted. The prophecy had sung of a sword to slay the king.

chars.name: Theresa
chars.desc: The mixed-blood King of Sarkaz who built Kazdel. An idealist who founded 'Babel' to break down the walls between races and nations · Operator Civilight Eterna

chars.name: Theresis
chars.desc: Theresa's twin and her sword for life. The general who holds Kazdel's military power.

chars.name: Ascalon
chars.desc: A Sarkaz girl Theresis took in from the wastes during a storm. She grows up as his student and becomes an assassin.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: Co-founder of Babel, and a doctor. Theresa's old friend.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: A young Cautus who survived a convoy accident in Rim Billiton. She suffers from Oripathy.

chars.name: Manfred
chars.desc: A Sarkaz raised in a Military Commission institution. Theresis's student and Ascalon's childhood friend.

chars.name: Odda
chars.desc: Son of the mercenary 'Goodluck.' A young Sarkaz man born and raised in Kazdel.

chars.name: Goodluck
chars.desc: A Sarkaz mercenary who renamed himself 'Goodluck' after making it back alive from the Scar Market.

chars.name: Scareye
chars.desc: The Cyclops who rules the Scar Market. A mercenary broker who puts a price even on prophecy.

chars.name: Julie
chars.desc: A red-haired mercenary of the Scar Market. Weary of fighting, she chooses to stand with the King.

chars.name: Laqeramaline
chars.desc: Lord of the Banshee Court. A friend who has backed the twins for more than a hundred years.

chars.name: Nezzsalem
chars.desc: The Nachzehrer King. Leader of the old War Council and the twins' mentor.

chars.name: Duq'arael
chars.desc: The Sanguinarch of the Vampires. Acutely sensitive to blood.

chars.name: Confessarius
chars.desc: A Sarkaz who sided with Theresis. An old acquaintance of Theresa's.

chars.name: Savage
chars.desc: A Cautus from Rim Billiton who traveled with the Doctor.

chars.name: Mantra
chars.desc: Coordinator of Babel's covert operations squad. Instead of speaking aloud, she sends her voice into others' minds.

chars.name: Pith
chars.desc: A Babel Caster. An instructor who teaches Arts to the members.

chars.name: Logos
chars.desc: A Banshee who serves in Babel. A single word from him can shatter a city gate.

terms.name: Babel
terms.desc: The organization Theresa founded inside Kazdel. Its members gathered under the ideal of moving past race and nation to solve the Originium problem and Oripathy together.

terms.name: Military Commission
terms.desc: The governing body Theresis set up in place of the War Council. It strips the Royal Courts of their privileges and seeks to bind the Sarkaz into a single military force.

terms.name: Scar Market
terms.desc: The mercenary market beneath Kazdel. Commissions, information, even prophecies — anything can be traded for money.

terms.name: Black Crown
terms.desc: The symbol of power handed down through generations of Sarkaz Kings. It holds vast memories and the power to command Sarkaz souls.

terms.name: Civilight Eterna
terms.desc: The Doctor's name for the King's power. Passed down through every King before her, it is Originium Arts in their most fundamental form.

terms.name: Soul Furnace
terms.desc: The enormous furnace that drives the nomadic city of Kazdel. To the Sarkaz, it stands for home itself.

blocks.x: Summer, 1094. On a cliff outside an abandoned village in Kazdel, the mist of the assassin **Ascalon** wound around the throat of the giant **Scareye**. The Cyclops, who had long sold prophecy, spoke at the edge of death the ending of a song his people had seen a thousand years before. "A sword to slay the regent king, a spear to pierce the royal ring."

Around the same time, in Londinium, Victoria, the Regent **Theresis** gave the surviving deathmongers leave to take revenge for 'her.' And aboard the Rhodes Island landship, **Kal'tsit** ran down a long corridor, melting locked doors as she went.

In the Convallis of the Banshees a nameless elegy rang out, and an old friend's voice lingered in Kal'tsit's ears. "Keep going, Kal'tsit." It had all begun sixty-four years earlier, on the day **Theresa**, King of Sarkaz, and her twin the general set foot in the mercenaries' underground market.
1. Prophecy Is Worth Nothing

Autumn, 1030. Into the **Scar Market**, the mercenary market beneath Kazdel, walked the mixed-blood Sarkaz general Theresis, carrying nothing but a longsword. He looked at the slaves locked in cages, drew his blade, and told them he would take them to Kazdel whether they wanted it or not.

Meanwhile, in a back room, Theresa sat across from the Market's master, Scareye. The might of the great powers was already no different from that of the enemies the Sarkaz had barely beaten 130 years before. She had come to borrow the mercenaries' strength to build a **Military Commission** in place of the old Royal Courts.
When Theresa asked whether he had ever truly seen the future, Scareye sidestepped. Prophecy, he said, came with a price tag.
I have no need of prophecy. Prophecy and fate are worth nothing at all.

On the way back, Theresa spoke again of the dream she had held while designing the city with Kal'tsit: a 'tower' beyond the bounds of race and nation, where want and disease would be overcome together. **Babel**. Theresis dismissed it as a mere dream. Yet he added this.
I still cannot accept your vision. But I support your decision.

blocks.cap: The nomadic city of Kazdel. The Soul Furnace has burned for more than a hundred years.

blocks.x: Around then, one of the slaves freed from the Scar Market made it back to the city alive. Saying the General had spared his life, he changed his name to **Goodluck**, and walked home through the crowded streets he knew so well.
2. The Future the King Revealed

Autumn, 1031. The War Council became the Military Commission. **Laqeramaline**, Lord of the Banshee Court, offered her support but said she could send no troops. The twins' old mentor, the Nachzehrer King **Nezzsalem**, raised no objection.
The only dissent came from the vampire **Duq'arael**. Theresa then used the King's power to show everyone present the future that was coming.

blocks.cap: The vision the King revealed. Lingones vanishes from the map.

blocks.x: Order in Gaul was collapsing, and a war that would shake all of Terra was drawing near. Theresis added one more plan to this. They would plunder other nations, seize their deepest secrets, and from now on the Sarkaz would steer the fate of Terra.
Theresa did not object. That day, a letter arrived from the Lich Fremont. It held a single line of warning: do not place all your hopes for the future in one basket.
And Babel opened its doors. Kal'tsit invited colleagues of other races and founded a school. But those who had Babel in their sights turned their blades even on innocent people in the streets.
3. The Path the Storms Opened

Autumn, 1068. The Kurfürst of Wasserland in Leithanien found the wheel tracks Kazdel had left behind and sent a fleet after it. His envoy slipped into the Scar Market and put out a commission to destroy the city's power.

But Scareye dragged the Leithanian, bundle and all, before the Soul Furnace and threw him into the flames. He was betting that the subjects of the prophecy the Cyclopes had seen a thousand years before were the twins.

Then the city plunged at full speed into the Catastrophe, and the twins led their warriors out beyond the walls. In that procession, a boy raised in a Military Commission institution was holding the hand of a small child who had slipped out to find his parents.
The child's father was named Goodluck. When the two children pushed through the crowd shouting "Goodluck!", the adults turned and sighed as one. Good luck was what everyone needed on this journey.

At dusk, with the decisive battle drawing near, their retreat was cut off by two storms. Then, where the two storms collided, a long, narrow passage opened. The twins stepped into it shoulder to shoulder, and the warriors followed, holding up their wounded.

blocks.cap: In the middle of the path the storms opened, a cloaked child looks back at the procession.

blocks.x: In the storm, a girl who could barely speak pointed a stone knife at them. Theresis seized the blade bare-handed, then showed her this was how a knife should be held. The child hesitated for a moment, then laid the knife in his hand and asked him to take her with them.
The prophecy of 'a sword to slay the regent king' crossed both their minds, but they paid it no heed. The child was given the name Ascalon.
4. What Victory Left Behind

Ten days later, on the night the furnace burned again, the medical camp of a Leithanian-born Babel doctor went down in flames. The doctor's killer was Logan, a Sarkaz whose son the Leithanians had burned alive. Dragged before the King, he only repeated that they had won.

The guards had been put under Arts hypnosis, but Theresis said he could not investigate Sarkaz on account of one outsider. Babel's activities were narrowed to medicine, education, and science and technology.

And the children did not come back to Babel's classroom. Many of the casualties had been students, and the parents of those who survived said they would no longer leave their children with teachers of other races.

blocks.cap: Babel's classroom. When lessons began, the seats were still empty.

blocks.x: Into that empty classroom, the boy from the procession followed Theresis. He said he wanted to change but did not know what to change. His name was **Manfred**.

Meanwhile, Ascalon, newly come to the city, saw only people weeping and dying. Theresa treated the child's injured hand and let her touch her horns, and for the first time Ascalon spoke. "Warm, here."

Around the same time, Goodluck told his son only that his mother was badly hurt and needed rest. He passed his wife's name on to the boy, and left the city, saying he would make the ones who hurt her pay. The son's new name was **Odda**.
5. The Son Who Waited at the Door

Summer, 1086. Goodluck appeared at the Scar Market looking for a well-paid commission. The job was to deal with a teacher who took the side of Babel's other races. Tracking the target, he stopped short in front of his own home.

It was the house Odda had secretly lent out as a classroom. The 'Teacher' taught the children not to be fooled by grand words, and to think for themselves to find their answers. And at some point, Odda had begun to sit at the door every day, waiting for someone to come back.
When the Teacher and Odda stepped out the door together, Goodluck's hand froze. Even so, believing this was the only way to give his son a better future, he tightened his grip on his blade.
That blade was never swung. Ascalon's smoke, guarding Babel, passed over him. Goodluck's luck had run out, and death had caught up with him.

Manfred, who had been watching from hiding, stepped into Ascalon's path. The two had grown up together under Theresis. After their sparring, young Ascalon used to tie Manfred to a post and laugh that she had won.

blocks.cap: Young Ascalon and Manfred sparring, in the days when Their Highnesses watched from nearby.

blocks.x: In those days, Theresa had said that as long as there was even one teacher left to tell the children about the future, the flame of hope would never go out. Now Manfred asked whether telling a child who had lost his father to make peace with the killer would not be the crueler thing.
Ascalon answered that the moment mercenaries were used, she would not stand by, and vanished. That night, Manfred took Goodluck's belongings and knocked on the door of Odda's home.
Odda took the belongings and said he would no longer have to wait for his father. Outside the door, Manfred heard the sobbing that leaked out from within.
6. Babel Leaves the City

Not long after, the Teacher quarreled with a student's father and killed him by accident, then fell, surrounded by an angry crowd. The spreading unrest died down only when the outer wall of Babel's office collapsed under fire from an unknown source.

Odda ran to Babel carrying an injured child. Beside the Teacher, fallen in the street, sat a young Banshee hidden from view, singing an elegy. The Teacher said there were no regrets, for there was a child who would understand, and died within the song.
In the end, Theresa decided to take Babel and leave the city. Laqeramaline entrusted her own son to them and left a promise: whichever of them should perish, the Banshee Court would sing their elegy.
Before leaving, Ascalon went to Theresis and told him she opposed her teacher's will. Theresis asked whether she had any convictions of her own.
To protect? That is nothing but vague, empty self-deception.
