Ascalon knelt before him, then vanished as mist. All that remained in Theresis's hand was the stone knife the child had handed him in the storm.

The twins, too, exchanged their last words. When Theresis said that if this rift could not be mended he might have to kill her, Theresa answered that if he became the greatest threat to the idealists, she would bring him down as well.
Then Babel's column passed through the city gate in silence. When one of the mercenaries keeping order broke ranks to embrace a friend in the crowd, the endless procession came to a halt.

blocks.cap: Beside the ruined Babel office, the people and the city part ways.

blocks.x: Odda was in the column too. He remembered the day long ago when he had gone out beyond the walls to find his parents, holding the hand of the older boy from next door.
I believe there's another way besides war, Dad.
7. The One Who Woke in the Sarcophagus

Summer, 1090. Deep inside the Rhodes Island landship, Kal'tsit and Theresa opened an ancient door. The one who woke in the sarcophagus confirmed that the last record was dated 4,755,954 days ago, and recognized Kal'tsit, who had walked the land for more than ten thousand years to come back.
He asked them simply to call him Doctor. When the Doctor held out both hands, Theresa took them, and saw sorrow in the eyes of this person from the past.

blocks.cap: The first meeting of two civilizations. Theresa takes the hand of the one from the past.

blocks.x: Theresa showed him the lives of Terra held within the **Black Crown**. The Doctor called it beautiful, but said no one would understand a love that went beyond the limits of civilization, and that people would hate her for it instead.

If it was a path that had to be walked, Theresa answered, she would accept it. But when the Doctor said Originium had developed differently from what he had imagined, she asked Kal'tsit what the Sarkaz were originally meant to be.

The Doctor set out to see the land for himself. On the road he rescued **Amiya**, a young Cautus who had lost her parents in a Rim Billiton convoy accident and contracted Oripathy, and walked on with the child beside his traveling companion **Savage**.
When Amiya said that with stones growing in her body she had no future, and so could stay by his side, he answered that they would have a future.

blocks.cap: Atop a galloping burdenbeast, Amiya reaches out to the Doctor.

blocks.x: On the day he fell off a burdenbeast's back into a puddle, the Doctor wrote to Kal'tsit that on this land he had heard the sound of his own life welling up.
8. A Flower Field in the Heart of the Catastrophe
Autumn, 1091. The Doctor and Amiya arrived at Babel. Theresa came out to meet them and, holding the sleeping Amiya, said this was Amiya's home now. Kal'tsit told the Doctor, welcome back.
Later, Theresa took the Doctor to a wasteland struck by frequent Catastrophes. Among heaps of Originium crystals, in a spot where even the wind blew gently, lay a small field of white flowers.

blocks.cap: In the heart of the Catastrophe, a field of white flowers blooming on a nameless plain.

blocks.x: The flowers were Originium. After painstaking effort, Babel had turned a palm-sized piece of active Originium into flowers.
I want to see the day when an overflowing sea of flowers fills not only the cliffs and valleys of Kazdel, but the whole of the land.

She dreamed of a day when Catastrophes would bring clouds instead of crystals, and stones would no longer grow in the bodies of the Infected. When she suggested giving a new name to this flower, once called 'Snow-in-summer,' the Doctor could not answer.
A single sentence had surfaced in his mind. A new path is opening up. A path to self-destruction.
9. The Warriors Who Did Not Follow the King

The Duke of Cavendish of Victoria invited Theresis to his demesne. Theresa went to the Scar Market to keep Kazdel from being dragged into someone else's war again, and in her way stood the **Confessarius**, speaking for Theresis.
The Regent had already decided on the expedition. The Market's mercenaries lowered their weapons and bowed their heads, and in their eyes the King saw a strange city burning.

blocks.cap: The King walks alone among the bowed mercenaries.

blocks.x: Take good care of yourselves in a foreign land. Even if you can never return to Kazdel, my warriors.

But at the Market's secret entrance, the red-haired mercenary **Julie** called her back. She was sick of fighting, she said. Behind her, mercenaries bearing torches stepped out of the dark one by one, until they formed an endless procession.

Meanwhile, with Theresa away, some officers of the Military Commission attacked the landship. The Doctor, in command, broke through the encirclement with a small force, but felt dizzy looking at the stretchers in the blood-soaked corridors. The battlefield was not numbers.
Winter, 1091. Their Highnesses at last declared each other enemies. The peace Kazdel had kept for nearly two hundred years ended there.
10. The Procession Beneath the Catastrophe

In the civil war, Odda took up a hammer in Ascalon's unit. When he said revenge does not change everything, Ascalon asked what he would do if his father's killer were a deathmonger with hands soaked in blood.

Winter, 1092. Mercenaries of unknown employ attacked a Babel medical outpost and cut off the roads and bridges. Medical staff, Infected, and wounded, 2,500 in all, were trapped beneath a vast Catastrophe. Theresa made it clear that this operation was not a battle.
**Mantra** used her Arts to locate all 2,313 of them, and **Pith**, holding the blizzard frozen in midair, shouted at her students to make it back alive.
Meanwhile, where the Doctor arrived, Julie was about to end the suffering of the Infected who could no longer move. Then Theresa appeared without a sound and knelt beside them.
It's time to sleep, children of Kazdel. Rest easy in the warmth of home.
Theresa did not let go of their hands until the bodies of the Infected had turned to glittering dust and scattered into the snowstorm. The Doctor had never before seen the Infected die that way.

blocks.cap: Beneath the Catastrophe, where the Infected had been left behind.

blocks.x: The withdrawing procession passed through the very center of the Military Commission's encirclement, yet none of the Casters and snipers lying in ambush attacked it. No one gave such an order, either.
11. The Destroyer Who Woke as Savior
After returning, the Doctor drove an Originium crystal into his own arm. Blood flowed and pain followed, but no sign of infection appeared.

Originium did not infect him. He studied his own blood and greatly lowered the crystal density in Amiya's blood, but he would not stop even when Kal'tsit tried to restrain him, and three months later he collapsed on deck.
Theresa laid her hand on the unconscious Doctor's forehead, and saw his memories.

blocks.cap: Inside the Doctor's memories. Originium grows without end and covers the land.

blocks.x: The plan was to blanket the land in Originium and return everything to a vast sea of information. The voice in the memories said it was not extinction but continuance, but all Theresa felt was a suffocating terror.

Kal'tsit said that Originium had decided the distant future of this land, and that there had been two choices. The Doctor was the one who had chosen one of them, and the only thing that could change a future they did not want was Theresa's **Civilight Eterna**.

Around the same time, the Doctor left a record no one else could see. Could he give up a spark he had waited ten thousand years to hold, for the sake of a few short years of wonder? He asked himself again and again.
I... woke as their savior, but I am their destroyer.
12. Beneath the Statue of the Heroes
Winter, 1093. The Doctor secretly summoned Theresis to Kazdel's rain-soaked frontier. There stood the statue of the 'Heroes,' honoring the twins who had built the nomadic city of Kazdel.

blocks.cap: Beneath the statue of the twins, Theresis and the Doctor.

blocks.x: The Doctor had broken the Military Commission's codes long ago, yet had kept it from Theresa. He offered a technology to control Originium, and asked Theresis to bring Babel down and bring Theresa into his plan.
Theresis said that was nowhere near enough. To make Babel accept defeat and leave, their King had to be killed. Then, he said, he would not annihilate those who surrendered.

The Doctor answered that he would tip the scales of destiny. Theresis asked whether he was the only evil spirit of a bygone age, and when the answer was yes, he said the judgment of that evil spirit would be his to carry out.
Until there are none left to toy with the fate of the Sarkaz.

Early 1094. Theresis accepted the Victorian duke's humiliating terms and left for Londinium. On the night before he set out, Ascalon put her blade to Manfred's throat, then drew it back. Next time she would truly cut, she said, and that was all.

Back on the landship, Ascalon confided that the Doctor had become like a machine that never made mistakes, and that she trusted the one who used to tumble off burdenbeasts more than any fine commander.

Theresa said that now, with the Military Commission's main force gone, was a chance that would never come again. When Ascalon said she would stay by her side, Theresa answered that one day she would have to protect more people, farther away. Only years later did Ascalon realize that the strange feeling left in her chest after Theresa left was an unwillingness to part.
13. Countdown

Spring, 1094. Julie volunteered for the mission to infiltrate Theresis's army in Londinium and start a rebellion. Ascalon gave her an old garment on which Theresa had once embroidered her name. Julie asked what the land outside was like, but left without waiting for an answer.
Then, on the day of the operation to retake Kazdel, Odda was ambushed while clearing an abandoned village on the flank. As Ascalon moved to rescue him, Scareye blocked her way.
The giant said he wanted to test whether a Cyclops could steer a prophecy. Just as on that day, when he had used prey as bait to lure her tribe into the storm.

blocks.cap: The mask shatters. Two eyes, hidden for nearly a hundred years.

blocks.x: The mask broke on the tip of Ascalon's blade. Calling it a free prophecy, the giant recited the song from a thousand years before, and Ascalon sent him over the cliff.
Having survived the fall, the giant laughed that he had overturned the prophecy. But soon the very ambushers he had placed himself turned their weapons on him, and he died on the stage he had built.
At the same moment in Londinium, Julie's assassins stood before Theresis. He sent Manfred back and gave them their chance, telling them to try to kill him. Do not disappoint Theresa, he said.

In Kazdel, meanwhile, a single word from **Logos** shattered the city gate, and for the first time in years Babel's flag rose again over the site of the old Babel office. But contact with the landship had been cut, and when Logos sensed something ominous, Kal'tsit went cold all over.

At that moment, the Doctor stood before the landship's defense system. As he wavered between ten thousand years of waiting and the lives of Terra, a voice from the day he had parted with Kal'tsit, in the distant past, passed through his mind.
In the Speaker's Office, Theresa cried out his name. And the countdown reached zero.
14. Goodbye, Take Care
The assassins boarded the now-defenseless landship unopposed. When Amiya, woken by the noise, came to the Speaker's Office holding a picture book, Theresa put her to sleep inside black bubbles.

Assassins who had cut off their horns and cast away their names stormed in. They said they did not even deserve to be remembered. As she struck them down, Theresa called out each one's name and their deeds in the old war.
I do not want you to die nameless. At the very least... I will remember.
When the bubbles cleared, Amiya saw the white dress stained with blood. Theresa said she did not have the power to change the ending of the doll in the picture book, but Amiya might.

blocks.cap: Theresa passes the Black Crown to Amiya. "Do you want to rewrite the ending?"

blocks.x: Unable to find her voice, Amiya nodded urgently, and a black blade passed through the child's chest, carrying the crown over. What remained in her was not pain, but warmth.
Then the Doctor came in, and behind him, out of the darkness, assassins poured in. Without raising her head, Theresa said, "So that is your answer, Doctor..."
When Theresa had felled the last assassin, the Doctor told her he could not give up a ten-thousand-year chance. If only she would die, he said, he would see to it that no more lives were lost.
Theresa forced herself to her feet and touched the face beneath his mask. He was crying.
I... still believe in you, Doctor. In who you really are.
She unraveled the Doctor's memories strand by strand, turning them back into thread. They were the hands that, long ago, had learned to sew beside Theresis.
Find yourself.

blocks.cap: Just as on the day they first met, Theresa takes the Doctor's hand.

blocks.x: The memories would die, and the soul would be born again. This, Theresa said, was her little revenge on him, and her last gift.
As her breath grew faint, she heard an elegy from far away. It was Laqeramaline's promise.
And then Kal'tsit arrived.

blocks.cap: To the very end, Theresa held Amiya in her arms.

blocks.x: Just as Kal'tsit confirmed Theresa's death, Amiya's eyes opened. Theresa's consciousness, lingering in the crown, borrowed the child's body to bid Kal'tsit farewell.

She said she had killed the Doctor, and saved him too. Kal'tsit decided to send him to Chernobog in Ursus. Theresa left these words: the King is not a ruler but a key, and Amiya would become the flame that burns away all that has rotted.
Epilogue. Those Left Behind
Around then, on the bloodstained steps of Londinium, Theresis stood before his compatriots. You have lost your King, and I have lost my only family, he said, but I will let no sacrifice be in vain.

blocks.cap: On the steps of Londinium, Theresis proclaims a new beginning.

blocks.x: And Ascalon, returning too late, stood before Babel's door with no one there to greet her. She swore she would make everyone involved pay, even Theresis, who had been her teacher.
They were my... my only two... people...
The child brought out of the storm had, in the end, seen nothing but death.

Long before that, in the winter of 898, King Yliš died and the old Kazdel lay buried in ruins. Following the call of the Sarkaz souls, the twins walked to the place where a seamstress and a swordsman had first made their vow.

blocks.cap: 898, atop the ruins. The Black Crown chose both twins at once.

blocks.x: Theresis said he was not the one who would bring hope. His sword would clear the path ahead, and she would lead the way. Then he placed the crown on Theresa's head.
I swear this to every Sarkaz... We will always be equal.

And before her breath gave out, Theresa walked through the Doctor's fading memories. Among people celebrating a victory, she saw herself pass by in a white dress. And there was the Doctor, reaching for a child inside a wrecked transport, saying he would never let go.

At the end of the memories, someone once called the 'Oracle' was waiting for her. Learning that the one Kal'tsit had believed in had truly been him, Theresa let go of the last thread, and walked toward hope, toward death.
The song from a thousand years before sang of a sword to slay the king. But the last words the King left behind were not a prophecy. You have to keep going.

act32side.tagline: An Earth special forces team searching for missing comrades drops through the ceiling of a penthouse in a strange world, lands on a pile of golf balls, and ends up as bodyguards to an eccentric art dealer. And two giant dancers for a neighborhood that forgot how to dance.

blocks.x: Magnethill No. 2, in the southern Urals. Team Rainbow's squad leader **Ela**, decoy-device specialist **Iana**, field medic **Doc**, and demolitions expert **Fuze** have come looking for the missing **Ash** squad. But Dr. Levi's lab is already gone, vanished wholesale with nothing but a crater left behind. And then the ground starts to rumble again.
Meanwhile, in a penthouse in a seaside city, red-haired Vulpo art dealer **Reynell** is just about to set the final ball atop 'The Fall of Order,' a sculpture made from a mountain of golf balls.
That's when soldiers armed with crossbows kick the door in. The impact topples the piece, and golf balls go bouncing in every direction. His secretary **Miłosz** murmurs, deadpan: "...'The Fall'?"
And then the ceiling gives way, and four dark figures drop onto what's left of the golf-ball pile.
1. Landing Zone: A Kidnapping, a Pile of Golf Balls, and Terra

The ones who fell are, of course, Ela's team. Reynell calmly offers everyone a drink: "You'd better duke it out amongst yourselves to decide who gets to kidnap me." Meanwhile, a baffled Fuze wonders, "A furry kidnapping party?"

Team Rainbow wins the firefight handily, but something bugs Doc. An enemy who took a shotgun blast at point-blank range is alive and well, and the animal ears on his head even have visible blood vessels.
Out on the balcony, the team is greeted by a sunset sea, high-rises, and tourists in swimsuits. Fuze sums it up: "If this is the Urals, then I'm George Clooney."

blocks.cap: A resort city where the sunset paints the sea. A far cry from the Urals.

blocks.x: "Welcome to the dark heart of Bolívar, Dossoles," Reynell says, and informs them that this land is called, naturally, 'Terra.' A curse slips out of Ela's mouth, and of all things, it comes out in the language of Reynell's homeland, Kazimierz.
Meanwhile, Iana silently stares at the horizon. Opposite the setting sun, two moons are rising.
2. The 32nd Bodyguard to Quit

When Reynell offers them rooms as thanks for saving his life, Ela says they can't stay for free and offers to work as his bodyguards instead. Miłosz wraps things up by suggesting they draft the employment contract before HR leaves for the day, and just like that, an Earth special forces team becomes an art dealer's security detail.

Meanwhile, in the **Street Art Community**, a slum in Dossoles, the Durin girl **Tecno** is back from tagging a gallery wall and grinding her teeth at the TV alongside **Diaz**, whom she calls 'old man.' On screen, Reynell has just dismissed the residents' festival as "some amateur arts festival," and to top it off, his glass gallery, **Galería Krysztauowa**, is opening on the very day of the festival.

Around the same time, Captain **Mateo** of Bolívar's Coalition Government, who ordered Reynell's kidnapping, receives word that it failed. What he's after is the Street Art Community's land. To build an entertainment district there, someone has to be 'dealt with': either Reynell, who holds the development rights, or the residents.

Then one day, the 'secret meeting' on Reynell's schedule turns out to be bungee jumping. When Ela tries to talk him out of it, Reynell fires back, "As your employer, I advise you to advise less," and jumps. Exasperated, Ela throws herself into the void after him.

blocks.cap: The sea of Dossoles, as seen by Ela hanging upside down at the end of a rope.

blocks.x: Then comes a splash. Reynell has unhooked his safety harness and dropped into the water. Saying she can't protect a man who plays games with his own life, Ela quits on the spot.
Reynell leaves her with an unexpected remark. He has a goal he's been chasing for a long time, and **until he achieves it, he'll value his own life more than anyone in the world.**

Meanwhile, Miłosz goes to see Mateo and strikes a deal: if the terms are right, the Street Art Community's land will be handed over, so Mateo's side should take care of the residents who oppose the development.
Back at the gallery, Miłosz's report is short. "He took the bait." Then he sighs that Ela makes the 32nd bodyguard to quit after getting fed up with Reynell.

But when Ela, on her way out, tips him off that the sculpture in the exhibition room is a fake, Reynell bursts out laughing and confesses he made it himself. Ela is the first person ever to notice, and once he promises to behave, she decides to stay after all.
3. Fake Robbers and a Darkened Warehouse

Around then, Rhodes Island's **Tequila** and his colleague **Catapult** arrive in Tequila's hometown of Dossoles with a shipment of Oripathy suppressants for the Street Art Community. Mateo seizes the medicine by copying the outfits and tactics of the 'mercenaries' who showed up at Reynell's office that day, and deliberately leaves witnesses behind.

Meanwhile, Iana and Doc, still reeling from the culture shock of ads for horn-polishing whetstones and 10-liter bottles of conditioner made specially for Vulpo, Lupo, and Feline, are hunting for the Street Art Community with a festival flyer in hand when they find Tecno collapsed in an alley. Brought round by Doc's first aid, Tecno shows them the Originium crystals growing on her knee and asks, "Aren't you scared of this?"

But Diaz, having seen a news story about 'Reynell's four-person bodyguard team,' pegs the two of them as the medicine thieves, and residents swarm in with bows, crossbows, and staffs. While a double created by Iana's **Gemini Replicator** serves as a decoy, the pair slip away down an alley, where they run into Tecno, who points them the way out and plays dumb. "I was just taking out the trash, and I didn't see anything, got it?"

Meanwhile, Mateo learns that Tequila, who handled the delivery, is a candidate to succeed **Candela**, the mayor of Dossoles, so he decides to hide the medicine in a warehouse owned by Reynell and pin the theft on him. Tequila's group, holding cargo records from Candela's side, and Team Rainbow, acting on Miłosz's request, both converge on the same warehouse.

Tecno, who sneaked in first, knocks out the dozing watchman, but while sampling his coffee she spills it on the keyboard, and the 'Broadcasting' light flicks on. With a tango echoing through the darkened warehouse, Fuze gets knocked out cold by the 'kid's' kick, while Ela and Tequila, each trying to avoid the other, end up circling the same wall over and over.

blocks.cap: A tango drifting through the darkened warehouse. "Someday I'd love to take your hand again, at the next corner♪"

blocks.x: In the end, both sides are locked in a standoff, each holding one hostage from the other, when a carefree voice calls from outside. "Hey! Anybody home? Delivery's here!"
4. Giant Dancers for a Neighborhood That Forgot How to Dance

The misunderstanding gets cleared up with that delivery man's 'cooperation,' and Ela's team hands out the recovered medicine to the residents. The masterpiece Tecno shows them in her workshop is a pair of giant wooden puppets. When the two moons set and the sun rises, they'll dance through the whole neighborhood to announce the start of the festival.
But when asked whether the audience will dance along too, Tecno hesitates. Ever since a fire broke out at the dance hall years ago, nobody in this neighborhood has danced.

During that fire, the firefighter who defied the order to abandon the rescue and charged into the flames was Diaz. He couldn't save everyone, and the puppets were his idea: even if he can't dance with people himself, they can dance again.

Meanwhile, at an auction with no rival bidders, Reynell keeps raising his own paddle until he's driven the price of an antique music box up to 150 million. Then he asks Ela, who has moved her lodgings to the Street Art Community, to keep an eye on the festival for him.

Around the same time, Mateo gets chewed out by his superiors after someone strips that delivery man naked and dumps him at the base's front gate, and on top of that, Miłosz informs him that Ela's team will be stepping in from now on. "If I don't get that land, I'll kill him with my own hands!"

And Diaz calls Ela out to a windswept beach to give her a warning: if she betrays Tecno or makes her sad, he'll make her pay, even if it kills him. Ever since he pulled that girl out of the fire, she's been as good as his daughter.

blocks.cap: The beach Diaz cleaned up himself. The wind is so strong that no one has ever managed to develop it.

blocks.x: 5. A Rehearsal Eight Stories Up

Meanwhile, Doc has become the 'new doctor,' filling in for the neighborhood physician who died of Oripathy. Though he does crumble when he learns that it's not just little Ellie: the whole neighborhood calls the pastry she hands him a 'ker-sont.'

Then one of the puppet's arms gets tangled in cables high up, and the technician who knows its insides can't bring himself to climb again after the shock of slipping. Bound by a promise to Diaz, Tecno insists on going up the rope herself, and when Fuze asks why Ela cares so much, she answers.
What's wrong with delusions? All they have to do is pull off that impossible-looking challenge they set for themselves and make everyone's jaw drop.

Ela rappels down from an eighth-floor window to Tecno's side and fixes the hydraulic control unit, while Tecno grumbles but stays right beside her handing over tools to the very end. Iana and Fuze take care of the lookouts tailing them.

That night, under a sky with two moons, the first rehearsal begins. As the two puppets twirl round and round, an improvised, conductor-less performance spills out of the neighborhood's windows, rooftops, and alleys, and people dance along with the puppets.

blocks.cap: The Street Art Community gleams like a frozen lake in the moonlight. On it, people dance.

blocks.x: Watching from a window, Fuze shakes his head. "It was well worth it."
Reynell was looking at the same moons. What flowed out of the music box with its newly made cylinder was a simple lullaby, a tune Reynell's mother had written herself for her young son.
6. The Secret of the Opening Date

Once the rehearsal makes the news, the whole city is abuzz. Standing before a reporter, Tecno reveals that the festival date is the day of the fire several years ago, a day to remember the friends they lost.

Watching the broadcast, Reynell is too excited to sleep. The music box was originally a birthday present his mother had promised him, but his father would not allow a genius's work to sit at a child's bedside. It was a gift that took more than a decade to reach its owner.

Around then, Miłosz calls Ela aside and tells her about Reynell's father, **Szczepan**. Kazimierz's greatest art dealer, a man who brought artists to heel with threats and money, and who treated even his own wife that way. And the date of the opening ceremony is the anniversary of Reynell's mother's death.

When Ela turns down his request to postpone the festival by just one day, Miłosz offers a warning in the guise of advice: once the opening ceremony is underway, no one will pay any attention to the puppet performance.

blocks.cap: Galería Krysztauowa on the eve of its opening. At the end of the corridor hangs a giant portrait of Reynell's father.

blocks.x: When Miłosz returns, Reynell admits that the works in the Street Art Community catch his eye more. Still, he says, no work of art can make waves to compare with 'a magnificent death.'
Miłosz reports, matter-of-factly. **"The last of the explosives are in place."**
7. A Demolition Called a Fire Inspection

Around then, Mayor Candela receives word that Mateo plans to move on the Street Art Community by force, and lets it happen. It is a chance to be rid of a nuisance that never listened to city hall, without lifting a finger. At the same time, Tequila is tracking explosives that entered the city and vanished without a trace, and the trail leads him to Galería Krysztauowa.

Then, on the night before the festival, armed soldiers enter the Street Art Community and seal off the streets with barbed wire. The pretext is a routine fire inspection. Diaz tells Tecno to take the elderly and the children and get out.

Calling them a hazard, the soldiers rip out the puppets' wiring and knock down the workers who try to stop them. Puppets that took half a year to build are taken apart in front of the residents. All that remains are two heads, leaning against each other.

blocks.cap: The workshop in the Street Art Community where the puppets could be seen through the window. Soldiers haul everything out.

blocks.x: When the commanding officer tries to take even the storage drive holding the blueprints for the residents' works, Tecno, back with Ela's team, snatches it away. The officer throws her to the ground and stomps down on the fist clutching the drive.
The moment he raises his foot again, a red beam from the rooftop puts a dot on his forehead. "Try stomping her again." At Doc's warning, the soldiers withdraw. But their mission was already done.

As he treats Tecno's hand, Doc tells her that from now on, delicate work like writing or drawing may be difficult with her right hand. If only they had been one minute faster, Doc says, and trails off.
8. The Golf Ball Always Goes In the Hole

The next day, Ela storms into the penthouse, and Reynell tells her he never gave the order. He only wanted to watch the captain do something stupid and get what was coming to him from the people of the Street Art Community.

When Ela presses him, saying he has effectively set the leader of an armed group on unarmed civilians, Reynell says that if anyone needs someone to hold responsible, they can name him. Then he turns away and swings his golf club.

blocks.cap: A ball that looked set to go wide bends strangely in midair and is drawn into the hole.

blocks.x: A ball that always goes in, no matter how it is hit. When Ela asks if he has ever simply let a ball fly where it will, Reynell answers that it was a pointless, tiresome exercise. With a sigh, Ela tosses a ball of her own. It bounces a few times on the green, then slowly rolls into the hole.
And what greets Ela's team when they return to the Street Art Community is despair.

blocks.cap: A street once full of care and inspiration. Now nothing is left.

blocks.x: As agitators planted by Mateo urge the crowd to make Reynell and his secretary pay with their lives, it is Diaz who breaks the silence. "Get your things and follow me. We're going to that glass building." But the things to bring are not weapons. They are sound equipment and instruments.
If they don't want to see us dance, then we'll make it so they have no choice but to watch.

Meanwhile, Tequila, who has slipped into the gallery disguised as a new hire, finds explosives stacked to the ceiling at the end of a hidden passage. Up in the penthouse, Reynell asks Miłosz to sit beside him and wait for tomorrow together.
9. Terra's First Virtual Artwork, Modeled on 'El Capitán Molesto'

The opening ceremony was scheduled to run through the night until morning. Before an audience that includes nearly half the investors in Terra's art world, Reynell announces the 'Collector's Virtual Art Piece Project,' which puts replicas of artworks on an intercity network to be bought and sold. When they protest that it is blasphemy, he snaps back that they are the ones who have only ever read the money in a work, never its meaning.
And the first work unveiled is the likeness of the person who welcomed him to Dossoles so 'kindly and warmly.'

blocks.cap: Terra's first virtual artwork, 'El Capitán Molesto.' The model himself is in the audience.

blocks.x: In the audience, Mateo says nothing. He checks a message that has arrived on his terminal and stands up. Then, using a terror alert about an approaching mob as a pretext, he herds the entire audience inside the gallery and confines Reynell to the balcony.
Some time later, the people of the Street Art Community arrive singing, and are met by an empty plaza. Only coats were left on the seats.
There was not a single person there.
10. Two Attacks, Four Nodes

Around then, the commanding officer moving artworks inside the gallery breaks a vase, and an Originium bomb falls out of it. He begs Mateo to run while they still can. Mateo sends him back, and as he runs for the stairs, an arrow pierces his back. "There's no turning back for me. Or for you."

Meanwhile, out in the plaza, Catapult learns what is going on through a call from Tequila. The bombs were Reynell's, the hostage situation Mateo's: a terrorist 'collage' layered together without either knowing the other's plan. When Ela draws up a hostage rescue operation, Diaz, Tecno, and even the residents volunteer. "We're not firefighters. But we're thinking the same thing you are."

Fuze opens the operation. Hanging from a rope alongside Catapult, he plants cluster charges on the wall of Mateo's makeshift headquarters, and the blast spreads into the explosives store inside, sweeping away the defending troops.

blocks.cap: Adhesive cluster charges blow the bunker open. In Fuze's words, "It's that simple."

blocks.x: Meanwhile, in the security room upstairs, soldiers who have the horror film 'Panic at the Museum: The Sankta Slaughter' playing are growing terrified as the comrades they sent out on patrol vanish one by one. Then, in the middle of the room, a pale woman with a halo appears.

blocks.cap: Bullets pass straight through her. And so Iana's double becomes 'a Sankta killer who uses teleportation Arts.'

blocks.x: As the hostages escape, Miłosz appears before Ela. If she saves Reynell, he will give her the information on the bombs. If she fails, he will stay behind and go down with Reynell. The bombs are set to go off at 10 a.m., and stopping them means dealing with four nodes scattered throughout the gallery.

Diaz, assigned to the node on the sixth-floor stairwell, works the connectors loose as a firefighter, with the same hands that once installed them in his Singas army days. Just as he is turning the last wire, soldiers with drawn blades rush him.
11. The Balcony at 9:50

Dragged onto the balcony, Diaz tells Mateo it is over: he has lost both the hostages and the art trucks. Diaz offers to disarm the remaining node if they take off his cuffs, but Reynell is unbothered, saying even one remaining node is enough to bring the gallery down. "Do the lives of a handful of people really matter that much?"

Around then, the half-disarmed bomb on the sixth floor goes off, and the only staircase to the upper floors collapses. The time is 9:35. Left alone above the rubble, Ela tells her teammates, who try to stop her, "I trust you. And I trust myself," and heads for the top by herself.

Upstairs, soldiers with no way out surround Ela. At that moment, the wall behind her bursts open. It is the missing Ash squad: Ash, **Tachanka**, **Blitz**, and **Frost**. Ela calls their names one by one. "Cohen, Tina, Kötz, Alexsandr..."

At the same moment on the balcony, Diaz says he has found a place he truly thinks of as home. The people there are his family, and together there is nothing they cannot overcome. Asked whether he has anyone like that, Reynell answers. "I did... But when we were together, I only ever did what I wanted..."
9:50. When Mateo offers to spare him in exchange for the elevator key, Reynell replies that his only worry is that Mateo's filthy blood might stain the artwork. Mateo swings a golf club.

blocks.cap: "It's fine, Diaz... Let this sad little man throw his tantrum."

blocks.x: Even while coughing badly, Reynell mocks Mateo as an 'arrogant burdenbeast.' Just as the enraged Mateo raises the club over Reynell's head, the wall explodes and a flash engulfs the balcony.

blocks.cap: Burning scraps of paintings swirl like a silent fury. Ela walks out of the smoke.

blocks.x: "Three individuals on the balcony: Diaz González, Reynell Kowalski, and... one sad little clown."
12. The Man Who Took Off His Jetpack
The gliding jetpacks Blitz hands out include one for Reynell, too. Ela says she promised someone she would save this man if she got the chance.

But Reynell brings up the day of the bungee jump. Back then, he still had something left to do, so his life mattered. Now that it is all done, what is the harm in playing games with his life? The moment Ela pulls him along and they jump together, Reynell slips off the jetpack in midair.

As he slips from Ela's grasp and falls, a golf ball squeezes its way into his hand. Glowing like Arts, the ball draws in the golf balls around it to hold up his back, and Reynell lands in the swimming pool, borne on a mat of golf balls.

The moment he is out of the water, Reynell looks for Miłosz first, but Ela blocks his way. Is throwing away a chance to save his life supposed to be rebellion? If no one can understand it, what meaning does that art, that rebellion, even have? Has he ever thought about how to truly rebel against his father?
"Ms. Ela, you are probably the only one who still cares about such things." At Reynell's retort, Ela speaks in a low voice.

blocks.cap: "Right. About what an... awful jackass you are."

blocks.x: Ela shouts that Miłosz even told her about his mother to get her to help him, and that the young Reynell once took after his mother.
But if your own art means destroying other artists' work, or even their lives... isn't that just plain evil?
Would your mother have been proud? Reynell gives no answer, and Ela says, "Reynell, please... grow up." Then her fist lands squarely on his face.
Knocked back into the pool, Reynell feels the gaze of a blurry figure standing on the far side, beyond the morning sunlight. A gaze he cannot read, worry or sorrow, and it reminds him of his mother.

blocks.cap: Beyond the dazzling morning sunlight, someone is watching him.

blocks.x: That person quietly leaves. Reynell was still alone.
Epilogue. A Dance You Can Share with Anyone

The bombs were defused, and Mateo and Reynell were arrested. Then the artists' festival is held in the gallery. The central hall becomes a ballroom, and artists, former hostages, and the police who were called in all dance together.
Reynell approaches Diaz, who is tapping his foot alone in a corner. When Diaz remarks that Reynell's 'dance partner' is nowhere to be seen, Reynell asks where Diaz's own partner has gone.
If I want to dance, I can dance with anyone here. Anyone but you.

Later, Tequila visits the holding cell to tell Reynell that he is being sent back to his homeland under pressure from the Kazimierz General Chamber of Commerce. It was his father Szczepan's connections at work.
On the transfer contract for his remaining fixed assets, Reynell writes the name of someone who happens to be passing by. It is Diaz.
"Let a true lover of art have it."

Then, on a desert road toward Kazimierz, the Chamber of Commerce escort goes down, and the one knocking on the car window is Miłosz. When Reynell tells him to choose the destination this time, Miłosz suggests they go wherever the car takes them until the fuel runs out. When he adds that he might leave the moment his patience runs out, Reynell answers.
"But not today." "No. Not today."
Meanwhile, in the middle of Galería Krysztauowa's scorched exhibition hall, Diaz's barbecue restaurant has opened.

blocks.cap: Amid broken glass and graffiti, the grill heats up on a round table.

blocks.x: The reunited Ash squad has not yet found any lead on getting back to Earth either. When Fuze asks if they would mind a few more companions on the journey, Tachanka laughs. "The more the merrier!"
Outside the window, Tecno holds up her drawing. She says she has gotten used to drawing with her left hand now.

The golf-ball sculpture 'The Fall of Order' was never finished, and the greatest ruin Reynell had prepared never came to pass. Instead, in that gallery, a neighborhood that had forgotten how to dance is dancing again.

act31side.tagline: A young-lord Candleholder who can barely cut a handful of rice gets packed off to a granary city — and ends up watching a summer in which the 'teacher' who guarded that land for a thousand years is erased from everyone's memory. The flowers have bloomed; it's time to go home.

chars.name: Shu
chars.desc: A kind Shouye Tianshi who teaches farming in Dahuang. Always looking out for her younger siblings.

chars.name: Nian
chars.desc: Shu's younger sister and an eccentric smith. She's lending a hand with building the Twelve Pagodas and Five Cities.

chars.name: Dusk
chars.desc: Shu's younger sister, a painter who can freely come and go from the worlds inside her own paintings.

chars.name: Zuo Le
chars.desc: A Candleholder of the Sui Regulator. Sent to Dahuang on his father's orders to help out with the farm work.

chars.name: He Sheng
chars.desc: Shu's student, a young Nongye Tianshi researching Originium-resistant crops. · Operator Wanqing

chars.name: Grain Buds
chars.desc: A cheerful Dahuang girl who can talk with stockbeasts and loves playing her flute. Her given name is Xiaoman.

chars.name: Yun Qingping
chars.desc: A sickly Record Keeper who came to Dahuang with Zuo Le. He keeps records instead of training in martial arts. Grain Buds calls him 'Inkbrush.'

chars.name: Ning Ciqiu
chars.desc: A young Assistant Minister sent to Dahuang by the Ministry of Rites. Has no patience for beating around the bush.

chars.name: Assistant Minister Wan
chars.desc: The Ministry of Works' Assistant Minister in charge of building the Twelve Pagodas and Five Cities. Makes no secret of his ambition.

chars.name: Rong Wanqing
chars.desc: A seasoned administrator the people of Dahuang call 'Old Xiangzhang.' She and Shu go way back.

chars.name: Ji
chars.desc: Shu's younger brother, a Proxy. A merchant magnate who roams all over Yan and is under the Sui Regulator's watch.

chars.name: Wang
chars.desc: The second of the Sui's Proxies. Loves weiqi, and is a convict who broke out of prison in the capital 100 years ago.

terms.name: Dahuang
terms.desc: A vast granary region at Yan's northern edge. Precious land with little Originium contamination, steeped in the legend of Shennong.

terms.name: Twelve Pagodas and Five Cities
terms.desc: A colossal structure being raised at Dahuang's core. A national project the court is rushing as a pillar of national defense.

terms.name: Shennong
terms.desc: The legendary figure said to have first cultivated Dahuang's wastelands a thousand years ago. Every year on Xiazhi, the summer solstice, the 'Shennong Festival' welcomes her return.

terms.name: Candleholder
terms.desc: An office of the Sui Regulator that watches over and liaises with the Proxies.

terms.name: Sui Regulator
terms.desc: The Yan bureau that manages and monitors the Proxies.

terms.name: Proxy
terms.desc: Beings born from a part of the Feranmut 'Sui' who live like humans. Shu and her siblings are among them.

terms.name: Wanqing Project
terms.desc: Dahuang's long-running research into crops that can grow even in Originium-contaminated soil.

blocks.x: A woman is walking through the middle of a golden rice field. When a child asks why she's out looking for crops yet again, she answers: 'These alone can't fill everyone's bellies.'

blocks.cap: "From the ground we sprout, and when we die, it is to the ground we return."

blocks.x: The woman who wakes from that dream is **Shu**, a Shouye Tianshi of **Dahuang** at Yan's northern edge (Tianshis are Yan's scholar-technocrats). With little Originium contamination, this land became the nation's granary, and it's steeped in the legend of **Shennong**, who first tilled its wastelands a thousand years ago. These days a national project is in full swing: the fields are being moved onto mobile plates, and a colossal structure called the **Twelve Pagodas and Five Cities** is going up in the middle of the city.

There's another plan riding on that project. Shu and her two younger sisters, **Nian** and **Dusk** — three sisters, each a **Proxy** of the Sui — mean to build a Feranmut-like 'heart' into the Twelve Pagodas and Five Cities and make it a 'home' they can lean on.

blocks.cap: "...Nian, could you help pull me out?"

blocks.x: 1. The Young Lord Candleholder Becomes a Scarecrow

**Zuo Le**, a **Candleholder** of the Sui Regulator, slipped up and turned in a written self-criticism to boot — but all his father Zuo Xuanliao gave him in return was an order: go to Dahuang and help with the spring planting. When he asked what exactly he was supposed to do there, he got two lines and nothing more.
See much. ...Think much.

In Dahuang, Zuo Le dutifully recites the Sui Regulator's request that Shu not leave the area for the time being, and Shu fires back with 'So, did you just come of age this year?' He spends whole days standing ramrod-straight and doing nothing but keeping watch, until a cheerful girl named **Grain Buds** hands him a lunch box, laughs that he looks like a scarecrow, and adds: 'But you're not planning to eat this for free, are you?'

And so the young lord, who can't work a rice transplanter or a Sky Pole (a farming drone), gets passed off as 'a distant relative from the capital' and starts out as the new guy under Shu's student, the young Nongye Tianshi **He Sheng**. Grain Buds, riffing on 'Candleholder,' dubs him 'Candlestick.'
A few months go by like that. Giant machines lift whole fields into the air, and Dahuang changes by the day.

blocks.cap: A nomadic city in the middle of 'growing up.' A new world for a new generation of Dahuang folk.

blocks.x: The seasoned administrator the farmers call '**Old Xiangzhang**' laughs that the shape of the land may change, but home stays right where it is. Still, a farmer born and raised here wonders aloud: what would Shennong think if she knew we'd moved the land?

Meanwhile, Zuo Le is still sweating buckets in the paddies. He's got plenty of arm strength but no idea how to use it, so after ages of swinging a sickle he has exactly one handful of rice to show for it — and the official robes he hung on a post have become a toy for the fowlbeasts.

blocks.cap: It's already lunchtime, and there's still this much left.

blocks.x: 2. The Mianmian Search Party Chases a Shooting Star

That day, Grain Buds dragged He Sheng and Zuo Le out to find Mianmian, a stockbeast that had gone missing. Grain Buds can talk with stockbeasts, and He Sheng — whom she calls 'Big Buffalo' — is a workaholic who knows nothing but farming.

The search somehow turned into fighting a wildfire (blame a student who tried to get revenge by roasting the eggs of the fowlbeast that ate their assignment). Zuo Le came back from the brush cradling two wild newborns that hadn't even opened their eyes yet, and got told off by He Sheng to think before he acts. As for Grain Buds, she tried to get close to the mute lumberjack who lives alone in the riverside woods — and got whacked and chased off.

That evening in the lab, He Sheng handed over the **Wanqing Project**'s report card. Even hearing that they'd been stuck at the wall of 25% Originium activity in the soil for several seasons running, Shu didn't get impatient.
Fifteen percent. That 'nearly impossible barrier' you're talking about was fifteen percent, twenty-five years ago.
That night, over the restorative soup Shu had made, Old Xiangzhang made it clear that only one person worries her: Shu's 'younger brother.' 'That man should not have come back now, of all times.'

Out in the fields, meanwhile, Grain Buds gave Zuo Le a bracelet braided from Mianmian's fur. When he admitted he didn't know what he was supposed to learn here, she laughed and told him her parents work far away as Tianshis too. Though nobody will tell her why she never hears from them.

blocks.cap: They say a good harvest comes wherever a shooting star falls.

blocks.x: If Mianmian fell at the end of the sky, Grain Buds will search to the end of the sky — even if it takes until they're both old and gray. **Yun Qingping**, the sickly Record Keeper who came along with Zuo Le, whispers to him that this might be exactly what he's meant to find. Tomorrow is Xiazhi, the summer solstice — the day of the Shennong Festival.
3. The Shennong Festival — A Handful of Seeds, Twelve Drumbeats

Watching the Shennong Festival play, He Sheng explained: Shennong died heading north in search of new seeds. Her remains never came home — only her basket and a pouch of rice seeds, which became her grave.

Around then, Zuo Le dug up one line in the Sui Regulator's records. Sixth of the Proxies, Shu — laid out the twenty-four jieqi, appeared in Dahuang during a great famine, and has stayed for a thousand years.

Shu, for her part, visited the riverside woods and gave the silent lumberjack cookies and fruit. When she said, 'We... couldn't protect any of it in the end,' he covered his face and sobbed. Grain Buds, who'd tagged along in secret, brought up a dream she'd had many times: droughts and floods, strange things drifting over from across the river, granaries scraped bare.

Over at the altar, the farmers each took a few seeds from their pockets and added them to the pile of grain. Wine brewed from this grain is shared at the next year's Shennong Festival — that's Dahuang's cycle. Zuo Le bowed too, praying for kind winds and timely rain in Dahuang and for peace in Yan, year after year.
At noon, the twelfth drumbeat sounded, and everyone shouted: 'Harvest time!'

blocks.cap: Amid firecrackers and cheers, the harvesters roll out into the golden fields.

blocks.x: But then summer thunder rumbled out of a clear sky, and rain poured from ink-black clouds. And right in the middle of a paddy, a small piece of Originium bloomed like a flower.
4. Moving the Plates to Turn the Flood

Originium shards washed down from upstream smashed the sluice gates, the dam gave way, and contaminated mud surged into the paddies. He Sheng grabbed Zuo Le just as he was about to throw himself into the breach, shoved a map into his hands, and told him to get people evacuated. 'Who do you think you are, that the people here need your protection?'

He Sheng's plan was to move the unfinished mobile plates and reroute the water itself. When a Tumu Tianshi hesitated, citing a lack of authority, he fired off orders using nothing but the map of the fields in his head. 'Plate A-9, five tiles east! Plate B-8, down five levels!'

Nian charged out of the factory and held the levee, and Dusk's paintings caught the stockbeasts about to tumble off the edge of a plate. Finally, Shu whispered, 'Scatter,' and the flood split into thin streams that ran off along the canals.

Afterward, in the meeting room, Old Xiangzhang — who wanted to slow construction and send the Tianshis to restore the farmland — squared off against the Ministry of Works' **Assistant Minister Wan**, who kept citing national defense. Here's what Old Xiangzhang told him:
Losing a thousandth of the food doesn't mean prices go up by a thousandth. It means a thousandth of the people go hungry.

When **Ning Ciqiu**, a young official sent by the Ministry of Rites, cut in to take responsibility, Old Xiangzhang snatched even that away, telling them to record it as her having forced the decision by threatening their lives. Assistant Minister Wan sighed and backed down. '...Well, at least the Ministry of Works is off the hook.'
A few days later, in a paddy where the flood had bowed every last stalk, Grain Buds found a single plant standing stiffly upright. Its ears were red — practically blood-red.

blocks.cap: A brilliant ear standing alone, as if it had drunk up all the life around it.

blocks.x: Around then, as Shu helped the fallen rice back up, she remembered someone from long ago. Someone with a mud-smeared face who said that if you keep going, one year at a time, you'll see results — someone who wasn't yet called 'Shennong.'
Just then, a caravan rolled up in a cloud of dust, and from the lead vehicle stepped a man in gorgeous, immaculate clothes.

blocks.cap: "Long time no see. My dear sister."

blocks.x: 5. Anything for Sale

The man was the younger brother who'd been sending Shu letters for ages. Once a boy who loved raising silkworms and followed Shu around everywhere, he's now a merchant magnate the Sui Regulator keeps a close eye on. Dusk says she hates that murky look in his eyes, and Nian chimes in that he's just like their jailbreaking second brother, the weiqi failure.

Meanwhile, huge machines rolled into the contaminated paddies. The one who pressed the switch to plow the crops under was Zuo Le — and the field was the corn test plot He Sheng had first been put in charge of.

blocks.cap: The fields after the storm. Every crop has to be thrown out.

blocks.x: Before long, the higher-ups decided to give up on the outer farmland and prioritize the core. Fistfights broke out between the Tumu Tianshis bulldozing the land and the farmers, and one Tumu Tianshi left with a parting shot: honestly, a place like Dahuang isn't strictly necessary.

While scolding a dejected He Sheng, Grain Buds stepped right on that man, who'd been napping among the rice. Calling himself a merchant, he offered to sell her a wish as payment for giving him directions. Grain Buds wished for a good harvest and peace in Dahuang, and tried to offer 'that song' as the price — the one she'd made for He Sheng on his exam day three years ago. But He Sheng asked what song she meant.
Grain Buds snapped 'You stupid buffalo!', paid the price by playing her flute on her own, and stormed off. Half-joking, He Sheng asked: can you sell a dream of feeding everyone, too?
Yes, that's possible. ...What can you pay to buy that grand ideal of yours?

That's when Zuo Le recognized the man and called him out. A Proxy on the Sui Regulator's watch list: Shu's younger brother, **Ji**. Rattling off even the suspicions about Zuo Le from his Yumen days, Ji casually asks whether he knows how many Tianshis the Chamber of Heaven's Designs — which holds back the demons north of Dahuang — has lost in the past three months, then suggests a deal.
6. Something from Across the River

From that day on, strange things kept happening. While searching for Mianmian, Grain Buds heard a stockbeast's voice — it was scared here, it said; that thing came from across the river; look beneath your feet. Then the lumberjack spoke for the first time, offering to take her to the stockbeast, and led her down to the riverbank.

Wading into the river as if in a trance, Grain Buds saw a memory that wasn't hers: a man clinging to 'Zushi,' howling that she could still be saved, and a voice saying it was too late, that they should raise a gravestone for her.

Just then, a shout of 'You idiot! Where are you going?!' and a flying clump of mud snapped her out of it. The shouter was a little Tianshi apprentice who skips school all the time — the one Grain Buds calls 'Megaphone.'

Megaphone promptly yanked out the red rice Grain Buds had found and told her that if she ever spotted anything like it again, she should quietly call for her and nobody else. When Grain Buds asked her to find out about her parents, Megaphone flared up, then trailed off, saying that when it was time for them to come back, someone would bring them.

Meanwhile, in a hallucination, He Sheng tilled a field with a hoe handed to him by a faceless farmer. The rice only grew and withered without ever leaving seed, and his hair went white. Zuo Le woke him up — and the moment he heard about the 'dark-red rice' from Grain Buds, he shouted that they had to check the granary first.

Ji, for his part, offered to take over Shu's job of breathing life into the 'heart' — and Nian turned him down flat. When Zuo Le set off alone after Ji, Dusk handed him a painting, saying it might hold Ji in place for at least a little while.

And in front of the Shennong Shrine, Ji grumbles that he doesn't like the Shennong statue. Shennong always wore a flower in her hair and liked wearing the clothes he made, he says, and her eyes looked like his sister's.

blocks.cap: The Shennong Shrine and the opera stage.

blocks.x: Ji pressed Shu hard: entrusting her life to that thing Nian built isn't a fair deal, and she must be so worn out that she failed to notice this sooner. Asked whether he had nothing to do with this disaster, Ji answered, 'When have I ever lied?' and Shu replied, 'You just never tell the truth.' He urged her to leave with him, but Shu said she would stay.
7. Rain

Long, long ago, on a day when the spring wind was still cold, an old woman set out for the north to find crops that could grow even in Originium-contaminated soil. When Shu tried to stop her, she tucked the year's first white flower into Shu's hair and told her she'd be back around harvest time — so make some restorative soup and wait for her.

blocks.cap: The day she left for the north. "Will that Ten Thousand Qing of Fertile Fields come true in the end?"

blocks.x: And now, the water in Dahuang's paddies drained into the earth in an instant, and the fields cracked into hard salt flats. The summer harvest in the granary had all turned dark red, too.

At the same moment, Zuo Le trapped Ji, who was about to leave, inside Dusk's painting and leveled his blade at him. Ji calmly laid out his calculations: why Yan wants to get rid of the Sui now, of all times; how to weigh the lives of siblings who have protected Yan for centuries.
Where is there any 'god'? In the end, we are all only human. Why won't you look beneath your own feet?

He Sheng, meanwhile, found that the source of the contamination lay underground, but Old Xiangzhang told him it had been decided: everyone would move to the core and head east, and the rest of the land would be abandoned. He Sheng did not back down. 'If Shennong could drive the enemy out of her home, so can we.'

Long ago, once more. When the old woman came back from the golden fields of the far north holding a single ear of rice, a farmer screamed at the sight of her. She collapsed on the cold ground, and before her, all Shu could do was ask that she be buried well. The farmers took the packet of seeds from her pocket, believing they were the seeds of legend.

A Tianshi of the Chamber brought Nian the same finding: the contamination beneath this land existed long before the Chamber of Heaven's Designs was ever founded. Nian murmured that her elder sister might have endured those thousand years alone.

That night, Old Xiangzhang remembered forty years ago. Back then she was a young Sui Regulator official, and when she demanded to know why Shu only watched when she had the power to help, Shu answered that if she helped, people would only wait for 'divine miracles' — and that one day, she would be gone.
And today, Old Xiangzhang went to ask Shu for her help, just this once. The room was empty. On the table sat a single bowl of soup, still warm.
It began to rain.

blocks.cap: Someone walks deep into the fields. Green sprouts wherever they step.

blocks.x: That figure vanished with the summer lightning. A fine, gentle rain filled the cracks in the earth, the grain regained its true color, and the soul bound here for a thousand years disappeared. As the painting faded away like spreading ink, Ji spoke to no one.
My dear sister... these people can do nothing without you. Rest a little now.
In the fields, the farmers choked up, saying Shennong had returned. And when Zuo Le came to and asked where Lady Shu was, He Sheng tilted his head. 'Who... did you say?'
8. The Heart Begins to Beat

With Shu gone, Dusk confronted Ji, but he shot back: wasn't it 'humans' who had bound her to this land for a thousand years? Then, before Nian could stop him, Ji floated a black seed in his palm and placed rice inside the unfinished device — and the heart began to beat.
At dawn the next day, swarms of out-of-control Sky Poles swept overhead, and half the sun turned blood-red.

blocks.cap: This land was no longer the home they knew.

blocks.x: Monsters like scraps of cloth crawled out of the ground, and crops withered wherever they passed. When the Twelve Pagodas and Five Cities at the city's center began giving off an ominous light, Zuo Le once again set out alone to stop the device, and He Sheng blocked his way. 'Who said anyone wants your life?'

Then Old Xiangzhang appeared, and Zuo Le recognized her: **Rong Wanqing**, the Sui Regulator legend who brought the Shanhaizhong to heel and saw through a convict's schemes. She told them that Shu had given her life to purify the demon underground, that Ji had used a piece of the demon to force the core awake, and that the monsters were the demon's shadows, growing stronger by feeding on fear.
Light the lamps, and leave behind even the faintest light. Do not forget.

Around then, in the factory, Assistant Minister Wan — who had accepted Ji's deal — stayed behind alone, holding the runaway core in check. Coughing up blood, he roared, 'You all underestimated me, Wan Qincheng!' And the monsters in the fields suddenly stopped.

In that lull, Grain Buds poured it all out to He Sheng: that she was actually scared, that he was the smartest person she'd ever met, that he shouldn't think nobody cares about him just because he has no family. Then she blurted out, 'If only Sister Shu were here.' He Sheng asked who that was — and Grain Buds, without knowing it herself, still remembered the name.
Saying the mute man by the river must still be out there, Grain Buds ran off, leaving only a promise to meet again in the central district.
9. The Flowers Have Bloomed — Time to Go Home

In the riverside woods, the lumberjack was fighting the monsters alone. The one he had loved was gone, and had never gotten to see the coming spring. For him, Grain Buds played the only song he had ever liked on her flute: 'Come Home Soon, Little Flower.'
The flowers have bloomed; it's time to come home. Listen, listen — it's me calling for you.

Cornered by monsters and screaming, Grain Buds still raised her flute to her lips once more, and when the lumberjack finally turned back, a small white hand took his. The red silk cord tied around his arm came loose and flew up into the sky, and Grain Buds never saw the tears running from his clouded eyes.

When Grain Buds, helping the wounded man along, finally collapsed, the lumberjack took up his axe again. A golden child stepped in front of him, and haltingly he called her 'Zushi.' Megaphone was the head of the Chamber of Heaven's Designs — the 'Old Tianshi.'
Go back. You have such a clever daughter — we can't let her lose both her parents, can we? ...Even if she doesn't recognize you.

On the defensive line, the farmers faced the monsters with hoes and stones. The monsters turned out to be the very pests that had always ravaged the fields, transformed, and a song from the Shennong Festival play, begun by someone, spread along the whole line.

Elsewhere, on the way to rescue stranded farmers, Zuo Le revealed that He Sheng was actually a year younger than him, and for the first time spoke to him plainly, without formalities. 'He Sheng, it's dangerous. Don't push yourself.' He carried the farmers one by one across the widening gaps between the plates, but when only the two of them were left, the gap had become a bottomless cliff, and blood was spreading across He Sheng's white clothes.

He Sheng tied his device, which held his experimental data, to Zuo Le's hand, turned it into a kite, and with the last of his strength raised a wind to send Zuo Le flying. 'You're actually a good guy.' As He Sheng receded into the distance, a monster lunged at him.
He Sheng opened his eyes in the fields. While everyone was out searching for him, it was Mianmian who carried him back on his back.

blocks.cap: The blood-red sunset fades, and the evening sun fills the fields with gold once more.

blocks.x: On the way back, in the Wanqing test plot, He Sheng found a single stalk of rice standing tall on the ravaged land. The boy hugged it and laughed, almost madly. 'The Ten Thousand Qing of Fertile Fields... there's hope. Now there's hope!'
10. Four Seasons Inside the Heart

Around then, Shu, held captive inside the heart, came face to face with a faint figure of Shennong. Shennong blamed herself, saying those thousand years had been not devotion but bondage; Shu answered that the only one she resented was herself, for not going north in her place. This Shennong was a fragment of memory held by what remained of Shu's consciousness inside the device.
What came next was chaos. A consciousness crushed under memories of war, plague and famine called itself 'Sui' and bore down on her, saying 'I am you' — and the fields were overrun with weeds.

blocks.cap: The moment eternal night set hard.

blocks.x: You're afraid. You've never truly lived, so you don't know what this land is really like. The world isn't something to be afraid of.

Nian and Dusk, held captive alongside her, each found an answer before their own visions: that having left something behind made her glad, and that was enough; that I am I, and what I see is all things.
Old thing, we didn't claw our way out of that pitch-black tomb just to live under your shadow.

Meanwhile, Zuo Le, having chased Ji to the very end, was met by silk pouring down from the sky. A cloth on which Ji had embroidered the Hundred Scenic Portraits of Great Yan, traveling from city to city and using the nation's 'splendor' as his dye — and the final piece was Dahuang.

blocks.cap: "How could I ever dislike this world?"

blocks.x: Freed from the heart, Nian and Dusk were still no match for Ji's silk — and just then, Shu appeared. Laying hands on your younger sisters is mean, she said, and after sixty-seven years he should at least stay for a meal. Then she called out the one who had been hiding: the weiqi failure, **Wang**.

Long ago, Wang had confided in Shu that he would return to the Sui's body, kill It and become It, and use that power to create a 'great windfall' for all living things. Shu's answer was a handful of seeds dropped onto the weiqi board: if he hasn't lost his way, they'll sprout when the time comes and bear the fruit he wanted.

Shu did not stop Ji. 'If you have any regrets left, come back alive.' Even when the Old Tianshi burst in late, flames blazing, Wang held her in place by asking whether she could really leave the northern defense line empty, and vanished.

Around then, in the factory, a hazy woman sat beside the fallen Assistant Minister Wan. His dream had been to build a city where no one is left out in the wind and rain — and the woman said she would take that dream instead of the life he had offered.
And Rong Wanqing, waking up in the fields, thanked a Nongye Tianshi who happened to pass by, then said softly to her retreating back: 'Goodbye, Shu. It's time you were free, too.'

In the lab, as He Sheng moved the surviving rice into an incubator, an unfamiliar teacher appeared before him as well. Not recognizing her, he said in an excited voice that he would devote everything to this rice.
Don't worry. I'm sure you'll reach the goal you're after. ...Goodbye.
'That teacher just now... somehow she seemed familiar...'

And Ji, about to set off for Baizao, was caught by the Old Tianshi. He confessed that his sister had been killed either way, and that certain people hiding in the shadows of the court had to pay for it. When he said a price had already been put on his own life too, the Old Tianshi let him go.
Epilogue — Each to Their Own Cycle

Outside the capital, the Grand Commandant calmly admitted to the Grand Tutor that he was also the one who had egged on the Shanhaizhong at Yumen. And Zuo Le received notice of his reinstatement. No longer afraid, now that he knows the Proxies have a human side, he heads for his next posting: Rhodes Island.

Not long after, He Sheng sets out for cultivation bases across the country with seeds of a new, highly resistant strain. Getting accurate results will take at least ten generations — ten years. Grain Buds saw him off playing her flute, and the sunset followed the two of them in their footsteps.
Dusk, for her part, painted pictures for her siblings, then set down her brush. '...Because of you all, I was never lonely.'

blocks.cap: Clothes of the Hundred Scenic Portraits. "It fits perfectly."

blocks.x: And Wang, trying on the clothes Ji had made, said they fit perfectly. The game will be decided by half a point — in life or in death.
Long, long ago in Dahuang, Ji was all excited about making his sister new winter clothes.

blocks.cap: "My dear sister, shall I make you some new clothes?"

blocks.x: Is this what 'human' life is like? It's... rather pleasant.
'It is,' Shu answered. You're already living it, after all.

And the elderly merchant who had raised Ji to be a merchant said his own road ended here, and passed down his lifelong creed: the people of the world flock together for profit. Then he added one more thing.
But if this world could be explained by 'profit' alone, it would be truly dull.
Asked to go and see, in the old man's place, whether there truly exists a 'great windfall' that benefits everyone, Ji answered that he would remember.

Spring rain wakes the sprouts, summer ripens the ears, autumn brings frost and winter brings snow. He Sheng no longer remembers that name, but the next cycle begins from the single stalk of rice he held in his arms — from one patch of green that someone planted over a thousand years.

act30side.tagline: A girl clutching her mother's 'remains' comes looking for a father whose face she's never seen, and, caught between a Victorian army that swears it's only sightseeing and a secret buried under a statue, hands him a bill for child support. And out on the ice: one against two thousand.

chars.name: Leto
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator whose real name is Rosalind. She came to Kjerag alone, carrying a box her mother entrusted to her

chars.name: Harold
chars.desc: A viscount from Victoria. He showed up with an army, insists they're all tourists, and has spent the past month treating Kjerag's burdenbeasts

chars.name: Degenbrecher
chars.desc: The 'Black Knight,' three-time consecutive champion of Kazimierz's knight competitions. Now with Karlan Trade, she lives in Kjerag

chars.name: Enciodes
chars.desc: Head of Clan Silverash, who runs Karlan Trade · Operator SilverAsh

chars.name: Enya
chars.desc: Kjerag's Saintess, who serves Kjeragandr · Operator Pramanix

chars.name: Kjarr
chars.desc: Head handmaiden to the Saintess Enya. She is not at all happy with the face on the new Kjeragandr statue · Operator Kjera

chars.name: Gnosis
chars.desc: Karlan Trade's chief technical executive. Cool-headed and meticulous

chars.name: Arctosz
chars.desc: Current head of Kjerag's Clan Paleroche. A big-hearted, hot-blooded lover of drink

chars.name: Elder Devotee
chars.desc: The old devotee who taught Leto how to pray in front of the Kjeragandr statue. He offers her a place to stay

chars.name: Tatyana
chars.desc: Leto's mother. Originally from Ursus, she loves exploring and anything new

chars.name: Sciurus
chars.desc: Younger sister of the head of Clan Browntail. A cheerful troublemaker who serves as a national envoy

chars.name: Ratatos
chars.desc: Head of Clan Browntail and Sciurus's older sister. She has a sharp eye for which way the political winds are blowing

chars.name: Trilby Asher
chars.desc: A spy working for a Victorian Duke. He goes around investigating Kjerag with his identity hidden

chars.name: Muelsyse
chars.desc: A lead researcher at Columbia's Rhine Lab

terms.name: Kjeragandr
terms.desc: The guardian deity of this land, worshipped by the people of Kjerag. Her existence has never been confirmed, but to the faithful She is unshakable belief itself

terms.name: Lake Silberneherze
terms.desc: A lake said to be Kjeragandr's first tear. The newly completed statue of Kjeragandr stands on its central island

terms.name: Karlan Trade
terms.desc: The Kjerag trading company Enciodes founded after returning from Victoria. It sits at the center of Kjerag's development, from mines to railways

terms.name: Vine-Bead Court
terms.desc: Kjerag's religious and administrative advisory body, centered on the Saintess

terms.name: Clan Paleroche
terms.desc: One of the three clans that have long upheld Kjerag. A conservative clan that has been in charge of faith and protection

terms.name: Clan Browntail
terms.desc: One of the three clans that have long upheld Kjerag. Skilled at politics and at getting along in the world

blocks.x: Winter, 1100, in Kjerag, the land of eternal snow. A 30-meter statue of **Kjeragandr** has just been completed on the island in the middle of Lake Silberneherze, and in two days, the Saintess **Enya** will personally preside over its unveiling ceremony.

blocks.cap: The Kjeragandr statue at Lake Silberneherze. It's set to become Kjerag's most eye-catching symbol.

blocks.x: The problem is the two thousand Victorian soldiers who've come to 'celebrate' it. They've been camped at the foot of the holy mountain for a month now, and the place they march off to with such grim determination is... the old rancher's tavern down the mountain.
Meanwhile, on a train bound for Kjerag sat a girl from Ursus: Rhodes Island operator **Leto**, real name Rosalind, hugging a box her mom had entrusted to her.
1. The Victorian Viscount Who Insists He's a Tourist

That same day, **Arctosz**, head of Clan Paleroche, is fuming and wants those Victorians thrown out right now, but the Saintess calms him down: they have no grounds to turn away guests who came to celebrate. Whatever **Enciodes** of Clan Silverash is scheming behind the scenes, she says, she and the Vine-Bead Court 'mustn't know' about it.

Enciodes himself, meanwhile, goes to deliver an invitation to the Victorian camp. Pressed with the reminder that even the Duke's patience has its limits, he promises to answer their offer of 'cooperation' within a few days. And the moment he leaves, Viscount **Harold** goes chasing after a subordinate who's sneaking off to drink, taking Harold's own cheese fondue with him.

Over at the station at the foot of the holy mountain, Leto gets off the train and runs right into those soldiers. Harold is whispering to one with a runny nose, asking why he isn't wearing the coat Harold bought him, and the soldier is holding out because the 'I ♥ Snow' embroidery is too embarrassing.

blocks.cap: "(I think so too.)" Leto, butting in on the side of the 'I ♥ Snow' coat being cute.

blocks.x: Saying they're tourists too, Harold shows Leto to the train for Lake Silberneherze. In their compartment, Leto tells him she was born in Kjerag but grew up in Ursus with her mom, and that the box she's hugging holds her mother's 'remains.' When Harold offers his condolences, she waves him off. It's not that sad, she says.

The plan: see the statue in her mom's place, carry the box to the top of the mountain next to Lake Silberneherze, and maybe find her dad. According to her mom, he was a famously handsome man in Kjerag.
Of course, this isn't going to be a tearful reunion. She had her friends help her calculate ten years' worth of living expenses, tuition, and medical bills, plus 'compensation for emotional absence.'
I don't care how handsome he is! You can't eat a pretty face!
2. Wanted by the Black Knight (Re: Burdenbeast Postnatal Care)

Meanwhile, on the same train, the Victorian Duke's spy, the **'Trilby Asher'**, was combing through the compartments one by one. He runs into Harold in Leto's compartment, and the two step out into the corridor to feel each other out. They both serve the Duke, and neither trusts the other one bit.
Then he opens the door to the last compartment, and there sits someone who's supposed to be up in the mountains training recruits.

blocks.cap: Enciodes's right hand, the 'Black Knight.' There's still blood on her gloves.

blocks.x: Without a sound, **Degenbrecher**, three-time consecutive champion of Kazimierz's knight competitions, slices the brim of the spy's hat as a warning, then announces that the person eavesdropping outside is exactly who she's been looking for. The eavesdropper, Harold, grabs Leto's hand and bolts.

After a chase across the whole train, Leto hides Harold under a table, but Degenbrecher's business turns out to be a letdown. The herdsman Leones urgently needs Harold, because 'Lily' is waiting for him.

"You forgot your mistress? Wow, you're trash." Here's the truth: Lily is a burdenbeast, the blood on the gloves came from giving Lily first aid when she went into early labor, and in just one month, Harold has become the burdenbeast vet every herder is talking about.

blocks.cap: Arriving at Lake Silberneherze Station. No hidden agenda, and no reason for a chase.

blocks.x: Harold hands Leto his contact info, promising to keep helping her look for her dad, and rushes off to Lily. Hearing about it, Degenbrecher asks just one short question. "Her father... is that what the girl said?"
But the 'Trilby Asher' won't let go of his suspicions, bringing up Karlan Trade's shady imports and exports. And he makes one thing very clear to Harold: this is no sightseeing trip.
3. Apparently Kjerag's Most Handsome Man Is Enciodes
On her own now, Leto casually asks a street vendor whether Kjerag has a man everyone agrees is handsome. "That'd be Sir Enciodes, wouldn't it?" "No way. Absolutely not!"

When she reaches the lakeshore, this time it's **Sciurus** of Clan Browntail who grabs Leto. She'd been pestering her husband over names like 'Dremomys' and 'Nut,' and now, following orders from her older sister and clan head **Ratatos**, she approaches Leto and invites her to the unveiling ceremony.

Then, beneath the statue, as Leto fumbles around because she doesn't know how to pray, a passing **Elder Devotee** shows her how, starting with how to hold her hands. Leto prays silently for a bit, then worries: what if Kjeragandr can't hear what's in her heart? So she looks up and yells.
Kjeragandr!! Please look after my mom! She's one of your followers!

blocks.cap: Beneath the Kjeragandr statue. Leto's prayer wasn't a quiet meditation. It was a shout.

blocks.x: When Leto turns around, the devotee sees her face and freezes on the spot. It's a familiarity he can't put into words, and after hearing her story, he offers her a place to stay.

At that same moment, Ratatos, Gnosis, and Degenbrecher meet in secret and talk about having deliberately put Leto in front of the 'Trilby Asher.' What exactly they're trying to hide, they never say out loud.

Meanwhile, the Saintess's head handmaiden **Kjarr**, who heard Leto's shout, chimes in that the girl has a point, and while she's at it, begs to have the statue's face fixed. Enya's answer is short. "Denied."
4. A Drunk Lives at the Devotee's House

That evening, the devotee takes Leto to a big mansion. Arctosz's man Gulo greets him as "the old master," and inside, Arctosz is blind drunk from 'taste-testing' the liquor for the party on the eve of the ceremony.

The Elder Devotee turns out to be the former head of Clan Paleroche, and Arctosz's father. Arctosz peers at Leto and mumbles, "Your face... I feel like I know it," but Leto shakes her head. Her dad is supposed to be handsome, so there's no way he's that shaggy-bearded drunk.

Meanwhile, in a dusty, empty room, the devotee takes out a stone engraved with Kjeragandr's blessing. In his memory is a winter when a foreign woman who'd done nothing wrong, carrying a small child, vanished in anger into the blizzard.
He was the one who drove mother and daughter out for the clan's sake, and the one who locked Arctosz in the woodshed to keep him quiet when he tried to protect them.
If there is anyone to blame, Tatyana, then blame me.

Meanwhile, the living room has turned into a drinking party. The honey drink Leto brings out gets Arctosz drunk on honey, of all things. According to Gulo, it runs in the family: his father's the same way.
