blocks.cap: "We people of Kjerag never skimp when it comes to treating our guests!" Arctosz, who has hauled over his entire liquor cellar.

blocks.x: The bottle he opens, one he'd sworn he would never bring out for anything, has gone sour. It was meant to be shared with 'that one' at the wedding reception, Arctosz says, trailing off, and Leto snatches the bottle and downs it.

She laughs that she's eaten moldy bread and drunk sewer water before, then says: when something meant that much to you, isn't it a waste to toss it just because the taste changed a little? The party goes on that night until the devotee and Arctosz pass out on the living room floor.
5. The Viscount's Dinner, the Siblings' Sparring

Around then, the Victorian camp was practically a card parlor. But this 'sightseeing trip,' which Harold had spent a fortune to secure, was really a chance to recuperate for old soldiers haunted by nightmares and left without the use of an arm.

Mulling over the warning from the 'Trilby Asher', Harold decides to throw a party, and entrusts the invitation to Weiss, Enciodes's man who has spent the entire month watching his camp. Weiss reports to his master: "The viscount respects his people, and he respects us."

So Enciodes personally opens Clan Silverash's old liquor cellar and brings a bottle of 'Snow Realm Spring 1072.' His father laid it down believing spring would soon come to Kjerag, but even after more than twenty years of waiting, that spring never came.
But at the table where Enya sits, the Saintess and the clan head trade polite barbs with no end in sight.

blocks.cap: "Ah, you are both such fine young people!" The host, hunting for a chance to cut in.

blocks.x: After all, nobody's going to sneak pocket money under your pillow anymore!
Enciodes gives as good as he gets: at least now he doesn't have to pay back his candy money threefold with interest. An old story only the two of them, who were once brother and sister, would know.

Finally, Harold gets to the point. It was the Duke of Caster who lent a hand when Karlan Trade took its first steps, so now it's time to collect some interest. When Enya asks what happens if no show of sincerity is made, he silently opens the window to let in the cold wind, then shuts it again.

Enya answers that Kjerag as it is today is a decision all its people made together. A fruit and cheese wrap that Kjarr had secretly ordered also shows up on the table that day, and after one bite, the two murmur the exact same thing. "...It's that taste."
That night, in the lobby of Karlan Trade's headquarters, Gnosis, having drunk a Victorian soldier under the table, was slumped on the stairs.

blocks.cap: A scene repeated countless times over the past ten years. Two drunks, and one handing them water.

blocks.x: When Enciodes dodges a question about how things stand with Enya, Degenbrecher lays into him and Gnosis both. You two are exactly the same, she says: you never tell the people who want to hear it the things you need to say. Then, when they both hold out a hand for more medicine at the same time, she smacks each one.
6. 'John Smith' Follows Her to the Summit
The next morning, Arctosz wakes up on the living room floor and hears the truth from his father. The girl from last night, Rosalind, is his daughter.

Overjoyed, Arctosz announces he's going to buy the foods she loved as a little kid and head up the mountain right now. That's when his father stops him: the girl came to return her mother's 'remains.'
"B-but Tatyana's still young, how could..." As he trails off, Ratatos arrives with another warning. Right now, Victorian spies are watching that girl.
Enciodes was the one who set that up. He leaked word to the 'Trilby Asher' that 'the Paleroche heir has secretly returned home,' using Leto as bait. He'd apologize to the Doctor later, he said.

Meanwhile, as Leto climbs the mountain, she fishes the 'Trilby Asher' out of a hunting trap. When he introduces himself as 'John Smith,' Leto's eyes light up. That's the name of the hero in a spy movie the Doctor was watching, she says.

blocks.cap: Where the cable car ends. From here to the summit, it's on foot.

blocks.x: When they finally reach the summit, 'John' notices that every railway in Kjerag passes Lake Silberneherze, while Leto searches for two old trees whose trunks have grown into one. Then, out of nowhere, Leto backs him up to the edge of the cliff. She never told him her name, so how does he know her full name?

Just as the interrogation is heating up, Arctosz charges in. "You Victorian bastard!! Get away from her!" He stomps, the snow at the cliff's edge gives way, and as Leto falls, Arctosz falls right along with her.
Left alone, the 'Trilby Asher' finds Degenbrecher blocking his way.
7. A Father Offers His Axe
Leto has a memory. Swinging her fists at the kids who taunted her as a bad girl with no dad, and shouting: "All I need is my mom. I don't need a dad!"
At the bottom of the cliff, Leto finds the trees she was looking for. Two of them really have grown together into one, and there, in front of them, she finishes what her mother asked of her.
Arctosz, pinned beneath her with an injured leg, begins to speak. This mountain is where he and Tatyana first met. "Rosalind, you're my daughter."
One snowy day more than twenty years ago, a young Arctosz lost his hunting party, and a clump of snow fell on his head from the intertwined trees. The woman sitting up there, laughing, was Tatyana.
The two married despite opposition. The Paleroche head at the time, who didn't stand in the way of that marriage, was the Elder Devotee: Leto's grandfather.

The happiness didn't last. After Leto was born, the reform-minded Silverash couple died in an 'accident,' and Arctosz says it was no simple accident. The conservative Clan Paleroche stood on the opposing side, and in people's eyes, Tatyana was nothing more than an Ursus woman who had come to ruin Kjerag.

"For the first time, I came to know fear." That, he says, is why he sent mother and daughter far away, and he throws his axe down in front of his daughter. She can hate him, she can swing it at him, and he won't dodge. He only asks whether she could call him dad, just once more.

blocks.cap: "Go to hell! In your dreams!!"

blocks.x: Leto demands an answer. He left her mother alone for years in a land full of hostility, made her raise a child there too, and the conclusion he came to was 'leave'? Her mom loved exploring and anything new. What could she possibly have gotten out of Kjerag back then?
There's not a trace of Tatyana Yevgenyevna Larina in anything you just said!

When she needed a dad, nobody came, so she fought her way through alone with nothing but her fists. She doesn't need one now, Leto says, and she has no intention of being the bridge that gets her mom to forgive him either. But Arctosz catches on something unexpected.
"Your mother forgive me...? But isn't your mother already gone...?" "Who says my mom's dead?!"

The 'remains' were down to her clumsy Kjerag. What Leto meant was a 'token.' Tatyana is alive; she just broke her leg right before the trip, so she sent her daughter on alone. Though a few years ago, during the Chernobog incident, she went into the Catastrophe zone searching for her daughter, who'd been caught up in it, and contracted Oripathy.

Having said everything she came to say, Leto kicks the man who calls himself her dad off into the snow below the cliff, then yells down at him: don't forget to settle the last ten-plus years of child support. She'll send the bill to his house.
8. Statue Face Slimming, at Your Service

At that same moment, up on the mountain, the 'Trilby Asher' meekly surrenders, then stops mid-turn and lays out his deductions. If Leto is the bait, then the real issue lies in the transport routes Clan Paleroche handles, and the secret is in the statue on the central island of Lake Silberneherze, where all of Kjerag's railways converge.

Degenbrecher's weapon comes flying at once. The 'Trilby Asher' borrows a burdenbeast to ride and a pair of skates to wear and flees all the way to the central island, and the fight ends up climbing onto the Kjeragandr statue itself.

And down below the statue, Kjarr is having the time of her life. She'd been grumbling that the statue's face was based on 'my portrait as drawn in the ancient texts,' and now, every time the two fighters chip something off the face, she calls out pointers. A little thinner on that side, and don't touch the sideburns.

blocks.cap: The 'Trilby Asher', kicked off the top of the statue and sent flying. Meanwhile, the statue's face has gotten a little slimmer.

blocks.x: A while later, the 'Trilby Asher', floating 'like a corpse' in a hole in the ice, is fished out by Harold and Leto as they pass by. Soon after, Enya shows up and invites all three of them to tonight's campfire.

Even so, he sneaks back to the central island, where a voice comes from somewhere. "She is tired. Come back tomorrow." When he comes to his senses, he's standing in the middle of a street in Lake Silberneherze.

He slaps his own cheek once, then, for the first time since coming to Kjerag, takes up a prayer pose toward the statue. And off in the distance, Kjarr sighs. Being a bystander is hard work too, you know.
Next, disguised as a liquor merchant, he slips into the station warehouse and finds metal in the barrels instead of liquor. The shipping records all point to the same place.
9. Live Rounds Loaded, Target: the Kjeragandr Statue

At the campfire that night, Harold is reunited with Lily, and the herdsman Leones gives him freshly made cheese as a parting gift, saying that everyone was wary of him at first, but now they all think of him as a friend.
That's when the 'Trilby Asher' quietly pulls him aside and spreads out photos and documents.
Beneath the island at the heart of the lake, without a doubt, lies a secret of Enciodes's... no, of this entire nation.
He mustn't go back empty-handed, the 'Trilby Asher' tells him; Enciodes has crossed a line. And then he addresses Harold like this: "O Great Hero."

On the way back to camp, Harold thinks of Kjerag's streets, changing by the day, and the golden barley fields of his childhood. Then he calls up once more the marching route he'd drawn up a week after arriving in Kjerag, the one that only stuck harder the more he tried to forget it.
Everyone, load live ammunition and stand by. The operation begins at dawn tomorrow. Our target is... the statue of Kjeragandr.

The next morning, Enya leads the way and is the first to set foot on frozen Lake Silberneherze. From afar, the ice looked like a flawless gem, but up close it's covered in scars, and beneath it, water rushes powerfully along.

And just like two days earlier, when they marched off to the tavern, the Victorian soldiers march in formation. This time toward the statue, weapons in hand. "Forgive me, my old friends." Harold orders the advance, declaring that Kjerag has been using the statue as cover to move military supplies.

Enciodes, meanwhile, reads this as a 'warning' rather than a 'show of force' and decides to hold out until the next guests of honor arrive, and Degenbrecher steps out alone. The condition is that it's a solo act, backed by neither Karlan Trade nor Kjerag, but she just smiles. "It's not like it's my first time, right?"
And when a single figure walks out of the thick fog, Harold, her number one fan, marvels that she's worth a thousand men, then suddenly asks: is she stalling for time?

blocks.cap: "No one goes past this point. ...Don't even think about it."

blocks.x: 10. One Against Two Thousand
The soldiers who tried to go around Degenbrecher are hurt the worst, and Harold steps to the front himself to protect his men. As their blades meet, he asks whether Degenbrecher is her real name.

Plenty of people in Leithanien's slums had no name, she answers. The day she watched a gendarme crush people's skulls with a pair of edgeless swordbreakers, she understood that what she had was not a code, and not a creed. It was violence.
So that day, I gave myself a name. I am Degenbrecher.

Meanwhile, beneath the statue, Enya presses Enciodes. Does he believe Degenbrecher will stop two thousand men? Does he believe she'll fight to the death until his scheme pays off? Enciodes answers that she is a citizen of Kjerag who stepped forward of her own will, and that he has only bet on the best outcome.
"Loosen your grip. You'll hurt yourself." At Enya's words, he is silent for a moment. Then he asks her a favor: to pray for Degenbrecher.
Even when Gnosis offers a last resort, blowing up the lake and plunging everyone into the freezing water, Enciodes's answer is the same. "Let's trust in Degenbrecher."
Out on the ice, meanwhile, Degenbrecher is wounded by Arts and scorched by shells, until at last she stops counting her wounds.

In a final attempt, Harold pleads with her: if Enciodes would just bow his head a little, he'll try to win over the Duke with only 30% of the terms. Degenbrecher sees right through him. He fled to Kjerag because he hates war, but in the end, he is a Victorian.
"I cannot do anything that harms Victoria's interests." "Good. Neither can I."

Names and identities had always come easily to her, and gone just as easily. Now even she has something she cannot give up. Degenbrecher brings her twin swordbreakers down on the ice, and it begins to crack.
Around then, aboard the Lake Silberneherze train that Sciurus had switched to an express, the 'Trilby Asher' opens the door to the last compartment. That is where Silverash's hidden card was.

blocks.cap: A packed compartment. Kazimierz's campaign knights and a spokesman for the Chamber of Commerce, squeezed into a single car.

blocks.x: Also on that train were the Doctor, Sharp, Rhine Lab's **Muelsyse**, and Leto.

When the train arrives, Sciurus welcomes the campaign knights and Enciodes welcomes Spokesman Mob. Then, at Enciodes's request, Mob calls out loud enough for the whole lake to hear: Karlan Trade is joining hands with Kazimierz, and Kjerag will be Kazimierz's steadfast partner.
That voice carries all the way out onto the ice. As her vision blurs, Degenbrecher hears it without making out the words, and for as long as she can still stand, she lets no one pass.
It is Harold who calls off the attack. They can't drag Kazimierz into this, he says, and half his soldiers have already gone into the water. "We're not fighting?" "No, we're not." "Good."
Degenbrecher signs her name on the card from her first championship that Harold holds out, but shakes her head at his offer to treat her wounds. Someone is waiting for her.
Epilogue. The Last Stop

Not a single person died. The soldiers whisper that it was Kjeragandr's protection, but Enya calls it a miracle both sides made together, and invites them to the banquet. Will they come to the banquet, or admit it was a military operation and go to prison?

As Kjarr prepares the banquet, Enya tells her that someday, outsiders will remember not just Karlan Trade, but the name 'Kjerag.' When she says that this time she won't lean on Kjeragandr's help, Kjarr smiles. A mother is always glad to see her child let go of her hand and start to walk.
Meanwhile, Arctosz, waiting for Leto out on the street, admits that his memories of the past ten-odd years let his weak self run away into prettied-up nostalgia, and apologizes.

Leto corrects him on just one thing. Her mom never once spoke badly of Kjerag or of him, and she even taught Leto how to pray to Kjeragandr. But don't get the wrong idea, Leto adds: her mom is too good to waste her life resenting him, and he isn't even worth it.
I'm the daughter of Tatyana Yevgenyevna Larina. My name is Rosalind Tatyanovna Larina, codename Leto. Remember that.
Leto presses the account number for the child support into his hand and turns to go. When he calls after her, asking if he could see Tatyana just once, the answer is a single line. "In your dreams!"

Having watched it all, the Elder Devotee hands a sacred stone to a villager on his lands, whose son married a Siracusan woman and who has just become the grandfather of a baby girl, praying that every child in Kjerag may grow up free of sorrow.

As for the 'Trilby Asher,' it turns out his real mission was to find out whether Kjeragandr actually exists. Concluding that a head-on clash isn't worth the cost, he pulls the limited-edition blind box that Harold couldn't get all month, right in front of him, and decides to stay in Kjerag for a while.

Around the same time, out on the ice, Enciodes brings up the debt he owes Degenbrecher. She says she only did what she could, because she'd started to think living here might not be so bad. And he tells her: "It's Kjerag that made you stay here, not me."
Enciodes, too, says that someday outsiders will remember the name 'Kjerag.' The exact same words Enya had spoken.

And beneath the noise of the banquet, Ratatos and Gnosis are listening to the clang of metal ringing out from under the statue. In the base they built beneath Lake Silberneherze under the pretext of putting up the statue, Project One is nearing completion.

blocks.cap: A high-speed battleship, built beneath the Kjeragandr statue.

blocks.x: When Gnosis asks whether they're really naming this ship the 'Walnut,' Ratatos laughs. It was her little sister's idea: once she has kids, she plans to tell them this battleship is their big brother.

A hospital corridor, before Leto left for Kjerag. Tatyana, who broke her leg tinkering with a jetpack, ignores the doctor's orders to stay in bed, comes back from a walk, and laughs that as soon as her leg heals, she'll take her daughter off to Sargon, or Sami, or wherever.

Mom's 'remains' were a token, the army that came to celebrate took aim at the statue, and beneath the statue lay a warship. At the last stop of the Lake Silberneherze train, Leto saw her dad's face and handed him the bill, and Kjerag took its first steps toward spring across the scarred ice.

act29side.tagline: A retired knight, called home by her father, finds herself caught between the Witch King's remnants and the Twin Empresses, and must part with the person she loves most by her own hand. That autumn, too, the sunset over Zwillingstürme never left the sky.

chars.name: Viviana
chars.desc: A retired 'Candle Knight' of Kazimierz. The hidden daughter of the Kurfürst of Sturmland, she becomes a candidate for Empresses' Voice at her father's wish.

chars.name: Ebenholz
chars.desc: Former Graf Urtica and the last of the Witch King's bloodline. A caster of Rhodes Island, he sets foot once more in the homeland he long turned his back on.

chars.name: Arturia
chars.desc: A Sankta cellist who wanders across borders. Her Originium Arts resonate with the deepest emotions in a person's heart · Operator Virtuosa

chars.name: Federico
chars.desc: An executor of Laterano's Notarial Hall. He has pursued the wanted fugitive Arturia all the way to Leithanien · Operator Executor the Ex Foedere

chars.name: Lessing
chars.desc: A taciturn swordsman raised under Fremont. Carrying a cloth-wrapped longsword, he keeps watch over Ebenholz.

chars.name: Cora
chars.desc: Instrument tuner for Leithanien's Reichsorchester. She is blind, and she is the one who sent the young Viviana to Kazimierz.

chars.name: Brandt
chars.desc: A Gesatzswächter. He grew up with Werner and his brother, and once swore loyalty to House Hochberg.

chars.name: Werner
chars.desc: The Kurfürst of Sturmland and Viviana's father. In his youth, he dreamed of becoming a poet.

chars.name: Lucinda
chars.desc: Viviana's mother. A commoner poet who met Werner at a poetry gathering in Marigold Alley.

chars.name: Loris
chars.desc: Commander of the Zwillingstürme Gendarmerie. A Liberi from Laterano, steeped in drink and bribes, who calls himself a failure.

chars.name: Yulia
chars.desc: A café owner who disappeared in Marigold Alley fifteen years ago. Jan's older sister.

chars.name: Michael
chars.desc: A young envoy who serves Empress Grimmacht alone. He carries a tuba on his back and watches for signs of trouble in the city.

chars.name: Grimmacht
chars.desc: Of the Twin Empresses, the mistress of the black spire. She is called the Austere Authority.

chars.name: Ewigegnade
chars.desc: Of the Twin Empresses, the mistress of the white spire. She is called the Eternal Grace.

chars.name: Fremont
chars.desc: A cantankerous old scholar who lives in the oldest spire of Ludwigs-Universität. He raised Lessing.

chars.name: Gerhard
chars.desc: A scholar at Ludwigs-Universität and a student of Fremont. Twenty-three years ago, he took part in the assault on the Witch King's Spire.

chars.name: Młynar
chars.desc: A knight of the Nearl family of Kazimierz.

terms.name: Güldenesgesatz
terms.desc: Leithanien's golden movement, composed a thousand years ago by the sages of ten tribes. It set the nation's institutions, its morals, and its standard of beauty.

terms.name: Zwillingstürme
terms.desc: The capital of Leithanien. The white and black spires of the two empresses stand side by side, earning it the name 'Twin Towers.' Its old name was Vedunien.

terms.name: Sturmland
terms.desc: A province in the north of Leithanien, often battered by wind and rain. House Hochberg holds its seat as Kurfürst.

terms.name: Gesatzswächter
terms.desc: Knights who have given their swords and Arts to the Güldenesgesatz and to Leithanien. They are dispatched across the land to carry out the empresses' will.

terms.name: Witch King
terms.desc: The tyrant of the previous era, brought down by the Twin Empresses twenty-three years ago. Even after his death, followers remain who cry out his name.

terms.name: Echoes of Herkunftshorn
terms.desc: The name the Witch King's remnant followers gave themselves. They operate behind masks.

terms.name: Genesis Horn
terms.desc: A rendering of the Witch King's name, 'Herkunftshorn.' The remnants use it for the final legacy the tyrant left somewhere in this land.

terms.name: Empresses' Voice
terms.desc: Envoys who act on behalf of the Twin Empresses, chosen from among the children of the regional nobility. Formal appointment takes place in the spires after the Kaiserinnensfest.

terms.name: Kaiserinnensfest
terms.desc: An annual festival commemorating the day the Witch King fell. It opens with an ensemble performance of the Güldenesgesatz and closes with a duet by the Twin Empresses.

terms.name: Marigold Alley
terms.desc: Karl Schmidt Street in the Bodenshof district of Zwillingstürme. An alley where painters and poets gather and live.

terms.name: Ludwigs-Universität
terms.desc: Leithanien's first university. Kurfürst Ludwig, called 'the Scholar,' founded it by opening the Urtica family's spire to the public.

terms.name: Voice of Mundane
terms.desc: The Witch King's melody, planted in Ebenholz's head. For years it tormented him with headaches.

terms.name: Kargereich
terms.desc: A space on the far side of reality, which the Liches call 'the beginning and end of all threads.'

blocks.x: Leithanien was born a thousand years ago, when ten tribes were bound together under a single movement: the **Güldenesgesatz**. Twenty-three years ago, in autumn, the Twin Empresses brought down the tyrant known as the Witch King, and every year the capital, Zwillingstürme, honors that day with the Kaiserinnensfest.

On a stormy night a few days before that year's festival, Werner, the Kurfürst of Sturmland in the north, died in his own spire. That same night, his hidden daughter **Viviana** sat in a general store in Sturmland with a candle lit, waiting for someone.
For twenty-three years, the sunset over the capital had been the same color. Beneath that light, many people still stood frozen on one step of a spiral staircase with no end in sight.
1. A Death in the Storm

The one who entered the store was a blind woman, **Cora**. As she told Viviana to put out the candle, the windows shattered and casters' Arts poured in. Cora 'tuned' the notes so they veered aside, and Viviana relit the candle and pinned the attackers with its shadows.
Cora traced Viviana's face with her hands, wept, and told her that Werner was dead. Thirteen years earlier, she had also been the one who took the young Viviana to Kazimierz.

Sensing that his death was near, Werner had wished for his daughter to represent the family as an **Empresses' Voice**, so that she could step away from the struggle for power and live under the empresses' protection.

That same night, in the Kurfürst's spire, the Gesatzswächter **Brandt** was questioning the traitors. The attendant who had harmed the Kurfürst had been controlled by mind-altering Arts, and the spire caster who fled died crying out 'Concertmaster' and 'Genesis Horn.'
Then the cellist **Arturia** left Sturmland for the capital. **Federico**, an executor of Laterano's Notarial Hall, followed her, for she was a wanted fugitive.

Around the same time, **Ebenholz**, former Graf Urtica and the last of the Witch King's bloodline, answered the empresses' summons and set foot in Leithanien again. In his head, a grating melody still had not stopped.
2. City of Sunset, Black Painting

In the capital, Cora introduced Viviana to **Ewigegnade**, the empress of the white spire. There, Brandt reported that the copy of the Güldenesgesatz kept in the Kurfürst's spire had been stolen by the Witch King's remnants.

Three days remained until the festival. Viviana offered to act herself, since no one knew who she was. The empress allowed it on the condition that Brandt go with her, and showed her the city steeped in sunset.

blocks.cap: Evening in Zwillingstürme. The colors of a classical painting, the timbre of accordions, the scent of marigolds.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, **Grimmacht**, the empress of the black spire, told Brandt that no one can avoid a choice forever.

The next incident broke out at the art gallery. The painter Frieda Seemann, who had unveiled her first new work in more than twenty years, died in front of her own painting, and the gendarmerie commander **Loris** tried to cover it up as death from overwork.

The painting was titled 'Der Tod des Hexenkönigs'—The Death of the Witch King. But the black spirals covering the canvas burrowed into the minds of those who looked at it and carved the name 'Witch King' there.

blocks.cap: A gallery painted over with black spirals, and a Sankta at its center.

blocks.x: It was Arturia who quieted that noise. As a girl, Frau Seemann had worshipped the Witch King like a god, she said, and on the day that god fell, she lost both love and the will to create.
Many people are trapped in whatever fateful moment changed the course of their lives, walking along an endless spiral staircase. ...Your father. And you as well.
Cora, arriving late, said the black paint was Originium mixed with the painter's own blood. Frau Seemann had been inside the Witch King's Spire that night twenty-three years ago.
3. The Hero Who Called Himself a Failure

Meanwhile, the Sankta Federico, who had fired a gun near the gallery, was detained by Loris. Twenty-three years ago, Loris had been the Liberi soldier who charged first into the Witch King's Spire. Now he lived on drink and bribes and called himself a failure.

In Marigold Alley, a boy named Jan sneered at Loris as a coward. Jan's sister **Yulia**, who vanished fifteen years ago, was the case Loris had never been able to solve. Planning to leave the country after the festival, Loris had already handed over his wallet, money for Jan's studies abroad and all.

That same afternoon, Ebenholz was in Forest Park, listening to a performance in memory of the victims of the Witch King's era. He had not yet played a single piece for his dead friend. Then the remnants' Arts surged out of the water at him.

blocks.cap: Forest Park. Wherever a tree now stands, a statue of a spiral horn once stood.

blocks.x: Driven into the sewers, Ebenholz faced masked figures who said the melody inside him was worth more than his mind, and who tried to erase his consciousness.

At the same moment, Loris sensed a fight near the park and tried to turn away. There was no telling which count might be behind the masks, and the man who had last seen Yulia had been beyond his reach because of his title.

Federico went after the sound of the cello alone, and the sound reached Loris, left behind, as well. Within the melody, he met again the old Liberi gendarme who had once pulled him, as a young man, out from under an execution.

blocks.who: The old gendarme who saved Loris
blocks.x: Same goes for you. If you feel guilty, then try saving a few more lives.

Muttering that he wanted to live, that he could not die like a hero, Loris went down into the sewers in the end. 'Go. My men are on their way.' Ebenholz ran without ever seeing the face of the man who had saved him.

Some time later, what was found in the sewers was a spiral-horn statue made from Loris's flesh and blood. Jan wept that Loris had died because of him, and Viviana promised that his death would not be buried as mere noise.
Then a cello piece rang out in Marigold Alley. 'This piece is dedicated to the return of the hero, Loris Bordin.'
4. Marigolds, Ten Minutes Late

When Ebenholz, who had been fleeing, opened his eyes again, he was in a room in a spire. His watcher **Lessing** and the old scholar Lessing called grandfather, **Fremont**, meant to use the melody in Ebenholz's head to summon the 'Genesis Horn.' But just before the ritual, Fremont's former student **Gerhard** spirited Ebenholz away.

Meanwhile, at Frau Seemann's house, which she visited with Cora, Viviana heard her parents' story for the first time. At a poetry gathering in this alley, back when the Witch King ruled, the young Werner from Sturmland had fallen in love at first sight with **Lucinda**, a commoner poet.

Then the sound of a cello came from somewhere, and Viviana was drawn into her father's memories. After the Witch King fell, Werner was made to take up the Kurfürst's seat. On the day he left, he waited for Lucinda, who never came, and at last got into the car.

blocks.cap: A daughter running down a golden alley. Her mother was surely somewhere in it.

blocks.x: Viviana ran through the golden alley but could not catch her mother's retreating figure. When the music stopped, the hidden remnants unleashed their Arts, and Brandt descended amid a violet melody and swept them away.

The last of the remnants crumbled into dust while delivering the Concertmaster's words. Twenty-three years ago, Werner's older brother Ernst had died because Brandt failed to help, and Werner, forced to become Kurfürst, lived out a melancholy life. 'You cannot avoid a choice forever.'

Back home, Cora told Viviana that on that day Lucinda had only stopped by the spice market and was running a little late. Had Werner waited ten more minutes, the two would have met. Those ten minutes became the regret of his life.
Viviana did not blame her father. She now understood that when one lacks the strength to face reality, the hopes of the past become wounds.

Then Viviana found the draft Frau Seemann had kept painting over to the very end. When Brandt's melody stripped away the overpainting, the inside of the Witch King's Spire twenty-three years ago was revealed. An empty throne, a painter behind a curtain, Loris entering the spire, Gerhard clearing the rubble.
5. Ludwigs-Universität, a Spire Risen Again

Viviana and Brandt went straight to Fremont at Ludwigs-Universität. As gendarmes acting on the empresses' orders searched the school, Brandt saw Fremont's shadow split into thousands of strings and recognized him as a Lich.

There, the boy **Michael**, who had been moving with Federico, appeared. He revealed that he was Grimmacht's envoy, and that Her Majesty's order was to help Fremont bring about the descent of the 'Genesis Horn' safely.

At the same time, Gerhard led Ebenholz to the Urtica secret chamber beneath the university. It was the very room where the Witch King had erased Siracusa from the movement and revised the Güldenesgesatz.
Masked remnants stepped out of the darkness. Even through a splitting headache, Ebenholz told Gerhard to run. This time, he said, he would protect him.
Gerhard raised a brass instrument and brought it down on his head.

blocks.cap: A boy before a throne wrapped in thorns. The cheers called him 'Witch King.'

blocks.x: It was also Gerhard who had planted the melody in Ebenholz's head, the 'Voice of Mundane,' when he was a child. Twenty-three years ago, Gerhard had lost nearly all the comrades he persuaded to fight in the Witch King's Spire, and he wanted forgiveness for the sin of killing that great king.
It was Lessing who cut a path, alone, all the way to the throne.

blocks.cap: "Herkunftshorn isn't the one sitting on that throne. His name is Ebenholz."

blocks.x: Meanwhile, inside the spire, students and gendarmes swept up in the sound of the pipe organ turned their fists on one another. At the top of the spire, Arturia did not play. She waited for the one she truly meant to play for.

Then, in the secret chamber, Gerhard used the missing copy of the movement to force out the Witch King's Arts, and dark red flames engulfed the school. Viviana tore through the black flames with her candle's shadow, entrusted the students to Michael, and stayed behind alone.
'My candleflame will go out sooner or later. To be able to choose a meaningful moment myself is enough.'

Outside the spire, Brandt began to close a golden curtain to wipe out the remnants, spire and all. Told that Viviana was still inside, Cora cried out, asking whether he had forgotten his promise to Werner.

In that moment, the voices of the Hochberg brothers he had failed to save twenty-three years ago rang in Brandt's ears, and a small gap opened in the curtain. That gap was what Arturia had been waiting for. When her cello sounded, a dark red spiral spire burst up through the earth.

blocks.cap: A dark red spiral spire tearing up through the ground. It resembled the Witch King's Spire that fell twenty-three years ago.

blocks.x: 6. After the False Spire Fell
Just before the black flames swallowed the school, a black flash split the clouds and fell, erasing the spire from the top down. On the ruins stood Grimmacht, longsword in hand.

Meanwhile, Gerhard, who had fled, was breaking down, unable to bear the Witch King's Arts. In Arturia's cello he found an answer: every person in Leithanien had been trapped by the Güldenesgesatz. Repeating that it was not his fault, he collapsed on the stairs with the copy of the movement and died.
Soon after, Arturia was taken away by Grimmacht's executioner, and Federico never got to take custody of her.

Meanwhile, on the stairs, Viviana found Pym, a gendarme whose body had been half burned away by the black flames. At the gallery he had said he was a fan of the 'Candle Knight.' He told her that her candleflame was warm, and died.
Cora, who found her in the rubble, said that Brandt had chosen Viviana over the spire. It was a choice made at the end of twenty-three years of guilt eating away at him.
That evening, the Liches who had been hiding in the school put out the black flames with a rain like starlight and left Leithanien's spires.

Around then, Ebenholz froze at the sound of a cello played exactly as his dead friend had played. The student's teacher was Arturia. If pain and joy alike had been given by someone else, was hope the same?
The next day, Grimmacht declared the case closed. The 'Voice of Mundane' that Fremont had drawn out of Ebenholz's head was not a key to opening the 'Genesis Horn.' It was only noise.

As Ebenholz laughed that his lifelong resistance had been a delusion, Lessing pointed his sword at him. Had he ever once visited those the Witch King had wounded? Had he ever looked back at his declining domain?
I never received a noble's education, so I don't talk about 'fate.' I only know that all the suffering is real.
Lessing proposed that they find the Witch King's true legacy together and put an end to it. Ebenholz asked him for an Arts unit.

Meanwhile, Federico found fifteen years' worth of files on the Yulia case in Loris's house. Then, on Loris's piano, he played 'Der Tod des Hexenkönigs,' the piece Arturia had composed using the witnesses' emotions as notes, and realized that emotions, too, are information.

blocks.cap: "Can you really... not see everything I see in the music?"

blocks.x: Arturia had not yet achieved her goal. Federico went to Viviana and asked her to stop Arturia with him.
7. The Small Room in the Spire

On the day of the festival, Viviana forged a secret order from Ewigegnade and went to see the isolated Arturia. She could no longer suppress the suspicion that the empresses might have caused her father's death.

blocks.cap: "Once upon a time, there was a child who lived in a spire at the heart of a storm."

blocks.x: Following Arturia's story, Viviana recalled the small room in the spire. One night, a child saw her father in a brightly lit banquet hall, and her mother, weeping, covered the child's eyes and ears. On the day she came down from the spire after her mother left, the child never raised her head, afraid her anger would show.

Why hadn't her father waited a little longer back then? Why had he written asking her to come home, only to go away again? Questions swallowed for twenty-two years were spoken aloud for the first time.

Werner had been Arturia's friend. Near death, lost in the sound of the cello, the ones he wished to see again were Lucinda and the daughter in the small room. He had given his life protecting the copy of the movement he promised the Twin Empresses to keep, casting the crisis out of his domain.

Leaving Arturia's room, Viviana pointed out that the remnants might be trying to use the Witch King's power on the movement itself. Soon, more than ten thousand people would perform the Güldenesgesatz together before the twin towers.

Backstage, about to perform, Cora asked Viviana to live with her. When Viviana asked how to stop the performance, Cora said she would stand with her whatever she did, and opened the way to the orchestra.
At the same time, Grimmacht refused Michael's plea to stop the festival. Then she told the boy she had kept at her side for seven years that it was time to let him go, and took up her violin.

As the sun sank, Viviana's shadows cut the link between some of the musicians and their instruments, but the performance began all the same. In the crowd in the square, Ebenholz shouted for people to run, but his Arts were lost among tens of thousands of lights.

blocks.cap: An ensemble of more than ten thousand casters. The twin towers and the whole city rang together.

blocks.x: Remembering the bell towers of Urtica that rang all at once at dusk, Ebenholz suddenly felt close to tears. In his heart, he too loved this land.
8. The Concertmaster
But the melody soon warped. People clutched their heads and vomited, and the Witch King's power ate into the movement.
The remnants hidden among the musicians revealed themselves. The one they called 'Concertmaster' was Cora, who had been holding Viviana's hand.
Viviana already knew. Frau Seemann's paintings had all vanished, and Cora had never stripped the overpainting from that draft all the way. Cora must have been among the witnesses in the painting.

Cora had entered the Witch King's Spire as a servant at fifteen and cleaned the resonance pipelines at its top. On that night twenty-three years ago, the moment she gave a pipeline a light push, a gap opened in the Witch King's defensive Arts. When she lay blinded and pinned on the stairs, it was Werner who pulled her out.

Becoming the remnants' 'Concertmaster' and luring them into the abyss was the mission the empresses had given her, and the bait was the copy of the movement Werner guarded. Having obtained the copy on the day Werner died, Cora resolved to use the Witch King's Arts to bring down the movement itself.
The Güldenesgesatz is the very spiral staircase that has trapped Leithanien.

How could she decide who would be the victims, Viviana asked; what guarantee was there that a new order would be better? Cora answered that she could hear every voice of the dying, and still, someone had to do it.
'You really are... too cruel.'
A vast shadow fell over Cora's feet like a storm in the night. Brandt's cry, too late, rang across the square.

blocks.cap: "Are the clouds beautiful today?"

blocks.x: Cora said she was glad that the one who killed her was the person she loved most. She had never once seen Viviana's parents. The stories of Marigold Alley were all scenes she had pictured from what Werner told her.
You deserve a better life than this, Viviana... If there really is one...
Cora's body was swept away by the black flames and was gone.
9. The Genesis Horn

The black flames gathered into the clouds. The remnants stabbed their own throats with their instruments and became one with the flames, and the Twin Empresses, the Gesatzswächter, and the Liches who had hurried back stood together against the Witch King in the sky.

At one side of the square, Ebenholz said the Witch King was the very sin he carried, and headed for the twin towers. Lessing handed him a knot woven from Lich threads and told him that he, of all people, could come back alive.

Meanwhile, Arturia, having broken out of confinement, faced Fremont in the Empresses' Spire. Seemann, Loris, Brandt, Gerhard, Cora. From the emotions of those who had witnessed the Witch King's death, she found his last words, and even as she was caught up in Fremont's 'Exile,' she drew her bow one last time.

blocks.cap: Like a giant eye opening in the clouds, the pitch-black spire of twenty-three years ago appeared.

blocks.x: Around then, Viviana, Federico, and Ebenholz, climbing the spiral staircase of the Empresses' Spire, lost one another before they knew it. The stairs stretched on without end.

There, Federico and Arturia each met Yulia, who had vanished fifteen years ago. Even after death, she kept watch over her own Marigold Alley, connecting resonance pipelines with devices salvaged from the empty places left by vanishing spires.

The truth Federico uncovered about her death was a simple accident. On the first day her café reopened, while waiting for Loris and Jan, she ran into remnants in the middle of an operation. Because it was early in the Twin Empresses' reign, the case was buried as having nothing to do with the Witch King.
When Yulia woke the resonance pipelines, the mist lifted. Beyond it, the spires of Leithanien's thousand years rose together in one place, and at their center Arturia saw the man on the throne.

blocks.cap: "Otto Dietmar Gustav von Urtica, Herkunftshorn... Your Majesty the Witch King."

blocks.x: 10. Echoes Before the Throne

Meanwhile, Ebenholz, climbing the stairs alone, heard endless condemnation. Voices telling him to repent in the tyrant's place, voices calling him the count who abandoned his domain, voices saying that his resistance, spent guarding a scrap of noise, had been a joke.
At the end of it, he saw the Witch King rewriting the movement, and realized he had never once in his life met the real Witch King.

blocks.cap: "Franz. Do not touch the notes in the air."

blocks.x: The Witch King asked: if the spire is a prison, how will you escape it, and who is your enemy? The Witch King that Ebenholz had cursed was a face made by stages and statues, and the self in the mirror asked why he could not forgive the self who had been protected.
He remembered words he had once heard: if we do not move toward the light, we will never leave that night.

'Well done, Franz. You have defeated your enemy.' Praised by the Witch King, Ebenholz burst out laughing. It was laughter that had not come once in nineteen years, and when it stopped, the throne was empty.

Meanwhile, Arturia asked the Witch King for an answer. Was a future possible in which everyone held their strongest feelings and, connected through emotion, could not be shaken by any disaster? The Witch King looked into her heart and said that such a future had worth, but that she, an empty vessel holding only the emotions of others, was the furthest of all from the answer.
Then the Twin Empresses entered his palace, and two generations of sovereigns clashed before the throne.
The Witch King proclaimed his final vision. If there is a Creator who would annihilate all things, that Creator must perish, and whoever brought him down must reach where he could not.
Leithanien shall stand, whose light will outshine the tallest beacon of hope. Leithanien shall live, whose name will outlast the longest river of time!

In the collapsing palace, the last thing to enfold him was the threads of his old friend Fremont. To the Lich who had come to reclaim the phylactery he lent 130 years ago, the Witch King said that he had returned it long ago, that death had caught up with him alone, and vanished.
11. The Last Knight, the Last Sunset

Around then, Viviana was opening more than a hundred doors. A life in which her parents married amid blessings, a life lived quietly in hiding, a life in which she stayed by Cora's side. Behind every door, parting came to her wearing a different face.

Meanwhile, Federico told Yulia of Loris's death. Yulia said he had never called himself a hero, but he was the only gendarme who would stand up to nobles for commoners, and that a person who holds on to hope is never defeated by disappointment.
With the words that she had meant to accept his proposal, Yulia vanished in the palace, shaken by the twins' intrusion.

blocks.cap: For the first time, he felt a person's final emotion. It was simple, and it was intense.

blocks.x: In another room Viviana opened was her younger self, reading 'The Last Knight' by candlelight. The child asked whether she wasn't hoping never to find a better answer, and whether that wasn't just like Papa.

As the collapse drew near, Viviana did not leave. She stood in front of the child. 'Never forget this, Viviana Droste: you are a knight!' As the darkness erased even emotion, a knight's swordspear, unworn by time, shone in her palm.

blocks.cap: A knight's light, grasped in the dark.

blocks.x: Cutting through the darkness, Viviana saw a swordspear driven deep into the chaos, and beyond it she felt countless gazes turned toward her. She knew that if this place collapsed, something more terrible would flood in.

Meanwhile, Ebenholz, falling into the void, saw a warm white light at its end. The smiles and music he had shared with his dead friend. That handful of hope had been given by no one. It was theirs alone.

At the same time, the theater in the real world was silent. As the void leaked out, people lost their emotions one by one, and Arturia, having lost her sound, accepted amid that crowd that she was someone who feared death.
And this time she played herself, sharing her own emotions with everyone.

blocks.cap: "I want to use this tiny shred of ego to connect every sorrow and joy."

blocks.x: Expression returned to people's faces, and the Lich threads and Lessing's knot held the passage once more. Michael blew the tuba Grimmacht had entrusted to him, telling the Gesatzswächter, who were preparing to erase Zwillingstürme, that everyone was safe.

Meanwhile, after the people escaped along the path of light Viviana opened, only the two empresses remained. While Ewigegnade's shield protected the twin towers and the people below, Grimmacht stood against the eyes writhing in the chaos.
Grimmacht built a new spire from the wreckage of the fallen one, walling off reality from Kargereich. Then, without looking back, she became part of that pitch-black monument.
This is my fate. But it is absolutely not... the fate of Leithanien and her people.
At last the dark clouds parted, and golden sunset poured between the twin towers. The people began to play a new melody, not the Güldenesgesatz.

blocks.cap: Leithanien's only empress, 'Gold der Zwillingstürme.' Tears ran down her cheeks.

blocks.x: Epilogue — Evening Glow
Half a month later, Michael delivered to Ebenholz a secret letter left by Grimmacht, who was 'temporarily absent.' Would he 'die' as a Leithanian and gain his freedom, or return to the Urtica domain?

Lessing told him the story of a boy. When a boy from a family of servants freed by the Witch King was notified that they must serve a new count again, the twelve-year-old Graf Urtica, plagued by headaches, threw the document away. The boy's name was Lessing Maeyer.

Ebenholz decided to return to the Urtica domain. To change Urtica, the castle one Witch King had transformed, once more, in a way entirely unlike his: that would be how he mocked the Witch King, and the path he would walk.

Meanwhile, Viviana visited the small garden in Bachshof that Cora had prepared so the two of them could live together. Brandt, taking off his helmet for the first time, told her not to blame herself, that Cora was someone who never looked back once she had decided, and then thanked her.

Viviana declined the post of Empresses' Voice. Her father had left no verse behind and held back the storm with all his strength; perhaps that life had been a poet's expression, she said, and so she did not resent him.
Her Leithanien remained as candles, books, and marigolds. In the language of flowers, the marigold means farewell.
To the lighthouses. To where once they were.
As she said her farewells, **Młynar** of the Nearl family arrived, to hear about the Nearl swordspear she had seen in the chaos.

Around then, Ewigegnade confided to Brandt that Hildegard—Grimmacht—was the one she could not protect. Hildegard's last words had been to have the sunset she wanted, and Ewigegnade declared that she would keep this sunset unchanged forever.
And Arturia was handed over to Laterano through the intervention of Pope Yvangelista XI. The Pope warned of a coming 'disaster,' and the Liches left for Kazdel, saying the hour of ruin was near.
Before leaving, Arturia passed the Witch King's last words to Federico. 'The invasion of chaos is inevitable. The master of all existence will awaken.'

blocks.cap: The most beautiful moment in Zwillingstürme. Night will soon come.

blocks.x: When night falls, where in Laterano are the lights lit first? Federico had long since found the answer to that question from his childhood, and the answer was as beautiful as ever.
That's why emotions never truly disappear. ...Like how the sunset has never truly left this sky.

The sunset over Zwillingstürme, the same light for twenty-three years, still colors the spires in that same light after that autumn. For that light, one empress remained in the chaos, and one knight, having come down the spiral staircase, bid farewell to Marigold Alley.

act28side.tagline: A mercenary sent to fix a power plant watches a town being driven out by its debts, and in the end robs the bank vault alongside its old folk. Tears cannot stand in for sorrow, but a gun can cry out for it.

chars.name: Jessica
chars.desc: A young Blacksteel sniper. Soft-hearted, she cannot hold back her tears in a crisis · Operator Jessica the Liberated

chars.name: Woodrow Bianchi
chars.desc: A taciturn old man who lives alone on the outskirts of Davistown, hunting. The townsfolk just call him 'Woody'

chars.name: Helena
chars.desc: Proprietress of the last restaurant left in Davistown. She has made herself guardian of the whole neighborhood · Operator Coldshot

chars.name: Leone Theremin
chars.desc: A blast engineer at the mine. A father who raised two sons on his own

chars.name: Benny
chars.desc: Leone's younger son. A precocious, gentle boy

chars.name: Carl
chars.desc: Leone's elder son, and Benny's older brother

chars.name: Miles
chars.desc: Davistown's boiler worker. An old Forte who spent half his life working in the energy tower

chars.name: Sylvia
chars.desc: A quiet young clerk at the Davistown bank

chars.name: 'Clip' Cliff
chars.desc: Head of Blacksteel Worldwide. He keeps business and feeling strictly apart

chars.name: Franka
chars.desc: A commander-level Blacksteel mercenary. Straightforward and quick with words

chars.name: Liskarm
chars.desc: Franka's partner. A careful, principled squad leader

chars.name: Laura
chars.desc: Blacksteel's chief technician. An optimist who talks to herself a lot · Operator Almond

terms.name: Davistown
terms.desc: A small mining plate stranded in the forests of eastern Columbia. It has been unable to move since its power plant exploded

terms.name: Blacksteel Worldwide
terms.desc: A mercenary company rooted in Columbia. Moderate on the surface, it takes on the dirty work behind the scenes

terms.name: Fort Barron
terms.desc: Blacksteel's mobile flagship. Large enough to tow an entire plate

terms.name: the frontier
terms.desc: The untamed wilderness at Columbia's edges, opened for settlement. Bankrupt debtors and convicts are sent there

terms.name: Camp Collus
terms.desc: A POW camp from the Columbian War of Independence. Infamous for the saying that of ten who go in, only one comes out

blocks.x: On the front lines in Chernobog, a mercenary told a young woman, tense with nerves, about his home. Davistown, a mining plate in the forests of eastern Columbia, was a place where everyone got through the winter warm on nothing but the waste heat of the energy tower. He said he wanted to go back and see it again.

That Davistown now sat stranded in the middle of the forest after its power plant exploded, on the edge of bankruptcy. The state government sent the mercenary company **Blacksteel Worldwide** to repair the power plant and return the plate to its route.
1. The Hunter in the Woods and the Bullet with No Owner

On the way to Davistown, Blacksteel's **Liskarm** squad first cleared out the bandits in the forest. The straight-talking commander **Franka** took the front, while the tender-hearted sniper **Jessica** and the chatty technician **Laura** rescued the town's boiler worker **Miles**, who had been held in the bandit camp.

But Jessica's communicator broke, and she lost her way in the forest. In her pocket was a velvet pouch holding a single rusted bullet, which her boss **'Clip' Cliff** had entrusted to her before departure, to be handed to **Woodrow Bianchi** of Davistown.

On the day he gave her the pouch, Cliff reproached Jessica, who since returning from Victoria had been putting residents ahead of orders, and told her never to repeat the mistake she had made in Victoria.
Let me remind you, Jessica. You're a mercenary. This is about business, not duty.

Back in the forest, the one who saved Jessica from a beast was an old hunter in a wide-brimmed hat. When he heard that the rescued hostage was an old Forte from the town, he set off ahead of her without a word.
Along the way, the two found a young beast caught in a trap. Its mother was the beast the hunter had just shot, and with its leg broken, the young one could not have survived anyway.
Jessica held it to her chest and stroked it until its cries faded away entirely. She could not save it, she said, but she could let it go in a warm embrace.

At the same hour, Franka was worried about Jessica, out there on her own. Twenty-three-year-old Jessica cried after every mission, and always came back to her teammates only after she had wiped away her tears.
When the fog finally lifted, Davistown came into view below the high ground. A giant track of broken branches ran down into the valley, and at its end the plate stood still.

blocks.cap: Davistown, stranded. The energy tower panted out white steam like a patient in critical condition.

blocks.x: 2. The Government Was in the Bank's Garage

At the plate's entrance, the one who greeted Blacksteel was not a government official but a bank clerk, **Sylvia**. No one had told her when they would arrive, and she had been standing in the cold wind since morning.

Liskarm went straight to the bank with Sylvia to hear how things stood. Last year's bankruptcy proceedings had cost most of the civil servants their jobs, City Hall itself had gone to auction, and the last mayor had fled with what remained of the town's funds. Full authority over government affairs had passed to the bank manager, who smiled politely.

blocks.cap: The garage lent by the bank. The mayor's secretary and a few temporary staff were all that remained of the government.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, the hunter brought Jessica to the plate. At the edge of town, Jessica watched an empty-handed man walk off into the snowfield without answering those who called after him, until he shrank to a small dot and vanished into the white snow.

The proprietress of the restaurant the hunter walked into, **Helena**, and the blast engineer **Leone Theremin** called him 'Woody.' Only then did Jessica, who had been looking for Woodrow Bianchi, realize who he was.

That evening Leone volunteered to advise on the power plant repairs, and admitted that everyone on the plate was in debt. The man who had walked into the snowfield was probably in debt too, he said, and when Jessica offered to go and save him, he told her to let it be.

The next day, Laura went into the energy tower and fell silent. The parts were either broken or had already been traded to caravans for canned food, and the Originium deposits built up in the pipes were on the verge of activating.

Laura went back in with only the Infected members of her team, saying that if they had not come out by eight o'clock, the residents should be evacuated. Waiting with the others at the restaurant, Sylvia confided that her mother had been the mayor here, and that she had only joined the bank because her mother fell ill.
At seven, just as Jessica, now back, was setting out for the tower with Woodrow, the door opened. Laura had brought her whole team back, but all they had saved was the most basic heating.
When Laura apologized that the plate could not be made to move again, Liskarm told her that everyone coming back safe was enough.
3. Waterlogged Coal

Some time later, the bank threw a reception party for Blacksteel. While the plate shivered, the bank alone stayed warm on its own power, and the manager, asking them to keep the peace, handed over a list of what were called 'the bandits' reserve army.'

That same day, Jessica rescued a boy whom thugs were trying to drag away. It was over his father's debts, they said, and the boy was Leone's son **Benny**. Leone had been borrowing large sums from the bank every year to hold on to his shares in the shuttered mine.

That night Sylvia counted the hundred steps from the bank's front door to the main switch, then counted her steps on the way home. Since her mother's death, she had been saying 'I'm home' to a door no one answered.

The next day, Jessica went to Woodrow to ask him to talk Leone around. In his chest of drawers she saw an old photograph of a young Woodrow, another Sankta, and her boss Cliff laughing together, along with a brown certificate gone yellow with age.

Around then, the households on the list that Liskarm and Franka visited turned out to be mostly honest people who simply could not pay their debts. The bank, Franka said, was trying to use Blacksteel's hands to drive them out.

Meanwhile, Leone pushed Jessica out the door when she urged him to sell his shares. Woodrow, who had come with her, did not take her side. He only said that if you try too hard to burn waterlogged coal, all you get is a faceful of ash.

That day the stove in Leone's house was wet and would hardly light. When Jessica came back and helped Benny get the fire going, Leone told her he had been abandoned at four and raised by miners, and that he had taken in **Carl** and Benny, the two children of a fellow miner.

Even so, Leone pointed to the door whenever the shares came up, until Jessica told him about Benny's attempted kidnapping. Then he broke. He could not pay his debts, he said, and he could not protect the people he wanted to protect. He would sell the shares.
Just then Woodrow came in carrying a box of coal and set it down by the stove, by way of an apology.

blocks.cap: Leone's house. The wet coal gave off nothing but smoke.

blocks.x: Afterward, at the bank, Sylvia pointed out that the figures on the paperwork came up short, and Jessica signed a check without Leone knowing. Informed of this, the manager said that the shares had been sold, and that there were plenty of people around the mine who could take care of the rest.
4. Her Arms

Some time later, a water pipe burst at Helena's restaurant. The bank suspected insurance fraud and refused the claim, and it would not honor the bankbook left behind by someone from her past who had already died, either.
At the same counter, an old woman was signing up for the Pioneer Plan: a contract to abandon her home and leave for **the frontier** in exchange for having part of her debt forgiven.

After Jessica wrote Helena a check as well, Leone treated Jessica to dinner as thanks. Helena, Woodrow, Miles, and Benny gathered at one table, and as the drinks went around, Leone and Miles sang an old miners' song.
She spread her arms, spread her heart, showed me that pretty face / And from that moment on, I found my dreams in her embrace
Jessica said that 'she' might be Davistown itself. Everyone joined in the song, but Jessica felt an unease she could not explain.
As spilled champagne dripped to the floor, Benny spoke up. Tomorrow, he said, he would leave Davistown for a school in Ironforge City.

His brother had held the household together in their father's place before becoming a mercenary, and a few years later only his belongings came back, along with a single line of regret. His brother must have had other choices too, Benny said, and so did he now.

blocks.cap: The son wanted his father's anger. The father held his head in his hands and said nothing.

blocks.x: Leone only repeated the same words: it was a good thing, of course he should go.
Walking Benny home, Jessica learned who Carl had been. His Blacksteel comrades had known him by the codename **Blackplate**.
When Carl fell in Chernobog, Jessica had been at his side. He used to tell her about a family deep in debt and a clever little brother, but she had never known his real name.

Benny said that the diamond-set silver ring his brother always wore had not been among his belongings. That same night, at the bank that had just processed its 120th pioneer contract, Sylvia clutched something round hanging from her neck and called Carl's name.
As they parted, Benny told Jessica not to try to mend the paper houses here with a precious golden nail. Thin paper could not bear its weight.
5. The Night Fort Barron Came

Half a month later, Blacksteel waited outside the plate for its flagship, **Fort Barron**. Then flames rose from the direction of the mine, and Jessica ran back into the plate without waiting for orders.
That night, thugs attacked all across the plate. Woodrow and Helena fought them off at the restaurant, Miles at the energy tower, and Leone, wandering the streets drunk, was beaten bloody.

At that hour, inside the bank, the manager soothed a frightened Sylvia. Once their partner arrived, those men would be of no further use. All the bank had done was look the other way while they helped themselves to a little before leaving.

When Jessica arrived, Leone's house was burning. Leone stopped her as she was about to rush into the flames. He had been miserable alone, staring at empty walls, he said. Maybe it was not so bad that it burned.

blocks.cap: Through the thick fog of the winter night, Fort Barron arrived.

blocks.x: Welcome or not, it had come.
6. Where Ten Go In and One Comes Out
Two people died in the riot. Cliff agreed with the bank president to send those captured to the frontier, as was customary, and said that hated dirty work could only fall to mercenaries.

Around then, at the restaurant, Jessica brought up the bullet and the photograph in the drawer with Woodrow. The bank and the mercenaries were driving out the residents, she said, and she asked him to persuade her boss as an old friend. Only then did Woodrow learn that Cliff had changed his name.
Asked why she was going this far, Jessica told him about Victoria, where she had only stood by and watched. Woodrow said only that he had been looking for the bullet for a long time, and thanked her.

Meanwhile, out in the street, Blacksteel mercenaries were dragging a woman raising a child alone out of her home. When Jessica offered them money, a mercenary sneered that if Raythean's little lady wanted to help, she could go to the bank and pay off everyone's debts.

Jessica went straight to the bank and, for the first time since joining Blacksteel, gave her father's name: Bernie Brynley. But the plate's debt, due by spring, came to 28,450,000 gold certificates, and her account could not buy the plate even a month of stability.

In the meantime, Woodrow went to Fort Barron to see Cliff, and Helena, left at the restaurant, told Jessica the story behind the photograph. During the War of Independence, she said, a choice Cliff made had left Woodrow and one other man captured by the enemy and imprisoned in **Camp Collus**.

blocks.cap: Autumn 1019, Camp Collus. Woodrow, who had survived, sat across from the comrade who never came.

blocks.x: Cliff had drawn up a rescue plan and never came. The Sankta captured alongside Woodrow fell ill with fever and died, letting go of Woodrow's sleeve. The brown certificate Jessica had seen was the color of dried blood.
Back in the present, aboard Fort Barron, Woodrow asked whether Cliff had ever gone to see that friend, buried on the hillside behind the camp. Cliff answered that he had not had the time.
The bullet was that friend's only keepsake. When Woodrow told him to stop driving out the residents, Cliff answered that the government would only send another company.
I swear—if any of them get hurt because you got involved, then so help me God I will return this bullet to you. In one piece.
That day Helena, too, gave Jessica back her check, saying she would leave for the frontier. And Liskarm's squad received orders to guard the bank around the clock.
7. A Song on New Year's Day

On New Year's Day, people gathered in front of the bank. Most of them had already signed pioneer contracts. Among them was Helena, who said she had come to see the ones responsible for making her part with all of this.
That's right. We walked this road ourselves, but you were the ones who pointed us down it...

On the television inside the bank, the governor announced a redevelopment plan for Davistown. Outside, the people sang. It was a song about giving everything for an empty check, only to find no place for themselves in the future.
Holding out a contract delegating emergency powers from the state government, the manager ordered Liskarm to disperse the crowd.

blocks.cap: Before the manager and the contract, Liskarm and Franka did not move.

blocks.x: Let me say this again—I will not open fire, nor will I allow any of my squad members to do so.

Those people had only come to say goodbye, Liskarm added, and partings were always sad. Franka told the manager to go back inside. It was an honest song, she said. It would do no harm to listen to it a while.

Meanwhile, Jessica ran to Fort Barron. Cliff, who said the residents' affairs had nothing to do with either of them, asked her in return why she, who had no shortage of money, had become a mercenary at all. Jessica answered that she had wanted to prove she was no less than her brothers and sisters.

When Cliff told her to be mature and rational, Jessica said that decades ago he had stood by while his friend was taken prisoner, and that now he was standing by while people were driven from their homes.
Then I'd rather stay naive my entire life... I'd rather remain a mediocre fool.
After Jessica left, Cliff made it clear to the bank president that no one would command his people without his consent.

That day, among papers from more than a decade before, Sylvia found a blank contract prepared in advance in Leone's name. The bank had been after everything here from the very beginning, and the manager did not hide it.
Meanwhile, at the restaurant, Helena told Woodrow it was fine to look back now and then, but not to have regrets, and asked him to dance.

That same night, as Sylvia stood alone before the vault, her mother's voice came back to her. Before that voice, which had said it would be proud of her no matter what she did, she murmured that she wanted to be her mom's pride forever.
8. Snow in the Vault

On the day they left for the frontier after the New Year, Miles, trying to comfort Jessica as she blamed herself, misspoke. He had never expected her to accomplish anything in the first place. Jessica said he was right. Nothing had changed.
At the same hour, Sylvia appeared before Leone, who was drinking alone at the restaurant. Seeing the silver ring hanging from her neck, Leone recognized who had given it to her.

When Helena and Woodrow returned, Sylvia told them that a fortune brought in by Blacksteel was locked in the vault. It was a reserve fund for new residents, and with that money, a great many people could start over on the frontier.

When Leone said he did not want to become scum like those thugs, Woodrow told him it was not the thugs who had done the most harm here. Sylvia recited the number of steps from the front door to the vault without a pause. It was a path she had walked countless times.

Helena brought out the weapons she had hidden beneath the floorboards, and Leone set a wrench down beside them. When Jessica came in just then, Woodrow leveled his gun at her and told her to forget all of it and go back.
Jessica walked past the muzzle to Sylvia, drew her own gun, and laid it down.

Then Jessica said goodbye to her squad. When Liskarm asked whether she knew what she was trading away, she answered that she did not, but that she had to do it. Laura, giving her one last hug, slipped a note into her pocket.
In the meantime, Leone gathered the mine's last explosives. His part was to blow up the energy tower, bury the secret passage, and hide Helena's trail.

Meanwhile, as Helena taught Jessica how to handle a welding torch, she finished the story of the man who had left her the restaurant. She had turned down his proposal and left, and by the time she came back after receiving his letter saying he had fulfilled his long-held wish, it was already too late. She had more than enough to wish undone, she said, but she regretted nothing.
In the forest after her squad had gone, Woodrow told Jessica that an answer only she believed in was not necessarily a wrong one.

blocks.cap: "You're still young. Got a long road ahead of you."

blocks.x: In the empty safehouse, Jessica unfolded the note and, as it instructed, found her gear behind the eighth plank. At the end of the note was written: "Goodbye, Jessica. I hope we got to say a proper goodbye."

Then, that night, the four of them hit the bank. The bank president spat out the password under a countdown, and the manager, reading out the numbers, mocked Leone: if he had not been so greedy, he could have taken his children and left.
The last security door was opened by Leone's explosives, as precisely as surgery.

blocks.cap: Torn banknotes poured down, more than all the snow in Davistown.

blocks.x: It was far less than what the bank had taken from them, Leone said. Jessica said it was the first time in her life she had ever wanted money this badly.
9. Run, and Don't Look Back

Blacksteel would arrive in ten minutes. Woodrow counted his bullets and stayed behind to buy an hour, thanking Jessica for carrying the bullet all this way. Leaving only a promise that they would meet again, he walked out into the dark.

Meanwhile, aboard Fort Barron, Cliff ordered that Jessica not be harmed and that Woodrow be taken alive. While Jessica pinned down the pursuers with a remote-controlled sniper rifle left in the restaurant, Woodrow held off several squads alone on the main street.

To a young man who called him a legendary mercenary, Woodrow answered that the one he had wanted to save had died before his eyes, and what he had wanted to protect was gone. He was nothing but an old beckbeast, and a failure.
Around then, inside the energy tower, Leone sent Helena off through the secret passage. He would hold everything off from behind, he said. She was to keep running forward and not look back.
As Leone, now alone, set the charges one by one, Miles, Benny, Carl, and the mother whose face he could not even remember appeared in the firelight one after another, then faded.
Over the radio, Leone left Jessica a message for Sylvia. Thank you for loving Carl. The living are allowed to choose once more. But Leone himself would not leave, he said.
My life didn't begin the day I was born. It began the day I got here. And it won't end the day I die. It'll end the day I leave this place.
He would not die, Leone said. He would live on forever in her embrace.

blocks.cap: An explosion sounded from high above. Then the snow fell.

blocks.x: Knocked down by the shockwave, Jessica tried to get up and run, but her body would not move. Smoke poured from the cracks in the tower, and no matter how long she waited, Leone did not come out.
At the same moment, in the underground passage, Helena began to look back, then stopped, and ran on into the dark without ever turning around.

That same night, Woodrow, his shoulder burned by the blast, traced the engraving on the bullet with his fingers. In Lateran, it read 'forgiveness.' What the heart cannot forgive, he muttered, only a bullet can.
10. For Their Sorrow

Instead of hiding, Woodrow headed for Fort Barron. Cliff said he had founded Blacksteel so that, if he could not end war, he could at least hold the switch. Then why, Woodrow asked, could he not stop for even a few seconds here? Davistown was not a battlefield, came the answer.
In his youth, Woodrow had carried a pen everywhere, hoping to leave a painting on the dome of a cathedral. Four of his fingers had since been severed and reattached.
At the same hour, Jessica walked the ruined alleys with weapons on her back. Liskarm and Franka, who said they had come as friends, reached her first, but she did not lower her gun.
Taking a life takes only a second, Jessica said, but forgetting that second takes a lifetime. Even so, this gun was the only thing she owned that had any power.
Liskarm cut her off. Five years ago, she had chosen Jessica as her assistant not for her gun, but for her tears.
Only someone who's able to empathize with the pain of others can throw herself into a cause for a group of strangers, or a place she barely knows.

Meanwhile, at Fort Barron, the wind tore Woodrow's hat away, and his halo flickered wildly. When Cliff asked by what right he meant to shoot, Woodrow answered: as an ordinary man who had lost everything and had nothing left but anger.

blocks.cap: Before the hat that had blown away touched the ground, the hands of both Sankta went for their guns at once.

blocks.x: A shot rang out, and it was Cliff who lost. When he asked Woodrow to finish him, Woodrow called him by an old name no one else knew. Rupert.

The communicator that rang just then carried word from the military, a sign of yet another war to come. Woodrow shot the communicator to pieces, told Cliff that this sin was his to answer for, then laid down his gun and raised both hands.

Back in the alley, Jessica looked over the battered industrial district. She knew the tower that had given people warmth, the restaurant that had sung all night, and the people whose tears no one ever noticed.

blocks.cap: Faces rising beyond the scope. A woman running across the snow, an old man drawing his gun in the dark, a man who departed into the flames.

blocks.x: My tears... can't stand in for their sadness. / But my gun will cry for their sorrow.
Jessica fired every bullet into the sky, and amid the echoes she heard her own tears falling to the ground. Then, with her gun still at her hip, she raised her hands.
The handcuffs Franka fastened on her were not cold; they had been held in a hand for too long. On the morning the snow stopped, Jessica hummed that song.
Epilogue — A Castle on the Sand

Woodrow, who had hit his head during the arrest, woke three days later, and Cliff told him that Jessica was safe. Helena was being escorted by Cliff's people. The money would be laundered and delivered to Sylvia, who was waiting on the frontier.
Woodrow turned down the offer to live out his days quietly at a house in the south, saying he would go to see his family. Cliff asked only one thing of him: don't die somewhere I don't know about.
Then Cliff called the bank president. The deal was this: he would cover the hole left by the missing money, in exchange for signatures on a few documents and the president's silence.

Meanwhile, Jessica told the lawyer her family had sent that she would go to the frontier. She had broken the law, so she had to pay the price. Because Cliff refused to accept her resignation, she went to the frontier still a Blacksteel employee.

Around the same time, as she prepared to ship out, Laura found a note in her coat pocket. Jessica had done the same thing during their farewell hug. If money ever ran short, it said, call this number.

And on the snowfield, Jessica set out for the frontier with Woodrow. She had always chased after things and arrived a step too late, she said, but this time she would be there from the very beginning.

blocks.cap: When she was little, her grandfather told her they would rebuild the sandcastle the waves had knocked down, together.

blocks.x: Even if you lose everything, the future is still there, so don't be afraid to start over. Her grandfather had told her that once. Only now did Jessica answer. Yes. Let's start over.

blocks.cap: The wide-brimmed hat hid half of Jessica's face.

blocks.x: Ain't nothing to be ashamed of, crying... Jessica. New lives always start in tears.

blocks.cap: Beneath the hat, the tears broke loose. The sky at the far edge of the snowfield turned red with dawn.

blocks.x: The old man did not bow his head; he kept his gaze on the horizon. In that crimson light, he too nearly wept.

The warm plate that a mercenary on the Chernobog front had wanted to go back and see had gone dark. Those who remembered that winter scattered to the frontier, and Jessica, who had made her gun cry for their sorrow, took that road too.

act27side.tagline: A volcanologist who came to sort through her parents' research gets roped into a treasure hunt by a talking sheep, and ends up running through an entire summer in a city that's about to move house. And then: pure white ash settling over an old hometown.

chars.name: Adele
chars.desc: Daughter of the Naumanns and a young volcanologist. Carries on her parents' research while living with Oripathy · Operator Eyjafjalla

chars.name: Dolly
chars.desc: A fluffy creature of unknown origin. Out of nowhere, he proposes a treasure hunt to Adele.

chars.name: Keller
chars.desc: An old colleague of the Naumanns and director of the new volcano museum. Seems to be hiding something.

chars.name: Kahn
chars.desc: A volcanologist who was once Magna Naumann's student. Can't shake his suspicions about Keller.

chars.name: Katia
chars.desc: Adele's father. A volcanologist who studied Originium.

chars.name: Magna
chars.desc: Adele's mother. A volcanologist who studied ecological environments.

chars.name: Swire
chars.desc: Superintendent of the Lungmen Guard Department. A conglomerate heiress who insists she's on vacation, though nobody believes it.

chars.name: Snowsant
