chars.desc: An engineer from Lungmen. Tags along on Swire's vacation thanks to a prize coupon.

chars.name: Bison
chars.desc: Heir to MountainDash Logistics. A conscientious young master trying to step out of his father's shadow.

chars.name: Enis
chars.desc: A Siesta boy juggling several part-time jobs to look after his family. His own health comes last.

chars.name: Harley
chars.desc: Owner of the cocktail bar 'White Volcano' and Enis's mother. Used to play rock.

chars.name: Liv
chars.desc: Enis's little sister. Insists she saw baby sheep.

chars.name: Byrd
chars.desc: A wandering singer from Columbia. Takes stories as payment for her songs.

chars.name: Costa
chars.desc: A city hall clerk going around collecting relocation letters of intent. Grandson of the owner of the shuttered Mockingbird Café.

chars.name: Pelipper
chars.desc: Owner of the Obsidian Hot Springs Hotel. A collector who can't resist anything made of obsidian.

chars.name: Ceylon
chars.desc: Daughter of Siesta's mayor and a Rhodes Island doctor. Things are awkward between her and her father.

chars.name: Herman
chars.desc: Mayor of Siesta. Draws the citizens' resentment by pushing through the city's relocation.

chars.name: Barbara
chars.desc: A scholar from Victoria. Frequented old Siesta's obsidian mines and helped the miners.

chars.name: Schwarz
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator who calls Ceylon 'Milady.'

terms.name: Siesta
terms.desc: A free city on the southern coast that made its living from its volcano, obsidian, and rock music. To escape volcanic activity, it moved onto a nomadic city.

terms.name: Little Black Sheep
terms.desc: Small fluffy sheep that keep turning up around Adele. They carry off anything that catches their eye in their mouths.

terms.name: Obsidian Festival
terms.desc: The rock music festival once held in Siesta. It came to an end when the city relocated.

terms.name: obsidian
terms.desc: Ore once mined from Siesta's volcano. It used to be the city's main source of income, until mining was banned over environmental damage.

terms.name: Volcano Watchers
terms.desc: A legendary plant said to change color with volcanic activity. The Naumanns searched for it while they were alive.

terms.name: Mount Unna
terms.desc: A volcano in northern Leithanien. The last place the Naumanns surveyed.

terms.name: White Volcano
terms.desc: The cocktail bar run by Enis's family. Its name comes from one of Siesta's legends.

terms.name: Mockingbird Café
terms.desc: An old café on the commercial street. Its doors have been shut for a year.

terms.name: Whistling Rock
terms.desc: A volcanic stone that sounds like a musical instrument when the wind blows through it. Fairly rare.

terms.name: Mountaincomm Trade
terms.desc: A subsidiary of MountainDash Logistics, with Bison at its head.

blocks.x: "Whoops, got it wrong again." Somewhere, someone is counting sheep. And at number five thousand seven hundred sixty-two, they lose count yet again.

**Siesta**, a free city on the southern coast, left its beach behind to escape volcanic activity and moved, lock, stock, and barrel, onto a nomadic city. It used to be a resort famous for its volcano, obsidian, and rock music, but the tourists stopped coming, and the Obsidian Festival disappeared too.

In the summer of 1099, the volcano back at that old hometown is finally about to erupt. **Adele** (Eyjafjalla), a young volcanologist invited to observe it, is about to meet two things in this city at once: the younger days of her parents, who are no longer in this world, and something very, very fluffy.
1. The Superintendent Who Calls It a Vacation, Then Rips Out a Bug

That summer, **Swire** of the Lungmen Guard Department insists that this time, it really is a vacation. Then, right next to **Snowsant**—who won a coupon and tagged along—she rummages through the car and fishes out a tracker with a built-in wiretap.

Scoffing that it's an old model the L.G.D. already phased out, she calls someone to report her arrival, then passes the tracker off to the truck waiting at the light beside them and sends it on a solo sightseeing tour of Siesta.

blocks.cap: Tracker in one hand, a leisurely phone call in the other.

blocks.x: Right in the middle of downtown, the buildings rise up in the shape of a mountain. You can't exactly bring a volcano with you, so they built them to look like one, in memory of the old hometown.

blocks.cap: A downtown 'volcano' rising out of the hot-spring mist.

blocks.x: Next, Swire presses a wad of bills into the hand of a passing delivery boy, **Enis**—twice—and rents his entire pickup truck. Enis is no pushover either: he quietly rigs the meter to squeeze out a little extra... though he confesses on the spot the moment Swire pulls out a lipstick.

Asked to shake off a tail, Enis floors it, declaring it's "for a just cause." They lose the tail, and the truck, which he'd only just fixed with two weeks' wages, breaks down all over again. And where they get out, in front of a shop with no sign, **Bison**, heir to MountainDash Logistics, appears.
2. The Protective Suit Behind the Glass

The same day, at the newly built volcano museum. Adele stands frozen in front of a volcano-survey protective suit still marked with cracks and soot. It belonged to someone who used to come running home covered in dust, calling, "Adele, I'm home."

blocks.cap: Between a hand reaching for the suit and a thick pane of glass. A memory, hung up as an exhibit.

blocks.x: The placard reads: Katia Naumann (1051–1095), Magna Naumann (1053–1095). Adele's dad and mom, who died in the accident on Mount Unna.

The one who invited Adele was **Keller**, an old colleague who spent over a decade on volcanoes with her parents. A Siesta native, she came back at the urging of Mayor **Herman** and built the museum—but when Adele asks to hear more about her parents' old days, Keller cuts her off: "Now is not the time to chat."

That night, Adele is walked home by **Kahn**, a volcanologist who was once her mother Magna's student. Oripathy has left Adele barely able to hear without a hearing aid, but she laughs that she's even mastered lip reading. Kahn mutters that it's unfair, and then, finally, warns her: watch out for Keller.
But his words don't quite reach Adele. Another voice, one only she can hear, keeps butting in. "My, my. Here's another one so stubborn it gives me a headache."
3. One Sheep, Two Sheep, Talking Sheep

After Kahn leaves, the owner of the voice drifts down like a cloud and plops onto a mailbox. A ball of fluff that looks exactly like the **Little Black Sheep** that always hang around Adele—except this one talks.
Following him to the unfinished plate, Adele finds countless sheep leaping and tumbling over the shipping containers, and only then does the flock's master introduce himself. "Call me **Dolly**."

blocks.cap: One, two, three... balls of fluff settling under the moonlight.

blocks.x: Dolly says these sheep are his alter egos, and that he remembers Adele's parents too. The volcano taking those two friends was, apparently, 'the eleventh worst thing' to happen in recent years. For the record, surfing in magma is the second best thing in the world.
The past isn't truly gone. It stays by your side, in one way or another.

Asked whether she's having fun right now, Adele answers that it's hard but rewarding. "So you're not happy," Dolly shoots back—and proposes a game. Find the **North Wind, a seed, and a fur** he lost in Siesta, and he'll give her "that which you have been seeking."
4. A Bidding War, and a Sheep That Eats Addresses

Meanwhile, at that sign-less shop—a cocktail bar—Swire and Bison are crossing swords. The Swire family's group has made the bidding list for redeveloping the commercial district. Bison has a logistics hub in mind, and Swire needles him ever so gently: "Why not turn the whole place into a hot spring resort instead?"

Overhearing this at the next table, Enis chokes on his drink. This bar, on this very street slated for demolition, is his home. The owner is Enis's mom, **Harley**, a former rocker who sends city hall clerk **Costa** and his relocation letters of intent packing: "This place is home to me and my three kids."
Then a package arrives at the museum from Wilhelm University in Leithanien. Inside one envelope, its edges chewed ragged, is a photo of Mount Unna.

blocks.who: Writing on the back of the photo
blocks.x: The volcano is a spectacular sight. The winds are strong at the peak. ——Love, Your Father

Adele asks around about the sender, but all that's left on the envelope is the word 'Volcano.' Then one day, visiting the hot spring hotel of obsessive collector **Pelipper** for an obsidian sample, she spots the culprit: a Little Black Sheep, slowly munching its way through a signpost and an address plate.

blocks.cap: Pelipper's Obsidian Hot Springs Hotel, where the sign thief showed up.

blocks.x: Chasing the sheep, Adele runs headlong into Enis, who's dashing along with his arms full of packages, and goes down.

When Adele comes to, the doctor, **Ceylon**, tells her that Enis paid for her treatment with every last bit of money he had on him. And Enis himself has Oripathy, with crystals growing close to his heart.
Alone in the hospital room, Adele takes out the photo and writes a letter. "Mutti, Vati, in just a few more years, I'll be the age you were when you had me."
Drip, drip. Tears fall onto the paper, and Adele erases what she wrote.
Around then, Enis is cursing out a truck that won't start when Swire catches him red-handed. The box on the passenger seat bears the Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals logo.
5. The White Volcano
What Swire offers is a deal: she'll pretend she never saw a thing, if he becomes her local helper in the bidding war.
Swire makes him promise not to put off his treatment, and when he asks if she's really fine being this close to one of the Infected, she answers briefly: "I have a friend who's Infected too."

Meanwhile, a little brother and sister have snuck into the museum looking for photos of their explorer dad. Adele tells them how their dad once rescued her parents when they got lost in the Sargon jungle—a slightly altered version of an old story she heard from her mother. "Science is also meant to give people 'hope.'"

Where she takes the kids home turns out to be that very bar. Enis and his two siblings are all adopted, each of a different race, and their dad, Chuck, wanders the land and only ever sends home photos.

Then Harley plants herself in front of Enis. Was he planning to take care of everything on his own, leave, and just wait to die of Oripathy somewhere far from home? Harley knew all along that he'd gotten infected secretly mining obsidian.
Enis, even if you didn't do a thing, you'd still be their big brother, and my son. This isn't the kind of relationship that needs a bargain.
The silence is broken by **Byrd**, a wandering musician who has become the bar's resident singer. When she sings an old song born in Siesta, Dolly cries out: "I remember now!"

blocks.cap: "The North Wind blows a hundred miles, visiting the first volcano ♪"

blocks.x: The first treasure, the 'North Wind,' was the lyrics to this song that had been ringing in his ears all along. A melody whose lyrics you can't remember is, so he says, the seventh most painful thing in the world.

Then Enis rehangs the broken sign, and the neon flickers to life. 'White Volcano.' It's the name of the legend Harley and Chuck chased in their youth: a volcano where the whole mountain turns white as a marshmallow.
Only then does Adele realize: the letter addressed to 'Volcano' was meant for this bar. A hope that was never spoken aloud found its way to its rightful owner after all.

That night, Kahn says it plainly this time. In the year before her parents died, the army of a Leithanian Kurfürst came and went from their lab, and back then, only one person had access to that research. "...Keller."
6. To Summon Sheep, Shout "Ice Cream"

That night, Adele dreams of being invited to a sheep party, and the next day Enis's little sister **Liv** insists she went to a baby-sheep party and gets banned from ice cream for it. Around the same time, Bison's trade fair warehouse is found turned upside down and covered in footprints.

Meanwhile, the 1095 Mount Unna expedition log turns up at the museum. Team members: Katia, Magna, Keller. According to Kahn, Keller suddenly left the team the day before the climb, and right after the accident, she showed up at a meeting with the Leithanian government.

Dolly, for his part, teaches Adele how to round up the culprits: don't call them 'Little Black Sheep'—shout the bait instead. Adele yells, "Ice cream over here!" and the ones who come swarming are... tourists. Dolly slips away in the commotion.

Soon after, a Little Black Sheep with the Whistling Rock that went missing from the museum tucked into its fleece makes off with a tourist's wallet too, and Adele gives chase across the commercial street.

blocks.cap: The commercial street, lined with old beach-style shops. Stage of the great Little Black Sheep chase.

blocks.x: The sheep ducks into **Mockingbird Café**, which has been locked up for a year. Costa shows up with the key, says this shop is going to be demolished soon too, and asks Adele to return a dusty copy of The Atlas of Terra's Volcanoes to Keller at the museum.

Keller, it turns out, used to be a regular here. One summer she left with two Leithanians and was never heard from again—until a few days ago, when her face reappeared, reflected in the glass of a museum display case. "You're... you're back?"
7. Flying Surfboards

A few days later, Costa holds out a relocation letter of intent to his bedridden grandfather, the owner of Mockingbird Café. Having asked for one song on the guitar and been turned down, the old man finally takes the pen and grumbles: "I should've tossed you into the sea back when you were making drip coffee with sparkling water."
"Thanks for not doing that... I love you, Grandpa."

Then, on the day Bison's trade fair opens, Swire has Adele close her eyes and leads her to the hot spring hotel she's borrowed from Pelipper. What opens up before them is a water park designed by Snowsant. Surf kayaks fly from channel to channel, and when they fall, airbags catch them.
Then, out of nowhere, surfboards start flying through the sky. Everyone else sees only surfboards, but Adele can see the sheep riding on top of them.

blocks.cap: Surfboards soaring on the hot-spring steam. Only Adele can see the passengers.

blocks.x: Swire and Snowsant eye each other suspiciously, then both turn to look at Adele—and Swire hops straight onto a surfboard anyway.
At dusk, Harley takes a surfboard back from Adele and, gazing at a street full of laughter, murmurs: "It's like we've gone back years and years."
That evening, Costa turns on the café lights for the first time in a year and brews coffee alone. And the customer who knocks on the door is Keller. "Are you still open?"

blocks.cap: Mockingbird Café, lit up for the first time in a year. The barista and an old regular.

blocks.x: The two of them talk about the old days. How Costa would deliberately blast heavy metal whenever 'those two very interesting people' came by the café. How he served them 'volcanic coffee,' secretly spiked with sparkling water.
Asked how those two are doing, Keller answers briefly. They parted ways a few years ago and she can never see them again, she says—so she built the museum to preserve their research.

As Adele, outside the window, quietly turns away, the sheep trot off in a line, each with a sparkling-water bottle cap in its mouth. According to Dolly, these are the second treasure, the 'seed': things that crossed to faraway lands, put down roots, and became something else entirely. One of the sheep, it seems, has had volcanic coffee in Columbia.
That night, Costa gets a phone call. His grandfather has passed away peacefully.
8. Before the Rain

And Adele dreams again. Wearing her mother's coat, she is joined by a gentle sheep and a solemn sheep, and the three of them buy 'knowledge,' 'curiosity,' and 'luck' to prepare for the climb up the volcano. The gentle sheep never manages to buy enough 'courage' to leave home, and she hides a 'photograph' deep in her bag so no one can steal it.
"What's a 'photograph'?" "Shh. I hope you never find out."

Leaping up into the sky, the sheep tell her the story of a pebble. A pebble planted in the ground wandered through countless mountains and rivers, became magma, and flowed on without looking back. Someday it will fall to the earth again as volcanic ash. So you, too, should plant a pebble of your own.
When Adele offers to buy flowers and make them a garland, the two sheep stop where they are and withdraw into the lights of the night.

blocks.cap: "We have to head up the volcano before it starts to rain."

blocks.x: This land is not pure. But nothing can stand in the way of a seeker's heart in search of answers.
"So long, Adele."

Later, Adele dozes off at the museum and wakes murmuring "...Mutti." Keller is beside her. Adele asks what happened at Wilhelm University that year, and whether 'rain' means something else. Keller bites her lip, then makes a promise. "When this observation is over, I will tell you everything."
From that day on, Dolly stops answering. Not a single sheep can be seen on the streets, and the broadcasts announce three days left until the eruption.

On the day the Mockingbird's sign comes down, Costa tells Enis, the kid from next door in the old days: there's no such thing as the best of times. So if there's something you want to do, do it before the familiar things lose their shape.
But that night, outside the office door, one sheep remains, a miner's lamp strapped to its back. It is the very sheep that ate the address off the letter.
9. Thump, Thump
And Byrd can see that sheep too. Playing her guitar on the shore within sight of old Siesta, she guesses that it eats signs because it is lost.

blocks.cap: The shore at the edge of the unfinished plate. Old Siesta is visible in the distance.

blocks.x: Setting off again, the sheep presses its head to Adele's chest and listens to her heartbeat, then hangs its head as if to say it isn't the one, and walks on. Following after it, Adele runs into Keller, who walks alongside her and begins to talk about the old days.

She first met Katia and Magna at Mockingbird Café. The two of them were like flames, brighter than obsidian. After Keller once stepped into a scalding pool, Magna never left her side for a moment. "...Some things, I've found, are truly hard to say aloud."

Meanwhile, with Enis leading the way, Ceylon tracks down the miners secretly digging for obsidian. Looking at Ceylon's face, an old miner is reminded of a scholar who used to come to the mines long ago. A woman from Victoria who came to the mine every day, even while pregnant, to help the miners: **Barbara**.

At Pelipper's hotel, where Ceylon goes to ask for help, he freezes when she gives her name. "Ceylon Doykos." The obsidian geode Pelipper brings out was a gift the miners had meant to give Barbara long ago, to celebrate her baby's birth, but never managed to deliver.

In that moment, the lost sheep comes running as if entranced and leans its head against Ceylon's chest. Thump, thump. The tiny heartbeat that once beat inside Barbara, long ago, had grown up this much.
For the first time, Ceylon sees the sheep. It touches the geode with the tip of its nose, then presses it to Ceylon's forehead, and vanishes into the mist. "...A farewell, and a reunion as well."
10. The Curtain Falls

Meanwhile, Swire, ahead in the opinion poll, offers to drop out of the bidding in exchange for shares in MountainDash's Siesta branch. Once the city hall staffer leaves, Bison bursts out laughing. "So the show's finally over?" The whole rivalry was staged by the two of them to fool their families' watchful eyes.

The counterattack comes right away. Bison's company is reported for illegally employing unregistered Infected, Swire receives a warning from her family, and Mayor Herman comes under pressure from Columbia over its law on medical insurance for the Infected.

Back from seeing Pelipper, Ceylon goes to her father Herman and, for the first time, tells him, "It's been hard for you, Dad," before proposing that they build a settlement zone and a treatment center for the Infected. Only then does Herman speak of Barbara, the wife he could never publicly acknowledge because she was from Victoria.
You never lived a single day with Barbara, and yet just now you said exactly what she would have said.

Meanwhile, Swire records a video for her grandfather Adams in Lungmen. This round, the one in which he was watching her, she has won. And she intends to start preparing now for how Lungmen will be kept in order once he is gone.

blocks.cap: "But if you are the one standing opposite me, then I've won this time."

blocks.x: At the same time, Bison reports to his father Eurill that **Mountaincomm Trade**, the company he runs, is going independent. He has already found a reliable partner, he says.

blocks.cap: The independence report, presented to his father Eurill.

blocks.x: 11. Volcano Day

On the night before the eruption, the people of the commercial district throw a container party on the unfinished plate. Bringing out a bottle she had been saving, Harley tells Enis how, on the day she and Chuck were about to leave to keep chasing the legend, they found a baby sleeping soundly in a corner of the old Fashion Street. "I care more about you kids than the White Volcano."

At the same time, the monitoring station halfway up the volcano sends back some strange data, and then its signal cuts out. Keller wants to write it off as an equipment failure, but Adele does not back down.
If we run away now... isn't that the same as admitting their sacrifice was for nothing?

Getting her mother's protective suit back, Adele climbs the volcano with Keller. At the foot of the mountain, Keller cannot take a single step, and Adele holds out her hand. Kahn comes after them, carrying the two missing notebook pages, written in Katia's hand and stamped with the wax seal of the Leithanian military.
While Kahn is confronting Keller, the volcano shakes. Adele shields her companions, and in the instant rocks come crashing down behind her, every sound stops.
In a stillness where time seems to have stopped, Dolly is there. All three of them are safe, he says, and he apologizes: it was the sheep playing in the crater that broke the monitoring equipment.

blocks.cap: "This is just the right temperature." Dolly in the boiling magma.

blocks.x: Dolly comes clean. The sheep are not his alter egos; they are creatures he made in the image of people he has met over long years, and they are not souls or anything of the kind. The last treasure, the 'fur,' was her mother's old protective suit, which had just been damaged once again.

Telling her it is all right to stop and cry her heart out when she is tired, Dolly kisses Adele on the cheek. And the promised reward, the **Volcano Watchers**, he had secretly planted on the far slope of this very volcano, which is about to erupt.

At the same time, on the beach where seawater is surging in, Enis finds Liv, who had gone out alone, and raises a wall of earth with Originium Arts he learned in secret. The wall crumbles, and just as the next wave is about to crash over them, countless sheep come running and build a levee out of their fleece.

blocks.cap: A levee of fleece, like white sea spray turned solid. The waves soaked in, every last drop.

blocks.x: And smoke rises from the crater. As if by prior agreement, people take the hands of whoever is beside them. When old Tom from the ice cream shop talks about his children in Columbia, Bison promises to send his postcards free of charge, and the old man sings an old song in an unsteady voice.

On the commercial street, before the eyes of Ceylon, standing beside the just-arrived **Schwarz**, pink dust covers half the sky and then slowly settles. Someone murmurs that the top of the volcano has turned white.

blocks.cap: "Goodbye, Siesta." The night an old hometown vanished beneath the ash.

blocks.x: Epilogue — A Clear Day

After the observation, Keller brings out a box, as promised. 'Projekt Regenschauer,' with 'Obsolete' stamped over 'Highly Confidential.' It shared its name with the 'rain' that the sheep in the dream had said they must go before.

Caught up in a dispute among the nobility, Katia handed part of his findings to the military so the research could continue, and Keller helped with the follow-up work. When the military's messenger came again the day before the Mount Unna climb, Keller went to the military in their place to buy time, so the two could finish their survey undisturbed. The accident happened in the meantime.
Keller says she will not ask for forgiveness. Adele answers that she does not suspect anyone, and then asks, "Professor Keller, can I give you a hug?"

At the very bottom of the box is a handwritten letter asking that these materials be used for the right things, signed 'Adele Keller.' It was the name of the student whom Magna, long ago, on the day they first climbed a volcano together, had called "such a lovely name."

Meanwhile, Enis, waking after three days, turns down Ceylon's job offer. He wants to ride that landship she mentioned, the one that goes to all sorts of places. He wants to see the sights his father saw.

Startled by the sound of construction, they rush over, but the White Volcano has not been torn down. City hall has decided to preserve the street as a tourist attraction, and the foreign company that bought up the shops is building a water park here.
In front of the bar sit a brand-new pickup truck and a note. "Helping a friend with some minor troubles."
Far away in Lungmen, old Adams watches the video, says, "She's finally pulled one off," and laughs heartily with Wei Yenwu, then collapses. Wei Yenwu hurriedly calls for a doctor.
And Adele writes a letter to her parents. She does not know where to send it, but there are things she wants them to know.

blocks.cap: A letter with nowhere to go. A letter that had to be written all the same.

blocks.x: Fear is not the opposite of courage, just as death is not the opposite of life. I love researching volcanoes, and at the same time, I love my own life too.
Enis, who offers to post the letter for her, is holding a single flower. He picked it on the far slope of the volcano, but it changed color once he came down the mountain.

blocks.cap: A single flower that changed color on the way down the volcano.

blocks.x: "Oh, and the thing you two came to Siesta looking for? I found that too."
And atop the volcano, now turned white, two sheep stand side by side. "How long will we have to wait to see the next eruption?" "It's all right. We have plenty of time."

One, two, three. Among the balls of fluff that ran all over Siesta that summer were little ones who wore the shapes of people now gone. Adele believes Dolly's words now: the past does not simply go away. It stays by your side, in another form.

act26side.tagline: A Saint, sent in the Pope's place to a monastery in the wastes, watches the garden that Sankta and Sarkaz tended together through years of hunger collapse in a single night. Must there really be only one paradise?

chars.name: Federico
chars.desc: An Executor of Laterano's Notarial Hall. He judges by regulation and lets no emotion in. The first person to receive the title of 'Saint' without being a Pope · Operator Executor the Ex Foedere

chars.name: Lemuen
chars.desc: A Cardinal Aide of the Curia. Contact with her was lost after she was sent to the monastery as a nuncio. She uses a wheelchair because of an injury to her legs

chars.name: Serpilia
chars.desc: A Sankta technician skilled at firearm maintenance. Lemuen's junior from school, she volunteered for this mission herself · Operator Spuria

chars.name: Richele
chars.desc: An Executor of the Notarial Hall sent along with Federico. He does the talking in place of the taciturn Federico

chars.name: Oren
chars.desc: A Legatus of Laterano. He was sent to the monastery with Lemuen, then vanished on his own

chars.name: Yvangelista XI
chars.desc: The Pope of Laterano. Warned of a crisis no one could name, he made Federico a Saint

chars.name: Arturia
chars.desc: A mysterious traveler who appears out of nowhere and plays the cello · Operator Virtuosa

chars.name: Stefano Torregrossa
chars.desc: An old bishop who has kept the mobile monastery Sanctilaminium Ambrosii for more than sixty years

chars.name: Gerald
chars.desc: A seasoned hunter who leads the band of Sarkaz settled at the monastery

chars.name: Clément
chars.desc: The monastery's gentle gardener, who tends its flowers with care

chars.name: Fortuna
chars.desc: A warm, sociable Sankta girl. Close to Delfina and Raimund since childhood

chars.name: Delfina
chars.desc: A Sankta girl. Fortuna's childhood friend, and one who sides with the Sarkaz she grew up with

chars.name: Raimund
chars.desc: A young Sarkaz in Gerald's band. He has grown up at the monastery since childhood

chars.name: Aulus
chars.desc: A gentle missionary who comes and goes from the monastery. He and Stefano go back a long way

chars.name: Erendel
chars.desc: A Liberi boy in ragged clothes. He waits for his mother with his twin, Estara

chars.name: Estara
chars.desc: A Liberi girl in ragged clothes. She waits for her mother with her twin, Erendel

terms.name: Sanctilaminium Ambrosii
terms.desc: A mobile monastery built jointly by Iberia and Laterano in 1011. It strayed from its route decades ago, and all word of it was lost.

terms.name: Saint
terms.desc: A title once reserved for the saints who founded Laterano. Federico is the first to receive it without being a Pope.

terms.name: Fallen Angel
terms.desc: A Sankta who has broken a taboo, so that the halo warps and horns grow from the forehead. They can no longer empathize with their own kind.

terms.name: Church of the Deep
terms.desc: A suspicious religious group said to be active along the coast of Iberia. It is said to turn people into something unknown.

blocks.x: Laterano is often called the eternal paradise. Free and orderly, it is one of the few clean places left on this troubled land.
Then one day, the faith shining above the head of Pope **Yvangelista XI** warned of a crisis. No one knew what the crisis would be or how it would come. All he had was a single list of names.

blocks.cap: "State of emergency." Danger level: maximum.

blocks.x: The first name on the list was **Federico Giallo**, an Executor of the Notarial Hall. The Pope granted him the title of 'Saint,' which in a thousand years no one but a Pope had received.

When Federico asked what disaster was coming, the Pope could not answer. Instead, he handed Federico a mission he had meant to take on himself. The destination was a mobile monastery that had come to a halt in the wastes.
1. Where the Last Flowers Remain

Sanctilaminium Ambrosii is a mobile monastery built jointly by Iberia and Laterano in 1011. Sixty-one years ago it strayed from its route and fell silent. Its fuel exhausted, it now stood still in the middle of the wastes.

The monastery was led by the old bishop **Stefano Torregrossa**. The fields of flowers that once covered it were gone. Only the flowers the gardener **Clément** grew in the sacrarium at the top remained.

blocks.cap: The sacrarium at the top of the monastery. This is the only place the flowers remain.

blocks.x: Before those flowers, the bishop opened his heart to **Arturia**, a traveler who played the cello. Even staying alive was hard now, he said. After drifting this long, he no longer knew whether he was still a man of Laterano.
Where does the believer go, if faith has betrayed itself?
Not only Sankta lived at the monastery. A band of Sarkaz who had drifted in from the wastes more than ten years earlier lived there too, taking on the hunting and the guard duty.

That day, too, the band's leader, the hunter **Gerald**, apologized to the inhabitants for how little game there was, and his comrade Hyman did not come back from the hunt. The young Sarkaz **Raimund** could not contain his anger. Were they really supposed to just accept this?
At the same hour, in the darkness underground, something that had lost its shape was chewing and swallowing without pause. Beside it, a gentle missionary murmured that he felt sorrow.

Meanwhile, in the chapel, the Sankta girls **Fortuna** and **Delfina** were quarreling. The monastery was holding a nuncio from Laterano. Fortuna wanted to go back. Delfina said she could not abandon Raimund and the others.
The two soon made up. Holding the broken patron firearm her father had given her, Fortuna said that one day they would fix it and use it together.
Around then, three people from Laterano reached the monastery. With Federico were his fellow Executor **Richele** and the firearms technician **Serpilia**.

blocks.cap: The monastery appears at the edge of the wastes. Federico chose to go straight through the front.

blocks.x: Their mission was to find the two nuncios who had gone silent: Cardinal Aide **Lemuen** and Legatus **Oren**. If both were already dead, Federico added, it would be enough to bring back their remains.
2. No Place for Sarkaz in Paradise
At the front gate, Raimund blocked their way. While Federico questioned his hostility and held his attention, Serpilia slipped inside alone.

Inside, Serpilia ran into Fortuna, who was carrying a meal to Lemuen. Serpilia pressed her about where Lemuen was. When Fortuna kept silent, Serpilia mentioned that she could repair the rusted patron firearm, took the bowl from her, and disappeared.
In the meantime, a gang of bandits attacked again, and Federico and Richele drove them off. Clément was grateful, but admitted he had expected Laterano to send people to call them to account.

When they finally faced the bishop in the chapel, he said only that Lemuen was being treated as a guest. As for Oren, he said, on the day they 'invited' Lemuen, Oren had broken through the encirclement and fled, and no one knew where he was.
There, saying he had something to confirm, Federico pulled back Gerald's hood. There were horns on his forehead.
Only then did the bishop explain. Laterano had promised aid and a return home. But Lemuen, who said she could concede anything, would not concede one thing. **"Sarkaz have no place in paradise."**
The bishop raised both arms and appealed to the Pope. Without them, we would not have survived. While we lived leaning on one another, where was Laterano, and what was it doing?
Federico's answer was brief. Sarkaz cannot exist in Laterano.

Then Gerald spoke first. He had already talked it over with the band. The Sarkaz would leave. The bishop asked to hold one more sermon and spend one last night here, and said he would give his answer after Matins the next morning.

blocks.cap: The monastery chapel. Here the bishop revealed Laterano's terms.

blocks.x: 3. Sawdust in the Bread

That day, Delfina brought winter clothes to the Sarkaz quarters. Caroline declined, saying they had plenty, and hid something behind her back. Delfina snatched that 'food' away and broke it in half. Inside were tree bark and sawdust.
Meanwhile, Serpilia went to Lemuen's room. The knock code the two had settled on in their school days meant 'Rescue successful. First to arrive.'

But Lemuen said she would not leave. She was not a prisoner; she had chosen to stay, and would wait for a chance to negotiate without provoking the bishop. Serpilia said those efforts would come to nothing and left the room. In the corridor, she exchanged messages with someone in secret.

Fortuna, who had been following her, said she had a favor to ask. In Serpilia's hands the patron firearm came back to life. Holding it, Fortuna was elated. It felt as if she had known how to use it since birth. To thank her, Fortuna brought out the flour and eggs she had been saving, to bake herb pizzelle.

Delfina could not bear the sight. She demanded to know whether Fortuna knew what Caroline was eating right now. Fortuna had changed since the Laterans came, she said, and asked whether it was Lemuen who had fixed that gun.
At the same hour, the bishop ordered this week's sermon moved up to today. When Clément asked whether he truly meant to give up on the others, the bishop told him only to ask no more.

A little later, Gerald walked beside Clément as he went to ring the bell. Gerald spoke of Eileen, a comrade who had died long ago. She was a Sarkaz who had loved looking at this monastery's flowers and hearing its bell. With too little medicine, her wounds festered, and she closed her eyes waiting for the bell to ring.
Gerald said he would go see Eileen. When Clément moved to follow, Gerald turned him back. The stairs up were Clément's path. "Take care, brother."

blocks.cap: The path to the bell. Here Gerald parted ways with Clément.

blocks.x: 4. The Gun They Meant to Share

In the meantime, the argument in Fortuna's room spiraled out of control. Delfina said there was no need to pray to a thing like that, that she was sick of the specialness of the Sankta, and demanded the gun. Fortuna said it was dangerous and would not let go.
A shot rang out.
Delfina never finished her words. "All I want... is for everyone... to stay together..."
Then, into the chapel where the bell had rung for the sermon, Fortuna walked in covered in blood.

blocks.cap: Fortuna enters the chapel. Black horns have grown from her forehead.

blocks.x: Her halo flickered unsteadily, and Fortuna could no longer feel the heart of any Sankta. Federico, who came in after her, spoke. A clear sign of falling. This child has broken the precepts.
Fortuna had become a Fallen Angel.

Fortuna said she had pulled the trigger herself. She would accept any punishment, she begged, if only they would save Fina. Serpilia ran to the room with Clément, but Delfina, shot at very close range, was already dead.
When Clément said the flowers in the sacrarium were medicinal and he would go pick them, Serpilia told him it was no use.

Federico said the sermon should be canceled, the facts kept hidden, and his team would take over the patrols. The bishop pushed back: this was not yet Laterano's land. He asked whether Federico could not hear the wailing of his own people, and when Federico did not deny it, the bishop spoke flatly. If you represent Laterano, then Laterano is not worthy of being my faith.
5. The Burning Sacrarium
That night, Fortuna asked Serpilia, who was keeping watch at her side, whether Fina was dead. Serpilia said she did not want to lie, so Fortuna should ask something else.
When Serpilia began to say that if only she had not fixed that gun, Fortuna stopped her. Then she said that now that she had horns, she was finally the same as Raimund and Caroline.
Meanwhile, a monster covered in scales appeared in Lemuen's room. Lemuen chased it in her wheelchair but lost it, and asked Federico, whom she met on the way, for his help.

At that moment, Federico was hearing the sound of a cello laced with Originium Arts. Lemuen told him she would chase the monster herself and he should follow the sound. Sometimes, she said, you have to trust your instincts.

In the rooftop sacrarium where the sound led him, the ragged twins **Erendel** and **Estara** were waiting. As 'the big sister' had told them, they were waiting for a scary-faced older brother with a black halo to take them to their mother. Then flames shot up.

blocks.cap: Flames that swallowed both the sacrarium and the flower bed.

blocks.x: Clément was held back as he tried to rush into the burning flower bed, and the Sarkaz Raimund had called ran over with buckets.

In the fire, the gun-bearing holy statue toppled toward Raimund, and Federico turned it aside with his arm, saving him. When Raimund asked whether it wasn't their holy statue, Federico answered that it did not matter.
After the fire was out, Federico declared that someone had set it on purpose. Then one of the inhabitants spoke up: earlier, they had seen Raimund near the sacrarium.
6. The Monster Who Tucked Them In
Federico said everyone who had been there was a suspect, and there was no evidence against Raimund. Nor was there any guarantee that a Sankta would not burn the sacrarium.

Then Gerald, who had been watching from a distance, stepped forward and called Federico to the Sarkaz quarters. There, the twins who had followed Federico said they had eaten nothing all day and were hungry. According to them, their mother never ate anything and always said she wasn't hungry.

Federico told them the truth: in that case, their mother must have been suffering the whole time. The children burst into tears. He knelt to meet their eyes and promised to find their mother, since finding missing inhabitants was also part of his mission. The children followed Raimund to Hyman's empty house to sleep.
The same night, Lemuen caught up with the monster, and **Aulus**, a missionary from Iberia, stood in her way. Lemuen pushed her wheelchair aside and stood up.

blocks.cap: Lemuen rises from her wheelchair. "Negotiations... have failed."

blocks.x: Around then, the bishop was repenting alone. He had broken his vow to help all who sought salvation, and he could no longer bear abandoning the few for the sake of the many. If he had to borrow the power of a heretical faith, he would.

blocks.cap: "Why should Laterano alone be paradise?"

blocks.x: Meanwhile, in the quarters, Federico asked Gerald his real reason for leaving. Gerald said it was not because they could not survive. They had to leave before quarrels turned into violence, so they could remain comrades who missed one another.

Then he told the twins' story. The Liberi children had been abandoned and were dying in the wastes when the Sarkaz Hyman secretly took them in, feeding them every day from her own share. Hyman had not come back from the hunt.
At the same hour, the monster had come into Hyman's hut. Murmuring that it was hungry, it gently laid its thick tail over the sleeping children. "Cold... blanket... cover... Eren... Sara..."

blocks.cap: A tail settles quietly over the sleeping children.

blocks.x: Later, facing the monster in front of the hut, Federico recited the regulation: a threat of unknown danger level may be shot on the spot. The monster did not flee. It stood where it was, like a statue.

Gerald stepped in front of it. "Hyman." He told Federico that the children were asleep behind that door and that they trusted him, and pressed down on Federico's gun hand. Little by little, the muzzle lowered.
7. The Hunter's Head

Before leaving the hut, Federico called Gerald by his real name. **Holst Tyfindale**: a mercenary who made his name in the Kazdel Civil War, a fugitive wanted by the Notarial Hall who had wiped out three of the Curia's Executor Maniples. What he knew, others could find out too. That was his final warning.
By then, outside the monastery, Lateran commandos were tightening their encirclement. A Sarkaz scouting party sent out to find a route had already been captured by them.
It was Oren, in hiding, who had called in the unit, and Serpilia had been in contact with him from the start. Their aim was to let not a single person who tried to leave this place get away.
Meanwhile, Raimund, who had just heard of Delfina's death from Clément, ran to get Fortuna out. Fortuna said she would not go. Everyone called Fina's death an 'accident,' but it was her sin.
Then the two overheard Oren and Serpilia talking about 'taking over' the monastery before dawn, and Fortuna changed her mind and decided to go with Raimund.

In the meantime, Gerald woke the band and decided they would leave before daybreak. Clément, who came to see him, also urged them not to wait for tomorrow but to go now. Then a comrade ran in with word that a Lateran unit was closing in on the monastery.
Gerald drew his dagger. In ten years, he said, his mind had never been as calm as it was today.
If only blood can end it all, then there's only one thing left for me to do. Don't worry. Sarkaz never shed blood for nothing.

Meanwhile, in the entrance hall, Federico stopped Oren. Oren said he would take over the monastery on the grounds that the Sarkaz Raimund had set the fire. Federico said Raimund was not the arsonist. Oren asked whether the truth mattered that much. If the Sarkaz resisted, so much the better.
Then the door opened. Clément stood alone in the moonlight.

blocks.cap: Clément, standing with his back to the moonlight. He carried a dagger and something wrapped in cloth.

blocks.x: What was wrapped in the cloth was Gerald's head. Clément said it was offered by the sinner Holst Tyfindale, who alone confessed to every crime.
In return, Gerald left a single request: that Fortuna, Raimund, and the other Sarkaz be let go.
8. A Wound That Does Not Heal

Long ago, Eileen had smiled at the flowers blooming before the holy statue. They had betrayed Her Highness Theresa the moment they left Kazdel, she said, so it was time to let the past go. She wondered what he would look like as a country hunter. Gerald told her that if she was curious, she could see for herself.

He had left Kazdel with his dying comrades and at last found a land that would accept Sarkaz. For a time, that wish came true. But life here slowly rotted, like a feast laid on the table that no one touched.

On the last night, Gerald left words with Clément. As long as he lived, they would have a pretext. He was only going ahead to see Eileen first. And he asked Clément to tell Stefano thank you, and that he was sorry.

When day broke, Clément searched the burned sacrarium for flowers, saying Gerald could not go to meet Eileen empty-handed. Those flowers stood for friendship and hope, and had once brought the Sarkaz and the inhabitants closer.

Federico pointed to a single bloom that had survived beneath the fallen holy statue. But Clément looked at its broken stem and scorched petals and said it was not the flower he wanted. Once a wound forms, however small, it never heals again.
Would Laterano still be Laterano?
After Clément left, saying he would go to Matins, Federico picked up the flower.

blocks.cap: Dawn. The Saint, alone in the empty sacrarium with a single scorched flower.

blocks.x: Federico turned Clément's question over but found no answer. Then it struck him: Clément's face had been far too calm.
Around then, in Hyman's hut, the twins woke. A worn blanket had been laid over them, and the children ran out to tell Federico that their mother had come in the night.
9. The Final Communion
Long ago, an old bishop entrusted this monastery to its youngest monk, Stefano, with one charge: let everyone live in paradise.

Before the final Matins, the bishop divided unleavened bread and wine into individual portions. There was not enough flour, so the bread was mixed with pollen Clément had dried. When an inhabitant who had asked whether everyone would be saved after today had gone, the bishop murmured to himself that they would all be saved.

At the same hour, Richele, searching underground, found a thick flour paste and unidentifiable fragments where the bread had been baked, and muttered that the devout bishop had chosen this path in the end.
Meanwhile, Lemuen blocked Oren's way as he went out to meet the commandos. When Oren told Serpilia to stop Lemuen, she refused.

Oren would not back down. Sarkaz who were set free would surely come back for revenge, he said, and the mere rumor that the monastery had colluded with Sarkaz would bring down Laterano's diplomacy. He would nip it in the bud with a unit of fifty.

Lemuen called it a massacre. The Sarkaz here were only hunters and farmers, and the one mercenary among them was already dead. When Oren tried to bring up her past, the wheelchair charged, and the muzzle of her sniper rifle rammed into his waist.
In the meantime, the commandos planted explosives along every escape route from the monastery and posted snipers. Raimund and Fortuna, slipping out through the front gate, ran straight into the unit.
And in the chapel, the final Matins began. The bishop called those seated side by side, Sankta and Sarkaz alike, neither 'believers' nor 'compatriots,' but 'inhabitants.'

blocks.cap: The final Matins. Sankta and Sarkaz sit in one chapel.

blocks.x: Sanctilaminium Ambrosii is not paradise. But this is our 'home.'
At the same hour, two gunshots split the dawn air outside.

blocks.cap: Warning shots that cut off an argument among three.

blocks.x: They were Federico's warning shots. He told Oren to pull the unit back one kilometer, and told Lemuen and Serpilia to calm the inhabitants. He would keep whatever order this monastery needed himself.
Some time later, when Richele and Oren opened the chapel doors, every plate was empty. Yet none of the inhabitants showed any sign of mutation.

The bishop admitted it. He had baked bread with the flesh and blood of a monster provided by the Church of the Deep, but he had locked that bread in a cabinet underground so the hungry would not eat it by mistake.

Underground, before Matins, amid the sound of Arturia's cello, the bishop's trembling hands had at last set the plate down. And at Matins, he proclaimed that Sanctilaminium Ambrosii would return to Laterano.
But when Lemuen went underground, she found the cabinet broken open and empty. According to the records, that 'communion' could never be undone once eaten, and someone had already taken it.
10. There Is No Savior
While all eyes were on the chapel, Federico opened another door. Arturia was there.

blocks.cap: "How long has it been, Federico?"

blocks.x: Arturia was wanted by Laterano, and she was the one Federico had called his elder sister when he lived in her home. It was a reunion after five or six years, but Federico said only that she was not the first matter he had to deal with.
The suspect he named was in the burned sacrarium. It was Clément, and Clément did not deny it.

Clément said this monastery had taken in those dying in the wastes. But those who caught Oripathy were sent to the old training room underground to die alone, and everyone looked away. Paradise had been an illusion, he said.
The monastery's underground was full of incendiaries he had hidden. Clément meant to end everything before it became irreversible. Federico fired, and the bullet destroyed the ignition device.
Asked why he had not killed him, Federico answered that the law would not sentence him to death.
Federico, is it the law of Laterano that wants to save me... or is it you, yourself?

Clément walked to the fallen holy statue. There were no flowers there, only a wooden plate holding a few pieces of bread. He said he had overheard the bishop's plan when he went to confess the night before, and he chewed and swallowed the bread, which tasted bitter as the sea.

He said he wanted to know whether there truly was anyone in this world who would save them. Federico knew he had to stop him, but with Arturia's cello sounding, for the first time he could not move his own body.
Clément collapsed, coughing up blood.

blocks.cap: The gardener, fallen between the two arms of the broken holy statue.

blocks.x: No mutation came. Clément laughed and said that even this had been fake; there had never been a god. When Federico asked for his last words, he said only that the monastery's paradise and Laterano's faith were both lies, and closed his eyes.

Arturia praised that melody, saying an ordinary man had proven with his life that there is no savior. Federico aimed his gun at her. Her Arts had driven another person to death, he said. His sin had not been deep enough to deserve death.

blocks.cap: "Federico, have you finally learned compassion?"

blocks.x: Then an envoy of a Leithanien Elector arrived to receive Arturia. Leaving word that the performance had never once stopped and he simply had not heard it, Arturia departed with the envoy.

Later, the twins came into the burned sacrarium and laid the blanket their mother had given them over the 'sleeping man' beneath the holy statue. He was the man who grew the pretty flowers their mother used to bring back in a vase. When he woke up, the children said, they hoped he would plant even more flowers.
Epilogue — Again, in That Paradise
Having confirmed Gerald's death, Raimund challenged Federico to a duel. To take up a Sarkaz mercenary's weapon was to inherit his name.

Federico refused. Gerald had been simply a hunter, and what he held was only a hunter's dagger. Raimund said he would lead everyone as the boss had, find a new path, and then come to claim it. Federico answered that he would keep it until then.

Fortuna, meanwhile, decided to leave with the Sarkaz. Serpilia let her go on one condition: wherever she lived, she must keep in touch. When Fortuna asked whether they were still the same kind, Serpilia asked back whether that mattered.
And far across the wastes, Aulus and Hyman watched the monastery begin to move again. Hyman asked whether the people of Laterano would be good to the children, and said she was no longer their kind.

Meanwhile, the bishop apologized to Lemuen. In his despair, he had once bowed to malice, and had even suspected that faith itself was self-deception. Lemuen handed him the notebook of a monk who had stayed here long ago.
The bishop said he would go to Laterano. Not with the inhabitants, though. He would walk there alone, and recover the faith he had lost.
Let us meet again in that paradise.
Around then, Federico reported to the Pope. The two nuncios were safe, and the monastery would reach the outskirts of Laterano before spring. Of its 153 inhabitants, 41 would leave. Three casualties.

He asked why, when no mistakes had been made, they had not reached the best outcome. Did their law fit every situation? The Pope said it was a question he himself could not answer, and that he was glad Federico had begun to ask such questions.
And in the morning sun, the old bishop's bent back slowly dissolved into the light. Lemuen had a feeling this would not be the last time she saw him.

blocks.cap: The monastery's front gate. The old man passed through it and set out alone for Laterano.

blocks.x: Laterano is still called the eternal paradise. The small garden that had stopped in the wastes never became one. As the bishop said, it was not paradise. It was their home.

act25side.tagline: A scientist deceives an entire nation with the lie of a superweapon, tears open the sky on everyone's behalf, and departs alone among the stars. Those left on the ground look down at their feet once more.

chars.name: Kristen
chars.desc: Control of Rhine Lab, the head of the entire company. Daughter of the Wrights, inventors who died challenging the sky.

chars.name: Saria
chars.desc: Former Director of Rhine Lab's Defense Section. Kristen's old friend, and a Vouivre who upholds reason and order.

chars.name: Muelsyse
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Ecological Section. She commands water, and is one of the few Elves left in the world.

chars.name: Silence
chars.desc: A researcher and doctor who came from Rhine Lab. Ifrit's attending physician. · Operator Silence the Paradigmatic

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: A doctor of Rhodes Island and its de facto leader. Cool-headed and sparing with words.

chars.name: Ifrit
chars.desc: A Sabra girl of Rhodes Island. She looks to Silence and Saria as family.

chars.name: Rosmontis
chars.desc: A Feline Elite Operator of Rhodes Island. She forgets what she wishes to forget, and records what must remain.

chars.name: Ho'olheyak
chars.desc: A special agent of the Maylander Foundation. A Liberi who pursues the bloodline and power of the ancient K'uk'ulkan.

chars.name: Tin Man
chars.desc: Head of the Maylander Foundation. A revenant detective encased in a metal exoskeleton.

chars.name: Nasti
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Engineering Section. A Sarkaz Banshee who wields bone pens.

chars.name: Ferdinand
chars.desc: Former Director of Rhine Lab's Energy Section. Envious of Kristen, he calls himself the finest high-energy physicist alive.

chars.name: Jara
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Human Resources Investigation Section. Once a celebrated star of the silver screen.

chars.name: Parvis
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Structural Section. An elderly Caprinae scholar, and Silence's teacher.

chars.name: Justin Jr.
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Business Section. A man who uses money and connections to help 'madmen succeed.'

chars.name: Loken
chars.desc: Prisoner No. 30 of the Federal Nomadic Prison. A fallen scientist, buried by academia.

chars.name: Blake
chars.desc: A colonel in Columbia's Department of Defense. He means to make up for his failure in Bolívar with 'Arc-01.'

chars.name: Jackson
chars.desc: Vice President of Columbia. In Trimounts, he proclaims the first step of a 'new era.'

terms.name: Starpod
terms.desc: An invisible barrier that caps Terra's sky at an altitude of about 6,000 meters. Humanity has never once gone beyond it.

terms.name: Rhine Lab
terms.desc: Columbia's foremost science and technology company, based in the science city of Trimounts. Founded by Kristen and Saria.

terms.name: Trimounts
terms.desc: Columbia's science city, forever beneath dark clouds. Home to Rhine Lab's headquarters.

terms.name: Arc-01
terms.desc: The superweapon at the heart of the Department of Defense's strategic weapons program, the 'Horizon Arc Project.' It is said to use the sky as a relay to strike targets at extreme range.

terms.name: Maylander Foundation
terms.desc: The organization that holds more of Columbia's secrets than any other. It presents itself as a historical society and commands special agents.

blocks.x: Terra's sky has an end. At roughly 6,000 meters lies an invisible barrier, the **Starpod**, and humanity has never once gone beyond it.

The Wrights, a pair of Columbian inventors, crashed and died trying to fly past that height, and the world laughed at them. On the day of the funeral, their daughter stayed behind alone at the grave. The sky she looked up at was very dark.

That daughter, **Kristen Wright**, grew up to become Control, the head of Rhine Lab in the science city of Trimounts. Then, in 1099, she vanished overnight, along with the core device of a superweapon into which the military had poured a fortune.

blocks.cap: “If, in a century or a millennium, our descendants walk among the stars, the masses will sing her praises.”

blocks.x: 1. The Day a Star Fell

At the Federal Nomadic Prison, Justin Jr., Director of Rhine Lab's Business Section, bought off the warden and came for Prisoner No. 30. It was Loken Williams, a scientist buried by academia. Kristen had entrusted him with research on Originium and the human body.

That same day, Vice President Jackson gave a speech announcing that in two weeks he would unveil a project that would change the balance of power on this land. But the project's owner had already disappeared. And before Colonel Blake of the Department of Defense appeared Ferdinand, the former Director of the Energy Section who had been driven out of Rhine Lab, offering to help find Kristen.

Meanwhile, in Control's empty office, **Muelsyse**, Director of the Ecological Section, was calling Kristen's name. Instead of an answer came Ho'olheyak, a special agent of the Maylander Foundation, who told her that perhaps there had never been a place for Muelsyse in Kristen's plans at all.

blocks.cap: The two clash in Control's empty office.

blocks.x: Around then, by a roadside outside the city, Kal'tsit of Rhodes Island sat across from Tin Man, head of the Maylander Foundation. A revenant clad in a metal exoskeleton, he hoped that this time, at least, they would stand on the same side.

On a nearby bench sat Ifrit and Rosmontis, who had come with Kal'tsit. Rosmontis was here because of a single letter calling her back to Columbia. Then, from a height humanity had not reached in thousands of years, a ball of fire split the sky like a falling star.
2. The Sky Was Not the Means, but the Goal

The star struck the Triton Chemical Plant in District 13 and blew it apart, and the military immediately sealed off the entire district. **Saria**, Kristen's old friend and the former Director of Rhine Lab's Defense Section, crossed the cordon with Tin Man's help and saw a giant ring-shaped machine lodged in the middle of the ruins.

Tin Man called it the 'Horizon Arc Project.' It was a strategic weapons program on which the Department of Defense had staked everything, and Kristen herself had proposed it after becoming a technical advisor to the military. Its centerpiece was 'Arc-01,' a superweapon that would use the sky as a relay to strike at extreme range. The fallen ring was a test flight of its core component, the H.A.M.H.R.R. focus generator.
Saria stated flatly that Kristen must have deceived her investors. If the sky was part of Kristen's plan, it would not be the means, but the goal itself.
The truth is, Kristen abhors the sky, Tin Man.

At the same time, **Silence** had also slipped into the sealed-off District 13. She was tracking the 'Transmitter' that had gone missing from Site 359, and she found traces of it at the scene, but her drone was shot down and she was nearly caught.

The one who got her out was Jara, Director of the Human Resources Investigation Section, whom the soldiers recognized as 'Marianne,' a star of the silver screen in years past. That day, Jara confessed to Tin Man that she still saw the day the Wrights died in her dreams.

Meanwhile, Ho'olheyak carried the black box that had vanished from the scene down to a giant well deep underground. There, Nasti, Director of the Engineering Section, had spent a month testing something alone.

blocks.cap: A ring-shaped well hundreds of meters underground. Nasti spent a month here.

blocks.x: In the wilderness at dusk, Kristen told Nasti a single number. 6,152.31 meters. The height of Terra's sky, and the last record left by the Wrights' aircraft.

Nasti said that of all the futures awaiting Kristen, death might be the most merciful. Kristen replied that this was nothing much. When Nasti said that stars beyond reach were merely hollow, Kristen answered her.
And yet, sometimes the unreachable can become a signpost.

blocks.cap: A conversation between the two in the wilderness at dusk.

blocks.x: Around then, Ferdinand read Blake's true intentions. For a man who had failed in Bolívar, 'Arc-01' was a last chance, and he meant to make the stalling Vice President pay the price. Rather than become part of that price, Ferdinand took his side.

Kal'tsit, meanwhile, judged that even all of Trimounts's energy would not be enough to drive this plan. And Rhine Lab's survey records, which had combed the poles, the deserts, and even the ground beneath Trimounts, all bore Kristen's signature.
Those materials were all destroyed when Rhine Lab's power armor raided their base, and Saria left for Rhine Lab to retrieve more.

That same day, following the Transmitter's signal, Silence met her teacher Parvis, Director of the Structural Section, in an abandoned industrial park in District 9. When she pressed him about the pioneers of Site 359 and the workers at the Triton plant who had been hurt, he answered without taking his eyes off the monitor.
This is science, Silence. As scientists, we need only consider one thing and one thing alone: how to accomplish our goal. Nothing more.
Meanwhile, Tin Man came to the Doctor. Tomorrow, when the Vice President visited Rhine Lab, the military would try to assassinate him. The Doctor decided to move together with Ifrit and Rosmontis.
4. Live Broadcast

The next day, while the Vice President's visit was broadcast live, Maylander's agents neutralized nine sniper positions and eleven assassins in advance. Inside the building, Rosmontis and Saria destroyed every one of the autonomous power armor units that had gone missing from the Defense Section.

The visit ended without incident. But Ifrit, who had stayed underground, found two agents who had planted explosives on a liquefied Originium gas pipe. Afraid the fire would spread, she locked her flamethrower and took both of them down with her bare hands.
At the same moment, Blake confirmed that the pipe ran beneath the Vice President's route home, and pressed the detonator with his own hand. For a moment, his hand paused on the cold button.

blocks.cap: Blake's monitoring room. The explosion happened without a sound, only on the screen.

blocks.x: The road collapsed, and Ifrit was trapped underground with the two fallen agents. Saria drove her calcium crystals through the gaps in the earth and stone to open a passage, took Ifrit's hand, and pulled her out.
Asked whether she had cried, Ifrit said she had only been anxious. Saria told her she had done truly well.
What the blast caught was a robotic vehicle. Jara had already put Jackson in a modified car she had prepared in advance and taken him out by another route.
5. A Gunshot, and Narcissa
Silence appeared there. Four years earlier, she had nearly lost Ifrit in this city, and at last she put the question to Saria, who always stopped at merely 'controlling' the situation.
Is the reason you can never truly stand against Rhine Lab that, from the very start, you were the same as them... the same as Control?
Just as Saria was about to answer, a gunshot rang out. The calcium crystals shielding the two scattered, and Saria, struck in the head, collapsed.

Blake, meanwhile, ordered that none of those who had interfered be allowed to escape. The Doctor and Rosmontis, on the run, slipped away wrapped in Muelsyse's water, while Jara hid the fallen Saria and the other two. That day, after taking a call from someone, Jackson decided to join hands with Blake.

That evening, a gaunt old man walked, coughing, into the place where Muelsyse had hidden the group. It was Loken Williams. When he called her 'Narcissa,' Rosmontis answered that her only name was Rosmontis.

blocks.cap: The hideout Loken came to in person.

blocks.x: Using the scent of flowers to stir the child's memories, Loken told her to fill her whole body with resentment toward him. Then he asked the Doctor whether they were not afraid of a 'weapon' that might fill with rage again. Because those words came from the very man who had made the child this way, the Doctor struck him.
Loken left, saying he would wait at that 'home.' When Muelsyse followed him, he asked her whether she truly wanted to stop Kristen, or to follow her. Muelsyse could not answer.
6. What Rolled Out of the Alley

That night, in an alley near District 13, Ho'olheyak faced her superior, Tin Man. She had learned his weakness in Maylander's top-secret archives, and a Banshee's curse, hidden by Nasti within the noise of a construction site, bound his body.

When Tin Man asked what she had seen in Kristen's dreams, Nasti answered: the future. Then she asked him in return where the land promised to the Sarkaz might be. A sigh dispersed in place of an answer, and the cigarette went out.

Some time later, at a meeting place set by a message from Maylander, a metal head came rolling out. Ho'olheyak tried to frame the Doctor as the one who had killed Maylander's head, but the hooded figure standing there was a water clone of Muelsyse that the Doctor had sent.

blocks.cap: The alley where Tin Man had arranged to meet.

blocks.x: Around then, Saria woke and, injured as she was, blocked the door so that Silence and Ifrit could escape. While Ifrit honed her fire as thin as a blade to cut through the reinforced glass, Saria answered Silence's question. Even if she could go back to when she first met Kristen,
I would not stop the Kristen of that time. I would not stop the birth of Rhine Lab. ... I would still stand with them all.

Silence hung the two of them from a drone and sent them to the building across the way, staying behind herself. The anger she had turned on Saria all this time had really been aimed at herself, for wanting the strong to solve everything.

She walked out before Ferdinand and injected the Transmitter from Site 359 into her own body. The Transmitter's new core was with Kristen, she said; if they took her along, she would be their signpost.
7. A Dance for Three
Meanwhile, Muelsyse took the Doctor and Rosmontis to her vivarium. Rosmontis said she would meet Loken again. This time, she would say a proper goodbye.

blocks.cap: Muelsyse's vivarium. The cleanest place in Trimounts.

blocks.x: After Rosmontis fell asleep, Muelsyse asked the Doctor to dance, and as water droplets followed the melody, she confessed that she was an Elf. That she was ten times more sensitive to Originium than others, and so had no choice but to move through clones. That the remote village she had found while tracing her parents' footsteps had been a graveyard of Elves.

On the first New Year's night after Rhine Lab was founded, she had pulled Saria and Kristen into a dance. None of them knew how to dance as three. Kristen had promised that one day, when she set out on her journey, she would take Muelsyse's dream with her.
After confessing that she was using everyone so that her kin could breathe freely, Muelsyse agreed to help find Loken.
8. She Answered: God
Loken recalled the day Kristen first showed him this research. When he asked who had given her this knowledge, which mocked centuries of science, Kristen answered in a single word. **God.**

The same night, at the military's energy well, the S.H.A.F.T., Ferdinand worked out that Nasti's propulsion system could never launch the H.A.M.H.R.R. He borrowed an experimental aircraft capable of reaching that altitude.

Blake, meanwhile, held a different lead. Aboard his aircraft, Silence used a neural stimulator to make the Transmitter in her body resonate, and even as the warning signs of a seizure appeared, she told them to raise the output. The coordinates locked in.

It was Jara who wiped the sweat from her face. Once a Maylander agent who had stayed by the Wrights' side, she said that the fireball that fell from the sky that day seemed to have entered that child's eyes, and to be burning there still.
I was never a mother. But I have a child.

The moment they neared the target building, a wall of wind brought the aircraft down, and Maylander's drones all went blind at once. Unmanned power armor fell upon the military, and the enemy commanding all of it was Ho'olheyak alone.

Saria arrived just before Blake's life fell into her hands. Ho'olheyak said that what she wanted was not victory, but a chance to reach eternal truth. Saria brought her down with a bare fist, without adding any Arts at all.

blocks.cap: Plain, unadorned strength. Saria's fist pierced the twisted air.

blocks.x: 9. Loken's Court

Meanwhile, the Doctor's group passed through underground tunnels and reached Loken's hideout. In Rosmontis's memories, her grandfather had come to the orphanage every Friday with flowers, and her older brothers had the same scars on the backs of their heads as she did.
The door closed, and only Rosmontis went inside. Loken called the place a court in which both plaintiff and defendant were himself.

One by one, he confessed: the greed that had led him to extract infected organs from dying patients, the weakness that had made him bow before the Department of Defense's money, and the failure that had cost him everything when Maylander took Narcissa away. Then he asked the child to become the scale that would weigh these sins.

blocks.cap: Loken asked the child to look upon his life.

blocks.x: The memories overflowed. Her brothers crying on the operating table. A cage where there had never been any garden at all. As Loken told her to strangle him, Rosmontis's Arts began to tear through the laboratory walls, and the military's power armor that had stormed in was torn apart like paper.

The one who stepped in front of Rosmontis was Ifrit, who had raced there in power armor modified by Saria. She would not use the other power implanted in her body, she said. This was a promise between her and Rosmontis.
We have the right to be angry, to yell, to destroy it all! But we don't have to!
When Ifrit took her hand, the tremors subsided. Hearing that the only ones who could control them were themselves, Rosmontis went back to Loken.
10. The Ring Rises
Beyond the collapsed wall lay a vivarium resembling Muelsyse's, and at its innermost point sat a sarcophagus. The very object in which the Doctor's memories had begun.
Only upon seeing that vivarium did Muelsyse make up her mind. Kristen had not forgotten her promise. Pushing the Doctor outside with her water, she asked them to tell Saria she was sorry.
Five minutes remained until takeoff. Jara let Silence go and told her to return to being a researcher, but Silence answered that she did not want to give up halfway.

With three minutes left, Saria realized this was not a building. As she wavered, thinking it was too late, Silence appeared before her and said that if she let go of balance, she might find her source again amid the chaos.

blocks.cap: Each to do what she must, the two parted here.

blocks.x: Once, I truly looked up to you. Once, I truly wanted to walk by your side.
With thirty seconds left, Rosmontis delivered her verdict. Not revenge: the people who are gone will not come back. Not destruction at your bidding: I am not your weapon.
You're nothing to me. You're just a criminal. So I'll do what the law and prison could not. I hereby sentence you to death.

Then an immense tremor rose from beneath their feet. The ring-shaped corridors, the vivarium, this entire laboratory: all of it was the **H.A.M.H.R.R.** On the evening of November 21, 1099, a giant ring that had been hidden among heaps of garbage rose into the night sky over Trimounts.

blocks.cap: The people of the city stopped in their tracks and looked up at the sky.

blocks.x: 11. Science in Human Hands
The H.A.M.H.R.R. headed for the sky above the energy well, and Silence commandeered a military vehicle and descended deep into that well.
Jara stood in her way. Kristen would not aim that energy anywhere on the ground, she said; like other scientists, she was simply going where no one had ever set foot.

Silence answered that if Kristen succeeded, countless scientists who stopped at nothing would take her as their model. Was Control's wish nobler, she asked, than that of a researcher who wanted to go home on time, or a soldier who wanted to take his family and run?
Someone has to step up and ensure that science... remains in the people's hands.

As Kristen's family, Jara said, she could not let Silence through, and the two fought. When the temperature in the well soared, Silence ran on deeper, and Jara looked up at the sky and told Kristen to fly to the high sky she had dreamed of.
Soon, a pillar of light rising from the energy well pierced the ring in the sky.

blocks.cap: Light joining earth and sky. Everyone looked up.

blocks.x: Deep underground beneath it, Silence found Parvis. His final research was to create an artificial consciousness, using the Transmitter as its soil. But his nerves were degenerating, and he confessed that he could not simply retire as a senile old man.

When Silence destroyed the Transmitter's core, Parvis said that following a strong soul was also a choice, and dissolved his own consciousness into the Transmitter to fill the shattered core. His body became an empty shell, and the wavering H.A.M.H.R.R. stabilized.

As Silence broke down, saying she had accomplished nothing, it was Ifrit, who had driven after her, who grabbed her by the collar. Why was she trying to face everyone alone? Weren't they right there beside her?

blocks.cap: “You're the strongest person I've ever seen in this whole land!”

blocks.x: Silence answered that she would see it through. Because they were with her.
12. The Preserver's Debate

Around then, Kal'tsit took the Doctor down into the underground cavern that Rhine Lab's survey records had pointed to. When Ho'olheyak blocked their path, the one who seized her was Tin Man, who had lost his head and yet appeared in a different body.
Deep in the cavern stood countless sarcophagi in rows. Kristen's energy source lay beneath this wasteland. When a strong light swept over the Doctor, something among them awoke.

blocks.cap: Sarcophagi stretching on without end.

blocks.x: What awoke called himself the 'Preserver.' He was the personality simulation of a project that had guarded the cold bodies of hundreds of thousands of his people for tens of thousands of years, and he called Kal'tsit 'AMa-10.' He was also the one who had given Kristen the last of his blood.
The people in the sarcophagi were **the Doctor's own people**, he said, and they would never wake again. Faced with the words 'your people,' the Doctor could give no answer.

The Preserver tested the two of them through a 'Debate.' In a vision where thoughts resonated, the Doctor faced the question of whether Babel's commander and their present self were the same person, and answered this way: I am myself, and have been from the very start.
When the Debate ended, Kal'tsit answered that she, born and raised on Terra, was a member of Rhodes Island, and the Doctor said the same.

Kal'tsit called the Preserver Trevor Friston. For tens of thousands of years he had cried out to the universe and received no reply, and the small life that came to find him in person was Kristen. He was only handing over the tinder, he said.
The only ones who can truly save Terra have always been the people of Terra themselves.
13. Galleria Stellaria

Around then, Saria was chasing the H.A.M.H.R.R. in the 'Arc-01' inspection aircraft Ferdinand had borrowed. He wanted to save Rhine Lab, Ferdinand said, and he desperately wanted to know what Kristen was trying to do.

blocks.cap: Two directors left out of Control's plan.

blocks.x: Saria silenced the drones with a pulse device and docked the aircraft onto the H.A.M.H.R.R. Ferdinand knew this laboratory would not survive the second firing, yet he stayed behind to keep recording, saying he could not let this knowledge be buried.

In the vivarium deep inside the laboratory was Muelsyse. 'Arc-01' had been nothing but a bundle of waste paper to fool the military; the true name of this laboratory was **'Galleria Stellaria.'** The vivarium carried a dream that somewhere beyond the barrier there might be a place that would take in the Elves, and 753 species of plants.
Long ago, on a night when the three of them watched the stars, Kristen had said this.
Scientists do not believe that dreams are false. Because what they are doing is proving to all humanity that every dream can come true.

This time it was two against one, Muelsyse said, and her water pressed down on Saria. But an energy overload brought down the gravity device, and Muelsyse alone was flung outside. Saria said she would bring Kristen back; from here on, it was between the two of them.
Kristen was waiting in the planetarium at its deepest point. The star trails visible now were fake, she said, and she had known Saria would come. Whether to stand beside her, or against her.

blocks.cap: The two face each other in the planetarium of Galleria Stellaria.

blocks.x: Kristen rained down stars of metal, and Saria, though struck by them, did not stop walking. She respected Kristen's parents' will, she said, but she could not accept sacrifice as a matter of course.
A real pioneer should be clearing the way for all humanity, instead of jumping headfirst into the abyss, never to return.
