The last of the calcium crystals spread across the back of Kristen's hand. Got you, Kristen.
14. The False Sky Is Torn

A thousand meters to the barrier. The control panel would not respond; Kristen had never intended for Galleria Stellaria to last long. When Saria told her there was no place for her in that future, Kristen answered that she wanted to be not a pioneer, but a starting point.

Told there were no escape pods, Saria held out her hand, saying she would wrap them both in calcium crystals. At that moment, the floor beneath her gave way. In the very middle of Galleria Stellaria, Kristen had built an exit for Saria, who she knew would come at the last moment.

blocks.cap: As Saria fell away, Kristen told her: this land, too, is so beautiful.

blocks.x: I am just a pair of eyes. Eyes that... gaze into the unfamiliar heights of the sky, on behalf of everyone who lives on this land.
The gathered light abandoned the ground and stretched toward the higher sky. Ripples ran across the black veil, and **the false sky was torn apart.** The ancient twin moons revealed their true faces.
15. Those Who Remained

An escape pod that had broken away from Galleria Stellaria was plummeting, damaged. When she saw Saria falling outside the window, wrapped in calcium crystals, Muelsyse inside spent all the water in her body to spread a wall of water like a lake across the sky.
Some time later, it was Silence who woke Saria. She had no serious injuries, and the staff in the escape pod had all survived.

blocks.cap: The dark clouds had cleared. Saria said the sky was really beautiful.

blocks.x: Silence said she would tell her everything that had happened on the ground. She could not carry her, so they would have to walk together.

Beneath the earth, the Preserver made a final request. Erase 4,765,403 days of twisted data, and let him die as Trevor Friston, even if only as a copy. And he told the Doctor that there was a reason behind the Doctor's lost memories, too.
As his memories were erased, he cried out in the darkness, searching for an answer. Ho'olheyak salvaged something into her memory-storing Arts unit and handed it to the Doctor.

When the Doctor and Kal'tsit came up into the energy well facility, a large screen called them to a stop. The one who spoke was not Jackson, but the 'pet' on his shoulder: the President of Columbia, **Mark Max**.

blocks.cap: The President, beyond the screen.

blocks.x: The President called Friston 'Father.' When Kal'tsit told him of Friston's death, the President let the group go, but declared that Columbia would become the sword and shield of Terra. Kal'tsit replied that Friston had never once wanted a tyrant.

Under the same sky, Loken sat in his wheelchair looking at the torn sky, and breathed his last. Rosmontis, who understood that he had called her so as not to die alone, said that she had only been waiting for him to die.
Then she wrote a single line in her notebook. The criminal Loken Williams has received his due judgment. Closing the notebook, she told him that she had forgotten him now.

At dawn, in Rhine Lab's flooded vivarium, the Doctor found Muelsyse. She had never managed to fit in even with the kin she met in the forests of Sami, and she said she was not a leaf, only a drop of water.

blocks.cap: The flooded vivarium. Even so, the Doctor held out a hand.

blocks.x: The Doctor answered that solitude is a kind of strength, too. That everything one experiences until one's life ends must have meaning.
Epilogue. Opening the Door to the Future

In a prison in D.C., Ferdinand filled even the backs of his manuscript pages with equations, crying out that he would be the one to bring that truth down to the earth. Justin Jr. went back to the warden he had bribed on the first day, and said that the people he was taking, as always, were madmen and freaks.

Two weeks later, Muelsyse returned as Director of the Ecological Section. The 753 species of plants were dying, but before that they had survived long enough beside the barrier. To Nasti, who was sketching a city floating in the air, she said that they were fellow travelers now.

In front of the door to the same conference hall, Silence spoke to Saria. There is no reality that cannot be changed, and no sacrifice that is simply a given. For the people forced to choose between dreams and reality, she would become a bridge.
And then she stepped into the conference room, as Olivia Silence, sponsor of the 'Trimounts Ethics in Scientific Research Joint Declaration.'
At the same hour, Jara left Rhine Lab and set out on a long journey, after looking up at a single star rising faintly in the twilight.

Five days, eight hours, and forty-three minutes after breaking through the barrier, Galleria Stellaria was still holding on. Kristen prepared to enter the life-support dormancy capsule Loken had built. Even she did not know how long she could live.

blocks.cap: Beyond the barrier, Kristen looked down upon Terra.

blocks.x: In her final record, she said there had been only two times in her life when she truly felt alive. When she took Saria to the tree stump in her hometown and told her about the beginning of everything, and now, having fulfilled her parents' dream. On a clear night, if you set up a telescope, there will be a single star in the sky twinkling for you.
Well then, good night, Terra. Good night, universe.

On this land, there had been no meaning in raising one's head to look at the sky. That night, one person became the eyes for everyone and departed into the sky, and those left on the ground raised their heads, then looked down at their feet once more. As Saria said, that sky was truly beautiful.

act24side.tagline: Yato and Noir Corne, tracking down the cause of a run of Oripathy cases, end up tangled with a fire-breathing wyvern and a band of Palicoes who tumbled in from another world — plus an old hunter who blocks their path growling 'that's my quarry.' Claw marks weren't the only thing buried under those fallen leaves.

chars.name: Yato
chars.desc: Leader of Rhodes Island's Op Team A4. An Oni. Cool-headed, and always puts the mission first · Operator Kirin R Yato

chars.name: Noir Corne
chars.desc: Yato's longtime partner and shield-bearer. Kind-hearted, always looking out for others · Operator Rathalos S Noir Corne

chars.name: Terra Research Commission
chars.desc: Three bipedal cats called 'Palicoes' who crossed over from another world: the Scholar Palico, the Artisan Palico, and the Companion Palico · Operator Terra Research Commission

chars.name: Yoshitaka Kashiwau
chars.desc: An old hunter of Roka Village. The only person in the village who still goes up into the mountains

chars.name: Akira Kashiwau
chars.desc: A young hunter of Roka Village

chars.name: Ataru Takii
chars.desc: The head of Roka Village. He turned a poor hunting village into the prosperous place it is today

chars.name: Mirai Takii
chars.desc: The village head's niece. An ecologist back from the city

chars.name: Kazuya
chars.desc: A village boy who looks up to hunters. He calls Yoshitaka 'Grandpa' and tags along after him

chars.name: Yutaka Rito
chars.desc: A native of Roka Village, from a family that has lived there for generations

terms.name: Roka Village
terms.desc: A village at the foot of the Soubo Mountains in Higashi. It once lived off hunting, then grew prosperous on its specialty tea, ironware, and woodcraft

terms.name: Soubo Mountains
terms.desc: A mountain range in Higashi. Deep forests and cliffs stretch out behind Roka Village

terms.name: Rathalos
terms.desc: A giant flying wyvern known in another world as the 'King of the Skies.' It breathes fire, and its talons are venomous. The Palicoes call it the 'Fire Wyvern'

terms.name: Demon Mode
terms.desc: A Dual Blades technique from the Palicoes' world. A state in which you throw away defense and press the attack like a wild beast

blocks.x: There's an old hunter who has spent three days and nights chasing a beast through the autumn forest. Every time he falls, a voice at his ear hauls him back up. 'Be angry. Fear, pain — your anger will wash all of it away.'

He slices his own palm on his spearhead to lure the beast out with the smell of blood, finally drives the spear through its throat, and collapses. In that instant he sees an enormous shadow flying off into the lightning, trailing flames behind it. 'That's the one. That's the one that left you there…'
1. Twenty-Three Misses, and the King of the Skies

Around the same time, in the **Soubo Mountains** of Higashi, **Yato**, leader of Rhodes Island's Op Team A4, and her longtime partner **Noir Corne** are hunting for the cause of a string of suspected Oripathy cases. They've taken twenty-three samples without a single trace of active Originium, and Noir Corne's suggestion that they put in for a ladder next time? 'Denied.'

Then Noir Corne spots a pile of fallen leaves swarming with water-fly larvae, in a spot with no puddles anywhere. Sweep the leaves aside and there are claw marks only a beast the size of a house could leave — and there, at long last, they detect active Originium.
That's when two fuzzballs, one yellow and one white, pop out and shout: 'It's the Fire Wyvern, meow!' And an enormous shadow descends from the sky.

blocks.cap: “The threat came from the sky.”

blocks.x: It's **Rathalos**, a fire-breathing wyvern. Yato springs off Noir Corne's shield and slashes down at the nape of its neck, but her blade glances right off its shell, and once its venomous talons rake her arm she can't even hold her sword, and goes down. The ones who load the pair onto a rickety wooden cart and make a run for it? Those same fuzzballs from earlier.

The two pushing the cart are the **Scholar Palico**, who claims to hail from a royal academic institute back in his home kingdom, and the **Artisan Palico**, who met him on the road and tagged along. They're not Felines, thank you very much, but a species called Palicoes — and they click their tongues at these 'New World Hunters' reckless enough to take on a Fire Wyvern without a single antidote.

Meanwhile, down in **Roka Village** at the foot of the mountains, a little kid is playing hunters with a friend. 'Hunters never lose!' But the friend shakes their head. 'My dad says there aren't any hunters anymore.'

blocks.cap: Roka Village under falling autumn leaves. Only the hunter's statue gazes off into the distance, alone.

blocks.x: A little later, Noir Corne reaches the village propping up a feverish Yato and asks for help, and that same kid, **Kazuya**, leads them to the home of the village's one and only hunter, the old man he calls Grandpa. But the moment the door opens, the Artisan Palico's hammer lands square on Noir Corne's head. Turns out the Palicoes had been raiding the village, got chased off, and of all places, hid in that very house.

Just as Yato's fever breaks thanks to an antidote the Scholar Palico brewed from the mushrooms on the shelf, the master of the house, **Yoshitaka Kashiwau**, comes home. The old man growls at them, yet still tells the injured Yato to rest and barks at Noir Corne to go boil some water first. Then the talk turns to a fire-breathing monster, and his face hardens. 'That's my quarry.'
When Yato suggests they hunt it together, he throws them both out, calling them useless worms. Then he looks at the empty doorway and mutters, 'The young lady's got some color back in her face.'
2. An Autumn Butterfly Is Only a Fallen Leaf

Back on her feet, Yato urges the village head, **Ataru Takii**, to evacuate. He just smiles and, before anything else, pours her a cup of the specialty tea that grows only on these mountains. This poor village used to stake its life on the hunt; thanks to this tea, plus its ironware and woodcraft, it finally managed to put up streetlights. He's not about to abandon his home over one set of claw marks.
If you see a butterfly dancing in autumn, it's only a fallen leaf. Perhaps what you saw was a fallen leaf, too.

blocks.cap: The village head's house. Along with the specialty tea, the advice to evacuate is politely declined.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, Yoshitaka wakes from a nightmare of being torn apart alive by a beast. He flatly refuses when Kazuya begs to come along on the monster hunt, then comforts the teary boy with a promise: 'Someday you'll be a real hunter.'
The residents' angiography results, meanwhile, are strange. They've all been exposed to faint traces of active Originium for years now, but ask them where they've been and they clam right up.

Then Yato barely manages to save the Ishitori family's child, who's been coughing up blood, and the kid spills everything. Dad went off to work in 'the hole' every day, came home with stones sprouting from his body, and said there was a huge monster inside — but everyone called him a liar, and he got dragged off to the village head.
Yato, leader of Rhodes Island's Op Team A4. I'll take your request. I don't break my promises.

Then a village native, **Yutaka Rito**, steps forward saying he knows where that hole is. The Palicoes come along too. They'd been mulling over Yato's offer to help find a way home, and after a thorough petting from the village kids, they signed on with a 'Well, since you ask so very nicely, we can't possibly refuse, meow.'
3. The Hole in the Hills

Inside the cave they sneak into are man-made tunnels and rails, plus clothes the child's father seems to have flung off while running for his life. Those clothes show active Originium a little denser than the claw marks did.

blocks.cap: The 'hole' in the hills behind Roka Village. The rails lead deeper still.

blocks.x: Further in, they find a slab of meat that's been dragged there recently. It's bait, meant to lure something out — and sure enough, a swarm of infected creatures soon comes pouring out of the depths of the cave.

While Noir Corne holds the line, Yato blows open a ventilation shaft — and naturally, the escape ladder snaps. Noir Corne catches the blast's shockwave on his shield and gets launched upward, and Yato, grabbing his hand, has just one thing to say: 'You need to eat less.'

At that very moment, Rito is calmly confessing to the village head. He lured 'that monster' in with the smell of blood, so whether the outsiders die or the monster does, the village comes out ahead. When word arrives that the cave has collapsed, Rito heads off, sure they've been buried along with it, and the village head, left alone, lets out a sigh. 'Akira, you were right…'
And somewhere in the forest, Yoshitaka looks up at the falling leaves. 'Autumn already… Come on, Akira. Let's go.'
4. Eggs, a Stench, and One Old Photo

Once they're out in the forest, the group decides to go all in and chase Rathalos deep into the woods. The pursuit does not go smoothly. The Artisan Palico shoves something into Noir Corne's arms and runs off — and of course it's the egg of a Fowlbeast, one that sprays a horrendous stench.

blocks.cap: Noir Corne's lesson from experience: do not enter those birds' nests. And whatever you do, never touch the eggs.

blocks.x: Stink bombs the Artisan Palico whips up from those very birds' droppings manage to halt a stampeding herd of Hornbeasts, but on the leader's snout they find a lure powder that drives beasts into a frenzy. Noir Corne remembers the rows of bottles on Yoshitaka's shelf, but Yato looks away and tells him not to get distracted by things that don't concern them.

When the sun goes down, every device goes dead, and the group gets stuck in a cliff zone that scrambles their sense of direction. After circling back to the same rock seven times, it's the Scholar Palico — lost on his own and trembling — who finds words carved into a tree: 'Landmarks unreliable. Follow the wind. Mirai.'

The lakeshore they emerge onto holds an abandoned hunters' camp. In a rusty chest is a finely crafted spear with the name **Akira Kashiwau** on its shaft, and a photo from nine years ago showing a young village head dressed as a hunter beside a young man carrying that very spear. Yoshitaka himself is nowhere in the picture.

When Noir Corne starts wondering about these people's story, Yato blows up at him. Don't get wrapped up in other families' business, she says — all we can do is keep people alive — and she makes it an order as team leader. '…Fine. But I'm worried about you, too.'
As Yato scouts the area alone, a voice from long ago echoes in her ears. 'They're dead… because of you. Stop running.'

Meanwhile, the Scholar Palico realizes that this forest has no apex predator to keep its ecosystem in balance — that at some point something vanished, and the order fell apart. And the new gear the Artisan Palico has been hammering away at all night is finally done.

blocks.cap: “Light, fast, strong.” Yato's verdict, later on. The other Operators were impressed by something else entirely.

blocks.x: Noir Corne gets armor and a long sword forged from Rathalos materials, and Yato gets dual blades and some very, very breezy armor made from Kirin materials. With the glare that always bothered her finally gone, Yato even takes off the mask she always wears — and Noir Corne, staring at her in a daze, trips and falls flat.
5. A Ghost by the Campfire
That night, Yoshitaka comes to the camp, drawn by its light. The flickering flames bring back that rainy night.

blocks.cap: The old man's face in the firelight. Its wrinkles looked older than anything he had ever lived through.

blocks.x: On that night, after three days and nights of hunting, when he saw the enormous shadow, the old man covered the beast's claw marks with fallen leaves. So no one else would find them — so it would stay his quarry and his alone. And he argued with the voice that always speaks in his ear: Akira.

If you'd listened to even one word I said that night, the old man says, you wouldn't have ended up a lump of meat no one could recognize; everything I'm doing is for you. The voice answers coldly. 'No, Yoshitaka. You're doing this for yourself.'

Just as the old man, clutching the camp's gear and shouting 'my quarry,' squares off with Yato, an unfamiliar voice rings out of the darkness. 'Hunters, douse that campfire! The Fire Wyvern approaches!'

Even the new weapons can't land a decisive blow on Rathalos, which has followed the firelight. That's when a seasoned **Companion Palico** jumps in — one who calls himself 'this old-timer' and never did manage to drop the 'meow' from the end of his sentences.

But then Yoshitaka shoves Yato aside and charges in alone. 'It's my quarry!' Yato takes the tail swipe meant for the old man, the Originium dust catches fire, and the flames swell to absurd size until they swallow the whole camp.

Rathalos takes to the air and vanishes, carrying off Noir Corne — still hanging from the long sword lodged in its body — and the Scholar Palico. The Companion Palico says he knows where its cave is, and Yato tells the old man: 'If you want to fight it again, your only option is to come with us.'
6. Seven Years Ago Tonight

Meanwhile, Noir Corne and the Scholar Palico, having fallen into a deep cave, find a heap of animal carcasses with no sign of being eaten, and the marks of mining. Below lay an Originium mine. This was the secret the village had been keeping.

The Scholar Palico asks why anyone would dig up a stone that brings incurable disease and disaster. Noir Corne pulls the battery out of his flashlight to show him. This light, the factories that turn out clothing, the nomadic cities that carry tens of thousands of people away from Catastrophes — all of it runs on Originium.
When disaster hits, you grab hold of any branch floating nearby. Whether it has thorns… that's not something you worry about then.

Then is it right, the Scholar Palico asks, for innocent people to be burdened with a sickness they never wanted? Noir Corne answers at once. 'Of course it isn't. That's why someone has to shoulder the cost and light the way ahead.'

At the same time, in the forest, the Companion Palico asks whether Rathalos really has to die, and Yoshitaka explodes. Leveling his spear, he cries out that because of them that young man is missing and the monster is still alive and well — and now they want to spare his quarry, too?

Yato walks toward the spearhead. From the start, she says, you only wanted to drive us off; you never meant to harm us. And right now you're only being dragged along by anger and regret. You can't even call yourself a hunter.
'Shoot. I'm right here.' When the spearhead only trembles, Yato asks quietly, '…Is this because of Akira Kashiwau?'
'Akira was… my son. He's dead.'

Seven years ago, on a night just like this one, the son ignored his father's cursing and his order to stay, and ran out into the forest where the beasts were howling, repeating only one thing. '**I'm the village's hunter**.'

When the father found his son again, he could not have recognized him without his clothes and gear. And the old man saw the backs of the village head and the hunters as they left that place. They had been there, and done nothing. That is what the old man believed.

The old man's trembling finger pulls the spear's firing mechanism. Because the Companion Palico is hanging on to him, the spearhead only grazes Yato's ear and sticks in the ground at her feet. Saying it is all their fault, the old man flees into the forest. Yato tries to follow, but collapses from the wound the tail dealt her earlier.
7. You, of All People, Must Not Stay Silent

Meanwhile, deep in the mine, Noir Corne rescues the ecologist **Mirai Takii**, who has been trapped there for three days. The village head's niece, and the one who left Rhodes Island's contact details in the first place, she warns that if the mining continues, a Catastrophe will strike this mountain. She proposes collapsing the mine and burying Rathalos with it.

Around then, Yato pulls a shard of stone out of her own thigh, and the Artisan Palico cauterizes the wound with a dagger heated in the fire. She records the whole process as a voice log, to use when reviewing her next mission.

As a sign of the coming Catastrophe, the morning sky sinks into black, and the beasts of the forest rise up all at once. Noir Corne radios that they need Yato's hands right now to bring the mine down. Yato hesitates for a moment, then answers that she will first save the old man who went off alone. 'I'm going to save everyone.'

At that moment, in the middle of the beast horde, Yoshitaka has dropped his spear and stands face to face with a vision of his son. Seven years ago, his son said he would go rescue the people who had gone into the forest with nothing but mining tools. 'I'm the village's hunter. At a time like this, I of all people can't stay silent.'
Now that voice whispers that if he wants to atone, he should die, and the old man nods. Yato leaps in front of him. 'Old man, it's not your time to die yet.'
Yoshitaka Kashiwau, you are Roka Village's hunter. Its one and only hunter. You, of all people, must not stay silent.
Guarding the home from the claws of beasts and bringing back the embers to live by — that is a hunter's work, Yato cries. And the old man asks the son in his vision what he said that day.
'I said I would win, no matter what.' 'And did you?' 'Father, I did.'
The old man takes a firmer grip on his son's spear. 'Your spear's not bad. Now go. And don't show yourself to me again.'
Then the Companion Palico tells Yato the secret of the dual blades: a state in which you throw away defense and press the attack like a wild beast — **Demon Mode**.

blocks.cap: Demon Mode. Into the heart of the beast horde, alongside the old hunter and the Companion Palico.

blocks.x: 8. The Vanished Beasts, the Burning Sky

Meanwhile, deep in the mine, which is seething like a volcano, Mirai explains that these tunnels were originally the nest of burrowing carnivorous beasts. When the vein was discovered seven years ago, Akira opposed the mining, but the village head went behind his back and, with the other hunters, slaughtered the beasts in the nest.

Robbed of their home and enraged, the beasts swept through the forest. That was the horde of seven years ago. All that species left behind were the piles of bones in the tunnels. And Akira, Mirai adds, was found not near the village, but near the mine.

At the end of the tunnel, Rathalos has built a nest of heaped Originium and lies there in pain. Just as Noir Corne murmurs that it, too, is a victim of Originium, the telescope the Scholar Palico dropped strikes it on the head, and sparks flare at the corners of its mouth.

blocks.cap: Black fog covers the sky and the mountain splits apart. A great calamity falls from the heavens.

blocks.x: At the same time, in the forest, trapped by an endless horde of beasts, Yoshitaka takes the lure powder from his coat. He confesses that he was the one who drove the Hornbeasts mad, too — he used too much while trying to draw out Rathalos. Then he volunteers as bait and douses himself in the powder. 'Young lady, you'll be sure to come back for me, won't you?'

While Yato hooks a grappling line onto a tree, the old man, in the middle of the horde, comes to understand what his son saw that night. Teeth surging in no matter how many he cut down; swinging his spear without a word, right up to the moment he sank down against a rock. 'Ah… so that's how it was.'
The moment Yato hauls the old man up, the beasts suddenly scatter. A pillar of Catastrophe fire has risen from the direction of the mine and become a whirlwind that is swallowing the mountain.

Before heading down to the village with Noir Corne and Mirai, who have rejoined them, Yato apologizes to the old man for hurting him without knowing his circumstances. And she tells him why she said she 'understood.'

Before coming to Rhodes Island, Yato was an assassin. She could not bring herself to kill the mother and daughter she had been ordered to kill, and let them go — but other assassins who came after killed the two anyway. For a long time they appeared in her dreams, asking why she had left them there. What pulled her free of them was the words of Noir Corne, who quit being an assassin on the same day she did.
The past is the past. Every regret and every sin of yours — pay them back with all the future ahead of you.

'The lives of this land weren't born to die easily.' That is why Yato will save people even if she has to force her will on them. The old man does not take her outstretched hand, but says this instead: 'It won't be an easy road. Good luck.'
9. The Hunters Were Always There

And the village is in chaos. While Rito was smuggling out his property, the fence Yoshitaka had reinforced with his own hands was broken, and the beasts poured in. Now Rito turns on the village head in front of everyone: didn't he know this disaster was coming, and still seal the mine, hide the monster, and even blow up the cave and kill the doctors?

The village head admits he knew excessive mining would one day bring a Catastrophe, and that he prepared a shelter. But the villagers, in despair, cry that they would rather die here than go back to nights of hunger without the mine. Just then Mirai returns and holds up a bottle: she has found the specialty tea plant growing in other lands, too. 'First, we have to survive.'

Rito tries to cut her off and ends up face-down in the dirt under Yato's foot. Yato reveals that he is the one who broke the fence and smuggled out his property, and gives an order. 'Walk to the shelter, or get knocked out by me and carried there. Choose.'

The village head entrusts the villagers to the two of them and takes up his blade. 'I am the head of Roka Village, and the leader of Roka Village's hunters.' The village men take up spears and follow him, and when a child asks what Dad meant about there being no more hunters, the child's mother answers. 'There were always hunters.'

Holding back the horde, the village head fights at the old man's side for the first time in seven years. When he begins to say that it wasn't that he chose not to save Akira that day, the old man speaks first. 'The lure powder. I'm that boy's father.'

That night, Akira rubbed the lure powder on his own body and drew the horde away from the mine. He had opposed the mining more than anyone, yet he told his master, the village head, that Originium was the village's chance to survive, and that he must hold on to it.
You taught me that a hunter steps forward so the pack can survive, Master. From now on, lead everyone… and survive!

And the words he left for his stubborn father: 'I'm sorry, Father.' The old man turns his back, saying the boy never once called him father. But long-held tears well up between his wrinkles. '…I miss him.'

Then Rathalos lands in the village. Yato and Noir Corne must guard the evacuation column; all they can do is trust the old man. He pours oil over his own house and sets it alight, muttering that a rotten past is best burned clean away.

blocks.cap: The flames devour the fragments of days gone by, and burn away even the regret in his eyes.

blocks.x: 'Akira, if you were here, you'd have done the same.' To the monster drawn in by the firelight, the old man shouts, 'Look at me, monster!'
10. Showdown! The Burning Hunter's Spirit!

Aiming through a gap in the flames, the old man fires his spearhead into Rathalos's head, but he cannot dodge its next charge. Coughing blood, he charges again until at last he falls — and Kazuya, aiming a bow with trembling arms, steps between him and the monster. 'I'm the village's hunter too!'

Noir Corne pulls the boy to safety, and the Palicoes load the child and the old man onto the cart and get them out. Covered in wounds, Yato picks up the old man's spear and plants it in the ground. 'Thank you for buying us time. Rest now. As for the rest…'

blocks.cap: “…leave it to us.”

blocks.x: Wreathed in dust, Rathalos grows even more ferocious and turns toward the shelter. To strike the head wound the old man gave it, they have to bring it down. Noir Corne gathers his spirit, vaults off the beast, and severs its tail with a Spirit Helm Breaker. But before Yato can close in, it rises again and takes to the sky.

The Flash Bombs that could have brought it down were already broken, but the Artisan Palico makes a substitute from an Originium Slug picked up in the Fowlbeast nest. Blinded by the light, Rathalos crashes down, and Yato, in Demon Mode, leaps into the air.

blocks.cap: The dual blades turn, and her body spins through the air as if dancing.

blocks.x: The Companion Palico binds it with rope. Noir Corne stops Yato before she can finish it off, and the Scholar Palico explains why. Its Originium crystals are inactive — traces of a body that resisted Originium — and its old, starved body no longer has the strength to go far.
When they first saw it, the Companion Palico adds, it was heading toward the volcano — perhaps toward home. Watching Rathalos struggle against its bonds, Yato speaks.

What lies beneath the sky was never ours alone. Every life on this land is only struggling to survive. Fighting one another over a single thread of a way to live… even if it means dying a glorious death.

Then, saying that anything outside the mission is for some busybody to handle, she turns back to help with the evacuation. A little later, in the shelter, Kazuya points at the sky. The monster is flying away.
Wiping his blade, the village head murmurs. 'Akira, you'd have done the same. And I know that back then, you let one of those beasts' young live.'
Epilogue — I Will Still Be Standing Here

Half a month later, Mirai tells the children a story. The hunter in the story could not defeat the monster, but the villagers all got away, and the wounded monster went back into the forest, vowing to return someday.

blocks.cap: The end of the story. The hunter stood facing the forest for a long time.

blocks.x: Kazuya shows off the spear Yato left in his keeping. Yoshitaka has yet to wake, but his wounds are said to have healed a great deal.

The story about the specialty tea growing in other lands was a lie Mirai told to get people to evacuate. Instead, she persuades the village head to put their mining experience to use and go learn how to handle Originium safely from the industry outside.
Only by respecting Originium, and the ruin that comes with it, can we accept the opportunities it brings.
And someday, she says, they will find a way to break free of Originium, too. For a tomorrow in which they can face the light instead of hiding in the shadow of disaster.

Around the same time, on their way back from a mission, Yato and Noir Corne visit the Soubo Mountains without telling the Doctor. The Palicoes have become Rhodes Island's 'Palico Special Operations Team,' though the Scholar Palico insists to this day on calling it the 'Terra Research Commission,' with himself as its self-appointed leader.
On the burned mountain, ash still falls like rain, and Rathalos circles above it. Yato catches a single falling flake of ash in her hand. 'I came… to watch it fall.'

blocks.cap: Amid the drifting ash, the King of the Skies flies high, and higher still.

blocks.x: It climbs higher and higher, as if pulled by a thread. Somewhere up there the thread will finally snap, and its spent body will fall to the earth. That much, they could foresee.
Noir Corne gazes at her lowered fingertips and quietly reaches out, then covers it by saying there was ash on her shoulder. '…Are you smiling?' 'It's nothing. Let's go.'

And the hunter in that story, it's said, spoke these last words: 'I will still be standing here.' Years passed, a young hunter came to stand where the old hunter once stood, and a new monster came before him.
And so the old man's hunt, which began in anger, passed like a fallen leaf into the hands of the next hunter.

act23side.tagline: The spring a Grandmaster who guarded a frontier fortress for a hundred years meant to leave, the sword he had no one to entrust to is stolen, and the city stops dead in the heart of a Catastrophe. And the eighteenth drumbeat of the Wangfeng Festival.

chars.name: Chongyue
chars.desc: The martial-arts Grandmaster who has guarded Yumen for a hundred years. He is about to step down and leave the city.

chars.name: Ling
chars.desc: A wandering poet who calls Chongyue her elder brother. She is fond of drink.

chars.name: Wei Yenwu
chars.desc: Governor of Lungmen and an old friend of the Grandmaster. He has come all the way to Yumen to see his old friend off.

chars.name: Zuo Xuanliao
chars.desc: The general who governs Yumen, the Lord Exorcist. Wounds from defending the city dozens of times have worn his body down.

chars.name: Grand Tutor
chars.desc: An elder statesman of the Yan court. On behalf of the Sui Regulator, he entrusts the Grandmaster with a task.

chars.name: Lin Yühsia
chars.desc: An envoy dispatched from Lungmen and the Rat King's daughter. She investigates a dangerous faction hiding in Yumen · Operator Lin

chars.name: Rat King
chars.desc: An old man known as the shadow of Lungmen. Lin Yühsia's father.

chars.name: Lee
chars.desc: A private detective from Lungmen. He has come to Yumen looking for a sworn brother he lost touch with long ago.

chars.name: Waai Fu
chars.desc: An employee of Lee's Detective Agency and a martial artist fresh out of university. She is climbing the rankings at Yumen's arena.

chars.name: Huai Tianpei
chars.desc: Waai Fu's father and Lee's sworn brother. A martial artist who left home without a word more than ten years ago, he trusts his fists over any weapon.

chars.name: Jieyun
chars.desc: An Anasa girl who wanders the wastes. She has slipped into Yumen to fulfil her late master's wish.

chars.name: Zuo Le
chars.desc: Son of Yumen's general Zuo Xuanliao and a young Candleholder of the Sui Regulator. He excels at qinggong.

chars.name: Qiubai
chars.desc: A swordswoman who has studied the sword at the Grandmaster's side for five years.

chars.name: Du Yaoye
chars.desc: A rookie boss from Shangshu who has founded a logistics company, 'Xingyu Logistics,' in Yumen. Fearless, she does her own legwork.

chars.name: Meng Tieyi
chars.desc: An old smith who owns the sword forge in the south of the city. The martial artists of Yumen hold him in deep regard.

chars.name: Record Keeper
chars.desc: The one who records the martial arts of the world at the Grandmaster's side, writing the Grandmaster's Book of Kung Fu on his behalf.

chars.name: Ch'en
chars.desc: Superintendent of the Lungmen Guard Department. She learned the Chi Xiao swordplay from Wei Yenwu.

terms.name: Yumen
terms.desc: A nomadic fortress-city of Yan that sails the desert, guarding the north. Defenses such as the Wind Aegis hold off Catastrophes and foreign enemies.

terms.name: Wangfeng Festival
terms.desc: A traditional three-day rite held in Yumen each spring. The drum is struck once for every disaster of the past year, so that each is remembered.

terms.name: Wind Aegis
terms.desc: Four mobile outer barriers that encircle Yumen. Normally folded away, they rise when a great Catastrophe approaches.

terms.name: sand sluice
terms.desc: A giant Originium turbine set into Yumen's outer wall. It digs away the sand along the city's path.

terms.name: Imperial Astronomical Bureau
terms.desc: The Yan agency that observes Catastrophes. It keeps observatories and Casters, and uses Catastrophe data to chart the courses of nomadic cities.

terms.name: Shanhaizhong
terms.desc: A fanatical cult that worships the Feranmuts. Twenty years ago it also targeted Yumen and did great damage.

terms.name: Feranmut
terms.desc: Colossal beings that have reigned over the land since ancient times. A thousand years ago, Yan hunted one of them.

terms.name: Sui
terms.desc: A Feranmut bound up with Yan. Its consciousness is divided into twelve.

terms.name: Sui Regulator
terms.desc: A special body the court set up to handle Feranmut-related affairs exclusively. Zuo Le is one of its 'Candleholders.'

terms.name: Anasa
terms.desc: A nomadic tribe that wanders the wastes with no settlement. In an ancient language, the name means 'one without roots.'

blocks.x: At the northern edge of Yan, sailing a thousand li of desert without rest to guard the frontier, is the nomadic fortress-city of **Yumen**. Every spring the city holds the **Wangfeng Festival**, striking the drum once for every disaster it suffered in the past year.

The Grandmaster of martial arts who has guarded this city for a hundred years is about to step down. Those who come to see him off, those searching for someone lost, and those after a single sword all converge on Yumen.
1. The Spring the Grandmaster Leaves

**Lee**, a private detective from Lungmen, has come to Yumen looking for **Huai Tianpei**, a sworn brother who vanished without a word more than ten years ago. Huai Tianpei's daughter **Waai Fu**, who came with him, is climbing the rankings at the arena in the hope that someone will notice her name. If she meets her father, she says, "I'm going to kick him in the jaw as hard as I can."
A girl in foreign dress who loses to Waai Fu in that arena confirms only the rumor that a special sword awaits whoever ranks first, then disappears.

That same day, **Zuo Le**, son of General **Zuo Xuanliao** and a young Candleholder of the Sui Regulator, returns home. **Qiubai**, who has studied the sword at the Grandmaster's side for five years, turns over his verdict that the intent of her sword is impure, and wonders when she will be able to defeat him.

Around then, on the city tower, the Grandmaster **Chongyue** tells his sister **Ling** about a dream from the night before. The desert outside the city had become a forest, and long branches wound around Yumen until it could no longer move.

blocks.cap: Brother and sister on the tower. Ling remarks that he still seems reluctant to leave this city.

blocks.x: Chongyue says he sealed his old name, 'Shuo,' and what remained of his soul inside a sword, and that he is now "just an ordinary man who knows a little kung fu."
2. Messengers Who Never Returned, Petals in the Camp

Meanwhile, in the desert outside the city, **Lin Yühsia**, an envoy from Lungmen, finds traces of a Catastrophe Messenger squad that never came back. She returns with Catastrophe observation data, and when an unknown band surrounds her inside the city, **Meng Tieyi**, the old smith of the sword forge in the south of the city, throws his hammer and saves her.

With Meng Tieyi is **Du Yaoye**, a young boss from Shangshu who has founded a logistics company, Xingyu Logistics. The two were on their way to meet two of her men, who had gone out on their first job escorting the messenger squad.

That day, Lungmen's Governor **Wei Yenwu**, here to see the Grandmaster off, and the **Grand Tutor** of the court gather in the general's tent. At the report that all ten members of the messenger squad have been killed, Zuo Xuanliao, who can no longer properly draw a bow, names what should have been rooted out twenty years ago: a cult that worships the Feranmuts, the **Shanhaizhong**.

The real matter the Grand Tutor raises is the Grandmaster's sword. Sealed within it is one-twelfth of the consciousness of the bestial **Sui** itself, and Chongyue's younger brother, whom the court calls 'the offender,' treats the world as a go board; no one knows where he will place his next stone. The Grand Tutor hands over the Sui Regulator's last commission: suppress the Shanhaizhong, and find someone to entrust the sword to.

Then the scent of peach blossoms, which do not bloom in Yumen in this season, drifts in. A blade appears out of thin air and drives in to just below Wei Yenwu's throat, and Chongyue catches it with his bare hand.
The assassin is a woman with a cold face. Neither the dream Ling spins nor an encirclement joined even by Lin Yühsia's father, the **Rat King**, can hold her.

blocks.cap: "If I wish to leave, who would dare stop me?" Spring pours from a blade like moonlight.

blocks.x: At the same moment, the girl in foreign dress slips into the Grandmaster's empty room. When Zuo Le blocks her way, she answers in halting Yanese, "Who has no loyalty, who betrays, does not deserve this sword," and, cut by his blade, vanishes with the sword in her arms.
3. Three Days' Grace, Seventeen Drumbeats

Zuo Xuanliao seals the city gates at once and gives his son three days: catch the assassin, recover the sword, and find the Shanhaizhong inside the city. But "no word must get out, and the people must not be alarmed."

Chongyue is ordered to remain in the camp. The reason given is that a Grandmaster who hides his true identity cannot well step into a matter involving the Feranmuts. To a frustrated Qiubai, Chongyue says to help Zuo Le instead.

That night at the inn, the Rat King, worrying over his daughter's future, coughs badly and asks Lee for a separate favor. Then the Wangfeng drums sound in the outer city. The seventeen beats stand for the disasters Yumen has suffered over the past year, and the beacons on the walls light the way home for the souls of the fallen.

blocks.cap: The first night of the Wangfeng Festival. The drums announce that the city, the land, and Yan are safe.

blocks.x: 4. The Giant Who Trusts Only His Fists, the Forge from a Story

The next day, the girl in foreign dress wakes in a clinic. The one who took her in is a burly Feline man who works there to pay the medical bills of the people he has hurt. When she says she only wants to bring this sword to her late master, the man, who trusts his fists rather than weapons, accepts her word.

Zuo Le comes to search the place, is seized by the collar at the door and thrown aside, and in the meantime the girl disappears. Then Lee and Qiubai rescue Zuo Le from a Shanhaizhong ambush in the market, and when Lee hears what the man at the clinic looks like, he is lost for words. "Could it really be him...?"

That evening at the sword forge, a wounded girl appears before Meng Tieyi as he sweeps sand from the yard. Her master had told her that in a nomadic city there was a skilled smith's forge, and in its yard a pagoda tree transplanted from far away.

blocks.cap: The sword forge in the south of the city. Spring comes late in the north, and the pagoda tree has yet to bud.

blocks.x: Long ago, in the desert after a battle, Shuo, Zuo Xuanliao, Meng Tieyi, and a swordswoman with a blade on her back carried a dying tree all the way to Yumen. "As long as it takes root in Yumen and keeps growing, our story today will be remembered too."

The girl's name is **Jieyun**, given to her by her master, who saved the wandering **Anasa** tribe and taught them to settle. The same person named the Grandmaster as well. Told that her master died of illness, the old man does not move until the fire in the forge goes out.

Meng Tieyi does not take the sword. Instead he tells her a way out of the city. Even the **sand sluice**, the giant turbine that digs sand away at the outer wall, might be passable tomorrow at the Hour of Yu, when the city is at its slowest.
5. The Bloodstained Armband

Meanwhile Lin Yühsia, going so far as to bring up a smuggler's family, learns where the suspicious band keeps its warehouse. It belongs to the sword forge, and the warehouse keeper's neck bears the burn marks that come only from wearing the masks of the **Imperial Astronomical Bureau**'s survey teams.

Lacking proof, she shows Du Yaoye a bloodstained armband taken from the murder scene outside the city and says she found it in the forge's warehouse. When Du Yaoye runs off, thinking her men may still be alive, Waai Fu asks whether she is using Yaoye. "She's not the only one in danger in this city."

That same night, Taihe, a Monitor Censor of the Department of Discipline and Supervision who had been hunting the Shanhaizhong, is found collapsed near the sword forge. He had been like a mountain to Zuo Le, and now he barely survives. The only answer from Zuo Le's father is a single line: "Keep to your duty." Believing that catching the culprit is his duty, Zuo Le leads a squad to the sword forge.

Around then, Meng Tieyi climbs the city tower for the first time in more than ten years and faces Zuo Xuanliao. His plea to at least recover the bodies of his dead brothers is refused, and what happened twenty years ago, long buried, bursts out.

blocks.cap: The tower at night, climbed for the first time in more than ten years. The beacons of the festival's second day light up one by one.

blocks.x: Twenty years ago, the Shanhaizhong entered the city disguised as martial artists and killed many people. Afterward Zuo Xuanliao no longer relied on the jianghu, and many martial artists were pushed out of Yumen.

Meng Tieyi admits that letting the bandits in was his own fault, but he demands to know whether driving out the jianghu folk who had bled for the city is how one takes responsibility. Zuo Xuanliao's answer is short. "Yumen is Yan's Yumen."
6. High Summer at the Sword Forge in the Third Month

Meanwhile, what greets Zuo Le and Du Yaoye as they burst into the sword forge is not Meng Tieyi but the Shanhaizhong. Jieyun, who was hiding there, rushes out, telling them not to wreck the yard her master used to speak of, and in the confusion Zuo Le snatches her sword.

Then the yard begins to grow hot. Cicadas sing in the third month, and water beading on a blade drips onto Qiubai's face. When a woman the Shanhaizhong call 'Master' appears, Zuo Le recognizes the blade that struck down Taihe, and Qiubai the assassin who went for Wei Yenwu.

As they are driven back against the pagoda tree, a burly man appears and knocks the blade aside with a punch to its spine. Qiubai calls him 'Huai the martial fanatic.' He is a martial artist who has stayed in Yumen for three years on a single promise: that once the Grandmaster retired, they would have a proper bout.

When jianghu folk and the garrison come flooding in, the woman withdraws. Zuo Le has the martial artists who blocked the pursuit, Du Yaoye among them, all hauled off to the camp, and in that gap Huai seizes the sword and vanishes. Waai Fu sees his shadow skim across the rooftops and quietly clenches her fist.
7. The Disciple Who Will Not Call Him Master

Qiubai was born in a water stockade on a river. One day an armored army fell on the village and buried her father beneath the river, and she followed the face of its leader, who had won yet did not rejoice, across Yan to Yumen. That man kept her identity hidden and kept her at his side for five years.

The next day, on the tower, Qiubai asks whether he has ever worried that she might kill him. Chongyue answers that, by poison or from the walls, had she truly meant it he would have died hundreds of times over; what worries him is only that she might kill him and still be unable to let go of her obsession.

Meanwhile, at the city's outskirts, Zuo Le catches up with Jieyun. Holding the sword, Huai tells them to fight with fists alone, the winner to keep the sword. Zuo Le never strikes back at his wounded opponent, and Jieyun wins. Huai hands her the sword, telling her to come back and pay her medical bills once she has repaid what she owes.

blocks.cap: The city outskirts. Fists fell like rain, and Zuo Le only blocked.

blocks.x: That same dawn, in the inn's backyard, Waai Fu practices the fist style her father taught her for the first time in a long while. When Lee says she is her father's daughter after all, she answers that she does not dislike this kung fu, "and I have my own life, too."
Meanwhile Du Yaoye, now released, learns the truth about the armband and tells Lin Yühsia, "You don't even get to apologize."
And Meng Tieyi stands outside his own forge, looking at the seal pasted across its door. "I couldn't even finish the last job cleanly..."
8. The Hammer Over the Enemy's Head

That same day, Chongyue takes his leave of the Grand Tutor. Yumen's destination this time is the capital, and if Sui awakens, this city must be prepared to die along with it. Chongyue says that Zuo Xuanliao kept the jianghu at arm's length twenty years ago because he knew a day would come when Yumen could rely on neither the Grandmaster nor the jianghu.

Then, at the Hour of Shen, Meng Tieyi calls Lin Yühsia out to the warehouse in the south of the city. He had worked with the Shanhaizhong to stage the killing of the messengers and swapped the Catastrophe data for fakes, but he had not actually killed the messenger squad. Huddled in a corner of the warehouse are Du Yaoye's two men, whom he had been holding.

blocks.cap: The warehouse in the south of the city. From inside its sealed walls, the approaching Catastrophe clouds cannot be seen.

blocks.x: He says one Catastrophe will not bring Yumen down; if anything, it will bind people's hearts together again. Lin Yühsia's reply is brief. "...Madman."

Meng Tieyi hands over the real data, and the Shanhaizhong's 'Master' appears to punish the traitor. The old man draws out a pitch-black hammer. "Hide? Me? I've been aching to beat every one of you to death!"

For more than seven thousand days of hammering iron, he had wished for this hammer to come down on his enemies' heads. He cries out that he joined hands with the Shanhaizhong only so that, when the Catastrophe came, he could offer their lives to Yumen as a sacrifice, his own included.

Du Yaoye, arriving late, shouts at him. No one can stop escort bureaus from becoming logistics companies or sword forges from becoming smithies, she says, and that the Yumen of today is not the Yumen of the past gives no one the right to test it with a Catastrophe.
Can you face this city with a clear conscience?! Can you even face yourself?!

In that instant Meng Tieyi hurls his hammer at an enemy closing in behind Du Yaoye, and a long, thin blade cuts open his back. "Xingyu Logistics... was a good idea..." Saying he could not just watch a fine young sprout be broken before his eyes, the old smith breathes his last.
9. Xingyu Logistics' First Delivery

Lin Yühsia hands Du Yaoye the box holding the real data, along with her token, and formally places an order with Xingyu Logistics. "It's a big order, but... fine. Xingyu Logistics accepts." While Lin Yühsia holds the woman back with a sandstorm, Du Yaoye runs.
Just as every glass blade has shattered and a long saber touches the space between Lin Yühsia's brows, a red sword light splits the sand and dust. It is **Ch'en**, who says she was only passing by.

blocks.cap: The red light of Chi Xiao cleaves the sand and dust, and a figure is reflected in the scattered shards of glass.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, for the running Du Yaoye, a few hundred meters stretch longer than a mountain road, and the small box in her arms weighs more than a porter's carrying pole. Words she heard at the sword forge come back to her.
Escort bureau or logistics, the root's the same. You stake people's lives on it, and what you're protecting is people's lives too.
An arrow pierces her shoulder, but while Waai Fu and Qiubai hold off the Shanhaizhong, Du Yaoye at last hands the box to the garrison and collapses.

Before the woman who soon gives chase, the street turns into a bleak autumn night, and not even Ch'en's Chi Xiao can cut through those Arts. As the blade's tip falls on Waai Fu, a back as broad as a wall blocks the way in front of her. It is her father's back, which she has not seen in more than ten years.

When Huai Tianpei sends the woman flying with his bare fists, she realizes the data has already been delivered and lowers her blade. "Yumen will not escape this Catastrophe." Then a scream rings through the street: "Brother Meng...!"

When Waai Fu asks whether he has anything else to say, her father answers, "No need." "Then brace yourself." As their fists meet, memories return of a yard paved with blue stone and of wooden training posts, but she already knows what she will use her kung fu for.

blocks.cap: Her fist reaches her father's chest. It feels like striking a thick wall.

blocks.x: "I lose." Huai Tianpei bursts out laughing. The one technique that kicked him in the jaw was not something he had taught her.
10. Meeting the Catastrophe Head-On

Around then, at the sand sluice, Jieyun is being cornered by the Shanhaizhong. Zuo Le, who as a child was harshly scolded by his father for trying to sneak out that way to play, appears and says he will trust her promise to return the sword. "If you break your word, I will come and bring you back myself."
As Zuo Le turns toward the enemy and draws his blade, Jieyun clutches the sword and leaps into the falling sand.

Meanwhile, recalculated with the real data, the Catastrophe proves to be a sandstorm three times the scale of the one four years ago, with Yumen at its very center. If the city splits apart to evade it, it will take half a year to regain its speed.

"Too late." Zuo Xuanliao decides to meet the Catastrophe head-on. The next day the great barrier, the **Wind Aegis**, rises and blots out half the sun, and in its shadow the people of the east evacuate westward.
11. Victory Lies with Oneself, Life and Death with Fate

On the day the Catastrophe clouds cover half the sky, Chongyue and Huai Tianpei face each other in the desert outside the city. Three years ago he broke off their first exchange because the Grandmaster would not fight at full strength, and since then Huai Tianpei has waited only for the day he steps down. Chongyue means for this bout to lift the morale of the soldiers standing before the Catastrophe.
Victory and defeat lie with oneself. / Life and death lie with fate.

Half a day earlier, Qiubai had drawn her sword on Chongyue. Grudge breeds grudge, and blood breeds blood. The families of those who passed the stockade and ended up buried in the riverbed must have hated her father too, and if she killed this man, someone would come to take revenge on her in turn.

blocks.cap: Before the sword's force has even run its course, Qiubai draws the blade back.

blocks.x: The sword slips from her hand and falls into a ditch, but her face is clear. "I struck at you, and this strike did not kill you."
That I cannot kill you does not mean I have given up on revenge. It is only that 'hatred' is no longer the reason I draw my sword.
When the desert bout begins, Chongyue, who had meant to give his wounded opponent time to catch his breath, holds his tongue. Such consideration would only insult this man.

blocks.cap: Huai Tianpei clenches his fist. Forty years are etched into every crease.

blocks.x: When all nine exchanges are blocked, Huai Tianpei feels as if he is throwing stones into a bottomless swamp, but he takes his stance again, reasoning that if the swamp will not fill, the stones are simply not heavy enough. The tenth exchange is a plain punch without a single change of form. The **Record Keeper**, chronicling the martial arts, sees pain cross the Grandmaster's face for the first time. The victor is Chongyue.

To Huai Tianpei, coughing blood and laughing, Chongyue says there is no need to train another three hundred years; he is already the first among men. As the soldiers beat their sheaths with their blades, Zuo Xuanliao, who has watched in silence, speaks. "The Catastrophe... is here."
12. The Poet Without a Cup, the Old Man Without His Coat

Around then, Jieyun lays the sword on her master's grave, marked by a poplar, and tells her she has seen the forge, the smith, and the pagoda tree. A distant voice speaks from the sword: no one can defeat that person, yet that person is foolish and pitiable, and does not belong to this world.
A scene flashes past like a dream. A man in a hurry, saying he will find a doctor to cure a sick woman, and the woman, looking at his face without a single wrinkle, saying, "We're not the same."

blocks.cap: The old sword is revealed. On its blade lies the shadow of a sun veiled by clouds.

blocks.x: When she draws the sword, words come from somewhere, "You are the one who became most like a 'human,'" and a wisp of lingering soul drifts slowly away. Jieyun turns back toward Yumen to ask him in person.
At the same moment, on the barbican, Ling sends all the Casters to the core, then faces the black clouds bearing down on the city and drinks straight from her gourd, without a cup. "Come!"

blocks.cap: Sand a hundred zhang high pours down like rain, and thunder and lightning rage on every side.

blocks.x: Meanwhile the Shanhaizhong, seizing on the chaos, are stopped by martial artists who have come back from evacuation and by Qiubai, guarding the sand sluice. Asked whether she has forgotten her revenge, Qiubai answers, "I've already found my answer."

Then, as the storm breaches the Wind Aegis and lashes at the core, the Rat King throws off his coat and stands among the Casters. When he coughs blood after taking four waves of the storm almost alone, Lin Yühsia, who has been watching her father's arm tremble like a withered branch, steps forward.

blocks.cap: Lin Yühsia steps in front of her wounded father and takes his place.

blocks.x: 13. Eight Thousand Springs, Eight Thousand Autumns

In the south of the city, where sand falls like rain, the yard of the masterless sword forge lies in ruins, but the pagoda tree alone still lives. There Chongyue reminds Zuo Le, who says he has nothing to be ashamed of before Heaven, of his father's final charge: the Sui Regulator, and even Yumen's return home, exist in the end for the very people he dragged off to the camp.
When handling matters, one must not forget the least measure of compassion and reason.

Before returning the sword, Jieyun asks why her master left twenty years ago. Chongyue does not answer. He says only that he went looking for a hermit who could cure her illness and never found one, and that just as he was about to search again, urgent word came that the Shanhaizhong had appeared in Yumen.

At the end, her master drank the last liquor she had brewed with the children, and while still alive she heard the Anasa song for sending off the dead all the way through. Asked whether he would have gone looking for her after she left, had she lived, Chongyue again does not answer, but he does not look away either. Jieyun says, "You are like the Anasa."

Then, in the central chamber of the core, Chongyue faces the woman of the peach blossoms. She stirred up the trouble to learn Sui's whereabouts from Yumen's navigation coordinates; the Shanhaizhong, who believed her their apostle, were only a tool for sowing chaos. The one seeking a Feranmut is another Feranmut: **Ya**, the beast said to cut away the seasons, slice off space, and hold it in its belly.

blocks.cap: Eight thousand springs, eight thousand autumns. In stopped time, the two stand at either end of a small boat.

blocks.x: In the small world she has carved out, Chongyue says he will hold her there. To her, the world outside may be drifting clouds that pass by, but to him it is not.
To me, it is city walls being destroyed, homes collapsing, soldiers and people suffering.

To Ya's fury that a fragment of that thing should protect a human city, Chongyue answers, "I am I, and it is it." Then he asks in return how a Feranmut that fled a thousand years ago and licked its wounds in this little world it carved out differs from the humans she scorns.

The boat stops, and a fist gathering ten thousand techniques into one strikes Ya's chest. Saying there is no point in killing her when a proxy's body can be replaced at any time, Chongyue only tells her to leave Yumen.
Epilogue — The Eighteenth Drumbeat

After the Catastrophe passes, the people of the east, evacuated in advance, are unharmed, but two of the Wind Aegis are broken, and Yumen will not be able to move again for two months. Chongyue entrusts his sword to Huai Tianpei, the only one to land a blow on him, and when Huai says he will train forty more years and come find him, Chongyue answers that he will wait.
Huai Tianpei leaves without a word once again. Waai Fu says she will not hurry to find him, and that next time they meet, a kick to the jaw will not be the end of it.

Somewhere in the desert, the Shanhaizhong ringleader burns a letter stamped with a sealing wax that fewer than five people at court may use. Ya, returned wounded, says she has already found where it lies.
Meanwhile, Lin Yühsia decides to stay in Lungmen instead of going to Victoria. A burden someone has set down must be taken up by someone else.
The Rat King's daughter isn't the Rat King, but she could become one. This time, it's my choice.

As Chongyue departs, Wei Yenwu uses his finger as a sword to show him the final move of the Chi Xiao swordplay: Heaven's Eye, the eye that pierces the sky. "The sword of Heaven's Eye: when it must sever, it severs."

blocks.cap: Sword energy drawn with a finger sends ripples across the tea in the cup.

blocks.x: Before the city gate, someone who has spent the whole afternoon playing go alone speaks to Chongyue. The unfamiliar voice says it learned something thanks to his sword, and tells him, who took a human body yet remained alone, that he was always an outsider. "Farewell, brother."

blocks.cap: A single ko remains in the corner. "...Fill the neutral points, and the endgame is done."

blocks.x: Chongyue places a single white stone. An impartial, orthodox move.
Hearing from the Record Keeper that the Grandmaster has gone, Zuo Xuanliao beats the drum himself that evening. "The road is long. Someone ought to see him off."

blocks.cap: The drums of the Wangfeng Festival spread out across the desert beneath the sunset.

blocks.x: Through seventeen drumbeats the man walks the desert, and the wind erases his footprints one by one. Then the eighteenth drum sounds. It stands for one more Catastrophe Yumen has just come through.
The man stops, but does not look back. "Time to go."

Even in that spring the Catastrophe swept through, the pagoda tree brought from the desert and rooted in Yumen still lived. As long as the tree kept growing, the story of that day would be remembered, a swordswoman had said long ago.

act22side.tagline: A spear-wielder who wandered the wilds under a hidden identity becomes the guide of a band of hunted Tarans, and in the end confesses that she is Dublinn's 'Leader.' In a land where the Lights-Out Bell tolls, she searches not for a fire that burns, but for one that lights the way.

chars.name: Reed
chars.desc: A spear-wielder who wanders the wilds alone, hiding who she is. She helps a band of hunted Taran drifters · Operator Reed the Flame Shadow

chars.name: Fionn
chars.desc: A talkative, warm-hearted Taran peddler. He appoints himself the one who keeps the fugitives' camp running

chars.name: Selmon
chars.desc: A rough Taran woman who goes about in Dublinn garb. She leads the band of fugitives from the front

chars.name: Moran
chars.desc: An Infected woman with night blindness. Quiet, but resolute

chars.name: Bagpipe
chars.desc: An operator and former Victorian soldier who insists on protecting ordinary people

chars.name: Ch'en
chars.desc: A swordswoman from Lungmen. Bagpipe's partner from their school days; together they track the Spectre Force

chars.name: Harmonie
chars.desc: A Feline who moves in County Trent's high society. A spy in disguise

chars.name: Fischer
chars.desc: An informant watching Harmonie in County Trent. He pursues the unanswered questions of an arson case · Operator Puzzle

chars.name: Outcast
chars.desc: The one who rescued Reed in County Hillock and brought her back. Bagpipe trusts her deeply

chars.name: The Brigadier
chars.desc: A member of the Duke of Wellington's guard and an officer of Dublinn. Carries out The Leader's orders alongside Harmonie

chars.name: Eblana
chars.desc: Reed's older sister. She has the same face and voice as her younger sister

chars.name: Earl of Warwick
chars.desc: An earl of County Oak Grove. He leads the 'Clan of Tarans,' a circle devoted to reviving Taran culture

chars.name: Duke of Caster
chars.desc: One of Victoria's great dukes. He is on close terms with the marquess who rules County Trent

chars.name: Duke of Wellington
chars.desc: One of Victoria's great dukes. He commands the elite Redsteel Guard

terms.name: Dublinn
terms.desc: An armed rebel group active across southern Victoria in the name of Taran liberation. It is led by a mysterious 'Leader'

terms.name: Spectre Force
terms.desc: A Dublinn unit, notorious for its brutal practice of leaving no witnesses

terms.name: Redsteel Guard
terms.desc: An elite unit under the Duke of Wellington

terms.name: Lights-Out Bell
terms.desc: A curfew bell that tolls each night over the Scáthanna Fields. Once it rings, not even a lamp may be lit outside the mines and factories

terms.name: Draco
terms.desc: The fire-bearing bloodline that once ruled the old Taran kingdom. Since Victoria took its throne, it has survived only in legend

terms.name: King Gaeil
terms.desc: The title of the Draco monarchs who ruled the old Taran kingdom

terms.name: Tarans
terms.desc: Natives annexed by Victoria and stripped of their name and language. They drift in the wake of nomadic cities, worn down by discrimination and Oripathy

terms.name: County Trent
terms.desc: A Victorian nomadic city with jurisdiction over the Scáthanna Fields. It is ruled by the Marquess of Trent

terms.name: County Hillock
terms.desc: A Victorian nomadic city. Last autumn it was the scene of a catastrophe involving Dublinn

terms.name: County Oak Grove
terms.desc: A Victorian nomadic city, where the Earl of Warwick's manor once stood

blocks.x: 1090, County Oak Grove. At the manor of the **Earl of Warwick**, a gathering was held to celebrate the success of a play that had put Taran history on the stage. The earl recited a line from the play by the poet Williams, and said that another red dragon might yet appear in Tara.
So that the Draco's own kin shall never again cross blades with one another. Unless a day comes when the red dragon's flame raises the fallen warriors anew from the forge.
Eight years later, in 1098, on the Scáthanna Fields. Here the Lights-Out Bell tolled every night, and once it rang, not a single lamp could be lit outside the mines and factories.
Through that darkness walked a white-haired spear-wielder, **Reed**, alone. She was searching for something, and it had to do with 'Dublinn.'
1. The Fields of the Lights-Out Bell

That night in the village of Redridge, the Taran drifters **Fionn** and Fergal were caught by a patrol while breaking a pharmacy window. Then flames shot up from a storehouse at the garrison, and while the soldiers ran to fight the fire, Reed freed the two from their bonds.

blocks.cap: 1098, Redridge. The night streets after the Lights-Out Bell.

blocks.x: After they fled into the marshes, Reed learned the rest. Fionn's band had killed two soldiers in a clash with a patrol, and as wanted men they had been circling the wilds for twelve days.

When the pursuers closed in, it was a Taran woman in Dublinn garb, **Selmon**, who saved them. When Selmon moved to finish off the fallen soldiers, Reed stopped her hand and asked why she was imitating the ways of the Spectre Force.
Asked whether she was a doctor, Reed said no. Even so, she said, she wanted to help them.
The next morning Selmon got rid of Reed with a lie about a companion who had not come back, and while Reed drew the patrol's eyes, she slipped away with the band.

The patrol captain questioned the captured Reed in Taran: was she not the white-haired Vouivre who had cut down Dublinn soldiers a few days before? When Reed asked why a Taran would hate them, the captain shouted at her never to use that name.

In that moment a voice rang inside Reed's head. "Go, Loughshinny. The best way to hide what you have done is to get rid of every witness." Reed answered that she would not. She struck down only the captain and withdrew.

Waiting for her in the woods was Fionn, who had come back because his conscience would not let him do otherwise. Reed said it did not matter; she was only a reed by the roadside. Fionn told her that her face said she was hurting.
Then Fionn asked a favor. Protect them until they could find a carrier and get aboard.
2. Fire Burning in a Dead Soldier's Eyes

Meanwhile, two Rhodes Island operators had come to the same wilds: **Bagpipe** and **Ch'en**. They had faced the Spectre Force once before in County Hillock, and now they were following Dublinn's trail.
The Spectre Force soldiers they cut down had already been dead for more than two days. In their eyes burned a purple flame.

blocks.cap: A purple flame burning in a dead warrior's eyes.

blocks.x: Bagpipe knew that flame. It was the Arts of the Caster who had led the Spectre Force in County Hillock.

Around the same time, a Feline named **Harmonie** was moving through the high society of County Trent. The informant watching her, **Fischer**, kept up his investigation without reporting to his superiors the Oripathy he had contracted on an earlier operation.

Some days later, out of food, Selmon's band raided a caravan. Ch'en, who was traveling with the caravan, subdued them with her sword still in its sheath. Reed, arriving too late to stop the raid, crossed weapons with Bagpipe before the two recognized each other.
Reed said she was now tracking Dublinn on her own. Someone in Dublinn had changed her fate, and there was something she wanted to take back from them.

At about the same time, Harmonie sat across from **'The Brigadier'**, a member of the Duke of Wellington's guard and an officer of Dublinn. The Brigadier reminded her of the mission The Leader had entrusted to her: track down Loughshinny, who had survived County Hillock.
3. Until They No Longer Need Me

After the band left a village with food, a number of Infected kept trailing behind them. Among them was **Moran**, whom Fionn had not heard from in a long time. A famine some years before had damaged her eyes, and she could not see at night. In a trembling voice, Reed said she would bring them along.
Asked what the point was of taking the Infected with them, Reed said she did not know. But someone had saved her all the same, she said. She, too, was Infected.
Reed said she would get supplies from Rhodes Island and take everyone to the domain of a duke who had reason to shelter Tarans. Selmon would not follow. She was going back to Dublinn.

Meanwhile, Ch'en and Bagpipe found a garrison that had been wiped out in an ambush a week earlier. Not a single enemy body remained. Reed called them wraiths: pitiful people who had surely died, yet could not find rest.

blocks.cap: The wilds where the annihilated garrison lay.

blocks.x: Selmon did not believe her. Dublinn had simply won and moved on to save more Tarans, she countered. Then she called Reed 'Leader' in mockery and walked off toward the battlefield.
Reed gathered the others and followed her. She had promised to protect them. Until they no longer needed her.
4. Haystacks and an Unusual Fire
Some time later, the band found shelter in a village. On the night the Lights-Out Bell rang, Bagpipe found Reed sitting outside alone and dragged her over to a haystack.

blocks.cap: A night lying in the hay. To Reed, it smelled not of hay but only of mud and dust.

blocks.x: Reed spoke of a city she had lived in long ago. Dark red brick walls, climbing flowers, a house where she watched from the study window for her parents to come home. That house was gone now.
She began to mention an older sister, then fell silent. Bagpipe said that Reed only ever said 'no' when she talked about herself, as if she were trying to get away from something.
Reed said she wanted to ask Outcast, who had saved her life, what she had seen in her. Bagpipe asked whether she had put that question to herself first.

Then Moran came out, feeling her way through the dark. She did not want to die quietly, she said; she wanted to walk with them for as long as her legs could carry her. Reed held out her hand. "Let's go together."

At the same hour, at a viscount's party, Harmonie heard a rumor from the countryside. The fire in an arson case a few days earlier had burned with explosive force, yet left no trace of an Originium explosion, and it had been extremely hard to put out.

blocks.cap: An unusual fire. To Harmonie, the description was familiar.

blocks.x: Harmonie recalled the name. Loughshinny. And from that moment on, Fischer, glass in hand, had his eyes fixed on her.

In an inner room at the same party, the **Duke of Caster** was waiting for Fischer. The duke knew even about his infection, and asked which he wanted once the mission was over: promotion or retirement.
5. Brother
After three days crossing the wilds, Reed's group watched from hiding as an elite Victorian squad walked into an ambush. The ambushers were Dublinn, dressed just like Selmon.

It was Fischer who had sent that squad. Having read every report from County Hillock, he had found testimony that the 'Leader' that day had not been one person. Lay two puzzle pieces of the same shape side by side, he said, and people will see one only as the other's shadow.

As the fighting spread, drifters who ran out to join Dublinn were attacked in silence by Dublinn soldiers. Ch'en, who pulled them out, said these soldiers were already dead. And as everyone fled, Selmon caught sight of someone among the dead soldiers and stopped. "...Brother."
That evening Fionn told them her story. Selmon's brother had joined Dublinn. Two years ago Selmon had followed him, then run away partway there.
That night Selmon attacked the column of dead soldiers alone. The mask came off a soldier who would not fall even under the blows of her wooden club, and beneath it was a familiar face.
Her brother's eyes did not see his sister. Just as on the night he resolved to seek out Dublinn, they looked only to the distant horizon, burning with the flame of longing.
As Selmon reached out blankly, a searing flame bloomed against the night sky. When it died down, the fallen soldiers did not rise again.

blocks.cap: The wilds at night, after the march of the dead had stopped.

blocks.x: 6. Younger Sisters in the Shadows

That flame was Reed's. Ever since her childhood, when she was called Loughshinny, there had been fire in her body, and her parents taught her to hide it. But her older sister, who had the same face and voice, secretly burned whatever she disliked, and always came out ahead.

On the night their parents died in a holiday blizzard, her sister **Eblana** pushed her forward and told her to knock on any door. Behind her burned a cold purple flame that had just taken their enemy's life.

After that the sisters were raised by their 'teacher.' One snowy night in the teacher's study, Loughshinny gave her answer: he had killed his political rivals, so taking his life was what they had to do.

blocks.cap: A snowy night. Eblana questions her younger sister in the teacher's study.

blocks.x: Eblana said no. Death would only carry him to his ideal, and the power she meant to hold was far greater than his daydreams. Then she asked her sister what she wanted. Loughshinny, who held only a small dream like the warm flame in a hearth, could not answer.
No matter, little sister. If you do not know where your desire lies, then first become me. One day, you and I will both be 'The Leader.'
That flame was watching her. And she became her sister's shadow.
Now, in the silence of the wilds, Selmon laid the mask back over her brother's face. Her brother had endured even burning on after death, she said, so why could she not even bear to look at him?

Selmon spoke of a day when she and her brother had skipped work and walked out to look down on wilds covered in wildflowers. Her brother had said that was Tara. The flame Reed had left him was as beautiful as those flowers, Selmon said. Then she asked.
What my brother was chasing right up until he died... the future Dublinn promised. Is it really nothing but an illusion?
Reed could not answer. In the light of the fire burning at her spear's tip, tears were running down Selmon's cheeks.
7. A Toast to Those Not Here

Afterward, tents sent by Rhodes Island went up on the outskirts of County Trent's jurisdiction. Bagpipe and Ch'en were to leave before dawn, and Reed said that once she had seen everyone settled, she would look for a way to help the Tarans.
That evening Ch'en called Reed a Draco. To Victorian eyes, she said, the only living Draco now was Dublinn's red dragon. But to some people, whether Reed was a Draco or not would hardly matter.
In the tent, singing began. The drifter Odhrán played a blade of grass like a whistle, and the people sang a Taran drinking song that raises a glass 'to those who are not here.'

blocks.cap: Campfire and song in the tent. Only days ago, these people had been struggling just to stay alive.

blocks.x: This is how their lives could have been all along. Better than this, of course. ...You gave them their lives back.
Pressed by the others, Reed sang a song too. Where does the wanderer go from here, setting out on a long road?

While the song went on, Fischer's unit was surrounding the clearing from the woods. When Fionn stepped out for some air and spotted them in the fog, it was Fischer who greeted him first. "Good evening."
8. The Name That Calls a Shadow

Fischer held a dagger to Bagpipe, but never took his eyes off Reed. Faced with a City Council writ of investigation, Bagpipe laid down her weapon, and the drifters were led into the woods with their hands bound.
In the tent, Fischer asked about Reed's former identity. A person with no records, who could give neither name nor origin. Was that not the same as a 'shadow'?
Fischer told her that Dublinn had come to rescue her, and offered not to pursue her past crimes if she came under his protection.
