The finishing blow lands at the representatives' meeting that follows. Catch confesses that he likes berry tomato wine — and Croque and Deculture, declaring they've wasted their time at a place built by someone like that, flip to backing the demolition on the spot.
The demolition passes, and a new landmark will go up in its place, chosen through a design competition between Stitch and Catch. But for someone who talked so big, Stitch looks oddly gloomy.
4. The Lupo Who Gave Up on the Surface

Around that time, Avdotya, who tags along claiming she's keeping an eye on the group, insists her name is 'a typical Durin name.' When Gavial pokes at it — 'But Avdotya is Ursine' — she slowly starts to open up.

blocks.cap: After Tomimi's shopping spree wrapped up: the spot where Avdotya opened up a little about home.

blocks.x: How she lost her status, her family, and her friends overnight, and fled Ursus. How, if all your memories of home are pain, home is no different from an inn you stopped at along the way.
To her, Zeruertza is a place with no exploitation, no schemes, no assassinations, which is why nothing from the surface — even with the best of intentions — can be let in.
Evil is learned, and it's contagious. The people down here have never experienced it, so they have no resistance to it.
'No matter how you dress it up, you can never become a real Durin.' To Gavial's straight pitch, she answers that even if she can't be Durin, she'll protect this innocence as a citizen of Zeruertza.
Gavial adds one more thing: 'Weren't you the one who said the Durin are good at solving their own problems?' The reply is firm: 'Stop using my own words against me!'
5. Summer's End, and the Winner Is... the Boat

On demolition day, by the water, Inam makes a serious request of Gavial: come back and become Acahualla's Lord Ameer. Otherwise, under a Lord Ameer sent by the Sargon court, the jungle won't stay as free as it is now.
When Gavial puts off her answer, Catch cuts in. What's meant to end will end someday, so how about a group photo before the slide disappears?

blocks.cap: "Tomimi, gimme a smile too!" A summer group photo, taken in front of a slide about to vanish.

blocks.x: When the countdown ends, the blast is quieter than expected, and the slide slowly collapses — or, to polish the wording a bit, melts into the water. Even Elysium, permanently marinated in booze, watches this one stone-cold sober.

Next up is the first season of Croque's brand-new 'Zeruertza Competition Series': a swimming race. It's really a scouting trip to the tunnel across the lake, but there's even a prize on the line. One month of unlimited craft beer.

The contestants: Elysium, 'Rhodes Island's sexiest man'; Gavial, swimming with Edge (who's coming along on the survey) on her back; and Zeruertza's representative Avdotya, who caved to Edge's sighing pleas and jumped in fully clothed. But then, from behind, Stitch crashes the race in a boat.
He'd been glaring at a blank blueprint, with no confidence he could win the citizens over, until Deculture sent him out on the pretext of an equipment errand. And there was no rule against vehicles.

Furious, Edge leaps onto the boat and whacks Stitch on the head, the two grapple, the control panel breaks, and the runaway boat crosses the finish line in first place. The winner, christened the 'Ale Keg' on the spot, keeps right on going, rams the tunnel entrance, and punches a big hole in it. Nobody gets the prize.
'...What on earth are these people doing.' Inam's one-line review, listening in on the broadcast.
6. What Lay Beyond the Tunnel

blocks.cap: The two people Stitch sees when he comes to: a soaking-wet Avdotya, and Croque, who brought a change of clothes.

blocks.x: What Stitch hears when he wakes up from being knocked out is a deafening roar. With the digging equipment busted, Gavial is single-handedly slicing the rock into neat blocks to widen the tunnel entrance.
But Elysium comes back from checking inside the tunnel with a stiff face. What everyone sees when they follow him is an active Originium vein, exposed right out of the rock.

The earthquake had warped the strata and shoved a vein that used to be far away right up to the city's doorstep — and with the dome's prospecting equipment broken, nobody knew. Edge's verdict: it'll blow in less than a month.

Soon an evacuation-prep broadcast goes out across the city, but the Durin stay calm. They already knew the risk back when they chose to build a slide instead of fixing the dome. 'Look at it another way — at least we had a great summer, right?'

Meanwhile, in front of the vein, the argument over how to evacuate hundreds of thousands of people heats up: Avdotya wants to go through the tunnel to a neighboring city, Edge wants to dig shelters on the far side, and both keep getting louder. Gavial, who's been listening quietly, tilts her head. Why not widen the elevator, all go up to the surface together, and stay with her tribe for a while?
**'Uh, you guys... you never even thought about going to the surface?'**
An entire city moving up to the surface has never happened in Durin history. But the elevator was originally built to haul ore, so it's sturdy, and there should be room to widen it.
7. Who Takes the Lord Ameer's Seat?

Avdotya points out one thing. If hundreds of thousands of people suddenly appear on Sargon soil, how will the local Lord Ameer — how will the nation of Sargon — respond? And Acahualla has no Lord Ameer.

blocks.cap: The resolve of the day she left the jungle to study medicine. And the tribe right in front of her.

blocks.x: For the first time, Gavial hesitates. It isn't that she shies away from responsibility. The resolve of the day she left to save people from Oripathy through medicine, and Acahualla itself — both are right, and she wants both.
Just as Gavial is about to speak, Tomimi cries out first. I'll become Lord Ameer. I'll bear that responsibility.
As Gavial falters, Eunectes speaks up. That axe — she actually stayed up several nights straight making it. And Gavial doesn't need to thank her for it.
Your fist is much bigger than you think, Gavial. Because you have me.
There's Tomimi, the people of Rhodes Island, everyone Gavial has ever saved — so all our fists are her fists. Watching that familiar scene, Inam lets out a quiet sigh, and makes a decision.
She'll take the Lord Ameer seat herself. As the Messenger and scout the Sargon government planted in Acahualla, she can contend for that seat — and that way, Tomimi can stay by Gavial's side.
They're... no, we're all just fools living in the jungle.
Meanwhile, Stitch gazes up at the dome alone. 'Teacher, it seems I'll never get the chance to surpass you now.' He disappears on a boat.
8. Even a Dying City Gets Dressed Up

Half a day after the evacuation broadcast, what the city's Durin throw themselves into isn't packing, but home renovation. A Durin city can't move, so if the end can't be avoided, they get to decide what it looks like when it comes. So that someday, whoever finds the ruins will marvel, and raise a glass in their memory.
It's what you'd call dressing up the city for its death.

blocks.cap: The street outside the library. Everyone's busy figuring out how to fix up their homes, not how to pack.

blocks.x: So the dome needs work too — but Stitch himself is nowhere to be seen. Stitch's mentor, **Finch Canvas**, was an architect who captivated the city with a single line, 'throw off our ceaseless desires,' and then one day left without a word. Catch, who used to be his assistant, thinks that masterpiece of a dome has become a burden for Stitch.

Elysium, as Catch's 'big brother,' gives him advice: don't say 'let's compete fairly' — cut off every escape route first, then tell him you'll work at it together. Deculture, on the other hand, says running away when it hurts isn't wrong either, and sends her robots to help Stitch.

Meanwhile, Inam, digging through maps in the library, opens up to Avdotya too. She also ran away to Acahualla, sick of the Lord Ameers' endless power struggles. But watching Gavial live as if there's nothing in the world worth bowing to, she just can't help helping her.

Eunectes, whose dream is to build the greatest machine on all of Terra, says that if fists don't work, she'll use an axe; if an axe doesn't, a hammer; and if nothing else works, she'll build a whole nomadic city if that's what it takes to help Gavial.

While everyone's caught up talking about Gavial, it's the High Priest and the robots who find the map — and Avdotya, after even getting called 'Avdotya, idiot' by a robot, steps up to take charge of persuading the residents.
9. The Medic Who Broke Down the Door

Literature representative Avdotya stands before the residents in the square, and before laying out the evacuation plan, she tells a story she has never told anyone: the past not of Avdotya Razorpen, but of Avdotya Nikolayevna Ivanova.

blocks.cap: "I was born to a noble family in Ursus..."

blocks.x: The origins she worked so hard to erase never did go away. But now that she has met Gavial and the people around her, she knows: it isn't really all that bad.
At the same moment, in the little lakeside house where Stitch once lived with his mentor. Right after Stitch shouts 'Don't come in!', there's a thunderous crash.

blocks.cap: The door and the wall came down together. 'Don't come in' was not accepted as an answer.

blocks.x: On the floor lies a crumpled dome blueprint with only a few lines drawn. Gavial tells him: the one who won't leave you alone isn't me — it's you, who won't show anyone what's inside.

Only then does Stitch open up. Eight years ago he survived an active Originium explosion and contracted Oripathy, and with nowhere to go, he was taken in by Finch, who even gave him his surname. The assignment his mentor left behind was to design a dome that would win everyone over — but not one of his proposals was ever adopted.
Now the dome looks to him like a birdcage his mentor built to lock him in. 'I'm already a failure.' Let Catch do the dome, he says.
Gavial asks: in the end, you couldn't abandon this city — so have you ever asked the people who rejected you why? '...No.'
Just then, Catch comes to say goodbye. He's just handed his acting design representative seat over to Stitch, and while the road is still open, he's going to the neighboring city to look for Finch.
Stitch's fist swings, then stops halfway and drops in midair. He knows they all mean well. That's exactly why he can't bear it.
Why won't you just leave me alone?! Why won't you let me keep hiding?! Why is everyone being so nice to me?!
Without a word, Catch picks the blueprint up off the floor and hands it over. 'You can do better than this, Stitch.'
Since when do you need a reason to be kind? What's wrong with not wanting someone to fall apart?
Then Gavial clenches her fist. He deceived the tribe from the very start and caused a lot of people trouble, so — he can take just one hit.

blocks.cap: Facing the incoming fist, Stitch realizes he has to let something go.

blocks.x: The joy of sitting in his mentor's lessons, the regret after his mentor left, the bitterness he swallowed every time he lost a competition. Here in front of him was someone trying to understand the feelings he'd been sure nobody ever could. Stitch decides he should take this punch.
THUD! What ended up with a deep dent was the desk. **'Relax, my fist only hits bad guys.'**
10. Hands Up for Option Three

Meanwhile, in the square, the vote begins. For the tunnel evacuation, which would leave about 30% of the residents unable to get out, a scattered few Durin ready to sacrifice themselves raise their hands; for digging shelters, more hands go up from burly Durin clutching bottles. For going to the surface, not a single hand.
Avdotya pushes once more. Acahualla is warm all year round — a natural Great Aquapit with lakes and waterfalls. The old her would have been the first to object, but now she believes this is right.

Then Gavial climbs onto the stage, shouts 'Acahualla welcomes all Durin!', and gets hustled right back off. The square starts buzzing. They're nice, and they're strong too — and apparently 'Stranger Things' is still being published up there!

Edge announces Catch's resignation and the successor he named, and Stitch takes the stage. Going to the surface is the safest option, and it'll give them time to dress up the city — and if he keeps designing and reinforcing the dome to the very end, it won't stop the explosion, but it can buy them time.
So let's go to the surface together. I'm sure my teacher... would think so too.

blocks.cap: One, two, three... hands rising for the third option.

blocks.x: Hands go up, one, then another, and far off on the high ground, Catch can be seen giving a brief wave. For the first time, Stitch learns how overwhelming it feels to be acknowledged.
Epilogue. A Jungle About to Get Even Louder

blocks.cap: A dome blueprint drawn in the middle of the square, in full view of everyone. Master Edge called this 'saving time.'

blocks.x: A few days later, Stitch is designing the dome in public, right in the middle of the square. He gets into long arguments with passersby handing out unsolicited advice, but apparently it isn't as much of a burden as he'd feared.

Edge hands Stitch a letter found at the very top of the dome. It's the letter Finch left for his student, and the mentor had known all along that Oripathy had made his student deeper — and more stubborn.
...that the biggest problem you ran into was neither a flaw in the design nor the difficulty of construction, but simply... persuading people.

Meanwhile, Catch doesn't change his mind about leaving. He truly wants to find Finch, and when the city is rebuilt, he wants to design something amazing with Stitch. Elysium, too, promises to look into Finch's whereabouts once he's back.

Croque, being Croque, gets greedy for surface business, sells Avdotya off as a liaison for the back-and-forth, and gets an earful for it. In the meantime, up on the surface, Yota and Yogi are boring through a cave, and Inam is getting ready to go meet the Padishah about the Lord Ameer business.

On the day the vein finally blew, the tremor could still be felt even after they'd come up by elevator. Every last resident made it to the surface, and Gavial comes up last of all, bringing Avdotya, who stayed until the city's final moment, and Stitch, who guarded the construction site to the end every single day and finally conked out.

blocks.cap: Gavial steps off the last elevator with a sleeping Stitch in her arms. In front of the cave, the Durin and the Tiacauh were waiting together.

blocks.x: 'The weather's nice today, so let's all go to the lake and have a blast!' The cheers erupt before she's even finished.

This summer, Gavial's fist never did find a bad guy to knock down. What opened the way were stories brought out into the open and hands raised together — which is why Acahualla is even louder than usual today. And it's only going to get louder.

act18side.tagline: A noble and a wanderer who carry the same curse inside them play a single piece together, and each tries to take on the other's share to end that curse. In a time as brief as the afterglow, neither of them would say that fate had won.

chars.name: Ebenholz
chars.desc: A young noble of unknown origin. He cuts into an unpaid audition without warning and asks to play a duet on the flute.

chars.name: Kreide
chars.desc: An aspiring cellist who has drifted from place to place with his frail grandfather. He entered the concert audition to earn money for his grandfather's treatment.

chars.name: Hibiscus
chars.desc: A Sarkaz Operator dispatched by Rhodes Island. She has come to investigate an abnormal improvement among the Infected of the Afterglow · Operator Hibiscus the Purifier

chars.name: Czerny
chars.desc: The only famous musician the Afterglow has ever produced. Ill as he is, he is preparing a farewell concert.

chars.name: Andante
chars.desc: A local Rhodes Island Operator stationed in Vyseheim's Afterglow. He is on easy terms with the Infected residents.

chars.name: Ursula
chars.desc: A distant relative of Czerny's, an old woman who runs his household. She likes to meddle and misses very little.

chars.name: Gertrude
chars.desc: The lord of Vyseheim and Czerny's longtime patron. She is putting unusual effort into this concert.

chars.name: Biegler
chars.desc: The manager of a café in the Afterglow. He offers coffee with good grace, but something about him is not ordinary.

chars.name: Lachmann
chars.desc: A suspicious Infected who has turned up in the Afterglow. He stirs people up with rumors of a prophecy.

chars.name: Lava
chars.desc: Hibiscus's younger sister, Infected like her. She is absorbed in her research on Originium Arts · Operator Lava the Purgatory

terms.name: Vyseheim
terms.desc: A nomadic city in Leithanien, ruled by the counts of House Strollo.

terms.name: Afterglow
terms.desc: The Infected settlement within Vyseheim. It was originally an industrial district.

terms.name: Afterglow Hall
terms.desc: The concert hall in the Afterglow. It was originally built as an Arts fortress in the Witch King's time.

terms.name: Cliffy Patio
terms.desc: Vyseheim's noble quarter. Infected from the Afterglow may not enter without permission.

terms.name: Voice of Mundane
terms.desc: A melody of unknown nature that dwells in the bodies of a very few. It grants powerful Arts, but wears down body and mind with headaches and auditory hallucinations.

terms.name: Witch King
terms.desc: The tyrant of Leithanien, brought down by the Twin Empresses twenty years ago. He was deeply versed in music, but every piece he left behind was destructive.

terms.name: Twin Empresses
terms.desc: The present rulers, who drove out the Witch King and came to govern Leithanien.

terms.name: Empresses' Voice
terms.desc: A force that answers directly to the Twin Empresses and acts on their will.

terms.name: False Recovery
terms.desc: A state in which an Infected's body forcibly compensates for Oripathy damage and only appears healthy. In truth, it is a sign that the disease is worsening rapidly.

terms.name: Morgen und Abend
terms.desc: Czerny's signature piece, written in his youth in memory of a friend who died. It is also the set piece for this concert's audition.

terms.name: Lied des klaren Himmels
terms.desc: A Leithanien song from 1078. Today only its opening verses are still passed down among the people.

blocks.x: In Leithanien there is a song of which only the opening verses survive.
The Sky is blue and fine, / The Breeze lilts by in Song; / The River murmurs clear, / My Heart is filled with Hope.
In that country's nomadic city of Vyseheim lies an Infected settlement called the Afterglow, and in it stands a concert hall that could be either a building or an enormous instrument: Afterglow Hall.

**Hibiscus**, a Sarkaz Operator dispatched by Rhodes Island, had come to investigate why the condition of the Infected here was improving for no clear reason. The day she arrived happened to be the application day for the farewell concert of **Czerny**, the one famous musician the Afterglow had ever produced.
At that concert a week later, a noble with a flute and a wanderer who had lost his cello would share a stage. Neither of them knew that they carried the same thing inside them.
1. An Unpaid Audition

**Andante**, the local operator who came to meet her, told Hibiscus the mission could wait until tomorrow and led her to the plaza. When Czerny, out on the streets for the first time in half a year, began to play the piano, the crowd filling the plaza fell silent all at once.
When the performance ended, a retainer of the lord, **Gertrude**, came to put a stop to street performances. Czerny sent him away, saying that in the Afterglow no one could stop him from playing.

blocks.cap: Afterglow Hall. The Afterglow takes its name from this concert hall.

blocks.x: That same day, the aspiring cellist **Kreide** left his ailing grandfather at home and went to the application session. There, on the audition stage, he heard for the first time that the concert paid nothing at all.
He had come to earn money for treatment, but he set a borrowed cello between his knees and began to play. Soon a young noble dressed in black stepped onto the stage, playing a flute.

He gave his name as **Ebenholz** and offered to pay for the grandfather's treatment if Kreide would form a team with him. Kreide accepted, and their piece was set: Czerny's signature work, 'Morgen und Abend.'
Meanwhile, uneasy about the noble's generosity, Hibiscus brought Kreide's grandfather to the office and gave him her own bed.

The audition the next day, judged by Czerny himself, was a disaster. Czerny pointed out that Ebenholz ignored the cello's feeling and held to his own tempo, and when Ebenholz bristled at being called 'coddled by flattery,' Czerny eliminated them on the spot.
2. An Offer of Freedom
On the way back, Ebenholz was struck by headaches again, and a voice from nowhere mocked him as a 'useless fake.'

That day Gertrude revealed her true reason for summoning him to Vyseheim. It was because of the **Voice of Mundane** inside him that he held a hollow title as **Graf Urtica**, and Gertrude offered to remove it.

Kreide carried a Voice of Mundane as well. When the two played together in Afterglow Hall, which the Witch King had built as an Arts fortress, a 'Resonanz' would arise, and the plan was to use it to move Ebenholz's Voice into Kreide. Afterward, Graf Urtica's death would be announced, and Gertrude would hold a card to play when the time was right: a count returned from the dead.
Asked what would become of Kreide, she said only that she would take care of it. Ebenholz asked for time to think.
The next day Czerny called the two back, saying the original performers had been hurt in a tavern brawl, and gave them a single day to practice and his own cello.

With nowhere suitable to practice, Ebenholz began staying that day at Kreide's home, which had only one bed. He kept stumbling over a single ornament, and when Kreide told him to just pass over it while he slowed the tempo, the two instruments came together for the first time.

blocks.cap: Flute and cello, together for the first time in a cramped room.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, Gertrude was refining a prophecy that borrowed the name of 'His Majesty.' She meant to stir up a small disturbance and drive Rhodes Island out of the Afterglow.

O'er lofty Hills, the Fiend steps into Twilight's Midst agaze. The Blood hides Plague within, slow beckons Death to creep all Ways. Pestilence from Shadow wanton spouts, spews Ruin in Prelude. Fades Finale's Ensemble; Woe deprives of Sun's last Rays.
3. The Devil
Hibiscus, meanwhile, went from house to house, examining the Infected and collecting blood samples. Cases of improvement were far more widespread than she had expected.

Toward dusk, a drunk man called her a 'devil,' saying she had drawn his father's blood. A suspicious Infected beside him fanned the flames with talk of casters who use Infected blood for their Arts, and the crowd surged in, invoking 'His Majesty's prophecy.'
Hibiscus neither fought nor fled. She said they could think her a devil if they wished; she only wanted to save more lives. But the people closed in around her.
Then Kreide pushed through the crowd and stepped in front of her.

blocks.cap: Kreide, standing in front of Hibiscus to shield her.

blocks.x: A man's Arts tore a hole in Kreide's cello. It was the cello Czerny had given him.

The next moment, the sound of a flute rang out from somewhere. The crowd understood what it meant, begged forgiveness, and scattered in an instant. It was Ebenholz. He said only that he was neither Infected nor from Vyseheim.

When the two brought the broken cello to Czerny, he apologized on behalf of the Afterglow and gave them a mass-produced cello. In the test that followed, he noticed that Kreide was adjusting himself to Ebenholz's habits, and passed them, saying they had barely reached his minimum standard.
4. A Cloak, a Coin

The next day, saying he would buy Kreide a new cello, Ebenholz took him into the Cliffy Patio, the noble quarter, though Kreide had no permit to enter. When a clerk at the instrument shop found fault with his clothes, Ebenholz said this was his cousin and put his own cloak around Kreide's shoulders.

blocks.cap: The streets of the Cliffy Patio, where the nobles live.

blocks.x: On the way back, Kreide hummed a song that Ebenholz felt he had heard somewhere before. Kreide said the face of the teacher who had taught him the cello was fading, and that he wanted to keep one keepsake from each person he did not want to forget. As the thing to remember Ebenholz by, he chose a coin with a hole punched through it.

At the house they went to straight after, Czerny pressed Ebenholz for skimming over the easy passages. When Ebenholz, angered, played again, Czerny said that was the best playing of the day. He had written the piece, he explained, with someone who defied him in mind.
Meanwhile, Hibiscus was confronted again by a hostile Infected and got away with the help of the café manager **Biegler**.
That evening the group gathered at the office and ate a meal prepared by Hibiscus and Czerny's distant relative **Ursula**. At the table, Czerny said this to Ebenholz:
Barbed words are one thing. But even hatred that cuts to the bone, if it can be expressed with the proper technique, has meaning in that alone.
Kreide said that eating together like this made them feel like a family.
5. It Was Not Recovery
At dawn the next morning, Hibiscus, her eyes red, knocked on the door of Kreide's home. The Infected of the Afterglow were not getting better, she said. They were in a state of **False Recovery**.
Their bodies were wringing out what function remained to patch the damage, so they looked healthy on the surface. Inside, Oripathy was spreading faster, and some had already entered acute attacks.

And at the center of it were the two of them. The phenomenon had begun right after Kreide came to Vyseheim, and since he met Ebenholz, what should have taken half a year had happened in a matter of days.
Hibiscus asked Ebenholz to leave Vyseheim at once. Ebenholz asked for time and said he would certainly come back.

blocks.cap: The Afterglow alley where Hibiscus called Ebenholz aside alone.

blocks.x: He went straight to Gertrude, and she already knew. Kreide's Voice of Mundane was damaged and constantly leaking, burning the Originium inside nearby Infected to force them into 'recovery,' and the Resonanz between the two had amplified that leak.
Ebenholz declared that he was withdrawing from the plan, and even thought of throwing himself from the nomadic city. Gertrude stood in his way and revealed the rest of the plan.

When the duet ended, chaos would be stirred up in the concert hall, and in the confusion Kreide would be killed and his body disguised as Ebenholz's. Kreide's False Recovery would end within two weeks anyway, she said.
Then she called him by another name. The rightful heir of Leithanien, **the last of the Witch King's bloodline**.
6. Fifteen of the Blood
Ebenholz collapsed where he stood, and old memories flooded into his mind.

His memory begins at the age of five or six, before the hem of a pure white skirt. That person gave him, the last of the Witch King's bloodline, the fief of Urtica, and told him to walk a different path from his kin.

But the people around him demanded nothing of him but loyalty to the Empresses. One day, through a crack in the door, he overheard a drinking party held by the count's proxy. The talk was of steeping him in drink until he ruined himself, making sure he left no heirs, and then quietly sending him off.

blocks.cap: Beyond the crack in the door, the drinking party of the count's proxy.

blocks.x: When he came to, he returned to Kreide's home and lay down as if collapsing. As his consciousness faded, the song Kreide used to hum reached him as the sound of a distant cello.

blocks.cap: Ebenholz, waking to the sound of a cello.

blocks.x: Sealed memories came back. At two or three, after his parents were executed, he was locked in a ruined building as one of fifteen who carried the Witch King's blood. The Witch King's remnants experimented on them, implanting in their bodies the melody the Witch King had left behind: the Voice of Mundane.

One by one, people left the room and did not return. The older girl who looked after the children and sang them the Lied des klaren Himmels vanished one day too, and one child memorized the song and hummed it all day long.
In the end, only he and that child were left. When asked who would go next, the child, trembling, smiled at him and said, 'I'll do it.'

Two months later the child came back alive, only to be carried out again a few days later, never to return. A few days after that, his own turn came. He survived, and was revered as the last one who could 'play' the Voice of Mundane.

Then the Empresses' Voice burst in. Amid the screams of the remnants, what he felt was relief. As he raised his Arts unit, an Empresses' Voice in flamboyant dress struck him on the head with a brass instrument. That one blow broke his short life in two.
When his memory had come back that far, Ebenholz looked at Kreide, who was holding his cello.
7. What the Afterglow Means

Meanwhile, Hibiscus went to Czerny and asked him at least to cancel the two's duet. Czerny refused, saying he could not throw away the hope of the whole Afterglow over a worry no one could prove, and Ursula led Hibiscus out then and there.
Because the sky grows dark, the afterglow shines all the more precious. If the night were never to end, could there be anything more dazzling, more moving, than the warm light of dusk?

The old story that Ursula and the stall owner told, sitting in front of the stall, went like this. This place had once been an industrial district. The former Graf Strollo walled it off, together with the Witch King's concert hall, as an Infected settlement, and even tore down the factories. The nobles called it the Afterglow, meaning that the time left to the Infected was as short as the evening glow.

At twenty, Czerny lost a friend who had been both his teacher's daughter and his rival, and for the first time he wrote a piece under his own name: 'Morgen und Abend.' It was the lord, Gertrude, who brought the piece into the world under his name, but the two soon parted ways.

Around then, Ebenholz was tailing **Lachmann**, the Infected who had stirred up the crowd on the day they cornered Hibiscus. The moment he caught him, Biegler appeared behind him, and in that opening Lachmann fled into the sewers.
Biegler produced a commission from the Empresses and revealed himself as a spy. Ebenholz went down into the sewers with him, on condition that he remain under Biegler's watch.

blocks.cap: The sewers beneath the Afterglow.

blocks.x: 8. A Performance for Originium Slugs

In the sewers, Originium slugs provoked by Lachmann were swarming and crawling toward the surface, and their poison gas was far deadlier to the Infected. It was the third line of the prophecy: 'Pestilence from Shadow wanton spouts.'
Ebenholz knocked Lachmann unconscious, and when Biegler opened a lock hidden in the wall, a laboratory appeared, piled with research notes and plans on the Voice of Mundane.
Meanwhile, the surface had descended into chaos. Those who had 'recovered' most recently suffered the worst poisoning, and Czerny went out himself to persuade the hospitals that were holding back.
Then the sound of a cello spread through the alleys. Kreide was drawing the Originium slugs toward himself.

blocks.cap: Ebenholz and Biegler cutting a path through the swarm of Originium slugs.

blocks.x: Ebenholz split from Biegler, who took the notes, and ran to him. Kreide told him calmly that he had meant to burn himself up along with the slugs. Since childhood he had made the Infected around him sick; if his merely being alive brought disaster, he said, it was better that he die.
But when Ebenholz spoke the words 'Voice of Mundane,' Kreide remembered everything. The experiments, the people who died, the Witch King's remnants, and Ebenholz.

To try to move the Voice of Mundane, the two played the melodies in their heads together, with the Originium slugs as their audience. The piercing flute and the hollow cello never blended, but when the final forte rang out like a siren, the slugs scattered.
Kreide's Voice of Mundane only grew clearer. When Ebenholz apologized, Kreide answered:
I only wanted to protect you, as my own beliefs told me to... just as you are trying to protect me now, as yours tell you to.

Then Kreide collapsed. At the office, as Hibiscus said she needed evidence, the grandfather who had disappeared appeared before her. He said the Voice of Mundane certainly existed, told them only to go and look in the concert hall's lounge, and left again.
9. The Concert Hall as a Weapon

When Ebenholz and Hibiscus went to him, Czerny, back from barely securing contracts with two hospitals, said he had signed over all his copyrights, even the recording rights to the concert, as the price. Before he could finish, he broke into a violent cough and collapsed.

When Ebenholz confessed that he had taken part in Gertrude's plan, Czerny was furious. Ebenholz returned his own words to him, that even hatred that cuts to the bone has meaning if it can be expressed, and answered that all he had wanted was freedom.

In the concert hall's lounge, where they went next, the speakers and record players had all been torn out and turned into loudspeakers, and the weakest Arts Ebenholz could cast came echoing back from outside the hall. The whole of Afterglow Hall was a giant Arts amplifier.
If the Voice of Mundane sounded on that stage, its power would spread across all of Vyseheim and infect every resident. When Czerny realized it, what showed on his face was not anger but pure terror.
Gertrude appeared then and offered Ebenholz a compromise: let it end with Kreide's life alone. When he refused, she proposed they settle it outside.

blocks.cap: Ebenholz and Gertrude, face to face.

blocks.x: Ebenholz won, but Gertrude stayed composed, saying it was they who had wrecked the lord's concert hall. Yet at Ebenholz's call, Biegler appeared, and on the strength of the research notes from the sewers, he took her away on charges of forbidden research into the Voice of Mundane.
As she was led away, Gertrude said he would regret betraying her. Ebenholz answered that he had regretted many things, but not this.
10. A Composition in One Night

Back at the office, Hibiscus proposed taking Kreide to the landship, but Ebenholz knew he would not last that long. He meant to move the Voice of Mundane through a duet, even if it cost him his own life.

Then the grandfather produced the Voice of Mundane plans he had stolen from Biegler. He too was a spy for the Empresses. Knowing that Kreide was a survivor of the experiments, he had watched over him for more than ten years.

Outside, the grandfather told Hibiscus about the past. In the Witch King's era, the Kurfürsten had to offer up Infected for Arts research, and some even drew lines of Originium across the arms of healthy people to make them Infected. That was how he had become Infected too.

As far as the Empresses were concerned, the Voice of Mundane was worth nothing. Kreide, his constitution ruined, had never been someone they meant to save. The grandfather asked in return whether the days of a boy who had drifted from place to place without making a single friend could truly be called a life.

Meanwhile, Czerny read the plans and found a way. While the two played 'Morgen und Abend,' he would draw out the Voice of Mundane within it and weave it all into a single new piece. If that failed, he would become the vessel himself.
Czerny said he had written 'Morgen und Abend' not in grief but in indignation. To resist a fate already decided: that, to him, was music.

When the playing began, a melody of ruin that would shatter everything poured out of Ebenholz, and out of Kreide, a void that would swallow everything. As the two forces tangled, Czerny stood before an endless wall called the Witch King, and coughed up blood.
Still, he sat down at the piano again. To Kreide, who only ever made himself smaller, he said self-sacrifice was not always a virtue, and pressed him to claim the dignity he deserved.
Right now, my opponent is myself.

blocks.cap: Czerny writing out the score through the night, with Hibiscus at his side.

blocks.x: Coughing up blood again and again, he filled the score. As dawn broke, Czerny murmured, 'It's finished,' and collapsed over the piano.
11. Licht und Schatten
On the day of the concert, Hibiscus said that as a doctor she ought to stop him, but she could not let a piece made by burning his life go unheard, and she helped Czerny to the concert hall.

blocks.cap: Czerny, supported by Hibiscus, on his way to the concert hall.

blocks.x: At the same hour, under Biegler's interrogation, Gertrude confessed that she was the one who had killed her brother, their father's successor.

In the lounge, meanwhile, Kreide was unusually talkative. He brought up their promise to exchange keepsakes and said he was still deciding what to give. When he said this might be their last performance, Ebenholz told him it would not be.
Just before they went on stage, Czerny told them the title of the piece: Trio for Flute, Cello, and Piano in B-flat minor, 'Licht und Schatten.'

blocks.cap: The premiere of 'Licht und Schatten.'

blocks.x: Past an opening like storm clouds, the flute and piano broke through into sunlight, and no one in the audience so much as breathed. But soon the faces of all three performers twisted in pain.

By then Gertrude, in a room where the performance could be heard, had begun to play the harp. It was she who had revived the Voice of Mundane project, and she who had left the laboratory for the spies to find. The amplifier was only a decoy. The real trap was the Resonanz she had tampered with.
Those who had been manipulating her for fifteen years were sitting in the audience. To inflict the same pain on them, and to die here along with Biegler, was her final gamble.
The Witch King, the Twin Empresses, I don't care about any of them. All I want is to live!

On stage, the entire concert hall was drinking in the performance. If they stopped, everyone in the hall would be swept away by the runaway Voice of Mundane. If they played to the end, Kreide's Voice of Mundane would be torn out of him whole.
When Ebenholz tried to become the vessel, Kreide's cello seized the current from him. Kreide said that he was this piece's ending, so it had to be him.
The piece ended as a duet for cello and piano. What the audience heard was a long sigh leaking out of the void. The applause, when it finally came, was soon buried under screams.
12. The Final Piece

As Originium crystals began to break out all over his body, Kreide asked to be taken outside while he could still hold it back. Ebenholz left the evacuation of the audience to Hibiscus and Czerny and lifted him into his arms.

blocks.cap: Ebenholz ran to the plaza with Kreide in his arms.

blocks.x: Asked whether he had meant for this to happen from the start, Kreide said he had only had a feeling. When he said that playing together had been the happiest he had ever been, Ebenholz sobbed and called him a liar.
In the plaza, as rain began to fall, Kreide said they had survived those experiments, met again, become friends, and even given a wonderful performance on stage. They could not possibly be unhappy.
We both wanted, gladly, to do that for each other. It just happened that, in the end, I was the one who did. That's all.
Then he left his 'dearest brother' one last request: to stop him from destroying this city.
Kreide walked to the middle of the plaza, and Originium crystals covered his body, becoming armor and an instrument. Everyone who saw it thought of the same name. The Witch King.

blocks.cap: Ebenholz, facing what had once been Kreide.

blocks.x: Because today, I shall die, and you... will be reborn!

Then the grandfather stepped in front of the monster and cried out for it to turn its hatred on him. Hibiscus stepped in and took the deadly melody it spewed at him. In that opening, Ebenholz struck the final blow.

At the same moment, Biegler drove a dagger into the back of Gertrude as she played the harp. Her lips shaped curses on the Afterglow and Leithanien, on Ebenholz, even on the Witch King, and Biegler left her with a parting word: 'Good night.'
When the Originium shell crumbled, only Kreide was left, on the edge of death. He told Ebenholz to live, and to make it through the long night.
Remember this, Ebenholz. Together we stood against an unfair fate. And we won! So whenever you think of me, don't cry. Smile for me.
He said he was sorry that he still had not decided what to give him as a keepsake. After that, Kreide answered no more.

Ebenholz carried his cooling friend to the concert hall's lounge. The voice in his head, which had been imitating Kreide's voice, fell silent at his warning, leaving only the words 'My foolish bloodline.'

Murmuring that he seemed to have been infected too, he laid Kreide on the sofa and took up the cello. And in place of the coin with a hole punched through it, he set the flute he had always played beside his friend.
Epilogue — A Song with Only Its Opening Verses

After the incident, the condition of most people in the Afterglow stabilized. Andante's investigation found that nearly all the Originium activated that day had shifted into a low-activity state, and after the Doctor's negotiations, the Empresses' Voice sent word that the Afterglow was not to be touched.

Meanwhile, Biegler, who found the grandfather in the sewers, admitted that it was they who had drawn Kreide to Vyseheim. The judgment had been to make the plan go off now, while the technique was still immature, before Gertrude, who had been chasing Kreide, could do something worse.
He did not kill the grandfather. Instead he took him along, saying they should talk about the two young men over coffee at the café.

On the Rhodes Island landship, Hibiscus was scolded by her tearful younger sister **Lava**. Her infection had worsened because of the Voice of Mundane but was already under control, she said, and she promised to take good care of herself.

Czerny, who had come to Rhodes Island with Ebenholz, applied for a transfer to the front lines. He had gone on stage prepared to die and had survived, he told the Doctor; now he wanted to fight for the Infected in a different way.

And on the deck of Rhodes Island, Ebenholz opened an envelope from Leithanien that the Doctor had handed him. Inside were a passport for Ebenholz the commoner, death certificates for Kreide and for Graf Urtica, and an unsigned letter asking him to make sure those deaths stayed certain.
Ebenholz set the letter alight with the tip of his cane, and the flames consumed the passport and the papers one after another.

Holding the cello close, he thought of his friend and played a short, light melody. It was a song from the early years of the Twin Empresses' reign, whose latter half had been forgotten, leaving only the opening verses.

blocks.cap: In the glow of sunset, Ebenholz plays his friend's cello.

blocks.x: No one sings the latter verses of that song anymore. The Mist parts overnight, the Earth welcomes Dawn's Light; Praise be Leithanien, where free Men find their Home.

act17side.tagline: Setting out from a town named for a lighthouse, Iberia and Ægir join hands and go to sea in search of a flagship lost sixty years ago. Most of those who kept the lantern burning did not come back.

chars.name: Jordi
chars.desc: An Ægir youth born and raised in Gran Faro. He works as a caregiver at the chapel. · Operator Lumen

chars.name: Thiago
chars.desc: Mayor of Gran Faro and the man who raised Jordi. Since losing his lover to the Inquisition, he has not gone near the sea.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: A doctor of Rhodes Island. Under the Inquisition's watch, she brokers cooperation between Iberia and Ægir.

chars.name: Carmen
chars.desc: A High Inquisitor of the Iberian Inquisition. At 123, he is the oldest of the Inquisitors, and is called 'the Saint.'

chars.name: Dario
chars.desc: A High Inquisitor of the Iberian Inquisition, and Irene's mentor.

chars.name: Irene
chars.desc: The young disciple of High Inquisitor Dario. She is firm in her conviction to protect Iberia with sword and lantern.

chars.name: Elysium
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island Operator. An Iberian-born Liberi, he waits for someone at the Gran Faro chapel.

chars.name: Amaia
chars.desc: A translator who lives in Gran Faro. She renders books from many countries into Iberian.

chars.name: Gladiia
chars.desc: Ægir's Technology Consul and the Abyssal Hunters' Chief Designer of Warfare. She pursues a way back to Ægir.

chars.name: Skadi
chars.desc: A Hunter of the Abyssal Hunters. She speaks little, but never hesitates to protect her comrades.

chars.name: Specter
chars.desc: A Hunter of the Abyssal Hunters. Her lost memories return little by little each time she meets the sea breeze. · Operator Specter the Unchained

chars.name: Ulpianus
chars.desc: A consul of the Abyssal Hunters, and the Hunter Skadi once called 'Captain.' Nothing had been heard of him for a long time.

chars.name: Breogan
chars.desc: Chief shipwright of Iberia's Golden Age. An Ægir who came from the sea.

chars.name: Alfonso
chars.desc: Captain of the Stultifera Navis. He was a duke of Iberia and Admiral of the Armada.

chars.name: Garcia
chars.desc: Chief mate of the Stultifera Navis. He stays at Alfonso's side.

chars.name: The Last Knight
chars.desc: A mysterious knight who appears before the Eye of Iberia. Lance in hand, he pursues the sea, vowing to break the waves.

terms.name: Gran Faro
terms.desc: A remote town on the Iberian coast, home to the families of laborers who came to repair the lighthouse and stayed.

terms.name: Eye of Iberia
terms.desc: The name of the great lighthouses that once guarded the Iberian coast. After the Profound Silence, only the one out at sea remained.

terms.name: Stultifera Navis
terms.desc: Flagship of the Iberian Armada, lost in the Profound Silence. It set sail laden with scholars and soldiers.

terms.name: Profound Silence
terms.desc: The catastrophe that engulfed Iberia in 1038. Ever since, the Ægir have been called 'Islanders' and regarded with suspicion.

terms.name: Sea Terror
terms.desc: Sea monsters that appear along the Iberian coast.

terms.name: Seaborn
terms.desc: Sea creatures ranked above the Sea Terrors. They learn to speak and come to resemble humans.

terms.name: Nethersea Brand
terms.desc: A fluorescent mark the sea leaves on land. Wherever it spreads becomes a home for Sea Terrors.

terms.name: Abyssal Hunters
terms.desc: Ægir's elite fighting force. Left stranded on land after their war with the Seaborn, the surviving Hunters search for a way back to the sea.

terms.name: Ishar-mla
terms.desc: A name the Seaborn call out in unison. What it refers to is not easily revealed.

terms.name: Alive Until Sunset
terms.desc: A rock band made up of Alty, Aya, Dan, and Frost. Longtime acquaintances of Kal'tsit.

blocks.x: Some sixty years ago, a catastrophe known as the Profound Silence fell upon Iberia's seas. The Armada and the coastal cities vanished, and Iberia forbade the sea. The Ægir who had come from the sea were called 'Islanders' and fell under the suspicion of the Inquisition.

blocks.cap: A deep well by the sea. An Inquisitor who has lived a hundred and twenty-three years, and Kal'tsit.

blocks.x: Left alone in Iberia under the Inquisition's watch, **Kal'tsit** of Rhodes Island was trying to persuade **Carmen**, an Inquisitor who had lived for 123 years. Carmen dropped a pebble into an old well, and for the few seconds before the splash, perfect silence passed between them.
"Before I die... you must prove it to Iberia." Prove that there truly was a way to defeat the Seaborn and their source. The stage for it was a remote town on the coast.
Gran Faro. In the old tongue of Iberia, it means 'the great lighthouse.'
1. A Town Named for a Lighthouse

Gran Faro is home to the families of laborers who came long ago to repair the lighthouse and never left. **Jordi**, a young Ægir, works at a chapel no one visits, tending to children and the injured. His parents left when he was small and never returned, and the mayor, **Thiago**, raised him.

In the chapel sat **Elysium** of Rhodes Island, who had been waiting a month for someone. To Jordi, who always shrank into himself for being Ægir, he said that some people would show him kindness, and that he should not lose heart.

Rumors ran through the town of a ghost ship, of cultists, of monsters on the coast. Thiago, who had lost his lover Marin to the Inquisition, feared that Jordi too would be taken, and the one who listened to that fear was the town's translator, **Amaia**.

blocks.cap: At the center of the plaza stands a statue modeled on a lighthouse.

blocks.x: Then, that day, the four members of the rock band **Alive Until Sunset** appeared in the plaza. They were the guests Elysium had been waiting for, and they had brought something Kal'tsit had entrusted to them. Thiago told Jordi not to get involved with these outsiders, who might be Ægir.
Around then, three of the **Abyssal Hunters**, **Gladiia**, **Skadi**, and **Specter**, were also heading for Gran Faro in search of a way back to Ægir. Specter was unusually quiet.
2. Death in the Statue's Shadow

Not long after, a dying **Sea Terror** was found in the shadow of the statue in the plaza. Its body bore not a single bullet wound. It looked less as though death had chosen it than as though it had chosen death.

When the townspeople said the Inquisition had to be told, Thiago shouted them down. The moment the Inquisition saw this, he said, Gran Faro would never know another peaceful day. Amaia took charge of the body.

At that same hour, Jordi was bandaging the wounds of his injured neighbor Juan in an alley. In broken Ægirian, Juan told him that he too might one day leave in search of that lighthouse, as his parents had, and then disappeared.

Meanwhile, a strange Ægir hunter appeared before Amaia and told her that the Bishop of Sal Viento was dead, and Amaia answered in Ægirian that she had never expected to meet one of the Abyssal Hunters alive.

At the chapel, meanwhile, Kal'tsit received from Alty the thing she had left in her keeping. Just then Juan came in carrying the Sea Terror's corpse, knelt and called it 'brother,' and forced its flesh into his own body. Kal'tsit called it 'assimilation.'
"...Repulsive." It was Carmen who appeared then. Declaring that they had defiled a sacred place of the Inquisition, the High Inquisitor raised his lantern before the cultists.

blocks.cap: The Gran Faro chapel. Thiago said it was an outpost the Inquisition had built to keep watch on the laborers.

blocks.x: 3. A Cradle of Failures

Around then, Thiago pressed Jordi to leave town at once. Of the Ægir taken by the Inquisition, not one had come back whole. When Jordi refused to go, the old man kept repeating it: Marin, the others, none of them had come back.
Jordi said he wanted to see the sea.

blocks.cap: An Ægir who could not remember the last time he had seen the sea.

blocks.x: Then, on the beach, Thiago told an old story. Decades ago, the people of Gran Faro had tried to make this place a fortress on the coastal defense line, and the final stage of that half-century plan was to relight the last lighthouse that had survived even the Profound Silence: the **Eye of Iberia**.

Jordi's grandparents and parents were Ægir who had given two generations to that plan. On the final attempt his parents volunteered to sail with the fleet and never returned, and the plan ended when the Inquisition began hauling the Ægir away in its hunt for spies.
They were heroes, Jordi. Marin said we should all become heroes. But none of us are heroes now. Only the dead are.

Like a pebble dropped into a deep well, their efforts had left no mark on fate. Gran Faro, Thiago said, was a cradle of failures. In the harbor there remained only a single boat, one the Penal Battalion had forgotten even to take.

Meanwhile, Gladiia ran into Aya and Dan on the beach and recognized at once that they, too, had come from the sea. Then Specter looked up at the sky and said that the children of the sea were crying. The town was under attack.
4. Don't Look Back

Then a swarm of Sea Terrors poured into the streets. While the Hunters cut them down, Carmen interrogated a captured believer, who pointed to the statue in the plaza. What the cultists were after was the Eye of Iberia.

At that moment glowing spots bloomed from the Sea Terror corpses, and Kal'tsit's black creature, Mon3tr, melted them away. It was what the Iberians call the **Nethersea Brand**, a trace born where sea and land meet.

Meanwhile, Amaia called the strange hunter **Ulpianus**. He said he had to find that ship before Gladiia did, and that she and the others must not return to Ægir knowing nothing. And when Elysium recovered documents bearing the name of the royal shipwright **Breogan** from the cultists' hideout, Ulpianus swung his blade at him, saying they had to be burned.

Meanwhile, frightened by word that an Inquisitor had appeared, the townspeople whispered that to clear themselves of suspicion, they would have to hand Jordi, the Ægir, over to the Inquisition. When the neighbors blocked the door of the house, Thiago and Jordi fled across the rooftops.

Thiago shouted that he had put money in Jordi's pocket and that he should go to another country. Falling behind, the old man watched the young man's back recede and told him not to look back, and at the last he cried out a farewell in Ægirian. "Farewell, Jordi!"

blocks.cap: A street in Gran Faro. Here Thiago pushed Jordi on his way.

blocks.x: Thiago called the neighbors who had chased them murderers. When Marin and his Ægir comrades were taken, he said, you stood beneath the banner of the Penal Battalion, and heedless even of the Sea Terrors passing by, he swung his fists until he was covered in blood.
5. A Town Already Fallen

Around then, as Jordi caught his breath in the wilderness, Ulpianus appeared before him, called him 'Breogan's descendant,' and told him to follow. Elysium set off a smoke screen and got Jordi away, and High Inquisitor **Dario** and his disciple **Irene** stood in Ulpianus's path.
Ulpianus vanished, leaving behind the words that Iberia was not yet worthy. Looking at the ash-stained ground, Dario made a brief judgment. Gran Faro had not been infiltrated. It had already fallen.

Meanwhile, hidden in a storehouse, Elysium told Jordi to take the townspeople and leave, but Jordi shook his head. This was the place where he had grown up reading the notes his parents left behind, and to him it was simply home.

Then, before the statue in the plaza, Iberia and Ægir faced each other across the negotiating table. Gladiia was searching for the **Stultifera Navis**, the flagship lost more than sixty years ago, and Carmen said the ship had very likely not sunk, but that the only way to find it on the wide sea was the Eye of Iberia.

blocks.cap: The central plaza of Gran Faro. The negotiations took place before the lighthouse statue.

blocks.x: The negotiations soon caught on an old grievance. To Gladiia, who said she could not trust an Iberia that had let its rage fall upon the Ægir after the Profound Silence, Carmen asked in return whether Ægir truly had nothing to do with the Silence. When the two fell quiet, Kal'tsit spoke.
Civilizations do not die. They are merely replaced, endlessly. And the next one will have nothing to do with humanity.
Saying there was no greater glory than survival, Carmen accepted the cooperation and had Dario and Irene open a sea route to the Eye of Iberia together with the Hunters.

Then Jordi, who had overheard the talk of the lighthouse, stepped forward. He said his parents had been lighthouse engineers and that he wanted to go and see the meaning of his home, and Carmen, hearing from him the name 'Jordi Fontanarossa,' ordered Irene to arrest him, and to take him along.
6. A Pair of Eyes Shut Tight

Around then, Amaia came to bid Thiago farewell. She told him to compare now with the rainy night when the Penal Battalion broke down the doors. In Gran Faro now, with no screams and no slaughter, only silence remained.

Meanwhile, aboard the boat, Jordi learned for the first time how vast the sea was. Irene told him that the Penal Battalion had tried seventeen times to land on the reef where the lighthouse stood, and that of the hundreds of warriors and three Inquisitors who went, none had returned alive.

blocks.cap: The Eye of Iberia. Only by lifting one's head could one make it out against the dark sky.

blocks.x: It was the first time Dario, too, had seen it with his own eyes. He told Irene to engrave upon her heart this building, the broken sword and lantern, this reef, and this sea.
If we do not revere sacrifice, the scales are meaningless.

Seeing that the tower looked exactly like the statue in the plaza, Jordi realized that the blueprints piled up at home had been plans of this lighthouse. Uncle Thiago had been right, he thought. They had all been heroes.

Then, wrapped in the Nethersea Brand, **The Last Knight** appeared before the lighthouse. Instead of attacking the Hunters, the knight charged the lighthouse with a roar, and Gladiia judged him to be a Seaborn.

Meanwhile, Irene and Jordi climbed the tower. As Jordi combed through his parents' notes and brought the control panels back to life one by one, power surged into the lighthouse, and the knight, as if he had lost interest, muttered "Ishar... mla..." and vanished along with the beast he called Rocinante.
It was Irene who pulled the last lever. A blinding light pierced the sea.
7. Sword, Lantern, and I
The lighthouse's recording device held a signal that a single ship had been sending without pause for decades. That ship was very close.

As the Nethersea Brand crept up from the base of the tower, Dario ordered Irene to go to that ship with the Hunters. When she said she would stay with him, he told her to burn the sea into her eyes. What had saved her in the ruins, he said, was the scripture in her hands, not him.
Dario told Jordi to leave as well, but Jordi stayed. Being Ægir, he had lived his life obeying others, he said, but exploring the lighthouse he had learned his own worth for the first time.
Before leaving, Gladiia began to say that they had endured the long wait on land, that they were going back to Ægir now, and then trailed off.

blocks.cap: The nape of Gladiia's neck. The skin, carefully hidden, was rough to the touch.

blocks.x: After the Hunters left, Dario told Jordi the truth: with the Nethersea Brand surrounding the coast, the two who remained had all but been sentenced to death. Then he told him to bring the lighthouse's defenses back to life and went out of the tower alone.
Between the ocean and Iberia, there is no such thing as justice, or evil. There is only sword and lantern... and me.
8. King of the Golden Ship
As the ship drew near, Specter's hand trembled. Gladiia took it without a word, and Skadi took it too. "Welcome home, Hunters."

blocks.cap: A silent ship lies deep in sleep upon the sea.

blocks.x: The Stultifera Navis they boarded was spotless, without a speck of dust, though sixty years had passed. The Hunters scattered to chase a **Seaborn** that appeared on deck and fled, and before a broken mirror in the golden hall, Specter came face to face with another Seaborn that had been waiting for her.

The Seaborn called her 'Laurentina.' In that instant, Specter's manner of speech changed. Her memories returned, down to her own name and the place she was born, and she said it had been a vivid dream.
Then a bell rang through the hall. A crowned Seaborn knelt beside the throne, and from behind it a man stepped forward.

blocks.cap: This Iberian ship had a throne.

blocks.x: He named himself **Alfonso**: Duke of Iberia, Admiral of the Armada, Captain of the Stultifera Navis. A hero whose hair had already been graying sixty years ago now stood there looking younger than he had then. The crowned Seaborn was his chief mate, **Garcia**.

Alfonso said this hall was his Iberia. He had survived by eating the flesh and blood of sea monsters, and he had executed with his own hands the sailors whose bodies were changing. He had thrown the last of them into the sea seven or eight years ago.
Alfonso told Skadi that the creatures had called her **Ishar-mla**. Skadi knew what the name meant, yet could not answer.

Garcia, at Alfonso's side, had all but lost the power of speech, but he was still human. When Alfonso spoke of giving up, Garcia wrote in Sea Terror blood: "I am your chief mate." Yet he hid the fact that a human heart remained in him, afraid that Alfonso, who could not tolerate the monster within himself, would be unable to accept him.
Around then, Irene heard Garcia playing an Iberian military song on a broken piano. Caught, Garcia gently laid a hand on her head. His clouded eyes were full of tenderness and longing.
9. Ishar-mla

Around then, in Gran Faro, Thiago appeared with the cultists before the captured Elysium. The cultists called Amaia their 'prophet.' Pretending not to know Elysium, Thiago said he would repay twice over what the Inquisition had destroyed.

Meanwhile, deep in the ship, Gladiia came upon Amaia and called her 'Bishop of the Deep.' The Seaborn left behind when Amaia departed tore off a piece of its own flesh and held it out, asking whether, if she ate it, the scales on her neck might grow and let her return to her true form.
Gladiia wavered for a moment. Then she opened the treasury deep in the ship with a key and saw Breogan's legacy, which joined Originium with Ægir technology.

blocks.cap: "However, it's still not enough." An old comrade revealed himself.

blocks.x: It was Ulpianus. The consul of the Abyssal Hunters, whom even Skadi had believed dead, said that in the deepest part of the Seaborn nest he had seen a 'construct' no one in Ægir could interpret, and countless 'things' filling it.
Seaborn not yet born, he said, had been murmuring the same name from within their embryos. Ishar-mla. **Or, Skadi.**

When the Hunters brought down the sea god, Ulpianus had survived by hiding inside its corpse, but Skadi had fought to the very end. That had not been a killing, he said. It was the entire species 'feeding' her.
If anything goes wrong, we must kill Skadi.

Gladiia said he was making the cruelest of accusations against his own Hunter. Ulpianus told her it was still too early to return to Ægir and that she should stay on land, and said that Skadi was his Hunter, and that he would take responsibility.
10. An Unanswered Question

Then, on the road where the cultists were dragging Elysium off to feed him to the Nethersea Brand, Mon3tr appeared. It was Thiago who had led the way, and the Inquisition spy hidden among the cultists revealed that she had been the daughter of a Gran Faro laborer.

"The Inquisition or you lot, you're all nothing but enemies who trampled our home." But one believer who survived Mon3tr's flames fell upon Thiago while turning into a monster, and Carmen, arriving too late, cut the believer down.
In Elysium's arms, Thiago asked Carmen whether there had truly been heretics among the Ægir taken from Gran Faro. At least tell me about Marin, he said. Carmen said he could not answer a civilian.
Thiago, who had been cursing the Inquisition, never finished his last words to Iberia. A single drop of water ran down a pillar and fell.

blocks.cap: A tavern no one visited. Thiago breathed his last here.

blocks.x: When Elysium, declaring himself an Iberian, asked for the truth, Carmen was silent for a moment before answering. Of the more than 130 Ægir taken, about half had been involved with the Church of the Deep, and their leader had been a female Ægir bishop. **People called that woman 'Marin.'**

At the same hour, aboard the ship, a wounded Seaborn fell upon Irene. Garcia saved her and asked her in halting Iberian not to let Alfonso know that he was still human, and moments later he was pierced by the Seaborn's teeth.
Irene remembered Dario's words. Even if the enemy trampled both faith and morality, the belief rebuilt afterward would hold her up. She had to become Iberia's last line of defense.

blocks.cap: "Now, as nothing more than an Iberian, I pass judgment on you."

blocks.x: Irene's handcannon spat fire, and a second hole opened in the Seaborn's hard body. Before an enemy not written of even in scripture, she passed judgment in the name of Iberia.
11. Consume Me

Meanwhile, in the golden hall now submerged in the Nethersea Brand, Amaia received Irene. She said the sea breeze had brought her word of Dario's death, and that his sacrifice meant nothing. Irene leveled her handcannon, saying there was no such thing as a meaningless sacrifice in the Inquisition.

Specter, who appeared next, sent Skadi and Irene on ahead and took Amaia's hand. It was Amaia who had first found her collapsed on the white sand and put her on the experiment table. Amaia told her that what held her Oripathy in check was the Seaborn blood flowing within her.

blocks.cap: "Are you, as you are now, Seaborn? Or one of the Abyssal Hunters?"

blocks.x: Specter did not waver. She, who had dreamed of becoming a sculptor as a child, let go of Amaia's hand and swung her weapon as she spoke. To make meaning within the form of a dead thing, to free it from meaningless emptiness, "just like my lovely destiny."

Meanwhile, on deck, Ulpianus struck down the Seaborn as it tried to flee into the sea. He told Skadi she had regressed, and saying he would teach her just once, as in the old days, he blew away a large part of the Seaborn's body with a single blow.
Then the Seaborn broke through the deck and went to Amaia. It knelt before the wounded Amaia and told her to eat it and survive.

blocks.cap: "There is nothing noble about sacrifice. Devotion is no virtue."

blocks.x: Amaia said that praising sacrifice and devotion was nothing but humanity's self-justification. The final answer she had sought in the sea was this: "Life has never been without order." Then she laid her hand on the Seaborn's body.
Do not forget me. Free me. Consume me.
12. The Silence Returns

Around then, Carmen and Kal'tsit reached the Eye of Iberia aboard the boat left on the beach at Gran Faro. Before the door, the charred corpses of Sea Terrors were heaped like a mountain, and in the midst of the flames stood Dario.

blocks.cap: The lantern had not gone out. Even in death, the High Inquisitor was still feared by the Sea Terrors.

blocks.x: He had died holding lantern and sword, standing as straight as in his youth when he trained as a sentry. Before the disciple who had fought alone until the moment of his death, Carmen said, "Be at peace," and then was silent for a long time.

At the top of the tower, Jordi, who had brought the Eye of Iberia back to life on his own, heard of the deaths of Dario and Thiago and sank to the floor. Carmen called old names out past the horizon. "Alfonso... Garcia... Touré... Julia... Are you still out there?"

Meanwhile, aboard the ship, the Hunters split apart. Before Gladiia, who meant to repair the ship and return to Ægir, Ulpianus sided with Alfonso, saying that until they had an answer about the creatures' god, anything they did would be in vain.

Then the sound of the waves and the sound of the wind faded away, one after another. Irene recalled the descriptions of the Profound Silence in the Inquisition's records. The Silence was quietly approaching.
Ulpianus told Skadi that she would always be their Hunter, then went up on deck with Specter.

blocks.cap: Beneath a sky full of stars, it looked down at Specter.

blocks.x: In the sky floated the Seaborn that had eaten Amaia. It said Amaia had taught it everything until she was broken down to the bone, and that it would take Specter home. Ulpianus's blade came down, but the Seaborn blocked the blow and hurled him into the sea.
Garcia charged too, but froze, seized by the thought of why he must attack his own kin. Then he called Alfonso's name.
Today is... the last day... of our voyage.

Saying he would die in battle as an Iberian, Garcia set his crown straight and charged, and the Seaborn pierced his body and threw him into the sea. The Seaborn said that in ten minutes this ship would sink.
13. The Last Monster Alfonso Slew

Meanwhile, at the Eye of Iberia, the boat that was to go rescue the Hunters was driven off by Sea Terrors and swept away. Mon3tr tried to bring back Jordi, who was aboard, but seeing the words 'Gran Faro' carved into the mast, Jordi did not take its hand and chose to seek out that ship alone.

Around then, inside the ship, the Hunters drove the Seaborn into a corner. The Seaborn told Skadi that the blood of the One flowed in her, so she herself was the One, and Skadi answered that she was Skadi of the Abyssal Hunters.

Irene blocked the Seaborn's escape, and Alfonso leapt down from the ceiling. When he asked how old Iberia remembered him, Irene answered: 'Alfonso Under the Pomegranate Tree,' 'The Hero, Alfonso,' 'The Sunken Alfonso.'
With the engines ablaze, Alfonso seized the Seaborn with his mutated hands, and the Hunters' blades split its body. Raising her weapon for the last blow, Specter said, "Goodbye, Amaia."
On the listing ship, Alfonso asked the Hunters to protect this Iberian. This was his Iberia, he said, and he could not betray his ship, and he sat upon the throne and closed his eyes.
Before his eyes passed the melodies of home, the warmth of Garcia's hand, Carmen's smiling face. In the flames he laughed aloud, and set a rusted blade to his own neck.
Remember this well, Irene! Return to land and sing of Alfonso's feats! The last monster that Alfonso slew... was himself!

blocks.cap: The Stultifera Navis sinks. An era has ended.

blocks.x: At that moment, at the Eye of Iberia, Carmen said he thought he had heard something, and Kal'tsit asked him whether he was crying.
Meanwhile, underwater, Irene clutched at the hem of Specter's clothes. Light was spilling up from the bottom of the sea, and as her vision dimmed she thought: so this is Ægir.

blocks.cap: The light came from the bottom of the sea.

blocks.x: Then, as the Seaborn regained its breath surrounded by its kin, Garcia sank his teeth into it and drove toward the seabed. Dissolving into the sea, he still would not let go, and in his place Ulpianus cut the Seaborn down.
"You will die a human being, Garcia." Garcia said thank you, and the two bodies sank to the bottom of the sea like two flowers blooming on a single stem.
Epilogue. A Lucky One

blocks.cap: "Hurry! Grab my hand!"

blocks.x: It was Jordi who held out a hand to Irene as she surfaced. He said he had found a pattern in the signal that ship had been sending and had come trusting to luck.

The Hunters said the light beneath the sea had been a city of Ægir who had fled all the way into Seaborn territory. The Ægir called Islanders, too, had been refugees who escaped from such fallen cities. Ulpianus was alive but refused to come with them, and Gladiia said they should return to the coast and regroup.
Our duty is to defend Ægir, not to 'go home.'
On the small boat, Jordi asked: am I a great person now?

Irene answered that he had only been a lucky one. Only those who are sacrificed deserve to be called great; everyone who survives and fights on is just an ordinary person carrying a responsibility. Still, she said, if human will could light this lantern, they were no different from the laborers of old Gran Faro.

Then, back at the lighthouse, Irene cried out before Dario's lantern that she would no longer hesitate. Carmen, having heard Alfonso's story, sat on the reef in silence until the whistles of the Penal Battalion sounded.

Meanwhile, in Gran Faro, Thiago's funeral was held on the Hill of Rebuilding, which looked out over a corner of the town. Alive Until Sunset played for the hero, and Elysium said that Iberia was his home too, and that he himself had not yet done anything.

blocks.cap: The Hill of Rebuilding. Elysium and the band saw Thiago off.

blocks.x: Then, in the town plaza, Carmen told Jordi to become the first Ægir to join the Inquisition, and Irene decided to set aside her post as Inquisitor in order to reach Ægir. When Irene asked whether he did not want to see the future Iberia had promised Gran Faro and Thiago, Jordi answered that he would think about it.

Around then, at the chapel, Gladiia told Kal'tsit of the truth Breogan had uncovered: the link between the Feranmut and the Leviathans. Kal'tsit said that the sea god the Hunters had killed was living inside Skadi's body, and that since the worst prediction had proven true, not returning to Ægir had been the right choice.
Chief Designer of Warfare, let us begin.
And out on the open sea, Ulpianus was with the knight and Rocinante. The knight cried out that he would never again allow the sea to raise so much as a ripple.

Like a pebble dropped into a deep well, the efforts of Gran Faro's people had seemed to make no sound at all. But after a few seconds of silence, the splash came. An Ægir who grew up in a town named for a lighthouse had lit the dark Eye of Iberia once more.

act16side.tagline: A trainee executor who dreams only of clocking out on time goes to check on a will, ends up taking in the eight-year-old girl left behind in its place, and hears a bell that hasn't rung in thousands of years. And a late goodbye, said to a mother.

chars.name: Cecelia
chars.desc: An eight-year-old Sankta girl. She lived alone with her mother and almost never left the house.

chars.name: Ezell
chars.desc: A Notarial Hall trainee executor whose life goal is clocking out on time. Also the nosiest busybody in all of Laterano.

chars.name: Fiammetta
chars.desc: A Liberi assigned as Mostima's bodyguard. She can't stand being called 'Shimmering Vigil.'

chars.name: Mostima
chars.desc: A Legatus and Fallen Angel who can't be bothered with anything. She comes back to Laterano once every few years.

chars.name: Lemuen
chars.desc: Fiammetta and Mostima's old comrade-in-arms. A once-famous sharpshooter, now in rehab at the hospital.

chars.name: Feoria
chars.desc: A Sankta woman who lived in Pagus Stevonus. Her neighbors knew her as a woman who lived alone.

chars.name: Federico
chars.desc: A Notarial Hall executor who goes strictly by the rules and shares no emotions through empathy · Operator Executor

chars.name: Patia
chars.desc: A Liberi from Iberia. What she hates most is Liberi who worship the Sankta like gods.

chars.name: Oren
chars.desc: A slick, quick-calculating Legatus in charge of Victoria.

chars.name: Velliv
chars.desc: A young cardinal who oversees the Legatus corps. Cautious about everything, and quick with the math.

chars.name: Pope
chars.desc: Laterano's supreme leader. An old man who loves desserts and is far craftier than he looks.

chars.name: Rosella
chars.desc: A Sarkaz woman who loves to sing. She is especially gentle with Cecelia.

chars.name: Andoain
chars.desc: A Sankta who had long been away from Laterano. His followers call him the 'Guide.'

terms.name: Legatus
terms.desc: A special messenger corps founded by the current Pope. Relying on Laterano's neutrality, they carry important information between nations.

terms.name: Notarial Hall
terms.desc: Laterano's administrative and law-enforcement body. Its executors handle everything from confirming wills to making arrests.

terms.name: Liberi
terms.desc: A race that lives alongside the Sankta in Laterano. They have no Halo, and no empathy.

terms.name: Halo
terms.desc: The ring of light above a Sankta's head. Through it, Sankta sense one another's emotions, a bond they call 'empathy.'

terms.name: Patron Firearm
terms.desc: A personal gun a Sankta receives through a rite upon reaching a certain age. When its owner dies, the Notarial Hall retrieves it.

terms.name: Fallen Angel
terms.desc: A Sankta who broke the commandments and fell. They can no longer share empathy with other Sankta, and even Patron Firearms reject them.

terms.name: Pathfinders
terms.desc: The name a heretical group gives itself; the Lateran Curia calls them the 'Astray.' They take in the people Laterano has turned away from.

terms.name: Tower of Revelations
terms.desc: Said to be the oldest tower in Laterano. Legend has it that a holy bell hangs inside.

blocks.x: March 1099, Laterano. One after another, the delegations the Pope invited through his Legatus corps are arriving, and the city is as noisy as ever, a place that has never known quiet or fatigue.

blocks.cap: One night, a man visits a woman in a wheelchair and swaps the withered flowers for fresh ones. As he leaves, she tells him just one thing: "Don't come back."

blocks.x: Meanwhile, in a small house in Pagus Stevonus, a mother was breathing her last. What she asked of her eight-year-old daughter **Cecelia** was this: stay hidden, go with the person who comes for her and find her papà, and tell him she was sorry.
"Run away... leave Laterano..." With those words, her mother's eyes closed, and the girl held the cooling hand tight.
Then comes a knock at the door. "Executor Federico of the Laterano Notarial Hall."
1. Explosions Go Through the Notarial Hall, Witnessed by an Executor

That same morning, a Columbian magnate out seeing the sights of Laterano watches a pillar on the street blow up right before his eyes. Two citizens were 'just dying to see what it would look like if it exploded,' so they filed an official report with the Notarial Hall and even evacuated the residents first: a perfectly legal demolition. The witness was trainee executor **Ezell**, whose life goal is clocking out on time. The only problem? Of all people, the magnate was standing right under the falling pillar.

Luckily, the pillar suddenly slowed as it toppled, and a Liberi used the moment to drag the magnate clear. The one who slowed down time was Legatus **Mostima**, and the rescuer was her bodyguard **Fiammetta**, who looked thoroughly disgusted when Mostima introduced her with "She's called Shimmering Vigil."
"It's just an explosion. Perfectly ordinary." Ezell's explanation leaves the magnate speechless, and Mostima greets him with a smile. "That's Lateran folk for you. Welcome to Laterano."

blocks.cap: The Legatus corps, traveling between nations. In 1099, the institution turned exactly thirty.

blocks.x: Fellow Legatus **Oren**, who had been watching the commotion, also heads for the Basilica where his colleagues have gathered. The young cardinal **Velliv** brings the room to order, and amid the hush, in walks the **Pope**. His very first words: "Good morning. Have you all had breakfast?"
2. No Will, Just a Child

Meanwhile, by-the-book executor **Federico** examines the body of a woman who lived alone at 7-265 Via Thervatius and reports it as a natural death. Cecelia, who had been keeping still the whole time, finally stepped out the door when friars in long robes took her mother away.

Then Ezell, assigned to confirm the will, arrives at the house. The deceased: head of household **Feoria** La Porta. Ezell receives her Patron Firearm from the friars and tilts his head, puzzled that there isn't even a pre-registered will.
