Just then, an unfamiliar little girl running away from Ezell trips and passes out on the spot. Ezell scoops her up and races to the hospital, while up on the rooftops, the Liberi **Patia** and her crew watch the whole thing.

Waking up in the hospital a while later, the girl introduces herself as Cecelia and says people in long robes took her mamma away. Convinced it's a kidnapping, Ezell blurts out a promise: "I'll help you find your mama."

blocks.cap: Cecelia opens her eyes in the hospital. Her first word: "Mamma..."

blocks.x: But in that moment, Cecelia's Halo sinks into darkness, and the pain that should pass naturally from one Sankta to another doesn't reach Ezell at all.

blocks.cap: Even in the most downcast moods, Sankta Halos don't dim like this.

blocks.x: Then a nurse calls Ezell up to the roof, saying the girl's situation is special. When Ezell tests her with "My colleagues are on their way," the 'nurse' turns out to be Patia, and her whole crew comes pouring out.
3. The Executor Who Went to Close the Window

Meanwhile, in the same hospital's recovery ward is **Lemuen**, Fiammetta and Mostima's old comrade-in-arms. She won last year's 'wheelchair rapid-fire competition' and promptly got banned from entering again by her doctors.
"Even though I'm the one who messed it all up." "That wasn't your fault, Lemuen." "And it wasn't yours either, Fiammetta."

blocks.cap: A hospital room in early spring. Same as always, as if nothing had ever happened.

blocks.x: Then a doctor walks in with some strange blood test results. Mostima skims them and immediately places a top-secret call to the Pope. "Some of the signs look very familiar."

Meanwhile, back in the ward, Patia's crew is trying to take Cecelia away. But then an explosion goes off by the window and smoke billows up. It's the very window Ezell said he'd go close before heading to the roof, 'so the kid doesn't catch a chill.'
Having planned ahead, Ezell slips away with Cecelia in his arms, and Patia shouts at his back: "Don't give her up to the Notarial Hall or the Lateran Curia! Or else, you'll regret it!"

Arriving a step too late, Fiammetta runs into Patia there. The junior who once followed her around calling her 'senior' back in their Guard days now only snaps at her coldly: "Don't you just love being surrounded by Sankta, Fiammetta?"
4. Mamma's Name Is Feoria

Out of the hospital and hiding in the crowds of Pagus Ambrosius, Ezell hesitates before his last chance to back out. But when Cecelia asks, "Is it still true, that you'll find Mamma?", he nods, ignores the order to report back, and heads for Pagus Stevonus, where her home is.

Meanwhile at the Basilica, Velliv hears out Mostima's report with a shake of the head. Some of the girl's indicators resemble those of Mostima, a Fallen Angel, but a small child couldn't have broken the commandments, and the only other possibility made no sense either. "If she were descended from the Sarkaz, she could never have a Halo."
The Pope sends Fiammetta alone after the girl, but the news goes straight through Oren to Patia. Oren, it turns out, has been working with Patia's side all along.

Around then, as Fiammetta leaves the Notarial Hall after looking up Ezell's location, Patia blocks her path. When Patia cries out, demanding to know why a Liberi would lay down her life for the Sankta, Fiammetta's answer is short: "If a person's views are that easy to change, they were never worth anything to begin with."

blocks.cap: Former senior and junior, face to face on the rooftops.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, Ezell reaches the girl's neighborhood and runs into a district office clerk. Nobody seems to know this girl who has supposedly lived here all her life, and when asked her mother's name, Cecelia answers: "Mamma's name is... Feoria."
Ezell freezes on the spot. A woman everyone believed lived alone: the very deceased whose body he had seen that morning.
5. A Sankta Who Shouldn't Have Turned Out as One

Inside the house, Ezell takes out Feoria's Patron Firearm, and Cecelia senses that something is wrong. After apologizing again and again, Ezell finally tells her the truth, but she can't understand what 'passed away' means. "Can you let me see Mamma one more time... I haven't even said goodbye to her..."

Then Oren shows up, saying he has come for the girl on the Pope's orders, and readily answers Ezell's questions. Cecelia is mixed-blood, he says. And yet a child of a Sankta and another race should never have a Halo or empathy.
She's a Sankta who shouldn't have turned out as one.

Fiammetta arrives soon after and sends Oren away, and Ezell asks only to be allowed to come along as far as the Basilica. At the same time in the Basilica, Velliv names who Feoria, having dodged the Notarial Hall to raise her daughter in hiding, would have entrusted the girl to: the heretical group known as the 'Astray.'
To the rigidly tense Velliv, the Pope asks breezily: "Don't be so uptight, Vel. Cream puff?"

On the way to the Basilica, while Fiammetta goes off to buy donuts, Cecelia hears the song her mamma taught her. When she asks the cotton candy food truck's vendor what the song is called, the startled vendor spills her sugar, and as her hood slips off, a pair of horns comes into view.
"Your horns look just like Papà's... Are you a Sarkaz too?"

blocks.cap: The street where the cotton candy truck stopped. The song Mamma taught her was drifting from there.

blocks.x: Ezell tells Fiammetta only that the vendor is a Sarkaz. That Cecelia's papà is a Sarkaz too, he never manages to say.
6. Where You Learn to Say Goodbye

While Fiammetta chases the fleeing Sarkaz, Ezell is told to go ahead to the Basilica. But if a Sarkaz with a Halo walks into the Basilica, will she ever walk out again? Ezell sticks his terminal under some envoy's official car and turns toward the Ecclesia Requietum, where Feoria lies.

Meanwhile, just as Fiammetta corners the Sarkaz in a dead-end alley, a familiar flash of Arts lights up before her, and under its cover the Sarkaz vanishes. Through gritted teeth, Fiammetta speaks the name: "An... do... ain..."

Around then at the Basilica, Mostima worries that everyone else has moved on, yet Fiammetta alone is still stuck on that rainy night eight years ago. When she suggests sending Fiammetta somewhere else, the Pope replies: "A person's path is theirs to find, theirs to choose, and theirs to walk."

At dusk, Ezell leaves the city behind and reaches the Ecclesia Requietum, where he places Feoria's Patron Firearm in Cecelia's hands. Then he tells her about his grandfather: when he died, an executor took his gun away, and only when Ezell happily called out to him that the flowers had bloomed did he realize his grandfather was gone.
Tears fall onto the floral pattern engraved on the gun. "Death is a goodbye after which you can never meet again." Behind them, a friar picks up where Ezell left off.
But to say goodbye is itself to overcome death. A 'goodbye' is the memory the living hold of the dead, and at the same time, proof that the dead existed.

blocks.cap: The Ecclesia Requietum of Pagus Stevonus. Here, the living say goodbye to the dead.

blocks.x: 7. Candlelight Reaches the Other Side

The next morning, when yesterday's cotton candy vendor walks into the chapel, the friar quietly stops Ezell, who has drawn his gun. The vendor introduces herself as **Rosella**, and when Cecelia says her horns are pretty, just like Papà's, Rosella smiles and tells her that her Halo is lovely too.
Outside the chapel, worshippers bow to the friar and greet him as "Guide." The friar tells Ezell he can simply call him by his name. **Andoain**.

Andoain speaks of an old Ursus man who lost everything to war, a Caprinae woman who was framed and fled from her burning home, and the Sarkaz, foes of a grudge thousands of years old. There is no place for them at the Basilica, he says, and not even the Liberi have ever truly been accepted.
Young executor, let me ask you. Why... are the Sankta the only ones who receive happiness, as if it were simply their due?

He has known about the mixed-blood child for years, he says, and once his work is done he will leave Laterano. Then he points to a graveyard full of wildflowers. "Tomorrow, that's where Feoria will be buried."

That night, while making candles for her mother with Rosella, Cecelia talks about her papà. He always appeared in the night forest wrapped in a heavy cloak and held her hand so tight it hurt, and when they parted, he would stand under a big tree until mother and daughter were out of sight.
Asked why Sarkaz can't come to Laterano, Rosella answers, "Love isn't a crime," and teaches her the song's lyrics. It was a Sarkaz song that sends off a hero on a long journey.
The hero sets out soon, down the road that leads far away, to make his dream come true... However long the road may be, surely, surely.
When Rosella says she'll keep vigil by her mother with her tonight, Andoain says: "The candlelight may be feeble, but it too can light up the other side."
8. Where the Irises Bloom
That same day, Fiammetta visits Lemuen again and admits she has seen Andoain. Lemuen answers calmly: "He's paid me a visit already." Then her gaze drifts to the vase on the desk.

Fiammetta can't hold it in any longer. Because of Andoain, Lemuen spent five years in a coma, and Mostima, who pointed her gun at him, became a Fallen Angel. And yet the two of them talk about him like they're talking about a weekend picnic.

Storming out of the room, Fiammetta pours out everything she has been holding in on Mostima, who followed her. She's sick of empathy, and why did Mostima think she followed her all the way to Victoria and Yan? The four of them were once a squad that trusted one another, and Andoain was always the one who fixed their reports.

blocks.cap: Fiammetta in the alley. Words she had swallowed for eight years burst out all at once.

blocks.x: For what reason... did he wreck all of it so easily...?! Those days... they meant so much to me...
Catching her breath, Fiammetta lets her eyes come to rest on a single flower. "Lateran irises." A flower that grows only in a few gardens and chapels, and in the Ecclesia Requietum of Pagus Stevonus.
It's Mostima who speaks first. "Come on, we'll go together."
9. A Funeral, and One More

On the morning of the funeral, when Cecelia asks whether her mother can really see this, Andoain doesn't lie to her. Much of what we do for others is, in the end, for ourselves, he says, and a funeral is a way of marking the road you have walked. And because only you can find your own road, he and his brothers and sisters call themselves the 'Pathfinders.'

A Sankta funeral is usually full of laughter, music, and desserts. But that day, the graveyard held only a slight girl struggling with a shovel far too heavy for her, and she laid the last of the earth over her mother's grave.

blocks.cap: The Ecclesia Requietum's graveyard, full of wildflowers. Feoria was buried here.

blocks.x: When I do a good job, Mamma can't praise me... When I do something bad, Mamma can't get angry at me... So what am I supposed to grow up for?
As Andoain soothes her, saying there's no need to rush, she still has plenty of time, someone cuts in. "Too bad, then, that yours just ran out."
It was Mostima and Fiammetta. When Andoain remarks that if they've come to mourn the deceased, they're a little late, Fiammetta replies: "That's fine. We'll have one more to mourn."

In the fight, Mostima calls on Ezell to bring the girl over, but when Rosella tells her, "You aren't done yet," Cecelia nods. After Andoain's Arts sweep across the area, the Pathfinders and Cecelia are gone.

Later, coming out of a meeting at the Basilica, Fiammetta tells Ezell that what's left is beyond his authority and he should go home and rest. Ezell forces out a cheerful shout: "Okay, let's clock out!"
10. The Girl Who Climbed the Bell Tower

That night at the hideout, Andoain tells Cecelia an old story. On a stormy night when villains descended on the poor town where he was staying, someone rang the alarm bell and woke the town. The battered body that the church watchman buried, grumbling all the while, belonged to the Sarkaz drunkard everyone used to point fingers at.

Was he a hero? Andoain says the Sarkaz climbed the bell tower simply because he wanted to, and that goodwill he could not go against is enough to make him no different from the hero in the song. And the song Andoain hums, searching his memory, is the very same one her mother and Rosella taught her.

The next morning, Ezell, who has taken the day off, finds Andoain standing before him with a crepe, one of only 200 made each day. When Ezell says all he ever wanted was a steady job where he could clock out on time, Andoain asks: "Then why haven't you left?"
When Ezell can't answer, Andoain leaves him a single piece of news and goes. Cecelia has gone to the old bell tower, to say goodbye.

Meanwhile, Oren is blocking the road to the bell tower. He says he was Feoria's old friend and that the girl can go anywhere she likes, as long as it isn't the Basilica, but Ezell plants himself in his way. "I promised Cecelia I'd find her mama with her, and be with her when she says goodbye."

"I'll definitely be fine!" Hearing that promise, Cecelia runs for the bell tower. Just as Ezell is cornered, with Pathfinder Messengers joining the fight, Federico appears. He had followed Feoria's travel logs all the way to Oren.

blocks.cap: "Oren Argiolas, your identity has been confirmed."

blocks.x: Meanwhile, climbing the bell tower, Cecelia thinks: whatever people may want from her, the thing she most needs to do is what she herself wants to do.
Whether that's Sankta, or Sarkaz. But I'm Cecelia. Just Cecelia.
As the air begins to tremble with a power unlike any Arts, Federico sends Ezell to the bell tower. When a breathless Ezell throws open the door at the top, the girl is singing the old Sarkaz song.

blocks.cap: The top of the bell tower. Pouring every feeling she had into it, the girl sang in her small, young voice.

blocks.x: And the bell rang. It was the holy bell of the Tower of Revelations, a tower said to be older than Laterano itself, and it had never once rung except in the days, thousands of years ago, when the first saints walked this land.
When an Apostolic Knight sent by the Pope arrives at the bell tower, the girl turns to the worried Ezell. "It's okay, Mister Ezell. Let's go."
11. A Question for the Pope

After the bells, explosions and fires break out across the city, and as most of the Gun-Knights are called away to the envoys' village, Andoain heads for the Basilica. Around then, in her hospital room, Lemuen hugs Fiammetta and apologizes, and tells her that Andoain seems about to ask the Pope a question no Sankta should ever ask.

Before heading to the Basilica, Fiammetta tracks down Patia, who has been stirring up trouble. Even facing Fiammetta, who only wants to protect her friends, Patia chases what she believes in to the very end, and Fiammetta brings her down and carries her somewhere safe.

At the same moment, Pope **Yvangelista XI**, facing Andoain, isn't even surprised. Andoain says he has closed the coffins of innocent children while comforting the mourners that salvation would surely come, yet nothing ever happened. "We will never find salvation, will we?"

The Pope answers that paradise is only paradise because the wastes beyond are so cold, and that paradise cannot be burned as kindling for a wildfire destined to go out. Andoain calls out the names one by one. Mrs. Baelen of the rock salt and sundries store. Deacon Landi of the Tidal Chapel. Little Sagre, who wove the ropes for the alarm bell.
Tell me, is there anything wrong with their faith, with their hope? ...Why did Rocamarea deserve to be destroyed?
Then the gunshots rang out almost at the same time. A Sankta aiming a gun at a Sankta: the one thing the law has carved into their very bones and blood as forbidden.

blocks.cap: The gunshots rang out almost at the same time.

blocks.x: The force unleashed by the Pope's Patron Firearm hurls Andoain into the wall. Yet beyond the smoke, the Pope's Halo is still shining, and Andoain's own Halo hasn't dimmed in the slightest.
"I see." The Pope says there has only ever been one true law: that we must go on existing. When Andoain asks who 'we' are, the answer is short. "Follow me."

blocks.cap: Past the bones of the saints and the tombstones of Popes past, deeper still.

blocks.x: In that place, recorded in no text, something was rumbling low. Beyond the reach of any interpretation or debate, it linked the Sankta, made the Sankta, and was the measure of all things. It was not the answer Andoain had wanted, but it existed, all the same.
12. Obsession

Meanwhile, Lemuen tells Fiammetta about Andoain's past. He grew up in Rocamarea, a small town in Iberia, and when the town was falling apart, he asked Laterano for the smallest bit of aid, only to be told: 'You are one of us, but they are not.' By the time he went back, his hometown had vanished as if it had never been there at all.

Around then, the Pope invites Ezell and Cecelia for tea. When the girl says she wants to leave Laterano, he asks, "If I said no, would you obey me?" When she answers that she probably wouldn't, he says, "Then go," and tells her to take her mother's Patron Firearm with her too; he'll pretend not to notice.
Ezell is handed a long-term field assignment: to leave with the girl. "Do I... really have the right to do that?" "Of course you do. You've already made your choice, haven't you?"
After the two of them leave, the Pope tells Velliv: we can never be the bonfire on a cold night, but we can at least serve a warm cup of tea to the one carrying the firewood.
And on the Basilica's roof, Fiammetta remembers that night eight years ago. She had stepped away only briefly to answer a call for backup, and when she came back, everything was beyond undoing.

blocks.cap: A rainy night eight years ago. Mostima holding Lemuen, who has collapsed.

blocks.x: Andoain appears before her, so broken that he mutters there has never been any light. Fiammetta shouts at him to pull himself together, to get on his knees and apologize to Mostima and Lemuen. There is only one reason she won't forgive him: he betrayed the people who believed in him.

blocks.cap: "Lemuen, Mostima, Yvangelista XI... even if all of Laterano forgives you, I will never forgive you."

blocks.x: When Andoain says that if it happened again, he would do exactly the same, Fiammetta tells him to draw his gun. Not to see how things turn out; she just wants to settle things with him, once and for all.
You, me, everyone. Aren't we all here because of our obsessions?
In that instant, a shot from far away knocks Andoain's gun out of his hand. It was Lemuen, sniping from atop a hotel sign, wheelchair and all.

blocks.cap: A sudden gunshot split the sky.

blocks.x: Andoain thought it was better this way. His gun would stay in Laterano. Then he looked up and said that everything we do is not to be saved, but to earn the right to save ourselves. "Thank you, Fiammetta."

But an explosion set off by Oren brings a pillar crashing down, and in the confusion Andoain disappears, leaving behind the wish that whenever and wherever they meet again, all of their obsessions will remain unchanged.

Then, on March 18th, 1099, Yvangelista XI uses a shortwave broadcast to call on the nations to found a council that would jointly guarantee one another's safety. "Terra must stand shoulder to shoulder and survive to the very end." It was the speech that would later be known as the 'Lateran Declaration.'
Epilogue. A Martyr's Sunset

Some time later, Lemuen decides to join the Lateran Curia's Seventh Tribunal, and informs Mostima, who had been thinking of quitting the Legatus corps, that "You answer to me now." Fiammetta, who keeps Andoain's gun in her care, is dispatched to Rhodes Island and picks 'Dawn Destroyer' as her new codename.

The captured Astray are released by the Pope's will, and Oren, stripped of his post, stays on as Velliv's subordinate. As for Federico, the reason he dug into this case to the very end was to find Arturia, a distant relative of his and a wanted criminal.
And the Ecclesia Requietum's graveyard. Cecelia, who has decided to set out with Ezell, now assigned to Rhodes Island, stands among the flowers and says goodbye to her mother.
Mamma, I'm leaving Laterano. But I'm not running away. I'm going to find Papà. I'll make sure to tell him what you said.

Just then, far off, she sees Andoain's group leaving Laterano. The setting sun overlaps the Halo of the man at the front, making it look like a crown, and Cecelia remembers a word her mother once spoke so carefully: 'Martyr.'

Her mother had said, "Run away... leave Laterano..." But the girl finishes her goodbye and sets out on a road of her own. Holding the young Sankta's hand tight, her steps are slow, but she does not look back.

act15side.tagline: A Lungmen detective comes to deliver one cheap wine cup as a favor for an old schoolmate, and ends up set down like a go stone in the middle of a game played by the Yan court, an escort association, and the 'Sui.' And what everyone chasing that cup found in the end was people.

blocks.x: **Shangshu** in Yan is a place where, instead of moving the mountains, people built their cities to fit them. The towns are scattered between the peaks, and every one of the scenic **Three Mounts and Seventeen Peaks** comes with a legend attached.

One early spring, **Lee**, who runs a private detective agency in Lungmen, arrives here carrying an antique box. Inside is an item a schoolmate he hasn't seen in over ten years asked for by letter: a **Black Wine Cup** that got thrown in as a freebie at a smugglers' auction. And yet, a strange number of people seem to be after this cheap little cup.

Around the same time, Rhodes Island's **Kroos** and soon-to-be-hired **Mr. Nothing** also arrive in Shangshu. The plan is to rest a day or two and then meet up with 'those sisters,' and Mr. Nothing spends the whole time showing off the scenery.

blocks.cap: "It's these rivers and hills before us, see." Why the people of Yan can never bring themselves to leave their home mountains.

blocks.x: 1. Two Plates of Peanuts for the First Guest, a Flying Chair for the Next

At the **Xingyu Inn** on Shangshu's Yingfeng Road, **Innkeeper Zheng** is lecturing a clerk who keeps going on about 'distinguished guests.' 'How would you ever know who's distinguished? You can't judge people by appearances alone.' Right then, in walk the first guests: Lee, and the old boatman who met him at the ferry, **Master Shen**.

Kroos and Mr. Nothing check into the same inn soon after, and then the door bursts open: a young lady called **Miss Du** storms in with her henchmen. She's after the thief who brought a wine cup from Lungmen, described as 'a man in flashy clothes and glasses who looks like a shady shaman.' So naturally, the first one to get a chair kicked at him is Mr. Nothing. But when a henchman whispers that 'the one in the letter is a Lung,' she turns her eyes to the second floor.

blocks.cap: "Personally, I thought my attire was just dandy." A Lungmenite with objections to his description.

blocks.x: Kroos recognizes that Lungmenite as 'Mr. Lee,' a Rhodes Island collaborator, and when Mr. Nothing calls for a truce, marveling at the odds of bumping into an old friend in a place as big as Shangshu, Miss Du shouts: 'I knew you were all in it together!'

In the chaos, Lee, Kroos and Master Shen slip away, leaving Mr. Nothing to hold off Miss Du all by himself with nothing but a fan. While the clerk stamps his feet begging someone to stop them, Innkeeper Zheng can only sigh. "Distinguished guests, my foot!"

When Innkeeper Zheng finally steps in and ends the fight, Mr. Nothing edges toward the door and vanishes without a trace. To Miss Du, left behind, Innkeeper Zheng says quietly that someone who knows neither what that cup is nor what kind of man that Lungmenite is 'isn't even fit to drag the escort association's name through the mud.'

Then, with Mr. Nothing back in the group and everyone about to head for the schoolmate's residence, Lee happens to glance behind him. Something he's never seen before, with a metal bowl on its back, is staring up at him.

blocks.cap: "Are these strange pets the new trend in Shangshu...?" Krrooo.

blocks.x: 2. A Schoolmate After Ten Years, and a Residence with Too Many Guests

Lee's schoolmate **Liang Xun** is the Magistrate of Shangshu, the official who governs this city. According to Lee, he's something like 'the Wei Yenwu of Shangshu,' and shoe-shiners and taxi drivers on the street alike give a thumbs-up at the mention of his name.

After hearing the smugglers' ghost story that the cup breathes life into the objects around it, Liang Xun only says he has one more favor to ask. Lee has asked Liang Xun a favor of his own, too: to find Huai Tianpei, an old friend and the father of **Waai Fu**, whom Lee has been looking after at his agency.

Lee has only just managed to get Liang Xun, who insists drinking leads to nothing but trouble, to sit down for a drink when the sweet voice of **Miss Ning**, a frequent visitor to the residence, cuts in. Declaring 'I'm merely the messenger,' Lee leaves the cup and bolts from the room, muttering: "...This guy's in for it now."

Meanwhile, in an alley at night, Kroos and Mr. Nothing try to lure out the daytime attackers and get caught instead. The man holding a blade to Mr. Nothing's throat is **Taihe**, Deputy Monitor Censor of the Department of Discipline and Supervision, and he demands to know why Infected have come to Shangshu, and why **Dusk** left her mountain without permission.

blocks.cap: "No need to be so confrontational, Uncle Taihe." Enter the self-styled 'court Messenger.'

blocks.x: The boy who stops him, **Zuo Le**, tells them to think of him as a court Messenger of sorts, and advises that if they're deeply tangled up with those sisters, they'd better not go too far. When Kroos says **Nian** is her friend and colleague, and Dusk is her friend's troublesome little sister, Zuo Le replies: 'It's already too late.'

Meanwhile, in Lee's guest room, Miss Du is waiting for him, having even helped herself to a pot of Liang Xun's tea. It turns out Innkeeper Zheng is actually her father, and that father has been commissioned by someone high up in the court to snatch the cup.

Her real name is **Du Yaoye**, and she says the idle-rich-girl act is just part of a plan her father drew up, a plan with no place in it for her. So she proposes they team up to make this job fall through, and in return she'll see to it that Lee gets back to Lungmen safe and sound. Surprisingly, Lee agrees without a fuss.
3. A Peak in a Dream, a Teapot in a Box

That night Lee dozes off and wakes up on an unfamiliar plank road along a cliff. A new signpost reads 'Zuanjiang Peak,' and a passerby sweeping snow corrects him: this isn't one of the Three Mounts and Seventeen Peaks, but one of the 'Eighteen Peaks.'

blocks.cap: A new sign, fresh lettering, an old inscription. The plank road up Zuanjiang Peak, climbed in a dream.

blocks.x: When he reaches the summit with its pavilion, words that aren't Lee's start spilling out of Lee's mouth. It's the voice of someone visiting an old friend after decades, holding out a pair of stones, one black and one white, and telling them to pick one; asked if he isn't afraid of losing everything, the voice answers that he 'was merely pushed along by the greater game.'

What wakes Lee is a commotion over a thief. A shadow clutching the box has gone over the wall, they say, but Lee calmly produces the real cup. What was in the box was a teapot from the kitchen, dyed black with ink.
Only then does Liang Xun bring up his second favor: find the cup's 'owner.'

Meanwhile, Kroos, chasing the thief, somehow ends up in a scrap with Miss Du at the night market. Miss Du insists she isn't the one who robbed the Liang estate, hints only that whoever hired the escort association is someone even Mr. Liang can't lay a finger on, and disappears.

That same night at the Xingyu Inn, Innkeeper Zheng is examining the fake cup together with Zuo Le. It was Zuo Le who went over the wall of the Liang estate, and Innkeeper Zheng who helped him slip away from Kroos.

Innkeeper Zheng recalls a night ten years ago, escorting this very cup, when bandits chased them through a torrential downpour in the wilderness. His wounded comrades never opened their eyes again, and the cargo was lost too. Back then, the rule of Zheng Qingyue, the 'Asker to the Frost,' the swordsman who led the **Xingyu Escort Association**, was 'save the goods, then the men.'
4. Wanted: Cup Owner (Gender, Age and Race Unknown; Enjoys Drinking in Pavilions)

This is everything Liang Xun knows about the owner: has never left Shangshu, hides out on one of the peaks of the Three Mounts, comes down once in a blue moon to buy wine at a tavern halfway up the mountain, and on fine days likes to lie in a pavilion reciting poetry.

The next day, climbing the mountain with Master Shen, Lee asks about the name from his dream. As it turns out, Zuanjiang Peak is the old name of **Qujiang Peak**, and at its summit there's nothing but an empty clearing called the 'Field of Forgotten Water.'

Around then, at the Liang estate, Liang Xun sits face to face with Taihe. Out comes his promise to General Zuo to fake the cup's theft once it arrived and hand it over to Lord Zuo, and the fact that the court's secret agency for the Sui, the **Sui Regulator**, has gone over the head of the **Ministry of Rites**. And the name of the person Liang Xun hopes to find through Lee is **Ling**.

When Liang Xun asks whether this isn't overstepping, Taihe answers that he's only repaying a debt of kindness to the General: 'garner loyalty and forsake righteousness.' That day, Miss Ning, looking around Liang Xun's study, takes note of a box that wasn't there before.

Around the same time, Miss Du clashes with her father. When he tells her she still has no eye for people, she fires back that living as a carefree young lady and living the way her father wants are both 'not me, in the end.'

Left alone, Liang Xun recalls a memory he has never been able to forget. As a child, on the day a Catastrophe struck the Three Mounts and everyone fled, he saw a woman in a mountaintop pavilion, collapsed drunk with her cup still raised to the sky, and neither the rescuers nor the grown-ups seemed able to see her. "...Was this the cup she drank from?"

blocks.cap: On the day they crossed the mountain fleeing disaster, a child saw a woman in a pavilion raising her cup to the sky.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, in a village at the foot of Qujiang Peak, Lee pays a pole-carrier named **Shang Zhong** to track down the pavilion and the tavern. He's a quiet man who goes up and down the mountain at a pace that astonishes tourists, and says he's just been to 'see' his son. Even Innkeeper Zheng's men, who had Lee surrounded, quietly back off once he shows up.

Meanwhile, as Kroos and Mr. Nothing wait for the sisters who've gone out of contact, an **Ink Spirit**, an ink beast from Dusk's paintings, appears before them. From inside the painting, Dusk asks a favor: find the cup's owner and talk her around before the court does, and buy time so the Sui Regulator can't take her away.
5. To Old Ambitions, Cheers

After running into more attackers on the mountain, Lee returns to the Liang estate and asks Liang Xun point-blank: just how big a secret are this cup and its owner hiding? Liang Xun can't bring himself to tell him everything, saying only that it concerns 'the people and the country.'

Instead, the two of them share a drink. There's Liang Xun in their school days, who said the world was too cold and lonely and he'd get everyone under heaven to build a fire together; Huai Tianpei, who said he'd make his name across the land through martial arts; and Lee himself, who jumped barely clear of the water and thought all of heaven and earth was his home.
Asked why Lungmen of all places, Lee answers that it's the very edge of Yan, and any farther out he'd have nowhere left to go. And when Liang Xun says he could always come back: he doesn't want to.

At the same time, Zuo Le calls Kroos aside. Openly admitting that the Sui Regulator has been watching all three, Nian and Dusk, 'incarnations of the Sui,' and Ling, hiding somewhere in Shangshu, and that Liang Xun has been acting on the Sui Regulator's secret orders from the start, he asks Rhodes Island to persuade Lee to hand over the cup.
That would make things easier, he says. 'The elimination of the Sui.'

And Lee, asleep after drinking, dreams again. This time he's playing go with someone in a pavilion, and the person across the board says Lee isn't 'him,' and asks whether he's holding that man's stones and playing in his stead. When Lee asks her name, she answers **Ling**, and says this is a dream from a hundred years ago.

blocks.cap: "Will you play in his stead, then? Mr. Lee of Lungmen?"

blocks.x: 6. The Thief Strikes Again, For Real This Time

At dawn the next day, Lee is woken by Miss Du's shouting. A Rim Billiton woman snooping outside Lee's room, the bounty hunter **Blacknight**, has been caught. In the commotion, one of her Slumberfoots grabs the cup from Liang Xun's study in its mouth and runs off.

At the same time, out on the street, Kroos and Mr. Nothing find themselves surrounded by a teapot with legs, a living hanging scroll, and a swarm of paperweights. Hit them and they turn back into ordinary objects, and somehow they look a lot like Dusk's Ink Spirits.

blocks.cap: Downtown Shangshu. Today's enemies: a teapot, a hanging scroll, and a vase.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, asked by Liang Xun to get the cup back first and foremost, Lee leaves a letter for Rhodes Island telling them to 'go find Master Shen' and sets off with Miss Du. He's not the one who wants the cup, after all, so they might as well sit back and watch how many anglers turn up and what big fish takes the bait.

Meanwhile, early in the morning, Liang Xun calls in Miss Ning and asks how she spent yesterday. Miss Ning smoothly lists the five people she met, all the way down to Uncle Bai, who works as a potter. Just routine business, she says.

Around then, in a mountain village, Innkeeper Zheng blocks Blacknight's path. He plucks a crossbow bolt out of the air bare-handed and offers her double her fee for the cup; Blacknight holds firm, saying she's only helping a friend. Then a bamboo carrying pole slams down, smashing the bricks underfoot to pieces. It's Shang Zhong.

Shang Zhong snatches the cup from Blacknight and glares at Innkeeper Zheng. On that rainy night ten years ago, a dozen-odd men of the escort association died, he says, and among them were his son and Du Yaoye's real father. You, who said the goods came first: didn't you lose both the goods and the men?
I'll be waiting atop the mountain. Go fetch your blade.
7. Waiting at the Field of Forgotten Water

Shang Zhong shows up at a teahouse halfway up the mountain with the cup brazenly hanging from his belt. When Miss Du explains that the free noon tea for pole-carriers is a policy that began after Liang Xun took office, he says 'You have a fine father' and gets up, and right after that the teahouse's bowls and the picture on its signboard all leap out at once and charge, wreathed in flames.

Then, on the trail, Zuo Le and Taihe block Shang Zhong's way. When Zuo Le calls the cup 'bait' to lure out those who would bring disaster upon the nation and its people, Shang Zhong counters that he's burying it at his son's grave. Declaring that the words he's hated most all his life are 'save the goods, then the men,' he trades blows with Taihe and then vanishes like the wind, leaving only word that he'll be waiting for Zheng Qingyue at the Field of Forgotten Water on Qujiang Peak.

Around then, Kroos, on her way to the summit, hears an old tale from Master Shen. Zuanjiang Peak once had a twin, 'Xunri Peak,' that pierced the sky like a sword, but it collapsed in a Catastrophe thirty years ago. And yet not a single person was hurt, and not even the rubble was left behind.

Then Zuo Le, running into Kroos again on the mountain path, comes clean. The cup was made by a great criminal, and part of the consciousness of a fearsome beast dwells inside it. The **Waregeists**, object apparitions that awaken wherever the cup passes, are the proof, and the cup's current owner is 'a certain poet.'

At the same time, at the Liang estate, Miss Ning presses Liang Xun. Is he going to keep searching, deceiving heaven, himself and everyone else? Doesn't he know that if things go wrong, he'll be the first to take the blame?
Liang Xun answers that if even a single brick or roof tile is damaged, the failing is his, so he's simply pushing on. And then he asks in return: is that a friend's advice, or...
...are you reproaching me as Ning Ciqiu, the court's Imperial Envoy of Vice-Second Rank and Assistant Minister of Rites?

blocks.cap: The Liang estate after an early nightfall. The other name of a gentle guest.

blocks.x: 8. A Match, Ten Years Later
Sunset on Qujiang Peak. Before Shang Zhong, who has carried his pole up and down this mountain every day for ten years, Zheng Qingyue appears with his blade.

Shang Zhong knew that Zheng Qingyue had taken in and raised a dead comrade's daughter, and that the inns and the teahouses were all an escape route for her. Even so, he says, running from the past after a single defeat was trampling on the dead.
Zheng Qingyue, 'Asker to the Frost,' Head of the Xingyu Escort Association. Shang Zhong, of the Polearm of the Shangs. Where blade and pole collide, Miss Du and Lee rush in.

Shang Zhong tells Miss Du everything. That night, Zheng Qingyue lost his brothers protecting the cargo, and her birth father was among them; afterward, her mother left Shangshu too. But Miss Du already knew all of it.
Escort association or inn, someday it'll all belong to the Du family. So I'm asking you two: don't get in my way.

Shang Zhong throws the cup to Lee and the three of them grapple; struck by Zheng Qingyue's blade, the Black Wine Cup flies off over the cliff. As Lee runs after it, Miss Du blocks Zuo Le from following. She made a promise to Mr. Lee, she says, and in the jianghu, a promise is worth a thousand gold. That is a rule too.

Mr. Nothing cuts in front of Zuo Le, Taihe hurls a boulder, and Kroos's crossbow bolts fly between them. When Zuo Le asks whether she won't cooperate with the Sui Regulator, Kroos answers briefly: she knows what kind of person Nian is, and at the very least, Nian is someone who helped her.

Meanwhile, at the teahouse halfway up the mountain, Liang Xun admits to Master Shen that Miss Ning may have seen through everything from the start, and that the thief in his study was likely her doing. Master Shen warns that the one man who must not be drawn in is **Tianshi Bai**, the Ministry of Rites tianshi living as a potter. If he unleashes his thunder and lightning, the Sui Regulator and the Ministry of Rites will be at each other's throats.

Liang Xun asks this old boatman, who once guarded the northern frontier, to stop Miss Ning's side before they make their move. And to the suggestion that they leave it to the will of heaven, he answers that the first words he learned at the Yan court were 'Heaven's mandate lies in man.'
9. Another Mountain atop the Mountain
Below the cliff, as Lee searches for the cup amid a swarm of Waregeists, a voice that isn't Lee's comes out of his mouth again. "...Move." Where the Waregeists draw back, Nian appears.

In front of Zuo Le, who has followed, Nian readily admits it. Part of the consciousness of 'our second brother' is trapped in the cup, and Lee, who was stuck with it for too long, is a victim. And she says it's time to rise up against their own great self, that one way or another she wants to kill 'that thing.'

At the same time, at the Field of Forgotten Water, a boatman in a bamboo hat takes the falling rain as his sword and shatters Shang Zhong's pole in a single stroke. Taihe calls out his name: **Shen Lou**, the 'Rainmaster of Duckweeds,' who served ten years in the army.
And above the Field of Forgotten Water, once an empty clearing, a peak and a pavilion that were never there suddenly appear.

In the pavilion, Zuo Le reveals why the Sui Regulator was in such a hurry. As the world grew more turbulent, the current court's **Grand Tutor** met with that 'great criminal,' learned where the cup was, and issued secret orders to the Sui Regulator.
Just then, a languid voice comes from somewhere: 'Do you seek me?'

blocks.cap: "With such beautiful scenery before you, must you still persist with such joyless talk?"

blocks.x: Ling takes one look at Lee and speaks to someone inside him. Isn't such a vulgar ploy beneath his dignity? 'He,' wearing Lee's face, grumbles that Ling threw away the cup he gave her, then laughs at his three younger siblings, and at himself, still so full of his own pride.

The Grand Tutor's 'personal letter' that Zuo Le hands over turns out not to be in the Grand Tutor's hand at all. At the words in the unfolded letter, 'affairs come in no more than threes,' the three sisters are left speechless.

blocks.cap: The wind has blown since ancient times, but this time was no longer that moment.

blocks.x: Then before the three sisters appears a colossal **'Sui-Xiang'**, shaped from the shadows of the three of them and the Sui. Ling picks up a wine jar with her tail, pours wine into the Black Wine Cup, raises it to the sky and offers, 'Care for a drink?' And it's 'he' who answers. When Lee's group comes to, they're sitting in a dark room where half of a painting titled 'The Way to Paradise' hangs.
What say you to a game with me?
10. I Am Me

Liang Xun and Miss Ning, who were at the teahouse halfway up the mountain, are summoned too and seated before the go board. 'He' tells Lee that the others will all think Liang Xun dragging him into this was a coincidence, but for Lee alone it wasn't, and hints that there must be a man named Huai. For the first time, Lee's face stiffens.

blocks.cap: A room where half of 'The Way to Paradise' hangs. A match played by a go player who hates go.

blocks.x: The game soon tips to one side, but Lee realizes the meaning of this match doesn't lie on the board. 'He' confides that after losing one of his siblings in an accident, his jar came up one black stone short, then says he underestimated his siblings far too much and abruptly concedes.

Meanwhile, before the rampaging Sui-Xiang, Dusk, who says she hid inside paintings for a hundred years without ever daring to close her eyes, trembles, while Nian grits her teeth, refusing to accept it. When Nian answers 'I don't know' to the question of what will become of them in the end, Ling tells her that isn't a good answer.
I am me. What has that thing got to do with me? The world has been drunk for ten thousand years. Am I not allowed even a single dream?

Meanwhile, on the mountainside, as blade and pole face off again, rocks come crashing down. Boulders he once would have split without raising a speck of dust, Zheng Qingyue can no longer cut down entirely.
He has grown old, but the child has grown up. Trying to save her father, Miss Du is struck by a rock and falls over the cliff, and Zheng Qingyue leaps after her without a moment's hesitation.

It was Shang Zhong who saved them both, reaching out at the last moment. As Zheng Qingyue weeps, clutching his unconscious daughter, Shang Zhong shouts that he doesn't even have the right to regret yet and urges him to strike the final blow; Zheng Qingyue says he can't bring himself to fight to the death with the man who just saved his child, and tells Shang Zhong to strike instead.

A mournful zither sounds from somewhere, and Ling sits silently atop a rock. In the end Shang Zhong never strikes, and watching the daughter wake up and scold the two of them, he murmurs: "Yaoye, you've grown up."

blocks.cap: A snow-covered forest below the cliff. Two enemies, and the child who grew up between them.

blocks.x: And in the sky above the pavilion, the giant shadow that had loomed over the land scatters on a gentle breeze. When Nian asks how Ling could shatter it so easily while they had to stake their very existence just to hold out, Ling answers that that's exactly why she's their big sister.

The Sui Regulator moves to send the three sisters out of Shangshu under watch, but at that moment **Leizi** appears. She says she persuaded Tianshi Bai to leave everyone some room, and she brings just one piece of news: the Grand Tutor is already in Shangshu.
Epilogue: The Grand Tutor's Game
That night at the Liang estate, an old man walks in before Zuo Le and Miss Ning, Taihe and Liang Xun.

blocks.cap: "Under the heavens of Yan, all I fear is that the people cannot live in peace and the nation cannot prosper."

blocks.x: After asking a few questions, the Grand Tutor sums up this round as 'an even game,' and tells Liang Xun to hand Shangshu over to his successor and come with him to the capital. Miss Ning offers her 'congratulations on the promotion,' then receives orders to leave for Yumen ahead of them.
When Taihe reports to the Grand Tutor that 'all is proceeding smoothly,' Zuo Le is left speechless. Taihe says he 'garnered loyalty and forsook righteousness,' and asks not to be blamed.

After it's all over, Lee lays out what Liang Xun was really thinking, piece by piece. Liang Xun had received the Sui Regulator's secret orders, yet wanted neither trouble breaking out in Shangshu nor a rift between the Sui Regulator and the Ministry of Rites. Someone who cared about him sent a bounty hunter to intercept the cup, and Shang Zhong, whom no one saw coming, dragged everyone up to the Field of Forgotten Water.
In the end, what I found wasn't the answer to who owns that cup. What I was looking for was you.

Whether he was still the same Liang Xun who once held such grand ambitions. To Lee, who says he's glad that Liang Xun, for all that he's grown a lot cleverer, is still himself, Liang Xun hands over a lead on Huai Tianpei's whereabouts, as if in return.

That same night, the Grand Tutor offers Nian a deal: help build cities and towers outside the Chamber of Heaven's Designs in the north, and the court will help her in turn. Ling tells her sisters that long ago, the Grand Tutor didn't play go against 'him' at all. He won a game played with Yan as the board and its people as the stones.

Meanwhile, Miss Ning sends Blacknight off to Tianshi Bai and confides that she couldn't simply take what Liang Xun wouldn't give her, and that she didn't want him dragged into all this without even knowing why.

And in the empty pavilion, Ling faces the voice in the cup. Asked whether the Xingyu Escort Association affair was his doing too, the voice answers 'not all of it,' then offers her some 'advice': her younger sisters, grown far too much like humans, will one day come to know fear.

When Ling says wine shouldn't be this chatty, all things come to a standstill, and one more peak rises among the Three Mounts and Seventeen Peaks. The cup with which someone long ago offered wine to the heavens and drove back the black clouds of Catastrophe now vanishes without a trace before those very black clouds.

Around then at the Xingyu Inn, Shang Zhong says he'll leave Shangshu: each of them wants to die at the other's hand, so there will never be an end to it. It isn't reconciliation, he says, only putting things off for a while. When Zheng Qingyue, who says he's retiring, answers that he'll wait for him in Shangshu, Miss Du bursts in and declares: "We're going to Yumen!"

blocks.cap: The Xingyu Inn. By escort association custom, grudges are never raised over drinks.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, with Mr. Nothing taken to the hospital with an injured leg, Kroos is called back by her office, and Lee declines to go with her, saying there's still someone he needs to find. When Kroos asks how Liang Xun is anything like Wei Yenwu, this was the answer Lee left her: neither of them can do a thing in front of the one they love.

Just as the innkeeper said, how would you ever know who's distinguished? This spring in Shangshu, the boatman, the pole-carrier and the gentle guest were all more than they seemed. And while everyone chased a single Black Wine Cup, Lee alone went looking for a person instead of the cup: whether a friend he was meeting again after ten years was still that same friend.

act14side.tagline: The Doctor follows the youngest Silverash up into the snowy mountains, only to be hauled off as a 'guest of honor' the moment they arrive, all thanks to her brother's bizarre gambit of handing his land over to a god. And then, the footsteps of a Saintess who stopped the blizzard in its tracks.

chars.name: Enya

chars.name: Gnosis

chars.name: Arctosz

chars.name: Ratatos

blocks.x: Kjerag, the nation of snowy mountains, has worshipped the mountain god **Kjeragandr** for over a thousand years. Silverash, Paleroche, and Browntail, the so-called **Three Clans**, divide up the land, while the **Vine-Bead Court** on the summit keeps the faith.

But when **Enciodes**, the young head of the Silverash clan, founded **Karlan Trade CO., LTD** and started laying railways, that old balance began to crack. That was right around when he invited the Doctor of Rhodes Island to Kjerag.

They say that even the tiniest external force, given just the lightest push, can set off an avalanche that swallows all of Kjerag. This story begins with that force setting foot on the snowy mountains.

blocks.cap: Mines and valleys, forests and lakes. A snowy nation split among three clans.

blocks.x: 1. The Charm Is Fake, the Voice Is Real

**Turicum**, a border city at Kjerag's southernmost tip. A Victorian accountant on a business trip is about to pay 50 pounds for a 'charm blessed by Kjeragandr' when **Ensia**, the youngest of the Silverash clan, cuts in and starts asking where it came from. The price promptly drops to 10 pounds.

Ensia had been getting Oripathy treatment at Rhodes Island, and has just brought the Doctor home with her. Her brother, who held the family together after their parents died when they were young, and her sister, who climbed the mountain to become the Saintess five years ago, stopped speaking to each other at some point. She wants to ask the Doctor how to bridge that gap, though she also worries that her anything-goes brother might use the Doctor.

Then, as the Doctor turns to leave, an unfamiliar voice speaks up. It's a warning: if you don't want to freeze to death, leave right now. But when the Doctor looks back at the balcony, there's nobody there.

Meanwhile, the Doctor's bodyguard **Sharp** sends **Aurora**, who came ahead to scout spots for a comms station, off to see her family. She joined Rhodes Island through the Silverash clan's talent fostering program, so this is her first time home in years. 'Nothing's more important than family.'

And so the train sets off for the sacred mountain. Ensia rattles off the name of every peak outside the window without a break, while **Weiss** (Courier), who serves the Silverash clan, listens with a smile, now and then gazing into the distance with a troubled look. Sharp, for his part, is busy being amazed at how rich Kjerag's internet content turns out to be.

blocks.cap: The view from the train window, back when this looked like it'd be a pretty nice trip.

blocks.x: 2. They Wanted the Land, So He Gave It to God

At the same moment, the Tri-Clan Council convenes atop **Mount Karlan**. Browntail head **Ratatos** and Paleroche head **Arctosz** sit on one side, Enciodes sits across from them, and in the middle is the **Great Elder** of the Vine-Bead Court.

blocks.cap: Anyone could tell whose side was whose. Enciodes, alone on the right.

blocks.x: On the agenda: punishing the Silverash clan. Karlan Trade had secretly expanded its mines right up to the foot of the sacred mountain and even attacked a survey team, so hand over the valleys and the mining regions. Enciodes points out that he has already dismissed **Gnosis**, the Chief Technology Officer behind it all, but Arctosz won't hear a word of it. That was your right-hand man's doing, he says.
So Enciodes meekly agrees to give up the land. Just not to the other two clans. To the Vine-Bead Court, and to the Saintess who speaks for Kjeragandr.
When Arctosz hits the roof, Enciodes drives the point home. 'Or do you think the Saintess is incapable of a fair ruling?'

No one in Kjerag can answer 'yes' to that. The Saintess **Enya**, who also happens to be Enciodes's own sister, is summoned. Arctosz declares he'd entrust her with his whole clan, and Ratatos bows her head as well. Enya calmly accepts the responsibility of leading Kjerag.

Outside the hall, meanwhile, the dismissed Gnosis silently endures the nobles' whispers. To **Monch**, who stays by his side, he lays out what's happening inside without even seeing it. 'Enciodes, so this is the step you took after all.'
3. VIP Treatment, Delivered in Custody

The transfer of power is set to take place during Kjerag's biggest festival, the **Grand Ceremony**, and Arctosz attaches one condition: the 'expert' Enciodes is bringing in to fill Gnosis's spot will be kept under his watch. And that expert? The Doctor, who has just stepped off the train without hearing a thing about any of this.

Soon Paleroche general **Gulo** shows up with soldiers in tow, looking for 'the one in the hood.' Ensia steps in to stop them, only to be told that this land just became the Vine-Bead Court's, and Enciodes signed off on it. She's left speechless, staring at Weiss, who knew all along and said nothing.

Then Enciodes's bodyguard **Degenbrecher** appears, and the soldiers part all on their own. The Doctor agrees to go along quietly, even thanking the 'Black Knight,' while Sharp just sighs. 'Can't be helped. Overtime again.'

Back at the manor, Degenbrecher reports that the Doctor didn't so much as blink. When she asks if he's just made himself another enemy, Enciodes shakes his head. The Doctor will become his ally. No, rather, he must become the Doctor's ally.

That same day, a Karlan Trade meeting formally announces Gnosis's dismissal. Gnosis, Enciodes's old friend who studied with him in Victoria for four years, snaps back that it was always his fate, then, to be used and thrown away, and storms out, slamming the door. No one saw the look on Enciodes's face in that moment.
Around then, the Doctor, 'escorted' to the Paleroche manor, gets locked in a guest room. And in that room, the voice from the market speaks up again. 'See? You got caught after all.'

The voice asks to be called **Kjera**, and when asked who she really is, she just laughs and says it's a secret. She has a 'friend' who wanted to change Kjerag but was blocked at every turn, she says, and then you happened to show up. The Doctor's answer is short. 'Come to mention it, maybe you can do me a favor.'
4. An Ambush at the Factory, a Bridge Hidden in the Mountain

The next day, word that the Doctor has been dragged off by the Paleroches cuts Aurora's vacation short. Sharp figures a few well-placed explosions would get them past the manor guards, and Aurora hurriedly talks him down. Just then, the Saintess's maid **Kjarr** pops up out of nowhere with a message from the Doctor.

Gnosis, meanwhile, is reaching out to the Browntail clan. His words to Ratatos's younger sister **Sciurus** are really meant for Ratatos, hiding behind the wall. The transfer of power is no compromise. The hint is the Grand Ceremony.
And Monch, Sciurus's most trusted subordinate, has been secretly taking orders from Gnosis.

Meanwhile, the Doctor begins the handover of the valley factories, accompanied by the minder, Paleroche general **Valais**, and Enciodes's secretary **Chester**. But in front of the factory, armed locals block the way. This foreigner, they say, has teamed up with Arctosz to shut the factory down for good.

When a brawl breaks out, Aurora throws the Doctor over her shoulder and bolts for the woods. The traces of whoever stirred up the locals point to the Browntails, but the Doctor suspects even that could be a trap. And among those caught is Aurora's own brother.

Admitting that the factory's safety problems are real, the Doctor asks Valais to let them go. Having watched the Doctor closely, Arctosz calls off the surveillance and swears before Kjeragandr that this attack was not the Paleroches' doing.

Around then, Gnosis takes Ratatos to an old road abandoned to the blizzards. A bridge hidden inside the cliffs juts out only when a train passes: a secret railway Enciodes has been using to bring in armed men and equipment out of Turicum's sight. Gnosis snaps his fingers, and the freight train on the bridge is torn apart by flames.

blocks.cap: With a snap of the young man's fingers, like a bonfire on a festival night.

blocks.x: Among the scattered cargo are Victorian-made military swords, and soon a masked unit appears. It's the private army Enciodes has been secretly raising, named after a legendary monster: the '**Tschäggättä**.' While Ratatos's soldiers capture them, Gnosis buries the evidence under an avalanche, and the two of them end up as accomplices in the same boat.
Yet when Enciodes hears the report, his reaction is a strange one. 'Of course Gnosis would pull off something like this.'
5. The Pilgrim Who Walked, the Saintess Who Took Up a Bow

On the eve of the Grand Ceremony, Enciodes sets out on foot from Turicum to the sacred mountain as a pilgrim. He follows the old tradition to the letter: not a sip of water, palms pressed together, head bowed. The people along the road who had been praying for his safety follow him, one by one, out into the snowfield.

Meanwhile, the Great Elder tells Enya that the Saintess's place is to sit and receive the prey. She refuses, saying she will take up a bow and join the hunt herself. Then, as her brother arrives on the stroke of the hour after walking for more than a day, she greets him with these words.
Whether your path is right or wrong, Kjerag has its own path to follow. No one may make decisions on behalf of all of Kjeragandr's people.

When the Holy Hunt begins, a herd of frenzied beasts crashes into the line. A silver arrow pierces the blizzard and strikes the beast right in front of a young warrior. The Saintess lowers her bow and walks forward with the two clans at either side, and the warriors cry out. 'For the Saintess!'

At the same moment, on another hunting ground, Enciodes is struck by an arrow from a hidden assassin. The assassin, striking while the beasts held his guards back, is Monch. As Enciodes cuts down incoming arrows with his cane, a warrior beside him reveals who he really is. It is Sharp, there on the Doctor's 'work.'
Cornered, Monch remembers Sciurus's voice. 'I knew you wouldn't lie to me!' Then, without hesitation, she throws herself off the cliff.

Enciodes is not surprised. Having said that whether the witness lives or dies doesn't matter, he carries on with the hunt, still bleeding. The red marks on the snow fade little by little, until they melt into white.

blocks.cap: No one tried to stop him. No one could.

blocks.x: 6. A Poisoned Cup at the Festival

The next day, rumors that Enciodes was attacked sweep across the festival square, and people begin to shout for the culprit to be caught. Watching the scene beside Kjarr, the Doctor murmurs that one other possibility still remains.

At last, the coronation begins. The Great Elder drains the wine offered by Valais of the Paleroches in one go, followed by a scarf from the Browntails and a dagger from the Silverashes. And the assassin Weiss brings in is Monch.

Monch stays silent to the end, but Sciurus bursts out. 'Monch is my subordinate!' By the time Ratatos shouts at her to be quiet, it is too late, and she reads her sister's silently moving lips. 'But I just wanted to do something for the Browntail clan!'

Then the Great Elder collapses, green liquid on his lips. Traces of poison turn up in the cup, and Enciodes points at Arctosz. The Paleroches, about to lose their privileges, conspired with Sciurus, he says. One went after him, the other after the Great Elder.
Then Gnosis emerges from among the Browntail people in the crowd, presses Ratatos, and gathers blue Arts to aim at Enciodes. Enciodes does not move. He only calls out a single name.

blocks.cap: "Time to rest, Gnosis."

blocks.x: With Gnosis subdued, Ratatos and Arctosz finally draw their swords. Enciodes orders Weiss to capture the two clan heads while keeping casualties to a minimum. It isn't time yet, he says.

The Doctor, meanwhile, realizes that everything, Gnosis's appearance included, is going according to Enciodes's plan, and orders Sharp to save the two clan heads. When Sharp asks why, given the danger, the Doctor has only one answer: to prevent a war, and to save lives.

Then Sharp appears before the two surrounded clan heads. He was one of the operators Courier was closest to at Rhodes Island, and when Weiss apologizes, he answers calmly that they are both just doing their jobs. Aurora guides the two heads out, but Sciurus's husband **Yucatan**, who had sent her ahead, is captured by Weiss.
Once the chaos settles, Enya returns to the Vine-Bead Court without resistance. At some point, she had come to know that all of this was a script her brother had written.

blocks.cap: Grief, resentment, and anger. Her gaze brushed past the Doctor at Kjarr's side.

blocks.x: **Matterhorn** of the Silverash clan avoids her eyes. Enciodes declares the two clan heads traitors, and it is his name, not the Saintess's, that rings out across the square.
The bell tolling from the summit does not sound like the Saintess's transfer of power. It sounds like an announcement that change has come.
7. It Was a Play from the Start

Meanwhile, on his way back to his own lands, Arctosz finds Valais blocking the road at the head of an army. Long ago, Valais's father was wounded shielding Arctosz during a Holy Hunt. Arctosz fed him the 'elixir' the Great Elder brought with his own hands, and he never got up again. The Great Elder called it the poison of the Tschäggättä, a judgment passed on one who had clashed with the Vine-Bead Court.

The wine Valais offered on coronation day held that very elixir, which had gone missing that day. Valais had heard this 'reality' from someone who called himself a researcher and was only half convinced, but became certain the moment the Great Elder collapsed. She bears no grudge, Valais says, but Kjerag needs change, and with that, she bars her old master's way.

Around then, Gnosis, locked in a cell, thinks back to his childhood. On the day he left Kjerag, after his parents were accused of killing Enciodes's parents, the two of them promised to make Kjerag the mightiest nation in the world. And when they met again in Victoria, Enciodes held out his hand, saying the age when one could live behind locked doors was over.

Now that same Enciodes comes to the cell, and the truth comes out. Their falling-out, Gnosis siding with Ratatos, the revolt on coronation day: all of it was a play the two of them had staged. Enciodes believed Kjerag would never accept power seized by violence alone, so it was Gnosis who volunteered to play the villain in his place.
Enciodes, I am not your chess piece. Much less your subordinate. I am your partner.

blocks.cap: "I am simply grateful that you are my friend."

blocks.x: Then a letter arrives from Ratatos. She will yield, so come to her, and she will tell him the truth about his parents' deaths as well. Gnosis calls it an obvious trap, but Enciodes says it is still worth going, and leaves him in command.

After Enciodes leaves, Gnosis visits the imprisoned Monch. Ever since Weiss, waiting at the foot of the cliff, rescued her, she had already guessed. If all of this was a play, then what role had she been given?

Gnosis tells her he gave her the most important role because he trusted her completely, and Monch finally asks. 'Why... why couldn't you trust me...' After he leaves, she repeats to herself: this time too, can I trust Sir Gnosis?
8. The Room Grandfather Built

A little earlier, Ratatos had slipped past a trap laid by a retainer who meant to sell her out to Enciodes. When Sciurus insists on going to take the blame alone, Ratatos stops her with a smile and sends her home. This is the same little sister who, as a child, threw a fit saying she'd be clan head herself so her big sister wouldn't get scolded.

The appointed meeting place is a Browntail villa standing on what was once Edelweiss land. Enciodes leaves Degenbrecher outside and comes in alone, and Ratatos tells him the truth. His parents really did die in a train accident, and her grandfather, Luca Browntail, pinned the blame on the Edelweiss family.

But her grandfather had meant to kill them all along, and this very room was built to lure them in and burn them. Arctosz's father had looked the other way. Ratatos twists the armrest; metal plates seal the windows, and the room catches fire.

blocks.cap: In the room her grandfather built for Enciodes's parents, the granddaughter and Enciodes sit face to face.

blocks.x: Amid the flames, Ratatos shows her true feelings for the first time. She had believed Enciodes's foreign trade would bind the three clans, which were drifting apart like strangers, back together. But seeing the munitions factories he was secretly building frightened her. It looked as if he meant to make Kjerag his own, or someone else's.
Enciodes answers just as honestly. Victoria, Columbia, Kazimierz: if none of them is coming for Kjerag now, it is only because they have no need to yet. Kjerag is out of time.
At that moment outside, Sciurus clings to the door, wailing. 'Ratatos! ...Sis!!' Degenbrecher pushes the pleading woman aside and cuts through the thick wall as if it were tofu, bringing it down.

Some time later, when Ratatos comes to, Enciodes silently drapes his own coat over her and leaves. But the eyes of the Browntail people around her are already full of hostility, and Ratatos murmurs. 'I've lost. Completely.'
Then Sharp appears before Ratatos. The Doctor would like to invite her for a talk, he says.
9. Breaking the Ice
Around then, Enya begins to act at the Vine-Bead Court. Before the confined elders muttering among themselves, she declares that until the Great Elder wakes, she will decide the Court's affairs.

Meanwhile, the Doctor brings Arctosz and Ratatos together. They cannot win, but they can rescue the Saintess. The plan is to use Yucatan's rescue as bait to draw the Silverashes' attention, and send Arctosz to the sacred mountain through the gap. Ratatos is stunned when Sharp says he will hold off Degenbrecher for ten minutes, and as she is worn out, Sciurus steps up in her place.

Aurora, meanwhile, brings the Doctor's request to Ensia, who is confined at the manor: climb the sacred mountain and stay by her sister's side. Chester defies his master's orders to let her go, thinking to himself that it has been far too long since he saw these siblings together and smiling.

Around then, the Great Elder wakes and summons Enya. Faith is idleness, escapism, and stagnation, he says, but because no one could ever tear it down, Kjerag has endured for a thousand years. Go and defeat Enciodes, he tells her, gripping her wrist.
Enya pries his fingers away one by one. Faith stood still only because the Vine-Bead Court held it still for a thousand years, she says. Nothing was ever meant to be. It simply has never changed yet.
I am the Saintess. Not the Saintess of the Vine-Bead Court, but the Saintess of Kjerag.
As she walks out without looking back, the Great Elder reaches after her, then lets his hand fall weakly. In the end, he could hold on to nothing.

Then the Doctor's plan goes into motion. While Gulo seizes the train station and blocks the tracks, and Sciurus sets the granary ablaze to rescue Yucatan, Arctosz's forces circle around the snowy hunting grounds and break through at the foot of the mountain.
Meanwhile, Ensia is climbing the cliffs behind the sacred mountain alone. Bringing her sister, who never much cared for mountains, back down from the summit had long been her dream.

blocks.cap: Drifting snow lashed her face, leaving traces like streaks of tears.

blocks.x: Ensia knew, really. That she could not rescue her sister from the mountain. That she could not mend what lay between her brother and sister. Even so, she drove her ice axe into the rock.

At the same moment, Degenbrecher comes to stop the hooded 'Doctor,' and the hood comes off. It is Sharp. As the Black Knight draws her twin blades, Sharp sets down his shield and grips his sword in both hands.
10. The Day the Clouds Parted

At last, Ensia reaches the clifftop and bursts into the Vine-Bead Court. Enya, thinking it a hallucination, reaches out a trembling hand. Before it can reach her, her little sister throws herself into her arms.

Ensia says the Doctor sent her to protect her sister, and to run away with her if need be. Hearing this, Enya realizes that both the one who must protect and the one who must fight back are herself. And she asks her little sister: 'Stay here with me.'

On the mountain path, meanwhile, just as Arctosz is about to be trapped in Matterhorn's encirclement, Aurora and the real Doctor arrive at his side, and Enciodes shows himself as well. Arctosz cries out, and the Paleroche warriors answer with a roar. 'Topple Enciodes, rescue the Saintess!'

blocks.cap: Defending Kjerag from enemies without. The Paleroches' age-old duty.

blocks.x: Then Enya rings a clear bell, and everyone who had been blocking her way collapses to the floor, all except Ensia. Enya leaves the rest to Kjarr and begins her descent of the mountain.

Left alone, Kjarr speaks to herself in the silent corridor. At every Saintess selection, she had disguised herself as a maid to watch over the girls. Enya, she says, was a child who climbed through the blizzard carrying disappointment and anger, not any wish to become the Saintess.
Congratulations, my child and my envoy, my friend, my sister.
Kjarr, who says she once rashly branded this land with her mark, lightly claps her hands twice. And everything changes.
Around then, Sharp, who has lost all feeling in his right hand, falls to Degenbrecher, yet remains calm. Holding her off was all the mission required, and in that, it had succeeded.
And the blizzard stopped.

blocks.cap: "A miracle... This is a miracle."

blocks.x: The dark clouds part to either side, and the Saintess walks down through the light. Gulo and Valais, Yucatan and Weiss, all stop fighting and look up at the sky. To every one of them, it was a miracle.
At that moment, in the Vine-Bead Court, Kjarr sits beside the bedridden Great Elder and whispers. 'Sweet dreams, Great Elder. You've worked hard.'

Meanwhile, holding Ensia, who says she is scared, Enya tells her: it's all right, your big sister will protect Kjerag. Every soldier on the mountain path lays down their weapons, and Arctosz is the first to kneel before the Saintess.
Before that sight, Gnosis asks Enciodes whether he has regrets. Enciodes answers that today, perhaps not entirely. Then he too walks out through the crowd and kneels before the Saintess.
Epilogue — A Draw

That day, Enya addresses all the people of Kjerag. Kjeragandr is a mother who cannot bear to see her children stand still, she says, so do not cling to tradition and fear what is new. The day she proclaimed that even foreigners may believe in Kjeragandr became Kjerag's national religious day.

Some time later, Enciodes plays chess with the Doctor. He confides that the valley affair was only ever bait that could fail without consequence, and that Gnosis is a friend who will never betray him, even without sharing information. The game ends in a draw.

blocks.cap: "Sometimes, a draw is a great victory. And other times, a draw is a crushing defeat."

blocks.x: His victory, he says, is assured. It is only that the Doctor opened up an entirely different possibility for that victory.

Arctosz takes responsibility for poisoning the Great Elder, steps down as clan head, and offers the Paleroche lands to the Saintess. The Browntails agree to a subordination agreement with the Silverashes. And Enciodes promises that the Doctor's name will not remain in any record of these events.

Enya, meanwhile, asks Kjarr whether her becoming leader was also Kjeragandr's will. Told that Kjeragandr has never once interfered with a Saintess's will, Enya makes a single wish. As in the old stories, she does not want to lose Kjarr as the price of her answer, so please, stay on as her maid.
Kjarr bursts out laughing and promises. So long as Enya does not lose the ideals she holds today, she will remain her head maid forever.

And Gnosis decides to go to Rhodes Island as Enciodes's representative. Before leaving, he visits Monch's room and finds it empty, with only the knife he once gave her lying on the table. Gnosis silently takes it and walks out the door.

On the day they leave Kjerag, that same merchant in Turicum is now selling carefully crafted Saintess souvenirs. Ensia stops in front of a painting hanging in the shop. It shows Enya and Enciodes shaking hands across a table.

Ensia confides to the Doctor that she didn't buy it. The painting is a lie. In the end, her brother only just barely gave her sister one step. Both of them followed their own beliefs, and the Doctor only nudged them along, a little at a time.
My other belief won't change easily either. Someday, I'm going to put things between my brother and sister back the way they used to be.

They said even the tiniest external force could set off an avalanche that swallows Kjerag. In the end, that force set off no avalanche. It only nudged the siblings to open Kjerag's doors, each by their own beliefs. The trials Kjerag must face may only just be beginning.

act13side.tagline: The Radiant Knight, once exiled, returns to a Major held in the merchants' grip and wins it, defeating even the hero of the Infected — only for that victory, too, to be put to use by the merchants. Even so, the knight chooses to remain a lighthouse.

chars.name: Margaret
chars.desc: Eldest daughter of the Nearl family and the youngest champion in the Major's history. Exiled six years ago for being Infected, she has come back home · Operator Nearl the Radiant Knight

chars.name: Maria
chars.desc: Margaret's younger sister. The Nearl family's engineer, she maintains her sister's weapons and armor herself.

chars.name: Młynar
chars.desc: Uncle to Margaret and Maria. He has stepped away from knighthood and lives as a company employee · Operator Młynar

chars.name: Zofia
chars.desc: Aunt to Margaret and Maria. A competition knight who made her name as 'the Whislash Knight' · Operator Whislash

chars.name: Vogelweide
chars.desc: A veteran campaign knight close to the Nearl family. A regular at the neighborhood bar.

chars.name: Sona
chars.desc: Leader of the Pinus Sylvestris Knightclub, a knightclub of Infected knights · Operator Flametail

chars.name: Justyna
chars.desc: An Infected sharpshooter of the Pinus Sylvestris Knightclub. She grew up on the legend of the Radiant Knight · Operator Fartooth

chars.name: Iwona
chars.desc: A hot-tempered Kuranta knight of the Pinus Sylvestris Knightclub. She does not hesitate to take on the Armorless Union head-on · Operator Wild Mane

chars.name: Greynuty
chars.desc: An Infected knight of the Pinus Sylvestris Knightclub and Sona's longtime comrade-in-arms · Operator Ashlock

chars.name: Szewczyk
chars.desc: A competition knight targeted by the General Chamber of Commerce. He is searching for his missing wife and child.

chars.name: Viviana
chars.desc: A Grand Knight from Leithanien, and one of the most popular knights in Kazimierz · Operator Viviana

chars.name: Tola
chars.desc: A mysterious newcomer with neither knightclub nor sponsor. A Kuranta who sings in an ancient tongue.

chars.name: Dikaiopolis
chars.desc: An Infected knight from Minos and champion of the previous Major. He is called 'the hero of the Infected.'

chars.name: Toland
chars.desc: A Sarkaz bounty hunter who has turned up in Kawalerielki. He and Młynar go back a long way.

chars.name: Ioleta Russell
chars.desc: Grandmaster of the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi. A veteran who rose from the ranks of the campaign knights.

chars.name: McKee
chars.desc: A spokesman for the General Chamber of Commerce. He handles the Candle Knight's schedule and contracts.

chars.name: Malkiewicz
chars.desc: A man abruptly made a spokesman for the General Chamber of Commerce, succeeding the dismissed Czarny.

chars.name: Roy
chars.desc: A 'Lazurite,' one of the Armorless Union's executives. He acts flippant, but his true intentions are impossible to read.

chars.name: Monique
chars.desc: A 'Lazurite,' one of the Armorless Union's executives. An archer from Victoria.

chars.name: Platinum
chars.desc: An Armorless Union killer. A Pegasus archer assigned to hunting down the Infected.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: Leader of Rhodes Island. She has come to Kazimierz under a medical contract for the Infected.

chars.name: Gravel
chars.desc: A fourth-order campaign knight assigned by the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi to the Doctor of Rhodes Island. She serves as the Doctor's bodyguard.

chars.name: Shining
chars.desc: A Sarkaz doctor of Rhodes Island who came to Kazimierz with Margaret.

chars.name: Nightingale
chars.desc: A Sarkaz doctor of Rhodes Island who came to Kazimierz with Margaret. Margaret calls her 'Liz.'

terms.name: Kawalerielki
terms.desc: A Grand Knight Territory of Kazimierz. Every few years it absorbs three nomadic cities, and the knights' special tournament, the Major, is held there.

terms.name: General Chamber of Commerce
terms.desc: The merchants' alliance that hosts Kazimierz's knight sports. Through its spokespeople, it has a hand in every matter of the Major, large or small.

terms.name: Adeptus Sprawiedliwi
terms.desc: A political faction of campaign knights and the nobility, locked in a long-running power struggle with the General Chamber of Commerce.

terms.name: campaign knight
terms.desc: Kazimierz's soldier-knights who fight on the battlefield, as distinct from the competition knights of the arena.

terms.name: National Council
terms.desc: The body responsible for Kazimierz's laws and trials.

terms.name: Area 0
terms.desc: A closed mobile platform attached to the Infected treatment and housing center. Many doubt that treatment is all that happens there.

terms.name: Armorless Union
terms.desc: An assassination organization secretly employed by the General Chamber of Commerce. Executives called 'Lazurites' direct its operations.

terms.name: Darksteel
terms.desc: A name for the Armorless Union's legendary founders — or for whatever stands at its apex. No one knows what it really is.

terms.name: Pinus Sylvestris Knightclub
terms.desc: A knightclub formed by Infected knights. It looks after the Infected hiding in the cracks of the city.

terms.name: Great Kawalerielki Separation
terms.desc: An incident three years ago, on the eve of the Major, when the core power reactor failed and the territory's sectors broke away.

terms.name: Wall of Champions
terms.desc: An exhibition hall displaying portraits of every Major champion. The awards ceremony is held there.

terms.name: Nightzmora
terms.desc: A Kuranta clan said to have overthrown the old nation of the Pegasi. Now thought to survive only in legend.

terms.name: Kheshig
