It is said that one who loses one's home becomes nothing at all. But when her home finally came to find her, Skadi left behind a song and a promise in a ruined tavern, and went on her way. Home lies behind. The path lies ahead.

act18d0.tagline: A power broker of Sargon's black market, his eye caught by a single signature on a Rhodes Island contract, calls in a promise of one gold coin deferred twenty-two years ago. From desert to snowfield, and on to the eve of a blizzard. The long road one person has walked.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: A doctor of Rhodes Island. Together with the strange creature Mon3tr, she has left her footprints across the continent.

chars.name: Heavyrain
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator. A stickler for principle, sent to deal with the Sargon black market.

chars.name: Sesa
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator, known as 'Bridge' in his days as an armaments tuner. He is pursuing the truth behind his brother's death.

chars.name: Elliot
chars.desc: A young researcher at the Blaine Formative Technologies Research Institute in Columbia, and assistant to Professor Thorne.

chars.name: Lillia
chars.desc: A medical researcher formerly of the Chernobog research institute. She lost her husband in the institute's 'accident.'

chars.name: Grand Duke Vanya
chars.desc: Former staff officer of the Ursus Fourth Army. A Grand Duke named as the likely mastermind behind the 'Sarcophagus Incident.'

chars.name: Witte
chars.desc: Viscount Islam Witte, Ursus's new Minister of Finance. An up-and-coming noble in the Emperor's favor.

chars.name: Heidi
chars.desc: Daughter of Thomson, a writer and merchant of Toron in Victoria. She slips into a New Year's party secretly wearing her mother's clothes.

chars.name: Count Vincent
chars.desc: Count of Toron County on the Victorian frontier, and master of the manor hosting the New Year's Eve party.

chars.name: Isin
chars.desc: A Savra fortune teller who calls himself 'Old Isin.' For over a century he has been searching for his lost memories.

chars.name: Passenger
chars.desc: A newcomer who has just signed a contract with Rhodes Island.

terms.name: Sand Soldier
terms.desc: The codename used by the foremost information broker of the Reefsteep Black Market. Twenty-two years ago, it was the operation codename of a Columbian unit sent into Sargon.

terms.name: Reefsteep
terms.desc: A former nomadic city in Sargon's Ibut region. Its name now survives only in a black market and a town.

terms.name: Sarcophagus Incident
terms.desc: A catastrophe at the Chernobog research institute. Officially recorded as an 'experimental accident.'

terms.name: Emperor's Blade
terms.desc: The royal guard of the Ursus Emperor. They wield power beyond human understanding.

blocks.x: The present day, the Ibut region of central Sargon. Rhodes Island's **Heavyrain** and **Sesa** had come to a meeting point in a nameless town to bring in medical research materials banned in Columbia, but the operators sent ahead of them had gone silent.

The one who appeared was the foremost information broker of the Reefsteep Black Market, codename **'Sand Soldier'**. He was holding the operators, yet he said he had no interest in the costly materials. What he wanted to know about was a single signature on the trade contract.
The signature was **Kal'tsit**'s. Plenty of people used that name, he said, and over the years he had turned up the wrong person more times than he could count. Then Sand Soldier asked:
Tell me, what kind of place is Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals?
And so the story goes back twenty-two years, into the sandstorms of that same Ibut.
Twenty-Two Years Ago: The Boy Who Carried a Corpse

The town of Redhorn in Ibut was burning. Mercenary units had converged on the tiny town, dragging even its civilians into the fighting, and what they were after was a single silver case belonging to the 'Sand Soldier' unit from Columbia.

blocks.cap: Redhorn, twenty-two years ago. A single silver case turned the town into a battlefield.

blocks.x: The unit's only survivor was a Liberi boy. Carrying an adult's body on his back, he fled through the collapsed houses, clinging to the corpse and sobbing that the bleeding would not stop, that there was still so much he had not been taught.
When a mercenary finally caught him and took the case, an unknown creature appeared and ran the mercenary through. Behind it, a woman called the boy by name. "Elliot, it's all right now."

The boy was **Elliot Glover**, a young researcher at Columbia's Blaine Formative Technologies Research Institute. The body on his back was his mentor, Professor Thorne, and the case held plans and samples made by the institute.
To the woman who said she had come to protect him, Elliot shouted that it was the case she meant to protect, not him. Not his teacher, either.

Telling him not to let the professor's sacrifice be in vain, the woman had him lay the body down. The creature dug into the sand, and the woman offered a prayer in an ancient Vouivran tongue. For that moment, even the shelling seemed to stop.
Only then did Elliot remember. Long ago his teacher had introduced him to a researcher he had taken for a pure theorist. Her name was Kal'tsit.
Even after Kal'tsit stepped out the door, Elliot stared blankly at the half-dug ground where his teacher lay, grieving that he lacked even the means to cremate the body.
The Operations Adviser Had Already Counted on Betrayal

Kal'tsit was an operations adviser for the Westin Security Company, a Columbian mercenary firm. When she joined the Riverblade Squad with Elliot and the case, the convoy ground to a halt in the middle of the desert, and soon the Stouthammer Squad, supposedly on their side, fell upon them.
Fewer than twenty survivors retreated into a cave afterward, and there Kal'tsit laid out the whole game before the squad captain.

blocks.cap: The cave where the Riverblade Squad took shelter. Dozens of their comrades were left behind in the desert.

blocks.x: The Columbian military had coerced the institute's shareholders into funneling the goods to an Ameer of Sargon, meaning to use that spark to start a war in Ibut. The Bureau, seeking to prevent this, had hired mercenaries to recover the case, but the military had already bought off the Stouthammer Squad.
Nor was the thing in the case a 'new energy engine.' It was an Arts prototype capable of turning half of Sargon's jungles into wasteland.
The squad captain had also received secret orders from the company to eliminate Kal'tsit. When at last he asked what she was doing all this for, Kal'tsit answered.
And war will bring ruin. I simply try to stop this all from coming, despite how weak my influence is.

When the captain lowered his weapon, Kal'tsit handed him a map marked with towns and Messenger stations, opening a route for the squad to escape to Minos. She herself set off separately, taking Elliot with her.
But soon after Kal'tsit left, Sarkaz mercenaries attacked the cave.

Meanwhile, walking through the desert, Kal'tsit told Elliot to hand over the case. When he refused to give up the institute's life's work, she told him that Professor Thorne had known the research could be put to other ends.

Elliot remembered the day they first came to Sargon, when the professor had murmured that if the day ever came when their research was used against its original purpose, they would have to stop it, whatever it took.

Kal'tsit decided to take Elliot with her, saying she did not want to watch another young person who knew the truth die before her eyes. When he asked who she really was, she answered only this: Kal'tsit, adviser and Arts instructor for the Westin Security Company of Columbia.
In the present, Sand Soldier repeated the name on the contract. She had moved between Columbia and Sargon to stop a war, but no one knows how long a road she has walked, or where she will go next.
Seventeen Years Ago: The Student Who Sought a Dead Director

Five years later, Ursus. In a village 147 km northwest of the route of the nomadic city Chernobog, Kal'tsit was living as a doctor the villagers quietly sheltered. Her former student **Lillia** came to find her, and together they fought for an old man stricken with acute Oripathy. He pulled through, but he was now Infected.

blocks.cap: A village 147 km northwest of Chernobog's route.

blocks.x: On the snowy road out of the village, Lillia finally spoke. Since the **Sarcophagus Incident** at the Chernobog research institute three years earlier, she had believed its director, Kal'tsit, to be dead. This was their first meeting since.
According to the official list, no one had left the institute alive, yet every victim's family had received anonymous help and a warning. Lillia had followed those traces all the way here.

That night at the institute, Lillia's husband Astrov had been shot through the neck by the first arrow loosed by an agent of the Fourth Army. Leaving their daughter Louisa, who could not yet speak or walk, with a friend, she was preparing her revenge.

Her target was **Grand Duke Vanya**, former staff officer of the Fourth Army and named as a likely mastermind of the Sarcophagus Incident. The Grand Duke spent every winter at the Pine Valley Retreat, and Lillia had bribed its head of security, soon to retire, to open a way in.
Kal'tsit tried to dissuade her: killing one old Grand Duke would mean nothing. Lillia answered that what she wanted was not righteous judgment but private retribution.
Louisa never even learned to say 'papa.'

And so a new doctor, 'Dr. Louisa,' and a Feline servant named Kal'tsit arrived at the Pine Valley Retreat. Lillia used her daughter's name as an alias. Kal'tsit kept her own, serving coffee and taking an old soldier's curses.

One day, alone with her on a balcony, Kal'tsit asked what she would do once the Grand Duke was dead. Lillia said she would return to Chernobog and settle accounts with Sergei, the colleague her husband had trusted and the man who betrayed him, and with Marquess Boris as well.
She knew she was digging her own grave, Lillia said, and she left only one request: look after her daughter Louisa, and do not let the next generation be crushed under hatred.
Kal'tsit promised. On his last night, before he left suddenly for the institute, Astrov had said he hoped Director Kal'tsit would be their daughter's teacher once she was old enough for school.
That day, an unexpected guest arrived at the retreat: Viscount **Islam Witte**, Ursus's new Minister of Finance and a favorite of the Emperor.
Thirteen Years Ago: The Cleric on a Snowy Night
Four years later, Toron County on the Victorian frontier. Guests gathered at **Count Vincent**'s manor on New Year's Eve, and among them was a girl secretly wearing her mother's clothes.

The girl was **Heidi**, daughter of Thomson, a renowned writer and wealthy merchant of Toron. The guest the Count most awaited that night was the Laterano cleric who had cured his wife's fever the year before, a woman, and a rare Feline at that.
At last the cleric Kal'tsit arrived. Heidi stumbled even over her own name.
Talk at the party drifted to Londinium, to Leithanien, and then to Ursus. When Heidi said she was interested in Ursus, Kal'tsit told her the story of an army that vanished over a single bottle.
It was the story of 'the Great Rebellion': one drunken soldier's bottle of vodka escalated into fighting between armies, until the Sixth Army vanished without a trace.

Kal'tsit said she would not claim that this was Ursus. But when she said that what she had seen was the aftermath of the Great Rebellion, an age on the brink of collapse, Heidi asked whether such an age would come to Victoria too. Kal'tsit answered that she could make no promises.

blocks.cap: The New Year's party at the Vincent Manor.

blocks.x: Then, alone together in the snow-covered garden, Heidi's carefree step came to a halt. Her father Thomson ran an intelligence network linking Messengers, laborers, and people of conviction across Victoria, and Heidi was the courier who had come to deliver its letters to Kal'tsit.
There are two letters in all. One from Victoria, and the other from 'Kazdel'...
Pine Lily: The Grand Duke's Last Afternoon

Back to seventeen years ago, at Pine Valley. When word came that the Grand Duke, unnerved by the Finance Minister's visit, would leave his quarters for once, Lillia moved the plan set for the following week up to that very day.

Kal'tsit urged her to go with her to Victoria by way of Siracusa, but Lillia shook her head. She could not allow a traitor to tread on the bloodstains her husband had left behind, not for a single second.

The drug Kal'tsit had prepared was called 'Eternal Rest.' That afternoon, the guards kept Dr. Lillia waiting outside the door and let in only the servant Kal'tsit, warning that if she did not come out within ten minutes, she would not leave alive.

At one end of the balcony, where the light did not reach, an old man lay. Grand Duke Vanya, blind since the month before, felt Kal'tsit's face with his fingers and told her she had wasted her effort. He would die today or tomorrow anyway.

The Grand Duke went through who might have sent her, one by one. If not the Finance Minister, and not the old cowards of the army, then perhaps His Majesty. One night, the Emperor's Blade had held a sword to his throat from barely an arm's length away.

Using a communicator Kal'tsit had found for him, the Grand Duke ordered the guards to keep out. Then the name brought back a memory: the director of the institute who had died in the flames at Chernobog that day had also been called Kal'tsit.
When Kal'tsit injected the drug, the Grand Duke asked how much time he had left. Told fifteen minutes, he asked whether the view before them was beautiful.

blocks.cap: "All the land is budding, and the sunshine will feed it, filling it with hope."

blocks.x: As a young man, wounded in the leg and struck on the head in battle against Kazimierz, he had crawled into a field of flowers and lost consciousness. After the war he brought those seeds back from the frontier, gave the flower a new name, and made it the flower of his city. That name was **Pine Lily**.
But the seeds he sowed here never sprouted. When the Grand Duke said he loved the land of Ursus, Kal'tsit answered that the poor and the Infected had become that land's fertilizer.
The Grand Duke said he was not asking for forgiveness. Murmuring that he wished to see pine lilies once more, he let out a long breath and said the sun was very warm.

Kal'tsit bid him farewell in the Ursus tongue, saying she hoped Ursus would forget him. With the word 'motherland' as his last, the Grand Duke fell asleep. It was a sleep from which he would never wake.

At the same moment, in the dining hall, the old friend Witte had come to visit cut off his own finger with a fruit knife. Unlike the fingers the war had taken, this was the only flesh of his he had ever severed by his own will, and he asked that it be buried in the soil of Deity Grypherburg.
Under cover of that commotion, Kal'tsit and Lillia slipped out of the retreat. When Lillia thanked her, Kal'tsit replied that it was not over yet. One day, they might have to face this empire again.
The Present: Sand Soldier's Offer
Back in present-day Ibut. The captured operators were all unharmed, but Heavyrain did not trust Sand Soldier.

Asked his purpose, Sand Soldier admitted that the Ameer of Ibut, who died three years ago in the great fire that burned Redhorn, had been his final quarry. Over twenty-odd years he had removed everyone tied to the affair, one by one. Now he wanted to leave this sickening land and start anew.

He revealed that he was Infected. He would give up all his wealth and connections, which rivaled an Ameer's, if Rhodes Island would treat him, and if they would let him meet Kal'tsit, the one who had saved his life.
Learning that Sesa was hunting the head of the Columbian military lab tied to his brother's death, he offered to help with that investigation as well.

Last of all, Sand Soldier brought up a name: Isin. Isin no longer existed, he said, but he hoped Kal'tsit would remember the promise. Then he asked whether she had happened to give them an ancient Sargonian gold coin. Heavyrain was left without words.

Just then came a report that a large, suspicious force was approaching the town. Before deciding, Sesa asked why, if he only needed to kill the Ameer, he had evacuated the people and then burned the whole town to ashes.
It was a long overdue cremation, nothing more.

Not long after, the war zone of Ibut was thick with the smell of burning. The weapons of the pursuing mercenaries had been made by Sand Soldier, and the arms he had tampered with in advance exploded in their hands.

blocks.cap: The war zone of Ibut. The smell of burning has not cleared.

blocks.x: In his hardest times, Sand Soldier said, he often thought back to that day. How Kal'tsit fought. How she controlled everything, as if looking down from above the clouds.
A Gold Coin, Twenty-Two Years Later

Back to twenty-two years ago. After more than seven hours walking the desert, Kal'tsit and Elliot reached the market towns that drift across the wastes. With a Sargonian gold coin in hand, Kal'tsit searched the crowds for the scattered remnants of 'Reefsteep.'
A bounty hunter from Vouivre lunged at them and fell to Mon3tr. Afterward, in the middle of the market, Kal'tsit stopped before a strange fortune teller.

blocks.cap: The strange fortune teller in the market. "Do you wish to take a peek at what destiny has laid out before you?"

blocks.x: The old Savra, who called himself 'Old Isin,' was being driven off by the townsfolk as a swindler. At dusk, Kal'tsit recited an old epic to him in Sargonian.

Did he remember the dazzling city that had stood in this desert 150 years ago? When Kal'tsit said the old Padishah had given this land a name that did not belong to Sargon, Isin spoke it aloud. **Reefsteep**.

Isin said he would get them out of Sargon so that not even the Padishah could find their trail. The price was a single gold coin, but he asked for it not now but twenty-two years from now, and begged her to remember the promise.

That night they stayed in an abandoned garden where those with nowhere to go lived together: 'the Sleeping Sargon.' Isin called the Mon3tr at Kal'tsit's side a beautiful creature, and saw that the two of them had walked a very long road together.
Lady Kal'tsit, is this glory of yours replete with nothing but loneliness?
Kal'tsit answered that loneliness had no bearing on her work, and went out to deal with their pursuers.

Waiting for her in the desert was a unit of Sarkaz mercenaries hired by Padishah Murad to retrieve the case. Most had been Infected from birth and had lived in Sargon's back alleys with their horns hidden. Even when Kal'tsit addressed him in an old Sarkaz tribal tongue, their leader said he had no intention of pledging loyalty to a Kazdel he had never seen.
Saying that a Sarkaz must never hold any dream, he ordered the charge.
When the fight was over, the fallen leader asked what that Kazdel she spoke of looked like now. Kal'tsit answered that it was still a mess, but the Sarkaz were building a home there.
The 'Teekaz' deserve a home.
He had never once left Sargon. Murmuring that it had a nice ring to it, he breathed his last.
The Shattered Crystal

Then they entered the Reefsteep Black Market. Someone approached offering 400 gold coins for the case, and Isin freely brought out the pure gold he had hoarded in his old home to prepare for the journey.

blocks.cap: The Reefsteep Black Market. The liveliest place in Ibut.

blocks.x: That night Elliot asked Kal'tsit whether, if he handed over the case, she would take revenge for them. Then he added that he had never needed the case in the first place. He remembered everything and could reproduce the results.

The day before they left, Isin, who had suffered for over a century unable to recall his old master's words, described a dream of soldiers racing toward the horizon across an endlessly scorching land. Kal'tsit recognized it as the conquest of the Kheshigs of Nightzmora more than a thousand years ago, and went on to work out that the Padishah of Reefsteep whom Isin had served was a Kuranta of Nightzmoran blood.
Isin finally remembered that he had been neither guardian nor confidant, only one among countless subjects. Sobbing, he asked to be left alone.
That same night, Kal'tsit handed the decision to Elliot. Now that they were leaving Sargon, the case no longer meant anything. What to do with it was his to decide.

When he opened the case, a bluish Originium crystal gave off light. Kal'tsit warned that it was a special crystal found only near a certain Sarkaz ruin, and that breaking it would expose him to Oripathy.
Elliot broke the crystal.
As the light died down, Elliot shouted. Did she hate the Infected? Now he would no longer owe her anything, would he?
Kal'tsit answered. I'm Infected too.
Writhing with acute infection, Elliot said he liked this fate better. Then he asked:
Do you really think you can decide somebody else's fate for them?
Kal'tsit said she had never thought so. Elliot answered that she was doing it all the same. Though no one could ever have told her she was wrong.

The next day, before a back route out of the black market known only to Isin, Kal'tsit asked Elliot whether he would come with her or stay. No one could decide another's fate, she said, so she could not decide his future either.

blocks.cap: The black market's back route, known only to Isin. Kal'tsit asked Elliot whether he would come with her.

blocks.x: Elliot said he would stay. The war had already begun, and he would track down those who had plotted it, one by one, from Sargon to Columbia. Isin, saying there was nothing wrong with leaving an ember behind, agreed to help him.
When Elliot said it was time to part, Isin spoke to Kal'tsit's back as she left.
Lady Kal'tsit, in some twenty years you will return with a gold coin to take away with you this helpless soul.
Kal'tsit walked out into the desert with only Mon3tr.
Black Snow

Back to thirteen years ago, in the garden of the Vincent Manor. Kal'tsit told Heidi that the Count, who looked like a feeble man who did nothing but throw parties, was in fact keeping the peace of Toron from behind that facade.

The letter from Kazdel had been handed to Thomson directly by a Sarkaz Messenger. The Messenger did not survive, and Thomson, not knowing how to honor a Sarkaz hero, cremated him and scattered his ashes along a nomadic city's route.
Kal'tsit said she could not reveal his name, but she would carry his story home. He would not be forgotten.
Heading back inside, Heidi took Kal'tsit's arm, saying it would keep them from drawing suspicion. Outside the window, heavy snow was falling.

blocks.cap: Heidi and Kal'tsit by a window as heavy snow falls.

blocks.x: Then Kal'tsit, looking out the window, murmured: black snow.

Kal'tsit told Heidi to quietly take control of the party and keep anyone from approaching the garden. If she did not come back, Heidi and her father were to bury the truth and dig no further. This was a warning, she said, and an order.
Out of the darkness of the garden emerged a royal guard of Ursus: the **Emperor's Blade**. Everyone who had let the traitor who harmed the Grand Duke escape had been sentenced, he said.
Kal'tsit knew that the guard carried within him a fragment of power left by a demon. The Blade drew his sword, saying he would start by making her confess how she knew that secret.

blocks.cap: "Avoid the black mist. That's not mist at all."

blocks.x: By the end of the fight both were badly wounded, and Kal'tsit kept herself going by injecting herself with a drug. Cracks began to spread across the Blade's mask.

Kal'tsit tried to persuade him. Had the Grand Duke died at the end of a political struggle, it would have sown the seeds of a new rebellion. But if it were the work of an ordinary assassin with a grudge, his crimes would be quietly buried. The young Emperor did not even know what had happened at Pine Valley.

The Blade raged that this was sophistry, but in the end he stood down. Asked how long she had lived and what she truly was, Kal'tsit answered that she was merely the Grand Duke's personal physician. The Blade left, saying they would meet again.

Once the Blade had gone, Kal'tsit had Mon3tr bring back two wild beasts and made the signs of the fight look like an animal attack. Then she asked Heidi to find a Messenger who could reach Sami. If that woman was still alive, she said, there might be a reply.

The letter she opened alone was soaked in blood. Written in **Theresa**'s hand, it asked Kal'tsit to come back and help prepare for the changes ahead, and reported that Rim Billiton's excavation team had found traces of the ruins Kal'tsit had described. At the end, it asked:
Kal'tsit, does the name... 'Rhodes Island' mean anything to you?

Twenty-two years ago in the desert, Kal'tsit had told Elliot she was going to Chernobog. Seventeen years ago, when Lillia asked her to come to Sami, she answered that she would go to Victoria by way of Siracusa. And thirteen years ago in Victoria, she told Heidi that someday she would have to leave.
Before returning to the party, Kal'tsit told Heidi to carry on the work she and her father had been doing in Victoria, and Count Vincent asked her to protect Thomson, his dearest friend.
A blizzard would fall on the road away from the manor, Kal'tsit said. Could Heidi have all the preparations done? Heidi gave a short answer. Yes.
Epilogue: Setting Sail
After Kal'tsit left, a Columbian apprentice came to the Reefsteep Black Market, as if he had been sold there. As soon as his broken arm had healed, Elliot began welding stolen steel into something.
Some ten years later, rumor spread among smugglers that 'Sand Soldier' had become Reefsteep's new master. But Kal'tsit's whereabouts were never found.

Then word came that the Ameer of Ibut would pass through Redhorn. Isin said he had seen, in a dream, someone like Kal'tsit standing beside the Kheshig expedition in ages long past, and sent him off to finish the revenge he had left undone.
Around that time, on a moonlit night, Isin vanished into the sand. The gold coin reached Elliot only three years later.

And in the Rhodes Island infirmary, a recruit who had just signed his contract, codename **Passenger**, faced Kal'tsit. Time, he said, had turned him into the face he once hated. Kal'tsit asked whether he was still that 'Sand Soldier.' He answered that he had a new name, and she called him by the old one anyway. Elliot.

blocks.cap: The Rhodes Island infirmary. A reunion after twenty-two years.

blocks.x: He asked her not to call him that. Meanwhile, a parcel from Heidi Thomson of Victoria arrived for Kal'tsit.
Passenger asked how long she would stay here this time. Would she vanish again after a few days, a few months, a few years?
Kal'tsit said she could give him hundreds, thousands of answers. When he told her to pick just one, she began. I...
Then, meeting the Doctor in the corridor, Kal'tsit asked the Doctor to stay by Amiya's side, and if all went smoothly, to tell everyone aboard the ship before sundown: Rhodes Island is setting sail.

The question Sand Soldier asked in present-day Sargon had also been written in Theresa's letter thirteen years before. What kind of place is Rhodes Island? At the end of the long road of a wanderer who walked out into the desert twenty-two years ago with only Mon3tr, that ship sets sail.

act17d0.tagline: Chasing a mad scientist, four operatives from Earth are dropped, lab and all, into a strange desert. They hold out for half a year leaning on a young doctor of the Infected, then see that town's rebellion through to the end beside him. And one person who scattered as light.

chars.name: Ash
chars.desc: Leader of Team Rainbow. Real name Cohen. Quick to judge, and decisive.

chars.name: Blitz
chars.desc: A shield-bearing Team Rainbow operative. Real name Kötz. Easygoing, and quick to pick up a strange language.

chars.name: Frost
chars.desc: A Team Rainbow operative. Real name Tina. Skilled at scouting, traps, and hunting.

chars.name: Tachanka
chars.desc: Team Rainbow's machine gunner. Real name Alexsandr Senaviev. His teammates call him 'Lord'.

chars.name: Ela
chars.desc: A Team Rainbow operative who handles mines.

chars.name: Iana
chars.desc: A Team Rainbow operative who uses the 'Gemini Replicator'.

chars.name: Levi
chars.desc: Chief scientist of the Magnethill No. 2 laboratory on Earth. The target Team Rainbow had come to take alive.

chars.name: Rangers
chars.desc: An elderly Rhodes Island field operator. He knows the Sargon wastelands like the back of his hand.

chars.name: Schwarz
chars.desc: A taciturn Rhodes Island operator. A Feline sniper who uses a crossbow.

chars.name: Liskarm
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator formerly of Blacksteel. A Vouivre who wields electricity.

chars.name: Franka
chars.desc: An operator who came from Blacksteel with Liskarm. Teasing Liskarm is her favorite pastime.

chars.name: Miarow
chars.desc: A young doctor who runs a clinic in Long Spring's Infected district. He is Infected himself.

chars.name: Drudge
chars.desc: Son of the Tulla family, lords of Long Spring. He gathers mercenaries to bring down his father.

chars.name: Occphen
chars.desc: The guard of the Rhodes Island safehouse in Long Spring. A reserve Logistics Operator.

chars.name: Picale
chars.desc: Daughter of the Tulla family, lords of Long Spring, and captain of the guard. She wields a great spear and charges headlong.

chars.name: Stormeye
chars.desc: An archer operator of Rhodes Island.

terms.name: Team Rainbow
terms.desc: The Earth operations team Ash and the others belong to. No one on Terra has ever heard the name.

terms.name: Long Spring
terms.desc: A small town in Bayalir territory, Sargon. It is named for its reliable well, a rarity in the wastelands.

terms.name: Ameer
terms.desc: A lord of Sargon. Within an Ameer's domain, his commandments are law.

terms.name: Originiutant
terms.desc: Mutant creatures Levi made from Originium. They burrow through the ground and are controlled by a Caster's Arts.

terms.name: Volvort Kochinski
terms.desc: A Columbian organization backing Drudge. It has its eyes on Long Spring's mines.

blocks.x: Four operatives of Earth's **Team Rainbow** stormed into the Magnethill No. 2 laboratory. The leader, **Ash**. **Blitz**, with his shield. **Frost**, on recon and cover. **Tachanka**, with his machine gun. Their objective was to take the lab's chief scientist, **Levi** Klitschko, alive.

When they entered the control room, Levi was already standing at the machine. Saying he would reclaim the results he should have had twenty years ago, he started a reactor holding a black crystal, and a shockwave swallowed the entire lab.
When the four opened their eyes, what lay beyond the collapsed walls was endless desert. No signal; no working compass. None of them knew where they were, or which way led home.
1. The Lab Is Gone

At that moment, the other two operatives, **Ela** and **Iana**, who had been clearing a path on the far side of the building, heard the roar and ran for the lab. Beyond the door there was no lab. Only a huge hole.

Meanwhile, in the middle of the desert, the four had no time to catch their breath before a huge, spider-like beast lunged at them. Bullets could not pierce its shell, and it tore Blitz's shield apart in a single bite.

Finding that only armor-piercing rounds got through, Ash deliberately lured the beast into the building. The moment it broke through the wall, they would finish it with their last grenade and Tachanka's armor-piercing rounds. That was how the fight ended.
When Blitz asked whether this was really Earth, Ash said there was no reason it shouldn't be, but they had to prepare for the worst.

blocks.cap: "With the wall collapsed, we can't even use this place as shelter."

blocks.x: The four set out across the desert in search of somewhere to stay.
2. The Old Ranger of the Wastes

Elsewhere in the Sargon wastelands, another group was traveling on foot after their vehicle had been stolen: Rhodes Island's elderly field operator **Rangers**, the taciturn sniper **Schwarz**, and **Liskarm** and **Franka**, formerly of Blacksteel. Their guide was a map Rangers had drawn by hand in his youth.

When Franka and Liskarm brought up the exploits of the 'Ranger of the Red Valley', Rangers laughed it off, saying he had only ever been an ordinary scout. But at the title of a tale Schwarz had heard, 'The Scimitar of the Bloody Valley', he fell silent for a moment.

Then a pack of giant sand beasts, their bodies studded with Originium crystals, burst out of the ground. When the fight was over, a distress signal from Long Spring's 'Watchtower 33', a Rhodes Island safehouse, came through and then cut out, and the group turned toward **Long Spring**.
Around the same time, in a mine cave, **Drudge**, who meant to bring down his father, was berating the scientist whose research he had funded for half a year. The mutant monsters were still too weak.
The scientist told him to bring corpses. Human corpses, of the Infected if possible. That scientist was Levi.

blocks.cap: The mine cave. Deep inside it, a machine not of Terra was running.

blocks.x: 3. Mission Log, Day 184

Then, on day 184, Ash left her last mission log on the recorder. The bandits had conjured fireballs out of thin air and hurled them, and the car taken from the bandit den ran on a strange engine with no fuel tank at all. The four could only conclude that this was not Earth.
So many roads lie before us... Which one of them leads home?

For nearly a month, the four had been living in an abandoned house on the outskirts of Long Spring, in the Infected district. The Infected, driven out of the town, shared food, water, and medicine with the four lost strangers.

But between the Infected and the townsfolk ran a hatred that went beyond exclusion. The Lord of Long Spring had never once left his residence, and Ash was also uneasy that Blitz, who had picked up the local language quickly, had grown too close to the townsfolk.

That day, as always, **Miarow**, the young doctor who ran a clinic in the Infected district, came by with medicine. Oripathy could not be cured, he said, but even the painkillers made from the Originium Slugs Frost caught were a blessing to the Infected.

blocks.cap: The abandoned house in the Infected district. Miarow brought medicine here.

blocks.x: Miarow said that someday he wanted to go to Columbia, finish his studies, and become a real doctor. He smiled and said he had no money, and that his patients needed him now. Ash told him he was still young; his chance would come one day.
Miarow also warned them not to go outside for a while. Monsters had recently appeared in the town and hurt many people, and resentment toward the Infected was growing.
4. The Day the Infected District Burned

Then Frost ran in. Armed townsfolk had blocked the road into the Infected district and were shouting for a big, fully wrapped outsider to be handed over. It was Blitz, who had gone into town that morning.

Miarow went out alone, saying the townsfolk would listen to him. As he stood in the crowd's way, he noticed that the man in the front row was not from this town. Meanwhile, Frost saw that the big men at the back were carrying greatswords wrapped in cloth.
They were Sarkaz mercenaries disguised as townsfolk. The moment they drew their weapons, Blitz shouted for Miarow to get down, and the four opened fire.

blocks.cap: The road into the Infected district, where townsfolk and Infected faced each other.

blocks.x: The mercenaries fell back, but the monsters bursting from the ground kept coming, and flames rose in the center of town as well. The Lord's soldiers were nowhere to be seen.
That day, more than forty Infected took refuge in Miarow's clinic. Many could not be found, and the elderly did not survive.

As bandages and ammunition ran low, Miarow remembered a fortress-like building at the southern edge of town, belonging to a pharmaceutical company called Rhodes Island. But when Ash and Blitz took him there, its door had been smashed in too, and the guard, **Occphen**, lay collapsed, injured from holding out against the attackers' threats.
Occphen hesitated, saying this was Rhodes Island property and he had no authority to decide. In the end he opened the door. Better to lose his job than his life, he said.
5. The Battle for the Safehouse

Around then, in the cave, Drudge was pressing Levi to make more monsters. Unknown gunmen had appeared, and at the manor his father's guards and his sister were still holding out. Levi corrected him: the monsters had a name. **Originiutants**.

Meanwhile, the four, now moved into the safehouse, tried to repair the broken communicator and gave up. The armory was full of Originium explosives and grenade launchers, but there was no ammunition that fit their guns.

blocks.cap: "I thought the people here didn't use weapons like these."

blocks.x: When Miarow said the four came from a faraway place where even Oripathy did not exist, Occphen's eyes went wide. Without Oripathy there would be no discrimination and no hatred. Wouldn't that be a world where everyone was equal? No one answered, and Occphen asked them to forget what he had just said.

Then horned Sarkaz mercenaries and Originiutants surrounded the safehouse. Just as it was becoming hard to hold, Rangers' group, who had been watching from afar, charged in, reasoning that whoever commanded monsters could hardly be in the right. Under Liskarm's lightning and Schwarz's bolts, the mercenaries fell back.

When they heard it was a Rhodes Island field team, Occphen cried out that he was saved. Rangers paid his respects to the four who had protected 43 Infected, and when they passed themselves off as mercenaries from a distant country to the south, he said that where they came from did not matter.
A Lord who had set up an Infected district and even allowed a safehouse would surely be fair, Rangers said, and he urged them not to act rashly, but to wait.
6. The Contract Is Void as of Today
A few quiet days followed. Liskarm tried to revive the dead communications equipment with current from her fingertips, but the connection never came through, and food was running out.

blocks.cap: Liskarm channeling current into the communications equipment.

blocks.x: Then Ash and Rangers' group, returning with food gathered from the homes the Infected had left behind, were followed. Only when they reached the safehouse did they realize their pursuers were the Lord's soldiers.

blocks.cap: The Lord's guards surrounding the safehouse.

blocks.x: At their head was **Picale** Tulla, daughter of the Lord of Long Spring and captain of the guard. Striking the ground with the butt of her spear, she declared that she would make them pay: the mercenaries bought by her brother, and Rhodes Island, which had abducted the residents.

When Ash shot back, asking where the Lord's soldiers had been when the raiders hit the Infected district, the mood turned uglier. Miarow stepped forward and swore an oath, and Picale believed his word, his alone. But she declared the contract with Rhodes Island void as of today.

As the guards led the Infected away, Tachanka saw Miarow off, saying he had a story to tell him the next time they met. Rangers pressed a refined Originium Ingot into Miarow's hand as payment for treating Occphen's leg.

Schwarz was suspicious. The Lord's side had been sluggish when the mercenaries fell on the Infected; now it had taken everyone away, and the timing was too neat. When she said she would follow them, Rangers did not stop her this time.

That night, Picale ordered that if the shelter ran short of room, the residents be given her father's chambers. That was what her late father would have done, she said. Moments later, Originiutants fell upon the convoy.

As Picale cut the monsters down, Miarow appeared before her, crying out for her not to go, and then Drudge showed himself. Picale charged at her brother, took the full force of a shockwave from a machine hidden behind a collapsed house, and fell.
7. Night at the Manor

Picale came to in the manor. She shouted that their father was already dead and that she was now the Lord of Long Spring, but Drudge, backed by an experimental Columbian Ultrasonic Impact Unit and Sarkaz mercenaries, only sneered. Their father's guards already lay dead in every alley, he said, and he would dig all the Originium out of the mines and make Long Spring the mining center of Bayalir.

If she wanted so badly to protect the Infected, Drudge said, she could become one herself, and he ordered his mercenaries to infect Picale. The captured Infected were to be handed over to the scientist, and the kid who looked ready to die at any moment was to be taken too, alive or dead.
The moment a mercenary raised his weapon, a bolt from the shadow of the garden wall brought him down. It was Schwarz.

blocks.cap: Schwarz's ambush. The mercenaries could not even find where it came from.

blocks.x: Picale swore to cut out the traitor's heart even if it cost her life, and Schwarz held her back. Only if Picale lived would the town live, Schwarz said, and she had already signaled her comrades.

Soon, at the signal, Ash's team and Rangers' group broke through the barricades and stormed the manor. But when the mercenaries brought out their experimental weapon and it unleashed a shockwave, the area around the manor was buried in rubble.

Meanwhile, in the garden, Picale and Schwarz were surrounded by an endless tide of monsters, and Miarow, who had been lying collapsed, pulled himself up. His whole body ached, every cough brought up blood, and he knew he would soon die.

In his hand was the Originium Ingot Rangers had given him. His Arts could make things made of Originium explode. Someone had once told him that with a gift like that he should become a soldier. He had chosen to become a doctor.
I don't want to die yet... But a doctor has to save people. More... more people...!

The young Infected pushed off the ground and ran. When the ultrasonic emitter blew apart, the Originiutants lost control and ran wild, and Picale hurled herself at Drudge. Then Ash's team poured into the garden.
8. Returning to the Earth

When the gunfire stopped, Ash looked for Miarow. The boy lay among scattered shards of Originium, and not an inch of his exposed skin was unharmed. The Originium that had exploded so close had driven the disease deep into his body.

When Ash cried out, asking whether Rhodes Island had no way to save him, Liskarm answered that with this much bleeding, these burns, and symptoms this acute, it would have been hard even aboard the landship. Tachanka held on to Miarow, telling him to picture the Columbia he had dreamed of.
A few more coughs, and then they stopped.
"...He's dead."
Tachanka went at a captured mercenary as if to kill him, and Blitz barely held him back. Then Liskarm saw the crystals in Miarow's skin begin to glow.

The Rhodes Island people hurriedly carried the body into a small room and sealed everything: the windows, the gaps in the door, the chimney, the vents. To Ash, who did not understand, Tachanka said only: don't look.
Light leaked through the cracks of the shut window.

blocks.cap: Glittering dust rises from the wounds of the one who has passed.

blocks.x: Glittering dust seeped from the wounds and spread through the still air, and then a dazzling light tore away every last scrap of darkness in the room. When the Originium dust drifting in the many-colored light settled, it was over.
And so an Infected returned to the earth that had birthed him.
9. He Was a Good Man
Afterward, a funeral was held in the shade of a dead tree. An elderly Infected sang in Sargonian: all shall return to dust, all shall return to nature.
Here lies our dear friend, Miarow. He was Infected, and he was a doctor. He was a good man.
Ash admitted she did not know whether they had done the right thing. They had set out to save the Infected without even knowing that Oripathy was not a disease, but a disaster.

Tachanka spoke of the nights he had watched from the rooftop. The nights the townsfolk carried hemp sacks as long as a person out into the rocky desert, and the glowing dust he saw scatter on the wind from between the rocks. The old woman who always sat at the door of the house a sack had come from was never seen again.

blocks.cap: "You asked whether we really did the right thing?"

blocks.x: Even after seeing all of it, Tachanka told Ash:
Don't turn your back on our good work. Following the morality and conscience in your heart is never wrong.

Picale came and bowed her head. As she clenched a golden seal in her fist, blue patterns rose on her arm guard, and the melted seal ran down onto the gravestone. It was the medal her father had received from the Lord Ameer.

The Tulla family was built on the blood and bones of miners, Picale said. Her father had grown rich on Originium, then closed the quarries, protected the Infected district, and cast out Drudge, who had turned wicked while studying in Columbia. Behind Drudge stood a Columbian organization called **Volvort Kochinski**.
Only now did she understand her father's words, Picale said: violence alone cannot defeat true evil. Drudge had only ever been one part of that evil.
Then Franka brought Miarow's box of belongings. Inside were an old map, a Sargonian-language travel guide to the cities of Columbia, a stash of saved Columbian checks, and a single note.

blocks.cap: The box Miarow left behind. It had been his mother's.

blocks.x: Please give the money to someone else. I surely won't have any use for it now. ...I don't know who you are, but I hope you live a happy life.
Franka said that for the Infected, dreams were a luxury, like fragile gemstones. Miarow had deserved a better life, Tachanka said. Then, saying he had a plan, he went to find Picale.
10. The Last Line of Defense

Around then, Drudge fled back to the mine cave, only to be met by his own mercenaries, already turned into Originiutants and standing at Levi's side. Showing the Originium tumor writhing on his arm, Levi said that once you became part of them, you could understand each other even without Arts. Then he bid farewell to Drudge, who was still invoking his bloodline.

Meanwhile, Tachanka recalled that on the night Miarow detonated the Originium Ingot, the monsters had abandoned their Casters' orders and chased the scattered fragments of Originium. A large enough chunk of Originium could draw the monsters underground up to the surface.

The bait was the Originium engine of the car taken from the bandit den. Liskarm and Franka recognized it as the vehicle they had lost, but Rangers told them to let it go for now. While the monsters were drawn to the surface, Ash's team would descend into the monster factory in the mine tunnels that the captured mercenary had revealed.
The modified engine roared, spewing light and smoke, and the monsters swarmed in. More than a hundred, and still they kept coming.

blocks.cap: Before the Lord's manor. The Rhodes Island group stayed as well.

blocks.x: When Franka hurt her leg shielding Liskarm, Liskarm carried her on her back and ran, and Occphen burst out of the shelter to clear the way. He was a Rhodes Island operator too, he said.

With ammunition and traps exhausted, Tachanka told Frost to take the Rhodes Island people to the shelter, and stayed behind himself. From the moment they pointed weapons at the Infected, this had been a war to him.

Frost reminded him that he was the one who always said not to play hero. Tachanka answered that he was only trying to do the right thing. Rangers stayed too, drawing a blade borrowed from the late Lord and swinging its curved edge as if in a dance.

On the day he and his comrades stained the valley red with blood, Rangers said, his name had been buried in the sand along with his past. Tachanka said that was all right. All that mattered now was that they had stayed together.
They told me I'd died. They were wrong. I was reborn.
11. The Lab Beneath Long Spring
At the same time, Ash, Blitz, and Schwarz went deeper from where Rangers' map ended, past Originiutants that had once been people, and reached a familiar corridor.
Most of the Magnethill No. 2 laboratory had fallen beneath Long Spring. Ash ground her teeth. She had lived in this town so long and never noticed.

Every cage in the row held the corpses of people and beasts, and in one of them Drudge was locked up, alive. As he held out his hand, saying the enemy of his enemy was his friend, Ash had Schwarz open the cage, then beat Drudge until he begged for his life.

blocks.cap: "And this one's for Miarow."

blocks.x: When Blitz stopped her, Ash drew back. Schwarz said she felt a little better, and Ash said she did too.

Lights came on deep inside the lab. Behind bulletproof glass, with an incubator at his back, Levi greeted his old friends from Team Rainbow. When Ash asked whether human life meant nothing to him, he answered that good and evil were merely subjective notions born of weakness, and that Originium was the truth of this world.

With a cry of 'Praise be!', the incubator shattered. A monster with a round mass of flesh for a head crawled out, its dark red spine pierced Levi's skull, and the two bodies twisted together into one.

blocks.cap: What broke out of the incubator. Levi became one with it.

blocks.x: The fallen monster split into lumps of flesh that refused to die, writhing as if putting out shoots. Blitz planted explosives, and the three raced for the exit before the blast.

Meanwhile, before the manor, Tachanka's ammunition ran out. Rangers, his hand wounded, remembered the young rangers who had laughed and sung war songs even knowing they would be buried in the wastelands. Those who fell became legends, he said, and those who survived honored them.

Then arrows rained down, piercing the heads and necks of the Originiutants. It was Rhodes Island's **Stormeye**, come in answer to the distress signal. Calling Rangers 'Old Ranger', Stormeye said it was an honor to fight at his side.
Then came another name for the old man. 'The Scimitar of the Bloody Valley'.
Epilogue — Walking the Land

Two weeks later, Picale bowed her head to the four on Long Spring's behalf. The residents could once again carry on their lives on the land where they had been born and raised. Ash answered that they had only finished what they had started.
Told to take anything from the manor in place of money, the four chose only a helmet and a glowing claw to mount on a shield.

Escorted by Stormeye's team, the four left Long Spring with Rangers' group. They were registered with Rhodes Island as collaborators rather than formal employees, gaining identities that let them travel this land freely.

blocks.cap: "So these are our new identities."

blocks.x: When Frost asked about their plans, Ash said that for once there was no written plan. They would make one as they came to know this world. Their first destination was a city called Siesta.
Until the day we make it home, we keep moving.

In her last mission log, Ash asked which road led home, and that question still has no answer. But the four now know how the Infected of this land live, and how they return as light. Across that land, they began to walk.

act16d5.tagline: Asked by Nian to bring her little sister home, Lava and company open the door of a thatched cottage in the mountains, and end up guarding New Year's Eve in a village inside a painting, where the sun and moon hang in the same sky. And a painter who says we are all Painting-Dwellers.

chars.name: Lava
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator. At Nian's request, she has come all the way to the backcountry of Yan to find Nian's little sister. Quick on the uptake.

chars.name: Kroos
chars.desc: A sniper who came along with Lava. She may look half-asleep, but she reads a situation faster than anyone.

chars.name: Mr. Nothing
chars.desc: A self-proclaimed messenger rescued by Lava's group while being chased by Gloompincers. He appoints himself their guide and tags along.

chars.name: Nian
chars.desc: Lava's colleague at Rhodes Island. The one who handed her this mission, asking her to find her little sister.

chars.name: Dusk
chars.desc: Nian's little sister, whom Nian says she hasn't seen in years. Almost nothing is known about her except that she's a painter.

chars.name: Umbrella-Boiling Hermit
chars.desc: The owner of a garden in P'o-shan Village. Every day at the Hour of Shen, he tells the villagers strange tales.

chars.name: Saga
chars.desc: A wandering monk from Higashi who rings the bell in P'o-shan Village. Oddly well-informed about how things work in the village.

chars.name: Dawn
chars.desc: The owner of P'o-shan Village's pawnshop. She keeps the shop alone, with few customers and fewer pledges, and speaks only in riddles.

chars.name: Ah Jan
chars.desc: A little girl in P'o-shan Village who goes around listening to the storyteller's tales.

chars.name: Beagle
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator close to Kroos.

terms.name: Painting-Dweller
terms.desc: Literally, "a person inside a painting."

terms.name: Mount Hui-ch'i
terms.desc: A mountain outside Kou-wu City. The place the address Nian handed over points to.

terms.name: Kou-wu City
terms.desc: A Yan city near Mount Hui-ch'i. Lava's group restocked there before setting out.

terms.name: P'o-shan Village
terms.desc: The village Lava's group find themselves in when they come to. The sun and moon hang in the same sky, and the farther west you go, the closer it gets to night.

terms.name: Ink Spirit
terms.desc: Monsters that come down from the western mountain around New Year's Eve to raid P'o-shan Village. Cut one down and it vanishes into an ink stain. Saga gave them the name.

terms.name: Scene of Crude Mounts Utmost Risen
terms.desc: A landscape scroll said to have been left by a nameless painter about a hundred years ago. Even the imperial family once offered a fortune for it.

terms.name: Dusk Beauty Flying to the Moon
terms.desc: An old tale of the Dusk Beauty, who flew alone toward the moon. It is said she meant to win love back from the heavens.

terms.name: True Lung
terms.desc: The most controversial emperor in Yan's history. Said to have waged a great hunt against Yan's gods of heaven and earth.

blocks.x: A month earlier, aboard the Rhodes Island landship. **Nian** springs a favor on **Lava** out of nowhere: bring home her little sister **Dusk**, whom she hasn't seen in years. And the only reason she gives? "I miss my family all the more on every festive day." That's it.

She's already cleared it with Closure, and she's even sending the sniper **Kroos** along. Asked why she doesn't just go herself, Nian shrugs it off: "She's been avoiding me for years. Why would I go asking for trouble?" Then she presses a mysterious object into Lava's hand, calling it a "charm."
The only leads are a one-line address, "outside Kou-wu City, near Mount Hui-ch'i," and the fact that she's a painter. Even so, Nian is confident. When the time comes, Lava will know her at a glance.
1. Open the Door, and There's a Sun and a Moon in One Sky

So the two make their way out to the wilds of Yan's backcountry, where they rescue a man who blundered into a Gloompincer nest. This self-proclaimed messenger says he's lost his car and every bit of his luggage, and yet his fishing rod and fan are perfectly fine, and he even pulls a cure-all elixir out of his emergency pouch. Suspicious, to say the least.
Asked for his name, he hesitates for a good long while before answering, "Just call me... Mr. Nothing." Lava fires right back: "You just came up with that, didn't you?!"

Still, a local guide is hard to turn down, so the group, now three with **Mr. Nothing**, tracks down a run-down thatched cottage deep in the woods of Mount Hui-ch'i. There's no sign of anyone living there. Lava carefully opens the door.

blocks.cap: A thatched cottage in the woods of Mount Hui-ch'i. The door is stained, and fallen leaves have piled up.

blocks.x: The next moment, the three are sitting in an unfamiliar garden, listening to the strange tale of a lame scholar who tried to paint something that didn't exist in this world and died in front of his painting. The storyteller's name is the **Umbrella-Boiling Hermit**. But when Mr. Nothing tries to leave the garden, he can't remember which way he came in, and Lava can't say for sure how many days they've been in this village.
Then they look up, and freeze like people seeing the sky for the very first time.

blocks.cap: The sun on one side, the moon on the other. It's broad daylight, yet the lanterns on the bridge are lit.

blocks.x: Lava is about to marvel at it ("Huh, so views like this exist") when she touches Nian's charm in her pocket and snaps out of it. She remembers opening the cottage door, but everything after that is a complete blank.

Just then a bell rings, and the villagers flee toward the sunlit side, crying that monsters are coming down from the western mountain. Leaving Mr. Nothing's shrieks of "let's just hide!" behind them, Lava and Kroos go straight for their weapons.
2. Ching-tso 7, a New Year's Eve Where the Sun Never Sets

Once they start fighting, they find that the monsters turn into black stains and vanish when shot, with no sign of infection. As thanks for protecting the village, the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit invites the three in, but every single thing he tells them is strange.

This is P'o-shan Village, a place none of them has ever heard of, and the year is "Ching-tso 7." Mr. Nothing goes white as a sheet: there hasn't been an era name like that for at least the last several hundred years.

Seventy years ago, a scroll turned up in the ashes of a wealthy merchant's burned-down house, as good as new. The merchant set out to find the auspicious spot it depicted, and what he built there is this village and this garden. The sun hangs forever in the east and the moon forever in the west, and the twelve double-hours of a day refer to the time it takes to get from the eastern edge, where the sun rises, to the western edge, where the moon rises.

And for several years now, around New Year's Eve, monsters have come down from the western mountain to run riot through the village for three to five days, and each time the people have hidden wherever the sun is. When Lava shows him Nian's charm, the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit says, "Craft to surpass nature," and seems about to say more, but trails off when word comes that the banquet is ready.

blocks.cap: The Umbrella-Boiling Hermit's garden. Every day at the Hour of Shen, he tells his stories here.

blocks.x: Around then, Mr. Nothing, wandering the village on his own, runs into **Saga**, a traveling monk from Higashi. Saga calls the monsters Ink Spirits, a name she took from an old tale her head priest told her when she was little.
Meanwhile, Lava strikes a deal with the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit. They'll guard the village through New Year's Eve, and once it's over, he'll help them leave. He nods. "Leaving is the easy part."
3. Quoth the Monk: "We Are Inside a Painting"

The bell rings again, and this time there are far more Ink Spirits. Saga cuts them down shouting "Cleanse the six senses!", "Sever all desires!" and "Aburaage!" No matter how many times you hear it, that last one is not a battle cry.
Saga can even understand what the Ink Spirits say, and simply lets one go when it claims to repent. Then she turns to a baffled Lava and calmly tells her: they're inside a painting.

Saga, too, spent a night in a thatched cottage below a waterfall on Mount Hui-ch'i and woke up here. She's wandered so long that, by her reckoning, the village spans about a hundred-odd scrolls, which leaves Lava speechless.

Right after, the two rush to a pawnshop with its lights on. Its owner, **Dawn**, faces an Ink Spirit and talks to it soothingly ("What did she say to you?") before sending it on its way. When Lava asks whether anything strange has attacked her, she answers without batting an eye: "Never seen anything like that."

blocks.cap: Dawn's pawnshop. No customer ever comes back to redeem a pledge.

blocks.x: Over cups of tea, Saga tells her own story. Raised by the head priest of a temple in Higashi, she once saw, as a child, the Scene of Crude Mounts Utmost Risen, a landscape scroll a full hundred meters long, and felt as though she had stepped right into it.

When the head priest was a young novice monk, he nearly drowned in the K'u-t'an River and was pulled out by a woman. He walked with her toward Mount Hui-ch'i, and it was she who painted the scroll. Saga doesn't know the name of this woman who never slept. She came to Mount Hui-ch'i to find the real scenery behind the painting, and that's how she ended up in here.
Having listened to the story, Dawn quietly asks Lava a question.
Miss Lava, do you mean to... go to all that trouble to fish the moon out of the water?

Even when the moon in the water is broken up by the waves, it turns round again once the water calms, so there's no need to get your shoes wet over it, and no need to go that far for their sake. A little later, the light reflected in the tea trembles. The sun, which had hung in the east forever, has begun to move.
4. The Day the Sun Moved
With the sun shifting, the Ink Spirits no longer fear the light. They pour into the daytime streets and start devouring people. This time, no bell rings.
In the street, a villager who has lost her husband screams at Lava. "We trusted you and did everything you said! Why? Why did my husband have to die?!"

blocks.cap: The day the sun moved. Ink Spirits flood the daytime streets.

blocks.x: With the Ink Spirits coming endlessly, Saga tells Lava to get the people to safety and holds the road alone. "Those who cross this line shall be cut down."

Meanwhile, Mr. Nothing, fleeing with a girl on his back who has just lost her mother, sees the villagers cornered too, and at last opens his fan and fells an Ink Spirit with a single blow. Lava unleashes the Arts she had been holding back for fear of damaging the buildings, and flames shoot into the sky over the garden.

When the chaos has passed, they learn that the girl Mr. Nothing carried is named **Ah Jan**. Her father left to find work and never came back, and now that she has lost her mother too, she won't eat a thing.

At the same hour, in the pawnshop, Dawn tells a story to the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit, who is unusually quiet. It is a story of people who abandoned their village when Originium tainted the water, of neighbors who starved to death on the road, and of a little girl abandoned by her family on the day she came back with an armful of fruit.

At the point where the girl, feeling the chill of death, saw "a strange person," Dawn breaks off and says she will tell the rest next time. Then the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit asks Saga, who has just walked in, whether she hasn't been in the painting long enough by now. Saga looks at him again. "Thou art not the storyteller..."

That night, Kroos brings up the fan with Mr. Nothing. Holding back and making excuses when you have the strength to help is selfish, she says. Mr. Nothing promises to tell them everything once they're out of here.
5. One Night's Sleep, and Nothing Ever Happened

The next morning, Lava goes to wake Kroos, who is sound asleep hugging her crossbow, and freezes at the sight outside the window. Ah Jan's mother, the one they thought was gone, is walking past with her daughter, who is hurrying her along so they won't be late for story time.

blocks.cap: The guest room after a night's sleep. The village outside the window is back to how it was before the chaos.

blocks.x: The eaves broken by Arts are intact, and the streets ring again with the calls of rice-cake and sweet-rice vendors. Ah Jan doesn't recognize Mr. Nothing, and says she spent all of yesterday flying kites with her mother.

At the pawnshop, where they head straight away, Saga explains the rule over a bowl of black sesame soup. When all four people from outside the painting fall asleep and close their eyes, no one is left to watch the world, and in that gap, the painting quietly reverts to how it was.

Dawn adds something more frightening. The longer you stay, the more you forget what you once took for granted, until you accept the painting, the painting accepts you, and you become a Painting-Dweller who can never leave. Kroos has also noticed that there is no Originium in this village at all.

Dawn herself remembers yesterday. "Because I made her a promise." Dawn knows she isn't the real "me," too. The woman behind all of this, she says, is someone they know, and she asks them not to speak her name.

The Ink Spirits are nothing but doodles that woman scribbles to pass the time when she's in a bad mood, and **this P'o-shan Village is the moon in the water**. It's easier, Dawn says, to think of it all as fake.

Even so, the group goes out once more to hold off the Ink Spirits. Beside Mr. Nothing, who says he can't just stand by and watch Ah Jan cry, Kroos adds, "Even so, I don't want to hear those screams. I'm sick of it."
6. A Master's Fan and Bamboo Firecrackers

After the fight, they call on the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit, who greets them between coughing fits as if they were guests he had never met, and the three end up staying in his guest room again. There, as promised, Mr. Nothing finally opens up.

At thirteen, he entered a martial arts school in Kou-wu City and trained under his master for over ten years. But last year, in a match between schools, he beat his opponent to death, a fighter who had signed his life away to step into the ring. His proud, unbending old master paid the price, shedding his blood in front of everyone, "by the rules."

With a gang surrounding the school, they couldn't even call an ambulance. He watched his master grow cold and buried him with his own hands. All he had left was the fan. Ever since, he has been posing as a fortune-teller, then as a messenger, trying to slip out of Kou-wu City. The car in the lake was no accident, either.

The days of holding off the Ink Spirits go on, and before long it is the seventh day. Kroos points out that Lava's Arts have grown dangerous enough to burn down several buildings, and that Mr. Nothing has started ignoring the small Ink Spirits since everything will be back tomorrow anyway. Guard a meaningless goal day after day, she says, and that is how people change. Don't forget what happened at Rim Billiton.

Around that time, in the pawnshop, Dawn faces an Ink Spirit and murmurs to herself, "Are you watching, Dusk?" Then she seeks out the group and offers an unexpected solution: the Ink Spirits are probably afraid of firecrackers, too.

Firecrackers remind Kroos of the part in Ancient Forge where Nian was scared of them. There's no way the market has any firecrackers, so the group stacks the bamboo the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit gives them like fuel in a stove, bursts it with Lava's fire, and drives the Ink Spirits off.

blocks.cap: Bamboo piled up at the edge of the village. Lava's fire stands in for firecrackers.

blocks.x: When Kroos asks why it works, Lava says, "You'd have to ask Nian." From somewhere, the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit's voice repeats the name. "...Nian?"
7. A Traveling Monk Wakes After Ten Years

At the same hour, Saga, who has spent seven days shut in her room meditating, opens her eyes in a thatched cottage in the mountains. When the Umbrella-Boiling Hermit sitting across from her asks how long it has been, Saga answers that she has watched the plum blossoms bloom and fall ten times.

Since entering the painting of Mount Sky, Saga has drifted through one painting after another for ten years. The old fisher atop Mount Sky, the old woman at her loom, the innkeeper of the Lungmen Inn, and now the storyteller of P'o-shan Village: every face that tried to wake her in all that time was the person in front of her now.

Saga confesses that her heart has long been bound up in the truth of why the Dusk Beauty flew to the moon in Dusk Beauty Flying to the Moon. Told that even that feeling was a lie painted on purpose, she answers that a legend being false cannot negate what it means. The Umbrella-Boiling Hermit calls her someone who takes after her master, and tells her it is time to wake up.

blocks.cap: "Finally awake?" The owner of the painting looks down at Saga lying on the floor.

blocks.x: When Saga opens her eyes again, the one before her is Nian's sister, Dusk. Saga asks the question she has carried all her life: why does the Scene of Crude Mounts Utmost Risen stop its brush where the waterfall ends and leave the rest blank?

The answer is an anticlimax. Dusk simply lost interest partway through and stopped, and the title she gave it only went as far as "Crude Mounts Utmost." The last word, "Risen," was added by Saga's master, and Dusk shows Saga what her master actually saw back then.

blocks.cap: A wasteland full of the starved. A young novice monk walks for three days and nights, praying.

blocks.x: Amid that horror, the young novice prayed two thousand and twenty-four times, and this time Dusk did not help him. He went back to Higashi and built a temple that takes in children with nowhere to go. Only now does Saga understand: her master added "Risen" to say that the humble mountains had not yet come to an end.
To Saga's last question, whether the people of the painting are real or false, Dusk answers.
No. You and I, all of us are Painting-Dwellers. People inside a painting.

It is no lie that Saga left the painting, but who could prove that this land, here and now, is not just another painting? Dusk tells Saga to leave first, and Saga, saying she promised Lava, hands Dusk that charm.
"You... this is...?!" In that instant, Nian's voice comes from somewhere. "...Found you."
8. Dreams of Their Own, and a Big Sister

Right after that, Dusk realizes what the charm really is and flings the group into dreams of their own. In his dream, Mr. Nothing hides out in Lungmen and holds on for five years with the help of an old man who had been close to his master, finally getting his revenge, only to die at the hands of an assassin posing as a customer on the day he opens a martial arts gym in Lungmen.
At that moment, Nian appears and shakes him awake. Getting yourself killed even in a dream, she says, is a bad deal.

Kroos's dream, meanwhile, begins in **Beagle**'s new home. A dream of spending a few days together and parting reluctantly drifts before long to Bolívar, where Kroos cries out that they have to stop Beagle no matter what.
Nian appears before Kroos and tells her that Dusk hasn't given them dreamlike lives; she has only sketched their lives out carelessly. "It's okay, it's okay. I'm here. I'm her big sister, after all."
And Nian appears before Lava as well, who was left in the dark without a single dream. Dodging the question of why Lava alone didn't fall into a dream, Nian tells her an old story.

blocks.cap: Long, long ago: a great hunt against the gods of heaven and earth in Yan.

blocks.x: The young True Lung threw the strength of the whole nation into a hunt against the arrogant gods of heaven and earth, who cared nothing for the people. The one who helped him was a being that had betrayed its own kind, and in his old age, rather than kill the last, oldest, and greatest of those beings, the True Lung made it serve Yan.

After that, the "gods" split themselves apart, dividing their power and souls among the pieces and hiding across the land. No dynasty anywhere in Terra had ever been able to seal away gods by imperial decree, Nian says. Yan really is a frightening place.
9. Big Sis's Two-Step Firecracker

Meanwhile, Kroos and Mr. Nothing wake up in the thatched cottage on Mount Hui-ch'i, and Dusk speaks coldly. Whatever Nian says, she has no intention of seeing her, so go home. For a rude bunch who have broken her peace again and again, that much punishment is light.

Then a ringing verse echoes from somewhere, and something explodes. It's a giant two-step firecracker of Nian's making, eight feet long and three feet wide. Nian points out that they may have been inside the painting from the moment they opened the door, or even from partway up the mountain. So much fit inside that tiny cottage, and no one could even see it as strange.

blocks.cap: "I'll break you and send you back to that mausoleum, 'Big Sis.'"

blocks.x: The sisters' fight that follows spreads from painting to painting. In the middle of it, Nian realizes that Dusk hasn't slept a wink in years. Because she knows she is only a Painting-Dweller, she is afraid that when she wakes, she will no longer exist.

When "we" wake and look down upon the land once more, Nian says, the you and me of now will be wiped away entirely, and she doesn't like that. Before "it" wakes, they have to borrow whatever they can and prepare. For themselves, and for the things they love.

Dusk pushes back. How can one part of a body resist the whole? Everything will vanish in the end, so what is the point? Is that really all the answer you came up with in all those years, Nian asks, and pulls out a second two-step firecracker.

Back in the thatched cottage, Nian asks Dusk to come to Rhodes Island with her. She cannot just stand by and watch her sink into madness and quietly vanish. Just as Dusk declares that today she is truly angry and squares up to her, an unexpected voice cuts in.
10. The Mountains Are but Mountains, the Water Is but Water

The voice belongs to Saga. Walking side by side with her self in the painting, she followed the roads of Yan back to her temple, and the moment she stepped through the gate, she remembered her head priest's sigh: "The mountains are but mountains, and the water is but water." When she came to, there was a dressing mirror in front of her, and when she turned her head, she was here.

Faced with someone who walked out of her painting on her own two feet, Dusk is at a loss for words. When Nian brings up a bet the two of them made long, long ago, Dusk finally admits she has lost. There's no point holding out, so she will stay by Nian's side and watch how far she gets.

And so the mission comes to an end. Nian, who had suggested eating something good on the way back, bickers with Dusk yet again over late-autumn scalebass versus hotpot, while Kroos has already mapped out a route that takes in seventeen local specialties. Mr. Nothing pesters them for a job, asking whether Rhodes Island is hiring.

Saga, meanwhile, doesn't go with them. She will wander wherever her heart leads, even beyond Yan. Hearing that her master is a hundred and twenty and still in good health, Dusk leaves a short message.
If you ever get the chance again, would you tell your master something for me? Adding that one extra word like that wasn't bad.

Then, the wasteland on the way home. Mr. Nothing spots a car tailing them and boasts that he'll teach them a lesson even without his fan, but when two more armed cars appear, he sheepishly turns to look at Lava. Lava sighs and steps forward.

blocks.cap: The wasteland on the way home. A car chasing Mr. Nothing closes in.

blocks.x: Epilogue. Will You Paint P'o-shan Village for Me?
One autumn, old and ill, Dawn lies awake night after night, thinking of the season when the hawthorn fruit ripens sweet. And at her bedside, after decades, Dusk comes to visit.

blocks.cap: A reunion after decades. Dawn has grown old; Dusk has not changed.

blocks.x: Dawn lost her home to a Catastrophe, was saved by Dusk, and lived for a long time inside Dusk's paintings. She made a bet that one day she would see through Dusk's paintings, the worlds within them, and Dusk herself, but after they parted, Dusk never came back.

Dusk chides Dawn for never once taking up a brush in her whole life when she had thought her a fine painter, yet says that Dawn may be the only one who ever truly surprised her. Dawn says she is at peace, and makes one last request: would Dusk paint P'o-shan Village for her?

All she remembers is the village's name and the pawnshop next to her house. How she wanted to be like the pawnshop keeper, always so neatly dressed. Dreams of meeting monsters on the distant mountain and losing her way. The Catastrophe clouds rising over its peak. Dusk answers that she has not left out a single thing.
Dawn asks Dusk to look at her with those eyes, and asks one last question.
Was my life... a happy one, I wonder?

And Dusk opens her eyes in a room on Rhodes Island. She tells Nian to get lost when Nian says they're one short for mahjong, and yet she is asking what kind of people the Doctor and Kal'tsit are, the ones in the operation files she secretly read.
Nian says she'll tell her everything, and that once she has heard it all, she'll understand why Nian likes this place.

The village where the sun and moon share one sky, the storyteller's face, the ink monsters. Nian's sister, the one Nian said Lava would know at a glance, was everywhere in that painting from the very start. And the painter who said we are all Painting-Dwellers wakes from her sleep, for the first time in a long while, beside her big sister.

act15d0.tagline: A researcher who quietly helped pull off a prison break gets cornered by the Ecological Director—who's rented out an entire bar—and ends up telling the whole jailbreak story from the top, only to run straight into the ugly truth about her company and her country. Still, there's one answer she holds onto to the end: Anthony isn't a lead. He's a person.

chars.name: Silence
chars.desc: A researcher from Rhine Lab's Structural department. She helped Anthony's prison break from behind the scenes.

chars.name: Mayer
chars.desc: A researcher from Rhine Lab Engineering. She followed Silence to Columbia. Pretty handy in the kitchen, too.

chars.name: Muelsyse
chars.desc: Director of Rhine Lab's Ecological department. She rented out an entire bar to summon Silence and company.

chars.name: Kafka
chars.desc: Silence's friend. She walks into Mansfield State Prison as an inmate—of her own free will.

chars.name: Robin
chars.desc: A woman who took an assassination contract to pay for her father's medical bills. She enters Mansfield State Prison as an inmate.

chars.name: Anthony
chars.desc: Only son of the fallen Simon family. He has spent six years locked up in Mansfield State Prison.

chars.name: Domma
chars.desc: A doctor and mortician who grew up inside Mansfield State Prison. Anthony's friend.

chars.name: Mina
chars.desc: A Liberi Kafka brought into the prison. Disguised as a laborer, she scopes out the prison's layout.

chars.name: Barton
chars.desc: Head jailer of Mansfield State Prison. Whenever the warden's away, he acts like he owns the place.

chars.name: Randal
chars.desc: Warden of Mansfield State Prison. He's the one who proposed turning an abandoned industrial platform into a prison.

chars.name: Jesselton
chars.desc: A man who comes and goes around the prison in a jailer's uniform. He keeps a quiet eye on Robin.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator. She offers Silence advice on her personal investigation.

chars.name: Saria
chars.desc: Former Defense Director of Rhine Lab. Now an operator at Rhodes Island.

chars.name: Ifrit
chars.desc: A girl who was once a Rhine Lab test subject. She now lives at Rhodes Island.

terms.name: Rhine Lab
terms.desc: A massive Columbian science corporation, split into departments like Structural, Ecological, and Energy.

terms.name: Energy Section
