terms.desc: One of Rhine Lab's departments. It works closely with Engineering.

terms.name: Mansfield State Prison
terms.desc: A mobile prison that roams the wastelands, docking at a city only once every few months.

terms.name: HydeBro
terms.desc: A building materials company in Bunkerhill City. The one that brought down Simon Co.

terms.name: Simon Co.
terms.desc: The company run by Anthony's family. It collapsed after being charged with smuggling Originium products.

terms.name: Diαbolic Crisis
terms.desc: An experimental accident inside Rhine Lab. It's what first made Silence start doubting the company.

blocks.x: A city in Columbia's borderlands. **Silence**, a researcher who left Rhine Lab to join Rhodes Island, gets a call over a Rhine Lab **internal frequency**. The voice on the other end says, 'I know you're the one who helped Anthony break out,' and asks to meet.

She and her Engineering colleague **Mayer** head to a bar without a single customer in it, and the one who greets them with a 'Hiya~' is **Muelsyse**, Rhine Lab's Ecological Director, who's rented out the whole place.

Not long ago, **Anthony Simon**, only son of a fallen family, escaped Mansfield State Prison—a prison on the move—and joined up with Silence's group. According to Silence, he's already left Columbia. What Muelsyse wants is to hear, from the very beginning, how that jailbreak actually played out inside the prison.

blocks.cap: "...Structural, Silence." Introducing herself to a director who insists these things need a little ritual.

blocks.x: 1. One Drink, One Question, One Answer

When Mayer asks whether she's the mastermind, it's Silence who shakes her head. If she were, she'd have no reason to track them down now that Anthony's gone. Muelsyse just smiles, pours them a drink, and proposes a game: they take turns, one question for one answer.

To the first question—how did you find us?—Muelsyse admits she has nothing to do with the **HydeBro** strike teams chasing Anthony, but yes, she did borrow their intel network. HydeBro is a heavyweight in Bunkerhill City's building materials trade: it fought **Simon Co.**, a logistics firm that muscled its way into building materials, so fiercely that rumors of bloodshed went around—and came out on top.

blocks.cap: Two companies that once split Bunkerhill City's building materials market. In the end, only one was left standing.

blocks.x: Anthony is the only son of Smith Simon, CEO of that very Simon Co. All Muelsyse knows is how it starts and how it ends—HydeBro's carefully laid assassination plan ended in a prison break—so she wants to hear everything in between.

blocks.cap: "The only parts I understand are the beginning—" Anthony, six years behind bars.

blocks.x: The helper Silence sent into the prison wasn't even a Rhine Lab employee—it was her friend **Kafka**. Saying she'd always wanted to try real prison life, Kafka went in as an inmate, and even brought along **Mina**, a Liberi, disguised as a carpentry worker.
2. Mansfield's Most Popular Group Activity

The story rewinds to Mansfield State Prison four and a half months earlier. Dropped in among the Infected inmates, Kafka had just swept the poker table with a royal flush and had everyone calling her 'Kafka, ma'am.' There were whispers she was dealing from the bottom of the deck, but hey—both her hands were empty.

Mansfield is a prison on the move: it roams the wastelands and docks at a city once every few months to take on supplies and new inmates. The Non-Infected live in A-Zone, the Infected in B-Zone, and the tower in the middle holds C-Zone, home to serious offenders who'll likely never get out.

blocks.cap: A prison that wanders the wastelands with an entire artificial mountain on its back—Mansfield.

blocks.x: That day just happened to be A-Zone vs. B-Zone brawl day. Instead of breaking it up, the jailers were betting on who'd win, and in the middle of the chaos, Kafka took note of a woman keeping one hand hidden.

Head jailer **Barton** shows up late and launches into a long-winded speech: 'This is prison. Not your battlefield.' He's the type to play king of the castle whenever Warden **Randal** is away. And the 'reinforcement' called in to end the fight? Anthony—a face Kafka already knew.

Anthony brought C-Zone to heel the moment he arrived, yet he's so polite to everyone that the inmates all follow him, and even Barton can't look him in the eye. Kafka bides her time, since she has 'something to discuss' with him—out of the jailers' earshot.
3. The Infirmary They Call the Morgue
Back at the bar, Silence asks Mayer to cook something, mostly to get her out of the room. There was something she still hadn't told Mayer: Rhine Lab's **Energy Section** is the one backing HydeBro.

blocks.cap: A line running back from HydeBro. Its far end reached all the way inside Rhine Lab.

blocks.x: Silence didn't even know there was an assassination plot. Half a year ago, all she'd figured out was that Anthony was being held in a different prison from his family, so she sent Kafka in thinking: great if she can meet him and help, no harm done if not.

When Muelsyse casually brings up the 'Diαbolic Crisis,' Silence coldly cuts her off: if this is about **Ifrit**, the conversation ends here. Muelsyse apologizes, and her next question is about **Robin**. She definitely went in as an assassin sent to kill Anthony—so how did she end up on the escape team?

Around then, Robin, freshly arrived, was bandaging an inmate hurt in the brawl. The infirmary is run solely by **Domma**, a doctor who doubles as a mortician, and since it's attached to the morgue, everyone calls it 'the Morgue' and steers clear.

Robin says she used to work for a private security firm and took this risk to pay for her father's treatment—he lost his job, drank himself sick, and wrecked his liver. One of the stories she gets in return for the bandages is about a tombstone outside the prison. It's for inmates who 'escaped'—and every one of them died in the wastelands.

Back in her cell, Robin thinks of 'Generous J'—the one who handed her a big pile of money and asked her to get into Mansfield and kill someone. She knows it isn't a good thing to do, but Robin resolves to give it her all, for her father's sake.

blocks.cap: "...Pop, looks like Anthony's a pricklier problem than I'd heard."

blocks.x: 4. A Country Where Even Prisons Turn a Profit

Back at the bar, Muelsyse first spells out what Mansfield really is. To Warden Randal—the man who came up with the idea of turning an abandoned industrial platform into a prison—it's a money machine: put someone you hate in there to die, or put someone you want protected in there to keep them safe.

HydeBro probably tried to bribe him too, but Anthony carries a lot of clout, and if he died the fallout would be hard to handle—so Randal likely played it safe. That's why they sent in assassins disguised as inmates, none of whom even knew the others existed.

Why go after Anthony alone? Because his family, locked up in Bunkerhill City Prison, didn't even need killing. In Columbia, Muelsyse says, death is far from the worst thing that can happen to a person. Silence starts to ask how a mere company could reach all the way into a prison—then arrives at the answer herself and falls silent. She hands the story off to Mayer and retreats to the kitchen.

Meanwhile, back in the prison, Robin has landed C-Zone cleaning duty with a homemade weapon tucked away. But before she can even look for an opening, two B-Zone inmates in Anthony's room knock out the jailers and prisoners and go for Anthony. Yet another set of assassins, separate from Robin.

blocks.cap: More assassins hiding among the cleaning crew. They beat Robin to the punch.

blocks.x: A small woman charges in yelling 'Whyn'tcha take this!' and gets flattened in one hit, and a jailer who came along with them lets out a snort. Then Robin takes a blow from behind and blacks out too.

According to Mayer, who picks up the story, Kafka was only faking it. Once Anthony takes down the two hitmen, she asks him to block the surveillance camera and whispers that she's here to help. The two head for the one person Anthony trusts in this whole prison: his friend Domma, and her infirmary.

blocks.cap: Infirmary and morgue in one. The only place in the prison where Anthony can let his guard down.

blocks.x: When he hears that Simon Co. was seized for smuggling Originium products and his whole family is in Bunkerhill City Prison, Anthony slams the table. Still, he says he's glad they're alive, and when he hears HydeBro is behind it all, he repeats the name his father used to bring up so often.

He's serving life without parole, so Kafka suggests a jailbreak. Anthony confides that the special treatment he gets comes on the warden's orders—and that he even suspects being sent to this prison was his father's plan from the start. Then he bows his head: 'Please, help me break out.'
5. A Person With No Lines, and the Notion of Doing Good

Back at the bar, Muelsyse brings up the Diαbolic Crisis with Mayer. After that incident, Defense Director **Saria** took all the blame and left the company—but the real reason, she says, was a falling-out with 'Control.' Saria had lines research must never cross. Control has no lines at all, so long as nothing gets in research's way.
Then, petting Mayer's robot 'Mibo,' she invites Mayer to come work in her department—and Mayer's answer is a breezy 'I'll think about it.'

Around the same time, Robin wakes up in the prison infirmary, and Anthony politely asks: they found a weapon on you, so are you an assassin too? Then he tells her he plans to break out and go after the people who destroyed his family, and asks for her help—once she's made up her mind, she can let Domma know.
Back at the bar, Muelsyse marvels at what a sophisticated mind game that was, then adds: they had no idea. Their whole plan had long since been in the palm of a man named **Jesselton**.

Meanwhile, in a corner of the kitchen with a bottle at her side, Silence apologizes to Mayer for dragging her into this and tells her about the Energy Section. Mayer takes it in stride—she always found the Energy Director scary anyway.

What Silence recalls is a conversation with **Kal'tsit** in a Rhodes Island corridor. Kal'tsit said Rhodes Island couldn't act as a mediator, then asked why she was so fixated on someone who had nothing to do with her. When Silence answered that she wanted to know what kind of company she'd been working for, Kal'tsit told her she might be disappointed.

blocks.cap: "But it'll be far better than knowing nothing." What Kal'tsit offered wasn't official support—just one piece of personal advice.

blocks.x: I hope you are able to maintain your notion from start to finish. ...The notion that you are doing something good.

But now, Silence says, she isn't sure it really is a good thing. Digging through her mentor's files after the Diαbolic Crisis, she learned that cases like the Simon family's are everywhere—in Rhine Lab, and all across Columbia—and now she's afraid she won't have the courage to deal with them.

Mayer passes along something Kafka once told Mina: she and Silence became friends after butting heads; Silence sees the world a little too rosily, but she's the only friend like that Kafka has, which is exactly why she treasures her.

After a cup of tea to sober up, Silence pushes down the urge to run and heads back to the table, determined to see this through. Not before leaving one remark: she'd better make a few preparations of her own.
6. Generous J
Once she's back, Silence says she's decided to be candid. It's because of one line she's never forgotten, from a mentor she doesn't particularly like.
What makes the schemers sweat is open talk.
Then she sets the record straight. Robin didn't join the group that easily—before that, someone from HydeBro's side paid her a visit.

Around the same time, as Robin agonizes in her cell, a jailer stops in front of her. It's the jailer who dropped by the infirmary the day Anthony reached out to her—Jesselton. He tells her he's an assassin after Anthony too, and that he overheard every word of the offer made in the infirmary.

What Jesselton reveals is something even Robin didn't know. Her father, once one of HydeBro's most capable men, ran BlackCloud Trade—and six years ago, it was one of the last companies the crumbling Simon family sank its teeth into.

'Pain's an equal mistress.' The son of a fallen family can't pay for her father's treatment, but he can, so she should think it over carefully—and from the way he says it, Robin realizes that Generous J, the one who hired her, is this very man.
Not long after, when Domma asks if she's made up her mind, Robin answers: '...I'm in.'
7. The One Who Won't Leave, and a 25-Year-Old Blueprint

Back at the bar, Muelsyse sums it up: Jesselton talked Robin into joining the group as a spy. One of Parasol's ace hatchet men and HydeBro's trump card, a man who'll move for anyone with money—Jesselton was a name even Muelsyse knew.
Silence says she can't stand the man, but snaps that what he told Robin was at least more honest than Muelsyse, who's tested her again and again. Muelsyse meekly apologizes.

Around then, in the infirmary, Domma confides to Robin that she has no intention of leaving with them. She was a child the previous mortician picked up while the prison was docked, and growing up surrounded by nothing but violence and death, she's afraid of the outside.

Anthony was her only friend—the one who recommended interesting books and told her stories about the outside world. When Domma says that if anything goes wrong, she'll make up for it even if it costs her life, Robin's face clouds over.

Even so, Robin tells her it'd be a real shame never to experience the outside just because she's scared—if anyone shouldn't be living in a prison like this, it's her. And Anthony would want her to have a better life, too. At that, Domma asks if she can think it over again.

When the story reaches the escape plan, Muelsyse spreads out a floor plan of the prison. The key was a 25-year-old blueprint gathering dust in the library—a library that only exists thanks to Anthony's suggestion. The C-Zone tower was built to sink underground in one piece, and from the main control room hidden at its top, you could drop the tower fast and even mess with the power.

blocks.cap: Cross-section of the C-Zone tower. A sinking tower, and the main control room at its top.

blocks.x: Domma knew the way out. One useless leftover passage under the mountain ran right past the morgue, so the group took turns heading down to dig through a wall three meters thick. Then they stole Barton's keycard, and during the few days the prison was docked at a city, confirmed that the tunnel reached the outside.
8. Escape Day, and One Person Missing

After Mina left the prison ahead of the others with the construction crew, D-Day was set for a cleaning day while the prison was docked at Nulaiteburgh. The plan was to sink the tower and cut the power from the control room, meet Domma underground, and slip out through the tunnel. Domma had even sewn a work outfit sized for Anthony.

But at the appointed time, Robin doesn't show. Kafka and Anthony go up to the control room alone, and in that dust-covered room they come face to face with Robin, who got there first with a backup card in hand.

Anthony subdues the prisoners with Robin in an instant, but Robin triggers a bomb, and the control room goes up in flames. Kafka, who'd said she forgot which button was which, manages to press one, and it's Anthony who catches Robin as she's about to fall into the elevator shaft.

blocks.cap: One button pressed at the top. The whole tower sinks, and every light in the prison goes out.

blocks.x: Inside the tower, sunk into darkness, Anthony tells her there's no need to think of this as betrayal. They were never close enough to speak of trust. But he knows the feelings she showed while they were together weren't an act, so he asks what drove her to this.

Robin tells him everything. Her kind father fell apart into drink and rage after his company went under; her mother left; all that remained was debt and illness. And everyone just keeps telling her to choose. She's so tired.
You have to think everything through and make your own choices. Then, you need to take responsibility for each of those choices. Otherwise, you'll never be able to take your fate into your own hands.

What matters most is the courage to choose, Anthony says. He won't claim to forgive her easily, but he asks her to think again about what she wants to do. Just then, a voice carries over from the direction of Domma's room: no need to worry about not being able to find me.
9. Five Seconds

In the infirmary, Jesselton has a group of prisoners holding Domma. He tells Robin that if she kills Anthony now, he'll pay her the promised money, and begins to count. What he wants to see isn't a killing, he says, but the moment a person faced with a choice casts off the face they wore before.

Five, four, three. Domma tries to take her own life so Anthony won't be held back on her account, but a prisoner stops her. Anthony says neither revenge nor the work ahead of him matters more than a friend's life—he won't sacrifice Domma, even if it costs him his own.
Two, one. Robin walks slowly toward Anthony and swings her dagger. The blade isn't aimed at Anthony, but at the prisoner holding Domma.

The Simon family's fall may have been what broke her father, Robin says, but what came after was his own responsibility—she knew it all along and just didn't want to admit it. She'll find another way to pay for his treatment, and if she can't, she'll answer to her father with her life.
That's my decision.

Jesselton says with a laugh that he'd like to applaud, then tells them that having no future begins right now. In that moment, the shackles Anthony and Kafka are wearing—restraint devices—bring them both down.

blocks.cap: "You haven't forgotten the shackles on you, have you?" A man who always has a backup plan ready.

blocks.x: Anthony gets back up anyway, and before him, Jesselton's hands turn into black blades. With Originium Arts that manipulate iron, plus metal plates implanted under his skin with Rhine Lab technology, even Anthony and Robin together can't land a hit.

On July 24th, six years ago, Anthony received nothing but a message from his father telling him to run. He fled without even seeing his parents' faces, and was caught. When Jesselton tells him there's nothing waiting for him outside, Anthony shouts back: he's getting out to find out what happened, and to let the people who destroyed his family know they aren't finished yet.

Just as Jesselton laughs that the other jailers will be here soon, a voice cuts in from the passage: the reaper won't be coming for a while—she's already dealt with the other guards. It's Saria, former Defense Director of Rhine Lab.
Jesselton recognizes her. She's the one who personally rejected his résumé. Each time their blades clash, it's Jesselton who gives ground; Saria's blade doesn't take a single crack.

blocks.cap: Twin black blades against a white hand-blade. The one cracking was Jesselton.

blocks.x: 'You're too small-minded.' With one final strike, Jesselton's blades are cut away, leaving a long, deep wound across his body.
Saria asks Anthony only one question: has he ever heard the name Ferdinand? When he answers that he thinks he heard it from his father, Saria murmurs under her breath. So it was his doing after all.
Epilogue. Not a Lead, but a Person
When the story ends, a single name is left hanging in the bar: Ferdinand, Director of Rhine Lab's Energy Section. But what truly shook Muelsyse was why Saria showed up at Mansfield.

Silence turns the question right back on her: Saria was supposed to be Muelsyse's helper, and she broke their agreement. Muelsyse finally admits that, with no one in the company she could trust, she told Saria about the whole affair.

Saria neither kept Anthony by her side nor handed him over to Muelsyse; instead, she had him go to Rhodes Island with Silence's group. As for Jesselton, Muelsyse can only guess that he was exposed as a fake jailer and locked up.

So Muelsyse's real business was a deal. If Silence builds a bridge between her and Rhodes Island, Muelsyse will give her a chance to return to Rhine Lab—a chance to make up for the Diαbolic Crisis. Not dressing the deal up as something pretty, she says, is how she shows Silence respect.
Silence refuses. Muelsyse never once asked what Silence wants for Anthony, she points out—she's called him a 'lead' this whole time, and Silence hates that word.
Anthony isn't a 'lead' to me. He's a person; he's alive.

When Muelsyse asks whether Silence really thinks she'll just let them go, Silence says she made a few arrangements over the meal and calls out a name. Anthony—who supposedly left Columbia—appears right there. His departure was a decoy; she'd brought him along just in case.

When Muelsyse invites him to come with her, Anthony answers: only if you can take me down. And he adds that there truly are beautiful things in this land. Muelsyse laughs that she's lost this round—the body sitting here is just a clone, and she isn't confident it could beat a burly man.
Before leaving, she points out that Simon Co. wasn't a pure victim either: both sides had plans to get rid of the other, and the Simons were simply one step too slow. Anthony can't deny it.

If you want to do the right thing, you need to first be able to tell what actually is the right thing. Beyond that, you also need to understand that doing the right thing doesn't necessarily mean you don't have to pay the price.
Muelsyse's clone melts into water, and from beyond that water comes her voice, saying she'll keep her hands off the Anthony matter. Only then do Silence's legs give out, and Mayer has to hold her up.

blocks.cap: An empty bar. The Ecological Director who sat across from them dissolved into water and was gone.

blocks.x: When Anthony asks what kind of place Rhodes Island is, Silence answers that it's a long road, so she'll explain slowly. Anthony says he's starting to look forward to this journey.

It was a night that began with one question for one answer. She still doesn't fully know what the right thing is, but on the last question, at least, Silence never wavered. Anthony isn't a lead—he's a person.

act13d5.tagline: The youngest daughter of a fading knightly house debuts in the arena behind her aunt's back — and on a stage tangled up in ads, bets, and backroom deals, she ends up asking who she's really fighting for. And then, after six years, the light returns.

chars.name: Maria Nearl
chars.desc: The youngest daughter of the Nearl family. A Kuranta girl who loves tinkering with machines, she throws herself into knight sports for the sake of her declining family · Operator Blemishine

chars.name: Zofia
chars.desc: Aunt to Margaret and Maria. A retired competition knight only five years older than Maria · Operator Whislash

chars.name: Margaret Nearl
chars.desc: Maria's older sister, and 'the Radiant Knight,' the youngest Major champion in history. She was exiled from Kazimierz six years ago · Operator Nearl the Radiant Knight

chars.name: Młynar
chars.desc: Uncle to Margaret and Maria. He has stepped away from knighthood and lives as a company employee.

chars.name: Bald Marcin
chars.desc: A former competition knight who lost an arm in the arena. He now owns the bar where retired knights gather.

chars.name: Vogelweide
chars.desc: A retired level-2 campaign knight. A regular at Marcin's bar who is forever bickering with Kowal.

chars.name: Kowal
chars.desc: A former senior craftsman of the Craftsman's Guild. He taught Maria how to maintain gear, and has sworn never to make knight equipment again.

chars.name: Greatmouth Mob
chars.desc: The arena's motor-mouthed MC. He never stops weaving ads and betting pitches into his match commentary.

chars.name: Szewczyk
chars.desc: Vanguard captain of the Roar Knightclub. A veteran competition knight who fights with a crossbow.

chars.name: Olmer Ingra

blocks.x: Central Kazimierz. Kawalerielki, a Grand Knight Territory formed by an alliance of four cities. Here, knights don't fight on the battlefield — they fight in the arena, beneath sponsor logos and betting boards. People call it knight sports.

Right in the middle of one of its streets, two old men who've just driven their car into a tree are busy blaming each other, while a blonde Kuranta girl pops the hood. She sparks the engine back to life with Originium Arts, a knack said to be the spitting image of her grandfather's. This girl is **Maria Nearl**, the youngest daughter of a knightly family in decline.

Of course, the revived car promptly overloads its engine, hits 80 mph without anyone touching the accelerator, and vanishes down the road. Maria just laughs it off sheepishly: "I messed up again, ehe."

blocks.cap: The streets of Kawalerielki. Somebody crashes a car, and somebody else fixes it.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, over at the Roar Arena, MC **Greatmouth Mob** is shouting himself hoarse introducing today's first competitor. A rookie with no title and no club — but with a surname that everyone in Kazimierz knows.
"Mariiiaaa!! Neeeaaarl!!!!" Today is the day the Radiant Knight's little sister makes her arena debut.
1. Into the Arena to Save the Family (Don't Tell Auntie)

News of her debut hits the sports headlines that very day. Over at a bar frequented by retired knights, Maria is busy fixing the jukebox — and when the door bangs open hard enough to nearly break, she ducks behind it.
"MA! RI! A!"

Striding in with a beaming smile is Aunt **Zofia**. She's aunt to both Margaret and Maria, but being only five years older than Maria, she can't stand being called 'Auntie.' In her day, she was a competition knight who ruled the arena under the title of the 'Whislash' Knight.

Maria has her reasons, though. The family is down to selling off its furniture, and the Knights Association keeps pressing them: a family without a representative knight can't be recognized as nobility. Her grandfather has passed away, her uncle keeps the Association at arm's length, and her older sister **Margaret Nearl** was driven out of Kazimierz long ago.

Asked by Zofia to talk Maria out of it, the bar's owner **Bald Marcin** surprisingly suggests they let her give it a shot. He does, however, hold up the mechanical arm that winning in the arena left him with — and adds that these days, even wiping a single glass is a struggle.
There's no mercy or respect in the arena. The only thing real there is the blood that splatters the ground.

Even so, Maria won't back down. As the youngest generation of the family, she says, she wants to protect what her sister and grandfather protected. At that, the two old regulars who crashed the car earlier — retired campaign knight **Vogelweide** and craftsman **Kowal** — raise their glasses: "To Maria!"
Then Maria blurts out, "Oh, I know! Zofia can just teach me!" — and the look in Zofia's eyes changes. Next morning: report to the garden training ground.

blocks.cap: Marcin's bar, the hangout of retired knights. The door gets replaced every time Zofia drops by.

blocks.x: 2. The Coach Who Promised to Use Only One Hand

But as Maria heads out, her uncle **Młynar** stops her. He coldly tells her that neither knight sports nor her wanting to compete in them is worthy of the Nearl name — and then, when his boss calls, he retreats upstairs, repeating "I'm sorry" over and over.

Then, Zofia's garden training ground. Even with Zofia fighting one-handed as promised, Maria can't land a single counterattack in ten minutes — and she's told that if she steps into the arena with her current skills, she'll be nothing but a sacrificial lamb.

Training was brutal. To survive team melees — one of which supposedly lasted an entire day — Zofia drilled her on nothing but the basics for a week, then three. The truth is, she designed the regimen hoping Maria would wear out and give up. But Maria, though she felt half dead, stayed cheerful to the very end.

Watching her, Zofia quietly grips her sword hilt with the hand she hasn't used all this time. But when she tries to draw, pain spreads from her waist down to her wrist, and she hurriedly lets go before the feeling leaves her.

About a month later, Maria absentmindedly grips her sword in a reverse hold — and knocks Zofia's sword clean out of her hand. Zofia finally gives her blessing and declares she'll be Maria's coach from start to finish... while Maria, of all things, flops down right there and falls asleep.

blocks.cap: Zofia's garden, where the weeds supposedly grow thicker than the lakeside woods. This is Maria's training ground.

blocks.x: 3. Plastic Rhythm and Pegasian Eyes

Her first match after training is against the vanguard captain of the Roar Knightclub, the 'Plastic Knight' **Szewczyk**. Before the match, someone calling himself Major 'staff' visited him with an order: wear sponsor Roar Guards' new Jack2 armor, and drag the fight out as long as possible. The pay? Three times his after-tax income from last year.
Spotting Zofia in the stands, Szewczyk sneers that he thought she'd never come back after getting hurt in the Major. Zofia fires right back: "You'd better watch yourself, Sir Plastic Toy."

blocks.cap: Qualifier matchup: Maria Nearl VS the Roar Knightclub. The MC kindly asks you to cheer with your wallets.

blocks.x: Right before the match, Maria repeats the Nearl family motto to herself: "Fear neither hardship nor darkness!" But once it starts, she spends nearly twenty minutes getting pummeled by Szewczyk's 'Plastic Rhythm' — stop, shoot, move, repeat.
That's when she remembers what Zofia told her on the training ground: observe a lot, and think. Over those words, a voice from long ago echoes: "You are gifted with a pair of pegasian eyes."

Looking again, she notices something odd. That armor, which wasn't in any product catalog, is running far too hot. Maria feints with her Arts to trigger its forced-cooling system, then strikes the instant the armor beeps a warning and locks up.

The finishing blow is a move Maria has been imitating for years. Zofia, in the stands, recognizes that reverse-grip strike as the one Margaret used on the day she won — and with that single hit, Szewczyk goes out cold.
Just before the winner is announced, someone sneaks into the commentary booth and whispers to Mob: let's say Szewczyk lost due to 'inexperience.' That's what 'Mr. Pavel' wants.
4. A Toast, a Refusal, and 'the Butcher of the Field'

After the match, the bar throws a victory party. Zofia, who has just watched her first match as a coach, silently knocks back drink after drink until her tongue is tied in knots and she's laid out on the sofa. "Don' call me Auntieee..."

Marcin fills them in on Zofia's past. Inspired by Margaret's championship, Zofia asked the old knights to train her and made it to the main stage without ever taking a single corporate sponsor — only to be badly injured in the Final 16 by the 'Fissure' Knight, who had flawless gear and full backing behind him.

Just then, an employee from a food company called Słoma pays a visit. His offer: join the Eszeweria Knightclub, which Słoma sponsors, and they'll promise her a peerage and a title in the name of the General Chamber of Commerce. Even Zofia, now sober, says it might be worth taking if it means protecting the family without getting hurt.

But Maria shakes her head. "I don't want the Nearl family crest to become some corporate accessory." The rejected employee, on the verge of tears, leaves behind a strange request: if someone else comes knocking next time, please accept if at all possible.

Then her next opponent is announced: the 'Brassrust Knight' **Olmer Ingra** of the Bloodboil Knightclub — 'the Butcher of the Field,' who has crippled opponents time and again, only to be acquitted every time by a National Council blinded by corporate donations.

blocks.cap: Maria Nearl VS the Bloodboil Knightclub. This match has no rules and no safety measures.

blocks.x: Right before she walks out, Zofia begs her for the first time: couldn't she forfeit just this one match? Maria's answer is short. "Now that I've entered... there's no retreat for a knight."
Facing Ingra's axe, Maria is soon covered in blood. Zofia screams at her to surrender, but her head is spinning so badly she can barely hear, and her shield grows heavier and heavier.

Before Ingra, who relishes the slaughter, Maria begins to question things for the first time. Is killing your opponent what knight sports are about? Is that monster a knight too? And what is a knight, anyway?

blocks.cap: Just before she blacks out — her sister, as she remembers her.

blocks.x: To be a knight is to be the noble light that illuminates the land.
When she opens her eyes, she's at home. She threw away her shield and fought back with a sword wreathed in light; in the end Maria went down — but so did Ingra, leaving the score tied.

Zofia lays down the law: get hurt like this one more time, and Maria's done competing. The old sword in the room turns out to be one Zofia used long ago — she'd brought it along to kill Ingra herself if he did anything to Maria.
Meanwhile, a new face walks into Marcin's bar. The adorable customer, **Platinum**, orders a 'Thorn Tear' because she likes the name.
5. A Predator System Melee and an Infected Who Smiles
Elsewhere, in a penthouse overlooking the city, **Spokesman Czarny** of the General Chamber of Commerce slides a secret contract over to Mob. As of today, he says, you're one of my people.

blocks.cap: A penthouse looking down on the city. This is where Czarny made the MC 'one of his people.'

blocks.x: Back on her feet, Maria finds a whopping thirteen sponsorship offers piled up in front of her — and decides to toss every one. The 'Nearl' that her grandfather and parents spent their whole lives protecting isn't something you can express with the numbers and charts of a brokerage report.
Instead, she picks a 15-knight melee at the Fireblade Arena. But just before the match, a new rule is announced: the 'Predator System,' where every point someone gains is a point someone else loses.
At the starting line, a knight who introduces herself as 'just a passing fan' challenges Maria out of nowhere — and then really does chase her around the whole match, stealing her points.

In the middle of crossing blades, she casually tosses out: "D'ja know? Fun fact, I'm Infected." Ever since the Blood Knight won, she explains, the Infected can become knights too — but only after surviving a cage crawling with gloompincers and stepping over the blood of other Infected.

She says she truly respects the Radiant Knight, so she doesn't knock Maria out — and the points she took can count as tuition for teaching her in Whislash's place. When Maria answers with a burst of light and snatches one point back, the knight laughs: now that's more like the Radiant Knight's little sister.

The winner is the 'Flametail Knight' **Sona** with 22 points, and Maria takes third. As the final signal sounds, their blades stop just shy of touching — and Sona playfully gives Maria's shield a little tap.
6. The People Who Want Her to Stop
As Maria racks up win after win, Marcin's bar is swamped with tourists. One even recognizes Marcin and chokes up: "The 'Tremoriron Knight' Marcin?"

After closing, Zofia says something unexpected. Maria already has enough points — she should run the next sprint race, then sit out every match for the rest of the season. According to a rumor passed along by the Słoma employee, who came all the way to the manor, Maria has caught the eye of the Knights Association's higher-ups too quickly, and if she doesn't quit at the right moment, 'they' will make their move.
In the arena, there's no victory for knights. Every victory belongs to Kazimierz... to the corporations.

Maria can't accept that. "I'm going to keep winning until I can't win anymore!" Zofia says that's exactly why she has to stop, tells her she'll file with the Association to suspend her matches, and storms out of the bar.

Meanwhile, Szewczyk — informed by Czarny, who went so far as to bring up his child's birthday, that he has been cut from the Roar Knightclub's roster — comes to Marcin's bar after Maria finishes the sprint race in second place. He leaves behind a rumor that the Radiant Knight is not actually Infected, and a warning that Czarny is likely targeting Maria as well. He became a knight, he says, after watching Marcin fight in his younger days. "Now, I'm going my own way." Marcin sees him off with a word of caution.

At home, Młynar is waiting for Maria. Margaret never saw her own foolishness, he tells her, not until the very end; she changed nothing and left the family's elders to clean up after her. Maria finally pushes back. Isn't he the one bowing and scraping to the corporations while he watches the family crumble?

Młynar doesn't argue. He admits that he is now nothing more than a burdenbeast bought by the corporations. To a niece who will not change her mind, he leaves only one line — "You're just like Margaret" — before being called away to a meeting.

blocks.cap: The living room of the Nearl manor. Uncle and niece never come to understand each other.

blocks.x: 7. Honor Has Merely Been Forgotten

Then Czarny comes to the bar himself to announce the next match. He needles the old men by calling Vogelweide by his old name, 'Batbayar,' which no one has used in half a century, and says that honor has merely been forgotten amid progress.
Most unfortunately, the people of Kazimierz no longer need honor.

The next opponent is the captain of the Blade Helmet Knightclub, the 'Left-hand Knight' **Tytus Topola** — a heavyweight Maria should never have drawn with her current points. Czarny offers to guarantee the Nearl family's standing as knightly nobility, even if she's eliminated partway, so long as she joins a knightclub of his choosing. Maria replies that she will make Kazimierz acknowledge the Nearls.
Then Czarny asks her a question in return: what exactly does she intend to prove in knight sports? Maria cannot answer. Czarny takes an incoming call and leaves.

At that very moment, Sona bursts into the bar carrying the badly wounded Ashlock Knight, Greynuty. It was an Armorless Union attack. While Maria tends to the wounded, the old men take up their bows and stand outside the door, and Marcin murmurs under his breath, "...They're here."

Three days later, on the morning of the match, the two leave, saying they don't want to cause the Nearls any more trouble. That day, the Fireblade Arena is packed with twelve news outlets and a crowd that leaves not a single seat empty.

blocks.cap: Maria Nearl VS the Blade Helmet Knightclub. Unprecedented bets piled up before the knights even entered.

blocks.x: The moment the match begins, Tytus knocks Maria's sword away. He waits for her to pick it up — then knocks it away again. The best way to stamp out a knight, he says, is to stamp out her dignity.
Maria's light is crumpled, shattered, and sullied.
8. A Small Light That Won't Go Out

At that same hour, back at the manor, Zofia finds her own old sword, restored by Maria as good as new and left out for her. It was the sword Maria's grandfather had given her. After a moment lost in memory, Zofia turns down even a ride and runs to the arena.

Meanwhile, word reaches the bar that Sona's group, stripped of their knight status, has slipped into the sewer pipes along with Infected children they bought out of the arena with everything they owned. Watching Maria on the screen, Marcin mutters that it isn't that she can't win — it's that she mustn't.
One hour and twenty-seven minutes into the match, Maria has fallen and risen again and again. Zofia reaches the stands and shouts: "Maria! Get up!"

Through her fading consciousness, she hears her grandfather's voice. The Nearl family motto is to fear neither hardship nor darkness, he says, and when Margaret chose a different path, he was truly glad. That child wants to become a light, he says, and drive away hardship and darkness.
Rising once more, Maria murmurs, "Uncle Młynar... you're wrong. It isn't... all just sighs..." Then, like her sister, she turns her wrist with her Arts and blocks Tytus's attacks — once, then again.
At last Tytus settles into a stance, ready to take her attack, and asks: why did she enter knight sports? For honor? Wealth? Family?
For... myself. That's all... Mr. Tytus.

Felled by a lightning-fast feint and the Arts gathered in her shield, Tytus concedes defeat: "You really do have the blood of a pegasus." The arena erupts with cheers that the Nearl family has worked another miracle.

blocks.cap: Maria raises her sword to the cheers. The tearing pain in her arm is drowned out by the applause.

blocks.x: Raising her sword, Maria thinks: honor, wealth, the family's revival — and yet something seems to be missing.
Zofia runs to hold her up and apologizes for taking her feelings too lightly — you're just like your sister, she says. Maria quietly shakes her head. "Maybe I... really am different from her."
9. One Empty Place, and Knights Not on the Bracket
After the match, Marcin goes to Młynar and asks him to help Maria. Młynar turns his back. "Any trouble those two sisters make should be theirs to sort out."

Meanwhile, in a corridor lined with portraits of past champions, Czarny stands face to face with the youngest 'Platinum' in Armorless Union history. The Black Knight, a three-time champion, had left Kazimierz as if handed over to a bigwig from Kjerag, and the Radiant Knight's place stood empty. Czarny asks her to keep watch on Młynar Nearl.

blocks.cap: The corridor of champions' portraits. Only the Radiant Knight's place is empty.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, rubbing ointment into Maria's wounds, Zofia tells her that Margaret, too, knew better than anyone what knight sports meant — and entered anyway, and reached the top. Perhaps, she says, that victory carried a hope that more people like her and Maria would come along.

Next is a rare two-on-two team battle. Zofia found Maria a partner: the 'Fartooth Knight' Justyna, a crossbow master who refuses corporate sponsorship and is building a knightclub on her own. But on the day of the match, the Fartooth Knight does not show. That day's sports papers report that she was caught up in a brawl between fans, badly injured, and is now missing.
Zofia tries to withdraw her, but Maria is already standing alone in the arena. Forfeiting before it has even begun, she says, is not something a knight does.

blocks.cap: Maria Nearl VS the Snowyheel Knightclub. That is what the bracket said.

blocks.x: But when her opponents enter with heavy footsteps, the 20,000-seat arena falls deathly silent. Even Tytus, in the stands, murmurs, "Not them." A shaken Mob introduces the pair as 'the Corrupted Knight and the Withered Knight.' And the crowd, realizing that the terror is aimed not at them but at one girl, applauds.

The two Sarkaz knights' mist smothers Maria's Arts and makes her wounds rot. Mob receives orders not to accept any forfeit. When Marcin holds back Zofia, who is trying to leap in, she cries out: "Dying together is better than Maria dying alone!"

At the same hour, Platinum blocks the way of Vogelweide and Kowal as they hurry toward the arena. She mentions that the previous Platinum's first mission was the assassination of a beautiful female campaign knight — and the two old men, just back from visiting the grave of their 'captain,' raise their weapons. "You have no right to speak that name."
And in the middle of the arena, a Sarkaz hammer rises high above the fallen Maria's head. In that instant, her vision fills with light — and someone sends the hammer flying.
10. The Radiant Knight

In a corner of the stands, an old campaign knight looks at that light and recalls an old story. On the day they were driven back by Ursus to the last line of defense, an old, golden-haired Pegasus appeared at Kazimierz's final encampment — and that dawn, two suns rose over the horizon.
And now, the sun bows its head to welcome a knight returned home. "Stand up, Maria." Standing before Maria as she raises her head is her sister Margaret, who left Kazimierz six years ago.
"You've done well, Maria." Through tears, Maria asks what took her so long, while Mob shouts himself hoarse that the exiled Radiant Knight has returned to save her sister.

As her sister worries over her wounds, Maria steps forward. Margaret always said a knight raises a shield to protect others — but in this arena, there is no one weak for her to protect. "I'll be your shield." Margaret sets down her shield and grips her hammer with both hands.

blocks.cap: The elder sister who set down her shield, and the younger sister who became her shield.

blocks.x: To be a knight! — Is to be the noble light that illuminates the land!

Each swing of the hammer bursts with a light that erases the two Sarkaz's Arts, while Maria blocks arrows forged from Arts. In the stands, Marcin is reminded of the old master of the Nearl house in his younger days.

After the final blow, the two Sarkaz sink to their knees. Margaret kneels on one knee before them and holds out her hand. "You should not give up on your destiny." They do not take it. They have no strength left to stand.
Turning away, Margaret says, "We've won." Czarny's instruction to Mob is a single word — concede — and the winners are declared: Maria Nearl, and the Radiant Knight, Margaret Nearl.

Around the same time, out on the streets, the sword-bearing Sarkaz **Shining** appears before Platinum, who has been blocking the old men's way. Platinum says her mission has been called off, and withdraws.
In the arena, Zofia leaps down from the stands and slaps Margaret across the face. "Why... did it take you this long!?" Then she adds: that one was for Maria. Her own share, she'll let go.

Margaret notices that Zofia just used her right hand and asks when that happened, but Zofia says this is no place to talk about it and hurries them toward an escape route. Meanwhile Shining, who has come down into the arena with her companion **Nightingale**, treats the wounds of the two fallen Sarkaz.
When told they should run, Margaret shakes her head: a victorious knight has no reason to flee in fear. Zofia speaks to her from the heart. "It's really great... that you came back."
Margaret once hated this land deeply. Even so, she turns to her sister and says, "...Maria, let's go home." Because this is her home.
Epilogue — After the Curtain Falls

After the match, Czarny stands before Platinum. Facing exile that very night, without any National Council proceedings, he makes one last request: that Szewczyk's son, who was at the scene, never be given the chance to tell the truth.

When the subject of the lackey at his side comes up, Czarny only says 'he's next' — and that 'next' comes soon. The Słoma employee **Malkiewicz**, left behind in Czarny's office, picks up a call on the spokesman's line, and for that reason alone he is informed of his dismissal and his appointment as spokesman for the General Chamber of Commerce in the same breath.
Platinum warns the bewildered new spokesman: beware the Pinus Sylvestris Knightclub. They openly oppose the Armorless Union.
Around then, Sona and the Ashlock Knight are preparing their next move from their hideout: exposing the truth of the Armorless Union to the whole world.

blocks.cap: Sona and the Ashlock Knight, in hiding. Behind their smiles, the two prepare to strike back.

blocks.x: Back at the Nearl manor, Maria tells her sister: don't leave like you did six years ago. This time, she will be at her side.

Then Młynar appears and tells Margaret — who means to enter knight sports and win back the family's honor — to take up her sword. Better to fall by his blade than in the shadow of the Armorless Union, he says; he will teach her all over again how to 'give up.'
Margaret's answer is short. "...As you wish."

Meanwhile, before a certain Grandmaster, **Senomy**, a girl from a family of campaign knights, relays her grandfather's bellowing word for word: if anything happens to the youngest daughter of the Nearl family, he'll flip over every desk in the National Council. Then she adds, "The people from Rhodes Island seem to have arrived already."

The 'Nearl' the MC used to stretch out at the top of his lungs was the best-selling name in that arena. The girl who carried that name into the arena fell and rose again and again, until she found her own answer — not for the family, not for honor, but for herself. And over that answer, after six years, the Radiant Knight returned.

act12d0.tagline: A medic heads home to her jungle for a vacation, gets shot down aircraft and all, and while chasing her stolen engine ends up saddled with the title of Great Chief. In a land where fists are everything, this is about the people who found a path other than their fists.

chars.name: Gavial
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island Medic Operator. Born in Acahualla, she settles most things with her fists.

chars.name: Tomimi
chars.desc: Gavial's junior from back home. Taught herself Sargonian just so she could talk with Gavial, and now leads the 'Gavial's Will' tribe.

chars.name: Eunectes
chars.desc: Chief of the Eunectes tribe. Her real name is Zumama, and she was Gavial's rival growing up. These days she's all about machines.

chars.name: Ceobe
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator. Bursting with energy, but always a beat behind on what's actually going on.

chars.name: Croissant
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator. Even where nobody speaks her language, she still manages to close a deal.

chars.name: Utage
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator who tagged along thinking it was a resort trip. Turns into a different person the moment a fight starts.

chars.name: Blaze
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island Elite Operator. She's the one who filed the request to use the aircraft for this vacation.

chars.name: Flint
chars.desc: A Tiacauh of the Flint tribe, who live scattered across the jungle. Called Kemar, she picks a fight first with anyone who looks strong.

chars.name: Lancet-2
chars.desc: Rhodes Island's medical work platform. Came along with aircraft repair know-how uploaded, too.

chars.name: Inam
chars.desc: The Messenger Sargon sent to Acahualla, and chief of the trade-loving 'Inam Committee.' A Liberi who adores her naps.

chars.name: Dylan
chars.desc: The pilot of Rhodes Island's low-altitude aircraft.

chars.name: High Priest
chars.desc: A short old Liberi who stays by Eunectes's side. He sits in the cockpit of the 'Big, Ugly Thing.'

terms.name: Acahualla
terms.desc: Gavial's homeland. A jungle inside Sargon's borders that the government leaves alone; the name means 'land where the forest overgrows.'

terms.name: Tiacauh
terms.desc: What the people of Acahualla call themselves, whatever their race. It means 'one valiant in war.'

terms.name: Mahuizzotia
terms.desc: The rite that chooses Acahualla's Great Chief. The name means 'strength and honor,' and whoever fights through to the end becomes Great Chief.

terms.name: Gavial's Will
terms.desc: The tribe Tomimi leads. It's 'Wilderness's Will,' the tribe Gavial once belonged to, under a new name.

terms.name: Stone Disease
terms.desc: Acahualla's name for Oripathy. It's seen as a common illness, so the sick aren't singled out or shunned.

terms.name: Big, Ugly Thing
terms.desc: A giant machine the Eunectes tribe spent years painstakingly building. Also called 'Big Ugly' for short.

terms.name: Alive Until Sunset
terms.desc: A famous rock band from the outside world, AUS for short. Last year they dropped by Acahualla, played shows for a while, and moved on.

blocks.x: A vast jungle inside Sargon's borders that even the government won't touch: **Acahualla**. Folks here settle most things by talking with their fists, and they even pick their Great Chief by fighting.

Rhodes Island Medic Operator **Gavial** hails from this very jungle. When a letter from her 'little sister' back home says the rite to choose the Great Chief is coming up, Gavial plans a vacation, saying it'll give the Doctor a chance to rest, too.
And that vacation kicks off with their aircraft getting shot down over the jungle.
1. Day One of Vacation: The Engine Gets Stolen

The Doctor comes to with someone slapping their cheeks, smack, smack. Next to Gavial, who's suggesting they try the whirlwind if that doesn't work, operator **Ceobe** is all sparkly-eyed, asking whether that's fun.

blocks.cap: "What you want to do is grab the person's legs or hands, then start spinning in a circle." Perfect timing on waking up, Doctor.

blocks.x: Gavial's explanation fits in a single line: "We crashed." The rest of the group bailed out partway down, apparently. She'd expected an attack, since the folks back home are a scrappy bunch, but she never figured they'd have anti-air weapons.

Over at the aircraft, a gang of local Archosauria is about to haul off the medical platform **Lancet-2**. Told that whatever falls from the sky belongs to whoever finds it first, Gavial nods along for a second, then throws a punch: if she beats every last one of them, it's hers.

Only after getting walloped does the gang recognize Gavial, and they run off saying they'll tell Chief Eunectes. But the pilot, **Dylan**, had been knocked out cold, and the gang had already ripped out the aircraft's entire engine and made off with it.

The Doctor goes pale. Before they left, Kal'tsit had made it crystal clear that the aircraft, of all things, had to come back undamaged. Kal'tsit had assumed Gavial left home because she was shunned there, but all Gavial had said was that she missed the place a little.

Just then, with a cry of "Gaaaaviiiiaaaaal!", her junior from back home, **Tomimi**, comes charging in. Tomimi, who even learned Sargonian just to talk with Gavial, has somehow become chief of Gavial's old tribe and renamed it **Gavial's Will**. Because everyone thinks Gavial's the best!

When Gavial pegs her childhood rival **Zumama**'s crew as the engine thieves, Tomimi falters for a moment, then tells her Zumama is now chief of a tribe and a front-runner for the next Great Chief. If they go to the **Mahuizzotia**, the rite being held at the Temple tomorrow, they can meet her there.

Meanwhile, Ceobe snacks on some roadside mushrooms, ends up battling an invisible Reunion, gets tied up tight, and is carted off to Tomimi's tribe along with Dylan and Lancet-2, who are staying behind to guard the aircraft.
2. Thin Tails vs. Thick Tails

The morning after a night camping in the jungle, Gavial jolts the Doctor awake with herbal soup and shows them around her homeland. People here don't care whether you're Archosauria, Phidia, or Liberi; they all call themselves **Tiacauh**, 'one valiant in war.'

blocks.cap: Tomimi's guide map of Acahualla. The crash site is marked with a big 'Boom!!'.

blocks.x: According to Tomimi, at the last rite Gavial beat up every single contestant and then left, so no Great Chief got chosen. Ever since, the tribes have splintered and been fighting each other.
Right now, three tribes are the strongest.

blocks.cap: First, Zumama's Eunectes tribe. They build bizarre tools and weapons near the ore veins.
Second, Kemar's Flint tribe. They live out in the jungle and trust only their own strength.
Third, the 'Inam Committee,' who'd rather do business than fight.

blocks.x: Then, by the roadside, they spot some Archosauria insisting thick tails are the best and ganging up on a thin-tail. Gavial was about to walk right past, but now she's fired up.
Take a good look at my thin tail here. Slim! Refined! Clean, distinct contours!

This being a place where tribes split over tail thickness, a brawl breaks out on the spot. When the thick-tail gang runs for it, the Gavial of old would've chased them to the ends of the earth, but now she just lets them go, saying they're kind of cute.

Instead, Gavial discovers that Tomimi's tail, which she hasn't seen in years, has gotten thicker. Tomimi tears up, saying she wants a thin tail too, but she's giggling again in no time when Gavial praises her Originium Arts as good enough for any operator. She's been training every day so she could help out when Gavial came back.
3. A Rite Set to Rock Music

All the way back to the Temple, Tiacauh chant "Gavial! Gavial!!" Among them is someone from the Eunectes tribe whose tail has sprouted stones from **Stone Disease**, but who's set on watching the rite no matter what.

And at the Temple, songs by **Alive Until Sunset**, a famous rock band from the outside world better known as AUS, are playing. They showed up out of nowhere last year, played shows for a while, then vanished just as suddenly, and the Tiacauh came to revere them as 'heralds of the Mahuizzotia.'

blocks.cap: The Temple where the Mahuizzotia is held. This year, it comes with a rock soundtrack.

blocks.x: Watching the rite, Tomimi brings up Gavial's very first one. When a tiny Gavial got mocked as an "orphan," she shot back, "My tribespeople are my family!" and then laid out a grown-up champion with two punches.

Gavial doesn't know her parents. In a place where one cold or one spell of bad weather can kill someone, that wasn't unusual, and she says calmly that she only learned it wasn't normal after she left.

Right then, Ceobe, having slipped her ropes, crashes the stage, mistakes Peta, a warrior of Tomimi's tribe, for a bounty hunter who kidnapped the Doctor, and sends Peta flying. Suddenly the new challenger, Ceobe knocks down opponent after opponent before charging outside after "Reunion," with Gavial chasing after her.
Left behind, Tomimi listens to the Doctor talk about Gavial's life on the outside, then suddenly declares: "When it comes to Gavial...! I-I'm not gonna lose to you, Doctor!"

Then she tells how that first rite ended. Zumama, already hooked on machines back then, stepped up to the young Gavial saying she'd test herself one last time, and the two fought from lunchtime until nightfall without a winner, until they were both worn out and tossed outside. From that day on, Zumama never fought Gavial again.
4. The Age of Machines Starts Now

Gavial gets back just as Zumama takes the stage. She's a chief now, going by **Eunectes**. Gavial had been worried by rumors that she talks to thin air, but seeing her in person, she looks perfectly fine.

Even when the other two chiefs team up and rush her with all their followers at once, Eunectes sweeps them all away by herself. Tomimi's plan was to wait until Eunectes wore herself out before stepping in, but Gavial leaps onto the stage first. She said she wasn't going to compete! Tomimi looks oddly flustered.

Facing off after all these years, Eunectes tells Gavial she relies on her fists too much, and that this is her limit, and this land's limit too. At that moment, to a chant of "Heave-ho, heave-ho," something enormous comes walking in from the forest.

blocks.cap: "...High Priest. Aim. Fire!"

blocks.x: It took one shot. Gavial goes down, and Eunectes declares:
We have no future if we rely on our fists, Gavial. From here on out, it's the age of machines.
5. Stone Disease

The first thing out of Gavial's mouth when she wakes up is "It's pretty badass!" The machine, called the **Big, Ugly Thing**, brought down the Temple itself, and Eunectes became Great Chief by proclaiming that with tools, anyone can be strong. Gavial owns it cleanly: this time, she really lost.

blocks.cap: The Temple, brought down by the mechanical beast. The rite came to an end here, too.

blocks.x: Just then, Yota of the Eunectes tribe collapses nearby. Originium crystals have broken out on his body: heart failure brought on by Oripathy. When his younger brother Yogi says their chief had them mining ore to build machines, Gavial's face hardens.

Here, Oripathy is a common illness called Stone Disease. The sick are cared for like any other patients, and since all anyone knew was that going into the mines made you catch it, people simply kept away from them.
Gavial has the disease herself. She caught it when young Tomimi snuck into a mine and Gavial went in after her. Tomimi, close to tears, says she wishes it had been her instead.

After that, people wouldn't let Gavial do anything. No hunting, no parties, and in the end, not even the rite. Tomimi, who stayed at her side and did everything for her, says that was when Gavial stopped smiling much.

Finally, Gavial got angry, threw herself into the rite, knocked everyone flat, and left. Being given dangerous work was fine by her, but having her freedom taken away and being kept from doing anything at all was more than she could bear. That was the truth behind the 'shunning' Kal'tsit had heard about.

Gavial vows that if Zumama is treating people's lives lightly, she's getting a few good punches for it. She sends Yota off to Lancet-2 and tells Yogi to let his chief know she's coming. Tomimi says she has something to prepare and arranges to meet up with them at the big waterfall deep in the jungle.
6. Inam the Merchant and the Sword-Wielding Monster

Heading deep into the jungle, Gavial and the Doctor run into **Inam**, who was just about to take a nap. She's a Liberi who became chief because people kept following her around on their own, but she's actually Sargon's 'Messenger' to these parts.

According to Inam, this place was a Sargonian mine a few hundred years ago until a Catastrophe left it abandoned, and a decade or so ago the government even tried moving a nomadic city here to work the mines again. Gavial saw that nomadic city pass by too, together with Zumama, and that was the day Zumama started acting strange.

And at the market Inam takes them to, their colleague **Croissant**, without a single word of the language in common, has gotten her hands on some ore using nothing but hand gestures and a pitiful-face act, and is grinning away: "What a prize~!"

blocks.cap: The market in Inam's village. Every sales pitch here was taught by Inam herself, apparently.

blocks.x: Then word comes that a sword-wielding monster is leading a gang of Archosauria in an attack. Just as Croissant guessed, it's **Utage**, who saw the village and charged in figuring a big brawl would be fun.
She beat up everyone who came at her and somehow ended up the new chief of the Great Wood Tribe, but she herself nearly jumps out of her skin, saying no way is she living without TV or AC.

Before they part, Inam hands over books like 'City Beauty' and 'Mastering Corporate Management in 100 Days,' asking them to pass them on to Tomimi. That's how Tomimi learned Sargonian, one word at a time from books like these. All to catch up with Gavial.
And the Doctor stops Inam as she's heading off for her nap, with one favor to ask.
7. All for Gavial

Meanwhile, in the Eunectes tribe's village, the short old Liberi known as the **High Priest** is reporting on the machine's overheating problem. He's the old man who stepped up when nobody else would ride the constantly exploding machine, and no matter how many times he gets blown sky-high, he always comes back alive.

When Yogi brings news of his brother, Eunectes gets angry: didn't she tell them never to go deep into the mine? She defends Gavial as someone who wouldn't come just to take her anger out on them, but says that the engine, at least, she won't give back. It's for this land's future.

Hearing this, **Kemar** sets out to stop Gavial. Around the same time, **Blaze**, on her second day lost in the jungle, climbs a tree in her swimsuit and is yelling at the top of her lungs when she happens to run right into Kemar. They can't understand a word the other says, but they both understand the other looks strong, and they go at it on the spot.
And at that very moment, somewhere in the jungle, the chiefs belonging to Gavial's Will are listening to someone speaking from the shadows.

blocks.cap: "Don't forget why we formed 'Gavial's Will'!"

blocks.x: The plan: once Gavial beats Zumama's machine, the figure in the shadows will become Great Chief next and make Gavial stay here. When one chief says, "I agree with Tomimi," they all shout together: "All for Gavial!"

Meanwhile, Blaze shows up in front of the Doctor's group carrying Kemar on her back, out cold after picking a fight and getting walloped. When Kemar comes to, she bows low to Blaze and asks to become her student, then declares she's lost all interest in Gavial. And from now on, she wants to be called **Flint**.
8. A Serious Dilemma by the Waterfall
Around then, Inam delivers the Doctor's letter to Dylan, who's been bored to death waiting by the aircraft. "...Lancet-2, looks like we've got work to do."
Meanwhile, the Doctor's group reaches the big waterfall. Utage is thrilled her swimsuit is finally paying off, while Blaze and Flint keep their conversation going with fists instead of words.

blocks.cap: It's no beach, but the water's nice and cool. Ceobe, the mushrooms not quite out of her system yet, cannonballs in yelling "The Mushroom Sea!"

blocks.x: In the middle of all this, Gavial very earnestly confides a worry to the Doctor. "Do you think my tail's gotten a little thicker than before?"

Soon Tomimi, done with her 'business,' joins them, and Utage drags her off, determined to fix the fashion sense she picked up all wrong from magazines. In the meantime, Ceobe runs off again, and of all directions, she's headed for Zumama's tribe.
9. Fists vs. Iron Fists

Meanwhile, over in the Eunectes tribe, people have been sticking the engine's pipes in wherever they please until they finally manage to wake up the Big Ugly. Ceobe barges in soon after, the group chasing her calms her down, and Gavial comes face to face with Eunectes.

Before even getting to the engine, Gavial demands to know whether Eunectes made her people mine even at the risk of giving them Oripathy. But it turns out Yota snuck in deeper on his own to dig up more ore for her, even though his chief had warned him again and again. And Yogi just says, "You didn't ask."

Eunectes lifts her clothes to show her body. She has Stone Disease too, and nobody knows better than her where in the mine the disease-causing ore lies. Gavial apologizes without a fuss, leaving only Utage, who was hoping for a big fight, looking a little sheepish.
The engine is already installed in the Big Ugly, and when Eunectes tells her to take it by force, Gavial answers, "Then bring it on!" Before the duel, Eunectes brings up that day.

blocks.cap: The end of a sparring match in their childhood, and a Sargonian nomadic city passing along the horizon. "It will never have anything to do with us."

blocks.x: Gavial just thought, "Wow, that's big," but Zumama felt utterly insignificant. From that day on she lost interest in fighting, got books from Inam to study Sargonian and machines, and after meeting the High Priest, started building the Big Ugly. And the 'talking to thin air' Gavial had worried about? She'd been talking to this very old man.

Eunectes says people only believe in fighting because strong people like Gavial are their role models, and she means to shatter that worship with an even greater power. Gavial's answer is simple: she has no intention of being anyone's role model. She only ever stands for herself.
Standing alone before the machine, Gavial dodges its shelling and takes its iron fist head-on with her bare body. So much so that Utage asks why on earth Gavial is a medic.

But when the High Priest switches on max performance mode, the machine starts going berserk. Eunectes tells Gavial to back off, saying she doesn't want to win like this, but Gavial steps up to stop it alongside her, and the Doctor takes command. Croissant, meanwhile, is yelling for triple overtime.
10. Great Chief Gavial's Inaugural Speech
In the end, the Big Ugly is wrecked. When Gavial says she's sorry, Eunectes just says "I know," hands back the engine, which still works, and asks whether Gavial has any thought of staying here.
"Is doctoring fun?" "Is building machines fun?" "Yeah." "Same here."

Still, it was Gavial who brought down the machine, so Gavial is the Great Chief. At a loss, Gavial spots Tomimi, who vanished right before the match was decided and reappeared saying she'd gone to the bathroom, and hits on a brilliant idea.
I beat the Big, Ugly Thing, so from now on I'm the Great Chief! And what I want to say to all of you is... your fists are everything!

Only, she has important business and has to leave, so Tomimi will give the orders in her place for the time being. And to Eunectes, who vows to challenge her again, Gavial says that first she's getting an Oripathy checkup at Rhodes Island, and Gavial will drag her there tied up on Great Chief's orders if she has to.
But Tomimi shakes her head. "I-I won't let you leave!"
11. Escape the Jungle

The one who set up this rite was Tomimi. Unless someone gathered the splintered tribes back together, the rite could never have been held, and the Doctor had found that strange from the start. The letter that called Gavial home was part of the plan, too.

When Tomimi was little and lost in the jungle, crying, the one who found her was Gavial, bleeding but still saying, "Let's go home." To Tomimi, Gavial is the one who saved her life, and that's why she's the best person in the whole world.

blocks.cap: The jungle where Gavial found little lost Tomimi.

blocks.x: And now, when Tomimi pulls out a line she learned from a book, "If you can't capture his heart, capture him," Utage groans that trashy romance novels have ruined the girl, and Tomimi's alliance charges in all at once.

Losing ground, Tomimi drags out Dylan and Lancet-2 as hostages. But the two of them are screaming way too enthusiastically. Turns out they were never tied up in the first place; they'd been carrying out the mission the Doctor gave them by letter.

The Doctor lays out the evidence. How she hesitated when Zumama first came up, how she panicked when Gavial jumped on stage. And the final proof, which Dylan smuggled in inside Lancet-2's body: a rocket launcher found in Tomimi's village. The very weapon that shot down the aircraft.
Tomimi bawls and begs forgiveness, and Gavial lays her face-down across her lap. "Naughty little whelps get tail spankings!"

Once the commotion is over, it's Eunectes's turn to fall apart. Seeing Lancet-2 move on its own and even talk, she starts trembling and asks if she could give it a hug, just once. The High Priest goes ahead and asks Lancet-2 out on a date.

Told that Rhodes Island can build machines like this, Eunectes resolves to join up and learn about machines there. Tomimi then announces 'Plan B' and tags along, and Flint says she's following Blaze, too.

Even with those three gone, there's nothing to worry about. The Tiacauh conclude in no time that they can just build machines while they fight, and the High Priest points out that even the first Great Chief was just a warrior who gave himself the title two hundred years ago.
My point is that people are resilient. Just because one tradition suddenly disappears doesn't mean their lives will fall apart.
Still, someone has to be Great Chief. Just then Inam shows up late, asking if it's all over already, and Gavial stares right at her. "Say, Inam, are you interested in being Great Chief at all?"
Epilogue — Welcome Back

Back at Rhodes Island, the group's report was summed up as 'after many twists and turns, found the engine and barely made it back,' and the repair costs were to come out of the Doctor's and Blaze's pay.

blocks.cap: Back at Rhodes Island, a time to settle accounts for the vacation.

blocks.x: Kal'tsit admits she had even prepared for the case where Gavial stayed home. But Gavial says she isn't leaving here. She left home for one reason only: she wanted to become a doctor.
If she hadn't come out into the world, she says, she would never have known how many illnesses didn't have to be fatal, or how much Oripathy is shunned. And one more thing.
I wouldn't have known that healing people is just as much fun as hitting them.
Gavial's dream now is to cure Oripathy. Saying there's no better place than here to study medicine, she heads off to give Zumama her checkup, and behind her, Kal'tsit says, "Welcome back."

To the Doctor, who remains, Kal'tsit says this trip is probably proof that this land is full of life. That they must look for the light of hope that slips out from between people, and that some things are not so far away.
Extra — Where the Singers Passed Through

Going back in time to a day last year, the car of the rock band Alive Until Sunset runs out of power partway across the wasteland and stops. In Alty's hand is a 'key' she received from a certain doctor in exchange for knowledge.

blocks.cap: The wasteland where Alive Until Sunset's car came to a halt.

blocks.x: Pushing the car into the jungle, the four were greeted by Zumama, and when the High Priest was called out, he and Alty recognized each other in surprise. Then Frost plugged a guitar into the ritual sound equipment and launched into an improvised solo, and the Tiacauh went wild, crying that a Cuicayotl, 'one who sings,' had come at last after all these years.
After two months of shows at the Temple, Alive Until Sunset left one day, with nothing but a single note in a tidied, empty room. "We're off. We hope the music brought you joy."
If you sing for people, and they like it... then maybe they'll start singing along too.
Back on the road, in the car, Alty gazes at the key and thinks: 'Kal'tsit... can that Rhodes Island of yours give this land the answer it's looking for?'

In a land where fists do all the talking, one person left to heal people, one built machines, and one tried to hold on to the person leaving and ended up following her out the door. Even so, Great Chief Gavial's inaugural speech stayed one line long to the very end. Your fists are everything!

act9d0.tagline: How a nameless Sarkaz who picked up a dead mercenary's sword came to inherit the name 'W,' lost a king, and finally handed a Sarkaz blade to a child of Chernobog. Who sets the price of a mercenary's life?

chars.desc: A mercenary who leads the company alongside Hoederer. Uses Arts that read shadows.

chars.name: W
chars.desc: A Sarkaz mercenary who inherited a dead comrade's name and weapons. Impossible to read.

chars.name: Theresa
chars.desc: King of the Sarkaz. Stands against the Regent over Kazdel · Operator Civilight Eterna

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: A doctor who stays at Theresa's side.

chars.name: Closure
chars.desc: An engineer who works aboard Theresa's ship.

chars.name: Talulah
chars.desc: The leader of Reunion.

chars.name: Scout

chars.name: Patriot
chars.desc: An old Sarkaz warrior in Reunion. Calls himself a man of Ursus.

blocks.x: The war in Kazdel has never stopped. For Sarkaz mercenaries, war is both a trade and a way to survive, and there is always a price on their lives.

The squad of the mercenary **Hoederer** walked into an ambush and lost a comrade, 'W.' W had brought down the ruins from the rear to give everyone a chance to escape, and paid for it. His body, left in enemy territory, could not be recovered.
That same day, a nameless Sarkaz woman carrying W's sword and gun was following them on foot.
1. To Take Up the Weapons of the Fallen
**Ines**, a fellow mercenary who has come out to meet them, wants the woman killed on the spot. Taking in a Sarkaz of unknown origin is madness, and Kazdel is full of people who want Hoederer's head.

Hoederer does not draw his sword. He gives her one last chance: put down the dead man's belongings, and she can walk away alive. Only then does the woman speak for the first time. She never had another choice, she says. His other hand had been on his hilt the whole time.
But you understand what it means to take up the weapons of the fallen, yes?
The woman answers, 'Of course,' and Hoederer calls her 'W.' From the moment he first saw her in those crumbling ruins, he had been certain. She would become the finest of all Sarkaz warriors.

blocks.cap: A Sarkaz who inherited a dead comrade's sword and gun, and his name.

blocks.x: A few months later, in the buffer zone between Kazdel's eastern and western fronts. Hoederer lures out an ambush with a deliberate opening and deals with it, then finds a note on the corpse of an assassin who was once a comrade.

The note lists mercenaries' aliases, with their bounties marked as numbers of candies. The stronger the mercenary, the higher the price; the higher the price, the greater the danger. But those who survive only grow stronger. Hoederer calls it the rules of the game.

W asks about the previous W. An oddball who made the day he killed a man from Laterano and took his gun into his birthday, and who wanted to earn the leader's spot so that everyone would have to wish him a happy birthday. He was always smiling, but his obsessiveness made him trust others more easily than anyone.
When Hoederer tells her she is the same sort as the old W, good at disguise and doing just as she pleases, W smiles for the first time.

blocks.cap: That smile resembled the dead W's.

blocks.x: From that day on, W became W. But as Ines had said, it was absurd.
2. An Escort Without Questions

Back at base, Hoederer brings bad news to Ines at the campfire. Their agent in Kazdel was thrown into a furnace, and the Messenger, on the way out of Kazdel, was seized by spies and came back with an order: escort a transport team coming from Rim Billiton.

Hoederer assigns the job to Ines and W. Ines objects that she cannot trust W, who kills and deceives without a second thought, but Hoederer answers that they have no options left. Wait for the war to end, and they will end along with it.
Ines tells him his shadow is wavering, and not to take so much on himself alone. When she presses him on who the Messenger met, Hoederer finally, after a long silence, gives a name. **Babel**.

Just before departure, the camp comes under attack. W, who was in charge of patrols, had wrecked another mercenary band's comms equipment and left them behind in the rear. While they hold the enemy off, Hoederer's squad slips far away. Hoederer states flatly that the Sarkaz in that camp have nothing to do with them.
W arrives at the rendezvous three hours late, and Ines, by the campfire, digs into her past. When W needles her about being weak in close combat, Ines has a blade on her in an instant.

blocks.cap: "In case you didn't know, every Sarkaz mercenary carries a blade."

blocks.x: W admits that she approached Hoederer on purpose from the start, because so many people in Kazdel wanted his head. Asked why she changed her mind, she only says this side looked more profitable.
Hoederer arrives after them and lays out the mission. Let no one near the target. Fire without warning on anyone who approaches. He cannot tell them the destination or the cargo.
Ines breaks the contract and sweeps the transport team with her Arts. There is a massive shadow there. A ship, or a frame?
3. One Head Out of Three
To the north of Kazdel lies a birch forest. Unconscious, Ines sees the shadows of pale, ashen trunks tangled across the snow.

blocks.cap: A birch forest at the end of a long winter, where only death awaits.

blocks.x: W wakes Ines and tells her they were hit by a surprise attack an hour ago; the squad is scattered and comms are down. Ines leaves the wounded W behind as bait, telling her: I never trusted you, not for a single moment.
