Before long the enemy finds W, but those lying in wait are blown apart by traps she had set in advance. Ines emerges from the shadows, seizes the last one, and tortures him. All he manages to spit out is that Kazdel will never forgive them.

After that, the enemy kept coming. They were dressed as mercenaries, but they knew the battlefield better than any mercenary. As W gets ready to charge in with grenades, Ines asks what meaning there is in a pointless death like that. W asks back what meaning there is in their being alive.

In the end, the enemy surrounding them makes an offer. Eighty percent of their squad has been wiped out. Of the three of them, counting their leader, two should join hands and bring back the head of the third. Ines and W agree that in that case they would kill Hoederer, then kick the offer away.

At the same moment, somewhere else, someone speaks. A leak has put the mercenaries in danger, and no one should be sacrificed for nothing. **Kal'tsit** tries to talk them out of it, but in the end says she will go too.
When W finally loses consciousness, Ines counts the approaching enemies. Fourteen, fifteen, more than that. Then the severed comms come back, and Hoederer comes running.

blocks.cap: Beyond her fading vision, someone with white hair.

blocks.x: The king of the Sarkaz... the king who lost Kazdel... is she... a woman with white hair?
4. A King Before a Broken Door

Every Sarkaz stopped. In the middle of the burning ruins appeared a woman who was not Sarkaz, and her expression did not change at all. What W, her ears injured by the blast, saw just before she passed out was a slender Sarkaz without a trace of hostility.

blocks.cap: The heart of a battlefield where every Sarkaz stood still.

blocks.x: W wakes aboard a ship. This ship was the main body of the transport team they had been escorting, and Hoederer has gone to negotiate with 'the master of this place.'

Wandering the ship in search of Hoederer, W comes across a Sarkaz in the corridor, wrestling alongside the engineer **Closure** with an automatic door that has shorted out for the seventh time. She introduces herself as **Theresa**. Her Majesty, who stood against the Regent and united the Sarkaz on her own, was fixing a broken door.
Theresa says she would like to call this ship 'Rhodes Island,' a name she found in records deep inside it. Then she asks W: 'W' is the name of a mercenary, so what is your name?
W has no name. It is common for Sarkaz born in Kazdel, she says, and memorizing names that will be forgotten anyway is inefficient.
I don't want to forget any of them. I mustn't.

Theresa tells her that when the day comes that she no longer has to live as 'W,' she may find a new name, and that whatever she has done in the past, she is welcome if she wants to stay. Kal'tsit makes it clear that W's record is rather dangerous, and that not everyone welcomes her.

W never managed to look Theresa straight in the eye. Someone who seemed so innocent had such sad eyes. On her way back, W meets the gaze of the hooded 'Doctor,' and through a fear she cannot explain, she remembers: this is Babel's battlefield commander.
5. A Flag That Must Fall
Some time later, Hoederer decides to leave Babel. Theresa had called him aside and even remembered where he came from, and Hoederer tells Kal'tsit that only Her Majesty could do such a thing.
Kal'tsit regrets his decision but does not hold him back, and Hoederer departs, leaving W behind at Babel.

Few Sarkaz follow them out of Babel, and they have no base. Hoederer says they have come back to the beginning, to when they met in the birch forest and decided to strike out on their own. All of the company's flags were left behind at Babel.

blocks.cap: Hoederer and Ines, having left Babel. Back where they began.

blocks.x: That flag had never once come down, from the west all the way to the east. Even when the seventieth, the eightieth standard-bearer died, they kept it standing, even if it meant driving the pole into their own belly.

But on the day they escorted Rhodes Island, enemy Arts from Kazdel swept over the hill like a landslide, and every flag was broken. The one holding the flag then was a child. Hoederer confesses that he could have caught that flag, and that the flag he never liked for a single moment ought to fall.
Of the mercenaries who started out together, only the two of them are still alive.

On the road, Ines points out that Hoederer deliberately left W at Her Majesty's side. The Theresa that Ines saw grieved more than anyone, yet was strong and gentle; and before the Doctor, Ines felt she would be a chess piece for the rest of her life.

Hoederer answers that it was a precaution. Since the Regent would never forgive them, someday they may have to side with Babel; but for now he is tired of fighting his own kin and wants to get as far from this war as he can. When he told W she could stay, she agreed without hesitation.
Meanwhile W, still at Babel, uses a small camera taken off a spy to secretly photograph Theresa and the others gathered on the bridge. Just before she pressed the shutter, Theresa smiled.

The war was getting tangled just as Hoederer had predicted, but W did not care what became of Kazdel. She was only worried about Theresa. That damned doctor is far stronger than she is, W thinks, so maybe she will protect Theresa. No. She has to.
6. Kazdel Without a King
Hoederer ran from Babel, from the place where W and Her Majesty were. If asked whether he regrets it, he probably does. But even had he been there, he could have done nothing.

Months after they left Babel, news reaches a mercenary camp in Kazdel's far north. A war that had held for so long tipped over in a single night, and contact with Babel has been lost. We were all lost in that warmth, Ines says.

By then, W was alone, hunting down the Sarkaz with Theresa's blood on their hands. Her last target tells her that Theresa is already dead, that Babel's halls are stained with everyone's blood. And that she is merely lost in a meaningless revenge.
W pulls the trigger without a trace of anger. He calls the Regent 'His Majesty' to the very end, and W tells him there is only one Majesty, and that is Theresa.
Hoederer and Ines find her there. The place where W, after months of wandering alone, had come to a stop was the very spot where the previous W died and the new W joined the squad.

blocks.cap: The edge of the western front. Where 'W' died, and where W became W.

blocks.x: Hoederer tells her the Regent has merged Kazdel's armed groups and the remaining mercenaries into a single army. He and Ines accepted that offer to survive, but they intend to go to Ursus, not Kazdel.

blocks.cap: Beyond Kazdel, the Infected are rising.

blocks.x: The core of Reunion, the Infected movement the Regent means to use, is in Ursus; if they join it and leave Kazdel, they can avoid suspicion. Saying that the one she is after is a real monster, and that the old woman is gone too, W decides to go with them.

blocks.cap: "Welcome back, 'W.'"

blocks.x: Hoederer thinks that perhaps the one who most wants to get out of Kazdel is himself.

On the road to Ursus, W, who saw the truth of what happened at Babel, never says a word about it. Then, beneath a Catastrophe cloud, she meets an informant and confirms there is no intel that the Regent has taken Rhodes Island.
At last, Reunion's leader **Talulah** receives them. 'Welcome, warriors from afar.' There was no running from the war.
7. The Street Trees of Chernobog

Months later, in Reunion-occupied Chernobog. Ines corners **Scout**, a Sarkaz who worked alongside W at Babel. Then she names the members of the Rhodes Island team he led, one by one, telling him who fell and where.

It was W who had them confirm the names, saying they ought to know whom they killed. Scout replies that the operators who were sacrificed were not soldiers, and says the W of old never bothered to remember the names of the dead.

The mercenary leader the Regent sent had already died by Scout's hand. And Scout had made a deal with W. Once he finished his mission, W's squad would come at him with everything they had and kill him.

Ines hoped he would simply run, but Scout heads for the city center. To Ines, following behind, he says: don't throw your life away before you see the truth with your own eyes. We Sarkaz cannot go on being used like this.

blocks.cap: Downtown Chernobog. Where Scout led Ines.

blocks.x: Ines looks with her Arts where he points and is left speechless, and Talulah, beyond, notices them. '...A Sarkaz?' Scout makes his move in that opening, but Hoederer, who had been tailing them, cuts him down.
...I'm sorry. Sleep now, old friend.
To Scout's last words, that they should not be here, Hoederer answers that he knew that from the start.
Once they are out of sight, Ines tells him what she saw. Talulah has two shadows. One was like a ruin, filled with the remnants of some power, ancient yet unbroken.

Talulah is deliberately tearing Reunion down, just as it was three years ago. Hoederer says that alone is not enough for them to act, but Ines sets off alone, saying W must be told. It was the first time she had ever defied Hoederer.

In an alley on the way to W, a Reunion soldier blocks Ines's path. He takes her to task for their past failures, and when she says she will report to Talulah herself, he answers that that is not the kind of 'accountability' they need.
Moments later, the soldier reports that Ines was killed in an attack. He gives no answer when asked whether the body was confirmed, and leaves a caster behind to blow up the street.
Fallen, Ines murmurs that not bringing Hoederer with her was the right call. Then she looks up at the trees along the street.
Come to think of it, the trees along Chernobog's streets... were birches...
8. To the Throne, Even on My Knees

Months earlier, on the night their negotiations with Reunion concluded. **Patriot**, an old Sarkaz warrior who calls himself a man of Ursus, came alone to ask what had happened in Theresa's Kazdel. His people may have been exiled, he said, but he is still Sarkaz.

blocks.cap: Ursus. A nameless wasteland on the outskirts.

blocks.x: And now, at the mercenary garrison in Chernobog. A Reunion soldier informs W that Ines was killed fighting enemy stragglers.

W asks where the enemy bodies are. Ines cannot use lethal Arts, yet the only answer she gets is that a Reunion caster blew the whole street away. W calls it far too obvious and raises her staff, and Hoederer holds her back.

Hoederer tells her about Talulah's two shadows and that Patriot has begun to move, and says the Regent will soon learn what has happened here. If no one reports to him, the Regent will discard them all, so Hoederer says he will go to Victoria himself.
Hoederer knows that W has been following Rhodes Island's trail, and that someone saw 'the ghost of Babel' in the battle for Chernobog. He felt he finally understood what W was after.

W tells him this is his chance to get away from Kazdel; if he goes past Lungmen and Ursus to somewhere far away, she will look the other way. Go back, and you will surely die. When she asks why he would risk his life to cover for her, Hoederer answers.
Her Majesty Theresa... remembered my name. And my family, too.
As long as Theresis sits on the throne, Hoederer says, he wants to reach it, even on his knees, and fathom what the man is thinking.
Then he passes on something Ines had said. That W looks more and more like a madwoman, yet her methods and temperament keep growing softer. Perhaps, Hoederer adds, all of them had trusted her.

Before leaving, Hoederer asks the Reunion soldiers whether anyone saw Ines's death with their own eyes. No one had. In how coldly they took the fall of a comrade, Hoederer catches the familiar scent of conspiracy and war.
9. A Price Set by Oneself

Londinium, at the end of a long journey. **Confessarius**, who serves the Regent, receives Hoederer's report and says that His Majesty the Regent knows of every Sarkaz affair, however trivial. He even says that by now 'a certain unpalatable individual' must have returned to Rhodes Island.

blocks.cap: Londinium, Victoria.

blocks.x: Victoria will keep watching Reunion, Confessarius says; there is not yet enough chaos. Told that he need not go back and should rest here, Hoederer finds himself held in a mansion in Londinium.
Hoederer realizes it. Theresis knew everything. The stories of Theresa and Theresis were not just stories.

Still, there is a way. From the very beginning, Hoederer had kept a secret transmitter under a ruin in Kazdel, and he entrusts the Messenger with a coded message to be relayed through it to his own squad.
When the Messenger says she thought he had lost his fighting spirit, Hoederer answers that it is the opposite. What he must do has only grown clearer.
Before he left Chernobog, W had come to Hoederer and asked: can you put a price on a mercenary's life? And who sets that price? When he answered that war does, W said that was boring.
Every Sarkaz mercenary should set their own price.
Not swayed by a price someone else puts on them, but setting it themselves, in the blood of the Sarkaz's enemies. And W told Hoederer to think carefully about what he needed to do in Kazdel.
10. To Take Up a Sarkaz Blade
Meanwhile, in Chernobog. On her way to see Talulah, W comes upon two children struggling to hold up a Sarkaz army-issue sword.
...Do you know what it means to take up a Sarkaz blade?

**Rublev**, the boy with the injured leg, runs off, refusing help from a devil, but black blood was already flowing from his wound. W follows the children and tells them there is medicine to suppress Oripathy in the basement of an abandoned hospital. Along with a warning: the place is full of Reunion rioters, and they could die there.

blocks.cap: The ruins of Chernobog after the Catastrophe.

blocks.x: The boy Rublev had pulled from the ruins said he would go, even with his legs shaking, and Rublev could not call him back. He did not even know the boy's name.

W keeps Rublev where he is, telling him not to move a single step. She says she is a killer who destroyed this city and hurt his parents and friends, and asks whose blood he thinks is on the blade he carries.
When Rublev insists the boy can't manage without him, W tells him that no one in this world can live without other people. No one at all.

As time passes, Rublev sobs that the boy must have run away, that he can't do anything right, that it's his fault Rublev hurt his leg in the first place. W cuts him off: until the boy comes back, he knows nothing.

W tells him that what decides a person's actions is not their origins, their status, or their past. It is the influences they have taken in over a lifetime, their ever-changing beliefs, and how firmly they believe in them. You saved that boy, she says, but because you saw yourself as his savior, you never trusted him.
Then she leaves, saying the blade is a gift she gives him in its owner's stead.

After W leaves, the boy returns, battered by an iron pipe, carrying an entire box of medical supplies. Only then does Rublev ask his name, and the boy smiles: you finally asked. **Andrey** Fyodorovich Ostrovsky.
From a distance, W watches the two children smile. Live. Only the living can feel pain. And then, whatever the cost, you will always be able to find something.
Then W asks quietly: 'Isn't that right... Talulah?'

A nameless Sarkaz inherited the name 'W' along with a dead comrade's sword. Now, with neither the captain who gave her that name, nor the comrade who claimed never to have trusted her for a single moment, nor the king who asked her name still at her side, W hands a Sarkaz blade to a child of Chernobog. The price of that blade is now his to set.

act11d0.tagline: A doctor comes to a nomadic town stranded by a Catastrophe, looking for a friend who has stopped answering. Hunting for whoever burned the clinic, she ends up standing in the middle of a town where people are setting each other on fire. On whom, or what, do I take my revenge?

chars.name: Folinic
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island Medical Department operator. She comes to Wolumonde looking for Atro, an old schoolmate who has stopped answering.

chars.name: Suzuran
chars.desc: A young nine-tailed Vulpo operator and a pupil of Kal'tsit. She follows Folinic to Wolumonde.

chars.name: Severin Hawthorn
chars.desc: Wolumonde's ranking officer, whom the townsfolk call 'Schultz.' Rarely without a cigarette in hand.

chars.name: Tatjana
chars.desc: Fiancée of Severin's son Thorwald. She helps Severin with his work and calls him 'Uncle.'

chars.name: Atro
chars.desc: An Infected doctor from Rhodes Island and Folinic's schoolmate. She stopped answering while caring for the Infected in Wolumonde.

chars.name: GreyThroat
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island crossbow operator. She once escorted Atro all the way to Wolumonde.

chars.name: Ayerscarpe
chars.desc: The operator assigned to guard Catastrophe Messenger Leonhardt. Curt.

chars.name: Click
chars.desc: An operator who went into the Winterwisp Mountains to shoot videos, got stranded, and had to be rescued.

chars.name: Mudrock
chars.desc: Captain of the 'Mudrock Squad,' a band of armed Infected circling Wolumonde. A Sarkaz.

chars.name: Biederman
chars.desc: A Catastrophe Messenger stationed in Wolumonde. He earned the townsfolk's resentment when he failed to prevent the Great Rift disaster.

terms.name: Wolumonde
terms.desc: A nomadic town in western Leithanien. Its name means 'the Eighth Moon.' After the Great Rift it was thrown off its route and left stranded.

terms.name: Great Rift
terms.desc: A colossal canyon, thousands of meters deep, with active Originium laid bare. The Catastrophe badly damaged Wolumonde and forced it off its normal route.

terms.name: Zwölftontechnik Strasse
terms.desc: The street in Wolumonde where the Infected live together. It was already the largest concentration of Infected in town.

terms.name: Winterwisp
terms.desc: A Caprinae tribe that ruled these mountains centuries ago. Most of their blood has since mixed with that of Wolumonde's people.

terms.name: Contingency Contract
terms.desc: The system through which Catastrophe Messengers exchange Catastrophe-response requests and payment.

terms.name: L-44 'Gramophone'
terms.desc: Wolumonde's Arts-generating device for town defense. Any Leithanian with a higher education can operate one.

blocks.x: **Wolumonde**, a nomadic town in western Leithanien, was a trading town whose name meant 'the Eighth Moon.' On the day the **Great Rift** split the earth, the town failed to get clear in time. It lost its farmland and supply facilities and was thrown off its normal route. That route now points toward the snowbound Winterwisp Mountains. This year, winter will come early.

Beneath an old oak outside the town, Schultz **Severin Hawthorn** hears the residents' council's decision from **Tatjana**, his son's fiancée. No one can say whether those who died in the recent fire were Infected, so they will be buried outside the town, and funerals are forbidden.

Severin goes through the names on the list one by one. Eckehard the tailor, who never missed a wedding. Biederman, the Catastrophe Messenger who lost his work over the Great Rift and still quietly bore his penance. Kevin, who lived only for his wife. And on that list is also the name of his only son, Thorwald.
Between coughs, Severin tells her to let them know he agrees.
1. Twenty-Seven Days of Silence

Meanwhile, aboard the Rhodes Island landship, Medical Department operator **Folinic** has kept watch in the communications room for twenty hours. The scheduled check-ins from **Atro**, an Infected doctor, her old schoolmate and dearest friend, have been silent for twenty-seven days.

When Folinic applies for a transfer to Leithanien, **Suzuran**, a young Vulpo operator and Kal'tsit's pupil, comes along. Then a local report arrives: a month ago, a Catastrophe struck the town where Atro was last seen.
The Wolumonde the two arrive in is nearly deserted. The Infected keep up their protests, insisting the fire was 'deliberate' and demanding an explanation for Atro and the Infected who died.

blocks.cap: Folinic and Suzuran enter the town of 'the Eighth Moon.'

blocks.x: When Folinic asks where Atro is, Severin, whom the townsfolk call 'Schultz,' says only that she is not in town right now. Only after they help him put down an armed disturbance in the Infected quarter does he speak. Atro is missing.

Atro had set up a camp outside town for Infected residents. Not long ago it caught fire, and after that, he says, she left Wolumonde. Severin calls the fire most likely an accident, and dismisses the armed Infected circling the town, Sarkaz among them, as petty thieves. Folinic raises the name 'Reunion,' then holds off on any conclusion and sets out to investigate herself.
After the two leave, Severin confides in the councilor. Watching Folinic's face, full of grief and anger, he wondered why Tatjana has never worn that look. Thorwald was about to be her husband.
2. No One Made It Out of the Tent

After parting with Severin, the two head for **Zwölftontechnik Strasse**, where the Infected live together. At a glance it is an ordinary street, but dead leaves pile up outside a shuttered bakery, and the stalls and public transport are gone. The whole street, Folinic says, has simply become a prison.

To Tatjana, who shows them the way, Atro was 'the hero of the Infected,' the one who stayed after the Catastrophe to care for them. At the back of the crowd in the square, Folinic spots a Sarkaz. In that moment, the attack begins.
A captured rebel resident shouts it out. They used that fire to kill Dr. Atro and her colleagues. Not one person made it out of that tent that day.

With the lie in pieces, Tatjana decides to tell them everything. Folinic calls the concealment nothing but excuses, yet answers that Rhodes Island will not abandon this town. Before the Catastrophe, Atro had said the same thing to Severin.

Tatjana takes them to the burned-out camp. Rhodes Island supply crates that Folinic herself had sent are still there. Even the tents' metal frames have melted, and the bodies look as though death came in an instant, with no time to struggle.

Tatjana counts eight victims. Three Infected from the town, and Atro. Three Infected who seem to have been drifters. And Thorwald, not Infected, who had been helping at the camp. Unable to leave with the town, they will remain in the ground outside it once Wolumonde moves on, and lose their home forever.
Sifting through the ashes, Suzuran picks up Atro's employee badge. It has not burned.

blocks.cap: Atro always grumbled that her badge got in the way of her work.

blocks.x: Then an explosion sounds from the direction of the town, and armed Infected storm in. Local Infected gathered around a core of Sarkaz, calling themselves the 'Mudrock Squad.'
3. No Matter Who

When the three reach the Rathaus, Severin is facing the armed Infected alone. He proposes a truce for the length of one cigarette and asks what they want. Only to go home and work again, the man answers. All that is left on that street is cracks and Originium. They were simply the first to be abandoned.

His matches are damp and will not light. Severin apologizes in advance for an 'unfortunate accident' that may occur, then subdues the man with his bare hands. The fallen Infected barely survives, thanks to Rhodes Island's first aid.

blocks.cap: The street leading to the Rathaus. Severin was the only regular soldier left in Wolumonde.

blocks.x: When Tatjana asks whether he really meant to kill him, Severin does not deny it.
If some great investor or prophet came to me and said that the sacrifice of just a few people would bring peace back to Wolumonde... I would do it gladly. Whoever it might be.
Then he says it once more. No matter who.
Moments later, a roar rises from underground. The armed group has slipped into the industrial district through underground passages and crippled the main power plant.

Around that time, one of his men says they lost four comrades in the blaze and wants to wipe out the town. **Mudrock**, the squad's captain, shakes his head. There is only one killer to deal with, he says. If they dirty their hands out of hatred, they will be no different from what they once were.
4. Eight in the Cellar

Meanwhile, other Rhodes Island operators have come to the burned camp. **GreyThroat**, the crossbow operator who once escorted Atro to Wolumonde. **Ayerscarpe**, bodyguard to Catastrophe Messenger Leonhardt. And **Click**, who got stranded in the Winterwisp Mountains and was rescued by the other two.

blocks.cap: On a supply crate, the dust is missing from one square patch, where something once lay.

blocks.x: GreyThroat guesses that what lay there was Atro's badge, and goes alone to find out what became of Atro.

Meanwhile, at the Rathaus, Severin finally admits to the famine. On the day the Great Rift opened, the farmland and supply facilities exploded, and with the power plant now lost, the town cannot leave the mountains before winter. When Suzuran asks why the quarantine zone was so poor, he asks her in return whether she thinks Oripathy is the only problem in this world.
When Folinic says this is a murder case, Severin sends the others away and takes the two below ground.

blocks.cap: A frozen cellar. Among bodies no one can identify, Folinic finds Atro.

blocks.x: Eight bodies lie in refrigeration units kept running by Severin's Arts. Folinic stops before one of them. Do you know how long I've been looking for you, she says. You stupid cat.
While they give her some space, Severin takes out another cigarette. Suzuran, trying to stop him, notices something. Severin asks her to keep it secret for now.

At length, Severin produces the autonomous Arts unit of the **L-44 'Gramophone'**, an Arts-generating device for town defense. Any Leithanian with a higher education can operate it, and overloaded, it becomes a weapon.

blocks.cap: The device that protected the town became the weapon that burned the camp.

blocks.x: Folinic says she will find the culprit and make them pay. When Suzuran says she mustn't, Folinic answers that she knows that better than anyone. Even so, there is one thing she will ask the culprit. Why. What for.

Then Tatjana brings news: most of those working with the Infected were not Infected themselves. Severin grinds his teeth. The **Winterwisp**. Those damned people have come to throw Wolumonde into turmoil again.
5. On Whom, or What, Do I Take My Revenge

When Folinic was small, her mother left for the place where the people who had tormented her father were, and never came back. The one who came for the girl left behind was Kal'tsit. Kal'tsit told her only that her mother lay buried with her father, deep in Ursus. And to one very simple question, she never gave an answer.
On whom, or what, do I take my revenge?

Around then, at the burned camp, Click and Ayerscarpe come face to face with an armored Sarkaz. Mudrock, who says he came only to lay flowers for his comrades, catches GreyThroat's bolt from behind with Arts of mud.

He shows the mark of Reunion, yet says he is no longer Reunion, only one more Infected. Four of his comrades died in that fire, and it was no accident. Someone did it. Until Wolumonde hands over the culprit, he has no reason to hold back the enraged Infected. With that, he leaves.

Meanwhile, Folinic and Suzuran go around the streets asking about the Winterwisp, but the residents clam up, saying it is the subject the old nobles hate most. As the sun sets, Folinic murmurs, as if to herself. What do I do, Mama.
6. Winterwisp Elegy

At dusk, a song no one can make out spreads through the streets, and even the rampaging protesters fall silent. Severin says it is a Winterwisp folk song once sung only at funerals, and reads it as a signal passed between the rebels.

blocks.cap: An alley at sundown, with nothing left but the singing.

blocks.x: The Winterwisp were a Caprinae tribe that ruled these mountains centuries ago. Severin says only that they came to their present state after clashing with Wolumonde. When Folinic presses him, he closes the subject. It would offend the nobles.

Soon the rebels begin attacking the streets with seized 'Gramophones.' Even uninfected residents join the protests, and Wolumonde splits in two. Severin declares martial law. Suzuran says something more terrible, where right and wrong are hard to tell apart, seems to have already begun.
The streets lined with wooden buildings begin to burn. Evacuating residents, Tatjana shields one of them and injures her ankle, and there she runs into an armed Infected shouting 'noble puppet.'

Around then, hearing that Folinic and Tatjana are still out on the streets, Severin shouts, and GreyThroat and Ayerscarpe appear before him. Judging that at this rate the town will run aground within thirty minutes at most, Severin asks the two to look after Tatjana and Folinic.

GreyThroat rescues the fallen Tatjana. From a captured rebel, Folinic learns why there is not a single gendarme in Wolumonde. A great noble in his high tower married the only daughter of another noble house, and every gendarme was tied up guarding the wedding in a neighboring nomadic town.

When they regroup, Folinic lashes out at GreyThroat. Would it have been different if you had stayed by Atro's side? GreyThroat answers that she is sorry she could not be there. Folinic lowers her head. She is the one who should apologize.

When she hears the rebels are calling themselves 'Reunion,' Folinic wants to go out, saying there is no need to show mercy. GreyThroat tells her to stay and tend the wounded. Suzuran agrees. If Folinic keeps fighting like this, she will stop being the Folinic Suzuran knows.
7. The Last Winterwisp

Meanwhile, at a base outside the town, Mudrock speaks to a Sarkaz warrior. The rebels will call themselves Reunion, and in the end it is his squad who will be caught. This place must not become a battlefield.

blocks.cap: The Mudrock Squad's base outside the town.

blocks.x: And at the meeting in the Rathaus, GreyThroat asks how the eight bodies were identified. By build, sex, age, and the missing persons list, comes the answer. Mudrock said he lost four comrades in that fire, but on Severin's list, the Infected from outside numbered three.
When Folinic cuts in, Severin draws a line. He is obliged to uncover the truth, but not to bear responsibility for her thirst for revenge. Outside the window, residents are shouting for a fight.

Around then, among the wounded, Suzuran meets an old man who says he is the last Winterwisp. He confesses that in his youth he killed peddlers and nobles for revenge, and that after Severin dealt with the other old men who had been with him, he lived hidden underground, alone. Bloodline, he says, is only an excuse people recall when their hatred burns.
And on the day the power plant fell, he saw it. **Biederman**, the Catastrophe Messenger who should have died in the fire, leading the Infected and smashing the power plant with Arts.
Winterwisp... Winterwisp is Wolumonde. It is the moon itself...

The old man says the road before him is the road to the mountains. It is an ordinary street leading to the Rathaus, but Suzuran tells him yes, it is the road to the mountains, and bids him farewell. Good night.

Hearing the old man's story, Severin speaks of Biederman. After the Great Rift, resented by the townsfolk, he shut himself away and did nothing but drink, until Atro broke down his door and got him back on his feet. Meanwhile, the agitated residents have handed out weapons and surged toward Zwölftontechnik Strasse.
A giant made of rock blocks their way, and the two sides curse each other, weapons in hand. Suzuran cries that they have to stop this. Folinic holds her back and silently shakes her head.
8. The Culprit Was Already Dead
Amid the chaos, while Folinic is going so far as to use poison to force out Biederman's whereabouts, Severin, taking Tatjana's report, coughs up black blood.
Folinic examines his throat and freezes. Originium crystals have spread from his lungs up into his throat. Severin is Infected, and the infection looks to predate the Catastrophe by a long way.

Severin asks her to keep his infection secret, and says he will confess to being the one who set the fire. Asked about the real culprit, he answers that at least it will take away people's excuse for killing one another.
When he asks for her help, Folinic answers that she has no authority to speak for Rhodes Island. But for Atro's sake, if nothing else, 'we' will not give up on Wolumonde.
Back at the Rathaus, GreyThroat reports that she has found Biederman. Folinic wants to go after him at once. The answer is brief. Biederman is already dead.

The body, found near a 'Gramophone,' bears a wound on the back of the head and ice crystals. He was struck down with Arts and died a few hours earlier. Folinic's face, so sure she had finally found someone to take revenge on, slowly sets hard.
Meanwhile, searching Biederman's house, Ayerscarpe and Click find an operation agreement from the **Contingency Contract**. Biederman was a Contingency Contract Catastrophe Messenger.

blocks.cap: Biederman's house. A Contingency Contract operation agreement was left behind.

blocks.x: Then, at the end of the street, a massive stone statue rises, and the rebels cheer that Reunion has come to liberate them. Before the statue, Mudrock stops one step short. It is the last chance he will give them, he says.
9. The Fall of the Moonlight

Meanwhile, the last 'Gramophone' is destroyed and the fire spreads. Before Tatjana's eyes, a resident engulfed in flames calls her name and begs for help. Tatjana freezes where she stands and thinks: did Thor suffer like this, back then?

blocks.cap: Fire spreads through the street where the last line of defense has fallen.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, Suzuran, holding back the rebels alone, is asked why she sides with the other side when she is Infected herself. She answers back: do not decide other people's fates for them. But faced with rebels who say no one here is innocent, her Arts reach their limit, and a bolt from GreyThroat saves her.

Mudrock tears off his Reunion insignia and steps forward. When Folinic smashes through the statue and charges at him, Mudrock asks whether her rage is for Dr. Atro. Folinic tells him not to speak Atro's name with that mouth.

Then Severin steps onto the battlefield, puts forward the dead Biederman as the true culprit, and shouts that he has been caught. But the rebels cry, what use is a true culprit now, and call for Reunion's new era. Severin tells Mudrock to kill him, asking only to borrow a light, since this will be his last cigarette.
Mudrock answers that if Severin dies, they will leave this place and make an example of his death. In that moment, Suzuran throws herself between them. Why does anyone have to die?
Ayerscarpe and Click tie up the remaining rebels, and GreyThroat aims a bolt at Mudrock. Folinic declares she will hold this square and the Rathaus, because this is the town Atro wanted to protect.
Mudrock asks: what caused that fire, and what did that fire cause in turn? When Folinic answers that the source of it all is already dead, Mudrock orders a withdrawal.
Would you get through the winter on the fire of your rage? Or would you burn the bodies of the innocent to keep out the cold?

When the rebels still refuse to back down, Mudrock uses an ancient Arts that eats away at his own lifespan to raise the entire ruins into a giant. Before that giant, which tells anyone still wishing to fight to bring him down first, the rebels finally abandon the town and leave.

The Sarkaz warrior says he has quit smoking and tosses his spare matches to Severin. Mudrock turns away, telling him to treasure the life he barely kept, and the last fragment of rock falls onto the burning street.
10. Upon the Ashes

After the riot, Ayerscarpe names Biederman as the source of it all. Some Messengers in the Contingency Contract will use any means to 'save' more people. If he meant to kill a Rhodes Island operator to draw outside attention, it would make sense.

But the 'Gramophone' Arts unit that Severin brings out shakes that theory. It was surely the source of the fire. But Biederman was not Leithanian and had been here only a little over half a year. He could not have overloaded the latest equipment and wielded Arts capable of vaporizing people in an instant.

blocks.cap: The Rathaus after the riot. The culprit's identity remains unknown.

blocks.x: Severin says he gave up on uncovering the truth on the day his son's funeral was canceled. All he hopes is that those who survived can at least live better lives.

GreyThroat's hand trembles as she urges him to get examined. To her, who admits she still fears the Infected, Severin tells of the day he was infected. Back when he was hunting down the old Winterwisp men, the last of them, by a lakeside, stabbed him in the chest with Originium, and the two of them fell into the lake together.
Around then, Tatjana greets Folinic with a slightly brighter face. At least the culprit has paid the price, she says. Folinic is silent for a moment, then answers that she is right.

Meanwhile, at the Rathaus, voices rise calling for a new Schultz to replace the Infected one, and up ahead, troops flying the Gendarmerie's flag are sighted. In the middle of that argument, the former Schultz, Severin Hawthorn, has fallen asleep from exhaustion.

In his dream, his son, now a giant, sweeps away the Catastrophe clouds, lifts up their hometown, and walks toward where the snow melts. In the dream he was smiling, but he could not stop the tears. They were the first tears he had shed since losing his son.
11. A Voice Through the Door

Back in time, after the Great Rift had passed. Biederman, beaten by the townsfolk, is consoled by Severin: it isn't your fault. Yet, thinking of the famine to come, he repeats it to himself. This is not my fault.

Seven days later, the one who kicked in his door was Atro. She asked him to help at the clinic, and Biederman could find no reason to refuse. Around that time, Severin confided to him a plan to put food for the Infected refugees gathered on Zwölftontechnik Strasse behind that of the official residents.

Then one day, a letter from the Contingency Contract lies in Biederman's room. A voice outside his door tells him not to open it, only to listen. The original plan, to deal with the matter of the wedding, has failed, it says. Now they will light a spark, so the nobles learn of the disaster in this land.

Biederman protests that Atro is a good doctor. Many people will die even if they do nothing, the voice answers. Better to clear the way first, so that as few as possible are sacrificed. And it says that it, too, will die in that riot.
All of it... for the sake of more lives.

When he opens the door, only ice crystals remain in the hallway. If no riot breaks out, those words will come to nothing, Biederman tells himself. At the very least, Dr. Atro must not be caught up in it.
But the voice has not yet left. Biederman calls out to the owner of that voice, who shook off pursuers in the snowfield by covering himself with cold Arts. **Thorwald.**

He lets the question of what he means to do about his father and that young woman pass. In his hand is the core of an Arts unit taken from a 'Gramophone.' When it is all over, he will be waiting over there, he says. That will be our grave.
You're afraid, Biederman says. Thorwald answers. Of course. Of course I'm afraid.
Epilogue — Mourning

Meanwhile, outside the town, the Mudrock Squad decides to leave for Kazdel before winter comes. It is the last stop for all the rootless who have no home or homeland to return to, Mudrock says, so it will take in their comrades who are not Sarkaz as well. To the worry that Severin might pin the crime on them, he answers that Severin is a man who always chooses whatever does the least harm to the town.
Around then, GreyThroat is waiting for someone at the burned camp. Folinic arrives and thanks her. Without you and Lisa, she says, I might have ruined everything.

blocks.cap: The burned camp. GreyThroat waits here for someone.

blocks.x: Folinic blames herself. She neither brought the culprit to justice nor saved the town Atro had protected. GreyThroat answers that the only one blaming her is herself. Atro would have patted her on the shoulder and had a drink with her.

Mudrock arrives with freshly picked wildflowers. Folinic confides that the eight casualties have now become hundreds of times that, and that rage and vengeance that were not even her own nearly broke her too. No one could have done it, Mudrock answers.
He tells them that rumors are spreading among Leithanien's Infected that Reunion has not vanished. Telling Rhodes Island's swallow, who fights for the Infected, that they will meet again, he leaves.
Folinic asks how long it took to cut off grief and move on. GreyThroat says it took quite a while. Until she had lost more. Then she asks what Folinic will do now.
We go back to Rhodes Island. Atro too... with us.

Wolumonde forbade funerals for the dead and chose to leave them in the ground of the wasteland. Those who cannot leave with the town lose their home forever. From that land, Folinic chooses to go home with her friend.

act5d0.tagline: A young master whose commute gets blown up on the first day of his internship races through Lungmen's festival night with Penguin Logistics—and ends up defusing a candy bomb. A night when the living have to be loud so the dead can leave in peace. Happy Sauin.

chars.name: Bison
chars.desc: Son of the president of MountainDash Logistics and the youngest Messenger in his family's history. Sent to Penguin Logistics as a temp on his father's orders.

chars.name: Mostima
chars.desc: A Penguin Logistics Messenger back in Lungmen after a long time away. A black-horned Sankta who prefers to work alone.

chars.name: Emperor
chars.desc: The boss of Penguin Logistics. A rapping penguin who calls himself an artist.

chars.name: Texas
chars.desc: Penguin Logistics' wolf-eared Messenger. A woman of few words, but put her behind a wheel or hand her a blade and nothing stops her.

chars.name: Exusiai
chars.desc: Penguin Logistics' Sankta sniper. Cheerful, free-spirited, and a magnet for trouble.

chars.name: Croissant
chars.desc: A hammer-swinging Penguin Logistics employee. Thick accent, and quick with the money math.

chars.name: Sora
chars.desc: A Penguin Logistics Messenger. Keeps watch over the boss's bar, The Ends of the Earth.

chars.name: Gambino
chars.desc: Boss of a mafia Family pushed out of Siracusa and into Lungmen. Clings to the old way, where nothing ends until blood is spilled.

chars.name: Capone
chars.desc: A ranking member of the Gambino Family. Came to Lungmen seven years ahead of the rest to lay the groundwork for the Family's business.

chars.name: Rat King
chars.desc: An old man rumored to rule Lungmen's slums. No one can say for certain who he really is.

chars.name: Jaye
chars.desc: A scary-looking young vendor. Tonight he's minding Uncle Tung's finball stall.

chars.name: Waai Fu
chars.desc: A student working part-time at a detective agency. Can't stand to see injustice.

chars.name: Uncle Tung
chars.desc: A street vendor known as 'Lungmen's premier finball master.' Jaye helps out at his stall.

chars.name: Wei Yenwu
chars.desc: The highest authority in Lungmen.

chars.name: Eurill
chars.desc: President of MountainDash Logistics. Bison's father.

chars.name: Lappland
chars.desc: A Lupo who turned up in Lungmen on Texas's trail. Knew Texas back in her Siracusa days.

terms.name: Sauin
terms.desc: A festival held every year in Lungmen. Originally a day to send off the souls of the dead, but these days it's better known as a festival full of candles and candy.

terms.name: Penguin Logistics
terms.desc: A private logistics company in Lungmen. On paper it's an ordinary delivery service, but in practice it's known as the most unpredictable armed group in the city.

terms.name: MountainDash Logistics
terms.desc: A major corporation that controls a large share of Lungmen's private Messenger business. Run by Bison's father.

terms.name: The Ends of the Earth
terms.desc: The bar on Sunset Boulevard that Penguin Logistics uses as a base. Despite the grand name, it's just a bar.

terms.name: Sicilian
terms.desc: What the mafiosi who came over from Siracusa call themselves. Originally the name of one of the roots of Siracusa's Twelve Families.

blocks.x: Lungmen's **Sauin** was originally a day to send off the souls of the dead. These days, though, candles, candy, and sale banners fill the streets for what's become 'the grandest festival in Lungmen.'

One cloudy night, at a corner table in a bar on Sunset Boulevard, **Gambino**, a mafia boss from Siracusa, and **Capone**, who'd already been settled in Lungmen for years, start arguing over a card game—and Gambino even suggests they just torch this tasteless bar. Unfortunately for him, the owner was listening.
Who you callin' 'tasteless?'

Then, on the evening of Sauin itself, **MountainDash Logistics**' young master, **Bison**, is sent by his father to work as a temp at **Penguin Logistics**. He finds out exactly what kind of 'logistics company' this is before he even clocks in.
1. First Day on the Job, and the Commute Blows Up

6:44 P.M., the Lungmen Ring Expressway. In the car, Bison—the youngest Messenger in his family's history—is listening to his old butler fret. More than half of Lungmen's private Messenger business already belongs to his father, and the last holdout, and the most suspicious company of all, is Penguin Logistics.
When the butler mentions that, it being Sauin, the young master could have been out on the town with his friends, Bison's reply is: '...Real funny. Me not having friends is a joke to you, huh?'

blocks.cap: "My father... he definitely has his own ideas." Bison in the car on his way to work.

blocks.x: That's when the expressway blows up. Gambino's crew had buried a bomb in the median. The one who drags Bison out of the smoke is **Exusiai**, a sniper who had already taken down the entire demolition team on her own.

**Croissant** clears a path with her hammer, but the three of them still end up cornered in a dead end. Nowhere left to run, and what does Exusiai say? 'We haven't properly introduced ourselves, have we?'

Then a voice rings out from somewhere: 'We got a serious emphasis on corporate culture. And today's culture buzzword is "courtesy."' The wolf **Texas** has the way out blocked, and **Emperor**, the boss of Penguin Logistics, hits the lights.

blocks.cap: "Welcome to Penguin Logistics, little doggies." No landing visa means deportation, apparently.

blocks.x: 2. Company Rule No. 1 Changes Every Day

The Penguin Logistics base they end up at is dark and a total mess. While Bison earnestly lays out countermeasures, calling the attack an act of terrorism against both companies, Emperor asks, in order, about dinner, the cigars in his drawer, and where his vinyl records went.

According to Exusiai, fights like this happen seventeen or eighteen times a month. The first important rule Emperor teaches the new guy is 'Don't sweat the small stuff'—but Exusiai says yesterday it was 'Live for the party,' and Croissant remembers it as 'Carpe diem.'

Then a candy box labeled 'Victorian Gumdrops' turns up under the boss's sofa. The instant Texas yells 'Get down!', the box explodes—taking with it the box of records the boss went to great lengths to get on the Columbian black market.

blocks.cap: One of Penguin Logistics' bases. There was a candy box under the sofa.

blocks.x: Once the penguin's wailing dies down, Emperor makes a declaration: 'Every ticket you rack up tonight is on me. We're burying those damn punks right alongside my records!!!'

The weapon of choice for the highway chase that follows is the 'peacemaker': forty-two sheets of logistics-grade cardboard glued together with industrial adhesive and fired by rubber bands. It's because of the rule against live ammo in downtown Lungmen—though according to Texas, this is the only time the boss ever follows the rules.

Rubber rounds punch through the windows and blow out a tire, and the mafia car drags the penguins' car into a pileup. Leaving his colleagues stuck in their airbags, Bison chases the mafia alone—until a bullet from somewhere goes for his fuel tank, and he loses his balance and falls off the interchange.
3. Twelve Meters Down: A Pile of Candles and Mostima

Meanwhile, at a finball stall in Lungmen's Central Park. The guidebook says it belongs to an old man known as 'The Godly Finball Uncle,' but the one selling finballs is **Jaye**, a scary-looking young man with a kitchen knife beside him, and the tourists are whispering.

**Waai Fu**, a part-timer at a detective agency, drops by to pay off a tab and is in a hurry—she has an exam in two days. Sauin these days isn't about sending off souls anymore, she says; it's just a moneymaker for businesses. Next to her, a horned Sankta woman is eating finballs with a guidebook spread open.

blocks.cap: "The Great Foodie Guide never gets it wrong." Those horns are way too real to be a Sauin costume.

blocks.x: And where does Bison land after falling twelve meters? In a pile of Sauin decoration candles stacked in the park. The one who hides him—horns stuck full of candles—from the mafia is that very Sankta: **Mostima**, a Messenger of Penguin Logistics.

Around then, Emperor spots Bison from afar and tells everyone not to worry, since 'she's' with him. Exusiai just asks, '...She's back?' As for Mostima, her advice to Bison is simple: if you want to keep up with Penguin Logistics' tempo, just give up on thinking.

Afterward, Mostima buys him a green tea ice cream and takes him to an old candy shop—the one where, when she first came to Lungmen without a penny to her name, she could only stare through the display window. The old shopkeeper, who used to hand out rainbow-colored candy to kids for free, remembers the Mostima of those days.

The old man says that Sauin was originally a day for sending off the souls of the dead, but if the living are enjoying themselves, there's no better tribute than that. And if you buy his fruit gumdrops imported from Victoria, he'll throw in a candle decoration for free.
Out of the shop and up on a bridge, Mostima calmly informs him that disguised mafiosi have been tailing them since the candy shop—three ahead, three behind. Then she adds: 'Jump. Now.'
By the time Bison, having completed his second fall of the day onto a cargo ship loaded with candy, lifts his head, Mostima is already gone.
4. We Forgot the New Guy

Around 8 P.M., Bison is getting chewed out by the candy's owner at the docks when **Sora** of Penguin Logistics recognizes him—apparently his horns look exactly like the MountainDash logo. Thrilled to have her first-ever 'junior,' Sora happily takes him to Texas.

Meanwhile in the park, the penguins have tied a captured mafioso, Fronzo, to a firework and are interrogating him. But at the mention of the candy box bomb, the mafioso jumps: 'I don't know nothin' about no candy box!' Instead, he was just about to drop the name 'Rat King,' claiming 'the big man' had signed off on everything they were doing to the penguins.

Just then Sora and Bison arrive, and the moment Texas gets as far as 'Mostima is Laterano's...', a dazed Exusiai's match touches the fuse. Fronzo goes straight up into the sky. Turns out the ad claiming those fireworks could launch a person wasn't false advertising.

blocks.cap: Back in Central Park. The onlookers think it's a movie shoot.

blocks.x: To shake off the swarming mafia, Texas has them split into pairs and regroup at The Ends of the Earth in an hour. Exusiai and Croissant, Texas and Sora steal mafia motorcycles and vanish—leaving behind only Bison and an awkward silence with the mafiosi.

Bison chases the bikes on a bicycle lent to him by an onlooker, and it's only after regrouping that the penguins realize they left the new guy behind: '...Where's Bison?' And waiting for Bison, who finally catches up with a string of mafiosi in tow, is Gambino.

'Thanks for leading the way.' Gambino knocks Bison out, takes him hostage, and demands a showdown—and Texas replies that that suits them just fine. They were thinking the same thing. Time to get Bison back.
5. The Price of Crossing a Finball Master

Meanwhile, cracks are forming on the mafia side too. Unlike Gambino, who insists on the 'Sicilian way' where things only end in blood, Capone—who's spent seven years building a base in Lungmen—thinks it's enough to just take the penguins' place. In the end, Capone sends his own men into the slums to find the Rat King.

The mafiosi storm the slums, beating up residents to find out where the Rat King is, and their next target is the finball shop across from the fishmonger's. As luck would have it, the ones standing there are Jaye and Waai Fu.

When the thugs call the residents 'trash,' Waai Fu's fist flies first, and Jaye grabs the crossbowman's arm, thinks it over, and then actually breaks it. A resident lying on the ground shouts to Jaye: the thugs' next target is **Uncle Tung**.

blocks.cap: "A rotten finfish three days after the freezer lost power." That's Jaye trying his best to sound cool.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, with Bison tied up in a car, Capone's man takes out Gambino's man, and Capone offers Bison a deal: he'll get rid of both Gambino and Penguin Logistics in exchange for the penguins' delivery routes.

Bison refuses—he can't accept an offer from a man who talks about family right after killing one of his own Family. When Capone sneers that he's scared, Bison shoots back: 'Young Minoans are famous for their boldness.'

Just as Capone is about to get rid of him, Mostima shows up. She's just a Messenger passing by, she says, looking for a lost package. After staring at the black-horned Sankta for a long moment, Capone backs off, saying he has no interest in a fight.
6. A Shortcut Through the Cemetery

Mostima decides to walk Bison back to The Ends of the Earth. Disguised as ghosts under tablecloths, they slip through back alleys thick with steam from the sewers and come out at a cemetery in the middle of the city.

Walking among mourners dressed in black, Mostima talks about where Sauin came from. It began with an ancient Sarkaz rite: a day to welcome back the souls of the departed, soothe the attachments they left in this world, and send them on into the cycle of rebirth. Now, she says, the living just dress up as ghosts and pay no attention to the real spirits in the cemetery.

blocks.cap: Among the mourners. "Maybe being alive just means making it out of a catastrophe."

blocks.x: As they pass through the cemetery, Mostima reveals her job: 'Take Bison to see the world.' The client was his father, and Bison's internship grade depends on her opinion too.

That same night, an old couple lights candles at the grave of Ah Faat, a young man who was practically their grandson. The old man, saying he never once gave the boy a light, offers him a smoke before he goes, and comforts his weeping wife. You don't cry on Sauin.
Meanwhile, Mostima walks Bison to where he can see a shop with a giant penguin painted by the door, then leaves again, telling him only to get along with everyone.
Meanwhile, Uncle Tung was beaten by the mafia on his way to bring food to that old couple. He never told them where the man they were looking for was. Rules are rules.

The one who comes to see him, hurt as he is, is his old friend **Lin**. 'Is the Rat King so important?' When Tung says it's Lin they're really after, Lin only smiles and says that's what puts his mind at ease.
Helping his friend to his feet, Lin tells him to let the past go. His finballs are a part of Lungmen too, a more important part than Lin himself. 'You are already free.'
7. A Welcome Party with One Chair Left

10:26 P.M., The Ends of the Earth. The penguins have started Bison's welcome party without Bison. Emperor correctly identifies the cheap wine—his 'reserve weapon'—as supermarket stock, and Exusiai has baked an apple pie.

Then the crossbow bolts come pouring in. When even the rubber rounds run out, Emperor hands out his expensive liquor one bottle at a time and tells everyone to aim for the head, while Croissant counts every bottle that shatters—'100K, 150K, 450K, 700K...'—until she can't take it anymore and charges out with Bison and his shield.

Even so, Emperor keeps his promise to Lungmen's leader, **Wei Yenwu**: no killing in Lungmen, and business problems get solved with business. Though, he adds, after spending five hours on the run today, surely a few 'tragic, unanticipated deaths' in his own bar wouldn't be a problem?

Gambino taunts Texas as 'the stray dog who ran off to Lungmen,' but ends up subdued. Then, declaring that for a Sicilian there's no winning or losing, only living or dying, he sets off a bomb and escapes.

Texas, lightly wounded, explains that the name **Sicilian** comes from the Sicilian Union, one of the origins of Siracusa's Twelve Families and the first to get results through violence. And the only thing left intact in the bar is the one chair Emperor was sitting in.

blocks.cap: The Ends of the Earth. The night's sole survivor: one chair.

blocks.x: Emperor changes his mind. If they're going to pick a fight even on Sauin, there's nothing left to do but follow Sauin tradition and lay them to rest.
8. Reunited After Four Years and Three Months, Then a Sandstorm

Then at 11 P.M., Gambino catches on to Capone's betrayal. The two grew up together and even made their first kills together, but since their crushing defeat in Siracusa, they've gone completely separate ways.
Meanwhile, Croissant and Bison, out scouting, are eavesdropping on Capone's men right after they've cut off Gambino's communications—when, once again, that sniper's gunshot gives away their position.
And that sniper turns out to be Bison's butler. Master's orders or not, he's now gone as far as attacking the young master himself, and he sighs that once this is over, he's going back home.

Meanwhile, **Yith**, Penguin Logistics' info specialist, hacks into the team's comms and fills them in on the enemy's infighting. Just as Gambino storms Capone's hideout and the two face off with blades drawn, a fleeing Croissant smashes through a wall and tumbles into that very room.

In the end, two mafia factions and the penguins are all tangled up in one alley, and the henchmen, unsure who's on whose side, start hitting each other. Into that chaos steps Mostima, blocking Gambino's attack.
'How are you all doing?' Among colleagues going 'How many years has it been?', only Exusiai answers precisely.
...It's been almost four years and three months, Mostima.

Mostima laughs it off, telling her not to make such a serious face—it makes her look like she's sick. But then the wind suddenly picks up, and right after Mostima shouts to Texas to pull back, the alley collapses under a sandstorm.

blocks.cap: The alley where three gangs got tangled up. Moments later, an entire building vanishes.

blocks.x: As the mafia scatters, an old man's voice rings out behind them: 'Strange... I don't remember you having any shots left.' It's the **Rat King** of the slums.

After escaping the storm, Mostima lists off the embarrassing history of a sand-covered Exusiai—right down to how the old school she accidentally blew up hung a banner reading 'Good luck in Lungmen, Exusiai!' 'You playing my big sister now?!' 'Yeah, pretty much.'

Exusiai asks why she came back now of all times, but in the end swallows what she really wants to ask. When Mostima tries to leave again, Exusiai starts, 'It's just a few hours for you, but for me...' and then changes course: 'You better buy me dinner sometime! Really!'
Right after that, the penguins—each wherever they happen to be—find themselves surrounded by ordinary-looking Lungmen citizens.
9. The Old Rat's Rules

Meanwhile, Mostima goes to see the Rat King. He says it was nothing but a few puppets slipping out of his control and hurting a finball master, but his face says otherwise. He can't just stand by while thugs trample the slums, he says—they kept breaking the rules.
Asked what she'd do if she came into money, Mostima says she'd buy that candy shop. The Rat King laughs: she can have everything but the cellar—what else can he say, it's his shop.

Then, around midnight, Lin walks with Uncle Tung among the graves of their old brothers in the cemetery. Uncle Tung, who took a bullet for Wei Yenwu and has never walked straight since, says it was no loss, since Lungmen is still standing, and asks Lin to outlive him—just by a little.

When his friend worries that Jaye might have gotten into trouble, Lin offers to go in his place, and tells him to live a long life, sell plenty of finballs, and take on apprentices. 'The Rat King still lives... It's not your turn to die yet.'

blocks.cap: The cemetery in the middle of the city. Rascally Chan, Fake Yama, Ah Faat... old neighbors, lying together.

blocks.x: Just after midnight, Jaye and Waai Fu, who had gone looking for the thugs who hurt Uncle Tung, find themselves cornered between Gambino and Capone. The Rat King appears, and when Waai Fu steps in front of him to shield him, he sends the two of them away, saying he made a promise that children wouldn't get dragged into this sort of thing.
As the ground sinks into sand, Gambino shouts that he'd rather die like a Sicilian than kneel. The one who stabs him is Capone, who immediately tells the Rat King that his Family will follow him.
But the Rat King's answer is cold. That's Lungmen's rule, not his. Capone's men had already finished making a deal with the Rat King.

The deal: if it ever came to brothers drawing blades on each other, they would surrender in exchange for the rest of their comrades being let go. Having lost everything, Capone grinds his teeth—'Lin Gray, you're more Sicilian than either of us'—but the Rat King lets him go without killing him.
10. A Funeral for One Penguin

Meanwhile, at 12:38 A.M., the penguins reach the outdoor party in the plaza that Emperor called them to. In a place reeking of candy, Waai Fu challenges Texas to a one-on-one, determined to fix their habit of dragging citizens into their messes every single time. If she wins, the penguins will follow the rules—for 'at least one month.'
Then the loudspeakers blare and rap god Emperor takes the stage. The crowd chants 'Emperor!', but Texas mutters that people would never move in such perfect lockstep.
The next moment, an old man is standing behind Emperor. 'Good night, Mr. Emperor. And a happy Sauin to you.' Emperor collapses, and the old man takes the mic.

blocks.cap: "People of Lungmen, good evening." The Rat King's special Sauin announcement.

blocks.x: The one who just died is nothing but an insignificant penguin, so the festival goes on, he says—and he asks everyone to find the gift a friend from Siracusa has hidden somewhere at the party. Nearly the whole crowd is the Rat King's people, and only then does Bison recognize the old man as the grandpa from the candy shop.

Meanwhile, high above the plaza, Mostima stands before the Rat King. When she says killing her boss isn't something she can just let slide, the Rat King replies that Penguin Logistics is far too high-handed and needs a sharp lesson.

blocks.cap: An Arts staff wreathed in flame. "Respecting my elders is kind of my thing."

blocks.x: Down below, surrounded and flustered, Bison finally picks up his communicator and calls the butler who's been secretly following him all along. He knows it was all his father's orders, so he won't hold it against him, he says—and gives an order: 'Send them all flying!'
Then he shoves Croissant aside and rams an enemy with his shield, sending them flying. From above, where she's fighting the Rat King, Mostima shouts: 'Bison, go with your heart—don't think!'
11. Happy Sauin

The whole penguin crew gathers before the Rat King, but blades snap on contact with the sand and the hammer gets swallowed by it. Mostima breaks his sand shield, Exusiai and Sora open a gap, and at last the tip of Texas's sword slices the old man's coat.
The Rat King is silent for a moment, then speaks. That coat was a gift from his daughter, and in all these long years, they're the first ones ever to lay a finger on it.
At that moment a gunshot rings out and the Rat King falls. The shooter is the butler. The Rat King was about to use his Arts, he says, and the young master's safety comes first.
When Bison asks if he was the bait, the butler swears the master never meant to use him, then leaves, taking the fallen Rat King with him. All that's left is the 'gift' the Rat King mentioned.

Searching for the gift, Bison thinks back to the candy box at the base and the Victorian gumdrops at the candy shop. Maybe the Rat King had been dropping hints from the very start. What he finds is a steel box 80 centimeters across, with a timer ticking.
As Bison, trusting his shield, gets ready to defuse it himself, Mostima chimes in: 'That wire's the same color as my hair.' Startled, Bison's fingers go 'snip'—and the timer hits zero.

The blast launches the two of them into the sky—but what rains down isn't fire, it's candy. As the candy rain falls, the mafia and the Rat King's men alike stop what they're doing. It was the signal to stand down.

blocks.cap: Candy from the sky?! That's the old candy-shop man's way of joining the festival.

blocks.x: Out from among the melted candy comes a single note: 'Happy Sauin.' Bison has only one reaction: '...Whaaaat????'
Epilogue. Around Daybreak

3:21 A.M. Toasts ring out again in the ruins of The Ends of the Earth. Croissant says she feels great, since someone's going to cover the hole in the budget—but Bison alone can't bring himself to laugh.

Cutting Mostima off just as she's about to tell him his grade, Bison speaks first. He won't be staying. Penguin Logistics might really be a mess—but maybe that's exactly why it's closer to his ideals.
I think there's room in this world for Messengers like this, and for living like this.

Mostima gives him her blessing as a fellow Messenger. To Exusiai, who clings to her saying she has so much to ask, Mostima says she'll tell her everything—about that business in Laterano, about Exusiai's sister, about her own horns—but not now.

To the butler waiting outside, Bison says he has a rough idea of what happened: his father and Emperor had it all arranged, and then the mafia dragged the Rat King into it. Then, turning away, he adds: 'I did have a pretty good time tonight.'

Meanwhile, inside the bar, beside a sleeping Exusiai, Mostima gives her regular report to an overseer from Laterano. The overseer's title changes every month; this time it's 'Suffering,' and last month it was 'Super Sticky.'

blocks.cap: Two people from Laterano, with a sleeping Exusiai between them. One of them is this month's 'Suffering.'

blocks.x: The one eavesdropping on that conversation is Emperor, whom everyone thought was dead. Ignoring the overseer's 'Wait, you're not dead...?', he promises the departing Mostima her next job. They'll all be seeing each other again soon, he says.

At dawn, Bison, lost and back at the cemetery again, spots Mostima praying—but she vanishes once more. When some punks who've pegged him for a rich kid come picking a fight, Bison bursts out laughing in disbelief: '...Again?'

A little later, the penguins tear off toward the docks in a new car to get 'Bison's revenge.' Three hours and twenty-five minutes until Bison leaves—plenty of time, they say, to beat everyone up and still throw him a farewell party.

And the Rat King was alive. The butler brought him to The Ends of the Earth, where he shares a drink with Wei Yenwu for the first time in a long while and talks about his daughter. Even if she chooses a road that leads nowhere, he has to know when to let go—and he'll hold on until the day Lungmen no longer needs a Rat King.

Then Emperor bursts in with a flying kick. The butler's shot was a planned setup, he fumes, but the hole in his own belly was real. The Rat King asks whether a bandage wouldn't take care of it. 'As if you could even die.'

Bison's father, **Eurill**, arriving right after, laughs and says his company will cover all of tonight's costs. And so the commotion ends, and watching the sun come up, the Rat King says to Wei Yenwu:
The road we walk... there's no one left to follow after us now.

And Gambino, who survived because Capone's blade missed his vitals, runs into Capone again on his way out of Lungmen. Before them appears **Lappland**, a wolf who says she came looking for Texas, and with a grin, she gives them ten seconds to try running.
According to Mostima, this whole commotion happened because somebody trashed the boss's taste in the boss's own bar.

Thanks to that, on Sauin night—a night for sending off the dead—Lungmen was especially loud. If the dead can only leave without regrets when the living celebrate noisily, there could hardly have been a grander send-off. Happy Sauin.

act3d0.tagline: The story of a beach-town vacation where believing the mayor's daughter when she says 'the volcano is about to blow' gets you wanted by City Hall and ends with a door blown clean off its hinges. And a paradise one man built for his wife, which will one day sink beneath the lava.

chars.name: Ceylon
chars.desc: Daughter of Siesta's mayor and an Originium researcher. Even with the observatory insisting nothing is wrong, she chases the volcano's warning signs on her own.

chars.name: Schwarz
chars.desc: The bodyguard who has looked after Ceylon since childhood. Warm as an older sister, yet hiding a skill with a certain chill to it.

chars.name: Herman
chars.desc: Mayor of Siesta and Ceylon's father. Has been away for a long time, supposedly on business in the new development district.

chars.name: Cronin
chars.desc: The mayor's secretary and Siesta's Catastrophe Messenger. Brushes off Ceylon's warnings, telling everyone not to worry about the volcano.

chars.name: Provence
chars.desc: A Catastrophe Messenger. A free spirit who loves poking around everywhere under the pretext of fieldwork.

chars.name: Skyfire
chars.desc: A scholar of volcanic ecology. Can't rest until she's said everything she wants to say, no matter who she's talking to.

chars.name: Eyjafjalla
chars.desc: Rhodes Island's volcanologist. Analyzes samples from Siesta's volcano over comms.

chars.name: Hellagur
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island veteran. Reads the situation coolly, with eyes that have seen it all.

chars.name: Ifrit
chars.desc: A young Caster who wields an Originium flamethrower. Has an uncanny nose for a fun fight.

chars.name: Vigna
chars.desc: A cheerful fighter who plays delivery girl, starting by breaking the door down.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: The leader of Rhodes Island. Came to Siesta on vacation with the Doctor.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: Rhodes Island's doctor. The one who recommended a Siesta vacation to the Doctor's group.

chars.name: Gummy
chars.desc: Rhodes Island's cook. Opens a stall selling special Ursus drinks on the beachside food street.

chars.name: Thorns
chars.desc: An Ægirian from Iberia. Blunt, but can't bring himself to ignore whatever is right in front of him.

chars.name: Elysium
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator. Stays behind to guard the ship and begs Thorns to get him a band autograph.

chars.name: Cutter
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator. Grills meat with Ifrit at a barbecue stall on the beach.

chars.name: Aya
chars.desc: A member of the band Alive Until Sunset. Strikes up a conversation with Thorns at the water's edge at dusk.

terms.name: Siesta
terms.desc: A tourist city between a volcano and the sea. Famous for its Obsidian, it hosts the Obsidian Festival every year.

terms.name: Obsidian Festival
terms.desc: A music festival held across the whole city for half a month. During it, Siesta is so packed with tourists there's barely room to stand.

terms.name: Obsidian
terms.desc: A special ore from Siesta's volcano. It became a craze on the claim that it suppresses Oripathy, but mining it is now banned.

terms.name: Alive Until Sunset
terms.desc: A popular band performing at the Obsidian Festival. Their songs about the sea are said to be especially popular with Ægirians.

blocks.x: They call it the sea, but strictly speaking it's a huge lake, and on its shore, beneath a volcano, sits the tourist city of **Siesta**. Famous for its Obsidian, the city boils over every year with the **Obsidian Festival**, half a month when the whole city becomes one big stage.

But ahead of the festival, one young researcher got her answer back: 'nothing abnormal.' The volcano observatory had rejected her request for a public warning, saying sample temperatures and steam emissions were both normal.

blocks.cap: The sample analysis sheet from the observatory. Conclusion: 'nothing abnormal.'

blocks.x: "The volcano has been in a very dangerous state since around this time last year!" With the authorities refusing to budge, she decides to find an expert among the tourists flooding in for the festival. This is her last chance, she says.
1. A Volcano Called Friend, and the Woman with the Whiskey
And among those tourists were Rhodes Island's Doctor and **Amiya**. The trip was **Kal'tsit**'s recommendation, though Kal'tsit herself bowed out with a single "Not interested."

36 degrees, the hottest day of the summer. Little Caster **Ifrit** ran off first thing in the morning yelling "Sea, here I come!" and promptly went missing, while Amiya quietly added that, strictly speaking, it's just a huge lake.

Meanwhile, the street broadcast features **Cronin**, the mayor's assistant and Siesta's Catastrophe Messenger. According to him, the Catastrophe passed the city by thanks to the volcano, and there are so few Infected here thanks to **Obsidian**, which supposedly suppresses Oripathy.

blocks.cap: "Siesta's volcano is like a friend to us."

blocks.x: He even mentions that mining is banned for harming the environment, but trading is still open. Amiya tilts her head: something about the way this man talks about scientific evidence just feels off to her.
Then they run into the scholar **Skyfire** and the Catastrophe Messenger **Provence** on the street, who are skipping the beach for a field survey at the foot of the volcano.

When even Amiya gets drafted to help out at **Gummy**'s stall on the beachside food street, the Doctor ends up alone at the open-air hotel bar on the beach. There, a stranger who picks up the tab for a glass of whiskey says: "To protect this place, I'll do whatever it takes."
When a bodyguard calls her 'Boss' and says Mr. Cronin is looking for her, the woman leaves, saying she hopes the Doctor will come to like this city.
Soon after, a call comes in from Provence. Is anyone else around? This might be a matter of the city's very survival.
2. The Scholar Who Wants to Burn the Forest, and the Young Lady Who Climbed the Mountain Alone

A little earlier, in the forest at the foot of the volcano. Skyfire was asking "Can't we just burn this whole area to the ground?" for the tenth time in an hour, and Provence was barely talking her down, pointing out that a forest fire would only make trouble for the Doctor.

blocks.cap: The forest at the foot of the volcano. Accompanied by one scholar who finds all these trees and weeds very much in the way.

blocks.x: But something was off about the forest. Even for summer, the temperature was abnormal, a sharp smell hung in the air, and the meter they'd gotten from their colleague **Eyjafjalla** started reacting. Even the Obsidian they pried off the rock face felt unusual to the touch.

Then came a scream from someone surrounded by a swarm of Originium Slugs, and the person they rescued was none other than that researcher. Seeing her in a suit and boots, Skyfire guesses right away that she rushed out the moment something occurred to her, without even changing.

Back at their lodgings, she formally introduces herself. **Ceylon** Doykos: a graduate of Victoria National University who majored in Originium research, and the daughter of this city's mayor. What she'd been chasing was evidence that the volcano might erupt.

Over comms, Eyjafjalla's analysis ran a full forty minutes. The conclusion matched Ceylon's hunch: volcanic activity was rising abnormally and would hit the critical point within two to four weeks. Next to Provence, who says by the time she snapped out of it the talk was already over, Ceylon's eyes light up as she promises to write it all down.

blocks.cap: "If at all possible, it would be best to start preparing the citizens for evacuation right away."

blocks.x: Ceylon's father, Mayor **Herman**, had been at the new development district for three months, leaving city affairs to his secretary Cronin, and Ceylon believed that as a Catastrophe Messenger he would understand the data the moment he saw it. In the meantime, Provence and Skyfire decide to go into the volcano to pin down when it will erupt.
3. Brought a Warning, Became a Fugitive

Then, 2 p.m., on the way to City Hall. Ceylon reminisces that jazz was all the rage when she was little, remembering the days she'd open a book at a café on Second Avenue and let the sea breeze wash over her.

Her mother died giving birth to her and her father buried himself in work, but the one who raised her was the family bodyguard, **Schwarz**. Not related by blood, but like an older sister, and above all, precious family.

But at City Hall, Cronin dismisses her material as baseless data. Did the Originium Slugs tell you that themselves? he sneers, before flatly declaring that the observation equipment the mayor himself planned shows nothing wrong.
Then he turns the blame on the Doctor, claiming that a gang jealous of Siesta's growth has fooled even the young lady. "Grab the young lady too, so she can calm down. Just don't hurt her!"

blocks.cap: Siesta City Hall. The one who brought a volcano warning became a 'suspicious tourist.'

blocks.x: The Doctor and Ceylon jump out the window and run for the crowds on the beach. And the one who blocks their way is, of all people, Schwarz, whose face the Doctor recognizes. She was the woman who bought the whiskey at the bar.
"Milady, while the master is away, you must listen to Mr. Cronin." Ceylon's delighted face freezes, and Schwarz orders the bodyguards to seize everyone, but never to let the young lady get hurt.
4. Medium Rare, and the Silver-Haired Sniper

That's when an old man cuts off the pursuit. "Doctor, go on ahead. I'll take care of things here." When the two of them reach the beach completely out of breath and the bodyguards catch up again, this time a blast of flame comes flying in from somewhere.

blocks.cap: The main road from City Hall to the beach. The Doctor and Ceylon's escape route.

blocks.x: "Who dares try to deal with the Doctor?!" It was Ifrit. When the Doctor asks her not to go too far, her compromise is "Fine, I'll make 'em medium rare!" and the bodyguards retreat clutching their singed hair and backsides.
But when Ceylon thanks her politely, Ifrit gets all flustered, says she was in the middle of grilling meat, and runs right off.

Meanwhile, out on the street, that old man, Rhodes Island's veteran **Hellagur**, was taking on Schwarz. Recognizing that this crossbow-wielding Feline was in a different league from the other bodyguards, Hellagur broke through head-on and got away.
