Back at the lodgings, Hellagur says he has someone in mind. A Feline woman from Columbia, silver hair, golden eyes, black crossbow. An assassin and mercenary said to have brought down a powerful family, and to have spent a month in the mountains picking off a band of outlaw patrolmen who raided the frontier, one by one.

That assassin has been missing for years, so it wouldn't be strange if she were now the mayor's assassin. The moment Hellagur says so: crash. Ceylon, who'd been about to pour them water, had heard it.

Ceylon admits that six years ago Schwarz left Victoria, saying it was her father's orders, yet insists she couldn't possibly be an assassin. Hellagur only replies that even the person you trust most isn't guaranteed to be hiding nothing.
5. Was Everything I Had Fake?
Hellagur draws a line: if City Hall is complicit in hiding the volcano data, it isn't Rhodes Island's place to step in. Ceylon goes out to clear her head, and the Doctor stays by her side.

Walking along the seaside street, Ceylon talks about her childhood. Building sandcastles alone back when this beach was still quiet. A father, always away building up the city, who felt less like a parent than a stranger living under the same roof.
And always beside her was Schwarz. The one who would warn her it was dangerous outside, yet in the end would come along anyway: "Please, never leave my sight."

blocks.cap: The street Ceylon and the Doctor walked together.

blocks.x: One day, Schwarz told her she had contracted Oripathy and asked to be called only when needed. Hearing that it was an incurable disease, one that doesn't hurt but kills you, young Ceylon cried out, "I'll beat Oripathy myself!"
That was why Ceylon studied Originium. Her studies in Victoria were so hard she wanted to give up again and again, and it was because of Schwarz that she held on.
Doctor, was everything I have... fake, all along?

When she asks whether she should give up, the Doctor reminds her that she, too, is a scholar of Originium. No one knows whether Oripathy can be beaten, or whether this calamity will ever end, but what she has accomplished was never in vain, so she should trust her own choice.

"You really are my senior, after all." Resolving to save this city even if no one stands with her, Ceylon lays out a plan: take over the broadcasting station next to Garrison Amusement Park and tell the whole city about the volcano.
6. The Young Lady Is the Bait, the Delivery Is a Kick

Before the operation, Hellagur asks the Doctor who will take responsibility if Rhodes Island gets involved. "If no one saw it, then Rhodes Island's involvement never happened, right?" The old soldier laughs that he's no match for the Doctor.
Then comes the day of the festival's biggest party, at Garrison Amusement Park. Schwarz, expecting Ceylon to show up at the broadcasting station, was already there waiting.

blocks.cap: The live stage at Garrison Amusement Park, where Ceylon waited alone for Schwarz.

blocks.x: Schwarz says that spreading the news would throw both the festival and the city into chaos, and that even the master's wrongdoings were all for the city's sake. When Ceylon asks her to treat her like a friend again, the way she used to, the answer is: "I am simply a servant of the Doykos family."

But Schwarz soon realizes: if the young lady is alone and not the least bit anxious, her real goal isn't the station but keeping Schwarz pinned down. Ceylon readily admits that Rhodes Island should be arriving at City Hall right about now.

At that very moment, outside City Hall, a cheerful "Delivery!" is answered with "Get lost," and the front door goes flying off entirely, with **Vigna** behind it reciting the line she's always wanted to say: "Open up! Delivery!"

Back at the amusement park, when Ceylon brings up the volcano, Schwarz's expression changes. What Cronin had told her was an entirely different story: that the young lady meant to expose all of the master's past secrets and drag him from office.
Ceylon replies that if that were her reason, she'd have gone through legal channels. She's doing this for her hometown. Schwarz only says, "You've grown, milady."
7. That's What Friends Are

"Why are you pushing me away?" Schwarz answers that a young lady who received a fine education in Victoria shouldn't be struggling in this city with the likes of her. She should go somewhere better. Asked whether it's because she has killed people, all Schwarz can say is: please, stop.

Ceylon says she already knows about her past, and that she's sorry. Then, for the first time, she raises her voice. She is no hothouse flower, no naive young lady who knows nothing of the world, and protecting Siesta isn't her father's job alone, or Schwarz's.
Thinking that keeping her shut away is for her own good is wrong, she says, and she doesn't care one bit about Schwarz's past. If Schwarz ever needs help, she will be right there beside her.
That's what friends are, isn't it? If only one side keeps giving, that's not friendship!
Asked whether they can be friends again, like when they were little, Schwarz apologizes for the misunderstanding her words and actions caused.
Milady, you are my friend. Always.

Ceylon confesses that she wants to publish her report officially, but she's actually a little scared, since the festival may be canceled and people may have to evacuate. "Milady, do you need my protection?" "Yes. Can I ask you for it?"

When Cronin's men ask whether she's defying orders, Schwarz reveals that cooperating with Cronin was only a cover. She had received two orders. One was the master's: to gather evidence that Cronin had secretly controlled V3 Industries and mined Obsidian. The other was the young lady's 'protect me,' just now.

The bodyguards go down in an instant, and Ceylon, marveling at how cool that was, corrects one thing. What she said just now wasn't an order but a request from a friend, so Schwarz can drop the formal speech. "I... All right."
8. The Mayor Who Was Away on Business

Meanwhile at City Hall, Vigna had taken down the bodyguards and the Doctor had found Cronin's ledgers and bonds. In a panic, Cronin jumped out the window, only to find Hellagur, Ceylon, and Schwarz waiting below.

"Last time, it was the Doctor and Miss Ceylon who jumped out of that window. This time, it's the honorable Catastrophe Messenger himself." Around then, on the main stage, an eighteen-hour nonstop joint concert was kicking off.

blocks.cap: The main stage of the joint concert. The showdown was settled right alongside the festival's roar.

blocks.x: The moment the cornered Cronin shouts that he knows what Herman has done, Herman, who was supposed to be away on business, appears. When rumors spread that banned Obsidian kept turning up on the market and that the Infected were being mistreated, he had pretended to leave the city and had Schwarz dig up the truth.

The secretly mined Obsidian had been flowing into an abandoned City Hall warehouse, yet Cronin only blusters, bringing up the Baru family, the TV tower collapse, and the absorption of the Tarak Tribe, and shouting that it was Herman who taught him results are all that matter.

"After all the trouble it took to scrape together a profit from Obsidian, you want it spent on patients who can't even be cured?" Better to let the volcano blow, keep the assets safe, and rebuild, he says. Herman, who says he has never gambled with Siesta, delivers a short verdict: "Cronin, you're fired."
Around then, Skyfire, surveying the volcano, was so lost in thought she didn't notice her hair getting singed, muttering that there might be a way after all.

Backed by a crowd of his men, Cronin spills it all. The observatory's data was wrong, the volcano is about to fully awaken, and he'll come back after the disaster to mine again. He cries that he can't forget the days he sheltered from the rain in a trash bin, and that he despises Herman's hypocrisy in spending that money on the Infected.
After even those men go down, the ground shakes. It's the small quake that comes before an eruption.

blocks.cap: "Turn into ashes along with this city!"

blocks.x: Cronin laughs that every emergency evacuation route is in his hands, so no one can escape. Just then, a call comes in from Eyjafjalla. The analysis is done, and with this method, the eruption can be delayed.

Ceylon volunteers to go to the volcano. To Schwarz, who tells her to leave it to someone else, she says "This is our mission," and Herman, saying "Let's trust her," sets out with Schwarz and Hellagur to evacuate the citizens.
9. Master of the Volcano
Meanwhile, on the far side of the volcano: a cave that has become a deep mine shaft because people dug out too much Obsidian.

Here's the conclusion Skyfire reached with Eyjafjalla. This volcano is home to 'lava Originium Slugs' that feed on Obsidian, and people have been following their traces to mine it. As overmining wrecked their habitat, the Slugs began expanding into new nests, and that is what caused the abnormal volcanic activity.
'If we don't treat the gifts of nature with reverence, nature will surely punish us'... That's the gist of it.
Calm the master that leads the swarm, and the eruption can be stopped. So they head down into the depths of the cave, where, with a roar that shakes the entire rock wall, it shows itself.

blocks.cap: "...Can you even call that a bug? It's basically a walking volcano!"

blocks.x: If that massive body were to burst open here, it would be a volcanic eruption, plain and simple. The three decide to drive it back into its original burrow and aim for weak spots through the cracks in the lava. While Ceylon holds off the swarming Slugs, Skyfire's and Provence's attacks land, and the giant Originium Slug retreats the way it came.

After saying it should be safe for a while, Provence starts to say something and swallows it. "But... this place... sooner or later..." Skyfire answers that she knows, but the city's choice must be respected.
10. A Paradise Built for Her

The beach, after the commotion. Amiya, who'd been giving everyone a firm talking-to for getting hurt, shushes the Doctor when they try to explain. This time, they'll just call it 'getting into a fight with other fans at a concert.'

Then Herman asks the Doctor to walk with him for a while. Cronin was someone he had raised himself. He had as much ability as ambition, so Herman overlooked his petty tricks, but once Cronin strayed from the path, Herman had no choice but to put Schwarz on him as a test.

He walks this beach because his wife, Barbara, sleeps in this sea. On a day with a beautiful sunset, she had said she wanted to stay here together forever. Left alone in the blink of an eye, he tells the Doctor to turn around and look.
Do you understand? This city is a paradise I built for her.
Herman calls the Doctor the same kind of person as himself. Some things can't be solved by good means. Good and evil lost their meaning long ago. All that remains are results, and this city.
Asked why he doesn't tell Ceylon, he says he isn't looking to be understood. Schwarz hopes Ceylon will never understand, and he himself lost the chance to choose long ago.

According to the new observation data, Siesta will one day sink beneath the lava. Herman plans to make the development district he has long labored over into a new nomadic city, and to move the city once this festival is over. And Ceylon, who wants to go to Rhodes Island, he will send off with Schwarz at her side. After all, Siesta is no longer her paradise.
That as long as the people of Siesta exist, Siesta will exist forever. That young people like them are the true 'Siesta.'
Left behind, Schwarz admits she had originally meant to teach the Doctor a lesson, yet thanks them all the same: without the Doctor, everything she held dear would have been buried by this volcano.

Just then, Ceylon comes running with an announcement. She's sending her résumé to Rhodes Island, she already has her father's permission, and Schwarz is coming with her. "...Understood. As you wish, milady."

And then, on the bridge of Rhodes Island. When Ceylon shouts that the experiment is about to start and that Schwarz should just carry the Doctor over, Schwarz politely asks the Doctor to walk there on their own, since that would hardly be a pretty sight.

blocks.cap: "Milady, we'll be there shortly."

blocks.x: Epilogue. A Sea That Isn't the Sea

**Thorns** was at the same festival too, in another corner of it. When **Elysium**, back on the ship, called to beg for an autograph from the band **Alive Until Sunset** and turned a three-line summary into four lines, the reply he got was "That's 25% over."

Thorns didn't follow Vigna when she wanted to go help the Doctor. Instead, he delivered an entire gang of pickpockets to the police station, and told **Cutter**, who was beating herself up over ruining the barbecue, that if she fails once, try twice, and if she fails twice, try three times.

Then, at the water's edge at dusk, Thorns runs into **Aya**, a member of that band. When she tells him this isn't the sea, Thorns flatly says she isn't his kind, and admits that his only home is Iberia, and that what he feels toward the sea is fear.
Then something was standing on the water. It spoke. "Æ... gir."
As Thorns struggles to breathe, Aya whispers in Ægirian that nothing on this land can rob him of his breath. Thorns chose to stay instead of running. Because he wanted to kill it.
I don't plan to die. There's a friend who wants your autograph, and I have to stay alive to bring it back.

And in Rhodes Island's infirmary: Alty, the same band's bassist, walks in without even being on the visitor list and asks Kal'tsit whether she doesn't already know what Alty really is. Mon3tr very nearly lunges out.

blocks.cap: Rhodes Island's infirmary. An uninvited guest has come calling.

blocks.x: AMa-10, Dr. Kal'tsit, tell me... those special Ægirians... how exactly were they born?

A sea that is strictly speaking just a lake, a volcano once called a friend, a paradise one man built for his wife. Siesta may one day sink beneath the lava, but as long as there are people of Siesta, Siesta will never disappear.

1stact.tagline: The story of a short Mounted Police officer who comes to rescue a mountain village turned bounty hunters' den, gets a blade pointed at her by her own colleague, teams up with an Infected hunter only to end up facing him, and finally opens the treasure chest with her own blood. Things worth more than gold coins that vanish once they're spent.

chars.name: Grani
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator and former member of the Victorian Mounted Police. Fights with a spear.

chars.name: Carol
chars.desc: Chief of Dewville. Only half a year into the job, she let the hunters capture her to protect her village.

chars.name: Big Bob
chars.desc: A well-built bounty hunter. Skilled at fieldcraft and disarming traps.

chars.name: Skadi
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island operator and a renowned bounty hunter. She is after the chief of Dewville.

chars.name: Captain
chars.desc: Leader of the bounty hunter band running roughshod over Dewville. Relentlessly pursues Grani and her companions.

chars.name: Specter
chars.desc: An operator confined to a Rhodes Island sickroom. Tormented by the same nightmare over and over.

chars.name: Nearl
chars.desc: The Rhodes Island operator who used to tell Grani stories about the knights of Kazimierz.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: One of Rhodes Island's leaders. Her rule for any deal is equivalent exchange.

chars.name: Mudrock
chars.desc: The one Big Bob writes to from Columbia.

terms.name: Dewville
terms.desc: A small village in the mountains on Kazimierz's border. Its people have lived self-sufficiently there for generations.

terms.name: Walking Catastrophe
terms.desc: The nickname bounty hunters use for a woman they dread. Rumor has it she once wiped an entire village off the map.

terms.name: Knight's Treasure
terms.desc: The riches an ancient knight of Kazimierz is said to have been buried with, along with his legacy. A legend passed around among bounty hunters.

terms.name: Key to the Treasure
terms.desc: The key to the treasure chest, handed down through the generations to the village chiefs alone.

terms.name: Mt. Mortica
terms.desc: A mountain in the Dewville area, named after a knight who died long ago.

terms.name: Abyssal Hunters
terms.desc: A band of Ægir warriors.

blocks.x: A small mountain village on the Kazimierz border: **Dewville**. Its people had lived self-sufficiently for generations, until a rumor that an old knight's treasure lay buried in the mountains turned the place into a den of bounty hunters.

The village chief, who had stepped forward claiming to know where the treasure was, had been left hanging under the scorching sun for over a day. Just as she was muttering 'I'll never tell' yet again, an unfamiliar voice cut in. 'Never thought I'd come all the way to Kazimierz just to find thugs running wild like this.'

blocks.cap: Cracked earth, a beating sun, and a ring of shadows. The orders were clear: not a single sip of water.

blocks.x: The voice's owner knocks the hunters flat in no time and pulls the chief away by the hand. 'Don't be afraid. Nobody's going to hurt you anymore.'
1. Not a Knight but Mounted Police, and a Girl, Thank You
The rescued girl, **Carol**, hides out at the house of a villager, Uncle Luke, and finally catches her breath. But when the villagers call her rescuer 'Miss Knight,' Carol's eyes go wide. 'M-Miss??'

'Ugh, yes! I'm a girl!' The short, spear-wielding rescuer, **Grani**, wasn't a knight of Kazimierz either. She was Victorian Mounted Police, so no taxes and no fees required, she says. And her ancestors were Kuranta who had crossed from Kazimierz into Victoria.

Part of why she took the request was that she wanted to see her parents' homeland, but once she arrived, things were worse than she'd thought. The knights in the capital couldn't care less about a remote border village, and Carol confesses she'd assumed their request for help had sunk to the bottom of the sea.

blocks.cap: "We've had to leave the village for a while to escape Catastrophes before, but this is still our home."

blocks.x: It all started a month ago, when a bounty hunter dug a knight's coffin and a chest of gold coins out of the mountains. And the gold coins Grani had collected as a 'settlement' from a hunter who picked a fight with her the moment she arrived? Those were the very same coins.

blocks.cap: Gold coins stamped with the crest of Kazimierz. That glitter is what lured the border's hunters in.

blocks.x: Among the hunters, a legend went around that the knights of old Kazimierz lie buried in their home soil even in death, guarding the land. And it always came with this line.
Only the bloodline of Kazimierz, which fears no danger and heeds no sacrifice, can overcome every obstacle.

Eventually, a rumor spread that someone in Dewville knew where the **Knight's Treasure** was, and the hunters started turning the village upside down again. As the two slip away, Uncle Luke asks Grani to take good care of the chief, and Grani freezes. 'Ch-chief?!'
She'd only had the job for half a year, Carol said with a shy smile, but even she had her pride as chief.
2. A Promise Made in the Attic

The place the two squeeze into is a pitch-dark, cramped attic. When both of them somehow fit into a gap that didn't look big enough for two, Grani yelps that their faces are way too close, and while she's at it, settles what Carol should call her. Not 'Officer.' Just Grani is fine.

blocks.cap: In a village whose mill and granary had both been wrecked, a spot beyond the hunters' eyes.

blocks.x: The **Key to the Treasure** and the treasure's location were secrets passed down only to the village chiefs. When Carol apologizes that she can't tell her yet, Grani says she can tell her once she trusts her completely.

After the hunters ruined the fields and even took the winter stores, Carol had stepped forward claiming to know about the treasure so the villagers wouldn't get hurt any further. She knew it was only a stopgap, but she adds: 'But then you came.'
What Carol really wanted was to drive the hunters out and bring peace back to the village. The treasure was just a means of hiring people to do it.
Even if we get our hands on gold coins, they'll be spent and gone someday. But we have to keep on living here, in our home.
When they try to check outside, the window is too high, so Grani hoists Carol up, and Carol, peering out, starts flailing. 'S-someone just went flying past the window...'
3. Hiding from a Monster, Right Next to the Enemy

Meanwhile, out on the village road, the hunters were scattering in a panic. The '**Walking Catastrophe**' they'd only ever heard about in rumors had sent their boss, the one they call '**Captain**,' flying into the river with a single blow.

blocks.cap: "All that standeth before me shall perish." Not that any of the hunters understood it, since it was in Ægirian.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, Grani, who'd caught sight of the woman through the window, freezes. She looks an awful lot like a fellow Rhodes Island operator, but Grani was sure she'd fought hard to land this mission all by herself.

She hurries down the stairs and flings the door open, smacking a hunter lying right outside it square in the nose. But instead of getting angry, the hunters go 'Shh!' and hold their breath. The Walking Catastrophe was passing by.

Caught up in the moment, Grani ends up crouched among the hunters, holding her breath right along with them, and when they say the Walking Catastrophe wiped out an entire village, she even shoots back, 'Now that's an exaggeration!'
Once the monster has passed, one relieved hunter glances to the side and nearly jumps out of his skin. 'The spear brat! And the chief's here too!'

Under Carol's narrowed eyes ('Grani, did you do that on purpose...?'), Grani protests that they talked to her so naturally that she just answered. Threatened with being torn to shreds, she fires back, 'With that broken sword?' In the end, the hunters even call in the swarm of bugs that had wrecked the rice paddies.
4. An Offer from a Well-Built Bounty Hunter

Surrounded by a swarm of sticky bugs, they hear a shout of 'Cover your ears!' and a stun grenade goes off. Following the man, who'd rather be called 'well-built' than 'fatty,' the three flee to a grove outside the village that only Carol and her childhood friend know about.

blocks.cap: A grove far from the village. Only Carol and her childhood friend know this place.

blocks.x: The man sets his chainsaw, ammo, and explosives down on the ground and proposes they join hands. Whoever claims the treasure, the hunters will fight over it and the village will be razed to bare earth, so he'll handle guiding, code-breaking, spotting traps, and the fighting too. The name he goes by: **Big Bob**.

Carol couldn't trust a hunter she'd only just met, but Grani's 'colleague' wasn't exactly sociable and was actually a bounty hunter herself, so leaning on her right now wasn't an option either. In the end, Carol came up with a plan to give out the treasure's location a little at a time, direction only, and Grani made a promise: 'Carol, I guarantee your safety!'

When Big Bob offers to guide them along a safe route through the hunter-infested northern forest, Grani makes it clear they have conditions too, and gets a seasoned reply. 'Fine. First, let's settle how the treasure gets split.'

Meanwhile, the Captain, fished out of the river, snaps at an underling offering him water that he's not thirsty, then grinds his teeth, counting on the traps laid in the forest. 'Take the treasure, take her head, take it all!'
5. In the Forest of Traps, a Colleague Draws Her Blade

Out in the northern forest, Big Bob reads the hunters' codes carved into the rocks and points out trap after trap: a bear trap, a hammer behind a tree, even a spike pit one step in front of Carol. When Grani marvels at him, he starts, 'I used to...' and trails off.

blocks.cap: Step only in Big Bob's footprints, and never, ever touch anything.

blocks.x: Then Big Bob stops in front of an unfamiliar code written in blood. '...Monster?' Grani knows at once who that monster is. 'Skadi... it's Skadi, right?'
But **Skadi**'s answer was cold. She ordered them to hand over the chief at once, then swung her blade at Grani. A 'warning,' she called it.

Just as the three are cornered by red eyes that chase them without so much as a ragged breath, the Captain's gang springs its ambush and opens fire on Skadi all at once. Before she knows it, Grani has thrown herself in front of her. 'I don't know why you're chasing us, but you're still my colleague!'

Slipping away in the chaos and taking down the hunters who followed, Grani spots Originium crystals sprouting from the wound on Big Bob's leg. He bellows, asking if she wants to get infected, but she bandages him anyway, saying saving the Infected is Rhodes Island's job. Only then does Carol learn that Grani is a Rhodes Island operator.

Asked whether she isn't scared, Grani says plenty of her colleagues are Infected too, but you can't really tell by looking. You only find out at bath time. Big Bob chuckles. 'Thanks, kid. You don't discriminate.'
6. Something Worth More Than This Little Gold Coin

After that, the three slip into a mine tunnel through the mountain. On the other side lies **Mt. Mortica**, with hardly any hunters around, and since the mountain was named after a knight who died long ago, Big Bob figured that's where the treasure would be.

blocks.cap: A tunnel straight through the mountain. Get past it, he said, and the hunters would be left behind.

blocks.x: Big Bob, who said he'd always laughed off the rumor that Skadi brought down a mountain, now reckoned that woman could take out every hunter on her own, and flatten a few villages along with them. When Grani said Skadi probably wasn't here for the treasure, his voice turned sharp. Rhodes Island raises a 'Walking Catastrophe' like that and calls itself an organization for the Infected? What has Rhodes Island ever done for the Infected?
Hmph, what's Rhodes Island to me? In this world, there's nothing worth more than this little gold coin!

Grani didn't make excuses. She apologized. She'd met many Infected but couldn't save them all, because neither she nor Rhodes Island was strong enough. But even knowing that, she said, she couldn't abandon an innocent Infected person suffering right in front of her.

Asked whether she trusts that 'colleague' who even pointed a blade at her, Grani answers that if Rhodes Island took her in, there must be a reason, and Big Bob says he went too far and tells her to forget it. When he says his injured leg will make him a burden, Grani shoots back that the only way he'd ever hold them back is by refusing to hand over the treasure at the end, and Big Bob laughs out loud.
Carol apologizes too, admitting she'd been scared because it was her first time seeing an Infected, and promises to pay him what he's due.
7. One Who Says 'Go On Ahead,' One Who Needs Time

But at the tunnel exit, the Captain lies collapsed, mumbling 'In...fected...', with masked Reunion members standing over him. Ignoring Grani's attempt to stop him, Big Bob charges in first and shouts that with his bad leg he can't move fast, so take Carol and go on ahead.
'All right, then promise me. I'll save your share, so you'd better make it back safe.' Big Bob chuckles and plants himself in front of Reunion.
As they make their way out of the forest, Carol worries about Big Bob, and Grani gives a curious answer. 'He probably just needs a little time.'
Only then did Carol reveal the last stretch of the route. The treasure rested in the second cave halfway up Mt. Mortica, at its very deepest point, past the forks and hidden passages.

When explosions and screams echo from the distance, Grani asks if she's scared. Carol says she's terrified, but to protect the peace of her home, she has to do her part too. Grani murmurs softly, '...You're strong, Carol.'
8. Whether You Can and Whether You Will Are Two Different Things

Soon they reach the cave, and Grani tells Carol, who knows the way, to go in alone and bring out the treasure while she stays at the entrance. Carol clings to her, saying she doesn't want to lose her and there's no need to risk her life in a place like this, but Grani says there's no such thing as a cause you mustn't risk your life for, and recites a verse.
Even if the barbarian's cruel blade pierces the heart, the spear of the royal cavalry shall not fall to the ground.

Aren't you fighting your own fight too, knowing full well it's dangerous? Grani said that when she saved Carol in the square, she'd made up her mind not to let anyone take so much as a single hair of hers. 'You're still just a little kid...' 'I'm not a kid! I'm just a bit short!' Carol laughed and went into the cave.

While the hunters and masked Reunion clash to the south, the hunters heading for the cave are stopped at the entrance by a small spearwoman. And behind them, Skadi walks up. 'I'm in a very bad mood right now.'
As Grani, now covered in blood, holds the hunters off, the ground shakes. Skadi has smashed through thick bedrock and punched a hole in the mountain.

Skadi presses her: where's the girl, and is she trying to sabotage Rhodes Island's mission? Grani pushes back. How can she attack a colleague without even saying what the mission is? Skadi asks in return, 'Who said I'm your colleague?'
She only blocked a light swing of the sword, yet it felt like her arm would snap. Even when asked whether strength like that could protect the girl, Grani didn't back down.
Whether I can or can't has nothing to do with whether I will or won't!

At that moment the hunters rush Skadi, and Grani vaults over their heads and dashes into the cave, leaving a parting line: tell me what the mission is and I'll think about telling you where Carol is, so cool your head down there for a while.
9. Blades Pointed Three Ways
Inside the cave, a maze of forks, lay fallen hunters and a hole that looked as if it had been blasted open. Yet Skadi could not have entered yet.

blocks.cap: The 'tomb hole' Carol spoke of. The treasure rests at its deepest point.

blocks.x: 'So you've decided what you're going to do.' At Grani's words, Big Bob answered from the dark. 'I thought I'd played my part well.'

Big Bob and his comrades had become Infected years ago and believed Reunion would change their lives. But there was still no shop that would sell them bread, no inn that would let them rest their feet. He left Reunion with his comrades, who were like brothers to him, and drifted until he heard the rumor of this treasure. With it, they could reach Columbia, a distant land where even the Infected can have villages and fields of their own.
Then Skadi entered, cutting down the masked group at Big Bob's side. She had no interest in what anyone was thinking. All of them were to get out of her sight at once.

blocks.cap: One side wants the treasure, one wants the chief, and one can hand over neither.

blocks.x: Grani asked what would become of Dewville if they took all the treasure. Big Bob said the village would get by somehow, but his people had no other road left; she, who did not discriminate against the Infected, should understand. Then he asked where Carol was. Grani shook her head. Having accepted the request, her only task was to deliver the treasure to Carol and bring peace back to the village.
All we want is to live, with this treasure to sustain us!

Big Bob proposed they take Skadi down together first. Just as Grani shouted that if they fought here there would be no turning back, Carol appeared, dragging the treasure chest. The moment Carol saw Big Bob and brightened, an explosive came flying in. It was Skadi who shielded her.
The explosive had no real force behind it. Big Bob said that with this, his debt to the girl was paid, and next time he would use the real thing.

Only then was Grani certain. Had Skadi been after the treasure, she would have seized it and fled in that moment. Skadi admitted she wanted not the treasure but a single object Carol carried, and that this target mattered so much to her that she had not wanted to drag anyone else into it.
Helping a fellow operator is only natural, Grani said, and tightened her grip on her spear. 'Big Bob, I'm sorry. This might hurt a little!'
10. The Key That Drinks Blood
As Big Bob bled, his comrades insisted they could still fight, but he stopped them. They fought to live; there was no reason to die fighting. 'I was weak. Let's give it up.'

Skadi held out her hand to Carol, who stood before the chest, and told her to hand over the key. The moment she opened the chest with it, she would die. The key tears open the user's hand and drinks their blood, and if the blood is not Kuranta, it simply shatters.

Taught by her father that guarding the key handed down for generations was a chief's most important duty, Carol would not give it up. She recalled the legend's words once more: only the bloodline of Kazimierz that heeds no sacrifice can clear away every obstacle. She was ready to pay the price, she said. She would open it herself.
'Grani, if anything happens to me, give the money from this treasure to everyone in the village!' Then she added quietly, 'I'm sorry, Father...'

Grani stopped her hand. From two things, that the key was smaller than expected and that Skadi had said it took more than an ordinary person could bear, Grani drew one conclusion: there was a limit to how much blood it could take.
Carol. I'll open the treasure chest.

The descendant of Kuranta who had crossed from Kazimierz into Victoria took the key. With Carol crying out for her to stop, Grani left Skadi just one line. 'Skadi, if I collapse, make sure you catch me.'
A short groan escaped her, and Carol cried out Grani's name.
11. A Few Days Later, a Big Cleanup for Two

A few days later, in front of a bounty hunter camp, as the Captain gathered his men, Skadi grumbled about why she had to help clean up the hunters. Grani told her she'd gotten the key she wanted, so she should do her job properly. Asked why she was risking her life again when she had only just survived, Grani answered simply. 'You're here too, aren't you?'

blocks.cap: "Let's finish this quickly. I need to get back to Rhodes Island."

blocks.x: Outside the village, Big Bob bowed his head, saying he had been no help in the end. Carol told him the villagers were afraid of the Infected too, so this could stay between them. Sincerely grateful for the two girls' decision, Big Bob tossed a gold coin to the departing Grani, and she smiled and said she would keep it as a memento.

Months later, Big Bob wrote a letter to **Mudrock** from the Columbian frontier. After the village was repaired, the girls had given them the rest of the treasure, and thanks to that his brothers had found a home to rest in. They were living self-sufficiently and even thinking of trying to grow hops.
Being Infected still comes with some inconvenience, but life under the sun is many times more beautiful than I ever imagined.

The letter closed by saying that Reunion is not the only place the Infected can call home, and that he hoped they would meet again in Columbia. Someone who read it replied briefly. 'That's good to hear.'
Epilogue. A Letter Never Sent, a Letter Folded and Flown

Meanwhile, while Grani was away on her mission, **Nearl** was writing her a long letter at Rhodes Island. Knights of Kazimierz were buried in mausoleums with their legacies, and inside there might be not only gold and jewels, but weapons the knights had researched, secrets they had guarded all their lives, or something even more dangerous. But it was too long and too dark, so Nearl decided to write only what truly needed saying, so as not to put pressure on the girl.

On the day Grani left Dewville, Carol, telling her to come visit at harvest time, handed her a letter that had arrived at the village. It was Nearl's short note: Skadi had headed to Dewville without permission and without a mission, so be careful if you run into her.
'Honestly, I'd already figured that out...' Grani folded the letter into a paper airplane. Rhodes Island paper is good quality, so it flies a long way.

blocks.cap: Dewville, with the hunters gone. The start of a new life.

blocks.x: Before all this, Skadi had stopped by a sickroom at Rhodes Island before setting out. **Specter**, tormented by nightmares of being dragged to the bottom of the deep sea, could not recall her name, but she recognized the scent of deep-sea blood that clung to her.
A scent I long for, and loathe.

blocks.cap: A sickroom no one may enter without Kal'tsit's permission.

blocks.x: Soon there would be a way to end the pain, Skadi said, and it was fine if Specter went on forgetting her as she did now. Then Skadi left, for a very, very distant place where a secret lay sleeping.
When Skadi returned, what she set before **Kal'tsit** was a 'stone' already infused with blood. Grani's blood.

blocks.cap: "You wanted this, right? Take it."

blocks.x: Kal'tsit knew that Skadi had lied about having a mission and clashed with another operator, and that the girl was keeping that secret for her even after coming back. What Skadi wanted in return was information: the source of the Originium nerve agent used on Specter.

Asked how she knew, Kal'tsit answered in Ægirian. '**Abyssal Hunters** are bound by blood.' Kal'tsit offered to help if Skadi obeyed her orders absolutely. Skadi said she only trusts those who can be trusted, and Kal'tsit answered that she, too, always keeps her word.

Instead of gold coins that vanish once spent, Dewville kept a home its people can go on living in, and Big Bob's brothers found a home under the sun. And the bloodline of Kazimierz that feared no danger and heeded no sacrifice turned out to be not a knight, but a short Mounted Police officer.

act51side.tagline: Students who surrounded a ballroom to save one comrade are thrown into an abandoned industrial district in the heart of the capital, and become an army of their own. Behind those walls, too, was an emperor who had hidden his name.

blocks.x: Deity Grypherburg, capital of Ursus. In midwinter, the State Council holds a hearing on the 'Katorga Incident.'

One noble delivers his verdict before it even begins. The students took up arms and broke through the walls of the quarantine zone, and their leader, 'General Zima' Sonya Mikhailivna, is a heinous traitor.

blocks.cap: Zoya on the witness stand. The gallery behind her had already split in two.

blocks.x: The first witness is **Absinthe** (Zoya), daughter of a police officer who died on duty in Chernobog. Before her testimony even begins, the nobles climb over their seats and come to blows.
As Zoya closes her eyes, the kind of shouting every Ursan has heard far too often piles up in her ears. It was the same at the Student Assembly.
1. Those Who Raised Their Hands

The Student Assembly, in her memory. The gathering of Deity Grypherburg's student groups had one item on its agenda: rescuing Rania, a student seized after speaking out on behalf of the miners of the Far North.

The meeting hall was a brawl. Faddey's 'Vanguards,' who called for force, and Leonid's 'Symposium,' who put theory first, had each other by the collar. The voice of **Olga**, president of the Petrachevsky Group and chair of the meeting, was lost in the shouting.
The uproar stopped when one person walked in: the leader of the Student Self-Government Group from Chernobog, 'General Zima.' **Zima** (Sonya).

The USSG had returned to Ursus on a mission to set up a Rhodes Island office. With her were her strategist **Istina** (Anna), **Rosa** (Natalya), heiress of a fallen house of counts, **Leto** (Rosalind), who loved a fight, and the youngest, **Gummy** (Lada).
When Zima blocked Faddey's plan to storm the prison, calling it suicide, Olga offered a compromise. On the day of the Winter Ball, they would surround the ballroom with no weapons, only placards.
At the vote, hands went up one by one. Hands shaking with anger. Hands relieved that no one had to carry a blade. Hands that rose only as high as the ear, for fear of being pushed out of the crowd.

blocks.cap: An overwhelming majority voted in favor. The USSG, which had opposed it, was told to prove its loyalty.

blocks.x: Zima chose to take part, on one condition: any student who did not want to join had to be free to stay out without penalty.
And on the winter-night street on the way back, Zima asked: why did we come back to Ursus?
Istina answered with a question. **Had they ever truly left Chernobog at all?**
2. The Ballroom Goes Dark
On the day of the ball, Rosa entered the palace as heiress of the House of Rostov, while the others listened in from outside through a bug made by **Botani**, the student in charge of communications.
**Countess Vorontsova**, an old friend of her mother's, taught Rosa the rules of society. Conversation here was not for stating opinions. It was for blending into the crowd.

The man who spilled his drink on Rosa's skirt was **Pavlovich**, the Magistrate in charge of Katorga Raion. Chairman **Witte** and the vice chairman arrived, but the Emperor did not. Then the windows lit up.

blocks.cap: Torches and slogans surrounded the ballroom. Someone began shouting for the Emperor's overthrow.

blocks.x: Back in the hearing room, the arbiter presses Zoya. Didn't she know that night that the Emperor had vanished, and keep it hidden?

The same day, Witte confides in the vice chairman about that night. When a bomb scare broke out just before the ball, he sent a guard to lead the Emperor to safety through an underground passage. The Emperor refused the escort of that guard, one of the **Emperor's Blade**, and the guard did not stop him.

blocks.cap: 'To take His Majesty outside, and let him see the Ursus beyond the window with his own eyes.'

blocks.x: It was what the Emperor himself had wanted. He vanished before the guard's eyes.
That night on the street, Zima warned of danger, but Olga was elated. When the lights went out and tear gas fell, military police marched in with batons.
Gummy saw her father's watch on a policeman's wrist and froze where she stood. Zima knocked down the officer about to strike Gummy, and took the rain of batons on her back.

blocks.cap: To Istina, reaching out her hand: 'This isn't an order from your leader. I'm asking you as a friend.'

blocks.x: So Zoya concludes her testimony. However you look at it, Sonya is closer to a victim.
3. The Nameless Child
The second witness is the vagrant **Ukusik**. The committee's papers state that the person who protected her died at the hands of the Student Self-Government Group.
Her mother died because there was no money for medicine. Her father abandoned her. On a pipe-cleaning crew, she watched children her own age suffocate inside the energy pipes.
Then, in a police station cell, she met **Antosha**. He had come with an Originium bomb to break out a fellow student, and he took along the child who said her home was the sewer.
In the Katorga Raion workshop she followed him to, a young man gave a name to the child with the sharp, rapid tongue. Ukusik. It was **Matvey**, who stood at Antosha's side.
For the first time, she had a place she would not be driven out of. Its name was the Unbound.

blocks.cap: The Unbound's house, built by Matvey's own hands.

blocks.x: Before his comrades, Antosha said every peaceful means had failed, and that their teacher had given his life for the 'peace' they had chosen.
What we long for is... freedom. What we want is... destruction.
Watching Antosha glance at the silent Matvey throughout the speech, Ukusik understood. If Antosha ever went wrong, Matvey would be the one to speak.
The Unbound were after Pavlovich, who held Katorga Raion in his grip. But their comrade **Yura**, who had slipped into the ball disguised as a servant, failed in his mission.
4. Noble Children Dumped in a Junkyard
That night, the police chief could neither jail the noble children he had arrested nor let them go. The place he thought of was Katorga Raion.
An industrial district in the heart of the capital, once used for convict labor and then abandoned. Plans were being floated to cast the whole district off into the wasteland.
When the students were carted in, Pavlovich told the thugs he had hired not to lay a hand on the noble guests. That order did not reach those who were not noble.

Two days later, the thugs shoved a sack holding a body in a school uniform through a hole in the wall. Among those watching from hiding were two who had crawled in through the energy pipes: Ukusik, who had come looking for the Unbound, and Leto, who had left nothing but a letter behind to come find Zima.

The two found Antosha alive, contrary to the rumors. When Zima appeared carrying a bloodied weapon, she and Antosha stepped forward at the same moment and clasped hands. Not as comrades, but as allies.

blocks.cap: An abandoned old industrial sector: Katorga Raion.

blocks.x: After they parted, Zima held Leto tight. Asked if she was scared, she denied it. Only after Leto had soothed her did she say it: she wasn't scared anymore.
Antosha's face, meanwhile, had darkened. The Student Assembly badge Zima wore was one he had helped design, back when he was the first leader of the Petrachevsky Group.
After their teacher died, Antosha was denounced and expelled, but students with family connections escaped punishment. The one now leading the group was Olga.
5. The Gray Padded Coat Beneath the Mound

In the meantime, Leonid led a party of students off to bargain over ransom with **Gromov**, boss of the 'Council of Sixteen.' The Symposium students left behind meant to follow, carrying a letter from Naum saying Gromov could be reasoned with.
Zima slapped a student trying to push past. A student who did nothing but write would never have handwriting that shaky, she said, so Naum had likely sold out his comrades' lives.
Here, Zima said, there were no Vanguards or Symposium, no nobles or commoners. To those thugs, they were just meat to be carved up and shared.
The student called 'Pencil Stub' raised his hand first, and Faddey followed. The rescue party saved Nika and Yeremey, who were cornered in an isolated house, but Leonid was already dead.

blocks.cap: The house where Nika and Yeremey held out behind a single table.

blocks.x: While fleeing, the two had struck down from behind a man who was stripping Leonid's clothes. Then the owner of the house came back. A woman looking for her husband.
Out of a mound of earth came a gray padded coat covered in patches. With work gone for two months, the people here had survived by collecting the clothes of those Gromov killed.
The woman threw the gold watch the students offered into Nika's face. Could that piece of metal bring Ivan back? They killed people so easily. Why couldn't they kill the one responsible?
Zima swore that Gromov would not live through this winter.

After everyone had left, Matvey pressed the gold watch back into the woman's hand. His own mother had buried, alone, a husband beaten to death by robbers. Live on, he told her, so that the sacrifice would not be in vain.
6. Cannon and Bonfire
Meanwhile, in the corridor of the adjourned hearing sits Varvara, in a wheelchair. She tells an old friend that no matter how long he stares, her legs will not grow back.

Back in Katorga Raion. The 'Council of Sixteen' had renamed itself the 'Sixteen Warriors.' Thugs claiming to be the sixteen warriors who followed Igor Velikiy had killed Leonid because his family was nowhere in the register of nobility, and they sat on captured students as if they were chairs.
Zima rescued Varvara moments before she was beaten to death and freed dozens of captive students. The moment someone said they were safe, Gromov appeared, dragging a cannon.
The shells fell. Varvara screamed that she could not feel her legs, and Faddey, pouring blood, shouted at Nika to get her out.
Alone now, Faddey felt the last of his strength drain away. So this was what it felt like to accomplish something and become a hero.

blocks.cap: A night of narrow survival. No one around the bonfire spoke of joy.

blocks.x: Antosha told her not to count on hothouse flowers. Pick a few quick ones, take out the two men in charge, and that would be enough. It is always the few who decide the outcome.
Zima shook her head. Look around the bonfire, she said. Everyone there is clenching their fists, whatever their station. **No one deserves to be thrown away.**
The chance to take on the cannon would come from their comrade beyond the wall. Zima was certain of it.
7. The Confession

When the recess ends, the next witness, Natalya Rostova, does not appear, so Zoya reads her written testimony in her place. What Countess Vorontsova had been waiting for was testimony that named specific people, the kind that would protect Natalya.

On the cover of Confession, the book the Countess had lent her, were the words that no ideology is worth trading a happy life for. But the confession Rosa submitted had every name struck out except Pavlovich's.

Right after the ball, acting on behalf of the students' parents, Rosa climbed the walls of Katorga Raion. When the whine of a power drill rang out, Pavlovich laughed. A dentist was removing the rotten part, he said. Teeth or ideas, it was all the same.
He offered a deal. If she moved the parents to block the State Council's resolution to abandon Katorga Raion, he would release the students.
As Rosa waited for Zima in the quarantine zone, a starving beast passed in front of her with a human finger in its mouth. Memories of Chernobog flooded in, and Rosa could not breathe.
Zima came running and told her she was not alone. Once Rosa had her breath back, Zima asked her to cut the supply line bringing weapons in over the walls.
Back in the city, Rosa visited a councilor, who let slip that the Emperor had not returned to the palace after the ball, and that some nobles hoped things would stay that way.
And Rosa called on a duke who had long backed Pavlovich. Having raised the rumor that his heir was tangled up in student activism, she let a single name drop at the very end. Poor Olga.

blocks.cap: Under the noon sun, Rosa waited for the duke's answer with the smile of a young noblewoman.

blocks.x: At that moment, Duke Treplev rises in the gallery. He is the very duke Rosa visited. He only agreed to cut back the arms, he shouts. His daughter Olga was being threatened.
On the day she handed over the confession, Rosa said to the Countess: if the descendants of the heroes who once stood against the Hippogriff's whip now wield that same whip, who would follow them?
If you asked me what right every person ought to have from the moment they're born... I'd say it is 'the right to choose.'
In the hearing room, the Countess says only that she is tired. No lie, however carefully crafted, can stand against facts one has lived through.
8. Istina on Stage
Next, Olga takes the stand. On the night of the ball, the students who fled with Istina to an abandoned theater blamed one another.
Leto grabbed a student mocking Sonya by the collar and left on her own. When those who remained began, one by one, to talk of 'going home,' Gummy spread her arms and blocked the exit.
Istina walked onto the stage. You were the ones who voted yes, she said. You were the ones who shouted the slogans. Then the lights came on.

blocks.cap: For the first time, every eye fell on the strategist who had always stood one step behind.

blocks.x: True failure isn't falling down. It's having the power to resist injustice, yet putting out the spark in your own heart... and bowing your head in servility.
The students rose again. Istina wove an intelligence network through their families and schools, and uncovered that House Treplev was even planning to send reinforcements to Pavlovich.
On the stand, Olga says that Anna locked her in a room. She escaped down a rope of knotted cloth, but was chased up to a window and fell. A pile of turf saved her life.
Asked whether she will accuse Anna Morozova, Olga gives a different name. The one responsible for every action the students took is Olga Danilovna Trepleva.
The arbiter hastily calls a recess. As Olga passes the witness stand, Zoya gives her a slight nod.
That day, the one who caught Olga's arm as she fell from the window was Istina.
Pulling Olga up, Istina told her she had only been running away. **Here, naivety is a sin, and hesitation the greatest accomplice.**
Olga told them about her father's secret passage leading to the mansion's basement. She would protect her own dignity and her family's, she said, in her own way.
9. The 374th Call

Around that time, in the quarantine zone, Zima taught the students the shield formation. Ursus would not protect them, so they had to become each other's fortress. Rosa's maneuvering worked, and the cannon and heavy weapons disappeared.
In the camp was a young man named Fedya, who said he could never speak of his past. He was also the one who had come back carrying the body of a student called 'Shorty.'
On the night of the ball, Emperor **Fyodor** was exhausted. He was worn down by pressure from the nobles, and even the palace could not keep its stoves properly lit this winter.
Slipping out through the underground passage, he was punched in the face trying to stop police from trampling a student, and was dumped in Katorga Raion along with the students.
'Shorty,' who saved him from a pack of beasts, called him Fedya. When Fyodor pressed a gold coin into the boy's hand to bribe the guards, 'Shorty' took the coin and went to the wall.
On Fyodor's secret radio, a voice had been calling for help all along. It was Botani's 374th call, from inside a wardrobe in the middle of the thugs' camp.

On a frequency no one had answered, Fedya answered. You have a firmer will than any high official in this city, he told her. With his guidance, Botani reached the camp, dragging along Pavalo, a ruined baron who had kept Gromov's ledgers.

blocks.cap: A night of raised glasses, filled with beer found in a chemical plant. To tomorrow. To victory.

blocks.x: To... souls happy and free.
After everyone was asleep, Zima confessed. She had dragged her friends into this mire.
Botani handed her the half glass she had not yet drunk. To her, she said, it seemed Sonya had already done it.
10. The Real Hamaxe
Following the map they got from Pavalo, the students struck the Sixteen Warriors' stronghold. 'Pencil Stub' fell with an arrow in his chest, and Yeremey and Nika fell before Gromov's hamaxe.
At the end, Nika thought: I knew it was a trap from the moment we talked about paying ransom. So why did I follow Yeremey?
Deep inside the stronghold, Gromov hid behind the glass wall of the 'Honor Room.' Zima saw a second hamaxe enshrined in the display case. The one Gromov had been swinging was a replica.

blocks.cap: 'The people you killed, the evils you let pass... Any last words, Gromov?'

blocks.x: As the hamaxe came down, Zima felt it grow light. It was neither legend nor relic. It was the very power to resist and to open a way out.

When the fighting was over, Antosha tried to kill Pavalo, and Zima stopped him: she had promised to spare the man in exchange for the information. Only if he walked out alive, she said, would opportunists like him learn that they could negotiate with the students.
In this country, Antosha said, the freedom of the rich was built on the corpses of the poor. From here on, the Unbound would go their own way.
As always, Antosha looked for Matvey's eyes. He was not there.

Smoking a bloodstained cigarette in the snow, Matvey spoke to Antosha when he came to find him: I didn't know you killed for the sake of killing. You're a noble, and you've never once given your own chances to anyone else.
That night Fedya rekindled the bonfire and called out the names one by one. 'Pencil Stub,' Yeremey, Nika, and 'Shorty.'

blocks.cap: The places where glasses had been raised stood empty. Fedya paid his respects alone.

blocks.x: His hand trembled. It was the hand that had given 'Shorty' the gold coin.
11. Sarcophagus, Satellite City

Meanwhile, in the city was another Rhodes Island operator, **Crownslayer** (Lyudmila). She siphoned off energy and handed it out cheap so the poor would not freeze to death, and she always worked alone.
Zima had once told her to say so if she ever needed help, and remembering those words, she slipped into the quarantine zone.

On her way back from meeting Zima, Crownslayer sat across the bonfire from Fedya, and she knew who he was. To the Emperor, who was shouting at her to kill him, she said: go back where you belong, and sign the right laws.
After she left, the Emperor's Blade appeared, but Fyodor said he would not go back. Tell Witte, he said. If he wants to take me back, let him come himself.

Once out of the quarantine zone, Crownslayer switched on the radio Zima had given her, and an unfamiliar man's voice came through. White Nights, Ice Empress, Dreamer, Gold Chervonets, Snow Girl... words that did not connect.
Gummy, beside her, recognized the voice. It was a voice Lada would never forget.

blocks.cap: 'How much land does a man need?' A fairy tale her father used to read to her.

blocks.x: Gummy said her papa had lied to her. All the land Ivan needed in his life was the size of a coffin.

The words pointed to the publication numbers of ten fairy-tale books, and the two words her father had added were 'Sarcophagus' and 'Satellite City.' Instructor **Dur-nar** read them as identification codes for Ursus military facilities.
In the meantime, in the quarantine zone, Pavlovich's men set fire to Zima's camp, and the Unbound's house, built by Matvey's own hands, burned too.
Zima told Dur-nar, who had come to find her, that the flames she had seen here had erased the scenes of Chernobog. Now she had friends at her back.
At the same hour, Witte kept the Imperial Guard waiting outside the quarantine zone. He would wait until those who meant to exploit the Emperor's disappearance could all be caught at once.
12. The Thousand-Year Statue
On the night before the decisive battle, Antosha wrote a letter for each comrade, to be sent to their homes. Whoever died, their families would not learn of it from the nation's casualty lists.

He did not write to his own home. Anton Shestov, grandson of a man who killed a landowner and became a count, cast off that name after seeing a maid his own age, caught stealing food, turned into a corpse covered in whip marks.

That same night, Matvey left Ukusik, who had secretly been drinking and fallen asleep, in the care of Zima's camp, and told an old story. On the night before his expulsion, Antosha leaned against the cherry tree they had planted to mark their hope, and stroked its leafless branches all night long.
When Zima told him to stay, Matvey shook his head. He had a promise to keep. Perhaps one made long before, he said.

Meanwhile, the reinforcements promised to Pavlovich never came. What he received was thirty military police under Captain Chicherin, and a red button that, when pressed, would bring artillery support from beyond the walls. Along with word that Ursus would grant him its highest 'honor.'
At dawn, when Leto and Dur-nar feigned flight and lured the thugs into a narrow alley, the windows flew open all at once and torches and explosives poured down.
The students had once worn different school uniforms. Now their chests bore the same mark: a clenched fist, painted on.
Zima held out her fist to Leto. Good work, General Leto.

Beside the wounded Leto was Gummy, who had gotten in by asking Crownslayer. When the right flank was pushed back, the workers Crownslayer had gathered appeared as if they had sprung from the ground, and explosions rang out behind the enemy lines.

Pavlovich, falling back onto the wall, never pressed the button. Zima struck the burning ground with her hamaxe and cut a path, and at its end, leaning against the main gate of the wall, stood the statue of Igor Velikiy.

For the voices that had been silenced, for the ideals that had frozen to death, she struck its pedestal. The students pushed the statue, and at some point Fedya laid his hands on it too and shouted with them. Ura.
'Your Majesty, protect us...' Pavlovich's last words were never finished. Fragments of Igor's statue rained down on him.

blocks.cap: One person crossed the ruins, and then ten, then a hundred followed.

blocks.x: In their heads rang Zima's words from the night before. Her answer to the offer: kneel and receive a pardon, bring back a comrade's blood and receive a medal.
But no, we say. That is our answer. ...To the children of Ursus, who refuse to kneel!
13. The One Who Survived

Back at the hearing, a surviving member of the Sixteen Warriors testifies that Captain Chicherin cut down the traitors and died an honorable death for his country. From the gallery, Ukusik shouts: liar.

On the battlefield, striking at the enemy's rear, the Unbound ran into the military police. Yura snatched the Originium bomb from Antosha, who had taken an arrow in the leg. Had he forgotten, Yura asked, which of them was the quickest?
The Unbound wiped out the enemy. Only Antosha came back.
Antosha told Zima to strike him down. She had killed Pavlovich, so why could she not see the crimes of the other nobles and the Emperor? If you want to go your way, walk over my corpse.
Zima refused. Throwing away your life does not make an ideal shine. As she turned away, Antosha tried to grab her, and Leto knocked him down.

blocks.cap: 'No more hurting your friends.'

blocks.x: Your friends may have chosen to sacrifice themselves for your ideals, Leto said. Maybe even for you. That day, Antosha tasted regret for the second time.
Ukusik woke and came running. Antosha asked her: those letters, are they still in your bag?
Meanwhile, when a noble who had brought the Imperial Guard declared he would purge the traitors, Fyodor asked: who are these 'traitors' you speak of?

blocks.cap: Leaving behind the car with its red carpet, the Emperor walked the streets of his own city for the first time.

blocks.x: Asked whether more than twenty years of holding on had come to nothing but that sea of fire, Witte did not answer, and stopped an attendant from going after the Emperor. This is what His Majesty wants, he said.
Epilogue — The Blank Notebook
With all testimony concluded, the arbiter declares the hearing closed. The final result will come in two hours.
Zoya says quietly: now. Without expression, the clerk holds up a notebook with nothing written in it.
While the police are concentrated on the hearing, Prison No. 3 is broken open, and Rania and the others held there are set free. Zoya's testimony had been meant to buy time from the very start.
As the USSG gathers again, Zima tells Zoya to wear the fist badge. You should have been one of us long ago, she says.
Crownslayer sets out in search of the 'Satellite City,' and Gummy, who has followed her, asks: you weren't at Peterheim back then, were you?
She shakes her head. But she was in Chernobog, and she must share the burden of Reunion's crimes.
Gummy presses a honey candy into her hand. A promise, she says.
Meanwhile, Antosha goes alone to Matvey's home. Beyond the window, Matvey's mother is ladling borscht into three bowls. Antosha tucks the death notice into the window frame and runs.
As he runs, Matvey is reflected in a mirror loaded on a cart. Without a single wound, a cherry blossom pinned to his chest.

blocks.cap: The friend in the mirror stood in the sunlight.

blocks.x: Because you still have the chance to live the life I once imagined.
Antosha decides to live. Resolving that someday he will carve Matvey, their teacher, and every one of the Unbound onto a monument to the martyrs, he follows at the very back of the workers' column.

At the other end of the column, a young man named Nikto gazes at the unfamiliar city. Somewhere, the commander-in-chief of the First Army orders a detonation test of a new weapon to be carried out 'discreetly.'
The hearing called them heinous traitors. Those who crossed the ruins of Katorga Raion were the children of Ursus who refused to kneel.

main_0.tagline: Having lost all memory, the Doctor wakes up in a coffin and, led by the hands of unfamiliar comrades, picks up the baton of command once more in a burning Chernobog. What's lost can simply be found again—what matters isn't the memories that vanished, but now.

terms.name: Rhodes Island
terms.desc: An organization of the Infected. Handles both treatment and conflict resolution.

terms.name: Reunion
terms.desc: An armed Infected organization that rose up in Ursus.

terms.name: Oripathy
terms.desc: An incurable disease caused by Originium. Those afflicted become the Infected.

terms.name: Catastrophe
terms.desc: A natural disaster that strikes Terra. Leaves Originium behind.

terms.name: Ursus
terms.desc: A military empire harsh toward the Infected.

terms.desc: Rhodes Island's support system. Accessed via neural connector.

terms.name: Kazimierz
terms.desc: Nearl's homeland. A country of knights.

blocks.x: In the world called Terra, a natural disaster known as the 'Catastrophe' strikes periodically. In the wake of a Catastrophe, a mineral called Originium is left behind, and people exposed to it for too long contract 'Oripathy' and become the 'Infected.'
The world treats the Infected not as the sick, but as a threat. Ursus, a military empire, is especially harsh toward them.
This story begins at the edge of a cliff in such a world, inside a single frozen coffin. Sleeping within it is a person who has lost every memory—someone people call 'the Doctor.'

blocks.cap: Somewhere in the fog. An unidentified voice whispers to the sleeping figure. "December 23rd... you must remember, no matter what."

blocks.x: 1. The One Who Woke Inside a Coffin
On a cold operating table, someone restarts a heart that had stopped. Urgent voices go back and forth, injecting cardioplegic solution and beginning the incision.
One of those voices quietly apologizes. "...I'm sorry. I hurt you again." Its owner never gives a name.

When the Doctor opens their eyes, the girl who'd been keeping watch grabs their hand, on the verge of tears. It's **Amiya**. Just moments ago, she'd even been bracing herself for the possibility that the Doctor might never wake up.
The medic beside her marvels—Amiya seems like a completely different person whenever the Doctor comes up. It's clear just how much this reunion means to her.
But the Doctor remembers nothing. Not Amiya, not their own name, nothing about everything that came before.

Amiya doesn't break down in front of them. She introduces herself as a member of Rhodes Island, and tells the Doctor over and over that they are her most precious comrade. She won't ask them to remember it all right now, she says—just give her a little time.
She swallows down just how great a price it took to get the Doctor back. Instead, she only says this: so much has changed, but one thing hasn't—that the Doctor is the person who matters most to her.

blocks.cap: "Take my hand!" — The hand Amiya reaches out pulls the memory-less Doctor out of the darkness.

blocks.x: 2. Handing the Baton to a Stranger
In that brief moment of reunion, an armed group storms the facility. A heavily armed Infected organization—**Reunion**.
Operators shield the Doctor behind cover, shouting urgently. Communication with Kal'tsit is dead—someone is jamming the signal.
Communications are down, and there's no reaching Kal'tsit, the commander for this operation. Even knowing the danger, Amiya asks the Doctor, who has just woken up, to take command.
There's only one basis for it: even having lost their memory, the Doctor was once a comrade who fought alongside them, and her unwavering belief in them.
Putting the Doctor back on the battlefield is agony for Amiya too. Even so, she says Rhodes Island needs the Doctor's wisdom right now, and hopes this battle will help them recover their instincts.
I know you can do it. I believe that. Please... command Rhodes Island...!
Under the Doctor's command, the first battle ends in a flawless victory. The body may not remember, but the fingertips still read the battlefield.

blocks.cap: A crest engraved with a single rook. "Enjoy my life and hone my craft" — this is Rhodes Island.

blocks.x: 3. Three Hours
As the battle ends, **Dobermann**, captain of another operations team, joins up. Her team was also hit by a Reunion raid and just made it over to this side.
Hearing that command was handed to someone who lost their memory, Dobermann is dumbfounded. She's not the type to easily trust a stranger, either.

Still, having witnessed the command with her own two eyes just now, she decides to give Amiya's words a try. She introduces herself to the Doctor as the captain of Operations Team E1, and says she'll escort them from Chernobog to Rhodes Island.

Right then, the neural connector unexpectedly activates, and the support system **PRTS** connects. With radio communication blocked, they still can't reach Kal'tsit, who hasn't made it back to Rhodes Island yet—but at least a channel is now open to tell the Doctor the next move.
Having verified authorization by fingerprint, PRTS offers a calm greeting. "Welcome back, Doctor."
Once preparations for the move are finished, Dobermann quietly lets only Amiya know the truth. In three hours, a Catastrophe will strike this city.
If they can't get out of Chernobog by then, it's over for everyone. Worried the team might panic, Dobermann hasn't told anyone else about the countdown yet.
4. The Ark of the Infected
On the retreat, the Doctor seems to ask again—what exactly is the Infected.
Amiya answers plainly. She herself, Dobermann, most of Rhodes Island, and even the Reunion they just fought—all suffer from the same disease.
It's Oripathy. Those afflicted are hunted everywhere, and Ursus justifies its persecution with reports that stoke fear of the Infected. Citizens even applaud it.
That very oppression is also why Reunion targeted this city. To Infected people crushed under it, Reunion looks like a way out.

Meanwhile, a medic operator wrangles with a Guard trying to dodge an injection, insisting regular treatment is needed to ease the symptoms. This noisy little tussle is just everyday life at a place called Rhodes Island.
Between it all, Rhodes Island carries two burdens at once—searching for a cure for Oripathy, while also cleaning up conflicts the Infected get tangled in.

Because leaning too far to either side means failing to protect the Infected's lives. Dobermann quietly tells the Doctor that since she too is Infected, these are burdens the Doctor might end up carrying from now on.
If a fight can be avoided, hold your tongue... but if it cannot be avoided, fight to the very end!

blocks.cap: Rhodes Island's creed has never once changed.

blocks.x: 5. Chernobog in Flames
Stepping out into the streets, the city is already hell. Explosions, fires, and street fighting all tangle together, and Reunion strikes at Ursus citizens indiscriminately.
Yet the propaganda broadcast calmly repeats, "situation resolved," over and over—even as, off-screen, the military police are actually being overrun by Reunion.

blocks.cap: "The glory of Ursus shall protect His Majesty and the citizens" — as the news of victory plays, the streets are burning.

blocks.x: Rhodes Island clears a path by striking down the Reunion forces using civilians as shields. Along the way, they run into an Ursus military police captain who, despite his contempt for these Infected, lets them pass, saying he doesn't care why they came so long as they're not here to destroy the city.

The captain flatly says he has no interest in what these Infected women are here for. But if they're here to destroy the city, he warns, Ursus's fury won't stop until they're dead. The resolve of a man holding his post.
Then he stays behind alone to defend the street, and falls, leaving behind the words: "An Ursus soldier never shows his back to the enemy."

blocks.cap: As the news of victory plays, there's a child left alone amid the flames on the street.

blocks.x: 6. What's Lost Can Simply Be Found Again

At the next rendezvous point, the veteran leader **Ace** comes out alone to greet them. He'd stationed his team at the meeting point in case of emergency, and came out himself to clear away any dangers directly.
Even hearing the Doctor has lost their memory, Ace isn't shaken. As long as their command ability is intact, that's all that matters to him, and he says he'll follow the Doctor's orders.
What's lost can simply be found again.

Reunion even unleashes infected beasts as soldiers. Dobermann realizes they're not mere beasts, but creatures closer to themselves than not, and Ace says there's nothing to do but release them from their suffering.
The three of them mull over what Reunion really is. Anyone who puts on the uniform and the mark is taken in, an endlessly swelling force fed on hatred and fear.
And a leader who uses and discards that force like chess pieces. Dobermann calls a person like that not a commander, but a 'tyrant'—someone who tramples even his own side to crush the enemy.

Dobermann adds bitterly. Poke just one small hole in the bars of a cage, and those trapped inside will rush out no matter what, even if the outside is a sea of fire. Reunion runs on exactly that kind of desperation as fuel.

Hearing that, Ace recalls something someone once told him. A pawn, if it's a pawn, you just capture it. A castle, if it's a castle, you just bring it down. A crown, if it's a crown, you just topple it. Whoever the enemy is, Rhodes Island simply carries out its mission.
7. The Boy Who Plays Games
Just before the final rendezvous point, an ambush strikes along with the fog. **Crownslayer**, a masked Reunion agent, has caught up with Rhodes Island.
But another figure who shows up right after sends her back. Crownslayer withdraws, leaving behind the words, "I do hope you fail spectacularly."
**Mephisto**. A boy commander who moves the Infected around as precisely as chess pieces. Finding Rhodes Island's way of fighting entertaining, he proposes a 'game'—survive, and he'll let them go.
What he really wants is the Doctor. He presses relentlessly—how did they possibly survive at that facility, who exactly are they—and demands the Doctor be handed over as a gift.
When Catastrophe looms right before your eyes... isn't that exactly the right time to throw a festival?
Mephisto's command is chillingly precise. He moves the frenzied Infected alone like pieces on a chessboard, sealing off one escape route after another, driving Rhodes Island into a corner.
At a single word from him, the Infected shift formation with precision. He hides casters behind defenders, then unleashes them the very moment Rhodes Island's ranks crack.
And die, like sparks in a rainy night!

blocks.cap: Beyond the fog, a commander who moves the Infected like chess pieces closes in on Rhodes Island.

blocks.x: 8. The Knight of Kazimierz

Just as the tide is turning against them, reinforcements who pinpointed the flare's location arrive and smash Reunion's formation from the side. It's **Nearl**, knight of Kazimierz, having already evacuated the citizens in advance.
Mephisto sends his taciturn sniper **Faust** to target Nearl. Faust's sniping is a crossfire raining down from multiple locations at once—enough to wipe out any other team in an instant if hit.
Nearl catches that sniper fire with her shield. Riding the brief opening Ace bought her, she charges straight into the heart of the enemy lines, tearing the encirclement wide open.
If you're seriously thinking of taking down a knight of Kazimierz... come back after a few more decades of training!

After breaking free of the encirclement, Ace and Nearl mull over that sniper. Judging by the minute timing gaps in the blasts, Faust seems to exist not as a single person but split across multiple locations. Reunion is a far more dangerous opponent than expected.

Nearl offers a word to the Doctor, who seems unsure about their own command. She says avoiding danger wasn't down to her own judgment but thanks to the Doctor's leadership, and tells them to have a little more confidence.
And upon hearing the Doctor has lost their memory, she just laughs it off as no big deal. One of her friends has lost their memory too, she says.
What matters most to you probably isn't the memories that vanished, but 'now.'
Epilogue — Unfinished, To Be Continued
As the Doctor's group makes it out of the city, Mephisto withdraws, leaving the pursuit to Faust. He says he needs to report the situation to his 'sister.'

Faust, having failed to catch Nearl in the end, apologizes for his own mistake. Mephisto soothes his sniper, saying the excess excitement was his own fault—and that above all, Faust's own safety matters most.
That sister has already seized Chernobog's central command tower. Whether to let the vermin that is Rhodes Island live or die is now hers to decide.
Comrades. Let us depart now. To greet our era!!

The Doctor, who lost every memory and woke inside a coffin, took hold of a hand that believed in them and picked up the baton of command once more in a burning city. What's lost can simply be found again, and what matters most isn't a vanished past but 'now.' And the time remaining until Catastrophe still hasn't run out completely.

rogue_1.tagline: A squad enters a fog-bound castle in search of a missing comrade and is drawn, step by step, onto the stage of the Crimson Troupe, a troupe believed long scattered. Where is the lead actor? The play has already begun.
