chars.name: Miss Christine
chars.desc: The cat who stays by Phantom's side.

chars.name: Tin Man
chars.desc: A detective with a mechanical face, sent by the 'Maylander Historical Association' to investigate the Crimson Troupe.

chars.name: Troupe Mouthpiece
chars.desc: The one who speaks for the Crimson Troupe and runs the stage in the castle.

chars.name: Playwright
chars.desc: The one who writes the Crimson Troupe's scripts.

terms.name: Crimson Troupe
terms.desc: An organization of killers disguised as a company of artists. Believed to have scattered after its leadership was murdered several years ago.

terms.name: Solitaire
terms.desc: The codename of the member said to have murdered several of the Crimson Troupe's leaders.

terms.name: Blood Diamond
terms.desc: The title of the lead actor whom the Crimson Troupe calls 'the troupe's rising star.'

blocks.x: The castle rose high above the forest, ruined just enough, and the troupe that had settled there built a stage for its play. Years of effort were beginning to bear fruit, but one question still had no answer.
Where is the lead actor? Where is the protagonist? In the silence, no one could answer.
Take the stage, rising star of the troupe, the troupe's Blood Diamond. All is ready, and the play has already begun.

blocks.cap: The troupe's stage, built inside the castle.

blocks.x: Into that castle comes a Rhodes Island squad. Another squad that went in before them has sent a distress signal, and they must find the operator **Phantom** somewhere inside.
1. 17:03, Mist-stricken Missteps
As the fog spread, the squad lost its way. They could not even tell whether they were moving forward or circling in place.
At 19:24, the setting sun filled the courtyard, but it was not the color of hope. Come in, you who have wandered astray. The castle welcomes you.

At 20:36, when they reached the 'Homeland Remnants,' where vines climbed the columns, the darkness seemed to retreat for a moment. The squad found a quiet corner, sorted their supplies, and caught their breath.
When someone began to tell the tales of heroes of old, squad members worn out by strange sights gathered round one by one to listen.

blocks.cap: A fire lit in a corner of the castle. The darkness drew back for a while.

blocks.x: Yet danger always lay in wait in the castle. The eerie surroundings, the enemies in the dark, and the strange happenings never ceased, and the darkness followed the squad like a shadow.
2. Those Who Came for Treasure
The squad was not the castle's only guest. After an old castle fell in tragedy, its story was handed down as a repertoire piece, but the castle's treasures still lay sleeping here, untouched.

Beside the rotting corpse of that tragedy's protagonist, the squad picked up a script manuscript written in his own hand. Half of it had already crumbled into dust. Whether the script came first or the history did, no one can say anymore.

Meanwhile, in a gaudily decorated room, two crowned Liberi calling themselves the sixth and eighth emperors of Gaul argued over the merits and failings of Corsica I, the last emperor of Gaul, then vanished into the mist.

A ragged old soldier they met atop the ruins also claimed to have fought alongside the emperor, and said he had come for the emperor's treasures to help revive Gaul. But his uniform was that of a militiaman drafted by the Gaulish Empire, and he even got the emperor's name wrong. The squad did not point it out, and heard his speech through to the end.

In the meantime, the squad stepped on rotten floorboards and tumbled into the basement, where they met three gloomy Zalak treasure hunters. They had gone to great lengths to find the treasure vault, only for someone quicker to strip it first, leaving nothing but trash.

Elsewhere, an old Feline lady reading a book of fairy tales atop a pile of boxes said these were all treasures forgotten by history when their owners lost everything. Among the owners' stories she told for a few coins was one about a child from a poor family who dreamed of becoming an actor, joined a troupe, and was never seen again.
3. 21:53, When the Candles Light
At 21:53, as darkness fell, the candles throughout the empty castle lit all at once. Silent nightmares began to roam the shadows, searching for prey that had lost its way.

Meanwhile, an adventurer preparing to leave said that a grand ghost theater opened here every midnight. The ghosts enjoyed the stage all night long, and he had nearly been attacked by madmen shouting strange lines.
At the ballroom, men and women in smiling masks danced without rest. Even as their voices went hoarse, even as their shoes wore through and their feet bled, no one stopped dancing.

When someone in the squad began to sing, the music followed like an accompaniment, and the dancers all stopped at once and watched in silence. "The leader would love your singing. He definitely would."

Meanwhile, in an open space, a masked Sarkaz woman in red dance shoes was dancing alone, and she held out her hand to the squad. After they danced together, she gave them a pair of dance shoes and vanished without a trace, and something seemed to be missing from their pockets.

blocks.cap: A woman in red dance shoes, dancing alone.

blocks.x: And all through the castle, scented candles burned with a sweet yet strange smell. In one room thick with the scent, well-dressed artists had lost their minds and were attacking one another, and some already lay on the floor. Why everyone in the castle seemed out of their mind, that scent was the likeliest answer.
4. Artists Who Answered the Call

Even so, artists kept gathering at the castle. A wandering musician said he had followed the trail of that 'troupe' in search of a legendary figure in the history of art, and that he wished to join it.

Meanwhile, a duck calling himself the Duck Lord silenced the party guests, who had been holding forth about art, with a single snap of his fingers, and said: "I know why all of you are here. So why not go home while you still have the chance?"

Around then, Leithanian nobles were talking about a party organized by a spire caster obsessed with the performing arts. The noble who handed the squad his invitation said the organizer had sunk into research on forbidden Arts and had been growing madder for years, and that he was glad someone would go in his stead.

From one room came the sound of an argument in thick Leithanian accents. "He really means to kill everyone at the party? Just for that play of his?" "He's been out of his mind ever since he ran into that Crimson Troupe!"
But when they opened the door, the room was empty, with only a broken staff lying on the floor. It was as if the argument had never happened.

Meanwhile, a middle-aged man muttering in front of a dressing table shouted, the moment he saw the squad, for them to deliver a crown wrapped in thorns to the actor. When the crown slipped from a thorn-pricked hand and half shattered, he left behind a remark that the actors had run off because none of them wanted to play the empress, and fled.

blocks.cap: The crown once wrapped in thorns. It fell to the floor and broke in half.

blocks.x: There were also traces that hinted at the castle's master. On the back of a tablet in a hidden room, and on the pedestal of a sculpture in a secret chamber that someone seemed to tidy often, were inscriptions beginning with 'Once, I.' The writer had been sullen under the barbs of fools and lost in radical artistic expression, but held that the true meaning of art is not hidden by a rough or ugly surface.

A junk peddler who saw the tablet cried out, "This belonged to the troupe leader..." then, realizing his slip, told them not to tell anyone and left. And the Durins guzzling the castle's wine in the cellar claimed to have the owner's permission; when the squad drained an entire barrel, they were left speechless, then marveled that it was wine the troupe leader had kept aging for 500 years.
5. The Captives

There were captives in the castle, too. In a gloomy jail, a slight girl bound to a pillar with massive chains claimed to be of the Sarkaz Vampire royal court and begged for blood to regain her strength.

Given blood, the girl snapped her chains and laughed like a madwoman, crying that she would take revenge on every one of the 'troupe members' who had bound her there. Her face split three ways, baring sharp fangs, and the jail's shadows gathered into twisted shapes and fell upon the squad.

blocks.cap: A gloomy jail, and a girl chained to a pillar.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, an elegant Sarkaz gentleman appeared, looking for a friend. Because of his own mistake, he said, the villagers had taken that friend for a Vampire and locked them up here. As the squad led the way, he told them the whole story, but shook his head and asked them not to ask where the villagers had gone.

In the dungeon, the prisoners silently carved something into the walls or lay on the floor muttering. When the squad drew near, one of them shouted, "Why do you disturb me? Why do you not let me finish my story?!" and rammed the iron door.
Meanwhile, a young Feline trembling under a table took a long time to believe that the squad were not demons come to drag him off and make him act and sing.
In another hall stood row upon row of statues in stage costumes. Lifelike, each in a different pose, they all had their eyes shut tight, as if asleep.

blocks.cap: Statues in stage costumes. All of them have their eyes closed.

blocks.x: And at last, the squad found the Rhodes Island squad that had sent the original distress signal. They had been scouting the area all along, and after the two exchanged information, the advance squad shared the supplies and experience they needed.
6. The Crimson Troupe

One eccentric they met in the castle wore a trench coat and a fedora, and beneath the hat was a face of metal and mechanical parts. Introducing himself as a detective, **Tin Man** had come from the 'Maylander Historical Association' to investigate an organization called the 'Crimson Troupe,' and was now trapped here along with the squad.

From what he had uncovered, the Crimson Troupe was an organization of killers disguised as a company of artists. Several years ago, he said, a member codenamed **Solitaire** murdered several of its leaders, and the troupe scattered.
All that has happened here in this castle shows that this organization was never truly destroyed. They are still bringing death and suffering to the innocent.

Then a gaunt, hunchbacked stranger laughed oddly, saying she knew whom the squad was looking for. "But you don't understand that Feline, do you?" Holding out her withered hands, she offered to sell them his past.

According to the stranger, that Feline, a member of the troupe, learned illusion Arts from 'Shadow,' dance-like combat from 'Bladedance,' and acting from 'Whiteflower.' And 'His Lordship' gave him a voice that captivates the heart.

But on the day he faced the truth that the teachers he revered were all irredeemable villains, a night of blood fell. The stranger laughed that the Feline's blade had proved sharper than 'Bladedance's' own and that 'Whiteflower' had fallen at her student's hand. But about 'His Lordship' alone she kept her mouth shut, saying she valued her life.

Meanwhile, at a teatime aboard Rhodes Island, **Iris** brought out half of a red ticket that had been tucked into a book as a bookmark in the Castle of Dreams. **Shalem**, who was serving the tea, at first passed it off as a voucher for a Londinium patisserie, but when Melantha pointed out its deep red and Iris thought of 'Crimson,' he finally admitted it was a ticket for a Crimson Troupe performance.
The ticket said nothing about what was being performed. There was no need for it to, Shalem said, and he put it this way.
The performers are puppets to their roles, and the roles choose the program themselves.

Asked whether it was something like the Castle of Dreams, that age-old Victorian legend, Shalem said it was. Only it was not a child's lovely wish, but a terrible tragedy that could strike without warning. Iris decided to return the ticket to where she had found it.
7. 00:00, Blood-soaked Corridor
At midnight, a blood-red moon shone through the windowpanes into the corridor. According to the records, a night of the blood moon had always marked the beginning of misfortune.
Against one wall sat a shabby wooden puppet with broken limbs. Its faded features seemed familiar, and hidden inside its chest was a red heart.

In another room hung an oil painting of a tragedy's ending. The protagonist, it was said, realized only at the very end that he had lived his whole life inside someone else's scheme, and threw himself from a high tower to escape every bond and every control. Just as the squad leaned in to look, a doll fell from above and shattered before them.

When the squad picked up the broken doll, a swarm of puppets moving to a strange rhythm poured in from the end of the corridor and blocked the way. They seemed to be after the broken doll rather than the squad, pulling at ears and trying to tie them up with string.

Clutching the doll tight, they broke through to the other end of the corridor, where a youth with a quill was writing something on paper. He glanced at the squad, handed them a pair of scissors, and before they knew it, he was gone.
One flight further up, a familiar figure stood by a window. He thanked them and handed over a letter, and when they asked his name, he stepped back, smiled, and leapt out the window.

The youth with the quill appeared in another room as well. Under flickering candlelight, he was dipping his quill in strangely colored ink and writing. When the squad approached, flames shot up from the quill, and he vanished into the smoke.
Meanwhile, in a place that might have been a dream or might have been real, an old box on a stone desk awaited the squad. If your life were a play, would it be a comedy, or a tragedy?

And then the 'Hall of Desires,' where even the hour has been erased. There, where pure and true desire reigns above the order of time, nothing remained but the thirst for beauty, for art, and for perfection.

blocks.cap: A candlelit staircase in the castle, and an actor in a red cloak.

blocks.x: 8. The First Ending — Crimson Finale
The story came to its end. The lights went out, the actors left, the red curtain slowly fell, and everything sank back into silence.

Phantom had regained himself, and he still remembered what he had done. That he, the lead actor, had been nothing but the troupe's bait, luring passionate, noble people again and again into a pit from which there was no return.
He had been rescued this time, but what about before? Had anyone ever been lost in this labyrinth? Had he ever pushed a comrade who reached out to him off the stage?
He did not dare to imagine it, and he felt ashamed.
Then someone called to him. "Lucian, it's time we went back." It was Shalem.

Shalem told him he had caused Rhodes Island a great deal of trouble, so he had better think up his lines for the Doctor in advance. Phantom replied that the very idea of rehearsing lines for the Doctor shamed him, and that he would make amends through his actions.
Looking around the stage, Shalem said the place felt truly familiar. It was a place every actor dreams of, he said, and asked whether Phantom didn't want to sing a song.
My voice brings nothing but disaster...

Shalem steadied his breath and apologized. He had only wanted to make sure, he said, that Phantom had truly come back. When Shalem offered to help him walk, Phantom was silent for a long while, then answered briefly: "...Thank you."
9. The Second Ending — Ridiculous Comedy

On the same stage after the curtain fell, this time a large doll lay collapsed without a sound. **Miss Christine**, the cat at Phantom's side, wanted to sharpen her claws on the doll's fabric or curl up in the stuffing spilling out of it, but before anything else she checked on Phantom.

From the moment Phantom lost his reason, Miss Christine had been leaving paw prints, claw marks, and bite marks as clues for the Rhodes Island operators. Whether or not they understood what she meant, the result pleased her very much.

Shalem, the Phidia who had once been a member of the troupe and still feared everything about it, was still examining the doll. He was worried the puppeteer might suddenly appear and take Phantom back into the shadows. Miss Christine had already seen that this would not happen.

Having finished his check, Shalem helped Phantom to his feet. His tone was guarded at first; only once he was sure Phantom had truly regained himself did he set down the weight on his mind, and the group stepped off the stage and headed for the castle's exit.
At the top of the stairs, Phantom stopped and tried to put his tangled thoughts in order. Miss Christine, licking her paw at his feet, absently turned her head to tend an itch on her back.
And then she froze. What she saw was an uninvited guest.
They had found the one they were looking for. But no one could say for sure that the exploration of the castle had really ended. Perhaps it was all only beginning.
10. The Third Ending — Grand Opening

This time it was the **'Troupe Mouthpiece'** who fell on the stage, and the strings in his hands dropped to the floor and tangled like a spiderweb. With these strings he had worked the castle's traps and controlled its wicked puppets.

With the fall of the Mouthpiece, a former member of the troupe, it was all over, and Phantom let out a sigh of relief. He had lived half his life under the Crimson Troupe's rule, and today he had broken free of its bonds once again. Now he would go back to living in peace, he thought.

But the lights flickered, and the curtain began to rise again. The stage seemed to be waiting for something still, and without knowing why, Phantom set the Mouthpiece's chair at center stage, sat down, and fell silent.
Sing, sing. For yourself.
A single syllable escaped his lips. Then another, and another; then lines, then an aria. The stage was silent no longer, and the lead actor sang to his heart's content.

From the shadows, barely audible sounds began to answer the melody. The fallen host rose too and cast aside his tangle of strings; the actor was ready, he said, so he too must carry out his duty, and he walked back to his place.
Around then, Shalem heard the singing. Once he found Phantom, the mission would be over. He opened the door.
The Mouthpiece greeted him. "Oh, our first guest." Before the horrified Shalem, the Mouthpiece rejoiced that the two wanderers had returned to the troupe's embrace.
Then, without further ado... the show begins.

blocks.cap: The troupe in the shadows, the 'Blood Diamond' in the light.

blocks.x: One by one, the nightmares of days past flashed before Shalem's eyes. The coachman cracking his whip, the host standing upright, the prop master and the lighting technician, the cook sharpening his knife, the silent butler, the writer at work on a script. The restlessly wavering 'Shadow,' 'Bladedance' giving off an eerie gleam, the smiling 'Whiteflower,' and even the troupe leader, staring at Shalem.
Every member of the troupe hid in the stage's shadows, red eyes gleaming. Only one stood in the light: **Lucian, the 'Blood Diamond'**. He cleared his throat and prepared to sing.
The opening and the close both belong to the host. When the show is over, offer him flowers.
11. The Fourth Ending — Silent Chapter
Every word the Playwright writes is true. The bleeding, the weeping, even life and death themselves.

On the same stage, the **Playwright** unfolded a script he had painstakingly polished. At the troupe's call, the protagonist returned to the stage, and the coward who had fled the troupe faced it once more, solely to save the one to whom he was bound by the thinnest of threads.

But the story ended like this: the protagonist and the coward both went home to Rhodes Island, and the host, who had abandoned his duties to take up the puppets' strings, was beaten down like the villains before him. The troupe gained nothing.

To the Playwright, such an ending was a desecration. So, he said, he had added to the story. He made the creator's hardship and rage into a wall and thrust it upon the protagonist, and as the price of that growth, the protagonist would carry his defiance of his creator through to the very end.
But once Rhodes Island intervened, the natures and fates he had wanted for his characters all changed, and the story's ending became something not even the Playwright himself could decide.
Failed works are all burned once they are written, and everything begins anew.

Creation came with unexpected errors, too. Foreshadowing was laid, yet the protagonist fell before it could pay off; supporting characters appeared who should not have, events occurred that should not have, walls were faced that should not have been, and choices were made that should never have been made.

Still, he said, it was fortunate that a few had shone brightly, and the Playwright recommended one of those scripts. It was a story in which every hardship is swept away with great effort and the beautiful ending everyone longs for is reached, yet a seed of darkness lies hidden deep in the heart.
When that seed blossoms and bears fruit, all that beauty will at last become the tragedy we have longed for.
Fate has already been decided, but the protagonist knows nothing. The troupe need only wait in the dark for the joy of that ending to arrive.
"What do you think?" The one the Playwright had been addressing all along was someone else. "My dear troupe leader."
The truth of the Crimson Troupe goes deeper than this. Seek it, discover it. And then, escape it.

Where is the lead actor? To the question posed by the castle's stage, the four acts each gave a different answer. Failed manuscripts are burned and everything begins again — the play has already begun.

main_1.tagline: One hour before the Catastrophe hits, they escape a burning Chernobog. To get the Doctor and Amiya to the southern exit, their comrades fall back one by one.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: Leader of Rhodes Island. She can't bring herself to abandon a single comrade.

chars.name: Dobermann
chars.desc: Captain of Operation Team E1. Wants Amiya to learn to stand on her own.

chars.name: Nearl
chars.desc: A knight of Kazimierz. Shields the Doctor with her own body.

chars.name: Ace
chars.desc: Veteran leader of the operation team. Remembers the Doctor.

chars.name: Talulah
chars.desc: The tyrant of Reunion. A flame sorceress who burns the whole land.

chars.name: Crownslayer
chars.desc: A Reunion agent at Talulah's side.

chars.name: Mephisto
chars.desc: A young Reunion commander who controls the Infected.

chars.name: W
chars.desc: An unidentified woman blocking the exit. She's after the Doctor.

terms.name: Catastrophe
terms.desc: A natural disaster striking Terra. Rains down massive Originium.

terms.name: Reunion
terms.desc: An armed Infected organization that has overrun Chernobog.

terms.name: Azazel
terms.desc: A secret clinic that quietly treated the Infected. Now in ruins.

terms.name: Oripathy
terms.desc: An incurable disease caused by Originium. Grants power, but ends in death.

terms.name: Chernobog
terms.desc: A city in Ursus. A place that has long persecuted the Infected.

blocks.x: Rhodes Island is getting the Doctor — who woke up in a coffin with no memories — out of a burning Chernobog. The Catastrophe is about to strike the city, and there's barely an hour left.
The streets are swarming with Reunion. Destruction, looting, and arson never let up. Overhead, the Catastrophe clouds are already gathering, heavy and ominous.
This is the final stage of the rescue operation. There's only one goal: reach the southern exit alive.
This is the record of that short escape route — of Rhodes Island learning, firsthand, what it means to be Infected, and what it means to protect a comrade.

blocks.cap: The Catastrophe clouds press down on the city, dark and heavy. "It's taking shape. A bad omen."

blocks.x: 1. A Clinic Called Azazel
Even amid the tension, Rhodes Island manages a brief laugh. When Nearl seriously dismisses Reunion as "a bunch of idiots on a picnic," a Medic can't help but burst out laughing.
Nearl belatedly realizes she'd just made a joke and turns awkward. Even Amiya smiles quietly at the clumsy attempt at humor.
We didn't found Rhodes Island to watch you all suffer.
As they move along, the group finds a clinic in ruins — a place Amiya has visited before, the Infected clinic **Azazel**.
There's not even a trace that anyone was here. Azazel was connected to Rhodes Island's communication network, yet it never called for help — and now it's gone, just like this.
One Operator is furious, saying their own arrogance brought this on themselves. But Ace quietly stops him — it wasn't entirely their fault.

blocks.cap: "The Infected can't easily trust others. After everything they've been through, of course they've grown wary and stubborn."

blocks.x: Amiya tells the Doctor what Azazel used to be — the last refuge Infected hiding their identities in the city would secretly seek out, to avoid being exiled to a quarantine zone.

Oripathy grants tremendous power, but in exchange it eats away the body and the whole of a life. It strips away social rights, and death always waits at the end. And the corpse becomes a new source of infection.
That's why people treat the Infected not as the sick, but as something to fear. Chernobog is the very symbol of that discrimination, exile, and extermination.
Azazel must have refused Reunion's demands — and paid the price for it. Amiya doesn't resent their wariness. She says she can understand it, and forgive it.
Very few Infected ever get the chance to join Reunion or take Rhodes Island's hand. Most have already lost everything, and simply wait for death in despair.

To the Doctor, who probably can't fully grasp all of this yet, Amiya calmly adds that a day will come when he'll face it himself — along with the thought that Rhodes Island, too, might end up just like Azazel.
2. Less Than an Hour Left
There's now less than an hour until the Catastrophe. There's no time for a detour — they have no choice but to break straight through the Reunion-held district ahead.

Dobermann leaves the call to the Doctor. Since Reunion's communications are primitive and their formations scattered, the plan is to punch through the front line with a surprise strike and slip into the next district before the enemy can regroup.
Amiya says without hesitation that she trusts the Doctor's choice. But Dobermann doesn't let that answer slide.
Borrowing the Doctor's strategic mind is fine, she says, but Amiya shouldn't lean on him too much. A leader also needs to know how to stand alone.
She says this because she cares about Amiya. Dobermann quietly asks the Doctor, too, to understand her wish for Amiya to keep learning and growing.
Still, Dobermann makes it clear: trust isn't built in a single battle. That said, she adds — more than once — that the Doctor is doing well so far.
At the signal to charge, Rhodes Island breaks through the blockade in one stroke. Reunion, regrouping too late, gives chase, but the group has already slipped into the next district.

Meanwhile, somewhere in the city, the young commander **Mephisto** is reading the situation. Faust is tracking Rhodes Island, he notes, and they're now trapped on the outskirts of the central district.
Mephisto notices they're trying to flee amid the chaos of the Catastrophe. If they might get in the way of his plans, he thinks, ending it here wouldn't be a bad idea.
3. When the Sky Turns Blood Red
Reaching the great plaza, the full horror of the city comes into view. Citizens who couldn't escape in time are pinned down and attacked by Reunion.
But this terrain puts Rhodes Island at a disadvantage. Ace states, calmly but heavily, that they can't afford to rush in to protect the citizens.

Passing through the ruined plaza, Ace seems to recall something — that a city which once persecuted the Infected is now suffering their retaliation. Though she swallows the rest, saying it's all in the past.
Just then, a massive number of Reunion troops pour in from the plaza's exit. Dobermann senses something's off — Reunion has no reason to defend this place, so why are there so many of them?
Far from fearing the Catastrophe, Reunion is exhilarated, shouting, "Our savior of the Infected has come!" Then, for no apparent reason, they begin collapsing one by one.
The sky turns blood red. Nearl murmurs an old verse under her breath. "When the surging clouds swirl within the flames……"

blocks.cap: "Fear steals away their voices, and the earth falls into silence…… as vast Originium comes pouring down from the sky."

blocks.x: Somewhere in the plaza, two figures look down on this scene. Reunion agent **Crownslayer**, and someone with dragon horns.

blocks.cap: "Take care of whoever's left alive." — Above the Catastrophe, two shadows watch over Rhodes Island.

blocks.x: Only then does Dobermann realize: this isn't revenge. Reunion has declared war, aiming to wipe out Chernobog entirely with the Catastrophe — a proclamation that the age of the Infected has arrived.
4. Beneath the Catastrophe
Massive meteorites begin raining down from the sky. Buildings collapse, and Reunion soldiers scream as they're reduced to ash.
Just as falling rubble is about to hit a Medic, the Doctor throws himself forward and shoves her out of the way — putting himself in danger instead.
Nearl rushes in with her shield raised to cover the Doctor. Even as her armor scorches and her shield shakes, she shouts at him to run, to run now.
No matter what happens, I won't allow the Doctor to be hurt. Especially not right in front of my eyes!
Once the danger passes, Nearl scolds the Doctor — don't do something that reckless alone. From now on, take her along at least, she says; she'll protect him.
The first wave of the Catastrophe barely passes. The meteorites thin out, and every Operator gets away with only minor injuries. For a moment, relief that everyone survived washes over them.
But Reunion crawls back out from the ruins everywhere. This isn't pursuit — it's simply the number that survived the Catastrophe.
Even with more than half wiped out, there are still enough left to overwhelm Rhodes Island. Even Nearl is stunned — where on earth did Reunion gather so many Infected?
With numbers like this, they might actually be able to take Chernobog, Dobermann mutters bitterly. Just where did Reunion pull together so many Infected?

From within the encirclement, a single figure walks toward them alone. Nearl catches the scent of steel, sulfur, something burning. If this were meant to be an envoy, the footsteps are far too ominous.
The tyrant of Reunion. Amiya quietly speaks the name from the files.
A flame that will burn the whole land…… is that it.
5. Talulah
Her name is **Talulah**. When she gathers heat at her fingertips, the air around her shimmers like a heat haze, and everything it touches melts away.
Nearl tells Amiya to take the Doctor and flee immediately. Left unchecked, that monster will turn the entire rescue team to ash. But Amiya doesn't back down.
When Talulah quietly murmurs, "Be quiet," Nearl's armor is shredded in an instant. Even so, when Dobermann tells her to fall back, Nearl shouts back for her to fall back instead.
Talulah declares that Chernobog has been liberated. Her goal is already achieved, she says. Resistance may let hope sprout in this land, but it cannot change your fate.
Still, she shows interest in Rhodes Island, saying they have the makings of liberators. But she doesn't like it — they must pay the price for not standing on the true side of the Infected.
Let me give you an ending, in the way I like best. ……Perish.

blocks.cap: "Perish." — Heat that could swallow the entire plaza whole is unleashed from Talulah's fingertips.

blocks.x: Nearl lunges forward to block it, but it's too late. In that instant, Amiya steps in front of everyone.
Amiya raises a barrier of shadow-like power, single-handedly holding back Talulah's Arts to keep it from spilling beyond the plaza.

blocks.cap: "I can't let any of you get hurt. That's…… something I will not allow!"

blocks.x: The barrier begins to burn. Dobermann shouts urgently — at this rate, Amiya's ring, the last seal holding her back, won't hold.
Still, Amiya doesn't let go. Even if she ends up bringing disaster upon them, she can never again lose someone precious right before her eyes — even offering the Doctor an apology in advance.
Talulah murmurs an admiring "Impressive" at the sight. But Amiya's body has already reached its limit.
Nearl also tries to wring out her last strength and charge in, reciting a knight's vow to devote her body to Kazimierz's light. Dobermann shouts at the Doctor to go now — they'll help Amiya.
Then Ace stands beside Amiya. You've already done more than enough, she says — now let us carry this together.
Let us share your pain, too.
Ace tells Dobermann to take everyone and go on ahead, saying she'll follow soon. But no one believes it.
To the Doctor, who has lost his memories, Ace confides one last thing. He doesn't remember her, but she remembers exactly what kind of person he was.
Someday, you and Amiya will have to stand against this cruel land. So watch over Amiya well, Doctor.
6. Those Left Behind
Nearl and Dobermann break through the encirclement with Amiya and the Doctor, carrying the unconscious Amiya on their back.

blocks.cap: A small few who broke through the encirclement. The names of those left behind can't be told to Amiya just yet.

blocks.x: When Nearl tries to say something, Dobermann quietly stops her — Amiya mustn't hear it. She's already carrying far too much.
This is a path their comrades opened with their lives. That effort can't be wasted. Dobermann steels herself — now isn't the time to grieve.
Then she mutters bitterly to herself. Now that she thinks about it, not a single one of the people who ever told her not to worry has come back.

When Amiya wakes, she senses something's wrong. She insists she only blacked out for a moment and can walk herself, but Ace and the others are nowhere to be seen. Still, she doesn't press further. She tells herself Ace will be fine — everyone at Rhodes Island is strong, after all.
The southern exit is right ahead. As she walks, Amiya asks the Doctor if she can lean on him, just for a moment. Just a moment, just for a little while.
7. The Woman Blocking the Exit
They finally reach the exit, only for someone to block the way. Not one of Talulah's subordinates, not a guard — a woman who calls herself **W**.
W says she's been waiting here not for Rhodes Island, but to meet the Doctor. She has something to ask him, she says, and asks that he be handed over — calling him by name.

W mentions offhandedly that she ran into a scouting team on her way here, disguised well enough to fool even Ursusans. Amiya feels a flicker of relief, hoping they're safe — but quickly grasps the real meaning behind those words.
W asks Amiya what kind of magic she used to turn people into subordinates willing to gladly lay down their lives. Whether those people are even worth the sacrifice, to her.
That was the one thing Amiya couldn't bear to hear.
Every human life has worth…… and you have no right to insult that!
Nearl steps forward to protect the Doctor, but W stays relaxed, saying she's no match for Talulah and isn't a defense specialist anyway — as if she just wants to talk with the Doctor.
After a brief clash, W realizes something. "Ah, ah, haha…… so that's how it is…… now I remember, Amiya." Then she steps back, saying they can go now that she's gotten what she wanted.
Reunion withdraws as well, on Talulah's orders. W, saying she can't stand being bored, leaves them with a promise to meet again — to Amiya, and to the Doctor.
Next time, I'll make you tell me the truth yourself, Doctor.
8. The Last Two

Around that time, one Operator left behind in the plaza finally comes to. He blames himself, saying he could do nothing but scream through the hell of watching that monster called Talulah reduce everyone to ash single-handedly.

He'd watched Guard Operators get flung aside like chess pieces, Defenders crushed to death like butter. That monster itself was the Catastrophe made flesh, the subordinate repeats in a trembling voice.
The one who saved him with emergency first aid was Ace, who had already lost one arm. She still has the other one, she says, and she'll use it to go stop Talulah.
The subordinate begs her to flee, but Ace doesn't budge. She can't run until the Doctor and Amiya's safety is secured.
Your life cost me one arm. Even if all I bought you was one more minute, I believe your life was worth that much.
Leaving behind a promise to return soon, Ace walks back toward the monster, telling him to hold on. The Operator left behind closes his eyes, hoping Amiya will fulfill everyone's wish.
In a place where half the street had turned to charcoal and even steel had melted, someone was still fighting. Persistent enough that even Talulah murmured, "I'll remember this, Rhodes Island."
Epilogue — Not Yet, These Tears
Among the group that made it out, a Medic finally breaks down in tears. Amiya sits beside her and quietly passes on words she once heard herself.
Tears…… have to be saved until the war is over. Right now, it's still…… not allowed.
On the way back, Amiya volunteers to escort the wounded Operators at the rear, repeating only that she's fine. Even to a worried Nearl, she just says she's okay.
Amiya still doesn't know the exact names of the comrades left behind. She has her guesses, but can't bring herself to ask — she can only keep walking forward.

In escaping through the last hour before the Catastrophe, Nearl protected the Doctor, Amiya held everyone safe behind her barrier, and Ace and nameless Operators stayed behind — all to get the Doctor and Amiya to the southern exit.
And so Rhodes Island turns its back on burning Chernobog, tears set aside until the war ends, heading toward the place they'll return to.

blocks.cap: "Let's go…… let's go home…… to Rhodes Island."

main_10.tagline: A story of the rootless fighting over Londinium, each staking their own idea of 'home.' The Sarkaz swallow the city to claim a home; the Victorians hold on to reclaim theirs; and Amiya goes to see for herself what anger and grief have gathered at that war's heart. And standing there, at its heart, was someone she thought she'd lost.

blocks.x: In the west of Terra, Victoria — once ruled by the Lion monarchy — has been wracked by the Grand Dukes' struggle for the throne for over twenty years since His Majesty's passing.

Amid that chaos, the Sarkaz from Kazdel swallowed the capital, Londinium, whole. Regent King Theresis's army occupies the city, while outside its walls, the Grand Dukes' armies watch each other warily, eyes fixed only on the ramparts.
This is a war fought by the rootless, each staking their own idea of 'home.' To see the heart of that war for themselves, Rhodes Island quietly makes its way into the city.
1. The Tower That Summons the Storm

blocks.cap: At the heart of Londinium, the great tower 'The Shard' rises. Toward its peak, a storm carrying the Sarkaz's grudge gathers.

blocks.x: In the heart of Londinium, Sarkaz Regent King **Theresis** plans to control even the storm itself with a great tower and an airship. Completion is ten days away.
At his side is the white-haired sovereign **Theresa**. She says she can hear the voice of the storm gathering at the tower's peak — the grudges of countless Sarkaz ghosts.

Theresis's dream is simple. Through this war, make sure neither Victoria nor Ursus will dare eye Kazdel again for a hundred years — and finally give the Sarkaz, who have had their home stolen from them every two hundred years, a real home at last.
If the Sarkaz want war, then the Sarkaz are war itself…… and once the war ends, the Sarkaz will surely have a home to return to.
Theresa has no objection. The voices in her head give her no other option. But she quietly asks — when the first bolt of lightning falls, isn't he afraid the flame will burn him too?
And Theresis adds one more thing: Rhodes Island is coming.
2. The Road Home
An abandoned mining site 527 km from Londinium. Kal'tsit's flagship is docked there, and Amiya and the Doctor approach the city with the Operators, disguised as a 'scrap recovery company.'

The advance team is the Glasgow gang: boss **Siege**, muscle **Indra**, brains **Morgan**, and former Tower knight **Dagda**. For Siege, a Londinium native, this is her first homecoming in five years.
They rescue a Londinium citizen named 'Thomas,' kidnapped by the Dublin rebels — their guide who will get them into the city.

But something's off about Thomas. He treats Amiya, whom he's meeting for the first time, like someone he's long been waiting for, his emotions subtly out of sync. Amiya swallows her unease and heads for the city anyway.

blocks.cap: "Time to go home." The disguised squad blends into the crowd, moving toward the airtight wall's inner side.

blocks.x: 3. Heads Down
As they reach the gate, citizens are pouring out of the city in the opposite direction. Ever since the Sarkaz started knocking on the door, everyone has been risking their lives to abandon Londinium.
Within that crowd is another spark of resistance. Victorian Lieutenant **Horn**. She pulls captured fellow soldiers out one by one, leading them past the Sarkaz's watch with the words, "Heads down."
Horn's goal isn't killing more enemies. First priority: survival. Second priority: more people's survival. A dying subordinate apologizes to her — sorry, but please, survive.
Now that Londinium, once their home, has become a prison, the soldiers have realized: even an honorable death is a luxury, and living is far harder than dying.

At the gate, a Sarkaz patrol, Dublin, and Rhodes Island collide. A chaotic melee breaks out with civilians caught in the middle, and Siege, unable to just stand by, shifts the operation to rescuing citizens.

Just then, lightning-like cannon fire rains down from the wall. Sarkaz general **Manfred** has turned the muzzle of the great cannon that once defended the city — the Wall Cannon — toward the city itself.

blocks.cap: For seventy years, the Wall Cannon aimed at outside enemies. Now, for the first time, it spits fire over the heads of Londinium's own citizens.

blocks.x: In that inferno, Thomas vanishes. It's later revealed he was a Sarkaz spy who wears the faces of the dead — he'd faked being 'rescued' to observe Amiya up close, then slipped away pretending to die in the blast.
4. The City's Veins
With nowhere to escape the bombardment, an unknown local appears before Rhodes Island and leads the group underground — into the vast pipelines stretching across the city, Londinium's 'veins.'

blocks.cap: Even without light, Londinium is alive. The machinery's roar is its throbbing blood; the turning gears, its steady breath.

blocks.x: The ones who led them here are **Fist** and **Rockrock** — the Londinium citizen Vigilante Corps. A resistance of ordinary people that has held on: for every one they take, ten new members join.
Their commander, **Clovisia**, is surprisingly young. Before anxious fighters in the meeting hall, she rests a slender hand on the table and silences the room with a single sentence.
We never, ever abandon a comrade.

blocks.cap: Slender shoulders carrying everyone's heavy hope. At the strangely familiar sight, the Operators, as if by agreement, all turn to look at Amiya.

blocks.x: Still, Rockrock never lets his guard down around the Sarkaz Closure. On the day his father was beaten to death by mercenaries, he saw a white-haired Sarkaz woman whom the group called 'Your Highness.' Rockrock can never forget that face.
Hearing this, Amiya's heart wavers. A white-haired woman with a sorrowful expression. Amiya says quietly that the person from whom she inherited her ideals passed away four years ago.
5. An Old Friend from the Wastes
Meanwhile, the old Sarkaz hero Nachzehrer King visits Kal'tsit's flagship in the wastes, demanding to know what killed the last pure-blooded Wendigo.
Instead of fighting, Kal'tsit gives him an answer: she was a witness to one Wendigo's soul returning to Kazdel. The old vampire accepts the answer and withdraws.
There's only one reason he let Rhodes Island go: Amiya. Even that wily old Sarkaz was curious what the Black Crown's heir would show him in Londinium.

Kal'tsit has no intention of persuading the monarchy. She simply doesn't want to watch war erupt before her eyes, or see meaningless sacrifice continue. Victorian or Sarkaz, enough blood has already been spilled.

On this journey, Rhodes Island also parts ways with a few longtime comrades. Shining and Nightingale go their separate ways to reclaim something they've lost, leaving word that they'll return whenever they're needed.
6. Raid on the Jelly Factory
Joining forces with the Vigilante Corps, Rhodes Island goes to rescue people trapped in an abandoned chemical factory. Inside is Kal'tsit's messenger and the Vigilante Corps's strategist, **Heidi**.

blocks.cap: Three entrances are stormed at once. But all of this is unfolding on top of a trap Manfred laid in advance.

blocks.x: The rescue comes at a heavy cost. Vigilante Corps fighters fall one by one, and near-massacre-level Originium Arts turn the corridors into a slaughterhouse. Even so, people carry each other forward.

Into that chaos, demolitions expert **W**, sent by Kal'tsit, appears and pulls Heidi out. And blocking her path is Manfred's mercenary **Hoederer**. The two are old comrades who know each other far too well.
In truth, Hoederer was once a Babel spy who, alongside now-dead friends, targeted Theresis's heart. But having lost an eye and many comrades, he had already paid the price he owed.

That spy, the Sarkaz who wears the faces of the dead, also appears in another form — the fighter 'Bill,' who was like a brother to Rockrock. But Fist realizes he's a fake because of a toy Metal Crab he'd made as a gift for Bill.
Because the real Bill would never have overlooked that gift. The exposed spy retreats, leaving one last line: Bill wanted all of you to survive. That was his final message.
7. Mandragora's Final Stand
That same night, Dublin commander **Mandragora** also infiltrates the factory, to rescue an old compatriot held by the Sarkaz — spy 'Killian.'
She's a Taran born in the cracks of the city — people treated as lower than even the Sarkaz, who, once black stone sprouts on their bodies, are thrown into the sewers to become food for Metal Crabs.
Thirteen deaths she has counted. She has endured, vowing to repay those thirteen lives twofold someday, but the 'Leader' she served had abandoned her long before.
Killian, breathing his last in her arms, gives one final plea: don't go to the Leader. Before Mandragora, left alone, Manfred's blade draws near.
Knowing she can't win, Mandragora rises again with her broken Arts unit. Not because of any order.
Simply…… because I want to.

blocks.cap: On the cooling floor, with her last strength, she reaches out to an old friend who has already lost his form. "No one's chasing us anymore. Let's go home."

blocks.x: 8. A Bloody Hunt, and a Button
Vampire King Sanguinaire pursues the Vigilante Corps as they retreat underground. Not for honor, not for combat. To him, people are merely prey whose scent of blood is worth recording.

blocks.cap: No fangs, no tentacles. A face as elegant as a young noble's. Only, a sea of blood beneath his feet.

blocks.x: Fleeing, Siege stops and tries to face him head-on, knowing she can't win. If the city above is going to fall, she says, she wants to be the first to embrace it.

In that moment, beneath the dust on the pipe wall, a button glows. The very button she first pressed at age three, carried on her teacher's back. Londinium's veins stretch out once more, toward its future king.

blocks.cap: The button, its dust wiped away. Siege knows exactly what it is. This city recognizes her.

blocks.x: The passage moves upward, opening an escape route. Siege was more than just a Londinium native. She was the true heir the city responds to.
9. The Strong, High Wall
To stop the bombardment, the control room atop the wall must be destroyed. Misery rends space to lift Amiya and the Doctor onto the wall, where Manfred is waiting.

Manfred is not a man who enjoys slaughter. He knows better than anyone the curse of Oripathy, the end of compatriots scattering into crystal. He simply believes Theresis is the only one who can give the Sarkaz a home, and he'll do anything for that belief.
From him, Amiya reads only cold wariness. He doesn't see Amiya as an heir, or as an object of curiosity. He only sees a 'dangerous enemy' to be eliminated.

Even so, Amiya doesn't back down. The fire that has burned in the Sarkaz's hearts for ten thousand years, she says, burns just the same within her own heart now — a fire more real and hotter than any Arts illusion.
Breaking that tense standoff, Victorian soldiers in tattered uniforms climb onto the wall. Horn and the soldiers she's protected, this time with no disguise at all.

blocks.cap: Regulation sabers, homemade crossbows, armor stained with comrades' blood. Their weapons and uniforms are all different, but their expressions are one: they won't retreat unless they fall.

blocks.x: To Manfred, who invokes the myth of "impregnable Londinium," Horn laughs. Isn't that legend even more laughable, she says, with a man like him standing right here?
Look. We're still standing here.

When her shield breaks, Horn takes up a sword; when she no longer even has the strength to hold a sword, she holds on through sheer will. At last, the control room explodes, a corner of the wall collapses, and the Wall Cannon falls silent.
Fatally wounded and falling from the wall, Horn is caught and pulled up by Roven and Misery. Her fight is not yet over.

Meanwhile, Siege sets Dagda free — don't be bound by an inherited vow, she says, find on your own who's truly worth your loyalty. Dagda, who had left, returns at the decisive moment leading noble reinforcements, opening an escape route for her comrades.
The Vigilante Corps and citizens board the recaptured train, and Rockrock, having gotten his brother Bill back, breaks into tears. The train carries the survivors, racing toward the city center.
10. The One Standing in the Eye of the Storm
The moment the train departs, Amiya freezes at the window. A Sarkaz walks into the ruins. The smoke scatters, the arrows fall silent, and only the wind stirs her white hair.

blocks.cap: There's no way she could see inside the train, and yet her expression seems to know exactly whose gaze is upon her. Gentle, melancholy eyes.

blocks.x: It was Theresa. The person from whom Amiya inherited her ideals, Rhodes Island, everything. The one she'd thought had passed away four years ago was standing in the ruins, now sovereign of the Sarkaz.
The true nature of the emotion that had gathered at the heart of Londinium and pressed down on Amiya finally comes into focus: the Sarkaz's endless rage, and beneath it, an endless sorrow.
Before Manfred, left behind, Theresa says calmly that she wanted to meet that child but came too late. Wiping the ash from her face, she lets slip an unfamiliar question.
That's right…… why don't I shed any tears?
Epilogue — Questions Left Hanging

In the holy royal palace, Theresis and the Confessor whisper. The one best suited to face a Devil King is another Devil King. They sent 'her' to the wall, and now they mean to get their hands on Amiya as well.
Theresis's true goal is to destroy the Black Crown itself. The Sarkaz must never be enslaved to anyone or anything — and if the Crown stands in the way, he'll tear that down too.
In the shadows, W grabs Kal'tsit and demands to know — how could she just stand by and let Theresa's body fall into Theresis's hands? Kal'tsit doesn't answer.
How could you…… how could you let Theresa's body fall into Theresis's hands!?
Meanwhile, Siege meets Alerdale, daughter of the Duke of Cumberland. It's the moment the city's noble resistance finally welcomes the true king they've spent years searching for.
Alerdale bows in greeting. Welcome home, she says, Her Highness Alexandrina. And she asks the Doctor one thing: does he have a keepsake of Edward Artorius?

Far away in the Ursus tundra, Talulah faces the undying monster Kashchey. She no longer believes killing him will solve anything. Someday, she thinks, the awakened people will cast aside their foolish rulers themselves.
And Talulah follows Nine and Reunion toward Victoria — to pay one visit to the city where the storm gathers, before returning to her final battle.

It feels like a new journey, and also like the very first starting point. The high walls are a prison and a graveyard to some, and a home of the past and future to others. Too many answers, and even more questions, lie sleeping here.

The rootless fought over Londinium, each staking their own home. The Sarkaz swallowed the city to gain a home; the Victorians stood atop a crumbling wall to reclaim theirs. And Amiya walked into the heart of a storm that swallowed both answers and questions alike, toward the person she'd thought she'd lost.

blocks.x: Victoria is a great power built of steam and steel. Flying Steam Knights were the nation's pride, and it was a land of ingenuity that fled even catastrophe aboard nomadic cities.
But now its capital, Londinium, is in the grip of Sarkaz mercenaries. On the throne sits neither a Draco nor an Aslan, but the Sarkaz regent-king, Theresis.
Rhodes Island returns to this ashen city. The Doctor and Amiya carry a single question: everyone shouts 'for Victoria' — but what, exactly, is Victoria?
1. Twenty-six years ago, the child in the attic
The story begins twenty-six years ago, at the Cumberland ducal estate. **Aledale**, a young girl who idolized the Steam Knights, slips away from her father into the attic.

blocks.cap: The dust-covered armor of the very first Steam Knight. The girl whispers to this old friend that she'll become a greater knight than her ancestors.

blocks.x: There, Aledale overhears a conspiracy by chance — whispers of those plotting to bring down the old lion, the king.
The plot's core was simple: transfer every Steam Knight to the border, then strike the king. Once the old lion was gone, they reasoned, the cub's crown wouldn't last long either.
Trying to flee out the window before she's caught, Aledale falls from the second floor. But something soft catches and lifts the girl up.

blocks.cap: Golden lions, as if walked straight out of myth. On their backs sat a young princess, the national sword clenched in her teeth.

blocks.x: A heavy voice echoes through Aledale's mind. "One day, you will meet Vina again." That very day, the king vanishes, and a 'miracle' occurs — the young princess Alexandrina appears, cradling the national sword that had gone missing.
Over the twenty-some years since, Aledale often glimpses those golden beings and that girl again in her dreams. Waiting for the day, foretold, when she meets 'Vina' once more.
2. The teacher who believed in the light
Four years ago, a small school in Osterig. The teacher **Golding** takes in poor children and teaches them letters and theater, believing that civilization can stand against violence.
But that night, a coup by the Grand Dukes sets Londinium ablaze. And the next morning, the streets are filled not with the Home Guard or Steam Knights, but with black-horned Sarkaz mercenaries.
From that day on, the Sarkaz never left Londinium, and Steam Knights were never seen on its streets again.

Golding spends over a year with the children preparing a play about a knight standing against a tyrant. As the clouds of war grow thicker, she insists — believing in beauty is what keeps you a person, not a beast.
As long as there's light, we'll keep moving toward it.

blocks.cap: A stage facing an audience of mysterious figures in an empty house. "What I follow is not a sovereign, but honesty and courage."

blocks.x: 3. The day the flag changed

The munitions plant at Highbury. Veteran representative **Catherine** submits to the Sarkaz, striving to keep even one more worker alive. To her, the plant is the pride her family built up over generations, shaping Londinium.
Strike it once, you get nothing but a lump of metal... strike it again and again, and you can forge steam armor. That's how we built Londinium.

But her grandson **Fist** can't bear the submission. He leaves the plant to join the vigilantes and stand against the Sarkaz. Catherine drives him out coldly — but really, she was afraid of losing another grandson, like Harvey, who marched out in a protest twenty-six years ago and never came back.
That day, Victoria's flag comes down off the plant roof, and the Sarkaz banner goes up. As if nothing had changed at all.
4. When the fog clears, war
In the present, Rhodes Island joins hands with the vigilantes. The black clouds covering Londinium's sky are no ordinary storm — they're an artificial catastrophe stirred up by **the Shard**.

Theresis means to use this weapon to aim war and storm at his enemies together — to borrow Victoria's own strength to destroy Victoria. Stopping this is Rhodes Island's first goal in coming to Londinium.

Theresis dreams of a future where the Sarkaz are no longer hunted, where they can finally put down roots. The future his dead sister Theresia envisioned — he means to seize it not through peace, but through struggle. Refusing to give up any possibility at all.

The operation splits in two. The Doctor, Fist, and Ascalon head to find the Sarkaz's hidden supply route, toward Highbury and the Home Guard command tower. And **Siege** sets out to recover the national sword, **King's Breath**, from the King's Rest.
Siege leads the Glasgow gang that heads the vigilante group Osterig. And she is also the princess who vanished twenty-six years ago — Alexandrina Vina Victoria herself.
Amiya reads a familiar grief in Aledale — the face of someone who's carried far too much alone. Even so, Amiya never forgets why they came here.
We came to help 'people.' Living people — and people who have the right to live.
5. Selling the armor
Bringing weapons into the city means paying a smuggler's steep price. What Aledale offers up is the last symbol of House Cumberland — the armor of the very first Steam Knight.
"House Cumberland is you, and me." Aledale tells the old butler Elshie flatly. Words like glory or honor mean nothing anymore, she says.
Siege blocks the deal — threatening the trader to keep the armor safe. She didn't want to watch Aledale lose anything more.

blocks.cap: A cramped back room, hands binding a wound. "We should've spent more time, in more places, together."

blocks.x: As she tends to the wound, the two imagine a life that could have been — tea in the garden, hunting, a tedious ball. When Siege, for the first time, puts into words a future that had always felt like fog, Aledale tells her that's exactly her greatest strength.
Only someone who knows how precious this moment is can speak of a future, she says. "Like right now."
6. A life for a life

Around then, at Highbury, plant representatives who know too much are being secretly executed. Catherine, too, is quietly hauled away — resigned that if her own life can save the others, that's enough.
But the workers, whom Catherine thought knew nothing, rise up. Those with nothing left to fear come forward on their own to rescue their representative.
Fist joins that line too — not as a vigilante, but as this plant's own grandson. Under cover from the Doctor and Ascalon, years of pent-up anger snap the thin violence like rotten wood.

At the execution ground was a young mercenary, Paprika, who had never killed anyone. Catherine hands her the yarn a dead comrade had left as a gift for the girl, and asks just what she's swinging that weapon for. Paprika, in the end, can't pull the trigger.
Once the rescue is done, Fist returns his badge to his grandmother and leaves — he's not a plant worker anymore. Catherine throws the badge right back at her grandson.

blocks.cap: The badge back in his hand. Wherever he ended up, this plant had always been his pride.

blocks.x: To me, my grandmother is the real hero. She was then, she is now, and she always will be.
7. Different paths
Not even all Sarkaz think alike. **Shining**, a confessor who turned her back on her clan, is invited to an old family dinner.

blocks.cap: The one empty seat at the long table. Kept open, always, for the traitor who fled years ago with a test subject.

blocks.x: The clan leader and her sister Salus urge her to come back. Liz, the Infected girl Shining risks her life to protect, was once their test subject, they say — and only the clan can hold her.
But Shining says Liz alone is her true family, and leaves the table, sword in her arms. Next time they meet, she says, it'll be on a battlefield.
You are not my family. Do I need to say it more plainly than that?
8. Night at the command tower

The raid on the Home Guard command tower begins. Commander Leto is a Gaul refugee who surrendered to the Sarkaz on the single hope of rebuilding his homeland, Gaul. But that hope was a weakness deceiving himself, and it drove his own soldiers into a death trap.

The vampire Sanguinaire treats Leto like a pet in a cage — telling him not to mistake it for the bird having tamed its master, choking him under the pretense of mercy. Leto has no choice but to swallow the humiliation.
At the same moment, the Cumberland estate burns in Sanguinaire's flames. Elshie, the butler who's been Aledale's only family since birth, dies in that fire.
Atop the command tower, Amiya breaks down. Through the ring Theresia left behind, the full weight of the Sarkaz's ancient sorrow and grudge pours into her at once.

Amiya sees the night, two hundred years ago, when Kazdel burned. Sarkaz slaughtered simply for being born of a different origin — and that Kal'tsit was present at that massacre, too. However well she thinks she knows Kal'tsit, faced with that memory, Amiya can't help but feel anger and grief.
Six heroes rising from the ruins charge the great army, bearing the burning banner of Kazdel. Answer, our enemy. Who are you, to declare that Kazdel deserves to fall? That cry seizes Amiya's heart.
As Amiya loses consciousness, the regent-king Theresis levels his blade at her. His goal is one thing only: killing the 'Devil' cradled in the Doctor's arms.

blocks.cap: Kal'tsit throws herself in front of the fatal blow. Something red and warm splashes across the Doctor's cheek.

blocks.x: Bloodied, Kal'tsit tells the Doctor to take Amiya and retreat, and stands alone against Theresis. "I will kill you once more, Kal'tsit."

Amid that chaos, the Banshee king **Logos** cuts through the vampire's veil of blood. What he follows, he says, is not the Devil's crown but the ideal Theresia laid out. The roots of the old monarchy have already rotted, he declares — the Sarkaz must change.
9. Where kings sleep
Meanwhile, Siege's party reaches deep underground, at the King's Rest. Behind the door opened by the Draco's key stand statues of every Victorian king who ever reigned.
But the passage held long-dried blood, and the corpses of over a hundred elite Sarkaz. And, having fallen while holding them back, dozens of shattered suits of steam armor.

blocks.cap: Armor cut by blade, burned by fire, run through by nails — and still holding the line. Not even death could bring them down.

blocks.x: Siege realizes why she never once heard steam vent through Londinium in these four years. Every Steam Knight had been here.

What happened here was no heroic legend. It was a trap — every Steam Knight lured into the King's Rest and sealed inside a Sarkaz encirclement — and the key that let them in wasn't handed over by one or two Grand Dukes, but by Victoria itself.

Dagda, too, was once a knight of the tower. After the king left, she guarded an empty palace with nothing left to protect, and was the child her mentor forced to survive before the final charge. She's never properly mourned those deaths.
Even knowing they'd been betrayed, that Dagda salutes each and every warrior who never took off their armor, tears streaming. Siege quietly wraps her arms around Dagda, trembling.
"Victoria isn't just the Parliament and the nobility — it's you, too. It's me, too. And there are still people who'll weep for them."

King's Breath carries a legend of its own. The Aslan Padishah once nearly cut down the Draco king with this blade — and after the two bloodlines sealed their pact, it was reforged into the very symbol of Victoria's glory. It's said the kings once even cleaved catastrophe itself with this sword.

blocks.cap: The blade that had always stood there, through a thousand years. King's Breath sat far more plainly than any legend.

blocks.x: 10. Don't look back
The moment Siege takes King's Breath in hand, a familiar voice calls out behind her. Asking for the sword. It was Aledale's voice.

Aledale had carried a 'mission' for some Grand Duke to take the national sword, from the very start. She'd wanted to protect the vigilantes and her friendship with Siege too, she says — but fate pushed her all the way here.
Siege rejects the word 'mission.' If the vigilantes believe in her, she's their leader; if she calls herself a friend, then that's what she is. Just then, something stirs among the wreckage.

It was the last Steam Knight — someone who watched his comrades slaughtered, and held on alone in the dark for four years, telling himself the armor filled the wound where his flesh and blood used to be. What he'd guarded was the national sword, the one single thing he called 'Victoria.'
He'd already forgotten his own name. No medicine, no light, no food — surviving on nothing but the light the sword gave him, pushing even death away, never knowing what it was he'd been loyal to.
The king was executed, and Parliament, the nobles, the people — all of them betrayed him. So he chose to believe the sword itself was Victoria, and charges at Siege for daring to take it from him.
What this sword can drive off isn't the storm — it's fear. Knight, this sword is not your Victoria.
Worn down, Aledale finally sets her mission aside. No Cumberland, no Grand Duke — just Aledale. And, true to the promise she made Elshie as a child, she chooses to face the Steam Knight herself.

blocks.cap: A raging wind drives everyone else out the door. Beyond the wreckage, only Aledale stood facing the knight.

blocks.x: I'll be the one to face you, my nightmare... my hope.
Just before the door shuts, Aledale's lips form one last word. Whether it was Vina, or Your Highness, that word was buried in the wreckage forever.
Epilogue — A storm rises
In the ashes of the ruined Cumberland estate, the warriors find House Cumberland's steam armor — the one said to have been lost to the fire, whole and intact.

blocks.cap: The old armor, pulled from the ashes. The hope this armor once held — not even the flames could take that from it.

blocks.x: Siege wishes Aledale could have seen it — that not every path was set in stone from the start. And she hopes that last Steam Knight will someday leave the darkness, and find something new worth protecting.
But the sky won't wait. The black clouds over Londinium tear apart, and it becomes clear this was no ordinary cloud at all.

blocks.cap: A colossal storm of catastrophe, unrecorded in any archive. A Sarkaz aircraft rises above Londinium, serving as its eye.

blocks.x: The Shard has activated. Under its gaze, every enemy of the Sarkaz has nowhere left to run. Theresis begins to move, beyond the wall, toward the true battlefield.

Even so, the vigilantes don't scatter. The mercenary Totter, and Home Guard soldiers rescued from the execution ground, choose to stay with Rhodes Island. They took heavy losses, but they gained one thing — intelligence on the Sarkaz supply route.

At Golding's school, the play a year in the making draws its curtain. But the children play as Steam Knights, shouting to "squeeze the Sarkaz dry." The teacher who believed civilization could win against violence breaks down, watching the age stain even the children with war.

In a distant city, Ch'en, Bagpipe, and Harmonie recognize familiar faces, and Reed leaves Rhodes Island for someone she needs to meet. And at the Duke of Wellington's estate, someone calling herself 'Her Highness of Eblana' comes calling.

Those who gave their lives for Victoria were betrayed by Victoria and buried in the dark. And even so, there were those who never took off their armor of glory. If Victoria is neither king, nor Parliament, nor nobility, then in the end it's you, and me, and those who will still weep for them. When the fog clears, war will come.

main_12.tagline: A soldier counting the days to leave, a back-alley gang guarding a boxing gym, both ground down as cogs of war on a single flying fortress. What the powerful call 'history' turns out to be a broken arm in the mud, and a stench that never fades.
