blocks.x: Long ago, someone asked **Mizuki** a question: "How do you become a better human?" Having only just escaped death, Mizuki could think of nothing then but shock.

Now, grown into a human while bearing a Seaborn's body, he was certain he could answer. So he followed the sea wind, the waves, and the guidance of **We Many**, the collective consciousness of the Seaborn, to the coast and to the old bishop's dwelling.
His doubts were soon to be settled. However.
"Mother, where are we going?"

blocks.cap: The coast where the sea wind and the waves led Mizuki.

blocks.x: 1. The Coast Where the Sea Refused Its People

Iberia was a nation brought down long ago by the **Profound Silence**, the catastrophe in which the sea swallowed the land. Now that sea was spreading onto the land once more, and the Doctor of Rhodes Island walked that coast with Mizuki.

Along the way, a funeral was underway at a cliffside cemetery. In memory, funerals in this land were burials at sea, but here the people burned the bodies, gave the ashes to the sea wind, and stood the coffins upright as gravestones.
The reason lay below the cliff. A fluorescent **Nethersea Brand** covered the sea and was creeping toward the cliffs. The people had not rejected the sea. The sea had refused them.

And all along the coast, the land was fading to an ashen white. The Seaborn's newest trick, the devouring dust, broke down everything it touched into white powder, and a city blanketed by it ceased to exist within hours.

At the edge of another cliff stood the last of Ægir's wave watchers. A fifth tsunami had passed in half a year and the hope of returning to Ægir kept shrinking, but he held his post, saying someone had to record what had happened at the heart of the sea.

Meanwhile, out on the waves, the **Last Knight**, lance in hand, was chasing the sea with his mount Rocinante. He roared that he would kill the sea that had swallowed the barley seeds, but the sea did not answer. Civilization hated him and nature cast him out. His enemy was Terra itself.

Around then, the Doctor met an Inquisitor of the **Inquisition** on a reef, one who had lost her lantern. Taking the lantern the Doctor offered, she held down something writhing in her sleeve with one hand and told them to leave quickly. She would light their way one last time.

blocks.cap: An Inquisitor leaning on her sword among the corpses of Sea Terrors.

blocks.x: 2. The Door Knew the Doctor's Face

In the meantime, nothing but bad news piled up on the communication terminal. The **Sea Terrors** were heading for land, the Penal Battalion's fleet had been wiped out, and believers of the **Church of the Deep** were attacking a fortress.

Most worrying were the **Abyssal Hunters**, who had entered Ægir aboard the Stultifera Navis. A bishop's documents that Mizuki found described a plan to deceive the Hunters, bring them to the sea, and revive 'Him,' along with research called 'Caerula' that traced the origin of the Seaborn, and a single location.
There was no time to tell anyone. The Doctor decided to descend into the deep sea with Mizuki.

blocks.cap: The Doctor and Mizuki at the mouth of a storm-lashed cave.

blocks.x: And at the place marked on the map lay a colossal carcass that never stopped growing, gnawed at by swarms of Sea Terrors. The two went inside, groped through the darkness for a long time, and at last found a laboratory that had been sealed for ages.
Mizuki could not open its heavy, locked door. But when the security system caught **the Doctor's face**, the lock released.

At the center of the garden, a giant tree spread its branches beyond the laboratory walls. Mizuki said it was His core organ. In theory He was already dead, yet He kept growing on the instinct to live, feeding We Many.

blocks.cap: A giant tree that does not stop growing even in death.

blocks.x: When Mizuki touched the bark, his body was slowly drawn into the tree. Soon the whole laboratory trembled, and He, awakened, looked at the Doctor and spoke.
Ishar-mla, will be stopped.
Then the two kept descending until they reached **Caerula Arbor**, an experimental hub set in Terra's mantle. It was the Seaborn's hatchery, and a Seaborn, too, could become part of it.

In a clean zone beside it, the Doctor saw two women asleep with their weapons in their grip. The Abyssal Hunters had gone to their sleep in human form, not as Seaborn, to the very last, and the Sea Terrors did not set foot there.

Elsewhere, on fragments of a monument fused with the Nethersea Brand, sentences surfaced and shifted without end, such as 'You will lead humanity in resisting the Seaborn, or become Seaborn and lead the species.' Mizuki stopped the Doctor from reading further. Whatever the Doctor read, We Many was reading too.
And He, standing before the singularity of evolution, asked Himself: "Who am I?" Depending on where that path ended, the sea's ending diverged.
3. "Precious Days" — The Girl Who Became a Dissonance
At the end of one path, Mizuki reached the dwelling of **Cicero**, an old Bishop of the Deep. There lay **Highmore**, a girl who had begun turning into a Seaborn and stopped partway.

Highmore had followed Cicero for years, learning from him. The old man had never given her the 'oath sworn with the Herald' she so wanted, and when he had not returned for two days, the girl opened the box and drank it.

The power filled her body but left her nothing beautiful. Grass and flowers withered wherever she stood, and even the singing voice inherited from her mother was drowned out by the call of We Many. She could accept neither We Many nor the humans who had killed her parents.

Beside her, Cicero said the child simply could not be as perfect as Mizuki. She had accepted the gift but refused to let anything be severed from herself, and so had become a dissonance in the natural world, somewhere between success and failure.

Mizuki answered that a future which rejects such weak individuals could not be called the evolution of humanity. It was Mizuki's answer to the very question Cicero had once asked him, about becoming a better human.
I will let Highmore live.
Satisfied with that answer, Cicero left, saying that as long as Mizuki did not stray from his path, they would meet again.

When Highmore woke, Mizuki was grilling, on skewers, the tissue that had fallen from her body. He had cut away all the tissue that had proliferated without completing its evolution, he said, so now she could live like an ordinary person.

blocks.cap: Mizuki and Highmore before a campfire at dusk.

blocks.x: Highmore said she had nothing left, and Mizuki asked whether the things she loved, the very things that had kept her from becoming Seaborn, were not reason enough to live. Then he said he knew a place with good people and plenty of good food, and asked her to come with him. After a long while, Highmore answered, "Okay."

Meanwhile, **Ulpianus** of the Abyssal Hunters, in pursuit of Cicero, found his laboratory. The letters there named Bishops of the Deep hidden throughout Ægir, and recorded that the nature of **Ishar-mla** still remained in the body of the Hunter who had slain Him.

The bishops meant to send that Hunter back to the sea and awaken Ishar-mla once more. Before Ulpianus could finish reading, seawater and Sea Terrors flooded the laboratory, and he raised his anchor. As long as he lived, he would not allow it.
4. "Age of the Silence" — The Knight Charged, Laughing
On another path, the Last Knight appeared before a groaning Mizuki.
In that instant, every sound vanished. At the end of the silence, the waves towered up, and Ishar-mla emerged at the head of We Many.

The knight leveled his lance across the sea and roared. The Seaborn instinct, which rejects fighting among kin, set his arms shaking, but he believed it was ecstasy. The monster before him was the source of the terrible waves he had sought for so long.

blocks.cap: The Last Knight before the source of the terrible waves.

blocks.x: The waves pressed down on his lance and the currents dragged him toward land. The whole world stood in his way, yet in the silence the madman laughed aloud and charged with all his strength.
And the knight fell before Ishar-mla. The Profound Silence swallowed every coastline, every sound in Terra vanished, and the armies of nation after nation collapsed before the Seaborn tide.

Afterward, **Kal'tsit** of Rhodes Island pleaded with the Feranmuts and made pacts with the Beast Aristocrats, and at last built humanity's final city. But the city could not take in every survivor, so its gates had to close once it was full, and Amiya wept over it many times.

There was something Kal'tsit did not know. Far away, in Iberia's old Royal Court, Ishar-mla was reaching across space to 'gaze' at the Doctor by Kal'tsit's side. That gaze was the only humanity Ishar-mla had left.
**Skadi** could never have imagined that the comfort she found in her own bonds would drive an entire species to ruin. Not until humanity was reduced to one last individual: the Doctor.

Meanwhile, Mizuki was swimming toward land with the Doctor on his back. Ishar-mla's pheromones demanded that he leave this human behind, but even Mizuki, who cared nothing for humanity's fate, knew that the Doctor did not want humanity to perish.
Breaking through his kin's blockade, Mizuki set the Doctor down on the shore and, smiling, told them to go back and tell their companions. He would try to hold back the Seaborn himself.
I am also Seaborn. They will believe me.

Once the Doctor was gone, Mizuki released pheromones of hostility toward the whole of We Many. The Seaborn swarmed him all at once, and that hostility lingered long in the consciousness of We Many, like a drop of blood on white paper. And at last, he too dissipated.

Sinking deep, Mizuki's body unraveled into a jellyfish-like form, and his core organ, its last strength spent, stopped beating. Death came quietly. His shriveled, regressed body became a single small cell drifting on the currents.
The cell came to rest on the remains of a Seaborn progenitor long dead, the **Creeping Branch**. Just as a young Seaborn moved to swallow it, a withered branch wrapped Mizuki in layer upon layer.
Years later, deep blue leaves sprouted from that withered branch.
5. "Price of Peace" — The Beach That Glows Every Year

On yet another path, Mizuki merged with the Creeping Branch, which had lost its consciousness, and used that power to challenge the 'Corrupting Heart.' It was the first battle between **Firstborn** since the birth of the new world, and the defeated Ishar-mla became a nameless member of We Many.

But Mizuki felt no joy. Before his eyes, another Firstborn, the 'Primordial Lifespring' that had caused the Profound Silence, was going mad. The Bishops of the Deep had driven it mad again to awaken the Corrupting Heart sleeping within Skadi.

The Lifespring, a mass of microorganisms that was one with the sea, could not be felled unless the sea ran dry. Even if Mizuki kept We Many away from the land, that restraint would give way someday, in ten years or in a generation, no one could say. All he could do was keep his promise to the Doctor before he lost his self and his humanity.

blocks.cap: Mizuki stepping into a sea stained crimson.

blocks.x: Mizuki entered the sea. As he reshaped his body into the same form as the Lifespring and soothed the madness of his kin, deep blue spread through the crimson sea, and his human body slowly faded away.
At the last moment, he turned to look at the land, and a single person's figure was reflected in his eyes. In the next moment the tide surged in, and no trace of Mizuki could be found.
The Seaborn returned to the depths, and people cheered a historic victory. And so a pharmaceutical company forever lost a trusted companion.
And the years passed. Every year, on one special day, the Doctor visited an empty Iberian beach, escorted by **Tulip**, Rhodes Island's chief officer in Iberia.
At night, the seawater there glowed with a deep blue fluorescence. An operator had calmed the tides but never returned, and all he left behind was this tide of light that appeared every year.

blocks.cap: A night beach glowing with deep blue fluorescence.

blocks.x: Will Mizuki hear? He will. Believing so, the Doctor told the sea everything, and a wave that struck their ankles as if to hold on before receding left a deep blue glow on their boots.

Meanwhile, the defeated Ishar-mla sealed Himself away, and Skadi's consciousness rose to the surface. Loathing her kin without knowing why, she swam toward land, and the moment she saw the back of a hooded figure on the beach, every memory came rushing back like a wave.
Father, mother, brothers and sisters. Ulpianus, Laurentina, Gladiia. Skadi remembered everything, and had lost everything.
Even if the Doctor forgave her, she could not forgive herself. Hidden in the waves, she sang as she wept, and the song she had perfected over thousands of renditions was broken like shattered glass.
On the beach, the Doctor suddenly looked back at the sea. There was only the sound of the waves.
6. "Stella Caerula" — From Mizuki to 'Mizuki'

On the last path, the human self handed its emotions, desires, and thoughts to the inhuman self, and He accepted all of it. He sculpted Mizuki's new body and gently laid that body, which housed a human soul, on a reef by the shore.

Waking, Mizuki welcomed the damp air and the warmth of the sunlight. When a tentacle tapped his head in a friendly way, he remembered there was one thing left to do before returning to the world: Mizuki bidding farewell to 'Mizuki.'
There never was a dull moment with you around. Thank you. …… Then, this is goodbye.

He answered in the Seaborn way. With a roar, holes opened in the earth, and Seaborn all across Terra rose into the sky at once. Even the mountain-sized Firstborn swam off toward the far side of the sky.

blocks.cap: Seaborn swimming up into the sky.

blocks.x: "O Mother, we have found our answer." We Many, born of the sea, departed for the sea once more, for the endless, shining sea of stars.
And on the land the Seaborn left behind, neither Originium nor wasteland remained. Plants covered the earth, and the slumbering Feranmuts awoke and roamed.

Mizuki set out to find humanity's last city, but all that remained in his memories of hundreds and thousands of years was the one person he had trusted most, who had brought him to the laboratory, and high walls. He lit fires in many places, carved messages, and waited on a mountain.
One night, a Liberi held a knife to his throat, and her insignia bore a tower emblem and small lettering. Rhodes Island.

Following the map he was given, Mizuki reached the last city. Before the Rhodes Island headquarters, which looked like the wreck of a nomadic plate, he hesitated for a long while, and when he finally stepped into the lobby, he heard a familiar voice.
You're back.

Apart from her clothes, Kal'tsit had not changed at all. When Mizuki said he too must be a villain for leaving humanity this diminished, Kal'tsit answered that the Doctor's plan to preserve the species by sacrificing the majority had been insane, but in the end the most rational choice.

Mizuki asked after the Doctor and immediately regretted it. Kal'tsit answered without a change of expression: still alive. The Sarcophagus that powered the city was also sustaining the Doctor's life, and Mizuki slumped into his chair, beaming.
Kal'tsit did not tell him that the Sarcophagus could heal wounds but not erase aging, and that as the Doctor's sleeps grew longer, that life too would eventually go out.

Years later, humanity reached the shore once more. A girl found a flower-like Seaborn hatchling asleep on the sand and offered it food, and the tentacle raised to strike stopped in midair and took it.
In that moment, from the seabed to the starry sky, a new view arose throughout We Many. **Humanity is no longer a threat. We can coexist with humans.**
7. Those Who Entrusted Their Lanterns
Beside the sea, records of other paths remain as well. In them, the Profound Silence did swallow the coast in the end, and people faced it each in their own way.

**Thorns**, an Ægir-born swordsman, did not leave even after the coastline collapsed, and there he came face to face with his former mentor, now a pure Seaborn: the Iberian missionary who had taught him. "What a joyous reunion, my child." Thorns slowly raised his sword and pointed it at his teacher.

On the last day, when the city fell, he stood alone on the coast holding a fluorescent reagent made from his teacher's body. He was confident he could keep his self, and even if he lost, there was the Doctor, who knew all his weaknesses. Slowly, he pushed his homeland into his own body.

In a cave in another record, an Inquisitor in a black cloak was leading a soldier and an Ægir. The soldier, suspecting her of being Seaborn, lunged at her and fell to her rapier, bleeding deep blue fluid, and at the exit, a tentacle showed beneath her cloak.
She entrusted the Inquisitor's lantern to the Ægir, saying Iberia's road ahead needed more light. "I am **Irene**, an Iberian." Then she walked toward the pitch-black sea.

In yet another record, **Jordi**, an Ægir secretary remaining in Iberia's last stronghold, typed into the missing persons list with trembling hands: "**Carmen** I Iberia - Confirmed Dead." It was his teacher's name.

Irene, now a High Inquisitor, gathered every Inquisitor's lantern they had recovered and forged them into a single new lantern. She entrusted it to Jordi, telling him the lantern was not a weapon but hope, and asking him to remember it and pass it on. The Seaborn she went out to slay bore the codename 'Gladiia.'

Years later, the aged Jordi set out to see the sea in the peace that We Many permitted. Sitting on a cliff, he told the sea the story of his life: Gran Faro, Ægir, Stultifera Navis, the Abyssal Hunters... and death and parting, shame and peace.
When Sea Terrors tangled together to form a small boat for him, Jordi smiled and shook his head. "You're wrong. I'm sorry, but you lost."
The sounds of wind, waves, and clashing shells merged into one and answered. "Goodbye, Jordi Fontanarossa."
8. How Many Are Left?

The Abyssal Hunters each had their own endings too. In one record, Ishar-mla's voice finally fell silent, but in the sea where that deplorable god, who had also been her dearest comrade, died, only Consul **Gladiia** survived. At the last moment, Ulpianus had given his chance of survival to her.

Seated on the seabed, no longer able to swim, she was watched over by the Seaborn like pilgrims. We Many wished for her to submit, but she believed death was not necessarily meaningless. And she put a question to We Many, who always answer the questions of their kin.
How many are left?

And **Laurentina**, in her endless 'ball' with the Seaborn, began to search her memory for her old partner, then stopped. At the end of that record, 'she,' who had forgotten even her own name, carved away a white stone on the seabed with a rotted weapon, and the waves washed away both the stone and her shadow.

Skadi, too, had many worlds. In a world where Ægir became part of We Many, she sang songs of embrace to young Seaborn; in a world where every Hunter had mutated, her song became a growl and remained only in her head.

And in a peaceful world, living alone and tending the seabed lights, she saw an unfamiliar self on a broken monument, carrying a greatsword. It was the Skadi who slaughtered Leviathans and lay in wait among the reefs under Ulpianus's command.
9. A Friend Who Chose Differently

Some paths were darker still. In a world where the Primordial Lifespring devoured the Firstborn and turned Terra into a Seaborn utopia, Mizuki and the 'Doctor' hid in a cave so as not to be swallowed by the order.

When everything had been turned into part of the Lifespring and nothing edible remained, Mizuki fed the Doctor tentacles cut from his own body. He hoped that in another world, the Doctor would not fall into an irreversible end like his.

And at some point, the thoughts of another 'Him' began to surface in Mizuki's mind like probabilities. Mizuki refused both the regret and the relief they might bring. He was only a reference case left by a friend who had made a different choice, and Mizuki even gave Him a name that came to mind while playing a game.
It would be years later that Mizuki told the Doctor about it, shared the other possibility that had almost become reality, and came to face the problems beyond the sea together with them.

"How do you become a better human?" Mizuki, who had come to the shore carrying that question, left a different answer on each path. He let Highmore live, sent the Doctor back to land, and said thank you to another self departing for the sea of stars.
"Mother, where are we going?" On one path, We Many chose the sea of stars as its answer, and the small Seaborn left on the shore accepted the food a girl held out.

rogue_3.tagline: An expedition enters Sami to see the end of the Endless Icefield and, guided by a Cyclops who foresees only misfortune, at last stands before a ring-shaped gate. The land asks: will you still go on?

chars.name: Magallan
chars.desc: A member of the joint expedition team. She surveys Sami and the icefield with her drones.

chars.name: Valarqvin
chars.desc: A Sarkaz Cyclops living in seclusion in the mountains of northern Sami. The expedition's guide.

chars.name: Typhon
chars.desc: A Sarkaz hunter of Sami. She escorts the expedition.

chars.name: Santalla
chars.desc: A Sami shaman who once served an old tree. She commands the blizzard.

chars.name: Eikthyrnir
chars.desc: The Snowpriest who leads the Warriors of the North. He does not fear the Cyclopes' prophecies.

chars.name: Maryam
chars.desc: A Kuranta explorer of Rhine Lab's Scientific Investigation Section. He walks with a wooden cane.

chars.name: Amma
chars.desc: A great pure-white hornbeast dwelling in the forests of Sami. Typhon calls it Grandmother.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: A doctor of Rhodes Island. She is involved in restoring the icefield's megastructure.

chars.name: Muelsyse
chars.desc: An Elf researcher at Rhine Lab. She shapes manifolds out of water.

chars.name: Angelina
chars.desc: A Messenger from Siracusa. She can read Sami's script.

terms.name: Endless Icefield
terms.desc: The icefield north of Sami, beyond the Fjal Vetrtonn. No one has ever seen its end.

terms.name: Clan Tree
terms.desc: A giant tree that a Sami tribe reveres and lives beneath. It migrates on foot.

terms.name: Foldartal
terms.desc: A tablet carved with Sami's revelations. Shamans and Snowpriests decipher them.

terms.name: Cyclops
terms.desc: A Sarkaz lineage who see the future. Rumor says they bring misfortune.

terms.name: Disaster
terms.desc: A calamity that stains the snowfields black and eats away at Sami. Southern scholars call it Collapsal.

terms.name: Warriors of the North
terms.desc: Sami warriors who have built walls in the Fjal Vetrtonn to hold back the Disaster.

terms.name: Megastructure
terms.desc: A giant ring-shaped structure rising at the edge of the icefield.

terms.name: Black Hole Protocol
terms.desc: A covenant among the nations of Terra to jointly study and restore the icefield's megastructure.

terms.name: Foehn Hotlands
terms.desc: A land of death at the southernmost edge of Terra. A zone of yellow sand where even time is tangled.

blocks.x: In **Sami**, the land of the far north, the forest, the snow and the wind are gods. North of it, beyond the Fjal Vetrtonn, lies the **Endless Icefield**, whose end no one has ever seen.

blocks.cap: Rings rising above the silver-white icefield. Where the expeditioners are headed.

blocks.x: On the twelfth day since the joint expedition team entered Sami, expedition member **Magallan** switched on her recorder. Thanks to two Sami friends, the journey was still going smoothly, she recorded, and the group would soon meet a remarkable prophet.
A large shadow was faintly visible in the fog. A Cyclops said to see misfortune was waiting to be their guide.
Reasoning and calculation no longer meant anything. The expeditioner set foot on the frozen earth and kept walking toward the fate that waited ahead.
1. I Will See It With My Own Eyes

Some months earlier, **Maryam**, a Kuranta explorer of Rhine Lab's Scientific Investigation Section, returned to headquarters in Trimounts and went to the office of Rhine Lab's Control. What he set down was a proposal for the largest polar expedition ever attempted: a team of fifteen.

Control, **Kristen**, asked whether he would give up if no one agreed. Maryam, a man of few words, gave a short laugh and only pointed at the application. Even if no one had approved, he would have taken up his wooden cane and set out for that horizon.
Kristen said she had met a being that could almost be called an omniscient 'god,' and offered to share what she had heard about the end of the icefield.
Then, at a research station. After hours of talk, the expedition accepted **Valarqvin**, a Sarkaz Cyclops living in seclusion in the mountains of northern Sami, as its guide.

When Maryam asked whether she had ever reached the end of the icefield, Valarqvin answered only that she could tell them of the dangers she had foreseen. Prophet. Omniscient. Maryam laughed, which he rarely did.
This isn't the first time someone has tried to tell me what the end of the Endless Icefield looks like. But I'll pass. I intend to see it with my own eyes.

blocks.cap: An expedition member checks the instruments laid out from an open equipment case.

blocks.x: 2. A Land That Waits to Be Found

In Sami, the **Clan Trees** walk on their own when they migrate, and shamans and Snowpriests read Sami's will in the patterns exposed when the bark splits. Those revelations are carved onto the Foldartals.
One shaman told the expedition that the gods dwell in all things, and that the first Foldartal was a cry that spread across the mountains and fields.

blocks.cap: A Clan Tree sunk in the middle of a swamp. Sami merchants gather on its trunk, on its roots and at the swamp's edge.

blocks.x: In that land, Magallan remembered something she had heard during her training at the Exploration Society: that before Sami, everyone is a child, and that Sami is waiting for someone to find It.
Deep in the forest slept **Amma**, a great pure-white hornbeast. It did not seem to live in the forest; rather, the forest seemed to exist so that It could rest.
**Typhon**, the Sarkaz hunter escorting the expedition, called Amma 'Grandmother.' She believed that all things in Sami speak through dreams, and she called Valarqvin by the name Arges.
Fate is like a snowball. The higher it falls from, the longer it takes to hit the ground. That's what Arges says.
3. Black Snow

But Sami had an enemy it had fought for a thousand years: the **Disaster**, which stains the snowfield black and swallows beasts and people alike. People also called them demons, and southern scholars called them Collapsals.

The forest was strewn with the carcasses of beasts covered in murky snow. When the expedition described what they had seen, the Sami warriors looked as though they knew what it was, but said not a word to outsiders.

blocks.cap: Beasts fallen beside a stream running black.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, in the Fjal Vetrtonn stood the walls of the **Warriors of the North**, who held back the Disaster. Their leader, the Snowpriest **Eikthyrnir**, was worthy to speak with Sami, and Sami answered nearly all of his questions.
With that foresight, the Warriors of the North helped the tribes migrate. But being able to foresee misfortune did not mean everyone could escape it.

Around that time, in a column of people fleeing south, a mother who was a shaman looked at the baby in her arms and said she was sorry. The child had been born into a Sami that knew no peace. Only after a long while did Eikthyrnir speak.
So am I.
4. Servant of the Old Tree

The shaman **Santalla** was born frail, and by tribal custom she was to be abandoned. But a branch of an old tree that had already died caught hold of the infant, and the Sami, who believe that every act of nature has meaning, raised her.

Born with a gift for commanding blizzards, she served the old tree all her life alongside the tribespeople who had chosen to stay beside the tree that could no longer walk. Until the Ursus massacred them.

The sole survivor of the massacre, Santalla sought out the tribe that had migrated and told them of the atrocity. But the people beneath the new Clan Tree were already forgetting the old tree, and she exiled herself.

On the day she returned, the old tree fell with a roar and was buried in the snow, and her hatred, resentment and regret were buried with it. If a new life was what the old tree wanted for her, then so be it. She left, taking nothing with her.
Then, on the road to a Rhodes Island safe house, inside a circle drawn by thorns, stood an old tree, a human and a giant three-eyed crow. They were waiting for her offering, for her 'words.'

blocks.cap: One old tree, one human, one giant crow.

blocks.x: Santalla embraced the old tree, shook hands with the human dressed as a Snowpriest, and held out a piece of candy to the crow. Each time, the offering was the same single phrase.
Thank you.
When she came to, she was standing before the door of the safe house. Warmth, and the care of friends: gifts she had won from fate.
5. A Tragedy, but Not the End

The **Cyclopes** are a Sarkaz lineage who see the future. The prophecy left by the Cyclops who took the throne of the King of Sarkaz a thousand years ago has been handed down through the generations: a shadow of darkness will spread from the edge of the icefield, reality will collapse, and even the land will be covered in void.

To build a barrier with their lives so that the tundra of the far north could endure another thousand years, they migrated north, and they did not trust outsiders. Valarqvin was a dissident among them.
When she was still young, Valarqvin once went after a group of reckless foreign explorers, though on the day she first saw them, she had already seen their deaths.

By the time she reached the cave, it was too late. The eyes of the explorers, turning into demons, begged to be saved, and with trembling hands she brought down her Necrosis Arts and carried out that fated death herself.
When she closed her eyes, her own grief-stricken shadow asked her: fate cares nothing for your efforts, so why did you follow them this far? As you saw, the future holds nothing but tragedy.
Yes. You are the tragedy I foresaw. But you are not the end.

Years passed, and Valarqvin climbed the walls of the Warriors of the North. Eikthyrnir, who had not exchanged words with a Cyclops in decades, agreed to talk for one reason: the vision she knew of and was keeping hidden.
She knew she had to reach the ring at the end of the icefield before the doom the Cyclopes had watched for a thousand years. Only then could the ring become a passage of hope rather than a dead end.
But a Cyclops does not fix the shape of fate in words. When she said it was a tragedy but not the end, Eikthyrnir, about to leave, asked with his back to her: you do not mean to cheat fate, do you?
"No, I only mean to accept it." As she descended the wall, the warriors no longer pointed their weapons at her.

Among the places Valarqvin led the expedition was an altar in a pitch-black cave. Before a rootless flower that the Cyclopes watched in silence, she murmured: "Virtual earth, a rootless flower, the key to the other side."

blocks.cap: A rootless flower floating above an altar in the dark. Reaching out, one could not touch it.

blocks.x: 6. The First Ending: "To Talk with the Mountains"
The expedition did not have just one end. The surviving records tell of several branching ends to the same journey.
In the first ending, as they left the Fjal Vetrtonn behind, a vast icefield came into view. Engulfed by the blizzard, Magallan heard a voice that reached her even with her ears covered.

blocks.cap: Mountain peaks wrapped in the blizzard. "Where are you headed?"

blocks.x: Where are you headed? With what will you walk forth? Magallan answered that she trusted in curiosity and courage, knowledge and technology, the experience of those before her and the help of her Sami friends.
Asked what she wished to take away, she named samples, data and the key that leads to the icefield, then added:
And... myself!
It was her teacher's lesson: only by surviving can knowledge be passed on. Then it was Magallan's turn to ask. Are you Sami itself? And where did the people who answered your questions go afterward?
The protector did not stop her as she walked out of Its embrace. Having accepted the outsider as Its own child, It pushed her into the fate that the Sami had calmly accepted.
"You okay, Maggy?" Typhon called. When Magallan said there must have been people who crossed the mountains and set out onto the icefield, Santalla answered that Sami never stops them.
Magallan did not tell them that in an instant she had come to know countless names never recorded in the history books. That none of those expeditioners had ever returned.
Sami did not wait for an answer. As the mountains vanished into the blizzard, an endless silver-white and a darkness with no end in sight spread out before her.

blocks.cap: Beyond the Fjal Vetrtonn, the party steps into the Endless Icefield.

blocks.x: In one record, when the expedition ran out of supplies and had to turn back, the Sami held a feast for them beneath the Clan Tree, and the next morning Magallan traded candy for jerky with a huntress and watched the sunrise beside her.

In another, Magallan rappelled down a great pit called the 'scar of the earth' and walked inside Sami's body. At its end, the beating tree was Sami's heart, and as a gift to the expeditioner, Sami showed her Its wounds and despair.
The rope back up was right beside her, and the Sami glyphs carved into the wall worried for her, but Magallan walked into the darkness again. She wanted to understand Sami a little better.
And another record. After the icefield exploration fever had gone on for years, Magallan was walking alone. Her companions, and the Sami locals she had asked for help, lay fallen along the way.

The only things moving on the paths of the Fjal Vetrtonn were warped, misshapen shadows. The book she had meant to leave to those who came after, and the unsent letter tucked inside it, were buried in black snow.
But I can tell. Even without a warning, however dangerous it is, in the end we will...
...move forward. Though her compass could no longer find north, she went north, and in the darkness the icefield glittered silver-white.
7. The Second Ending: "Winterfall"

The second ending, meanwhile, comes on the northern front. The will of Sami sometimes plays favorites: to a daughter born in the cold It gave the power to command blizzards, and to a dying warrior the life of a branch.
The most trusted Snowpriest among the Warriors of the North had his mortal wounds healed by the power of the earth, and a branch took the place of the horn he had lost.

Santalla told the others to leave at once while she held back the blizzard, and gave them a message for the Warriors of the North: a Disaster beyond all past records had come again, a vital position on the front had fallen, and the parting ceremony had been entrusted to the shaman Santalla.

blocks.cap: His horn is broken.

blocks.x: Demonic corruption could not be undone, and Santalla raised her staff high to send the warriors off. The hero led his warriors toward their final enemy, toward the fate that awaited them. No one cried out, no one questioned, no one looked back.

And so the warriors' lives froze. Santalla passed their gravestones on her way to the next camp, resolved from this day on to keep brushing away the black snow left on this land. Until that day comes.

The records surrounding this ending tell of different possibilities. In one, Eikthyrnir pursued the Demon's Blade wandering the forests into the Sami heartlands, and at the forest's edge, where death had gathered into a stream, he met Santalla. Or rather, what had once been Santalla.

She had destroyed the Demon's Blade, but could not erase the death it spread. Beneath the newborn Disaster, the Frozen Monstrosity, the warriors fell one after another, taking their own lives so as not to become food for the demons.

Eikthyrnir's blow reached the core of the Disaster, but the scattered armor of the Blade rose up and took aim at his back. A cold harder than ice burst from the Snowpriest's body, and after a few long seconds, neither Snowpriest nor demon, neither life nor death, remained.

In another record, it was Eikthyrnir who fell. Having witnessed the will of the warriors who fought beside him to the death, Santalla once again performed the ceremonies she had turned away from for years, and the exile returned to her place. **The daughter of the Santalla Tree knows no surrender.**

In yet another record, what remained was a mass of ice grown into the shape of the Santalla Tree. It was the Arts a Snowpriest had completed years before at the cost of her life, and the warrior who prayed before it did not even know what their enemy was. Only the Snowpriest's 'eye,' crystallized within the ice, recorded her final questions.
Did I truly use every means I had? Did I really pray with all my heart? Where are my people to go now?
Upon the empty black land, the mass of ice alone shed a single tear.
8. The Third Ending: "Long into an Abyss"
The future I foresaw... lies before my eyes now.
In the third ending, following the Cyclops's guidance, the expedition at last reached the end of the Endless Icefield. Beneath an unimaginably vast structure, rootless flowers were in full bloom.
If the door could be opened, what waited beyond it would surely be misfortune. But Valarqvin, who had been walking toward this door ever since the moment she left her cave, was already walking to it.
Typhon had watched that back walk toward fate countless times, but this time, she wanted to hold her back.
...Arges, don't go!

blocks.cap: Hearing the call, the Cyclops turned her head.

blocks.x: The ring-shaped structure began to spin, pouring out a darkness like starlight. Before a collapse far beyond anything on record, Valarqvin lowered a pitch-black veil and cut her companions off from the Disaster.
A smile appeared on the Cyclops's face, always so full of sorrow. "This is my fate."
I do not know what will become of fate's daughter. I only hope that you... can live freely, by your own will.
Typhon threw down her heavy bow and reached out toward that lonely back. In that moment, a spotless silver-white hornbeast leapt up beside her.

blocks.cap: A ray of light tore through the darkness like an aurora and soared upward.

blocks.x: Sami's Sovereign of Beasts charged at the demon. The silver frost scattered by the hornbeast vanished together with the terribly glittering stars, and warm droplets fell at the end of the icefield. Amma's love melted gently on the hand of Its daughter, stretched out toward the abyss of fate.
The demon's shadow and the silver-white hornbeast both vanished. The team members passed back and forth through the ring, but no one could make the door move again.
Typhon searched for a snowball bearing the hornbeast's mark. "If Grandmother came, she'd have left a blessing for sure. Arges... don't you think?" Valarqvin only slowly shook her head.
The storm had passed, but the prophecy had not ended. Just as her death was fated, humanity would one day open that door.

One record of this ending looks further back, to Valarqvin meditating in her cave. She, who had always looked only to the future, for once recalled the past: herself, on the day the black snow rose into the sky, approaching a dying child lying atop the corpses of her family.
Fate warned her. The child would grow up to become a hollow shadow corrupted by the demons, would declare her a heinous criminal, and would become her executioner.
Even so, she closed her eyes and embraced the child. Only in her arms did the girl finally break down in tears, and a single tear fell onto Valarqvin's collar.
9. Those Who Depart Do Not Return
After Amma left, Typhon did not use the word 'death.' The souls of the dead remain in the land of Sami, but those who depart never return.
Yet nothing changed in Sami, and no one noticed that Amma had gone. There was no one to say farewell with her, and no one to prepare a funeral.
As her grief was turning to anger, a Snowpriest, the first to believe Typhon's words, spoke. Beings like Amma belong to no single land; It stayed only because It loved the land and the lives of Sami.
It is quite the opposite, child. Amma's love has never once left.
Meanwhile, Valarqvin, who had returned alive, told the Warriors of the North, the Snowpriests and the Cyclopes everything she had seen. She was not forgiven, but neither was she executed.
After a long silence, one person rose. The most powerful enemy behind the door had already fallen. Was this not, then, the best chance they would ever have?

In a record from some years later, Valarqvin lost her life during an experiment to activate the megastructure. The researchers told Typhon she had likely been attacked by a Collapsal beyond the ring, but they did not mention the more likely hypothesis: that the high-threat Collapsal the research team had been forced to eliminate was Valarqvin herself, changed after crossing the ring.

Typhon carried in her quiver a scrap of Valarqvin's clothing that people had brought back from before the ring. Just as, in the days when Amma was still there, she had carried little snowballs in her pocket.

And then the ring was dismantled. It was a decision to end, with a single hardship, the war the Sami had fought on everyone's behalf for a thousand years, and to win an eternal peace. Typhon, who heard the news late, did not like it.
We did see it. That's why we chose to challenge it, to deny it.
The steel forest of the southerners glittered before her, and Typhon felt her bow grow heavy. No eternal peace is ever granted for a single hardship. Her weapon had recognized its prey.
10. The Black Hole Protocol

Meanwhile, in another branch of the future, the ring was not dismantled but restored. On the observation deck in Čappat, the Tin Man, proxy of the Columbian President, stood facing **Kal'tsit** and relayed the President's prediction: the nations would fight over control, and war would break out before any exploration.

When Kal'tsit put forward an absolutely neutral non-governmental organization with operations across all of Terra as a partner, the President doll in the Tin Man's pocket replied that it would give the idea positive consideration.

Afterward, Kal'tsit and the **Doctor** drew up the plan. Only those who passed a Collapse recognition test would join an expedition; each team would include one member who could purify Collapse; and supply lines would be run together with every Catastrophe Messenger. The resulting "Terra Icefield Megastructure Research and Restoration Convention" came to be called the **Black Hole Protocol**.

Around then, **Muelsyse**, an Elf researcher at Rhine Lab, had a long dream in which she learned ancient knowledge from fellow Elves living hidden in Sami. When she woke, it was the day of the physical examinations for Rhine Lab personnel taking part in the Black Hole Protocol. Sami was waiting for her visit.

When the Collapsals had visibly dwindled, **Angelina**, a Messenger from Siracusa who had learned to read Sami's script, delivered a letter from the Doctor to her old friend, a Sami Snowpriest. Since the icefield was melting, it invited Sami's trees to return home.
But the reply was a refusal. Sami departed, taking with It those who wished to follow.
We are people who follow the All-Father. It is He who will choose the path ahead of us.
When Angelina asked whether they would meet again, the Snowpriest answered: of course, for Terra too is the All-Father's home. Where Sami, the Feranmut, had departed, a vast hollow remained.
11. The Fourth Ending: "From Start To End"

The fourth ending is the story of those who opened the door. At the base on the edge of the icefield, after the final power supply test, Kal'tsit gave the engineering teams twelve hours of rest. Of the members who would be the first to cross the structure, only Typhon fell asleep, and even she was soon dragged out by Magallan.
Santalla chose to stay in the cold lands, and Valarqvin said only that this was not the end of fate.

Magallan asked the Doctor, who stood alone by the command center window, what exactly they were hoping for, and the Doctor said nothing at the time. Twelve hours later, before the structure, Magallan recalled the Doctor's answer.
Myself.
All a person can cast into the abyss of the unknown is their own shadow. So go forth. Go and find yourself.

What lay beyond the door was the front of the palace of the King of Kings, a land of yellow sand that scholars had never surveyed. A place where gold and iron melt, where even time has returned to chaos and lost its end.

From the horizon to right before their eyes, two vast armies charged endlessly at each other. This land of death, created at the southernmost edge of Terra by the war between the King of Kings and the Khagan, was the **Foehn Hotlands**.

blocks.cap: The two commanders of a war that never ended.

blocks.x: The expeditioners barely held on in the heat, and at the end of a time stretched without limit, the structure activated again. The spatial stabilization device was broken, and the door would stay open for only a very short time.

As she stepped into the broken door, Magallan, at the tail of the line, looked back at the battlefield. She remembered the annihilation she had witnessed years ago when they first reached the end of the icefield, and the melting snow that had fallen on her.

She understood the last great deed of the two commanders. The terrible energy that had turned jungle into desert had not come from their war. They, too, had once driven back enemies coming through the ring.
Now the door opens. The world the expeditioner sees has widened into the distant past, and the expeditioner heads toward a far future that not even fate can predict.

blocks.cap: The land of yellow sand seen through the ring.

blocks.x: In a record left from this ending, a Sami tribal leader, whose people had for a thousand years asked the same question of the warriors who went north, declared at a ceremony:
What divination cannot foresee, let us witness with our own eyes, as you once did. And let us believe that those who come after us will find the answer.

And beside the research team using the structure as a foothold to explore the Foehn Hotlands was Valarqvin. She was always silent, but people believed that she was gazing at fate, and that the fate of humankind held boundless possibilities.
12. The Fleetest of Light

After the Black Hole Protocol was concluded, a settlement with facilities even for docking landships rose in the polar region, and deep inside an unexcavated ruin, Kal'tsit removed the memory units from a large information terminal.

Warp drives, high-energy cores, starship maintenance data. That Terra's geniuses might use them to uncover the ancient glory of this land was exactly what she had done everything to prevent, and as she had for thousands of years, she meant to hold back the hands of those who chase knowledge.

But looking at the structure hauled up from the snow and the ruins brought back to life, Kal'tsit thought that she should no longer interfere in Terra's development. Three days later, people found those memory units in the ruins.

All that remains of the fifth ending, "The Fleetest of Light," is a few short lines: a wrong deduction, a wrong responsibility, a wrong sacrifice. A way here was found for those who will follow, but the depths of fate remain unknowable.
On the ridge, nature asked the expeditioner: will you keep going? The expeditioner sets foot on the frozen earth and keeps walking toward the fate that waits ahead.

rogue_4.tagline: The story of Sarkaz storytellers who promised to tell their ancestors of a finer Kazdel, and who, each time an imagined Kazdel ends, come face to face with a girl wearing a black crown. Every ending closes, but the story does not end.

chars.name: Nymph
chars.desc: A Sarkaz storyteller who tells stories to the Revenants.

chars.name: Tin Man
chars.desc: A Revenant from Columbia. He links the storytellers and the ancestors.

chars.name: Fremont
chars.desc: Lord of the Liches. Guardian of the Temple of Knowledge, which watches over the Soul Furnace.

chars.name: Ermengarde
chars.desc: A young Lich, Fremont's student.

chars.name: Mudrock
chars.desc: A Sarkaz in heavy work clothes who works on the rebuilding of Kazdel.

chars.name: Crownie
chars.desc: An unemployed Sarkaz seamstress who dreams of the legendary Kazdel beneath the earth.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: A Cautus girl, the leader of Rhodes Island.

chars.name: Theresa
chars.desc: King of Sarkaz. Theresis's twin younger sister.

chars.name: Theresis
chars.desc: Theresa's twin older brother.

chars.name: Kal'tsit
chars.desc: A doctor of Rhodes Island.

chars.name: Buldrokkas'tee
chars.desc: Holy Gun-Knight who guards the Pilgrim Gate of Kazdel, the Holy City.
