chars.desc: An enlightened one of the Anasa. He walks west with the storytellers.

terms.name: Soul Furnace
terms.desc: The heart of Kazdel. It burns the souls of the Revenants to keep the city running.

terms.name: Revenant
terms.desc: The souls of Sarkaz of old, burning inside the Soul Furnace.

terms.name: Teekaz
terms.desc: The primordial ancestors of the Sarkaz. Hunters shaped by Originium.

terms.name: Anasa
terms.desc: Sarkaz who attained liberation in the East. A black ring floats behind their heads.

terms.name: Katsidiya
terms.desc: 'Kazdel' in the Anasa tongue. The largest city of the Anasa.

terms.name: Civilight Eterna
terms.desc: A record of civilization that dwells in the black crown.

blocks.x: At the heart of Kazdel lies the Soul Furnace. In its flames, the souls of the Sarkaz of old, the **Revenants**, have burned for ages to keep the city moving.
The Sarkaz storyteller **Nymph** promised them better stories, a finer Kazdel. And as if in answer to that promise, the ancestors placed pens in the storytellers' hands.
A place with no heavy past and no hopeless future. There, where nothing had yet happened and nothing had yet ended, the Sarkaz began to write a Kazdel that had never been told.

blocks.cap: Nymph and Tin Man on a road not yet written.

blocks.x: 1. A Kazdel Written Inside the Furnace
Nymph opened her eyes inside the Soul Furnace. Beside her was **Tin Man**, a metal body in a hat, who told her that the ancestors had now put pens in their hands.
Wake those old-timers' curiosity and thrills, their anger and their laughter. Let their souls, burned down to almost nothing, taste life once more.
The Furnace was quiet. The Revenants were no longer in the flames, but Nymph could feel them gathered together, watching, deliberating, quarreling.

blocks.cap: Kazdel's Soul Furnace.

blocks.x: Nymph was not the only storyteller. Fremont's student, the young Lich **Ermengarde**; **Mudrock** in her heavy work clothes; the unemployed seamstress **Crownie**; Qalaiša and other Sarkaz of Kazdel came in with her, and Tin Man, himself a Revenant, became the bridge between the storytellers and the ancestors.
The Kazdel of the stories changed shape at a single word. In one story Kazdel rose into the sky, and the junk thrown overboard to lighten the load rained down beneath the clouds.

blocks.cap: What poured down from a Kazdel lifted into the sky.

blocks.x: In another, Kazdel sank into the earth overnight, and around the great pit sprang up ticket booths and swindlers selling 'Kazdel, the Lost City.' There was a Kazdel where two kings shared the crown, a Kazdel where the Sarkaz gained halos and wings, a Kazdel where Sarkaz who had gone east attained enlightenment.
But ending a story was not up to the storytellers. When a story displeased them, the Revenants leapt into it, tore the sky and stitched it back together, and ripped the story to shreds.
2. The End? — A Story Cut Short

In one ending, the story simply broke off. Nymph woke at the Furnace core, where **Fremont** was scolding his student. Lord of the Liches and guardian of the Temple of Knowledge, he knew that Ermengarde had slipped past him and dragged a band of Sarkaz into the Furnace.

Ermengarde protested that the Furnace had only calmed down because the Revenants had stormed off in a huff. Fremont silenced her and told the Sarkaz to go home. Kazdel had so many places that needed hands for rebuilding; they should not shut themselves away in here, amusing the old ones in the Furnace with idle fancies.
If you truly believe there is even the slightest chance of making the Kazdel you dream of real, then go and do it yourselves.

Then Fremont barred Tin Man's way as he tried to leave. The Soul Furnace's historical mission was drawing to a close, and there was now technology that would spare them the guilt of burning their own kin.

Afterward, with the core sealed off, Tin Man went to the Furnace platform to see his old friends. He laid out Columbian fast food and tossed a bag of fries into the fire, and as it turned to ash and melted away, the Revenants 'tasted' the food in a frenzy.

blocks.cap: Columbian food laid out before the Furnace.

blocks.x: Sweetness came from old fruit, saltiness from falling tears. Broken memories came together to shape the idea of a meal, and the ancestors felt a pleasure they had all but forgotten.

Tin Man said he could take them with him. Not as a mass of burning consciousness, but as individuals, as his own people. With three tin dolls beside him, he lit his pipe and sat at the mouth of the Furnace, waiting for an answer.
Ol' Curly, Big Larry, Lil' Mo, it's time to go. Life is waiting for you.
3. Furnace Syndrome

The storytellers who had been driven out returned to their daily lives, but none of them truly settled back in. A Babel doctor called it 'Furnace Syndrome.' Nymph did nothing but sleep, and Crownie could not forget the legendary Kazdel beneath the earth.

Meanwhile the Revenants, with no more stories to hear, raged until they threatened Fremont with a strike, and even the heating was cut off. Fremont hauled the storytellers back to the Furnace and told them to tell one last story, just once.

After that, people left one by one. On the day Tin Man left for Columbia, the storytellers saw him off beyond the city walls under a blazing sun, and Nymph handed him a box of 'fries' carved from scrap metal salvaged while repairing the Great Furnace.

A month later Qalaiša left without telling anyone, leaving on the empty lot only a letter and ointments to soothe the festering skin of the Nachzehrer soldiers. When the Furnace's renovation was finished, the Revenants left it too, and Crownie packed her bags to follow a designer's path instead of the lost city.

Instead of tourists, the Infected from the settlements outside the walls came flocking to Kazdel. In the Great Furnace the Revenants had left, a new flame burned quietly, and in it Nymph felt the breath of a city that would not stop growing.

Meanwhile, in a shabby room in Columbia, Tin Man lived with three Revenants who had gained bodies in the form of a metal hot dog, a donut, and a cheeseburger. That day he had waited a long time before the Furnace, but only these three had come running out, and he wanted to share with them all the beautiful things he had seen and lived through.

And before the Foundation committee, Tin Man reported that trying to divine Kazdel's future from the Furnace's visions was futile. Those who once could only survive by making it could now survive without it, so there was nothing to regret.

Around that time, Nymph had the same dream again and again. Sarkaz caked in Originium dust murmured forgotten old words in snow-covered ruins, and among them appeared a woman wearing a black crown and dressed in white.
I shall turn countless lives into memories.
The dream stopped on the day she met Amiya and the Doctor, returned to Kazdel. Nymph faintly glimpsed scenes in which Amiya was no longer alone, and so the last embers of the Revenants went out.
4. Twin Crowns — A Kazdel of Two Kings

In another ending, the storytellers stood before Kazdel's new parliament building. The black crown had split in two and floated above the heads of the siblings **Theresa** and **Theresis**. It was a Kazdel ruled by two Kings of Sarkaz together.

blocks.cap: The two Kings of Sarkaz, a crown between them.

blocks.x: The two kings saw that their strange guests meant no harm and let them roam the city freely. But Nymph did not want the story to end. Her body would not obey her, time ground to a sticky halt, and her being left her body and shot up into the sky.
The rumbling in the sky meant the Revenants were satisfied and the story was drawing to a close. An unseen force caught Nymph as she fell, and a white figure rose above her head. It was **Amiya**.

blocks.cap: Amiya beneath a pure-white crown, and the siblings beneath a pitch-black one.

blocks.x: For the two Kings, Amiya was their deepest regret. In their world, the siblings had taken in a Cautus girl with no one to rely on, and the girl had followed their ideals until she died of Oripathy.

When Amiya raised her hand, the pure-white crown appeared; when the siblings raised theirs, the pitch-black crown. As the two crowns overlapped, through **Civilight Eterna** the deaths and regrets, the joys and hopes of both worlds flowed into one another.
Nymph opened her eyes again in a Rhodes Island sickroom. It was Amiya who had entered the Revenants' space and pulled her out.

Out the window there was nothing but old buildings in a dust-laden fog. Nymph told Amiya about the Kazdel she had seen before she lost consciousness, a city hung with banners for the museum's hundredth anniversary, where every race came and went without discrimination, and said she wanted to learn more at Rhodes Island and someday build a Kazdel like that.
5. The Day They Tried to Open the Sky

The Amiya of that world was an Infected girl, the lone survivor among a cluster of wrecked vehicles. Theresa, separated from her brother after an ambush in Rim Billiton, rescued and adopted her, and the girl outlived the prediction that she would not last five years and grew to adulthood.

Some twenty years later she went missing, and all that remained in her place was a dust-covered medicine box, a torn white coat, and a damaged ID. She had left Kazdel alone, without the Kings' help, to wander lands of Catastrophe and war saving people, and inside the medicine box she had left Oripathy observation notes for the Kings. When Theresa took them out, she could no longer hold back her tears.

blocks.cap: A garden the two Kings built in memory of friends who had passed. Amiya is among the names.

blocks.x: Then, following the memories Amiya had shared, the two Kings went to Kal'tsit in the prison at the very bottom of Babel. From Kal'tsit's memories they drew out who the hooded 'human' always at Amiya's side had been, and four months later Babel woke that person from sleep in the ruins of a ship.
Theresa shared everything about this land with that person, hoping for salvation. But what came back after a long silence was a question no one could answer: "Where is Priestess?"

Even so, the knowledge the Doctor shared sent Terra leaping forward, and once the gaps between people had closed, the siblings turned their eyes to the sky. In Kazdel's silo, built above the clouds, energy gathered that could shatter the sky.

Then, just before the countdown ended, a black cocoon enveloped the sun and everything stopped. A falling black droplet drained the silo's energy, and the one who held it in her hand was a small King of Sarkaz whose eyes held nothing but sorrow.

She said that the moment the sky opened, this land would perish. Theresis sent word to the Doctor to prepare countermeasures and drew his sword. Darkness clashed with darkness, and darkness melted into darkness.

Meanwhile, deep inside the ship, the Doctor was waiting for her. The Doctor admitted that this civilization was not yet ready, yet said the effort these people had poured into a future with so little hope could not be dismissed.

She answered that she had seen the same ruin the Doctor had seen, and that she had come to offer a new choice. Just before being swallowed by a black sphere, the Doctor called her a pause and a lullaby, and spoke her name one last time. "...Amiya."

While the Doctor deliberately stood in her way, Theresa used the access the Doctor had opened for her to reach a withered garden. There, the small King of Sarkaz was a gardener, plucking fragments of stories from dead branches and sealing them away.

Theresa took her into her arms. Would the ending have been different had she been there on that journey in search of kindness? It was that regret she now wished to soothe. A King embracing a King, darkness embracing darkness, the two rose into the sky and became the sun, and day and night vanished from Terra.
But you are not in this story. Now, shall we talk about yours?
6. City of Angels — Sarkaz with Halos
In another ending, Kazdel was a holy city. The **Teekaz**, bearing the Sarkaz's name from long ago, wore halos above their heads, and the holy knights advanced in formation, firing as they came.

The gun-knight at the very front, **Buldrokkas'tee**, looked frighteningly familiar. He called the storytellers 'brethren who have not received grace' and held out his hand, offering to take them to Kazdel so they would suffer in the darkness no longer.

blocks.cap: Guardian of the Holy City, Buldrokkas'tee.

blocks.x: At that moment **Kal'tsit** appeared and shouted for the Sarkaz to follow her. Sankta gunfire cut between her and the Sarkaz, and behind her, Elders, Ancients, and Fallen emerged from their hiding places.

blocks.cap: Kal'tsit and the resistance, facing the holy knights.

blocks.x: The Buldrokkas'tee of that city had a Cautus daughter not of his blood, **Yelena**. She wanted to join the holy knights, and though each time he tried to let himself be persuaded, he could never give her a firm answer. His own son, Grrovae'zeeal, had already left Kazdel and stood with the resistance.
Meanwhile, Nymph had been held for days in Kal'tsit's guerrilla camp. All the companions who had come with her had vanished, and Kal'tsit offered only cryptic words as to why.
A point of reference need not refer to itself, nor does it lose its way on the plains of decision.

Nymph's meeting with the Pope of Kazdel had results no one foresaw. Declaring that the Law commanded them to accept the 'Sarkaz,' the Pope began carrying Originium crystals into the city, and Kal'tsit, saying there was no time, took Nymph and Yelena deep into the city.
7. The Gate of Salvation

blocks.cap: Kazdel, the pure-white Holy City.

blocks.x: At that same moment, Buldrokkas'tee laid down his guardian gun and stood before the Pope with a halberd in hand. Remembering his son's words, that enlightenment must be a choice and never a compulsion, he leveled its point at the Pope, who was filled with a manic joy.

Meanwhile, Kal'tsit led them beneath the Holy City to the 'Gate of Salvation,' which no one had visited in thousands of years. She said Nymph had to tell the one inside everything she had been through. If the decision had not changed, that person would surely try to save this land.
But the sarcophagus inside the gate was empty; only the shell of a broken black egg remained. Nymph's coming, Kal'tsit said, had already changed the decision.

Then the halberd at last pierced the Pope's chest. Crystals flowing from the wound covered the pure-white hall, and from beyond the curtain of crystals a face appeared, wearing a black veil beneath a floating black crown, and laid a hand on Buldrokkas'tee's brow.

He saw a ravaged city, Originium overrunning the land, and a King of Sarkaz turning ten million people into memories. She said she had already heard his roar within countless crystals, and that now that she had come, she would forgive everything.
Buldrokkas'tee's rage hardened deep in his throat, and the claws he had stretched toward her stopped in midair. Salvation had already come.
8. Wisdom of Kaśjñāna — The Sarkaz of the East

In another story, the King of Sarkaz led the clans east, and the Sarkaz who attained enlightenment became the **Anasa**. With the enlightened one **Qui'lon**, the storytellers walked west from a willow-lined lakeshore in Yan, debating endlessly as they went.

Mudrock was the first of the group to awaken as an Anasa and bear a black ring, but instead of liberation she gained more questions. Tin Man, who took up the practice to test whether he could shed the bonds of a Revenant, realized those bonds had already vanished before he ever entered the Furnace.

blocks.cap: The enlightened one and the group, resting beneath a tree.

blocks.x: Nymph tried to find the hardships she was meant to let go of, but could not. As life in Kazdel had improved, they seemed to have slowly melted away already.

Then, on an oasis road through a wasteland pounded by lightning, a bell rang, and for an instant Nymph was back inside the Furnace before standing once again before the enlightened one. Her companions were nowhere to be seen.

In the Anasa tongue, the city of Kazdel was 'Nagara **Katsidiya**.' In that city, the heart of the 'Anasa Road' linking Victoria, Ursus, and Yan, clerics with halos and monks with black rings debated the Law and the Dharma.

To Nymph's eyes, the city's great bell tower was identical to the Soul Furnace. The four statues before it were the first King of Sarkaz, called the 'Farchaser,' and his three successors, and the enlightened one revealed that one of them was himself: Qui'lon, the 'Wrathful Cerulean Flame.'
9. The City Where the Bell Fell Silent

To Nymph, the inside of the bell tower was the Furnace's maintenance passage; to Qui'lon, it was a white wall. Still, they walked together and reached the same place, and Qui'lon told her a short tale of the Pandita, the sage who cast the first great bell.

The Pandita, who had said that even if a great calamity came he could not change it, was enlightened by a single word from Qui'lon, and left once he had done everything he could. Qui'lon left Nymph with this: not to carry the worlds she had imagined as a burden on her heart, and to remember the Pandita's last words.
What a wonder to peacefully exist outside the laws of dharma, to perhaps not lose yourself within fleeting illusions. Wonderful.
With a final cry that their conversation was the answer to Katsidiya's 'continuation,' Nymph left Katsidiya.

Then, more than a thousand years after the last one clinging to attachment in Lokadhatu attained enlightenment, by a pond in Katsidiya where pilgrims and chanting were long gone, Qui'lon sat facing a girl in a black veil and ragged white clothes. She too was a King of Sarkaz, bearing the same black crown as Qui'lon.

It is said that if all is emptiness, sorrow vanishes too; but the King of Sarkaz asked whether paradise still remains once every feeling is gone. Then she turned a white lotus back into a bud and wrapped it inside a black fruit.

Qui'lon said he had already entrusted the law of this world to another to carry away. He apologized that he could not lead her to liberation, and she answered that the mission of salvation could not be laid on someone else.
Even if I must take on more sorrow... I will find a warm ending, no matter what.
Beneath the Ashoka tree, only the King of Sarkaz in white remained. The bell in the tower rang again, but its sound no longer carried.
10. Impeccable Day — The Guise of the Ending

With every story, Nymph's inspiration ran drier. When she had told every true story, every adapted story, every imagined story, the Revenants rummaged through the thoughts Nymph shied away from and made a story of their own: a prophecy about the King of Sarkaz, about Amiya, in which no ideal ending exists.

The moment Nymph surrendered control of the story, the longing for an end summoned the Ending, and it walked out of the void wearing 'Amiya' as a guise. Nymph wove the beginning, change, and end of 'Amiya' together with the power of the King of Sarkaz she had imagined, and forged a key.

blocks.cap: Nymph and 'Amiya' in the void.

blocks.x: When the key sank into the body of 'Amiya,' darkness wrapped around her. When Nymph looked back, Tin Man was gone, Ermengarde was gone, Qalaiša was gone, and even the road they had come by had vanished without a trace.

'Amiya' picked up the key that had reappeared in midair, returned it to Nymph, and smiled. She was the incarnation of the Ending, come to bring everything to a close, yet she was also the Amiya that Nymph knew. Compassion and goodwill do not disappear just because one's identity changes.

In Nymph's hand the key turned into a white cocoon, and on the black shell spreading over it, the stories of 'Amiya' were reflected. Death by man-made disaster, death by Originium, death by Catastrophe.

A storyteller whose imagination has run dry and whose inspiration is lost will chase an ending blindly until meeting their own. The warm white cocoon wrapped the storytellers like afternoon drowsiness; sorrow was cut off, joy remained, and death was driven away.

blocks.cap: The white cocoon and the black shell, with 'Amiya' at their center.

blocks.x: Where the storytellers had been, only human-shaped hollows remained. They can return to where they came from at any time, but Amiya, as part of the story, remains in this void forever.
She gazed far into the distance, sending a heart that wished for nothing but blessings toward whoever would overcome countless mighty foes and stand before the door at the end.
The story closes like this: "For now, let this be the full stop on the final page."
11. Goodbye, Sarkaz Lady

That 'Amiya,' too, had a world. As a child, Amiya was separated from her parents in a forest where her caravan was caught up in a battle, and there she met a pink-haired Sarkaz, bleeding, a black crown floating above her.
When arrows and Arts from the pursuing soldiers came flying, Theresa pulled Amiya into her arms. Amiya felt something pierce her chest, but it did not hurt, and something warm flowed into her heart.
She woke in her parents' arms, and the Sarkaz lady was nowhere to be found. Amiya looked back at the silent forest and said farewell. "Goodbye, Sarkaz lady."

No one bade the Sarkaz farewell after that. When the last Sarkaz's head fell, the extinction of the Sarkaz was proclaimed, and the nations, having lost their common enemy, turned their blades on one another again, naming new 'Sarkaz' and slaughtering them without end.

Grown up, Amiya was a doctor caring for the Infected at a field hospital on that battlefield. Beside a soldier slowly turning to crystal, she listened to the very end as he told how his family had been swallowed by the war one by one, then tore out a page not yet wet with tears, folded it into a paper fowlbeast, and pressed it into his hand.

And on the day people opened the gates of hell with their own hands, doctors, patients, and mercenaries died alike in the barrage. The mercenary band's foremost fighter, fleeing with Amiya, melted away, shield and all.

Years later, Amiya was dragged along by a squad searching for a weapon to end the war and was caught in an explosion in underground ruins. Looking down at her as she lay dying was a spherical machine glowing red, and within her it read both 'Civilight Eterna' and Originium.
I do have hopes for you, of course, but every one of them rests on the premise that you are alive. So survive.

As Originium swallowed her body inside a sarcophagus, a small crown was revealed. In a primordial palace, two gods tried to wrap her in light and black stone so that she would never grieve again, but Amiya refused. Stasis was neither an answer nor salvation.

Amiya wanted to save as many people as she could. But when the dying all across Terra were wrapped in white light and then turned to black stone, people united for the first time, calling for the death of the source: the Cautus of the black crown.
Under that banner the Infected were dissected, and death did not leave; it only changed its shell.
Until she found an answer that would end all suffering, Amiya decided to seal all of it away. Everything on the planet stopped, and her story became a small planet orbiting the black crown.

blocks.cap: 'Amiya,' with the stories she sealed away orbiting her like planets.

blocks.x: Setting out in search of an answer, she found only more sorrow. A Kazdel sinking into the void, the twin kings' prosperity decaying with time, the halos of the Teekaz losing their light, the gathas of the Anasa that no one hears. And at the end of each, the traces of one squad of Sarkaz.
12. You, Beyond the Boundary
Amiya knew she was a made thing. The deus ex machina that descends when the storytellers reach a dead end, the closing of the story: that was the role she had been given.

Watching every story begin in the Furnace and end before her, she thought the storytellers too might have been made by someone. And at one moment, as she was sealing Nymph away, she saw you, beyond a void drained of light.

No attack, no word, no deed of hers could reach you. Instead she learned that the hooded Doctor, always beside 'Amiya' in countless stories, was your shadow, and that you too had lived through helplessness, regret, and severance.

blocks.cap: In a picture, a Cautus girl and a hooded figure walking side by side.

blocks.x: If she could, she would have sealed you away so that you would suffer no more. But you only waited for the darkness of each ending to pass, and she never once received a reply from you.

Then one day you did not hurry past. You waited, and read words you had never seen before: her goodwill and her blessing. Much later, behind her picture, three boxes appeared with nothing written on them.
The moment you pressed one of them, Amiya felt what you felt. The boundary still divided the two worlds, but a channel of communication had opened. Even in the void, meaning is born.
Amiya set out.

The stories meant to tell the ancestors of a finer Kazdel stopped, each time, before a girl wearing a black crown, and that girl sets out once more in search of a warm ending for every story. Nothing has ended. Not yet.

rogue_5.tagline: The story of three people who climb a mountain to put Sui back to sleep, meet a god who works as a tour guide and a Feranmut who wants a round of mahjong, and end up opening the shrine of someone whose name no one remembers. One drop of ink, and it becomes a word again.

chars.name: Yi
chars.desc: The Sui Proxy who owns the Garden. Simply can't resist a rare collectible.

chars.name: Liang
chars.desc: The Garden's steward, created by Yi. Handles both the guests and the paperwork.

chars.name: Lin Qingyan
chars.desc: A Tianshi of the Tianshi Bureau. Wields Cangtong, a sword handed down through her family.

chars.name: Zuo Le
chars.desc: A young Candleholder of the Sui Regulator. Hasn't passed his trial yet.

chars.name: Yun Qingping
chars.desc: A wanderer serving as a Candleholder for the time being. Writes down everything he sees and hears.

chars.name: Wang
chars.desc: A Sui Proxy. A master of weiqi and stratagems.

chars.name: Nian
chars.desc: A Sui Proxy. A red-horned Feranmut who loves mahjong.

chars.name: Ling
chars.desc: A Sui Proxy. A Feranmut fond of wine cups and coin games.

chars.name: Shu
chars.desc: A Sui Proxy. Grows wishes in her fields and harvests their karma.

chars.name: Dusk
chars.desc: A Sui Proxy. A painter who dwells in the worlds inside her paintings.

chars.name: Yu
chars.desc: A Sui Proxy. A cook chasing the flavors of the human world.

chars.name: Chongyue
chars.desc: The eldest of the Sui Proxy siblings. A martial artist devoted to the way of arms.

chars.name: Leizi
chars.desc: A Tianshi of the Tianshi Bureau. Calls down thunder with her sword to aid the ascension rite.

terms.name: Sui
terms.desc: A colossal ancient Feranmut sleeping beneath a mountain in Yan. Its tomb is its very body.

terms.name: Garden of Grotesqueries
terms.desc: A garden built by the Sui Proxy Yi. A tourist spot by day, a seal that holds Sui down by night.

terms.name: Sui Proxies
terms.desc: Twelve siblings who awoke from the thoughts of the sleeping Sui.

terms.name: Placation
terms.desc: A ritual held in the Garden every year to disperse Sui's power.

terms.name: Candleholder
terms.desc: Members of the Sui Regulator who carry out the Placation. They light candles to ascend into Sui's Remnant Consciousness.

terms.name: Sui Regulator
terms.desc: The Yan institution that keeps watch over Sui. Every Garden employee belongs to it.

terms.name: Geists
terms.desc: Uncanny beings born from Sui's power. They hide all over the Garden.

terms.name: Remnant Consciousness
terms.desc: A world formed from Sui's lingering consciousness, centered on the Tomb of Sui.

terms.name: Jianzi Shrine
terms.desc: The shrine at the Garden's summit. Not a single character on its plaque or its stele.

terms.name: Great Hunt
terms.desc: An age of high antiquity when humans and Feranmuts joined forces to hunt gods.

terms.name: Carved Inkstick
terms.desc: A stele-shaped waregeist that a Placation squad offered at Jianzi Shrine.

blocks.x: Beneath a certain mountain in Yan sleeps a colossal ancient Feranmut, **Sui**. The twelve siblings who awoke from the sleeping god's thoughts are known as the **Sui Proxies**, and one of them, **Yi**, built a garden right on top of that mountain. It's the **Garden of Grotesqueries**, which gathers all of Yan's finest scenery in one place.

A tourist attraction selling admission tickets by day, a sealed ground where **Geists** roam by night. When Sui's power builds up, the Geists run wild, so every year the Garden holds a ritual to scatter that power: the **Placation**.

This year, three people are making the climb. **Lin Qingyan**, a Tianshi of the Tianshi Bureau; **Zuo Le**, a Candleholder of the Sui Regulator who still hasn't passed his trial; and **Yun Qingping**, who somehow found himself a temporary Candleholder. The catch? None of the three has ever met the Garden's owner who invited them.

blocks.cap: The garden a Sui Proxy built with his own hands has turned the past into rockeries and seals, into characters and traces of ink.

blocks.x: No Refined Taste, No Entry

Waiting for them at the entrance is the Garden's steward, **Liang**. When Lin Qingyan remarks, "It just looks like an ordinary garden...", Liang explains: to those with no bond to 'Sui' it is an ordinary garden, but those without 'refined taste' can't even see it at all.

According to Zuo Le, the foot of the mountain is nothing but ordinary day-trippers, but the higher you climb, the less predictable things get. When Lin Qingyan asks, "Have you passed your trial?", Zuo Le trails off: "I've applied several times..."

When Yun Qingping asks why they'd trust complete strangers like them, Liang only says that if fate allows, they can ask Yi in person. He warns them to tread carefully, since the Garden's objects are often tangled up with people's pasts, and hands them a special coin as 'a little insurance.'

Every human employee of the Garden belongs to the Sui Regulator. By day they're tour guides, gardeners, and security guards, but once the gates close they become lamp-holders and candle-wielders who keep watch over the uncanny and lure the Geists.

blocks.cap: The Hall of Candles, where tourists burn incense by day. After closing time, it becomes the Sui Regulator's headquarters for running the Garden.

blocks.x: A Candleholder who lights a candle and steadies their mind can 'ascend' in Sui's name and enter the **Remnant Consciousness**, a world formed from what is left of Sui's mind. Passing through the Garden, they suppress with authority and soothe with thought, and at the end they face a Sui Proxy and drive humanity's authority into Sui's weak spot. That's the Placation.
One Round of Mahjong, Three Cups of Wine, and Half Your Fortune

Geists aren't the only thing you'll run into on the road. If a red-horned, white-bodied Feranmut calls out from a mahjong table with two copper giants already seated, "We're one short, hurry up!", that's **Nian**.

blocks.cap: "Just so you know, the stakes are a little high. That's what makes it fun."

blocks.x: **Ling**, tipping a wine cup the size of a mountain among the clouds, offers you three cups and then proposes a coin-toss bet, while the sky-blue Feranmut **Shu** wraps her tail around a field where any wish you plant comes back as a harvest. Wander into a painting by mistake, and **Dusk** will be thoroughly unamused.

Then a Feranmut with green scales and a pink mane swoops down to ask if you need any help, and from the voice, it's the Garden's owner. Seeing as he names half your fortune as the price of his guidance, right off the bat, he clearly has no idea how haggling works.
Gods Who Lived Among Humans

The proxies have lived among humans for centuries. Nian once played mahjong deep into the night with the Grand Tutor and the High Minister of Works, and when a rookie Candleholder slammed down a furious Big Three Dragons, she declared, "Young folks really are full of fire!", tossed him a glowing White Dragon tile, and left.

Dusk, meanwhile, went up against the greatest painter of the age as a nameless artist and painted him the face of his youth that he had long forgotten. And Ling, back in the days of a drinking ban, turned the authorities upside down with a single poem, then got drunk once out on a lake and woke up to find a hundred years had gone by.

Far off in the Yumen garrison, the eldest brother **Chongyue**, called 'the Grandmaster,' stripped off his robe and knelt beside his men when they were flogged for breaking military orders. Shu beat a gong beside the farmers to lead the season's first plowing, and **Yu**, cooking finmeat noodles as the little army cook of a desert marching unit, realized that the flavor he loved most was plain home cooking.

Yi, for his part, spent years sneaking into the dreams of Ch'en of Lungmen, coveting Chi Xiao, until he lost by a single sword move and came home with a freshly forged Chi Xiao that carries Ch'en's style. As a bonus, he sleeps in his treasure vault hugging three Chi Xiaos and mumbling "I've waited 400 years..." in his sleep.
But the same shadow always hung over their days. When Sui awakens, everything that belongs to the proxies returns to its source, and every trace that they ever existed vanishes along with it.
Tearing up the little worlds inside her paintings and tossing them into the stove, Dusk thinks: the moment Sui awakens, she is nothing more than a figure in a painting.
The Great Hunt, and Where the Fireworks Came From

Sui was once a 'god' that Yan worshipped. In the **Great Hunt**, the war of high antiquity in which humans hunted the Feranmuts, Sui was the 'ally' who put spears that could kill Feranmuts into human hands.
But Yan saw through the scheme: Sui had stoked the war to reap the spoils and become the one and only god of this land. Sui was defeated, sealed, and put to sleep.

Zuo Le lives through that age in a dream when he nods off briefly during the ritual. In the dream, a young general leaps by kite onto the back of a Feranmut hidden like a mountain peak and packs it with gunpowder, wishing only that such sacrifices would grow fewer and fewer.

As the war dragged on, a woman handing out candles cried, "If only there had never been this arrogant Great Hunt!", and the general cut her down in the middle of the crowd. When he shouted that they might as well burn every last one of those candles, the people answered that night by lighting their precious candles and lining the roadsides with them. It was their own way of 'taking a stand.'

In the final scene, the general points his blade at the defeated old 'god.' The god laughs like a madman and curses them: once the outside enemy is gone, humans will slaughter one another until they perish. After a long hesitation, the general lowers his blade and orders it to help with the rebuilding through its power and wisdom.
When we... rise again, see it with your own eyes. See whether the Yan of that day truly becomes what you said. We shall prevail over ourselves.

Meanwhile, the firecrackers the Garden still sets off at the end of every year trace back to a custom from the Great Hunt, when the True Lung granted tax-exemption tongbao to those who gave up their fortunes or went to the front. The shares meant for families from which no one came home were melted down into Baizao's Monument of Martyrs, and the survivors who passed on their experience of fighting Feranmuts became the beginning of the Sui Regulator.

blocks.cap: The fireworks that light up Yan's sky at every year's end. They began on the battlefields of the Great Hunt.

blocks.x: The ritual normally ends in front of the shrine at the summit, **Jianzi Shrine**. But behind the shrine, a ladder Yi left there leads underground, and at the bottom lies the Tomb of Sui, where Sui's body sleeps. How far down the group goes decides which ending awaits them at the summit.
Orderly Placation — We Thought It Was a Fight to the Death

The one blocking their way at the summit is Liang. Zuo Le, who has built up decent teamwork with his 'Auntie Tianshi' Lin Qingyan while fighting off Geists along the way, unleashes a killing blow at the same moment she does, when the clouds in midair coil around her sword Cangtong and force it to a halt.
"Sheathe your sword, Tianshi Lin. Sui's power has been scattered, so you've completed your mission just fine." Only then can everyone clearly see the Garden's owner.

blocks.cap: The summit after the ritual. The Garden's owner finally shows himself.

blocks.x: "Is this... the end?" To a baffled Zuo Le, Liang kindly explains that this is a ritual, not a fight to the death. When Yun Qingping teases him, asking whether he really expected a life-or-death struggle with a Feranmut's shadow, Zuo Le deflates: "It's not... that, but..."

Receiving the jade rule as her token, Lin Qingyan asks why such a dangerous garden is open to the public. Yi's answer is a proposal from 300 years ago: that keeping Sui in check isn't a job for the Tianshi Bureau, the Imperial Guard, and the Ministry of War alone.
Holding back Sui's power with the energy of people sounded like a joke back then, but the more the Garden opens up, the easier the ritual gets each year.

And that's where the touching part ends. Yi promptly declares that Lin Qingyan's family heirloom sword is a must-have for his collection and starts haggling over a price, and Lin Qingyan beats a retreat with a "...Well then, farewell!" When Liang asks why he doesn't want Young Master Zuo's sword, Yi's answer is, "The ominous aura is way too strong. Not something I'd keep at home."
After everyone leaves, Yi looks back at the shrine where not a single character is carved. The name he could never bring himself to say becomes, in the end, a single word: 'sister.'
That proposal I made 300 years ago is paying off nicely. I hope the life in this garden can bring you even a little joy. I won't forget you.

After that, the Garden goes back to business as usual. Yi, lost in admiring his treasures, gets caught by Liang and a pile of paperwork and begs for just one more hour. Then he heads to a restaurant in front of the ticket office at the foot of the mountain and regales the tourists with tales of the garden while cracking sunflower seeds, and when Liang comes back, the signed documents are stacked neatly on the desk.

Meanwhile, after more than half a month of reports and questioning, the trio decides to visit the Garden once more before going their separate ways, this time as tourists. They buy tickets at the restaurant and wait, a shuttle bus pulls up, and out hops a tour guide in a sun visor, holding a flag that reads 'Welcome, guests from all over the country.'
"I'm 'Yi,' and I'll be your guide for this tour of the Garden of Grotesqueries." The three 'Placation VIPs' freeze on the spot.

Mu, a student in the same tour group, looks out from the observation deck and sees a vision of the dark crowds moving through the Garden spreading like flames toward the summit. Flames that turned stagnant air into vitality, and mountains and rivers into a human world. When she murmurs to herself, wondering whether there will still be fire here once the Garden closes, the guide mutters in reply:
How could there not be? That candlelight, you see, is truly bright.
Scroll of Scars — A Picture of Twelve, Missing One

In another ending, Zuo Le watches a Feranmut he thought could never be beaten fall apart. Writhing in midair, Sui opens like a book. Its scales fall like torn pages, and the characters on them scatter into the wind.

blocks.cap: When a god dies, heaven and earth are said to change. Yet the falling Feranmut comes apart as a book.

blocks.x: The exposed heart is the color of sunlight, beating calmly like a woman in deep sleep. Inside it, a girl with horns and a tail, her hands covered in earth-colored markings, lies curled up, her lips moving as if trying to say something.

That is not 'Sui.' The moment Zuo Le realizes this, he wakes at the summit, and no matter how hard he tries, what he just saw will not come together into a whole memory. When he looks back, the **Carved Inkstick** the group brought lies on the altar inside the shrine, and above it hangs a portrait with a blurred face.

"To think they would... find that person." Once the guests are far away, Yi sighs, barely audible. They were the first to enter this shrine in a hundred years. But finding the 'ink' means nothing without a way to record it, he says, and tells Liang to close the doors.

A hundred and twenty years ago, after the second sibling, **Wang**, entered the Tomb of Sui, Sui reappeared, half awake. The Sui Regulator barred every proxy from approaching. Wind and thunder, fire and rain flashed by turns across the sky, and a battle that began on a quiet afternoon did not end until the next morning.

When it was all over, Yi found in a pavilion several paintings missing their titles and several books with no words in them, but he could not recall even the name of the one who was gone. All he remembered was the character 'Yi,' which she had given him and which he had used for a long time.

A few days later, ordered to reinforce the seal, Yi picked up broken stones bearing marks like characters in front of the tomb, gathered the torn pages and scattered fragments, and brought his power to bear. That is how a shrine came to stand at the Garden's highest point, like a wedge pressing down on the tomb.
In that shrine, where every place meant for a record stood empty, hung only a single broken portrait. Memories of her surfaced only inside the shrine. Step out the door, and they vanished like smoke.
At least this way, I, we, and everyone in the world won't forget you, sister.
Each time the ritual ended, Yi came to the shrine and repeated these words, a little differently each time. Meanwhile, with every change of season, another piece of the portrait fell away.

A hundred and twenty years ago, it was she who heard Sui's heartbeat before any of her kin. She slipped past the watch and went deep into the tomb. She knew that if Sui woke, humans would come to strike it down without hesitation, and that life would once again be plunged into misery. And she told no one.

The 'Sui' that people finally cornered was not as strong as expected, and seemed to have little will to fight. The moment the Tianshis' Arts pierced its heart, everyone saw the truth inside. But as 'Sui' fell, that truth vanished along with every trace she had left in the world.
**When she cast away her name and put 'Sui' in its place, she wound the clockwork of oblivion herself.** Still, it was necessary. Her kin were able to survive.

She entrusted all her wishes to others and willingly accepted being forgotten. Then, on the day the Carved Inkstick was laid on the altar that had never once received an offering, a scrap of the portrait carried by the wind settled on it and was stained the color of ink. Now that scrap does not disappear, whatever the season.
Black-White Abstrusity — Into the Shrine After 120 Years

In this ending, the group passes Jianzi Shrine and goes all the way down to the tomb. Taking the weiqi board Wang left in the Garden as heaven, and the movable-type printing plate revealed beneath it as earth, they opened the gate of the Tomb of Sui.

blocks.cap: The Tomb of Sui, thrown open with weiqi and characters as heaven and earth.

blocks.x: Perhaps that recklessness angered the scheming proxy. Weiqi stones fell from the sky, characters burst up from the ground, and at last a streak of blue light swept the group away. Liang set the dazed visitors down in the clearing in front of the shrine and saw them off to the foot of the mountain.

Once the guests were out of sight, Yi turned toward the shrine. Inside stood another proxy, alone. It was Wang, who for 120 years had dwelt on his guilt, regret, and resentment, resenting everything that had buried her there, himself included. In all that time, he had never once dared to come to this shrine.

The name of the woman in the portrait was forgotten, but her expression was as calm as ever. To pass on the Way, to teach learning, and to carry ink on through a thousand autumns. The face in memory and the presence felt inside the tomb seemed to speak of the same wish.

"If you think those people could bring her back, why drive them away again?" Wang replied that, reckless as they were, they would have been better left buried down there, but he could not finish the thought. They were the first ever to bring that stele back from the distant past.

Find a single trace of ink in a Feranmut's memory, and it becomes a character. Once it becomes a character, her meaning can be restored. When Yi held out his hand as if asking for something, then broke into a broad smile under his elder brother's sharp glare, the weiqi board and the characters in Wang's hands merged into a wordless scroll.

blocks.cap: The wordless scroll draws close behind Wang, like a pair of arms opened wide.

blocks.x: ...I leave it to you.
"I'll do my best." The face in the painting was still smiling gently.

Long ago, a younger sister gave a name to her ever-silent second brother. The name a maker of characters had given her was 'Jie.' For the brother who was always gazing into the distance, she suggested 'Wang,' meaning 'to gaze.'
Then, calling it a human game, she brought out a weiqi board of nineteen lines by nineteen and asked him to choose black or white. Wang chose black.

Wang went on holding black after that. Every sixty-year cycle he played a 'game of heaven and earth' against the Grand Tutor with Yan as the board, and when he noticed an unfamiliar move intruding on the game, he laid down 181 black stones to draw the unknown player holding white onto the board.

There is also a record of what came after the matter of Sui was settled. Wang, his power gone, obtained a wordless scroll at a gallery. When he placed on it the amber in which Yi had sealed the portrait's last fragment, the outline of a woman slowly emerged. Perhaps the sister the world forgot remains somewhere in Yan as an ordinary person, Wang thought.
Out of Nothingness — A Single Drop of Ink

This time, the group follows the scroll deep into the tomb and stands inside Sui's memory, on the final battlefield of the Great Hunt. Beyond the orderly army camp tower the last two Feranmuts other than Sui.

blocks.cap: Inside Sui's memory: the two Feranmuts left at the end of the Great Hunt.

blocks.x: When heaven, earth, and mountains had all been dyed red, Ju, who had stood against the war to stop it, became its sacrifice, its body scattered in every direction. Hou, the great tree on its back withered, lay prostrate, then sent off its last resistance as a butterfly-shaped beam of light and vanished from every record.

While Lin Qingyan and Zuo Le charged to the front line, Yun Qingping stayed behind alone and wrote everything down. Even if the records were lost and memory itself vanished, as at Jianzi Shrine, that was his duty.

If history holds, Yan will next seal the god, Sui will sleep, and Baizao will be built. Standing before Sui's head, the True Lung regarded this 'ally' as an equal, neither looking up nor looking down, and then declared the god's end.

Meanwhile, in the Garden's treasure vault, Yi slowly unrolled a scroll identical to the one entrusted to the Sui Regulator. The Great Hunt in the painting unfolded just as history had, until the scene of the god's sealing. There, it changed. The True Lung accepted the pledge and granted Sui the status of a human.
Unlike the Yan of old, which tried to tear out the root because it was afraid, the Yan of today has a new choice. If people stand above heaven, what reason is there not to forgive and embrace?

When Yi unrolled the painting to its end, the place where Sui should have been drawn held only a single blot of ink. Unlike all the illusions before it, this ink remained, unmistakably, on the scroll.

blocks.cap: The blot of ink left where Sui should be. With this one drop, one can make characters, write books, and found learning.

blocks.x: Yi carried the scroll to Jianzi Shrine, touched the ink blot lightly with a finger wet with cloud and rain, and pressed it firmly onto the shrine's plaque. **For the first time in 120 years, a trace of writing remained in the shrine.**

Sui's memory held its dreams as well. Sui, which saw humans as tools for its own evolution, even dreamed of dividing its body among humans and taking the nation of Yan itself as its body, to live forever. Wang made that empty obsession into a trial for those performing the ritual to overcome, so that it would be shattered by human hands.
No Regrets — One Black Stone Left on the Board
Of all Sui's delusions, this may have been the most dangerous: after waking, to cast off its shell, swallow a proxy, take Chongyue's body for its own, and slip into the shadows of the land.

Once, there was a single proxy born carrying nothing but Sui's wrath. In the turmoil after the Great Hunt, he slipped in among humans and led refugees, became an official, and finally rose to the seat of the True Lung, waiting only for the day he would burn Yan to the ground.

But walking thousands of miles with the refugees, he came for the first time to see humans as living beings, and in the end he could not carry out Sui's will. Admitting that he was not a beast, he became a perfect True Lung, left behind a book holding the answer to everything in the world, and shut the palace gates for a hundred years.

In a nation where every answer was written down, people stopped asking. One day a torch held by an old man in a remote place spread, and when the people opened the palace gates, only the dragon robe and crown sat on the throne.
Around then, as he played weiqi at the top of the Garden, a white-haired old man with no light in his eyes handed him a single black stone.
I need your help, Chongyue.

It was the name he had chosen for himself before becoming the True Lung, a name no one but him would remember now. When his fingertips touched the stone, the scenery melted like oil paint. His great deeds, his resistance, his despair, all of it had been nothing more than a trivial fancy dreamed by the sleeping Sui.
Wang explains. Sui melted down the proxies' memories to mold that figure, and its form came from the eldest brother, the only one who had been given a new life.

Inside the delusion, Chongyue cuts his way through countless versions of himself who had bowed to Sui, a tyrant, a great merchant, an apothecary spreading poison, a smith forging instruments of torture, and comes to understand: violence alone cannot stop Sui.

It was Sui who never taught the newborn proxies how to stand or how to walk. It was humans who gave them shelter, nurtured their tastes, and taught them ethics. Chongyue sealed that understanding in the black stone and hurled it with all his strength into Sui's thoughts.

And in the tomb, in reality, Wang caught the collapsing puppet and slowly laid it on the ground. He had borrowed his siblings' powers and used the opening made when humans and 'Chongyue' clashed to strip emotion and memory, consciousness and cognition from Sui's delusion.

What remained was a halo of light as pure as a wish born from twelve dreams. When 'Little Moji,' a creature born from ink that follows traces, ate its fill of that light and fell asleep, Wang took it into his arms with a care he had never shown in front of others.
"What exactly did you send us to do?" the Tianshi **Leizi** demands. All the way here, she says, the token showed nothing but Yan burned to ruin and its people in misery.

Instead of answering, Wang handed over the sleeping Little Moji as their token and sent Leizi and the rest of the Placation squad out of the tomb. Even if he answered, they would not remember once they left the Garden.

Outside the tomb, across Yan's mountains and rivers, a game called 'life' awaited them. And he, 'one in a hundred and eighty-one,' had to remain in the lonely tomb and keep playing against a god that had not yet awoken.

Only after sending back the people and Little Moji, and cutting away every last trace of his humanity and compassion, can Wang finally face Sui's ever-evolving malice. Before making the move that would seize life, Wang erased all of his own hope.

blocks.cap: The shadow of a black Feranmut cast over a ruined land.

blocks.x: Epilogue — The Garden That Opens Its Gates Again

The Garden of Grotesqueries is a garden in which a Sui Proxy turned the past into rockeries and seals, characters and traces of ink. At its summit stands a shrine with a blank plaque, and the woman in the portrait hanging inside chose, willingly, to be forgotten.

Still, the Garden opens its gates every year, tourists climb the mountain in long lines, and those left behind keep searching for a single drop of ink. With ink, words can be written again. And as the guide said, that candlelight is truly bright.

act19mini.tagline: A Tianshi goes looking for a missing scholar in a town that appears on no map, and watches, one by one, the stories of objects awakened by human obsession. Holding on and letting go were, in the end, matters of the heart.

chars.name: Lin Qingyan
chars.desc: Heir to the Lei Fa of the Tianshi Bureau. She came to Mangshan Town looking for the missing Yun Qingping · Operator Leizi the Thunderbringer

chars.name: Yun Qingping
chars.desc: A record keeper who writes down kung fu at the Grandmaster's side. He himself is a scholar who never managed to learn martial arts · Operator Record Keeper

chars.name: Zuo Le
chars.desc: A young official of the Sui Regulator. He calls Lin Qingyan 'Auntie' and sent her a letter asking for help.

chars.name: Hu Jun
chars.desc: A server at the teahouse in the south of town. He wants to leave this town.

chars.name: Mr. Pu
chars.desc: The schoolteacher of Mangshan Town. The townsfolk come to him whenever something goes wrong.

chars.name: Mo Yi
chars.desc: A clever girl who roams the jianghu. She goes around selling the secret tome of the Grandmaster of Yumen.

chars.name: Liang
chars.desc: A being who handles chores at the Garden of Grotesqueries. He calls himself half a laboring Geist.

chars.name: Chongyue
chars.desc: The Grandmaster of Yumen. A martial artist whose kung fu is said to have reached the divine.

chars.name: Huai Tianpei
chars.desc: Waai Fu's father. A martial artist who dueled the Grandmaster at Yumen six months ago.

chars.name: Waai Fu
chars.desc: A girl trained in martial arts. She is chasing her father, who suddenly disappeared.

chars.name: Lee
chars.desc: A seasoned tracker who set out with Waai Fu to find her father.

terms.name: Mangshan Town
terms.desc: A remote town at the foot of Mt. Mang near Baizao. It appears on no map, and no communications signal reaches it.

terms.name: Geist
terms.desc: A consciousness born when a person's obsession settles into an object. It perishes if the object breaks or the obsession fades.

terms.name: Tomb of Sui
terms.desc: Where the Feranmut 'Sui' has slept under seal for a thousand years. The power that leaks out turns objects into Geists.

terms.name: Book of Kung Fu
terms.desc: A book holding the lifelong martial learning of the Grandmaster of Yumen. Rumor says it contains the secret to turning objects into humans.

terms.name: Garden of Grotesqueries
terms.desc: A garden built atop the Tomb of Sui. It belongs to the collector 'Yi.'

terms.name: Tianshi Bureau
terms.desc: Where the Tianshi of Yan belong. Being close to Mt. Mang, it has long put down the town's Geist disturbances.

terms.name: Sui Regulator
terms.desc: The Yan office in charge of matters concerning the Feranmut 'Sui.' Every year it inspects the seal on the Tomb of Sui.

terms.name: Shanhaizhong
terms.desc: An old group that has long studied the Feranmuts. It is on bad terms with the Sui Regulator.

terms.name: Placation
terms.desc: The annual rite in which the Sui Regulator checks on Sui's slumber and reinforces the sealing apparatus of the Tomb of Sui.

terms.name: Yumen
terms.desc: A frontier fortress of Yan. The Grandmaster guards it.

blocks.x: North of Baizao, a city of Yan, at the foot of Mt. Mang, there is a small town that appears on no map. Signals cut out the moment you enter, and few people know the way out.

**Lin Qingyan**, heir to the Lei Fa of the Tianshi Bureau, had stepped down as deputy minister of the Judicial Review Office and was on her way back to the Bureau when a letter reached her from **Zuo Le**, a Sui Regulator official who calls her 'Auntie.' His friend **Yun Qingping**, who had come with him to Baizao, had vanished without a word three days earlier. Zuo Le asked her to look for him in the direction of Mt. Mang.
Along the way, without realizing it, Lin Qingyan walked into that town. There she would meet, one after another, objects that held hearts people could not let go.
1. The Girl Who Counted to Nine Thousand

The first person she met was a smiling old man. He said he had never heard of the Tianshi Bureau and had never been outside the town, pressed a hot pancake from his robe into her hands, and was gone the moment she looked away.

blocks.cap: A street in Mangshan Town. Few passersby; it is quiet.

blocks.x: Next, a girl holding an umbrella on a clear day bumped into her while counting. The girl said the person she was to meet at the tofu stall had told her to come only after counting to nine thousand, and she was truly afraid of the warning that telling the secret would get her killed.
The letter the girl dropped was marked 'Classified. Not to be disclosed to others.' Lin Qingyan followed her to return it.

Meanwhile, the girl, **Xiaoshu**, met with **Hu Jun**, a server at the teahouse. She had taken the letter from her teacher's drawer and lost it on the way, but she had read it first. Three quarters past the Hour of Wei. A deal at the old teahouse.
Hu Jun said that if things went well, he had meant to take her with him and leave the town. But Xiaoshu was not ready yet, and she had not kept the secret.
Seeing his wet eyes, Xiaoshu blew on them to dry them, as her teacher had taught her. When she told him that holding her hand so tightly would crumple it, Hu Jun said goodbye.
“Goodbye, Xiaoshu.”
When Lin Qingyan reached the alley, too late, all she found was an umbrella lying on the ground. Xiaoshu was nowhere.
2. Three Quarters Past the Hour of Wei, the Old Teahouse

Then, at three quarters past the Hour of Wei, in the teahouse in the south of town, the Lu brothers of the 'Three Blades of Wind and Cloud' were waiting for a girl. A few days earlier she had framed them with the Grandmaster of Yumen's secret tome, and it had cost them their third brother.

blocks.cap: The teahouse in the south of town. The server had polished the floor to a shine.

blocks.x: The **Clever Girl** smiled even at blade-point and haggled over the price of the tome. The eldest brother took the tome and was about to silence her for good when the blade fell from his hand.

It was Hu Jun, the server, who had drugged the tea. He tied the three of them up like bundles of straw and sat them against the wall. Asked why he wanted the tome, he said it was because he wanted to leave the town.
This little town has some five hundred and twenty households, and two thousand nine hundred steps will take you all the way around it. Years have passed, and neither number has changed at all.
A scholar rose from the corner and urged him to hand them over to the authorities and kill no more. It was Yun Qingping. Hu Jun said he could not trust him yet and tied him up with the others.

Lin Qingyan arrived a little later and did not touch the tea she was served. Instead she pointed out that the paint on Hu Jun's lapel was the same color as the paint on the umbrella left in the alley, and asked whether the deal at three quarters past the Hour of Wei was already done.
Hu Jun overturned the table and fled upstairs, but waiting there was a heartless swordswoman who demanded the tome.

Meanwhile Lin Qingyan followed a cry of 'Help!' and freed Yun Qingping. But the girl had already vanished, leaving only a cut rope, and with a crash from outside, Hu Jun tumbled down from the second floor.
When Lin Qingyan ran to him, what she found was not a body. Only the shards of a shattered teapot.
3. A Teacher of Objects
That night Lin Qingyan visited **Mr. Pu**, the schoolteacher said to be Hu Jun's friend. In this town with no magistrate's office, people brought every trouble to his 'School.'

Hoping to recover Hu Jun's 'remains,' Mr. Pu swapped Lin Qingyan's bundle while a candlestick and a chair toppled over on their own. But when he opened it after she left, there was nothing inside but pebbles.

Late at night, a broom, a pair of embroidered shoes, a carrying pole, and a medicine bottle trailed after Lin Qingyan in a line. But the one who snatched Mr. Pu from the end of the procession was the heartless swordswoman from earlier.

The swordswoman said she had to leave this town and demanded he teach her the 'personification' technique written in the tome. Mr. Pu rebuked her: she wanted to become human, yet had learned hatred and violence first. He held firm. She could kill him, but he would not deceive a student.
At that moment a sword wreathed in lightning flew in, and the swordswoman fled through the window. A talking broom had brought Lin Qingyan.
Back at the school, as a tray carried teacups over by itself, Mr. Pu admitted that all of his students were 'Geists.'

Power leaking from the Feranmut sealed for a thousand years in the nearby **Tomb of Sui** had given consciousness to objects that held human obsession. Mr. Pu, once a Feranmutologist at the Sui Regulator, had been teaching them human rites and virtues, so that they could live among people instead of causing trouble and being destroyed.

blocks.cap: The School. Its students are all objects from the town.

blocks.x: The seed of the trouble was a letter that had reached him a few days earlier. It carried a rumor: the secret tome of the Grandmaster of Yumen, said to be a Feranmut incarnation with a human body, held the secret to turning objects into 'humans.'

A Geist dies when its object breaks or the human obsession behind it fades, Mr. Pu said, but if the object is mended well, its consciousness might one day return. Hu Jun's owner had been a tea farmer who went to the sea at the southernmost tip of Yan in search of the finest tea and never came back. That obsession had settled into the teapot.
Lin Qingyan handed Mr. Pu the box holding the teapot shards.
4. An Ordinary Stone

Next, old Mr. Wan, on his sickbed, asked Lin Qingyan to find a missing stone. It was an ordinary stone he had picked up on a riverbank as a child, but the old man offered half his fortune to whoever found it.
Long ago, a kindly man approached the child who had found the stone in the river and offered any price for it. The child refused. If the man wanted it that badly, it had to be a more precious stone.
When a landslide took the child's home, that stone was all he had left. He wore it around his neck, built a business from nothing, and turned the man away again when he came back.

In middle age, on the day bandits took everything he had, the man came once more. He meant to borrow money against the stone and start over. The man would not take the stone. Instead he plucked a feather from a pure-gold fowlbeast and gave it to him.
What I want is just an ordinary stone. As long as you have not let go of your obsession with it, it is too heavy for me to take.

Meanwhile Lin Qingyan went to that river and, behind a tree on a bank that had become a graveyard, heard the voices of two children. One said it came from a garden called the 'Garden of Grotesqueries,' and that the master had woken all its siblings from the same basket.

The other said the one who woke it was a stubborn man who plowed his field even in the rain, and that it could not understand why he never gave up. When Lin Qingyan approached, the voices stopped. Only a smooth, polished stone remained in the grass.

Back at the mansion, Lin Qingyan revealed that the thief had been after the inheritance in the cabinet, not the stone. On a rainy night someone had fumbled at the lock and dropped the box, and the stone had rolled out. She told the second son, so that only he could hear, to restrain himself. Then she handed him the stone she had found and told him to take it to the old man.

blocks.cap: A stone that shows a mysterious sheen in the sunlight.

blocks.x: At the old man's side was that same man, wearing the same smile as on the day they first met. Asked whether it had not been painful to go home empty-handed his whole life, the man spoke of the wind and clouds and the interesting people he had seen along the way.

The man had known, from the day he stood on that riverbank, that the old man would never let go of the stone. When the old man offered it to him, he answered that the stone had already awakened in the old man's hands, so the stone should choose for itself. He told him he could put it down now.

And then, the riverbank of his childhood. The child looked at the stone in his hand for a long time, smiled bitterly, and let it fall into the river. As he closed his eyes, he heard thunder, wind, and the earth of the mountain pouring down.
5. A Hundred-Year Deadlock

Meanwhile Yun Qingping, on his way to the mountain where 'that person' awaited him, met **Bai Jin** in the woods, a woman searching for her husband. He had gone up the mountain for firewood and never come back. He was a stubborn man lost in weiqi. The two climbed the mountain behind the town together.
In the pavilion on the mountain, a taciturn youth named **Lan Ke** sat before a weiqi board. He had been promised one wish if he won this game, and he kept his place there, pondering his next move.
The board was a triple ko. As it stood, the game would end in a draw. But he said a draw would not do. His wish was for two people parted by death to meet again.

blocks.cap: The pavilion on the mountain. Moonlight, rain, and snow passed over that board.

blocks.x: When they reached the pavilion, Bai Jin vanished. Only Old Luo was there, a man whose family had been coming to this place since his grandfather's day.

Studying the board, Yun Qingping recalled the days he had spent writing down the Grandmaster's kung fu with a body that could not learn martial arts. At the end of that torment, like being tied up in front of a feast, he had found one answer.
First give, then observe, and finally, take.

He left the ko fight of a hundred-odd tangled moves alone and placed a white stone somewhere else entirely. Black captured a great many white stones, but the game tilted toward White instead, and the deadlock broke.
Lan Ke took the old man for little Luo Qin from his childhood, but the old man was Luo Qin's grandson. More than a hundred years had passed.

Then Bai Jin appeared. Lan Ke said the Xian had kept his promise and they could go home now. Only when he saw her silence did he murmur, 'I was already... long ago...' The game was over, and Lan Ke had nothing left to regret.

What remained of 'Bai Jin' said she was the joss paper laid before her cenotaph, soaked in Lan Ke's tears and longing. She asked them to bury her husband beside the cenotaph and burn her there. Then she became a bundle of joss paper.

One hundred and twenty years earlier, on the night Geists swept over the town like a flood, Lan Ke was carried off while saving many people, Luo Qin among them. Bai Jin, who pulled him out, died that day. Old Luo put what remained into his basket and went down the mountain.
Next appeared **Liang**, who called himself half a laboring Geist, and led Yun Qingping to the summit. The one who had summoned him was the Clever Girl who had vanished from the teahouse.
6. The Swordsman Who Lost His Sword

Meanwhile, in one of the town's teahouses, a swordsman had been waiting two days for someone. It was the seventh year he had met her here, once a year. They had agreed never to ask each other's names.

Seven years earlier, the day after he lost his sword in this town, a woman carrying a sword had grabbed him and demanded he teach her swordsmanship. He refused, saying he had put his bloody past behind him and was leaving the jianghu. She said he was lying, and bet him he could not live a year without a sword.
The next year she showed him the swordplay she had taught herself, and said she could tell which forms were clumsy just by looking at his face.

In the sixth year, someone using his moniker, the 'Delivering Blade,' spilled blood across several nomadic cities. He said he would give her the name. She answered that she had not yet found a way out of this town.
And in the seventh year, the teahouse keeper told him she was the culprit who had hurt many people over the tome. She had first appeared in town around the time he lost his sword.
When she faced Lin Qingyan in the street, the swordsman stepped in front of her. Only then did he understand. The sword had been at his side all along.
Last year, when we met, you tried to give me the name 'Delivering Blade'... when the 'Delivering Blade' is me.

She had wanted to live, under her own name, the jianghu he had grown sick of. But Geists were held back by an invisible barrier and could not leave this town. She had stolen the Book of Kung Fu to get past that barrier.
“If you want to stop me, break me!” Dark clouds rolled over the clear sky, and lightning gathered in the Tianshi's palm.

The swordsman stepped forward to share the blame. But Lin Qingyan said that she, the incarnation of a sword, could hurt innocent people out there, and that the more desperate the wish, the less she could let her go.

blocks.cap: Heavenly thunder. Lightning that falls when it must fall.

blocks.x: Where the lightning ended, only a copy of the Book of Kung Fu lay on the ground. A man named Huai Tianpei rushed in, crying 'Found it at last!', and after that only the swordsman remained in the street.

Before the lightning fell, he had asked Lin Qingyan one favor, saying he would repay all the damage and turn himself in. Lin Qingyan thought that once this was over, she would have to confess her own wrongs to the Tianshi Bureau first.
All this time I thought I was the one calming her down. It was her calming me.

Then, on the road out of town, he met a woman who said she was lost. She remembered nothing, and though her body was not whole, she said she wanted to go on ahead. He asked whether she would travel with him for a while.
7. The Banquet of Heroes

Earlier, at Yumen, the Grandmaster's Book of Kung Fu disappeared while **Huai Tianpei**, the man who had dueled the Grandmaster six months before, ran riot on the training grounds. All that was left was a note from Mo Yi of the **Shanhaizhong**: 'Borrowing a book.'
Mo Yi promised Huai Tianpei, who had helped her get the book, that in ten days he would face the Grandmaster again atop Mt. Mang.

Around the same time, Huai Tianpei's daughter **Waai Fu** was following her father's trail with **Lee**. He had taught her never to bully the weak or harm the innocent. She could not understand how he had come to this.
The town clinic they stopped at was full of people hurt in fights over the tome, and by a stranger who challenged every martial artist he saw to a duel. There they ran into Lin Qingyan.

Meanwhile, on the summit, Yun Qingping, who had taken down the Grandmaster's dictation himself, confirmed that the Book of Kung Fu Mo Yi held out was the original. Mo Yi asked Liang whether the master of the Garden of Grotesqueries might take an interest in this treasure.
Mo Yi said the reason for all this trouble was that watching heroes trade blows over grudges was more entertaining than a play.

Before long, the town's tables, chairs, and brooms all took human form and climbed the mountain. On a summit so packed with jianghu fighters and Geists there was no room to stand, Mo Yi held up the Book of Kung Fu and declared that whoever took it and held it to the end would be its owner.

blocks.cap: The summit of Mt. Mang. The site of the 'Banquet of Heroes' Mo Yi hosted.

blocks.x: As people turned their weapons on one another, Yun Qingping stepped forward. If this book held some mysterious power, he asked, how could he, who wrote it, have failed to learn even one martial art? Then he took a printed copy of the Book of Kung Fu from his robe.

The Grandmaster had never meant to hide this book, he said. If they wanted it, he would print more and hand them out. At that, the crowd's anger turned on Mo Yi. Yun Qingping asked her to return the book to Yumen, and said that all he saw here were people trying to train in kung fu.
8. Thirty Exchanges at the Cliff's Edge

Then Lin Qingyan, having pushed through the Geists, stood before Mo Yi. Mo Yi sneered that she was ruining her plans by playing the righteous hero just when everyone's lives were at stake. Then she took the book to the highest point of the summit and recited an incantation.
“The Shanhaizhong humbly beseech thee. First of the Twelve, whose name is Shuo, manifest!”
The sky split open and a vast shadow appeared, overwhelming heaven and earth. 'Master?' slipped from Yun Qingping's lips.
When the shadow brought its palm down, the whole mountain shook, and Lin Qingyan's Lei Fa was useless, as if striking empty air. Yun Qingping said it was only an illusion cast by the Book of Kung Fu.
As the crowd scattered, one man walked toward the shadow, step by step. It was Huai Tianpei.
I lost my sword. I broke my promise. I have no right to face you.

blocks.cap: Huai Tianpei before the incarnation of martial might.

blocks.x: He did not dodge. He met force with force and fist with fist, closing the distance, and with every exchange Shuo's form grew clearer. Without realizing it, Yun Qingping took out his brush and paper.
Thirty exchanges passed and he did not fall. But he was already at the edge of the cliff. One more punch, and he would go over.
“Dad!!”
At Waai Fu's cry he faltered, and what he had forgotten came back to him. A forty-year promise made to someone. A daughter to protect. His own name.
He had never lost to anyone. Then the only opponent left was himself, and if there was no road ahead, he had to look back.
Huai Tianpei leapt high and drove his fist into Shuo's chest. Shuo's form vanished into the air, and he fell from the cliff.

As the sky regained its light, Zuo Le arrived with Yumen soldiers and had them search the foot of the mountain. Told they would not be held to account, the jianghu fighters dispersed. Mo Yi had slipped away in the meantime.

The remaining Geists were scolded by Mr. Pu, who arrived late: if they wanted to become human, they should learn conscience first. Mr. Pu bowed to Lin Qingyan from afar and limped down the mountain, and the Geists, back in their original forms, followed him in a line.
9. The Gate of the Garden of Grotesqueries
In the end Mo Yi fell, her blade broken by Lin Qingyan's lightning. Just as Lin Qingyan was about to knock her out and take her in, fire plunged from the sky and split the lightning apart.

The one who appeared with the flames was an old Tianshi, whom Lin Qingyan greeted with full ceremony as 'Zushi.' The Old Tianshi recognized Mo Yi of the Shanhaizhong as an heir of 'the old carpenter.'

Mo Yi said the great hunt of a thousand years ago had gone against the ideals of their founder. And the way to end this war, she said, was to meet the master of the Garden of Grotesqueries and be allowed to search the garden for an object left behind by a vanished proxy.

Summoned by the Old Tianshi, Liang appeared and proposed entrusting this year's **Placation** to these guests. It is the rite in which the Sui Regulator checks on Sui's sleep each year and reinforces the seal. But a few days earlier a proxy had entered the tomb and not been heard from since, and even the Sui Regulator was at a loss.

'Tell them I allowed it,' said the Old Tianshi, and took Mo Yi along. When Liang took Yun Qingping's weiqi board and the Book of Kung Fu, the peak turned into a wide plain, and a gate hidden behind a folding screen appeared.
“Welcome to the Garden of Grotesqueries, everyone.”
Epilogue — A Record of the Town
Long ago, an anomaly from the Tomb of Sui struck a town. Its people died or scattered, and the objects left behind were steeped in that power and slowly gained consciousness.
The master of the Garden of Grotesqueries, 'Yi,' could not leave a ruin haunted by Geists beside his garden. Liang was ordered to bring only the useful ones to the garden and dispose of the rest.
Yi, who was away traveling at the time, was by Liang's account someone who could talk with a child for three days and nights to obtain a single stone.

Then one day a man returned to the ruins. As a child he had been the sole survivor of the disaster and had settled in Jiangqi. Now he repaired a house and tilled a field here, saying he would never leave again.
As the old saying goes, given enough time, even objects grow attached to a place. How much more so a person?

blocks.cap: A collapsed house. The man said that even broken, this was his home.

blocks.x: After seeing the man off, Liang called out a vase that had been hiding. The vase said it wanted neither to be disposed of nor to go to the garden.

According to the vase, it had been made by Lan Ke and Bai Jin. The two had said it would be the first thing in their new home, but they never came back after the disaster, and the vase had been waiting for them ever since.
The school's bamboo slips bowed again and again, begging Liang not to blame the vase, and a sword stood in front of them. Liang said he had not known they could feel longing like people.
Liang asked them. Did they remember how the town had looked back then? Could they bring it back? And were they willing to live among people?

Some time later, Yi laughed that he had told Liang to clear the ruins and Liang had built a town instead. Liang answered that he had promised the Sui Regulator he would oversee it, and Yi said a town so close to the garden would be enough to hold back the steps of those with ill intent.
Then he told Liang to tidy the garden and prepare to receive guests.

In that town with no place on any map, people and objects alike were holding on to what they could not let go. First give, then observe, and finally, take. The move Yun Qingping placed on that weiqi board was the question left to all of them.
