That night they sleep inside a hollow tree, and thanks to the dreamcatcher Oakcup gave them, no nightmares come. Instead, Magallan dreams she's a creature like Emperor, lying down beside a giant, pure-white hornbeast.

blocks.cap: A pure-white hornbeast asleep in a dream. Until the dream ended, she never saw its eyes.

blocks.x: In a dream within the dream, a shadow drags a contaminated trail toward the tree where everyone sleeps. Black snow punches a hole in Santalla's frost, but when a hornbeast leaps up, the hole is sealed over with frost again, and the shadow limps off after it.
In the morning, the Amma's Affection in her pocket has melted away. Typhon says Amma may have quietly cleared a great threat out of their path without them ever knowing.

Back on the road, the group comes across a mother rockhorn wounded by a demon-contaminated beast. Knowing it's too late to save her, Oakcup has Typhon cover the calf's eyes, then sings the mother on her way.
No more pain, no more sorrow♪ With the souls of all life... roam free on Sami's back♪
Oakcup decides to stay in the forest with the calf and wait for his teacher, and Santalla asks him to tell his teacher that Ursus's 'Black Mark' is tangled up in all this.

Around that time, somewhere in the forest, something contaminated kills a beast but leaves it uneaten, staggering off in search of new prey. Not far away, the sound of human breathing can be heard. Hffff... hoooo...
7. Siblings Who Came Home on the Same Day

Out of the forest, the group reaches the market of a wetland tribe. It is quiet. The bodies of warriors have come back from the Northern Front, and the tribe, which has no Snowpriest, asks Santalla to examine them.

Seven or eight years ago, during the great snowfall, this tribe received no revelation and split in two. The older brother followed Eikthyrnir's call north to stop the snowfall. The younger sister led the others south, guided by her divinations. The two even turned their weapons on each other, and afterward both left home and never returned.

But that sister came back on the same day as her brother's body. Known at home as **Ragna**, she is **Gitano**, a fortune-teller of Rhodes Island. She had come after seeing, in her crystal ball, a prophecy of misfortune befalling her brother.

Examining the bodies, Santalla notices something odd. There is not a drop of blood on the shaman's drum, yet its owner was gravely wounded without a weapon in hand, and half a bottle of vodka remains in his fur coat. Told that an Ursus caravan brought the bodies back, she promises to return for the funeral and goes after them.

Left behind, Magallan absently scoops muddy swamp water with the empty flagon the caravan gave her, and only comes to when Typhon says, "Let go." A vine Typhon wraps around her finger soon calms her. But that remedy only works against demons.

Meanwhile, the tribe's shamans argue over the funeral. Some want to send the dead home along the waterways. Others say the dead are now part of the calamity. Gitano divines the wishes of the dead. Most want the funeral. Only one stays silent.
That night, the tribe loads their belongings onto boats and sets out on the water with the bodies. In this rite, the dead sink with the boats, and the living leave their home behind.

blocks.cap: The horn sounded. From now on, no one may look back.

blocks.x: On the boat, Gitano speaks to her brother **Lazal** through a fifth divination. She lost so many people getting out of the blizzard that she simply lacked the courage to look back. It was not resentment of him that kept her away.
Brother, why will you not answer me?
The crystal ball shows only darkness and mist.
8. Don't Look Back

Meanwhile, by the swamp, the Ursus caravan drinks and remembers that day. The Sami warriors lost their lives helping them, and never even knew what had happened. One of them never made peace with his sister. Giving that man's flagon away to the young lady has weighed on them ever since.

On the funeral boats, the beacon Magallan dropped into the water keeps moving beneath the surface until its signal cuts out. Gitano pushes herself to divine again, but the fate of the dead is pitch black, and one of them is still silent. Typhon says the swamp is pulling them in.

At the same moment, Santalla catches up with the caravan and asks whether they saw black blood when they moved the bodies. The traders, who claimed to know nothing beyond a Liberi who went off to Čappat alone, say that much they saw clearly.
Santalla cries out, "How could I make such a terrible mistake?!"

Back on the swamp, Typhon raises a current to hold up the sinking boats. The contamination of the countless northern warriors buried here has built up into a single body, she says, and some of the latest dead must have been victims of the Disaster too. She has the people turn the boats around and stays alone at the very back.
Don't look back. Follow the others and row. Leave what's behind you to me.

For more than a decade, Typhon has dreamed of everything around her turning pitch black. She knew that if she turned her head, she would see her parents. She never once looked back. A hunter must always keep her eyes on the prey before her.

blocks.cap: Between the Disaster and the people. The place a hunter with a contaminated bow must stand.

blocks.x: As her arrow flies beneath the water, a whisper in Sami answers. "Water withered, hard ice becomes." The swamp freezes in an instant, and as promised, Santalla returns with a blizzard.

But Gitano looks back after all, and sees the shadows seeping out of the contaminated bodies drawing near. Typhon has Magallan take her hand. Santalla tells her not to blame herself, and not to think of her brother as the source of this.

The darkness swallows arrows and Arts alike. Santalla steps forward: "I made a mistake, so the responsibility is mine too." Unable to help herself, Magallan looks back. All she sees is endless darkness.

In that moment, thorny brambles grind the shadows to pieces. Beyond a wooden palisade stand the warriors of the Treescar tribe. A single man with a hammer steps forward and sweeps away every last one of the transformed warriors. It is Eikthyrnir.
9. One Who Says Endure, One Who Leaves

Eikthyrnir had been heading south to persuade the departing tribes to stay, and arrived early after receiving a call for help. When the wetland shaman says the migration cannot be helped, he answers that there is nowhere left to retreat. Even when told that fear becomes a breeding ground for demons, he does not waver.
Everyone feels fear. But anyone can overcome it.
Meanwhile, Magallan, filming the conversation with her drone, writes down the name they use for the Disaster: 'Andskotarnir,' Sami for 'enemy.' It sounds like a word she has heard somewhere before.
And Typhon, belatedly, answers the question Santalla asked her during the fight. Honestly, she is afraid too. When she hunts, she simply has no time to be.
Eikthyrnir recognizes Santalla as well: the shaman who hesitated, unable to leave the Old Tree's shade, and never became a Snowpriest.

She tells him her Oripathy leaves her little time. He replies that revenge is hollow, and so it never ends—will she still wander the icefield in pursuit of it? Santalla does not answer. She only says it is time to leave for Čappat with her companions.

Meanwhile, Gitano has left alone, saying only that she will contact Rhodes Island once she has sorted out her thoughts. In the empty village everyone has abandoned, she murmurs, "Brother, I now know what you saw when you looked back."
Sitting by the water, she spots a flagon sunk beneath the surface. Carved on it is a prayer of blessing from home, one she knows well.

blocks.who: The prayer carved on the flagon
blocks.x: Grant my home lasting peace. May my people rest easy, like snow falling in a dream.
Sleep now. One day, we will all return to a calm and quiet dream.
Epilogue. The Journey of Discovery Must Never End

At last they reach **Čappat**, Sami's southernmost city, where a resort district caters to Columbian tourists. Santalla finds 'the coordinates from the transmission' in Magallan's Ursine-language guidebook and says this is where they part ways.

blocks.cap: Čappat, at Sami's southern tip. A resort district built for southerners.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, the client waiting for Typhon turns out to be Arges herself. She had glimpsed a fleeting fate in which Typhon would deliver a box in this town.

At the Rhine Lab office, the box Magallan receives bears Director Maryam's employee number. Arges had followed the missing expedition into the icefield. After they met the demons, only Arges and the box's owner survived. That survivor went on alone, deep into the icefield, leaving behind the box and a single message.
The journey of discovery must never end.

Inside the box is a single colorless flower, like a shadow cast on ice, with no telling where its roots might be. The moment the sample box is opened, the air in the lab is stained an invisible color. When Typhon's shout brings her back to her senses, every pane of glass is shattered, and Magallan hurriedly seals the flower away again.
Only then does Magallan remember those words. "Once the box is opened, Andskotarnir will notice." ...And she has already opened it.

Why didn't Professor Mary send word not to open it? Magallan murmurs that it's strange. The researchers, though, are thrilled—phenomena that defy common sense are science's newest gold mine—and want to put together an even bigger expedition. Typhon says nothing.

A little later, Typhon calls Magallan outside and passes on Arges's words: the southerners will come to know Sami in their own way, so there is no need to stop them. Still, Typhon adds, she has to warn her. A Cyclops's foresight always ends in tragedy, so if anything happens, Magallan must come find her.
Magallan suddenly feels a chill and looks back. Outside the window, a blizzard has begun to rage.

Around that time, Santalla is interrogating a captured Liberi with her cold. The man, who called her 'the Witch,' finally confesses. 'Black Mark' is a missing member of the Emperor's Royal Guard, wholly devoured by demons and defiling the land of Sami.
We are Sami's fangs, sinking into the demons' tracks. And you... are not even worthy of being called 'enemies.'
That is the end of her business with the Ursines. Fate has once again turned her gaze back to the contaminated land, Santalla says; the time has come to return to the blizzards of the icefield.
Don't answer. Don't look back. With everything she learned crossing Sami written in her notebook, Magallan now prepares to head back into the endless icefield beyond.

act14mini.tagline: A boy who called himself a bandit chief is caught by a wandering swordswoman and taken back to the home he left three years ago, only to find his name about to be put on a stranger's death. About the record left behind by someone who vanished without a name.

chars.name: Qiubai
chars.desc: A swordswoman who wanders the jianghu. She takes nothing that is not hers and always pays what she owes.

chars.name: Fang Xiaoshi
chars.desc: A boy from Moushan Village who left home to make a name for himself.

chars.name: Hunter
chars.desc: Fang Xiaoshi's father. A sick former hunter with a bent back.

chars.name: Clan Elder
chars.desc: The aged village headman and clan elder of Moushan Village.

chars.name: Saga
chars.desc: A wandering monk from Higashi.

chars.name: Mulberry
chars.desc: A member of the disaster relief team Chun-qian.

chars.name: Wind Chimes
chars.desc: A Catastrophe Messenger who travels the mountain country alone.

terms.name: Moushan Village
terms.desc: A poor village buried in the remote mountains of northwestern Yan, home to about a hundred people, all surnamed Zhou. Legend says an ancestor dug through a mountain to found it a thousand years ago.

terms.name: Yishan Temple
terms.desc: Moushan Village's temple to the ancestor who moved a mountain with a single hoe and founded the village.

terms.name: Sanmusan
terms.desc: The field Fang Xiaoshi and his father worked. It was once barren ground where not even weeds would grow.

terms.name: Chidao
terms.desc: The road network Yan has laid to reach the lands nomadic cities cannot. When a Catastrophe destroys it, it is built again.

terms.name: Shanhaizhong
terms.desc: A gang of bandits that lives by plunder, based in a mountain cave.

terms.name: Yumen
terms.desc: A nomadic city of Yan that runs across the desert. Sandstorms blow there all year round.

terms.name: Chun-qian
terms.desc: A disaster relief organization. It carries out rescues at disaster sites and investigates the damage and its causes.

blocks.x: In the northwest of Yan, deep in mountain country where ridge follows ridge with no end in sight, lies **Moushan Village**. Legend says an ancestor dug through a mountain with a single hoe to make it, a thousand years ago. About a hundred people live there, all surnamed Zhou, all of them poor.

Three years ago, a boy named **Fang Xiaoshi** ran away from that village, swearing he would not return until his name was known throughout the land. The vow broke when he was caught by **Qiubai**, a swordswoman wandering the jianghu.
And the village he was dragged back to had already decided to use his name for something else.
1. The Boy Who Called Himself a Bandit Chief

Cornered at the edge of a cliff, the boy pulled out an explosive and shouted that he was the chief of the Shanhaizhong bandits. In truth, the gang had been almost entirely cut down after some of its members went to Yumen and crossed this swordswoman. The boy was only a young errand runner who had sold the burdenbeast left in his care and traded it for jerky.

Among his scattered belongings was a house key with a talisman tied to it, marked 'Moushan Village.' Instead of handing him over to the authorities, Qiubai decided to take him home. When he drew a dagger and said he would die before going back, her blade was at his throat before he could blink.
They walked together for two weeks. At the last inn before the mountains, the boy wrote 'I've been kidnapped' on the table in tea and ran.

blocks.cap: The only inn in the last town before the mountains. From here on, it is more than a week of hard mountain road.

blocks.x: He was caught again in the forest, and in that forest they met a starving tuskbeast. Qiubai shielded the boy where he had fallen, and the beast's claws raked her.
That night the boy offered her a wound salve he had made the way his father taught him. To show it was not poison, he cut his own forearm and put it on himself first.

The boy said that anyone who is not feared by everyone just gets pushed around. Qiubai answered that the only way to make no enemies is to treat no one as an enemy. She refused when he asked to become her disciple.
When he asked where her home was, her answer was short. "The place is gone, and so are the people." She told him only that her name meant 'vengeance' and 'snow.'
2. The Road No One Knows Who Builds
A few days later, on the last ridge before the village, the boy stood on tiptoe hoping to glimpse Yumen. All he could see was a gray road winding across the wasteland: the Chidao.

The boy asked why anyone would build a road a Catastrophe could ruin overnight. Qiubai answered that every place the nomadic cities cannot reach has to rely on roads like this. If it is destroyed, it gets built again. But very few people remember that someone is always doing that work.
The boy made a vow on the spot. The next time he stood here, he would be a hero whose name was known throughout the land.

Then they crossed the mountain and reached Moushan Village. A villager plowing a field saw the boy, said "You're alive?", and ran to fetch the village head. Beside the old shrine at the village entrance was a fresh grave. Not knowing whose it was, the boy bowed before it in earnest.

blocks.cap: Moushan Village. Though it was the end of March, the acacia trees in these mountains were still withered.

blocks.x: The house was empty. While the boy went looking for his father, villagers who had heard the news gathered and surrounded the two of them without a word.
3. The Child Who Blew Up the Temple

Three years earlier, the village had decided to move the Yishan Temple, its shrine to the ancestor, onto the boy's family field, Sanmusan. This was after his father had spent long years making that weedless ground fertile. Theirs was the only household in the village with a different surname.
The boy, eleven or twelve at the time, blew up the temple with homemade explosives he had learned to make by watching his father. Wounded by the blast, he fled bleeding into the wilderness.

Now a man with a back bent like a bow came into the yard carrying timber on his shoulders. It was the boy's father, the **Hunter**. He did not answer his son. He held out the animal hides left in the house and asked that they be given to the woman as compensation.

Meanwhile, the old man **Zhou Shun**, village headman and Clan Elder, told Qiubai about the village's troubles. Drought and heavy rain had come by turns, and the harvests had failed for years. When the child disappeared three years ago, the whole village searched for days and never found him. Who could hold a grudge against a child barely ten years old, he said.

In the cabin, father and son sat facing each other awkwardly. The timber the father had carried in was meant for his own coffin. The coffin wood he had saved before had already been given up to repair the ruined Yishan Temple. The boy promised to behave from now on.
At dusk, Qiubai granted the boy his request for a farewell he had read in martial arts novels, and left the village.
Until we meet again, in the jianghu.

blocks.cap: The village road at nightfall. The Clan Elder walked her to the village entrance in silence.

blocks.x: That night the whole village gathered at the Yishan Temple. The Clan Elder said they would put the past behind them and formally accept the Hunter and his son into the clan. Then he asked the boy:
**"Xiaoshi, for the sake of this village... would you be a dead man, just this once?"**
4. The Boy Lying Beside the Chidao
The village has an old story. A man whose way was blocked by a mountain ground a stone into a hoe and began to dig. After half a year, the villagers joined him one by one.
A voice from somewhere asked why they insisted on standing against the mountain. The man answered:
The mountain will not change. But the people who stand against it will keep growing in number, without end.

The voice said they had been making a racket on its tail for more than five years, and that it would leave. The next morning the mountain was gone without a trace. The villagers said a god, moved by their devotion, had moved the mountain for them.
A few days ago, after a night of heavy rain, a mudslide brought down a stretch of the Chidao outside the village. Beside it lay a boy no one knew, dead, a camera clutched tight in his hand.

Anyone who dies on the job building the Chidao is owed more than a million in compensation. One villager looked at the dead boy's face and said that if the Hunter's son were still in the village, he would be just about that age.

Afterward, the Clan Elder prostrated himself alone before the ancestor's statue in the Yishan Temple. With that money they could fix the ditches and buy irrigation equipment and seed, he said, and so he had no choice but to borrow that child's body and Fang Xiaoshi's name. At the end he added: "I don't want to be a bad man..."
Someone behind the ancestor's statue heard that prayer. It was **Saga**, a wandering monk from Higashi, who had stopped to rest in the temple out of the rain.

blocks.cap: The monk, seated with her back against the ancestor's statue. She had not meant to eavesdrop.

blocks.x: 5. Timber Passed Off as a Bow

Xiaoshi was then locked in a storehouse. A neighbor woman who brought his food tried to soothe him. It was only a name, she said, and if he made this sacrifice for the village, everyone would look after him and his father.

The boy spat out the food and shouted, "I want to live like a person!" But when she told him this was the will of the whole village, and that the Clan Elder and even his own father had agreed, he had nothing left to say.

Around then, Qiubai, whom everyone thought had left, opened the door of the Hunter's cabin. He was carving the timber he had carried in the day before, and he claimed he was making a new bow. She asked whether anyone made a bow from dry, stiff walnut.
"I thought you were making a grave marker. Xiaoshi's grave marker."

blocks.cap: The Hunter's cabin. The timber, sawn in half, was slowly taking on a squared shape.

blocks.x: At first the Hunter had refused. But when he heard the compensation would come to him first, he thought of using the money to go and search for his missing son. Then his son came back on his own.
Now he wanted only one thing. Once this was over, his son could spend at least half of the life ahead of him in peace in this village.

Qiubai asked what the villagers would do if Xiaoshi refused to the end to give up his name and resisted hard enough to ruin the plan. Once evil raises its head, she said, it does not easily stop. She would stay in the village for a while.

Meanwhile, some children secretly took the camera from the Clan Elder's room and switched it on. The person on the screen, they said, was the Messenger lady who often came to the village. The Clan Elder muttered, "That boy... he didn't come alone...?"
6. The Investigator Who Wasn't

The Clan Elder had traps laid on the mountain path to keep the Messenger out of the village. But the next day, the first to come up that path was **Mulberry**, a member of the disaster relief team **Chun-qian**. The villager watching the path, knowing nothing, gave her directions.

He stayed at his post, stepped into a trap his fellow villagers had set, and was hurt. The Messenger, passing by, looked at his leg. A poor liar, he ended up admitting that he had been sent to stop her.

The Clan Elder, waiting at the village entrance, took Mulberry for an investigator from the authorities. He told her Fang Xiaoshi had been a good boy who died guarding Chidao supplies, then asked when the compensation would come. But Mulberry had come only to investigate the cause of the mudslide.

She said the slopes on both sides of the Chidao are reinforced with protective works in advance, so they should not collapse unless something unexpected happened. When she said she would go up the mountain to look, the Clan Elder tried to hold her back, citing the busy farming season. Saga stepped forward and offered to guide her.

Meanwhile, at the fresh grave by the village entrance, the villagers hurried to raise the grave marker. The Hunter dropped it, asking who could promise how they would treat him and his son once the money was paid. The villagers seized him by the arms and dragged him along.
He hung his head like a broken-in burdenbeast, and the marker, not yet carved with a single character, sank into the ground little by little. Then a sword flashed, and the marker split in two.

blocks.cap: When she left Yumen, she had said she would find a place where this sword could serve its purpose.

blocks.x: The cut was uneven. Is it the way of a hero to draw a sword on unarmed people? But if one does not right an injustice, what is the reason to carry a sword at all?
A corpse, a name, a sum of money. Can you only find a way to live by trampling on the dignity of others?
7. Powder Left on the Ridge

When someone shouted that a hero knew nothing of their lives, Qiubai answered that she was no different from them. In her memory were the government notice announcing a purge of those in league with the river bandits, her mother begging for it all to stop, and her father telling her to blame the high mountains and the fierce currents.

Five years from Jiangqi to Yumen, and five more wandering borderlands like this one. Had even a little wickedness crept in, she said, she too would have become someone like the Shanhaizhong. She understood their hardship, but it was no reason to commit injustice. Never.
As soon as she heard that Xiaoshi had been taken to the mountain behind the village, the swordswoman vanished. The Hunter stood dazed for a moment, then ran after her with everything he had.

At the same time, Mulberry and Saga had climbed to the ridge where the landslide began. Examining the protective works, which had not collapsed, Mulberry found powder residue. It was not the standard explosive used by construction crews but a crude, old-fashioned homemade one.
On her way here, Saga had seen explosives like that used to seal sand beast nests. And where a stone she kicked came to rest, a line of vehicle tracks ran on, almost buried in sand.

blocks.cap: The highest point, where the landslide began. The protective works stood intact.

blocks.x: At dusk, the Clan Elder, stunned and empty, walked aimlessly outside the village and sank to the ground. The exhausted Messenger appeared before him and set down a heavy package.

It was the subsidy the Clan Elder had applied to the authorities for two years before. It had only been delayed by the Catastrophe; the authorities had not forgotten Moushan Village. Once this year's sowing was done, she said, the village would have good irrigation equipment too.

It felt as if the mountain the ancestor had cleared away a thousand years ago had come back to press down on his chest. When the Clan Elder said to release Fang Xiaoshi at once, a villager brought word.
"Fang Xiaoshi... he jumped off the mountain..."
8. 'Fang Xiaoshi' Must Not Be Alive

A little earlier, atop the cliff on the mountain behind the village. Xiaoshi said he would go down and expose everything, and the villager Zhou Si drove him to the edge of the drop. At that moment Qiubai appeared and knocked the two men out in an instant.

blocks.cap: Atop the cliff behind the village. The spring wind on this mountain was as dry as ever.

blocks.x: "This is the second time I've saved your life. I hope there won't be a third."

The Hunter came up late, gasping for breath, and caught his son by the arm as the boy tried to go down to the village. Only then did the boy understand. His father had not come to save him. He had come to stop him.

The Hunter told Qiubai that people with a sword and martial skill never truly find themselves with nowhere to turn. In these remote mountains, a sword can do nothing about barren land or a fickle sky. Please, he said, leave us be.
"It's because I understand that I can't stand by and watch," she answered. Xiaoshi stepped in front of her. This was between him and his father, he said. He would speak for himself.

The boy counted off what his father had given up. When the village wanted to move the temple onto their field because their surname was different, his father allowed it. Now they wanted his name, and his father allowed that too. If they asked next for the house and their lives, would he allow that as well?

The son said he would go to a nomadic city, find work, learn martial arts, and cure his father's illness. The Hunter said, "You really do take after your mother." His wife had wanted to leave the mountains and live a different life. She went off with a peddler, and he chased them all the way into the wilderness and managed to bring back only their son.
She died a few years ago. The death compensation sent as her son's share went to repairing the Yishan Temple her son had destroyed.
He had meant to leave the house behind and go looking for his son once the compensation came. Now that his son had returned, he could not let him go again, whatever it took.

"If the peaceful life you're talking about means having even my name taken from me, I don't want it!" The boy shouted that he was not a weed on the mountain or a beast in the wilderness. The Hunter said that if his son went down, he himself would jump off the cliff.
No one spoke. Qiubai quietly took a few steps toward the edge.
"Dad, everyone can only be happy if Fang Xiaoshi dies, right?"
Yes... 'Fang Xiaoshi' must not be alive.
As a small child, the boy had liked to kick stones off the cliff and listen to them fall. Now he was the stone.
As he fell, he remembered the last look in the eyes of the beast in the forest. How bitter and afraid it must have been. And how free it must have felt.
And the wind rose up beneath the boy's back.
9. The Sword With No Edge
Around then, Saga switched on again the camera the village children had been handling. What remained on it was a woman's angry voice. "Stop following me!"

At the Yishan Temple, the Clan Elder knelt with his forehead pressed to the cracked floor tiles. He truly had not known, he said. Not that an investigator would come, and not that a boy would be walking the Chidao on that rainy night.

**It was the Clan Elder who had planted the explosives on the mountain.** He had thought that if the Chidao collapsed, the repairs would drag on and the villagers could earn more in wages. He used the early spring rain to make it look like an accident.
The explosives were the ones he had confiscated from Xiaoshi's room three years earlier, after the temple was destroyed.

blocks.cap: The Yishan Temple. The clay statue of the ancestor gave no answer.

blocks.x: Saga appeared, eating fruit from the offering table, and said she had heard everything, his prayer a few days earlier included. The Clan Elder said he would never have done this if she had come just a little sooner. Saga asked in return who among men harbors no evil thought in his heart.
She told the story of a swordsman. He no longer wished to kill, so he never put an edge on the sword he had forged with such care. But it is not the sword that wounds, she said. It is oneself.
Evil thought and evil deed differ by a single word, yet their consequences lie as far apart as heaven and earth.

The Clan Elder had hidden one last explosive in his robes, meaning to take his own life. Saga cut it in two and asked him: if that boy had not passed along that road that night, would he be trying to die as he was now?
The old man said he would confess everything to the authorities. Then, with the halved explosive before him, he pressed his forehead to the ground once more.
10. The Nameless
When the boy opened his eyes, Qiubai was beside him. "That makes three times I've saved you."
She said she had no intention of going back to the village, and that if he had nowhere to go, he could come with her for now. The boy answered, "...Okay."

blocks.cap: The road that does not lead back to the village. The boy followed the swordswoman.

blocks.x: Only then did Qiubai tell her own story. When the government army attacked the river fort at Jiangqi, her father, a river bandit, was killed along with all his comrades. Only she escaped. "In this country, I am a person without a name too."
There are many nameless people in this land, she said. Like her, like him, and like the boy who nearly became 'Fang Xiaoshi.'
Of course a name matters to a person. But what matters more is what that name stands for.

She said she would teach him martial arts for a while. But if he gained strength and turned to evil, she would kill him herself. Then, saying it was something like 'until we meet again in the jianghu,' she added one more line. "The days ahead are long."
Epilogue. The Director's Notes

Some months earlier, a man who had only ever walked on the artificial ground of nomadic cities was diagnosed with Oripathy. He decided to spend the time he had left filming a documentary about the people of forgotten corners of the land, and he left with nothing but a short farewell letter to his parents and friends.
At a post office, he asked a Messenger setting out with 337 letters and 25 packages on her back to let him travel with her. He said he had lost his ID on the way.

blocks.cap: In front of the post office. The Messenger, loaded with a mountain of letters and packages, sets out for the mountain country.

blocks.x: The Messenger was Infected. She had stayed alone in her hometown after all the young people left for the nomadic cities. If she left, she asked, who would deliver the letters? With the camera off, she also told him how, one rainy night, she had rammed a falling rock with her horns to protect the cargo, and broken her left horn.

But when he said this place had to change, she finally lost her temper. He had never once tried to understand the people here, she said; his concern was nothing but pity steeped in superiority. What Saga heard on the camera was her voice from that night.

Some time later, the repaired camera was in the hands of the Messenger, **Wind Chimes**. Mulberry checked the missing-persons records at Chun-qian headquarters, but no one matched the boy who died in the landslide. Wind Chimes said little beyond the fact that he too had been Infected, and that she would keep looking.

When she returned to Moushan Village two months later, there were more wells, new irrigation equipment stood along the paddy ridges, and the acacia at the village entrance was in bloom. The children said that since the Clan Elder left, there had been plenty of work in the village: digging wells, cutting channels, rebuilding the Yishan Temple.

The children, who had built a tractor out of discarded Chidao construction tools, said they would go to Lungmen someday. Wind Chimes raised the camera and filmed the two of them, so that even when they were no longer here, they could remember what home looked like.
Like the forgotten villages, like the people who have left, they too may one day quietly disappear. But there is a way to leave a trace that they were here.

And on the camera was an apology he had recorded alone. He had never meant to look down on her, he said. He had only wanted to accomplish something, as she had. He hoped this letter would reach her someday.
After that there was one more short scene. A boy who had run into him in the wilderness asked whether being recorded in this machine meant lasting forever, then stood in front of the camera.
I'm Fang Xiaoshi! A man out to become the greatest hero of all! Remember my name. You're sure to hear it again somewhere before long.
"Yes, I'll be sure to remember." The boy said something terrifying was chasing him, shouted that he had to go, and ran off.

blocks.cap: The wilderness where the fleeing boy passed in front of the camera.

blocks.x: Fang Xiaoshi wanted his name known throughout the land, and Moushan Village wanted to trade that name for compensation money. And the one who promised to remember that name, leaving not even his own behind, very nearly went into the ground as 'Fang Xiaoshi.'

act12mini.tagline: A knight who laid down his sword to search for his vanished family borrows another man's blade to stop an old friend who would wake Kazimierz with war. One letter he never answered, and one last question.

blocks.x: A man was walking the late-autumn plains of southern Kazimierz with no sword, no armor, and no attendants. **Młynar**, of the Nearl family. Once he had stood against the powerful and taken in wandering refugees. Now he was retracing the villages he had passed through long ago, following the traces of his vanished family.

blocks.cap: The late-autumn plains of southern Kazimierz. Młynar remembered every road here.

blocks.x: He had no need to ask the way. But at the end of that road waited friends he had parted from long ago, and a letter he had never answered.
1. The Knight Without a Sword

November 27th, a village in the southern countryside. An old teacher named **Sommer**, writing out a warning notice, recognized Młynar. More than twenty years earlier he had fled Leithanien, cut off his antlers, and lived as a Kuranta ever since. He had not forgotten that Młynar once looked the other way about who he really was.

A Campaign Knight had delivered the notice. Bandits had appeared nearby, and there had been an attack inside the city of Dzwonek. Meanwhile, Gale Industries, which was building Dzwonek's new district, was hiring even the Infected. As nearby villages sold their land to corporations, more than a few young people meant to take the money and go live in the city.
Młynar was looking for a Campaign Knight in golden armor. Sommer answered that every Campaign Knight seen around here in recent years had worn silver, and offered to guide him.
Told that no work vehicles had come through lately, Młynar declined the offer. He remembered the way.
In that moment, old voices passed through him. An Infected wanderer begging to be saved, and the Grand Knight's answer.
Sorry, Młynar. I can't answer that.
A sharp horn cut the memory short. A large General Chamber of Commerce transport ground its way down the dirt road.

blocks.cap: Through exhaust and dust, a General Chamber of Commerce transport cuts across the late-autumn plain.

blocks.x: The knight without a sword faced the great mass of steel in silence. Only once he was alone did he walk slowly on, along the road he had marked. Beside the tire tracks, his steps left no trace.
Sommer, left behind, murmured to himself. For what reason had a knight of Kazimierz laid down his sword, and for what reason did he still go on? And perhaps it was time he, too, left this place.
2. The Letter That Was Never Answered

Around that time, in a village near the valley, **Czcibor**, the silver-armored captain of a Campaign Knight order, came to see **Toland**, chief of a band of Sarkaz bounty hunters. The two were old friends.

While investigating the attack, the Campaign Knights had detained several of Toland's men. Czcibor promised to release them unharmed, but asked Toland to keep away, for now, from the corporations handling the redevelopment of Dzwonek.
Through the window of the hideout stood the industrial park built where the manor of House Paleniskos had once been. Asked whether he missed the old days, Czcibor answered only: a little.

blocks.cap: The hideout of Toland's band. From here, one could see clear across the valley.

blocks.x: Toland recognized the sword at his hip. Czcibor had run into Młynar near the factory and taken the sword from him, offering to have it maintained. Toland said he had assumed Młynar would head for Ursus when he set out to find his family.

Then Czcibor brought up a personal grievance. Years ago, before **Celina** was taken to the Grand Knight Territory and died an unjust death, he had written to Młynar asking for help. No reply ever came. Today, Młynar had admitted that he read the letter, but would say nothing more.
When did he become the sort of man who'd turn away when faced with questions of right and wrong?
Toland asked whether he wanted Młynar as an ally, or wanted revenge. Czcibor only asked him not to misunderstand.
3. The Undefeated Lawyer

The next day, on a country lane barely fit for cars. **Deszcz**, a lawyer whose rental car had broken down and left her wandering the wilds, was walking with Młynar because they happened to be heading the same way. She said she had seen him three years earlier at a Gale Industries bidding meeting, a sales employee of a large corporation sweating as he entertained clients. He said only that he did not remember.

Her case concerned the land of the village of **Twierdza**. Marek, a noble knight, had mortgaged the village land to Gale Industries and then sold it again to the villagers. Only after he died did the villagers, some of whom had gone into debt to buy it, learn that the land was not theirs.
And Deszcz was Gale Industries' representative.

Hamm, the villagers' lawyer, demanded housing and a relocation subsidy of 80,000 marks per household. Deszcz offered housing in the city and 800 marks for demolition, then laid out, one after another, the rough mountain roads, the bankrupt brewery, and the figures on dwindling farm households. The land, she stated, already belonged to Gale Industries by law. This money was not a price for land but compensation.

With that, the negotiation was over. At the tavern, Deszcz admitted that whatever she saved out of the million marks Gale Industries had entrusted to her would be her cut. The bartender, who had been boasting of a beer that could only be brewed with Twierdza's hops, said that with the land sold, there might be no hops the next time.

blocks.cap: The tavern in Twierdza. Her negotiation done, Deszcz raised a glass 'to a smooth agreement.'

blocks.x: When Hamm remarked bitterly that the word 'fairness' appears nowhere in the legal code, Deszcz said the bartender would throw her out if he knew she was the crooked lawyer who had slashed the compensation, and stepped outside for some air.
4. A Constellation Shaped Like Scales

That night, outside the Grand Knight Territory, stars could still be seen in the sky. Deszcz remembered her first day at work, when she had vowed to uphold the dignity and fairness of the law and had been laughed at for it.

blocks.cap: Twierdza at night. It had been years since Deszcz last saw a sky full of stars.

blocks.x: Młynar, held in the village by the blocked road, handed her the severed lanyard of her ID and said someone seemed to be after her. Deszcz asked whether, three years ago, he had known of a rival company's shoddy methods and won the contract to protect a hospital construction project. Młynar called that naive, took it as an insult, and left.
Deszcz lay down in a harvested field and traced the stars with her finger.
Where are the stars that make up Libra right now?

The next day, she handed Hamm the contract between Gale Industries and Marek, calling it 'a test.' It had been signed not by Marek but by his son, a Campaign Knight, and there was no document proving he had the authority to act for his father.

Claiming she had merely lost the documents by mistake, Deszcz told him he should have challenged the legality of the ownership from the start. Asked why she would take the risk, she said only that she wanted to keep drinking Twierdza's beer.

Meanwhile, the village mail carrier was talking about an old man among those killed the night before, when a car bound for Dzwonek crashed. In more than ten years he had never sent anyone a letter, and, unusually for a man who taught others, he had never even bought a newspaper.
When Młynar said he was going to Dzwonek, Deszcz went with him. Before looking for a new job, she said, she was giving herself a vacation.
5. There Will Always Be Sacrifices

Some years earlier, a letter from Czcibor had reached Młynar. Celina, his most loyal knight, his comrade-in-arms, and the one he loved, had been arrested. Before the National Council and the General Chamber of Commerce he was powerless, so he asked Młynar to submit the enclosed evidence in his place.
I simply ask that one worthy knight save another.
That letter, put back into its already-opened envelope, lay buried in a pile of papers on a cluttered shelf.
Then, November 29th, Dzwonek. The news reported that **Zeno** Shelvin, ringleader of the Infected riot, had turned himself in.

blocks.cap: The streets of Dzwonek. A public screen announced the riot leader's surrender.

blocks.x: Watching the screen, **Flametail** and **Ashlock** could not believe it. The two knights of Pinus Sylvestris had come to Dzwonek on their first mission for Rhodes Island, and two days earlier they had been attacked in the middle of the riot. The one who had hidden them then was Zeno.

Zeno, an Infected foreman and a fan of Ashlock, had told them he ended up in this by supporting the union protesting against Gale Industries, and asked them not to tell anyone they had met him. At the very hour the riot broke out, he had been with the two knights.

Meanwhile, Młynar stood before the statue symbolizing the friendship between the two nations. A **Leithanian Noble** who introduced himself as a tourist asked whether he had been a Campaign Knight. Młynar replied that he, too, was only a tourist passing through.
In the meantime, the two knights found Zeno in an unfinished Gale Industries building, held captive by plainclothes fighters. But Zeno said he could not go with them.
The most my life is worth is making my family's lives a bit better...

Fleeing their pursuers, Flametail thrust her sword at a presence behind her, and the man who caught the blade in his gauntlet was Młynar. When he heard what had happened, Ashlock cried out that no one else should be sacrificed to the schemes of politics and corporations. They were the same words written in Czcibor's letter.
Młynar glanced back, but the end of the alley was empty. There will always be sacrifices, he said. Perhaps you and I already are.
Shortly after, Młynar persuaded Gale Industries to drop the charges, and Zeno was released.

Only then did Zeno confess. Gale Industries, backed into a corner, needed a convenient explanation, and he needed money for his family. And the one who had proposed the deal was **a Campaign Knight**.

At the same hour, a voice on the other end of a phone line, hearing that the Dzwonek deployment had been approved, murmured to itself. That Nearl still believes in justice and still stands against them. Then why, back then?
6. The Abandoned District

The night of November 30th, Dzwonek. **Szewczyk**, a retired arena knight once called 'Plastic,' had been living in hiding with his family in this frontier city, hoping the name would be forgotten. When the news reported another riot, he put on full armor and went out to bring his son home.

Around then, the Leithanian Noble, with only his bodyguard Aloisia, visited the abandoned district, a slum. Młynar was there too with Zeno, looking for someone called 'the Weaver.' Then flames rose from the streets.

blocks.cap: The abandoned district. Vagrants and the Infected lived hidden among empty buildings and containers.

blocks.x: Separated from his bodyguard, the noble saw a child pinned under the edge of a steel sheet. Fearing someone might be after him, he did not use his Arts and stayed hidden. Młynar, arriving after, freed the child and sent them to the hospital, then called the noble out of hiding.
At the same time, Szewczyk pressed money into refugees' hands to get them to bring the children out, and pinned a falling sign to the wall with a single arrow.
The noble confided to Młynar that he envied Kazimierz. He wanted to see for himself whom this city drove out, learn from it, and change his own domain.

When a second explosion went off, the noble used his Arts to open the door of a room from which a voice had been calling for help. The person in the rubble did not move. Only a communications device was still running, relaying military transmissions about platoon deployments near Dzwonek and a 'coming war' with Leithanien.
Someone smashed the device, and the noble went pale. He shouted to his bodyguard, who had come up behind Młynar: "Aloisia! Kill him!"
It was Zeno who seized the noble's Arts unit and stood in the way. The moment Młynar shoved him aside, an arrow grazed Zeno's cheek.

While Szewczyk, who had loosed the arrow, demanded answers from Młynar Nearl for keeping company with the riot's ringleader, the Leithanians fled. Młynar told Szewczyk that if he was looking for a purple-haired child, they would have gone to the hospital, then left to meet the bounty hunters.
7. Too Late for an Interview

A little later, at the district's exit, reporters crowded around Szewczyk, calling him the hero who had saved twenty-two children. Long ago, on the day he stepped into the arena, he had said he would take on the big corporations in plastic armor he made himself, and declare in his victory interview that he had made it.

blocks.cap: The arena. Szewczyk stood here in plastic armor he had made with his own hands.

blocks.x: "It's too late for an interview." Saying he had to go get his son, he pushed the reporters aside.

Around that time, at a camp in the forest, Czcibor was receiving a report. Apart from one informant sacrificed as planned, there were no casualties, and the target had returned to the hotel with his bodyguard. Had the target been caught up in the incident in the abandoned district, Czcibor said with regret, they could have seized the upper hand in negotiations.
That night, a letter from Toland arrived. He had obtained records of the cooperation between Gale Industries and the knights. It was time to stop.

Meanwhile, at Szewczyk's home. His son said he wanted to be a knight who saved his friends, like his dad. Szewczyk began, "That wasn't even me who..." then trailed off, and told him not to even dream of becoming a knight.
The bigger the dream, the bigger the disappointment.
8. Give Me a Sword
November 30th, 11:20 P.M., a village outside Dzwonek. Młynar left Zeno in Toland's care. In Toland's hands were materials the lawyer from the Grand Knight Territory had brought in person.

Behind Marek's son, who had signed the Twierdza contract, stood the knights. At their request, Gale Industries had recruited Infected workers and paid the press to inflate the attacks. Czcibor had detained the bounty hunters to keep them from reaching these records.

The next day was the opening ceremony of the 'Voice of the Knights.' Toland said the worst outcome would be for Młynar to watch Leithanians die in front of the statue of friendship. Młynar stood, saying Czcibor would not go that far, and that he should talk to him.

That same night, at the forest camp, Czcibor burned Celina's notebook while telling a young Campaign Knight an old story. He had been the son of a retainer of House Paleniskos. When the house conspired with Leithanien to commit treason, he called on someone else to stop it, and the young wanderer who burst into the banquet let not a single conspirator escape. **That wanderer was Młynar.**

Celina's death had not come from some complicated political struggle either. She had helped people crushed by taxes and people who had lost their homes to General Chamber of Commerce construction vehicles. Those she had angered took her life as a warning to him.
No knight should ever bow down to wealth and power, but there is no shame in kneeling before suffering.

So, he said, he would pound the earth with the fire of the battlefield and find a way out of this dead end. The knights of his order, eager to prove themselves on the battlefield, had all chosen to follow him.

And in the memory of a certain field, a knight had questioned his father's letter. Who decided that he was the farmer, and others the crops? But a knight had to have an answer he could be sure of himself, so he left that question out of his reply.
Meanwhile, Młynar said he could no longer stand by while Czcibor staked all his hopes on war. When word came that the Leithanian Noble was secretly leaving the city, he asked Toland to protect him.
Toland asked whether he was really going only to talk. Instead of answering, Młynar held out his hand.

blocks.cap: "...Give me a sword."

blocks.x: At that moment, an order from the Grand Knight reached Czcibor. He was to report to the Grand Knight Territory at once, with his entire order.
9. Empty Armor

December 1st, 2:15 A.M. Czcibor ignored the order and gave the command to begin the operation. When a subordinate stood in his way, saying command had already passed to the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi, Czcibor cut him down himself.
As he sheathed his blood-darkened sword and left the tent, dozens of elite Campaign Knights stood in ranks beside him. No one followed him, no one stopped him, no one saluted.

blocks.cap: The camp in the forest. The knights only stood in silence beside the path he walked.

blocks.x: Meanwhile, at a fake checkpoint by the city exit, the Leithanian Noble's car was surrounded by archers. Czcibor had authorized even javelins. Then Młynar appeared before him.
Młynar said he had only come to collect his sword, as promised. Czcibor told him the Grand Knight Territory had intervened and the knights had obeyed the order. Młynar had not known.

Młynar asked why Czcibor had staged a leak of military intelligence to set him against the Leithanian guest. Czcibor replied that he was simply as disappointed in Młynar as he was in Kazimierz. What Kazimierz needed, he said, was a war to overturn the world. Młynar said he had never once thought so, and they crossed weapons.
At the same time, at the checkpoint, Toland's band brought down the ambush, spirited the noble away, and put him on a medical supply transport running through the underground logistics tunnels.

In the forest, Czcibor spoke of Celina. A single word from you would have ended it, he said. He did not believe Młynar had been that powerless. Młynar answered that there had been thirteen defendants, and the law alone could not bring fairness to the innocent.
Czcibor said he had returned to the Campaign Knights to find people who would walk with him. He did not want war. He wanted to show that a person could choose to sacrifice themselves for others.
The honor of a knight needs no testimony.

Silver fragments scattered in the rain, and blood seeped through the gaps in the broken armor. Młynar told him he had lost. Czcibor took up his spear again and asked: lost to whom, would you have me say? The nobles of the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi? The merchants?
Czcibor said he had simply found no other road to walk. Młynar put away his sword. All he had wanted was for Czcibor to stop.
Collapsed on the ground, Czcibor asked: your anger burns hotter than mine, so why do you not draw your sword? In the rain, no answer came.

blocks.cap: Two knights in the rain. Through his blurring vision, Czcibor could not make out Młynar's face as he looked down at him.

blocks.x: He thought of a wreath of wildflowers drifting down a stream, and made one last confession. For fifteen years the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi had ignored Młynar's questions about two Nearls. **Some years ago, while infiltrating Leithanien, Czcibor had met them by chance.**
Asked whether he had told anyone else, Czcibor slowly shook his head. Młynar waited for a word of blame or regret to follow, but all that came back was heavy breathing and a faint clink of metal.
The Campaign Knight's body came to rest against the spear driven into the ground. Like the empty suits of armor they had seen so many times in the barrenlands.
Młynar knelt in the rain and offered a knight's salute to one who had once walked the same road.
Epilogue. A Farewell

Elsewhere, **Margaret** stopped by, for the first time in a while, at a tavern where old friends of the Nearl family gathered. Back from her grandfather Kirill's grave, she admitted that some within the General Chamber of Commerce were threatening her, and the old men thought of her father, Schnitz. It seemed Młynar's reply had not reached Margaret yet either.
And Twierdza. Toland, who had found Młynar once more, told him that with Gale Industries under investigation, the village's land deals had been voided.

blocks.cap: Twierdza. By the original schedule, construction would have begun on this very day.

blocks.x: What Młynar said of Czcibor was brief. A man captive to his own convictions had spoken of a knightly ideal that could never be realized, and that was the last thing he did.
Toland asked what he thought now. A knight must have an answer he can be sure of himself. But Młynar's answer was different.
...I've never had an answer. Kazimierz does not need an answer from me, either.
When Toland told him not to take the blame for Czcibor's death on himself, Młynar answered that he had never said he would stand aside.
However, I was the one who refuted his ideals. I listened to him until the very end... and I killed him.
Even so, he said, because he respected that life, he had to answer his final question.

Meanwhile, an Infected worker who had been sent home returned to his house in a corner of the village. The neighbors were discussing supplies for the winter. They would no longer have to wonder where to spend this winter if the construction crews came.

Toland handed him an invitation from Rhodes Island, guessing that their 'Doctor' had something to tell Młynar about his brother and his brother's wife. Asked whether he would keep searching without a single word of news, Młynar said that even a baseless hope was enough.
A car stopped by the roadside. A young father, on his way to buy his daughter a Leithanian piccolo, asked the way to Dzwonek. Told that Młynar did not know, he drove on.

He remembered nearly every road. But there was not a single signpost by which to follow a city that kept moving forward. Now that every road already pointed to a destination, what he was looking for lay outside them all.

And every one of these stories is... to be continued.
