blocks.x: Even after the big upheavals have come and gone, people's days carry on. Someone stands in a banquet hall in a foreign country, someone drinks one last cup of tea before leaving, and someone stays up all night writing letters in a prison cell.

A young lady of Kjerag off in Victoria, the young magistrate of Shangshu, two Siracusan mafiosi in Lungmen, an assassin in Kazimierz, the mayor of Siesta, and a company man in a Columbian prison. These are six 'what happened next' stories from six places that have nothing to do with one another.
And not one of these stories ends here.
1. Our Guest from Kjelac

Before the trip to Victoria, **Ratatos**, head of the **Browntail** clan, gives her younger sister **Sciurus** a long list of warnings. She's going as the clan's representative, so she should watch a lot, think a lot, and talk as little as humanly possible.

Sciurus grumbles that she's heard it a million times, and her husband **Yucatan**, who was nodding along with her sister, gets asked whose side he's on, anyway. Still, right before they leave, Sciurus slips in a question: wasn't it actually her sister who wanted to go?

Then, Victoria. Their contract partner, the magnate **Harrison**, has one problem: he's far too kind. He offers to show her how to use the cutlery, and when she suggests going over the contract terms again, he cuts her off — he's already given them so many perks, after all.

He insists on calling Kjerag 'Kjelac' the entire time, and says he's heard they put on circus acts at banquets over there, so he'd simply love to visit. Then he whispers to another guest: it's just some backwater up in the mountains, nothing to worry about.
Stepping out into the garden, Sciurus takes a few deep breaths — then Yucatan mentions that there's nobody around anymore, and she explodes. "AAAARGH, HE DRIVES ME UP THE WALL!!!"

blocks.cap: The garden outside the banquet hall. If it weren't for the contract, she says, she'd have punched him.

blocks.x: Yucatan hands her some water and obligingly strokes her back when she demands it. But once Sciurus has vented every last drop, her conclusion is: let's go back inside. This contract is the Browntails' first step toward joining hands with the outside world, and she can't afford to ruin it.

Giant trains gliding smoothly along, a banquet hall lit by electric lamps instead of candles — everything she's seen these past two days is something Kjerag doesn't have. "Someday, when our kids are born, I want all of this to be normal for them."
Then she hears what she just said: 'our kids.' While Sciurus flusters that she meant Kjerag's future, Yucatan is busy getting flustered right along with her.
2. The Report Her Sister Couldn't Put Down

The conversation drifts to **Enciodes**, who brought railways and factories to Kjerag. Even Sciurus, who swore she'd hate that family for the rest of her life, admits that if he saw all of this first, she can understand him a little.
Then a memory from years ago comes back to her. That day, Ratatos held on to a report for a long time — a report saying that Enciodes had left to study in Victoria.
Young Sciurus sneered that he'd just run away because he couldn't hack it in Kjerag, and that she would never leave. Ratatos, her face gone pale, only said that he had made a decision.
The decision to abandon everything.

Not long after, their grandfather passed away. Between hiding how ill he had been and holding off everyone who had their eyes on a young clan head, Ratatos barely had time to sleep. And all Sciurus did was fight with her, every single day.
"Do you think... the Browntail clan has been holding her back this whole time?" Sciurus confesses that she was a fool back then, and asks that he, of all people, not hold it against her.
Yucatan answers that he has never once thought that, and that the Matriarch has always tried to trust her. Taking everything on alone, he says, is something the two sisters have in common.

Just then, a commotion breaks out over by the banquet hall. Viscount Evans, a Victorian noble, has stormed in with his men, accusing Harrison of quietly snatching his partners' shares and buying up land.

blocks.cap: Harrison's manor. A viscount who was supposed to be on holiday sent over a 'gift' without warning.

blocks.x: While threats fly about how it could all be written off as a dueling accident, Yucatan moves at Sciurus's signal, and the viscount's men drop one by one. Assuming Harrison called in backup, the viscount retreats, warning that this isn't over.
Sciurus smiles sweetly. Looks like his partnership with the viscount is finished — and losing a partner right when you're trying to grow your company must really sting, mustn't it?
"We Browntails are one of Kjerag's Three Clans. A puny Victorian noble poses no threat to us." So — shall we discuss that contract again?
3. Shangshu, and a Play That's Not Bad

Meanwhile, in **Shangshu**, a riverside region of Yan. Early in the morning at the ferry landing, the Grand Tutor — who will be taking Magistrate **Liang Xun** back to the capital with him tonight — steps aboard a boatman's boat.

The boatman admits he worries about the young magistrate like he would a nephew, and the Grand Tutor replies that if Liang Xun can only endure, he will make a name for himself. The boatman starts to ask what happens if he can't — then takes the question back himself.

That same morning, Liang Xun has come to a teahouse halfway up the mountain to keep his 'promise' to watch a play with **Miss Ning**. Miss Ning laughs that it wasn't really a promise, and refills the cup of a man who surely didn't sleep a wink, busy handing over his duties all night.
Liang Xun remembered the sweet fritters Miss Ning once praised, and beside the fiery stew at his estate, there's always a soothing broth set out just for her.

blocks.cap: The teahouse halfway up the mountain. The play is so-so; the tea is still warm.

blocks.x: In truth, Liang Xun hadn't wanted to go to the capital, and while he hesitated, Miss Ning accepted on his behalf. What the Grand Tutor offers will be the hardest of opportunities, she says — and if he had turned it down, he would surely have regretted it.
Then she adds: if he had agreed to go without a moment's hesitation, she might have been a little upset. When he asks if she's joking, she says she isn't.

When Miss Ning's grandfather was about to retire, he called her in and asked whether she would use her talents for the country, for the people, and for the realm. Liang Xun speaks the answer she gave him before she can.
"...Even if it cost me my life—" "—I would not refuse."

Before they part, Liang Xun tells her that if she ever wants to see flowers, she needn't make the long trip — just send a letter, and he'll plant them himself. Instead of answering, Miss Ning asks a question of her own: when is he going to take out that jewelry case he's been clutching in his pocket all this time?
4. An Itinerary, an 'Auntie,' and a Friend Peeking In
Over at the inn, meanwhile, **Miss Du** — Yaoye — is getting ready to lead a group of young people off to Yumen. Her father, Innkeeper Zheng, just won't let go of the itinerary.

When Yaoye carefully asks whether he'd ever thought of coming to Yumen with them if they closed the inn, Zheng answers that the inn was always meant to be hers anyway — so if she doesn't want it, it's fine to close it.

"Now that you've stepped up to lead, your words and decisions aren't yours alone anymore." Telling her never to back down no matter how hard it gets, her father hands over the itinerary, with all the rough roads marked.

blocks.cap: Miss Du's family inn. A father's worries don't all fit on one itinerary.

blocks.x: But at his final bit of nagging — find yourself a decent young man along the way — Yaoye shrieks and storms off to go give Lee a piece of her mind.

At the same time, in a corner of the inn, **Zuo Le** is fuming at **Leizi**, who's been blocking his way since morning. She's here in a private capacity this time, Leizi points out, so what is he supposed to call her? Zuo Le answers grudgingly: "...Auntie."

Leizi tells him there's more going on behind this Shangshu business than meets the eye, and states flatly that once it's over, he's coming back to the capital with her. It's General Zuo's wish, so Zuo Le has no choice but to obey.

Meanwhile, on a mountain path overlooking the teahouse, **Lee**, visiting from Lungmen, has been secretly watching the two of them. He grumbles about how much his friend has changed in the decade-plus since they last met, but in the end, Lee never steps forward.
I wanted one last drink with an old friend. Guess that's a tough one to swing.
5. Would You Like Some Mayonnaise Teppanyaki Macaroni?
And then there's Lungmen. **Capone** and **Gambino**, mafiosi run out of Siracusa, now work for 'that psycho,' **Lappland** — on the condition that one single slip-up means they're dead.

Today's job: pick up a letter from a contact. The passphrase is "Would you like some mayonnaise teppanyaki macaroni?" answered with "Supersize, for two." But the meeting time comes and goes, and the contact never shows.

Suspecting the old underlings who betrayed them, Capone heads for their hideout. There, though, those same underlings are playing blackjack in broad daylight, moaning that these days they can't even scrape together errand money.
Guys they took in under the name of the Family, reduced to running errands? Gambino, who's supposed to be hiding, can't help blurting something out.

blocks.cap: Near the old underlings' hideout. Gambino's temper is way too short for hiding and eavesdropping.

blocks.x: Just then, an explosion goes off a few blocks away. They rush over to find a man in a black coat with a whole row of Lungmen mobsters collapsed around him — every one of them still breathing.

"Would you like some mayonnaise teppanyaki macaroni?" The man handing over the letter turns out to be Tommaso, Gambino's old underling. He insists he's only the messenger, and that he'd sooner die than tell them who gave him the letter.
But one look at the wax seal on the envelope, and the two of them freeze. Why would a letter from 'that woman' be here in Lungmen? In that moment, Tommaso vanishes, and the L.G.D. comes storming in.

Cornered in a dead-end alley, the two barely slip away while Gambino charges out to draw attention. When an L.G.D. officer remarks that the crossbowman's aim is terrible, Capone snaps that if this weren't Lungmen, it would've been a headshot ages ago.
6. Rubber-Tipped Bolts and a Table for Two

When the two finally make it back, Lappland takes the letter — and bursts out laughing at what it says: bury the pair of them out in the wastes. Then she makes a gleeful suggestion. Why not kill each other, right here, right now? That would win back at least a little of their honor.

On the count of three, the two of them go for — not each other, but Lappland. Without even drawing a blade, though, Lappland handles them both, then catches the bolt Capone fired and holds it to his throat.

Capone pulls a knife, pointing out that this is Lungmen, so his bolts are rubber-tipped and can't kill anyone — but he's far too slow for Lappland, who notes it's easy enough if you go for the aorta. "Congrats. You saved your life."
Gambino resigns himself: they should've died long ago, so at least they'll go out like real Sicilians. And that's the moment Lappland holds Signora Sicilia's letter over the fire.

"It's just a scrap of paper full of pompous nonsense." Bored that they're so scared of her they can't even bear to watch her letter burn, Lappland pulls the two of them back to their feet. They still have work to do, she says.
There's more than one lone wolf in this city.

Meanwhile, in a Lungmen park, the **Rat King** is serving tea to **Cadeddu**, who has come to deliver Signora Sicilia's message. That morning, some locals mistook him for Siracusan reinforcements and jumped him, and the Rat King thanks him for going easy on them.

blocks.cap: Tea in the park. They say Siracusans only drink tea when they're sick, but this is Lungmen.

blocks.x: The Signora won't meddle any further with the Siracusans who've drifted into Lungmen, but the two 'lone wolves' can't leave the pack. The Rat King says he'll stay out of that conflict — but makes it clear that in Lungmen, they follow Lungmen's rules.
And when he's told that graciously accepting your host's hospitality is also one of Lungmen's rules, Cadeddu downs the tea he hadn't touched in a single gulp and leaves.

One of the wolves is with Emperor, so that's taken care of; the Rat King tells his subordinate to keep an eye on the other until she leaves Lungmen. Asked what to do if she doesn't leave, he goes quiet for a long while — then asks whether today is Friday.
The Ice Castle Hotel has 30% off today, so he'd like a dinner for two booked for tonight. He's just having a meal with an old friend, he says.
7. New Face, New Name, a Better Life
Meanwhile, in Kazimierz, the reason the assassin **Roy** joined the **Armorless Union** is simple. It pays far better than hunting fowlbeasts on his own. Everyone works for a better life, don't they?

Together with his partner **Monique**, Roy tracks down the **Blood Knight**, who has been living in hiding, before anyone else can — and makes him an offer. Do them one small favor, and they'll give him a chance to get out. If need be, they're even willing to leave the Union.

Not long after, every screen in the streets is running the same news. The Blood Knight's hideout was attacked; the attackers' bodies and his blood were left at the scene, and the chances that he survived are extremely slim.
The Union has already chosen a new candidate to take Roy's place as a 'Lazurite.' In two hours he goes into surgery, and when he comes out, Roy will be Joel Tyrell.

In the meantime, as Roy eats some street food, an Infected knight next to him rages at the news. There's no way the Blood Knight would die at the hands of some assassin. His flailing arm catches the company employee in the next seat on the head, and Roy ends up joining them for apology drinks.

blocks.cap: An all-night bar. Three strangers clink glasses.

blocks.x: The Infected knight turns out to be the 'Ironwrist Knight,' who narrowly lost a match earlier that day. There are people who won't let the Infected win, he confides, and he has probably become a thorn in their side as well.

Roy, who introduced himself as a hunter from the sticks, gets up to leave and offers some advice in return for the drinks. Stay in this bar for the rest of the night, and when morning comes, stick to crowded places.

As a child, Roy survived in the forest by catching and eating fowlbeasts. The one who took him in was an old man called 'Darksteel.' When the old man asked if he wanted a better life, of course Roy did.

Then, at dawn, the Ironwrist Knight — who wrote that advice off as a drunk's ramblings — heads home. On the streets of Kawalerielki, empty but for trash and discarded knight posters, the Armorless Union's killers are waiting for him.

blocks.cap: Kawalerielki at dawn. Not a soul in sight.

blocks.x: The Blood Knight can no longer protect you.

And after the surgery, Roy opens his eyes to a new face wrapped in bandages. He is Joel now, and Monique is his wife, Donna Tyrell. After Joel bids the doctor farewell, Donna tells him the body is his to deal with, and Joel replies: dead men tell no tales.

Almost in passing, Joel mentions that the Infected knights who followed the Blood Knight are being eliminated, and that he met one of them last night to check. Donna cuts him off: they have nothing to do with the Union anymore.

Joel muses about buying a villa in the countryside and going hunting together, but Donna says she's going on vacation by herself, somewhere like Dossoles or Siesta. Joel asks: once he's taken care of the loose ends, why don't they go together?
8. A Watch That's Allowed to Stop Time

And then, the seaside city of **Siesta**. Its residents are in the middle of relocating so the city can be reborn as a nomadic city, but its logistics capacity is falling woefully short, so Mayor **Herman** decides to team up with an outside freight company.

The ones who show up are **Eurill**, president of Lungmen's **MountainDash Logistics**, and his son, **Bison**. After the wristwatch he offers as a greeting gift is politely declined, Eurill floats the idea that they might do this job free of charge.

In exchange, he'd like permission to set up a MountainDash-led logistics company in Siesta. Use that network to build trade agreements tied to no political faction, he says, and Siesta could become a neutral trade hub.
Once the city leaves this beach, Eurill asks, whose hands will the decisions fall into? Time won't wait for Siesta. Only then does Herman realize what the wristwatch meant.

When Herman asks whether he hopes the deal goes through, Bison answers, clearly and carefully, that the future of logistics isn't just moving goods — it's the exchange of economies and cultures. Herman smiles, and brings up his daughter, who used to think a great deal about Siesta's future.
The nomadic city of Siesta will be a truly beautiful place.

At sunset on the beach, vendors are doing their last business before the move. In front of 'charcoal-grilled sandworm legs,' apparently all the rage since the Obsidian Festival, Eurill and his son freeze up side by side.

blocks.cap: The beach, soon to be left behind. One vendor plans to fill a bottle with sand before leaving.

blocks.x: Over dinner, Eurill tells the story of how he won first place in a tug-of-war when Bison was four — and ended up becoming every other kid's 'dad' too. Herman counters with the story of how his daughter, back in university, hired someone to pretend to be her father. When he adds that he has since hired that fake father himself, the secretary beside him clears his throat.

Eurill shares that a few years ago, when he thought about letting go of the company, his sick wife scolded him in more than ten letters — and that it's thanks to those letters that he and his son are who they are today. Herman watches the waves in silence for a moment, then says he hopes she gets well soon.

Eurill pours the wine he brought from Lungmen, and when Herman worries that his hand might shake and break the glass, Eurill offers to steady it with the very hand that conquered an entire school at tug-of-war. Under the setting sun, the sea rolls even more dazzlingly than it did by day.
"The wine you brought from Lungmen is excellent." It will suit the tastes not only of Siesta, Herman says, but of people from other countries too.
9. A Day in the Life of a Dignified Prisoner

Last up: **Mansfield State Prison** in Columbia. In the small hours, **Jesselton** is writing a letter to 'Mr. K' at his company. The reply he has kept tells him to keep quiet, stay out of trouble, and that he is still an important asset to **Beachbrella**.

Having gone undercover as a jailer to kill someone, only to end up an inmate himself, he's the prison's favorite punching bag. A jailer makes him clean the toilets without even a brush, sneering that he can just whip one up with his Arts.

Even so, Jesselton fakes running into the bars so he can go to the infirmary and dig up information on the condition of **Rick**, a newly arrived inmate. Then he gets dragged off by the A-Zone prisoners to take part in a showdown with the Infected prisoners of B-Zone.

In the middle of the arena, Jesselton just stands there like a pillar. Clubs bend and saw blades chip, but there isn't a scratch on him — until eventually A-Zone and B-Zone, now beating on him together, wear themselves out and collapse.

blocks.cap: The inter-zone showdown. The jailers place bets on the side.

blocks.x: "If my presence has helped the two sides make some progress, then this hasn't been such a bad thing." Just as he's about to make a dignified exit, a B-Zone prisoner dumps a bucket of toilet-cleaning water over his head.
Once again, Jesselton doesn't lift a finger, and simply turns away. It's all just their petty amusement anyway, he says.
10. Your Humblest Servant
When Jesselton comes back in his soaked clothes, Rick brings him a change of clothes. So naive, Jesselton thinks — he can hardly wait to see the look on this guy's face when he reads the letter.

Claiming he got them from the doctor, he hands Rick two things: a diagnosis saying he doesn't have long to live, and a letter from his wife, Patty. The letter is a fake — Jesselton stayed up all night last week imitating her handwriting.

"I have decided to marry Bill..." Except, of all names, Bill happens to be the name of Rick's fifteen-year-old brother. When Jesselton covers by suggesting it could be a different Bill, Rick remembers the old carpenter Bill Dickinson and flies into a rage.

Jesselton fans the flames as if he's been waiting for this. How much is love really worth in Columbia? All that's left is money and power. He has connections both inside and outside the prison, he says, and he'd be glad to introduce Rick to them.
Right then, a jailer calls for Rick. His family has posted his bail. The name of the person who paid it: Patty.

The jailer sneers. They knew a week ago that Patty had scraped the bail together, and the warden knew all about Jesselton's little 'making friends' scheme. So they held up the paperwork and sat back to watch him scramble to buy connections on the cheap.

A dark energy gathers in Jesselton's hand — then disperses. "Only fools resort to violence to vent their anger." The jailer holds out a bucket and some detergent. C-Zone's toilets are still waiting, after all.

And once more, the letter to Mr. K. He writes that he knows that to Mr. K, he is merely one of countless employees, and begs to be gotten out as soon as possible — and then the pen stops at the signature. Jesselton grits his teeth and crosses out what he originally wrote.
Your humblest servant, Jesselton Williams.
"Chin up, Jesselton. You've been Beachbrella's employee of the year five years running. The company will never abandon you."
Epilogue — Channel 58, Same Time Next Week
Then, in some bar, an excited voice drifts out of the TV. "Whatever will become of Jesselton Williams? Find out same time next week, on episode 173 of 'True Stories'!"

blocks.cap: In front of the bar's TV. Two people are in stitches.

blocks.x: The two in front of the TV are doubled over laughing. The actor playing Jesselton is brilliant, they agree, and they raise a toast to his success.
Then one of them asks: what if that guy isn't an actor at all, and actually exists? After a brief silence, the two of them burst out laughing again.
"'True Stories' is a work of fiction. Any resemblance to actual persons, groups, organizations, or companies is purely coincidental."

The contract at the banquet, the farewell in Shangshu, the wolves of Lungmen, the assassin with a new face, the city about to leave its beach, the letters from prison. None of these stories is over yet. To be continued, next time.

act10mini.tagline: An Infected girl saves six thousand five hundred pounds and becomes the owner of the shop she dreamed of, only to sink to the ground before its ashes at dawn the very next day. And at the edge of the dark clouds, small sparks that have not yet gone out.

chars.desc: A member of the Reunion remnants. He urges his comrades to become a force that helps the Infected.

chars.name: Nine
chars.desc: One of the leaders of the Reunion remnants.

chars.name: Cannot
chars.desc: A wasteland trader in a bucket-shaped iron helmet. He calls everyone 'friend.'

terms.name: Caladon
terms.desc: A nomadic city of Victoria. Its Infected community takes in Infected from other cities and gives them work.

terms.name: Green Spark
terms.desc: An arboretum and lighting shop in the Infected community. Everyone takes it for a pub. One of the few places where Infected workers can rest.

terms.name: Witch Forest
terms.desc: An organization that once took in Infected Casters. Five years ago it was burned out of existence by the Victorian army.

terms.name: the Boil
terms.desc: Caladon's lawless district. Overrun with gangs, it lies beyond the reach of the city guard.

terms.name: Rusthammer
terms.desc: An armed group roaming the wastes. Outsiders regard them as a band of raiders.

blocks.x: In **Caladon**, a nomadic city of Victoria, there was an Infected community that took in even the Infected of other cities and gave them work. At nine at night, workers coming off their factory shifts gathered at one shop there.

Everyone took it for a pub, but it was in fact an arboretum and lighting shop: the **Green Spark**. **Susie**, an Infected Feline girl, had poured drinks there for years, saving money toward a single dream: to buy the shop.
Susie knew, too, that for the Infected, a dream is a story from a faraway place no one can reach.
1. The Regulars of the Green Spark

On the night of November 16th, 1097, James, a non-Infected worker, raised a toast to his bonus, and Stone, an Infected, called Susie 'Sparky' and laughed that he was going to die someday anyway. Susie turned serious and told him sharply to look after himself.

Another regular was **Bitter Root**, a Rhodes Island 'professional' hired by the nobles of the city council. At first there had even been a baseless rumor that Rhodes Island abducted the Infected for experiments, but the customers of this shop, at least, now trusted Rhodes Island.

That night, the newspaper the regular Bean was reading reported that a new bill limiting Infected workers to no more than fifteen hours of work a day had ended in a tie in the council vote. Beside it ran stories like 'Strange Sounds Beneath the City' and 'Infected Smugglers Spotted in Abandoned District.'

blocks.cap: The Green Spark, an arboretum and lighting shop in the Infected community. Its customers call it a pub.

blocks.x: 2. How Not to Fight Back

The next morning, out on a delivery, Susie was struck in the face by a loud-mouthed man among protesters demanding that the Infected be driven out. Holding down the sparks that had risen to her fingertips, she told herself this was not the first time.

Then **Red**, a worker from Ursus who used to read books at the shop instead of drinking, stepped in. Calmly noting that there was a crystal right where he had just been hit, that there was blood at the corner of his own mouth, and that the man's hand was scraped, he sent the man running to the hospital. Afterward he admitted to Susie that it could never spread that easily.

That evening, all **Grani** of the Mounted Police could do when she came to the shop was take a report. She was a Kuranta temporarily put in charge of the Infected community, one of the few officers of the law willing to help the Infected.

Red knew the man. A month before he had joined the protests as a factory worker, two months before as a merchant, each time blaming the Infected. Bean said it looked like the work of **the Boil**, a district overrun with gangs.

That night Susie dreamed of five years before: the day she left a home that could not bear the extra cost of one Infected, reassuring her mother that in Caladon part of her wages would be paid in medicine.

blocks.cap: Five years ago, the day she left home. Her mother kept saying she was sorry.

blocks.x: After Susie left, things got a little better at home. For Susie, that was enough.
3. A Bridge of Six Thousand Five Hundred Pounds

The day after, **Quercus** returned: a Messenger known as the 'Druid of Gododdin,' and the shop's manager. To Susie, who had spent years scrimping on food and clothing to save for the shop, she promised to arrange a meeting with the owner.

That night **Skyfire** came by as well, a young lady of the Mountbelan family and a Rhodes Island specialist. She could not contain her anger: the councilors had read only one page of the Infected policy she had spent two weeks drafting.
At the same table, Stone hung his head. His wife and daughter were coming to see him, and how could he face them looking like this? Susie took out scissors and a comb and cut his tangled hair short.
It's because life's so hard that we should find our own ways to live better.

Then, on the morning of November 23rd, six thousand five hundred pounds lay before Susie. Enough to buy who knew how many hundred-and-fifty-pound Originium lamps, each once worth a month of her mother's income. A bridge built up stitch by stitch, leading to her dream.
But the person who appeared as the shop's owner was Bitter Root. The shop had in fact belonged to Rhodes Island.

Asked what she meant to do next, Susie thought of her father, who had been a barber. People who want to look their best still believe in life, she said, so she wanted to open a hair salon in the Infected community. Bitter Root agreed on the spot.
Outside, the regulars were waiting. When Quercus told her to take good care of the shop, calling her Manager Susie, Susie finally broke down in tears.

blocks.cap: An alley in the Infected community. The regulars were waiting for their new manager.

blocks.x: For an Infected, it was an extravagant thing. Am I one of the lucky ones? Susie wondered.
4. The Light Went Out
At 6:35 the next morning, one corner of the Infected community was swallowed by smoke.

Held back as she tried to run toward the flames, Susie watched the sign that read 'Green Spark' turn into a few charred fragments. Her past dreams and her future life were buried beneath the ruins, and she could not even know why.
The girl sank to the ground. The lingering heat burned her hands and feet, and broken shards cut into her skin.
The light went out.
5. The Witch of Stray Cats

A little earlier, on the night of November 19th, security guards chasing a petty thief kept coming back to the same signpost until they gave up and left. Laughing at their retreating backs, the Feline **Haze** went straight on to bring bread and medicine to Minnie, an Infected girl, who called her 'Miss Witch.'

For three months Haze had suffered the pain of Oripathy. She had to leave before her crystals turned to dust and hurt others, she thought; a Caster of **the Witch Forest** should meet her end alone, and with grace.

Caladon's Infected community had eight bars and thirty-two stray cats. For a witch who had drifted through five cities and broken out of prison seventeen times, Caladon was not a bad place to end her life.
Then, on the night of November 23rd, Haze slipped into a warehouse near the abandoned district and overheard men in black plotting to kidnap several Infected and an old councilor.

blocks.cap: A rundown warehouse near the abandoned district. Haze heard something she was never meant to hear.

blocks.x: Discovered, Haze took an arrow to the shoulder and fled into a room of a small mansion nearby. The old Savra noble inside, startled by her black mist, fell, clutched his chest, and collapsed. Haze called a servant and slipped away. The servant who rushed in called him 'Master Angst.'
Pursued by the men, Haze hid in a shop in the Infected community. Its sign read 'Green Spark.'
No one cares whether the Infected live or die, the men reasoned, so it would make good cover. In the middle of a densely built street, they threw an incendiary into the shop. Haze escaped the flames.
6. Tomorrow's Sun

Three days later, Haze, coughing up blood, gave Minnie some coins, a wide-brimmed black hat, and a ring. In the name of the Hundred and Thirteenth Witch of the Witch Forest, she accepted Minnie as a new witch, and told her to wear the ring and use her Arts only on bad people.

At dawn the next day, Haze climbed a derelict building in the abandoned district that looked out over the endless wastes, and sat down against a wall. The kind Great Witch Grant, her old companions, the night the Victorian army's cannons burned the Witch Forest: they passed before her one by one. Soon it would all be over.
Then she heard sobbing. At a window of the derelict building, a Feline girl swayed on her feet, apologizing to her mother. It was Susie.

blocks.cap: The abandoned district on the outskirts of Caladon. That night, two Felines were in the same derelict building.

blocks.x: When Haze said her friends would grieve tomorrow, Susie thought of Quercus and stepped back from the window. Susie said someone had broken her dream and she did not even know why. Then why, Haze asked, was she trying to ruin the last thing she had left?

If something was taken from you, Haze said, find a way and take it back. The one who should fall from this building is the bad guy who wrecked your dream. Susie let out a long breath and gave a tired smile.
The Great Witch used to say that as long as you can see tomorrow's sun, there is still hope for everything.
Before she could finish, Haze collapsed.

Susie carried Haze on her back toward the city. When she realized that what was soaking her back was blood running from Haze's mouth and nose, she understood what it meant. Every Infected knew what it meant.

Since leaving home she had grown numb to the deaths of the Infected, but this time she could not bear it. When Susie cried out for help in the empty abandoned district, slow footsteps approached from far off. It was Red.
7. The King's Wand

Meanwhile, Skyfire had been frequenting the city council at Councilor Angst's invitation. Between councilors who pretended to care about the Infected while looking after their own interests and an opposition that wanted every Infected from elsewhere driven out, she railed at a banquet one night, until she was drunk, that the Reunion incident must never be allowed to happen again.

The next morning word came that Councilor Angst had collapsed from heart disease after a commotion with an intruder the night before. Skyfire attended an event to hear the views of the Infected in his place, and at the end of story after story of unpaid wages, she heard that the Green Spark had burned down.
At that moment, an explosion went off. Rioters with crystals on their bodies tied up the Infected and loaded them into a vehicle, and Skyfire let herself be taken along to see what they were after.

They arrived at an empty factory, stripped of all its equipment. Grumbling that they had brought back some girl instead of the old councilor, the rioters planted bombs, and talked about the explosives left in the safehouse in the abandoned district and about the 'Danton brothers' getting ready to slip out of the city.

blocks.cap: A factory stripped of all its equipment. Only the bombs remained.

blocks.x: Skyfire burned through her ropes with her Arts and hurled fireballs. In the heat, the rioters' crystals fell away. They were glass, painted black. None of them were Infected.
When her flames burned the bombs' cores before they could go off, one rioter tried to flee, crying out 'King's Wand' and the name of the Mountbelan family.
...Kneel before the flame of the heavens.
When the red light had passed, the rioters all lay on the floor. A hidden mercenary lunged at her from behind, but a shadow that appeared from the ceiling vent brought him down and vanished.
8. The Lone Mounted Police Officer

Some days earlier, Grani had been looking into six reopened entrances to the abandoned structural layers, and the sound of something being dragged underground every night. The guard captain snapped at her to stop wasting her time and solve the theft at Count Bishmer's mansion instead.

Then, on the evening of November 24th, Grani stood before the Green Spark, now a heap of ashes. The guards had ruled it an accidental fire, but the fragment a firefighter handed her was a shard of a military incendiary, the kind Grani had seen in training.

Two days later, Grani paid another visit to the loud-mouthed man who had hit Susie. He confessed that he had bought a crate of incendiaries on the Boil's black market and sold them all to the Danton brothers, Siracusan immigrant mafiosi. And in Caladon, the only place that made military supplies like that was Count Bishmer's factory.

The next day, when the guard captain flew into a rage at the idea of investigating a factory belonging to a councilor's family, Grani confronted him with the fact that he was Bishmer's relative, and made it plain that as the officer in charge of the Mounted Police unit called in by the city council, she was his equal.

The following night, November 28th, Grani tracked down the two men in black who had chased Haze, the Danton brothers, at a bar in the Boil. Though nine armed men rose to their feet, Grani did not back down, and the brothers fled with broken hands.

The house the brothers ran into belonged to 'Miss Witch.' Recognizing bad people, Minnie sent violet lightning leaping from her fingertips, and the brothers, thrown out through the window, ran for the safehouse in the abandoned district.

Inside the dark house, hoping to shake off Grani, the brothers pulled the pin on their last incendiary and threw it into a dark corner. Only when the room lit up did they see that it was packed with Originium explosives and dangerous chemicals.

In the same instant, Grani's pike pierced the concrete wall, and the blast echoed across all of Caladon. The ground caved in down to the structural layer below, and suspects, evidence, and truth alike turned to black smoke and blew away on the wind.

blocks.cap: The abandoned district on the outskirts of Caladon. Where the derelict house had stood, only a huge, smoking hole remained.

blocks.x: Knocked down by the shock, Grani did not know what had happened.
9. The Bounty on the Wanted Poster

Meanwhile, in the wastes 40 km from Caladon, Quercus held a funeral for Mae, an Infected who had not lasted the three weeks it would take for the wine Quercus had promised her to be ready. When a wanderer asked why she helped them, she asked in return whether they would believe that there were people who had been rescuing and helping the Infected all along.
On the afternoon of November 28th, at the Rhodes Island office, Susie heard Quercus call Bitter Root 'Captain,' and only then understood. Quercus was with Rhodes Island too.

Haze lay on a bed in the office. When Susie asked whether Oripathy could be cured, Quercus answered that there was no cure, but there was medicine to slow it down, and she eased Haze's fever with her Arts.

blocks.cap: The Rhodes Island office in Caladon. Haze woke up here.

blocks.x: When she came to, Haze confessed that she had overheard talk of kidnapping a councilor that night, been chased, and hidden in the Green Spark, and that the men had thrown an incendiary into it. When Haze apologized, Susie said that if Haze had not hidden there, some other Infected's home would have burned.
Bitter Root called her the 'Big Hat of the Witch Forest.' Haze said she had meant to sleep forever in this city, but sometimes she wanted to struggle on, and to see more cats.
Bitter Root sent Susie to the guards with a document laying out the clues. The idea was that the bounty on the wanted posters might make up, if only a little, for the shop's losses.

But going over the map again, Bitter Root noticed something odd. The building where the men had been stood right next to Bishmer's munitions factory, which had shut down a month and a half earlier for 'equipment inspections.' And the guard captain was Bishmer's relative.
Three hours had passed since Susie went to the guards.
Quercus and Skyfire rushed out, and Bitter Root obtained plans of the old underground logistics passages from **Kazemaru** at the city hall archives and narrowed them down to seven likely entrances.
10. The Price to Be Paid

By then, Susie had woken up in an abandoned underground logistics passage. She had gone along when the guard captain asked her to come to the scene with him, and had been struck on the back of the head.

blocks.cap: The abandoned logistics passages beneath Caladon. The missing factory equipment was here.

blocks.x: Bishmer, arguing nearby, laid it all bare. They had moved equipment bought with city council money underground, then had rioters disguised as Infected stage a kidnapping and blow up the empty factory. They could then claim that the Infected had bombed it.
When the plan fell apart, Bishmer ordered that Susie be dealt with somewhere else. The sight of blood made him dizzy, he said.
When Susie asked whether they had burned her shop too, the guard captain told her that the Infected never lived long anyway, so she should accept it. Susie closed her eyes.
Then an explosion sounded overhead. The structural layers of the abandoned district collapsed one after another, and tons of steel beams fell on the guard captain's head.

In the chaos, it was Red who saved the fleeing Susie. Cutting down a pursuer with his blade, he said he was sorry at the edge of a broken platform, threw Susie four meters across to the other side, and disappeared into the darkness beyond the fallen beams.
At a dead end, Bishmer confronted her, struck her across the face, and blamed everything on the damned Infected. Susie no longer shrank back.

Asking whether he had burned her shop and tried to harm countless Infected just for money, the girl seized the councilor by the throat. Sparks flew, and Bishmer, who had been begging for his life, foamed at the mouth as his breathing grew faint.

Then giant vines broke through the concrete. Quercus, who had subdued the twenty or so mercenaries guarding the passage entrance with her vines, held Susie tight and would not let go, even as the sparks burned her skin.
When Quercus said a man like this was not even worth her killing, Susie asked where she could go back to, now that the Green Spark was gone. Quercus told her what she always said.
Life always finds a place where it belongs.
Susie sobbed quietly, as if she had set down a heavy burden.
11. The Times Must Change

Two days later, Skyfire visited Councilor Angst and told him that his bill had passed the city council by a single vote. The opposition had already signed a petition asking that he be stripped of his title once the Duke returned, but the 153-year-old Savra said he did not cling to his title.

More than twenty years earlier, the scientist Janet Longfellow had warned of the dangers of Originium industrial emissions, only to leave Victoria after being ridiculed. Over the past ten years, Victoria's Infected had grown to a worrying number. The old man, who had watched the palace of Gaul fall, said that if Victoria did not change, it would become another Gaul.
The times must change.

And in an alley of the Infected community, Grani, Quercus, and Haze were with Susie. Named 'The City's Hero,' Susie had received a certificate of honorary citizenship and made the front page, and Bishmer had been arrested. But the city council had seized all of his assets, leaving no money to make good Susie's losses.
Susie said she no longer knew what to do. Quercus asked whether she might try making drinks somewhere else.

blocks.cap: The Green Spark is gone, but there are still many Infected who need a place to share a drink.

blocks.x: Grani added that Rhodes Island had few professional barbers. Susie thought about what kind of place it might be, the place everyone kept talking about.

Earlier, on the night of November 28th, in the collapsed underground passage, Red stood before the mercenaries. He had once been called 'Redblade' in Ursus. His comrades appeared at his side, and his longsword was wreathed in flame.
Epilogue. Those Who Took Off the Symbol

On December 21st, a little over three weeks later, in old ruins in the Bleached Wasteland, the Reunion remnants were growing potatoes on a hydroponic farm and had sewn new clothes from cloth obtained thanks to Caladon's Infected workers. The clothes bore no Reunion symbol.
What binds us together is not a symbol but a spirit, **Guard** said. Then a Phantom Crossbowman back from Caladon reported in: 'Bean, reporting back.'

blocks.cap: Old ruins in the Bleached Wasteland. Reunion was hiding here.

blocks.x: In the warehouse, 'Captain Red' was unloading an engine brought back from Caladon. The old logistics passages had been exposed by the explosion and could no longer be used, Red reported, but thanks to that accident they had been able to bring the engine out without a trace.

The engine was to be fitted to a flying vehicle discarded by the Columbian military. On December 24th, instead of cargo, **Cannot**, the trader in the bucket-shaped helmet who had agreed to supply the remaining parts, showed them a convoy of armed vehicles being ambushed by a giant Metal Crab and **Rusthammer** warriors. The parts were what that convoy had been carrying.

Red drew his weapon, saying he did not deal with bandits, but the standoff eased when Elba recognized Rusthammer's Gareth 'Swiftblade.' He was an old comrade they had thought dead. Gareth said that Illa was expecting a child, and that the child would grow up to be a better person than he was.

When **Nine** asked why he was helping them, Cannot spoke of the shadow over the northern tundra, the darkness that had swallowed the sea, and the calamity buried beneath the earth, and said the world was falling apart. When Nine told him to seek out Rhodes Island, he replied that the good move they had made in Kazimierz was not enough to change the whole game, but that it was a comfort to know such people existed.
Even at the edge of the dark clouds, a spark still glimmers.

For the Infected, a dream is a story from a faraway place no one can reach. In a single night that dream turned to ash, but Susie survived, and where the light of the Green Spark went out, a small spark has not yet gone out.

act9mini.tagline: Knights who set out to protect the Infected accept a deal that would put a city to sleep, and an archer who dreamed of knighthood becomes a Knight-Assassin. Under neon that never goes dark, the Chamber's phone rings once again.

terms.name: Grand Knight Territory

terms.name: General Chamber of Commerce
terms.desc: The vast commercial power that effectively rules Kazimierz.

terms.name: Armorless Union

terms.name: Pinus Sylvestris
terms.desc: A new knightclub Sona formed by gathering Infected knights.

terms.name: Campaign Knight
terms.desc: A Kazimierz knight who fights on the battlefield rather than in the arena.

blocks.x: In Kazimierz's **Grand Knight Territory**, knights are stars, and they are products. Betting terminals and advertisements flood the arenas, and under the neon the city's nights never go dark.
In the darkest corners of the same city, Infected with nowhere else to go live in hiding. Infected knights must stake their lives in underground arenas just to bring a knight's title within reach.
In that city, a few Infected knights decided to trust one another. An ordinary employee was dressed in a big shot's clothes. And an archer who had dreamed of knighthood came to aim her bow elsewhere.
1. An Alliance Forged in a Melee

Just before a fifteen-knight melee, **Sona**, a Zalak Infected who was always grinning, spoke to an unfamiliar Zalak knight who was glaring at the stands. Reading contempt and anger in that gaze, Sona proposed that they join forces.
Some of the Infected had already made 'arrangements', she explained, and meant to climb over others for a better life. It was not the prize money Sona wanted. She wanted to stop them from winning.
If someone wins, someone loses. That doesn't matter. But if someone lives... then someone has to die.

The other knight called it an important moment for earning the Knights Association's recognition, and accepted. She gave her name, calling her surname a joke. She was a brusque Zalak with a cannonlance: **Greynuty Kaliska**.

blocks.cap: Fifteen knights, fifteen chances at the prize. The stage of a melee where the Infected wager their lives.

blocks.x: Some time later, Sona was planning to form a knightclub of Infected, and had already chosen its name. **Pinus Sylvestris.** It was the name of a pine that had once grown thick in her homeland near Victoria, and that had vanished in recent years.

From that name, Greynuty understood. Sona was a Zalak from the territory the Kaliska family had abandoned during that Catastrophe. Asked whether her infection was the Kaliskas' fault too, Sona said it had nothing to do with Greynuty, who had left the family. Then she let it go: Greynuty had snatched the win at the very end of that melee, so they could call it 'even'.
After that, the knightclub sought out Infected knights. The loud 'Wild Mane Knight' **Iwona** and the taciturn sniper 'Fartooth Knight' **Justyna** joined in turn.
2. Terms to Put a City to Sleep

The knights' prize money went toward hiding Infected with nowhere to go in the city's shadows. That morning, too, miners infected in a small industrial accident came to them. Their subcontractor had refused to pay for treatment, and now the police were after them.

They were the tenth or more this month alone. As long as they hid in this city, Iwona said, they would be found sooner or later; they needed a plan. She added that Sona should not carry it alone. They were here.

It was then that the **Adeptus Sprawiedliwi** began to come up. The word was that the Adeptus might give the Infected legal identities again. Justyna said nothing was certain yet, and the Adeptus's stance on the Infected was ambiguous. Sona said that if it truly came to that, there would be no other choice.
There, Iwona calmly revealed that twenty-five years ago, among the scouts sent to strike Ursus and wiped out at the border, had been her grandparents and her relatives.

Meanwhile, the **Armorless Union** stepped into Sona's path. They were Knight-Assassins who disposed of disobedient knights in the shadows for the General Chamber of Commerce. When Sona scoffed at their demand to hand over the Infected she was hiding, they answered that anyone the Chamber had marked was as good as dead.
Biological death is not the only kind of death, Flametail Knight.
At that moment, Greynuty's cannon fire came in from the rear. While Justyna covered them with sniper fire, Iwona charged in first.

Around the same time, **Platinum** of the Armorless Union asked a subordinate whether the Infected cry. The Infected were neither monsters nor villains, he said, and he had no heart for this job. But compassion was a luxury in times like these, he added, and left for another assignment.

Then the Infected's shelter was raided. The Armorless Union sealed off the area and drove people from their homes with gas. A few knights blocked arrows with their own bodies, but they could not protect everyone.
When someone suggested leaving the city, Greynuty answered that their status as Infected knights was the one thing that had protected them so far. The only path left to Sona was the Adeptus.

Sona returned from meeting the Adeptus and named her contact. Demian, vice-president of the Knights Association: once a renowned Campaign Knight, he had abruptly retired to take a desk post, a heavyweight now. His condition came down to a single phrase.
...A Great Separation. He wants to use our hands... to put this city... to sleep.

On the day they set out to move the Infected, Sona asked whether they could succeed. Greynuty said she would not give up until the knight nobility bowed their heads. Iwona said it was enough not to die. Justyna said that as long as Pinus Sylvestris remained as it was, that alone was enough.
After that, Sona often drifted off. One day she dozed on a bench, and in her dream were a sea of fire and Originium, and a voice saying the Kaliska family had abandoned the people of its territory.

When she woke, Sona watched the passersby hurrying through the neon. What would they think if they knew an Infected was sitting here? The answer came to her unbidden: 'They wouldn't think much of it.'

blocks.cap: People keep moving, and life melts into the neon.

blocks.x: Then Greynuty called. They had found the underground shelter. They could not save everyone, but they had to save as many as they could.
A few words slipped from Sona's mouth. "This... is what it is to be Infected!"
3. This Shell Is for the Spectators
As a child, **Greynuty** followed her stern grandmother to the arena for training. She remembered clearly the drill her grandmother had taught her.
Shield up, cannon up, and fire! ...When the cannon roars, victory is within sight!
Her grandmother clicked her tongue that her money-blinded children had forgotten even that maxim, and told her granddaughter never to grow up crooked.

blocks.cap: The road to the arena for training, following her grandmother.

blocks.x: And now the commentator introduced her: once part of the Kaliska Group, the old magnates of southern forestry; now nothing more than an Infected, fighting for Pinus Sylvestris. Her opponent was Ingra, the 'Brassrust Knight' of the Bloodboil Knightclub.
Ingra called her Oripathic filth and a rock-rat, and sneered that a petty firm like the Kaliskas would not even collect her corpse. Greynuty did not answer a single word. She only pulled the trigger.

In the stands, Sona told Iwona and Justyna about Greynuty's past. Once she was infected, the Kaliska clan blamed her for the family's decline and stripped her of her standing by unanimous vote. Even her parents, under threat, raised their hands.

Some even wanted her gone from the world, and on that day it was Sona who stood beside her and stopped them. That was why she was dragging the match out, Sona said: to thoroughly crush a proud knight, and to quiet her own anger.

Greynuty used the recoil of her own shot to sidestep the final charge, then pressed the muzzle to Ingra's back and pulled the trigger. When the fallen Ingra snarled that not one of them, not one Infected, would get away, she turned the muzzle to the sky.
This shell is an offering to the spectators. You don't deserve it.

Amid the cheers, Greynuty thought of her father. The Kaliska family had not produced a true cannonlancer in generations, he had said, so she must not disappoint their ancestors. And she had answered that she would not.
When Sona asked the dazed Greynuty why she had fired her last shell into the sky, Greynuty answered that laying a hand on a match already decided would make her no different from him.
4. Enlisted for Three Days' Meals

Before that, Sona and Greynuty had seen news of an Infected knight on television. The 'Wild Mane Knight' **Iwona**, who had fought her way up from the underground arenas, had come to blows with another competitor in a lounge and now faced suspension.

A few days later, released by the General Chamber of Commerce, Iwona slipped out past the reporters to find Sona and Greynuty waiting. She joined, saying she would go along for now with anywhere that had no knight nobles, and asked to borrow enough for three days' meals and her weapon repairs. Sona pressed the money into the hand of a woman who did not even know why she had been released.

The next day, evicted by her landlord, Iwona came to the hideout with her belongings and was startled to find not even a sofa. The one member left there told her that Sona spent most of her prize money settling the Infected.

blocks.cap: An abandoned office building. The hideout of Pinus Sylvestris.

blocks.x: Pressed by Iwona, the member admitted it. The two of them had also made up the shortfall in her bail, and since they had dealt with the Chamber, there would have been a price. Right now, the two had gone to evacuate the Infected.

Then Iwona found Sona in an alley, five hunters closing in, an Infected child hidden away. Iwona asked whether she wanted to help more of the Infected. When Sona said yes, Iwona asked why she would ever refuse, and told her to invite her properly.
If Pinus Sylvestris can change the lives of the Infected and protect the people in front of us... then I'll stake my life alongside you, Sona.
Iwona told her to take the child first, and faced the hunters alone.

When it was over, Iwona said she would give all her prize money to the knightclub. She had never thought of making money with the strength she had trained to become a Campaign Knight, and she had long wanted to do something for the Infected, like the Blood Knight.

She also gave the name **'Justice Knight'** to an old fire-support robot she had dragged out of a junk heap. Once an Infected engineer from the neighborhood had worked on it, the machine came back to life.
5. If the Wind Could Carry a Voice

**Justyna** was a country girl who practiced between farm chores, climbing haystacks to gaze toward the Grand Knight Territory. When she said she would return once she became a knight, the voices of home promised to wait for her to come back in glory.

Now she was taking down Armorless Union assassins from long range while leading 'Plastic Knight' **Szewczyk**, whom she had pulled out of a hospital, through the encirclement. He made it clear that he took no orders from an Infected; they had joined hands only because they shared an enemy.
Justyna said she had watched his matches and, truth be told, did not like him. But he knew as well as she did that he could not face the Armorless Union alone.

Ten days earlier, Justyna had been surrounded by assailants hidden in a crowd when Sona and Greynuty appeared. Sona held out her hand to the wounded Justyna and asked her to come with them. Justyna answered that she trusted them, because they were the same.

After her wounds were treated, in the Infected's neighborhood, Justyna spoke of 'two three-week periods'. She had been infected on her way to the Grand Knight Territory, was refused knight registration, and drifted for three weeks without even a hotel to stay in.

In the third week, the Blood Knight won the Major. Three weeks after that, a registration window for Infected knights opened. She fought illegal matches on the black market to scrape together the fee.

blocks.cap: The neighborhood where the Infected live in hiding. Most were infected in accidents and lost anywhere else to go.

blocks.x: She became a titled star competitor, yet Justyna said there was no future for Infected knights. Having turned down recruitment offers and declared she would found an independent knightclub, she had become a thorn in the Chamber's side.
When she said she had nowhere to go, Sona brought up the knightclub. Justyna answered briefly. "Us... together."

On the day she left home, she was asked to play her grass whistle one more time. Everyone worried about her, knowing how easily she grew lonely, yet they believed she would become a great knight, like the Radiant Knight she adored.

Then, with the hideout ahead of them, Justyna revealed that rescuing Szewczyk had been her own decision. The Armorless Union had reached for his son as well, and the people Sona sent had protected the boy. Without his father, that child would have no home to return to.
Justyna the Knight has a home, with family and friends waiting for her. But Justyna the Infected has none of that.

If the wind really could carry her voice, she said, she would send nothing but the sound of her grass whistle. She wanted to leave the Justyna her hometown remembered as nothing more than a girl dreaming of knighthood.
6. A Duel the Victor Could Not Smile About

Meanwhile, in the courtyard of the Nearl house, a duel had ended. The 'Radiant Knight' **Margaret Nearl**, home at last after a long journey, had knocked the sword from her uncle **Młynar**'s hand. Młynar had not used his Arts, but he said flatly that a win was a win.

Młynar said his niece was trampling on her grandfather's will. When Margaret countered, 'Fear neither hardship nor darkness!', he told her to face reality and the lives of others, said that one day she would be disappointed, and left.
Her younger sister **Maria Nearl** and their aunt **Zofia** came running. Maria said that if Margaret won the Major again, their uncle would not say a word. What was all of this for?

blocks.cap: For the family. For oneself. For the glory of knighthood.

blocks.x: The truth is, she already knows that most of what can be won in this nation of knights today lies far from glory. Maria suddenly fell silent.

Margaret said she would enter the Major. If everyone hid in the corners and stood by, telling themselves 'nothing can be done', when would the knights of Kazimierz ever reclaim true glory? Light, she said, is sometimes meant to open new sight for those who have lost their way.
With too little time left to gather points, Maria offered her own, saying knights of the same house could transfer points to one another. When Margaret refused, Maria told her what she truly felt.
Honestly, I don't really want to be a knight. Knights can't change the knighthood, Margaret.

She had become a knight because she did not want to lose anyone, not her grandfather, not their father, not her sister, yet nothing had changed. All she wanted was for this house to remain their home. Margaret only answered that she would think on it a little longer.
In the meantime, Zofia urged Młynar to talk openly with the girls, and got only a cold reply. Zofia told him she was disappointed in the man who had once been everyone's hero, and turned away.
7. Before the Wall of Champions
Around then, Platinum of the Armorless Union ordered his subordinates to keep watching the Radiant Knight, hoping she would stay quietly at home.

Margaret's companions **Shining** and **Nightingale**, at the third Infected settlement they had found, watched a construction crew tear down the buildings and the underground sections. Asked what would happen if people were still down there, Shining only said to remember everything they had seen today.

Meanwhile, Margaret was walking a corridor hung with endless portraits of past champions when she came upon a man. He introduced himself as 'the spokes— no, the staff member responsible for maintaining this wall.' It was **Malkiewicz**.

blocks.cap: A corridor of champions' portraits stretching on without end. The Radiant Knight's portrait hangs here too.

blocks.x: With the woman from the portrait standing beside him, Malkiewicz was seized by a strange premonition that what had always stood firm might finally begin to shake. As an ordinary fan of knights and a resident of the Territory, he offered a few words.
Welcome back to Kazimierz, Radiant Knight. All of this is only the beginning. Isn't it?

At home, when Maria asked what she had been through these past years, Margaret said she would tell her someday. A very long story, she said, and one that did not necessarily end happily, as the knight novels did.
Then the commentator called out the name. The Radiant Knight, back in the arena: Margaret Nearl. Home at last after a long journey, the knight pressed forward, as she always had.
8. A Suit He Cannot Take Off

On the day of the forum the General Chamber of Commerce held before the Major's main stage, Spokesman Malkiewicz kept fidgeting with the jacket of his tailored suit. Even when a staff worker told him the spokesman was the true heavyweight, he kept telling himself he did not belong in a place like this.

Until a few days earlier, he had been a corporate employee worrying about rent. He had been fretting that his pay would be cut after he failed to persuade Maria Nearl, running small errands for Mr. Czarny, when a single phone call made him spokesman.
I dialed the spokesman's number, and you answered. Therefore, you are the spokesman.
Another voice made it clear that he now represented the General Chamber of Commerce, and that he had no right to 'ask questions'.

The staff worker turned out to be Team Leader **Gerald**, whom he had once worked alongside. The list of rookies the two had been tasked with connecting to knightclubs had included the Flametail Knight and the Fartooth Knight. Gerald had told those two to read their contracts carefully, and the recruitment never went through.

When Malkiewicz confessed that all of this felt like a dream and frightened him, Gerald politely drew a line. Many people would trade places with you, he said. Whatever you think, to everyone you already look like a heavyweight.

blocks.cap: The corridor just outside the forum hall. Here, an old colleague drew a line.

blocks.x: At the forum, a corporate employee spilled a drink on his clothes and told him to take off his jacket, but Malkiewicz desperately declined.
So much of what happens has nothing to do with what one thinks, he murmured to himself. **"Now... somehow, I don't think I can take this suit off anymore."**
9. You Never Know When the Phone Will Ring

After finishing school, **Centaurea** placed second in the Rose Paper Union's knight auditions and became a freelance knight. She was a fine archer, fairly pretty, and willing to follow company policy.

But while she waited for her knight title, she grew sick of knights. Orders to throw matches were routine, followed by baseless scandals and schedules changed at whim. A product, at least, is finished once it is sold. She was not even that.

In a match she had been told to lose just before receiving her title, her Kuranta opponent, from a distinguished family, chased her to the very end and humiliated her, even after she signaled she would go down.
Then a call came from a stranger. He offered her a better job. If she wished, he said, her arrows could pierce even the night of the Grand Knight Territory.

At a flower shop at the address he gave, she received a bouquet. Inside were the name of the Kuranta from that last match and a military arrow with no serial number. Having been invited, she had no way back to knighthood, and if she failed the test, she would be the one in the next day's papers.
She drew her bowstring. The arrow pierced the window and struck him between the eyes as he sat in his massage chair. The chair kept running, but he never got up again.
The man on the phone said she was a member of the Armorless Union as of today, and her contract with the Rose Paper Union had already been dissolved. He told her to call him Platinum.

Three months later, people had forgotten a knight named Centaurea entirely. Her manager had taken on another knight, and the fans who used to wait outside her home did not recognize their former idol when she walked past.

She learned management and command from Platinum, and watched him endure a spokesman's tirade of more than an hour and thirty-six minutes without a single word of rebuttal. Knight or Knight-Assassin, in the end they were all just employees hired by the General Chamber of Commerce.

One rainy night, **Lazurite** from higher up came to her. Platinum had betrayed them and died while fleeing, he said. Centaurea had known he was wavering in front of his last target, but she had never thought he would throw away his life.
Told that she would be Platinum now, she could not answer. Lazurite pressed Platinum's badge into her hand and left, saying he would take silence as consent.

For Centaurea, now Platinum, the Chamber's calls clung to her like a ghost. One day's call asked her to make sure the chairman of Glorious Shield Industries, a director of the Chamber, did not attend the next day's board meeting.

The headquarters building stood wide open. There were no guards, and every camera was down for maintenance. In the top-floor lounge she broke the chairman's neck, then opened the curtains and waited for the next call.

blocks.cap: The top floor of Glorious Shield Industries headquarters. The chairman's private lounge.

blocks.x: Outside the window spread the night of the Grand Knight Territory, its lights never going out. Her parents had said her sharp eyes would bring glory to the family, but what she had come to be certain of was an invisible hand that worked even the directors like puppets.
**As long as she remains on this land, there is no escaping that hand.**
Then the phone rang.
So tired... I want... to rest...

Tonight, as every night, the Grand Knight Territory does not go dark. Sona on her bench and Platinum on the top floor looked out at the same neon. Beneath that light, some chose to trust one another, and someone, tonight as always, picks up the phone.

act8mini.tagline: The memory-less Doctor passes through the wasteland, a Catastrophe storm, and a storeroom of the dead's belongings, slowly coming face to face with the 'Doctor' that others remember. To hold on to hope is a cruel thing.
