blocks.x: Months after waking in a sarcophagus in Chernobog, the **Doctor** knows who they once were only from the mouths of others. The stories told by the physician **Kal'tsit**, and the days remembered by **Amiya**, the leader of Rhodes Island: that is all there is.
In sleep, a voice comes. It asks whether, having lost everything, the Doctor still tried to leave behind one small hope. To hold on to hope, it says, is a very cruel thing.
In the wasteland, in the storm, among things whose owners are gone, the Doctor meets that question again. Through the gaps slip nights of Babel that the Doctor cannot remember.
1. The Samples That Vanished in Tkaronto

In a back alley of Tkaronto, a city of Columbia, Rhodes Island pilot Dylan stood holding one half of the crossbow that had been aimed at him moments before. The 'policeman' who fired it lay unconscious from a single blow by the Feline operator **Blaze**.

A day after the delegation reached the city, a band posing as police seized their hotel and took every last drug sample. In the attack, the Doctor and Amiya had escaped separately by car, and nothing had been heard from them since.
Meanwhile, the Doctor was deep in a long dream. As a familiar woman slowly drifted away, a voice said, "Hope is enough to drive a perfectly good person mad."
When the Doctor finally opened their eyes, it was in a barren desert of rock, where a man in a helmet like an iron drum offered a greeting: "Good morning, good afternoon, and good evening!"

blocks.cap: The Gaspar Wildland, eastern Columbia.

blocks.x: The man introduced himself as a merchant named **Cannot**, or Mr. Goodenough. The two had survived a fall from a cliff, but they had no communicator and no food. Below the cliff, the vehicles of the mercenaries who had chased them were still smoking.

When Cannot remarked that only a large corporation could hire mercenaries like these, Amiya thought of **Mama John's**. Tkaronto's largest firm had offered to sell Rhodes Island's drugs on its behalf, and she had refused, saying the painkiller was still in testing. Cannot warned that the police there could not be trusted. For two refined Originium Ingots, he agreed to guide them to the nearest Messenger Outpost.
2. Wild Greens by the Campfire
Five hours into the walk, the Doctor was exhausted. When Cannot said that at this rate their water and food would run short, Amiya asked whether there was a forest nearby.

That night, by a campfire in a ravine, Amiya cooked supper from the greens and mushrooms she had gathered. The Doctor had taught her this years ago. When a young Amiya asked whether something was safe to eat, the Doctor had told her it was, as long as it was cooked: the very words Amiya had just said.

blocks.cap: A ravine at night. The crackle of firewood mixed with Amiya's humming.

blocks.x: "It was so very hard, but those were happy days." Something seemed to surface in the Doctor's mind, then vanished like a bubble. Amiya said it was all right not to remember and went back to stirring the mess tin, but her smile was somehow lonely.
Cannot said the wasteland was crawling with bandits, bounty hunters, and **Rusthammer**, a loose organization that took in everyone from the Sarkaz Fiends Gang to Catastrophe worshippers.
The voice came that night too. "By the time you awaken, no one will be at your side. No one will know of your sacrifice, let alone remember it."

At dawn the next day, the Doctor admitted to having lost their memory. Cannot said there was a way to get it all back at once, but told the Doctor to take it slowly, for the Doctor's own sake and for Amiya's.

As the sun rose, Amiya took the Doctor's hand and said that on their very first night in the wasteland, they had greeted the sunrise like this too. The Doctor tried to recall the scene, but all that remained in hand was the 'story' Kal'tsit had told.
3. Those Who Die in Hope
After another day on foot they reached the Messenger Outpost: a small pocket of civilization in the middle of the wasteland, with dozens of vehicles ringed around a cluster of shacks.

blocks.cap: The Messenger Outpost. One of the shacks bore the Mama John's logo.

blocks.x: On the radio, a police statement announced that a foreign company called 'Rhodes Island' was involved in the armed clash in Tkaronto. The ones who had been attacked had somehow become the targets of a terrorism investigation.

Then Cannot took the two of them to the office of the Mama John's frontier development corps. Dave, an Infected settler, begged for next month's medicine in advance because his wife had grown worse. The only answer he got was the rules.
Amiya examined the medicine Cannot handed her and said it was not an Oripathy suppressant. One was a painkiller; the other, a nutritional supplement.

Mama John's, which began as a donut chain, had been using production lines it bought up to sell painkillers as if they were suppressants. If it used Rhodes Island's samples to make a more convincing 'suppressant,' Cannot predicted, the settlers would become its test subjects, and the front page would carry the headline 'New Hope for the Infected!'
"People come to Columbia with hope, create value with hope, and die with hope." Having stated flatly that no one could save them, Cannot said almost exactly what the Doctor had heard in the dream.
To hold on to hope is a cruel thing indeed. ... Hope is enough to drive even a flawless person mad.
Amiya's ears slowly drooped. Still, the Doctor spoke.
Even if holding on to hope brings pain, I think it's worth it. If we give up on hope, would the lives we've lived mean anything at all?
Cannot said he was not persuaded, but he had felt the Doctor's sincerity. When he asked what someone who could not even fight meant to do now, the Doctor answered: use their wits.
4. The Detention Center They Walked Into

Four days later, Amiya was waiting when the Doctor walked out the gate of a Columbian detention center. Beside her, as she cried out how worried she had been, Cannot called it a very clever scheme and said the Doctor now frightened him a little.

blocks.cap: A Columbian detention center. The Doctor spent three days here.

blocks.x: The Doctor had turned themselves in to Columbian Customs and Border Protection, confessing that the company they belonged to had smuggled in Oripathy drugs. Mama John's would have destroyed every contract document to erase the traces of the attack, so the samples in its hands became nothing but contraband, and the government seized every one.

Blaze, who appeared soon after, listed off the fines, the compensation and the detention, and demanded to know how the Doctor planned to explain this to Dr. Kal'tsit. Cannot left, saying they would meet again before long, and Blaze muttered that something about him was off.
Three days earlier, the Doctor had asked Cannot for one thing: that 'your comrades' keep Amiya safe until they were out. Hadn't someone been following them the whole way here?
Beneath the iron helmet, Cannot was silent for a long time. Then he said, "Well done." The deal was struck: the Doctor would pretend not to have seen the documents he had taken from the vehicles.

Once the Doctor had gone, members of the Fiends Gang and Rusthammer who had been hiding came into view. Asked why he had saved Rhodes Island, Cannot answered that this land would only get more interesting if people like that lived a long time.
5. Full Speed Through the Cyclones

Aboard Rhodes Island as it crossed the wasteland after leaving Lungmen, Kal'tsit had scanned the Doctor's brain seven times over the past month or so. The Doctor's memories of themselves were gone, but the command skills the body had learned were returning fast. Kal'tsit told the Doctor not to push too hard. She was worried about them.

Some time later, in the corridor outside the bridge, a pilot was trying to set aside a storm warning from the Catastrophe Messenger **Earthspirit**. The Doctor appeared, took the report containing the warning, and went straight to Amiya.

Minutes later the wind speed spiked and visibility dropped. A supercell storm. A Catastrophe. Several small cyclones were about to merge into a core two kilometers across. It was too late to change course, and holding position could cost lives.

The Doctor said to press on. The control room staff protested that it was suicide, but Amiya said she trusted the Doctor. As Earthspirit murmured that the formula the Doctor had dashed off looked somehow familiar, Amiya handed full command of the ship to the Doctor.

blocks.cap: "Rhodes Island, all ahead full!"

blocks.x: The Doctor turned to starboard to avoid a downburst, and ordered the ship onward even as cyclones closed in from both sides.

blocks.cap: "Seventy-five meters. Fifty meters. Thirty meters..."

blocks.x: Gripping the Doctor's hand tightly, Amiya said she was tense, but not afraid.
The closer we come to despair, the grander and more beautiful the view we face with hope. That's something you taught me, Doctor.

"Hope comes from the commitment to never give in, even at the bitter end." Amiya said the Doctor had told her the very same thing long ago. At last the wind died down, and Rhodes Island left the Catastrophe zone without a single injury.
Amiya held the Doctor tight. "Thank you... for staying by my side."
6. The Formula Never Forgotten

After the storm passed, Kal'tsit pointed to the formula. It was one the Doctor had created in the past, and even with their memories gone, Kal'tsit said, the Doctor had **never for a moment forgotten being a researcher of Originium**.

blocks.cap: After the storm. Kal'tsit and the Doctor, alone.

blocks.x: Kal'tsit asked why the Doctor clung to research, and on hearing the answer, said she had heard something similar before. It was the answer of someone who longed for unknown truths, someone who had told her, "But sometimes, salvation also means destruction."
Seven examinations had proven that the Doctor had forgotten even what they had done to Theresa. Even so, Kal'tsit said, doubt was rising in her again. Who, exactly, was standing before her?

After saying that her resentment toward the Doctor of the past was not the whole of it, Kal'tsit asked a question of her own. If the Doctor regained their memories, they would learn where her resentment and W's came from, and where Amiya's unconditional trust came from. But those memories might swallow the Doctor as they were now. "Are you ready?"

The Doctor said nothing. Kal'tsit added that a malfunctioning life function restoration device could hardly have erased, of all things, only the memories that would most affect the Doctor's choices. "It seems she trusted you even more than I ever knew."

That evening, the Doctor approved the young volcanologist **Eyjafjalla**'s application to the operations department and handed her their own Catastrophe research notes. She had tracked down the signs of rapidly proliferating Originium; hers was the report that had let the Doctor see the storm coming.
Hugging the notes tightly, she said, "If you're working this hard, Professor, what reason do any of us have to give up? Please keep leading Rhodes Island."
7. A Shield Without an Owner

Once, the Elite Operator **Ace** and the Sarkaz mercenary **Scout** made a bet over a red machine in a drifters' settlement. Ace bet it was junk; Scout bet it meant something. When the Doctor suggested they go see it together, Scout made sure there would be no backing out.

Then, three months after waking in Chernobog, the Doctor suddenly had a day off when Kal'tsit went out and a meeting was postponed. At breakfast in the cafeteria, Noir Corne began, "After all, back then we..." and was stopped by Yato.

The Doctor did not remember that 'back then.' Many people had died in the clash that rescued the Doctor. They had known the Doctor, but the Doctor had not known them. **Had all of this truly been worth it?**

That afternoon, in a storeroom piled with things no one had claimed, the Perro operator **Beagle** was polishing a badly broken shield. It was Ace's. The Doctor remembered that big operator and his easy laugh, but knew nothing of him beyond the fact that they had been old friends.

blocks.cap: The Integrated Bioprocessing Unit. A storeroom piled with unclaimed belongings.

blocks.x: Beagle said she came here every week to polish the shield. The Doctor tried to help, but could not lift it even a centimeter. Beagle laughed: Ace had once said the Doctor alone was a match for half an army.
In a corner of a shelf sat a box of belongings left by Reunion members in Lungmen. On the back of a silver pendant was an engraving: "To Ivana, our beloved daughter. May you be happy."

Ursus, the Infected, and we ourselves all lived through disaster. Was any of it truly worth it? Beagle said operators heading out on missions sometimes ask that. After Beagle ran off to the training grounds, the Doctor noticed an unfamiliar red shape among the stored things.
8. Beer in a Red Box

Around that time, in the power section on the ship's lowest deck, the Sarkaz mercenary **W** was saying goodbye to the Sarkaz boiler workers. When W asked why they had stayed when everyone else had left, a boiler worker answered that guarding this home Her Majesty had left them was his calling.
When **Ascalon**, in the shadows, pressed her to leave, W said, "You're not my boss anymore," and walked away, saying they would meet again in Londinium.

blocks.cap: The lower decks of the Rhodes Island main ship. The power section.

blocks.x: Some time later, the Doctor came down there. The boiler worker, who said he had once served under the Doctor's command, poured tea and urged the Doctor to open up to Amiya and Kal'tsit. "We keep moving forward, but in the end we meet again the very first people and events we came across."

That evening, Amiya admitted that Kal'tsit's outing had really been meant to give the tired-looking Doctor some rest. The red machine the Doctor had seen in the storeroom, according to Amiya, was the 'red industrial scrap' Ace and Scout had brought back. Chief engineer **Closure** had broken three cutting machines without managing to open even its outer shell, and had left it there.
Back in the storeroom, the Doctor tapped lightly on its shell. The machine beeped and opened like a hatch. Inside was beer. It was a vending machine.
The Doctor said it was just junk, but it had given them beer, and suggested placing it beside Ace's shield. "The bet was won, after all."
9. Marco the Traitor

Kazdel, before the Doctor lost their memory. **Babel**, led by the Sarkaz king **Theresa**, had been driven into a corner. As the **Military Council** grew in strength, Babel faced being besieged that autumn, and Theresa decided on a full withdrawal, away from Kazdel.
The Doctor said many Sarkaz would follow her, but that they themselves would not help with that choice, only watch. Theresa answered that, for now, that was best.

blocks.cap: Babel on the eve of withdrawal. Theresa said things would get better someday.

blocks.x: Thirteen days later, a Sarkaz soldier slipped into the camp, waiting for a moment when the Doctor was alone. He raged that Her Majesty kept an outsider at her side, and as Scout moved to cut his throat, the Doctor stepped in.

The Doctor told him that it was not the Doctor he could not trust, but his own Majesty; that he was afraid of the part of himself that could no longer trust Theresa, and was laying the blame on someone else. The Doctor said they remembered him carrying the wounded Ascalon back, and hoped he would leave this place alive.
Theresa, arriving then, recognized him. "You... don't trust me? Marco?"
Scout said military law allowed only death, and Kal'tsit, too, said he must not be let go. But the Doctor said to release him and see what he would choose.

Theresa sent him to Ascalon and let Babel decide his crime. Told that he could not leave as long as he thought of himself as a Sarkaz of Kazdel, **Marco** broke down. He cried out for them to kill him: she was still the war hero they had looked up to, and the Sarkaz had been waiting for their blood-soaked history to burn again.
Not long after, the Doctor relayed word from Ascalon. **Marco had taken his own life.** He had not wanted to bring harm to his king.
Theresa, who had said she had only seen a kind of shadow in him, said only that she understood. Then she said to the Doctor, "Don't worry, I trust you."
Theresa said she hoped the sight they longed for would come at least a little closer within the years they would live to see. The Doctor answered briefly. "...Indeed. I'm already used to it."
10. What Do You Fight For
"Only by acting on your own will, moment to moment, can you say you are truly alive." Someone once said that to Kal'tsit.

Now, on the deck at sunset, Kal'tsit went through the Doctor's schedule item by item. Rhodes Island was discussing a trip to Londinium while moving its patients to a medical facility in Connor County.

blocks.cap: The deck at dusk. Kal'tsit said proper rest was needed, too.

blocks.x: Nights of Babel overlapped with that schedule. Scout had tried to take sole blame for an operation caught in an ambush, to protect the honor of Reyka, a soldier who had enlisted to repay a debt to Theresa. The Doctor clapped him on the shoulder, punished no one, and had him answer with the operations to come.

Meanwhile, in front of Kal'tsit, Closure began to say that in the last few days before losing their memory, the Doctor had grown stranger and stranger, and was cut off. Above all, she was not to tell the Doctor.

And one dawn in Babel, Theresa, who suffered from Oripathy, smiled wearily when the Doctor said the enemy would soon realize its defeat. When a young Amiya, woken by the sounds of an expedition being readied, peeked into the command room, Theresa soothed the child: had any battle the Doctor commanded ever failed to end quickly? "Doctor, Kal'tsit, the day we win this war can't be far off, can it?"

blocks.cap: "Doctor, what does it mean to truly live?"

blocks.x: Back on the deck, Kal'tsit asked: a life spent obeying another's will, with no reason of its own to go on, or a life with a body but no memories. Which would the Doctor choose?
To the Doctor, who chose to be a person rather than a puppet, Kal'tsit said that freedom comes at a price. She had not been able to give many choices to the Doctor who woke without memories.
...Look into my eyes. And tell me, Doctor, what is it that you fight for?
As everything since waking in Chernobog welled up, the Doctor answered without thinking. Kal'tsit told the Doctor never to forget that answer. The Doctor, too, would be able to find their own path.
11. A Gamble on One Person

Meanwhile, while servicing **PRTS**, the ship's brain, Closure found the simulation records for the sarcophagus rescue operation. Of 167 processes, only two ended with the Doctor rescued and a safe withdrawal, and the real losses had been more than three times the calculation.

blocks.cap: Routine maintenance of PRTS.

blocks.x: Closure said that if the operation had been voted down, they might have lost the future. PRTS asked whether it was truly rational to stake the future on a single person.

Closure told an old story. She had been shut away in the attic of her Vampire clan when one day Theresa opened the locked door, walked in, and said she was looking for people to break the chains of tradition. Closure followed out of sheer curiosity, and the one who met her at the rendezvous point was the Doctor.

And the Doctor who came back to Rhodes Island won one battle through precise calculation and the next by reading the enemy's mind without a single equation. The same person, Closure said, but clearly different inside.
In the two years after Theresa was gone, they lost too many people. It was Amiya who proposed bringing the Doctor back. It was a gamble, Closure said, but time had proven Amiya right.
When PRTS said it could not approve of a gamble, Closure told it that it lacked one thing: something that could lead people to great deeds or turn them into monsters. Obsession.
Finishing the maintenance and heading out, Closure came face to face with the Doctor, standing in the doorway.
Epilogue. Insufficient Permissions
After Closure left, the Doctor asked PRTS who **Priestess** was, and why not even Kal'tsit would say anything about that person.
After a long silence, an alarm sounded.
Insufficient permissions. At this time, no registered member possesses the permissions required to receive an answer to this question.
PRTS told the Doctor to find the answer another way. Then, while running a self-check, it found a single undated video stored under special permissions.

blocks.cap: <PRTS's First Functional Test>, <Ship Video Record 000000001α>.

blocks.x: "Your question has been answered, Doctor." PRTS announced that the program would end in three seconds and the permissions would lock again. Three, two, one.

The merchant of the wasteland said hope was cruel. Kal'tsit asked if the Doctor was ready. Beagle asked whether all of it had been worth it. The Doctor had not yet regained their memories. But the words that hope comes from the commitment to never give in, even at the bitter end, were the same before the memories were lost and now.

terms.desc: An armed band roaming the wastes, made up of people who turned their backs on civilization and chose to belong to the wastes.

blocks.x: The wastes of Ursus, the borderlands of Minos, a rec room aboard Rhodes Island, the ruins of Iberia, the back alleys of Leithanien, and the road toward Kjerag. In places that have nothing to do with one another, people who've never met are each looking for somewhere to stay.
Some are being chased and running, some are holding their ground because they have something to protect, and someone was just playing a video game. For now, they're small, scattered lights.
1. Entrance Exam: One Month in the Canyon

We start in the wastes just past the Ursus border. **Illa** and **Gareth** fought side by side in Reunion, and now they're walking away from Ursus together. Less than half the food they took from the warehouse is left, maybe four days' worth if they're lucky.

They're looking for a band called '**Rusthammer**.' Ursus soldiers called them wasteland savages who kill for fun, but the Rusthammer Gareth ran into back in the army was something else. Hundreds, maybe thousands of them stormed a border camp, beating on scrap metal as they came. They broke open two Infected mines, freed everyone held there, and burned down five supply depots.

When the two finally reach the boulder on the peak, there it is, just like the rumors said: a rusted hammer stuck upside-down in the rock, a black rag fluttering from it like a flag. A man steps out from behind the boulder and looks them up and down.

blocks.cap: North from the second peak, atop a massive boulder. Where Rusthammer waits.

blocks.x: You don't need to be sharp, but you do need to be tenacious.

The man calls them 'livestock awaiting slaughter,' then tosses them a shovel, a pickaxe, and a beast trap. Survive a month down in that gorge, and he'll accept them as people who belong to the wastes.

When Gareth snaps that tormenting the Infected must be some hobby of theirs, the man doubles over laughing and calls out **Boone**, an Infected man covered in ugly crystals, from behind the rock. Boone's answer is short: "Bullshit. I have no comrades this weak."

Out here, nobody cares if you're Infected, a fallen noble, or a Sarkaz. Embrace the wastes, cut yourself off from civilization, and you're one of them. Gareth wants to turn back, but it's Illa who stops him. Their food is nearly gone, she says, and she's noticed he hasn't eaten in two days.
2. The Day the Mossoats Sprouted, and the Bootprints

Fifteen days in, the two have become proper wastelanders. They trap and smoke a wild burdenbeast, and Illa suggests trading the extra meat for seeds at a wanderers' settlement. Gareth, who's never farmed a day in his life, gets teased as a 'little city kid' for it.

The cave they live in looks like an ancient mine shaft. Gareth guesses it might be a trace of the nations that rose and vanished on this land back before Ursus was Ursus and Kazimierz was Kazimierz. Illa laughs and says that if more people come and it grows into a town, she'll be mayor and Gareth can be deputy mayor.

blocks.cap: The cave in the gorge. Maybe someone's mine shaft, long ago.

blocks.x: At dawn on the twenty-ninth day, mossoat sprouts poke up from the soil they'd dusted with burdenbeast bone meal. But on a trip to look for water, Gareth spots Ursus army bootprints. At least twenty soldiers, by the look of them.

Gareth says they've come for him and that the two of them have to leave right now, and for the first time, Illa shouts at him. She's already lost the people of her village, her little sister, Sharla, and the captain along the way. Does she have to throw everything away and run again?
This whole month, I've lived like a person! Not like some beast just dragging out its life!

The moment Gareth says he'll stay and fight, a voice rings out: "Excellent!" Rusthammer had been checking every day to see if the two were still alive, and now they welcome Illa as a sister and Gareth as a brother. Compromise and escape are never-ending, they add.

Soon, twenty-four Ursus soldiers march into the gorge. They call Gareth a deserter, a corporal who ran off with army rations, and order him in Colonel Lomono's name to take his own life. But when a Rusthammer warrior strikes the ground three times with his weapon, warriors in battered iron armor rise up along both cliffs, packed shoulder to shoulder.
When Illa says she's glad to fight alongside them, the warrior corrects her. They don't 'battle.' Civilization stole everything from the land and made people weak, so all they do is destroy.
Catastrophes sweep the wastelands... Rusthammers smash the world!
3. The Goddess's Tent (The Sauna Is Mixed)
"You have no place in this world any longer." A warrior who had never once backed down before an enemy's war cries heard those words, and ran.

Meanwhile, in **Akroti**, a border region of Minos adjoining Sargon. The rain has gone on for days, and a Kuranta warrior who crossed over from the Sargon side lies collapsed at the border. The one who's been watching her for two hours is a **Sarkaz mercenary** hired by Minos, and he warns that she could be Sargon's bait.

But **Pallas**, the priestess whom the villages of Minos revere as their 'Goddess,' decides to pitch a tent near the border and treat the girl herself. There's a reason she put a Sarkaz on watch, too. The kindhearted Minoans wouldn't have lasted ten minutes before running over to lend a hand.

A while later, the Kuranta warrior **Heavyrain** wakes up in the tent. The moment Pallas hands back her weapon, she swings it, and all it does is thud against the canvas. She insists she's no longer a Sargon mercenary and just wants to leave, and then her stomach growls. Pallas sets down her own weapon and suggests she start with this delicious free meal.

When they step outside, the Minoan soldiers who were supposedly standing guard have gone off to eat lunch, drink, sing, and even recite poetry. As Heavyrain tries to leave, Pallas pitches the theater, the cinema, a Minoan restaurant, and the sauna, one after another. One remark from the Sarkaz, that the sauna is mixed, ends the sales pitch for good.

blocks.cap: Outside the tent. While the Minoan soldiers are off at lunch, the Sarkaz stands watch alone.

blocks.x: Heavyrain never does give her name, but Pallas hands her a compass that actually works. Someday a kind soul will come along, she says, one who'll give their all for you and flee the clutches of Death with you. Decide again when that day comes.

The Sarkaz grumbles that her words have a strange way of coming true, so she'd better watch what she says. Heavyrain answers that it doesn't matter what happens; maybe the destination of this journey is the journey itself. Pallas promises to pray for her and leaves her with one last thought.
And the most important thing we must face is... to find a place for ourselves.
4. A Night Left Unrecorded

That night at the border post, a Minoan soldier changing shifts asks the Sarkaz mercenary for his name. When the war is over and they carve the heroes' names, does he really want to go down as just 'Sarkaz'?
The Sarkaz laughs it off and says to ask again once they've survived. Inside, though, he thinks it wouldn't be so bad for a Sarkaz to be known as a hero.

Then Pallas appears at the post. The Kuranta she met earlier was so completely ordinary that it's been weighing on her, she says. She came to see what lies behind a girl who left as if she were fleeing an evil spirit.

Out of the darkness steps another Sarkaz, a **Sarkaz assassin**. He's been tracking the Kuranta warrior to dispose of a 'deserter,' and when Pallas blocks his path, he swings his blade at her. The one who stops it is the Sarkaz mercenary.

blocks.cap: Night at the border post. Two Sarkaz blades, pointed at each other.

blocks.x: The Sarkaz mercenary tells the assassin, "Nothing to do with the priestess. That job you took is just pathetic."
Pallas, too, declares that for the Kuranta traveler's safety, she won't let the assassin leave alive.
The fight that night was never recorded. All we're told is that one soul is still running, and before long it will burn brighter and gather at Rhodes Island.
5. The Ghost Story That Comes After the True End

Meanwhile, aboard the Rhodes Island landship. **Bena** has been hunting for her best friend **Annie**, asking her Victorian coin, 'Sir Barkeley,' for directions along the way, and finds her in the common rest area. Annie points at an older girl playing a game in front of the TV and signals Bena to keep quiet so she won't startle her.
When Bena asks if this calls for a bit of a 'show,' Annie answers with a single word: "Yes."

That older girl is **Kirara**, an operator who's painfully shy around strangers. She's right on the verge of the true ending in the horror-suspense game 'Nukenin,' but she can't bring herself to turn down a little kid who looks about to cry over not getting to play. The moment she hands over the controller, a big-mouthed monster pops out, and Kirara scrambles to switch off the blood effects and the disturbing content.

But the kid, who's only just learned the basic controls, rattles off combos that even Kirara only recently mastered. Together they strip the boss 'Sawara the Silentious' of his invincibility shield with the 'Sachet of Consecration,' and after a fifteen-minute slugfest, they reach the true end.

blocks.cap: The common rest area. The boss Kirara couldn't beat fell to a little kid.

blocks.x: According to a very excited Kirara, every ghost story in Shin-Aki City, Higashi's city of urban legends, branched out from Sawara, the oldest one of all. And since ghost stories only survive as long as people remember them, once the truth comes out and the mystery is gone, they lose their reason to exist.

Bena thinks to herself that she'd like this lady to 'remember' something too. She brings Kirara a cup of water and silently cheers, 'Bait taken~.' Then, when Kirara tells Bena her name, saying it's not every day someone wants to talk to her, Bena returns the favor with a ghost story from Victoria.

The story begins in rainy Lyndon, in Victoria. A little Caprinae kid, whose parents said to wait at a fountain square and never came back, carries a fallen old lady's apple basket for her and follows her all the way home.

blocks.cap: A rainy street in Lyndon. Where Bena's story begins.

blocks.x: In the warm house, the old lady even heals the kid's scrapes, then shows the kid an exquisite doll about the same size in a dark room upstairs. This is her granddaughter **Annie**, she says, an adorable Caprinae. "Just like you."
"Take your delectable, kindly soul... and hand it over." No one ever saw that child again, and in house after house, all that was left was a doll named Annie.
As Kirara trembles, Bena says, "Annie, come say hello."
Hello, Miss Kirara. I am Annie.

Once the prank is over, Annie scolds Bena for going too far. Asked if she made the story up, Bena readily admits she did, but Annie's worry is about something else entirely: Grandmother is going to be upset that it wasn't scary enough.

Actually, the kid who carried the apple basket was Bena herself. Only what the old lady said, smiling kindly, was real. If she'd run off with that basket that day, those five apples would have been all she ever got to eat, and if she'd taken even one bite of the food on the table, she'd have been sent right back out into the storm.

As it turns out, the one who'd been secretly playing this game for three nights, twenty-four hours in all, was Annie. It was fun, so she wanted Bena to play too. The two sit side by side and start the game from the beginning, and Bena wonders whether the story she told to scare Kirara might take root in Kirara's homeland and become a new ghost story.
6. That Tower Was a Lighthouse

And in northern Iberia, an abandoned town on the coast. **Blue Poison** and the engineer **Glaucus** head into an unidentified building to investigate. Past an entrance someone hacked open with an axe, they go down, and further down.

In a passage where every light is dead, Blue Poison teases Glaucus with ghost stories, and Glaucus walks on clutching the hem of Blue Poison's clothes. At the end of the passage lies the body of a Kuranta bounty hunter who drowned tangled in seagrass, and the walls bear the marks of seawater flooding in twice.

blocks.cap: A lightless underground. Where the sea rose and drained away twice.

blocks.x: Blue Poison brings up the 'disaster,' something Iberians aren't even allowed to speak of. Over a hundred years ago, Ægirs took her ancestors, who could wield poison, and drew toxins from them without end. It was to fight an enormous creature that doesn't exist on land. Something, most likely, from the sea.

Even the day she ran into Skadi in the corridor, she couldn't bring herself to ask. She wasn't sure she had the courage to look at the truth. And yet she has never once set her poison down. Maybe, she says, it's because deep down she has always believed it would one day meet the enemy it was meant for.

Around the time they've lost count of how many floors they've gone down, a white light floats up out of the darkness. Blue Poison's bolt splits in two to surround it, and when Glaucus fires her Franker at maximum power, a scream bursts out of the light: "I mean no harm!"

The light belongs to **Aria**, a Caster from Iberia. She'd handed over her last coins to ask about a chance to strike it rich and got pointed to these ruins. By any measure, she's been scammed. And she's the one who tells them: this building is a lighthouse.

Aria is an apprentice lighthouse keeper who grew up in the lighthouse of a small seaside town. Ever since that day decades ago, when every coastline in Iberia went dark, the lighthouse has never shone again. But her teacher still tries to light it every night, and the two of them still keep watch over it.
When Blue Poison asks whether she'd keep watch even if this coast, where not a single ship comes or goes, stays silent forever, Aria doesn't hesitate.
Yes. Even so.

At the top, where Aria leads them, all that's left is a broken energy core. When Glaucus says she'd like to bring it back to Rhodes Island and study it with **Closure**, Aria's eyes light up. She asks them to take her along too, and collapses mid-sentence.

blocks.cap: The top of the lighthouse. All that remained was a single broken energy core.

blocks.x: Blue Poison's neurotoxin had only just kicked in. She'd assumed Aria had some special immunity, but no. Aria was just a little slow to react.

By the time they're out of the lighthouse and the comms are back, Aria has come to, and Blue Poison tells **Elysium** they'll be bringing her to Rhodes Island. She adds that this lighthouse could make a good new Rhodes Island office.
With refugees streaming out of the ruined cities to the south, she says, it may not shine the way it used to, but this lighthouse might still be able to watch over this coast.
7. A Maverick in Leithanien

Meanwhile in Leithanien, **Carnelian** of Sargon has come on behalf of **Count Hohenlohe** to sign a partnership contract with Sir Feuerbach's household. Eyeing the black Solidified Origincrystals that decorate the reception room's table, she remarks that if you gathered all the blood spilled for these crystals, it would fill Sir Feuerbach's bathtub.

Sir Feuerbach's attendant replies that the recent mining accident will be handled like dusting off a carpet. He adds that compared to the age of the **Witch King**, when a neighboring town could be covered in withered corpses overnight under a red sky, the Empresses' rule at least leaves you some way to deal with things.

blocks.cap: The reception room of Sir Feuerbach's household. The black crystals on the table came from hundreds of meters underground.

blocks.x: After leaving, Carnelian walks past the bustling streets out to an alley on the outskirts, where she spots a girl being chased by guards and hides her from them. The girl is Infected, with crystals showing beneath her collar.

The girl's eyes sparkle at Carnelian's tales of Sargon, with rivers that fall from the sky and trees bigger than villages, and she deflates when the treasure-cave story ends with '...just kidding.' But when Carnelian mentions that in Sargon, the Infected aren't treated like a disaster, the girl begins to tell her own story.

blocks.cap: After shaking off the guards. The girl listens closely to stories of a faraway land she's never heard of.

blocks.x: Her parents never came back after a mine shaft collapsed, and the guards sealed off the neighborhood, then forced their way into every home and dragged people away. She escaped with some other kids, but they got separated the day before yesterday, and she's been alone ever since.

Then the Leithanian Caster who'd been chasing the girl appears. Carnelian says she's seen them dragging Infected slaves along when they cast their Arts, and presses him: are they still studying the cruel techniques the Witch King left behind? The Caster says he has no intention of making an enemy of Count Hohenlohe and hands over the girl, then withdraws with a parting word: Leithanien has its own rules.
When the girl asks what happened to the grown-ups who were taken, Carnelian tells her the truth instead of a comforting lie. Most likely, nothing good.
The girl cries, then soon wipes away her tears. She's the oldest, she says, so she'll find the scattered kids and protect them. She doesn't have much left to lose anyway.
Carnelian leaves the girl in the care of the 'specialist' who'd been hiding nearby, a Rhodes Island operator. When he reminds her that she's one of them too, she just laughs it off.

When the girl asks if they'll meet again, Carnelian answers that as long as she holds on to what she believes now, they will someday. A Sargonian who won't whittle herself down to fit a foreign land. Better to be the odd one out. All she has to be is herself.
8. A Letter for the Holy Mountain (Courier Wanted)

Back on Rhodes Island, 6:50 a.m. **Cliffheart** is seeing off **Courier** and **Matterhorn** as they head home, and she gives Matterhorn the slip to pull Courier aside alone. She has one favor to ask: deliver a letter to her older sister **Enya** on Kjerag's holy mountain.

blocks.cap: Having given Matterhorn the slip, just the two of them. Cliffheart's request begins.

blocks.x: But Courier shakes his head. Things in Kjerag have gotten complicated, and contact with the Saintess is strictly forbidden. Cliffheart sulks that her brother **SilverAsh** never told her any of this, then gives up surprisingly easily, telling him to bring back loads of cystymilk curds and pulled meat.

Of course, she hadn't given up at all. Some time later, she takes the mission closest to Kjerag, sends her teammates back first once it's done, and sets off alone. When a fellow operator mentions seeing her head out loaded with snow-mountain climbing gear, Courier rushes after her.
And on a road with Kjerag's snow-white mountains visible in the distance, Courier finally catches up with Cliffheart. Only then does she open up.

The day Enya left home, Cliffheart was hiding nearby. She knew her sister didn't want to go and believed their brother would protect her, but he didn't stop those people from taking her away. Her sister didn't cry.
If only she had cried.

The Saintess's face, seen from afar, was frozen like ice, and that's when Cliffheart knew: this wasn't the life her sister wanted. She's afraid that if their family never tries to understand one another, the day may come when they become enemies, and she can't just sit still.

When she says that if her sister isn't doing well, she'll climb the holy mountain and kidnap her back if she has to, Courier finally bursts out laughing. Faced with a young lady who won't give up even if her brother objects or locks her up, he throws up his hands and takes the letter.
The conditions: he'll take it only as far as the monastery near the holy mountain, and he can't promise her sister will receive it. And she's not to even think about climbing the mountain herself.
Then Courier murmurs under his breath that this might not be such a bad thing after all.
Epilogue. The Unused Climbing Gear

Some time later, in the Rhodes Island cafeteria. Cliffheart challenged Closure, who hadn't eaten in three days while fixing equipment wrecked in the clashes with Reunion, to an eating contest, and lost spectacularly. As for the snow-mountain gear Closure ordered for her half a year ago, Cliffheart says she just hasn't needed it yet.

blocks.cap: The Rhodes Island cafeteria. Never challenge an engineer who hasn't eaten in three days to an eating contest.

blocks.x: Just then, Courier comes by, back from a mission. When she asks if it's another letter from 'her,' he says yes, but he doesn't look well. Cliffheart presses him, demanding to know if something has happened to her sister or brother, and after a long hesitation, Courier speaks.
There is something Master SilverAsh asked that you deliver in his stead, my lady.

A canyon in the wastes, a tent on the border, a TV in the rest area, a darkened lighthouse, an alley in Leithanien, a letter sent to Kjerag. Some chose to stay where they were and some set off again, but all of them are still searching for a place of their own. And a few of those small lights are already gathering at Rhodes Island.

blocks.x: Dawn in Lungmen, the wastes of Siracusa, a country village in Victoria, a Catastrophe warning zone in Rim Billiton, a forest in Columbia, and the fringes of Iberia. In places with nothing to do with one another, people who've never met are each gazing out past their own 'here.'

Some stayed behind, thinking of a comrade who left. Some, having been kicked out anyway, declare a fresh start. And some are stepping out of the house for the very first time in their lives. So what lies beyond 'here,' anyway?
1. Two Portions of Chow Fun, Out of Habit

First up, Lungmen. At 5:57 a.m., **Hoshiguma**, an inspector of the Lungmen Guard Department, knocks on her neighbor's door and asks for help picking out shoes. The Guard Department's 'Missy,' **Swire** — who has only just come home from an all-nighter and is off duty today, mind you — is livid, threatening to hit the alarm and write her up for disturbing the peace.

There's a mountain of work, and of course 'that stinking dragon' isn't around when it matters. When Hoshiguma tells her she's the one who'll lead the Guard Department from here on, Swire chokes up for a moment, then yells that if that dragon never comes back, she'll just take over the whole department herself.

blocks.cap: Early dawn in Lungmen. The off-duty inspector's holiday begins with picking out shoes.

blocks.x: The breakfast Hoshiguma brought is chow fun, and when asked why she bought two, the inspector mumbles that it was "just habit." Three-mushroom shredded fowl, saa sin sauce, extra noodles. Every bit of it is 'that one's' usual order.

Hoshiguma even turns down Swire's first-ever 'date' — a shopping trip together — then hands out chow fun to the Guard Department officers too, and takes her trusty bike out to the outskirts for the first time in ages.
Out on the road, she wonders aloud why Ch'en has to be so stubborn — and **Shirayuki**, who serves Madam Fumizuki, abruptly appears to correct her. "Miss Ch'en is no fossilized bonehead."

Hoshiguma admits she doesn't mind Ch'en taking a few knocks; what worries her is that Ch'en might never get back up. And when Shirayuki says Inspector Hoshiguma is a gallant hero too, she shakes her head and answers like this.
Stories get to end at the best possible times. Life doesn't.

What Shirayuki silently hands her is a manga, a new artist's debut — and the hero on the cover is a strangely familiar tall figure holding a shield. Hoshiguma laughs, "They've got guts. Still, they kept it tasteful," and decides that the next time she sees Ch'en, she'll try calling her 'Operator Ch'en.'

Then, the racetrack on the outskirts. Just as her youthful blood starts to boil again, the latest-model bike she's only ever seen in ads closes in from behind and overtakes her on a curve. The 'ghost rider' said to haunt the winding roads at night turns out to be Madam **Fumizuki**.

blocks.cap: The racetrack on the outskirts. A one-horned Oni and her trusty bike cut through the wind for the first time in ages.

blocks.x: What the inspector couldn't quite bring herself to say was about the bike parked outside the Governor's building these past few days. That luxury bike, which didn't suit Wei Yenwu's taste one bit — so it really wasn't his after all.
2. 'Bury Me in the Wilds'... and Then He Snores

Around then, out in the Siracusan wastes, a stolen car has broken down. Fixing it are the white-haired **Aosta** and the taciturn **Broca**; squatting beside them watching a parade of bugs is **Chiave**, who was coughing up blood just thirty minutes ago.

The three stood up to their boss Layton, who was planning to sell them off for cash, kicked up a ruckus, and fled Vite City last night. So, smack in the middle of the wastes, Chiave makes a proclamation: from now on, you're members of the **Chiave Famiglia**! Aosta is the consigliere, and Broca is the underboss!

On the way they come across merchants being robbed by a gang of bandits, and Chiave has a 'great idea': beat up the bandits and get the merchants to share a few supplies. But Aosta gets the merchants out of there first, so they don't get a single crumb — and only the bandits keep chasing them, all the way.

They shake off the bandits just before the fuel runs dry, and once the walls of Locomotiva City come into view, the three start pushing the car. Old stories come out while they push. Aosta was sent to 'take care of' Chiave, but the two hit it off mid-fight and became friends — and it was these two who rescued Broca when his own family was about to sell him off.
Meanwhile, Chiave's coughing keeps getting worse. Chiave and Broca both have Oripathy, and when Chiave warns that Aosta will catch it someday too, Aosta answers calmly.
It'll be better than just watching you two suffer.

Laid out in the back seat, Chiave says that once he's head of the Thirteen Families, he'll solve this disease and build a big hospital — then suddenly mutters that dying out here in the wastes wouldn't be so bad either. Dig a hole, lie down in it, close your eyes, and "Pow... one person's dead."
The car stereo, playing "Bury me out in the boundless wilds," cuts off with a click, and Aosta screams Chiave's name. Chiave... was snoring.

blocks.cap: The endless Siracusan wastes. Day one of a brand-new Famiglia with no fuel, no food, and nowhere to go.

blocks.x: Right then, a passing Rhodes Island operator pulls over. "Hey, you look like you've got car problems. Need some help?"

Some time later, in the Rhodes Island cafeteria. Over a sashimi platter served up by **Jaye**, the three tell the rest of the story. Thanks to an operator named Straightedge, Chiave got treatment, and Aosta handed over the car to pay for the medicine. When another family came after them, Straightedge bailed them out again — and in the end, the three joined Rhodes Island for good.
3. A Fairy Who Can't Grant a Single Wish

Meanwhile, in Victoria. **Iris**, raised in 'the Castle,' has stepped outside it for the first time. She has come to return a precious thing a child left in the Castle's keeping over ten years ago, right on the promised date.
I'll prove it... that fairytales are everlasting.

But where Tonnerre Village once stood, there is only the hum of factory equipment for a plant some noble is building. There is no sign of Mabel, the child she's looking for, and the villagers all left long ago. Nearly twenty years have passed, so it's no surprise. Iris begins searching the nearby villages, one by one.

blocks.cap: The site of the old village Iris came looking for. Everyone who lived here is long gone.

blocks.x: In fairytales nothing is impossible, but in reality, it all comes down to how persistent you are. In one village she reaches, Iris runs into a suspicious, masked Rhodes Island field operator. After a wordless stare-down, the operator ends up helping with her search.

Just then, a couple's argument drifts out of a house. Their daughter **Dora** has caught Oripathy, and in Victoria, hiding an Infected person is a grave crime. The mother cries out that she can't hand her daughter over to the isolation zone.
A little later, Iris slips past the closed window into Dora's room. Dora had been playing alone with her doll, scratching at her aching arm.

blocks.cap: The room of a child who can't go outside. Her only playmate is a doll.

blocks.x: Dora says she wants to visit the castle where fairies hold tea parties, the one only good children can go to. When Iris suggests leaving her doll with the fairies so it comes back as a doll that can move, Dora shakes her head.
You protect your own treasure yourself, right?

The doll was a birthday present from her mommy and daddy, and she promised to look after it for a long, long time. And since she's her mommy and daddy's treasure, as long as she's good and stays home, they'll protect her.

When Dora asks whether she can make a wish to the fairy, Iris says of course — but she can't grant any of them. Not curing her illness, not making her mommy stop crying, not letting her grow up faster. "None of it... I can't grant any of it..."
Yet Dora isn't disappointed. If she meets the fairy, she says, she'll keep those wishes a secret. Think how sad the fairy would be to learn she couldn't grant them.
All Iris can manage is "Thank you..."

When she leaves the room, the operator who had been waiting says they've told the couple about a place where the Infected can get proper treatment, but whether to leave is for the couple to decide. As Iris blames herself because neither fairytales nor dreams can save that child, the operator speaks.
But they give people hope.

You have to know what's good first before you can move toward it. Then the operator reveals that they know someone who matches Mabel's description in every detail. It may already be too late, though — Iris should go and meet her herself.
4. A Nun Who Came to Save Her Monastery, and Fell for the Wide World

Back in Lungmen. **Hildegard**, a nun of Laterano's Landen Monastery, declines when **Bison** of MountainDash Logistics says the company will cover her stay. As a member of the monastery, she says, she can't lean on other people's money.

After a few years that were far too peaceful, the Notarial Hall has snatched up all their work, not a single new recruit has joined, and the old men have even cut off their budget. At this rate, the venerable monastery is going to go 'bankrupt.'

Out exploring the neighborhood, she runs into **Snowsant**, an engineer staying in the room across the hall. Hildegard offers her one of the two cakes she bought because they were supposedly famous, Snowsant wolfs it down like an animal that hasn't eaten in three days, and the two end up strolling around Lungmen together.

The next night, sitting across from **Eurill** — the company's president and Bison's father — at a bar, she finds the contract already all set. But Eurill's vision is far bigger. Starting with a route to Laterano, he wants to send Messengers out ahead and reach across this whole divided land.
But that's no reason such a bridge shouldn't exist, is it?

That night, with her work suddenly gone, Penguin Logistics' **Texas**, **Croissant**, and **Sora** are drifting down a downtown road outside her window, chasing a thief. Hearing that Sora used to be a famous idol, the two put her concert footage on the hotel TV, and even after Snowsant dozes off, Hildegard lies awake picturing the outside world she has never seen.

blocks.cap: A stage inside a little box. The monastery had a TV too, but she's never seen anything like this.

blocks.x: Too wired to sleep, Hildegard heads out into the night streets, where **Emperor**, a penguin who talks in rap, appears before her. He sends some respect to Paul Landen, the monastery's founder, then takes a phone call about counterfeits, yells "Blow up their boat, right now!" and vanishes.

The bar she visits again before leaving Lungmen is called 'The Ends of the Earth.' She was supposed to leave the next morning, but Hildegard says this land is far more interesting than she imagined, so she'd like to look around a little longer.

blocks.cap: The bar 'The Ends of the Earth.' Where a nun and a logistics company president raised a toast.

blocks.x: When Eurill asks whether this business will ever be recognized, Hildegard answers with a monastery fable, 'La Bestia Superba': the tale of an upstart who couldn't be bothered to climb the stairs, glimpsed only a shadow through the window, and slandered the mural. Breaking that kind of arrogance, she says, is exactly what Eurill is trying to do.
Before they part, Eurill hands her a note Emperor asked him to pass along. Written next to a contact address is a company name: Rhodes Island.
5. Catastrophe Messengers Are Bad Omens by Trade

Around then, in a Catastrophe warning zone on the Rim Billiton frontier, a buggy driven by Catastrophe Messenger **Leonhardt** is tearing across the wastes. Riding along are his partner, the swordsman **Ayerscarpe**, and **Greyy**, a young Caster who insisted on tagging along for his first rescue mission. They're on their way to help a nomadic city stranded by a power failure.

When Greyy says Catastrophe Messengers are good people who warn everyone of danger, Ayerscarpe answers. When a Catastrophe does hit, people are so glad to survive that they forget who warned them — and if it still hasn't come after a few months, they start scorning the ill-omened Messenger who ruined their everyday lives.

blocks.cap: The sky over the warning zone. The ones who read clouds like these first sometimes end up the ones resented.

blocks.x: Greyy has things he wants to do. He wants to see with his own eyes what Rhodes Island works so hard for, repay the ship that took him in, and save up money to find his mom and dad. But if that civil war keeps going... he trails off.
Leonhardt, hopeless at this sort of thing, quietly passes the buck, and Ayerscarpe speaks up.
What matters isn't what you did, or how great your results were. It's what you were striving for.

Someone out there is fighting to give you a better life right now, so don't make letting them down the price of your goals — hearing that, Greyy starts to feel bad about the big brothers and sisters in Medical. After that, the car gets rowdy again: Greyy's embarrassing history of collapsing from overwork, a joke about the recording device built by 'the ever-so-brilliant Miss **Closure**,' and Leonhardt's weird dream about an Iberian sea breeze that left his throat hoarse.

Three thousand meters from the target, Leonhardt brings out the good news and the bad news. They have at least half a month before the Catastrophe, but the distress signal could be a trap set by rioters, and the life signs he's picking up are too few, and too tightly bunched together, to be a city.
As Greyy freezes up, Leonhardt tells him: bad guys are everywhere, and they're no better than the ones he saw when he was driven from his hometown.
But as long as you still want to, there's always something you can try to do for somebody else.
Greyy answers, "Yes!"
6. The Sword and the Scales

Meanwhile, in a Columbian forest, **Ch'en** blocks the path of a fleeing Infected man. He has been framed for the murder of a foreign mercenary — because he exchanged a few words with the man on the street, and because traces of Arts at the scene meant it must have been one of the Infected. On the way to the police station he injured two officers, then slipped out of the city overnight.

Ch'en believes he didn't kill anyone. But attacking the police and running away is his crime, she says, and she won't step aside. He should defend himself in a Columbian court, where there are juries and the public can watch.

blocks.cap: A Columbian forest. Ch'en stands in front of a wrongly accused fugitive and will not move aside.

blocks.x: Before Ch'en came to this country, **Amiya** had told her that in many places, cruelty is hidden beneath a pretty tablecloth — and that she was worried Ch'en would be disappointed.

The man scoffs that the fine gentlemen of the jury pay people to badmouth the Infected, then brings up old **Tom**, who once tried to swipe Ch'en's bracelet and was taught a lesson for it. The old man would con and steal without a second thought, but all of it was to buy dresses and jewelry for his granddaughter.

Ch'en once asked herself who has the right to judge another person's crimes, and with Amiya not there, **Rosmontis** answered. Amiya and Dr. **Kal'tsit** would say no one can judge anyone, she said, but the 'big, kind people' she fought alongside told her that if you know someone has done wrong, you can hold them guilty. So she will do what Ch'en can't bring herself to do, Rosmontis offers. If someone hurts another person, can't you just cut off the hand they did it with?
I'll grow up as hard as I can, and get that measuring stick for myself. I'll tell good from evil, and I'll be the one who judges.

Back in the forest. The man tells her Tom is already dead. He crossed someone he shouldn't have, was dragged off and beaten, and nobody stepped in. His granddaughter never once agreed to see him, right to the end.
Nobody's going to make trouble for some big shot just because one sick pauper died!
As the sounds of the pursuers draw near, Ch'en, still blocking the path, makes him a promise. If he is given an unjust punishment, she will not stand by and watch. She will not let him die.
No one should have to bear a punishment heavier than they deserve. If anyone takes that for granted, they're the ones who are wrong.

Ch'en once thought Rhodes Island's ideals were naive; now she knows she is no different. She has never regretted turning down the path **Wei Yenwu** laid out for her and leaving Lungmen. This isn't an ideal, she says, but something she has to do — and she's glad to be walking that road with Rhodes Island.

Some time later, at the Rhodes Island office in that city, a clerk whispers a rumor to Ch'en. The man arrested for the murder was released in under two days. And the real killer didn't turn himself in — someone left him tied up with the evidence at the entrance of the police station.
When the clerk says this figure the tabloids are calling a 'champion of justice' sounds pretty cool, Ch'en shakes her head.
If anything, I'd rather that mystery figure never get the chance to appear again.

That day, Ch'en's squad gained one temporary member with a covered face. He brought no luggage at all, saying there was nothing here worth remembering. Countless setbacks and disappointments lie ahead, but Ch'en knows she will not stop.
7. An Iberian Ghost-Story Session, and a Missionary Comes to the Village

Elsewhere, in some forest: **Myrrh**, a Medic out gathering herbs, the social butterfly **Utage**, and **Beanstalk**, who commands her animal friends. Utage's contacts include an 'Afternoon Nails Club' and even a 'Peeps That Don't Do Events But Pay Up' list, and Myrrh quietly trembles, thinking she'd cry if she ended up in one of those. Luckily, Myrrh is on the 'Medical Department' list, and Beanstalk on 'Gonna Treat Lunch Some Time.'

When they learn that the land beyond the northern greenery Beanstalk's animal friends found is Iberia, an impromptu ghost-story session breaks out on the spot. Cities that merge into a monster that swallows everything; a ghost town where anyone who wanders in slowly stiffens into a solid-gold statue; corpses that climb out of their graves and fill the streets on festival day.
Beanstalk freezes and Utage is having a blast, but Myrrh suddenly wonders: what kind of place is Iberia really, to have such terrifying rumors swirling around it?
Meanwhile, in a country village in that very Iberia, a scrawny boy named **José** trips and falls while running from **Antonio**. José had told the teacher he saw Antonio stealing a wallet.

blocks.cap: A country village in Iberia. Today, an important person from the city is coming to give a speech.

blocks.x: The one who helps the mud-covered José to his feet is a missionary who has come from the city to give a speech. Realizing the missionary heard everything, José clings to him in tears, begging him not to take Antonio away — he only lied out of jealousy. The older boy next door, taken away for stealing, never came back.

Then Antonio shouts that he's the one who stole it. He did it to pay the tuition for José, who's the best student around but will soon have to quit school for lack of money. He'll take the punishment, he says, but he doesn't regret it.

The missionary doesn't scold them. He lets the two realize for themselves that they had no choice because they were weak, then tells them that the law punishes, but it's the heart that leads people toward good — and that caring for one another is what makes us strong.
Just as the kids tilt their heads, saying it's too hard to understand, a village woman runs up and calls out to the missionary: "Reverend Bishop!"
The Bishop of Iberia leads the two children to the plaza, telling them to admit their mistakes alongside everyone there, and to become stronger and better still.
The power that makes Iberia — that makes us — better comes from the heart. Do not forget this, everyone. Believe in yourselves.

Two portions of chow fun, a car stereo in the wastes, a doll that doesn't move, a bar called 'The Ends of the Earth,' clouds over a warning zone, a Columbian forest, and a map spread out toward Iberia. Those who stayed behind and those stepping out the door for the first time are all looking past their own 'here.' What lies out there, though, nobody knows just yet.
