blocks.x: Rhodes Island is home to people who have each left somewhere behind. Hometowns they can no longer go back to, hometowns they've decided not to go back to, and hometowns so hazy they can't even say where they were.

In an old mining village on the Kazdel frontier, in the ship's repair workshop, rest area and canteen, in the fog-bound forests of Leithanien — like a breeze blowing backwards, everyone's past rewinds for a brief moment.
The first scene: a girl stepping into an unfamiliar village, looking for a street from her memories.
1. Looking for the Village in Her Memories — Straight Through the Mine

**Bellony Village**, on the outskirts of Kazdel, is a small nomadic town that's basically one giant mining truck. A cave-in a few months back sealed off both the mine and the trade routes, and not a single city offered to help.

**Surtr**, who has "personal reasons," tags along with **Meteorite**, the Sarkaz operator handling the preliminary survey. After seeing some kids squabble over a single ice cream, Surtr grumbles that she's not angry, not at all — and Meteorite thinks to herself: (She's totally angry...)

blocks.cap: Bellony Village. The fences have fallen apart, and no one bothers to fix them.

blocks.x: Thanks to a memory disorder of unknown cause, Surtr has so many memories overlapping in her head that she can't tell which ones are real. So she's been visiting the places in her memories one at a time — and this time, something about this region in Kal'tsit's files felt familiar.
Once she's actually there, though, it's similar but somehow different, and Surtr insists she can handle it alone. Meteorite, who has fought long and hard for a Sarkaz home, offers her a few words.
Maybe we're all just looking for a place to belong in the end.

Then, in front of the collapsed tunnel that once led to the neighboring village, Surtr stops. "I think I remember this path." Told they should wait until the passage is cleared, she says only "I'm not willing to wait that long" — and smashes right through the caved-in entrance.

The tunnel has turned into an Originium Slug nest, and beneath it Surtr finds a huge underground cavern. The outlines of buildings buried in the rock: the ruins of a city that might be hundreds of years old. And down there, Surtr seems to have found something.

blocks.cap: Beneath the mine, a deeper cavern. Among the glow of Originium Slugs, the outlines of buried buildings emerge.

blocks.x: When Surtr finally bursts back out through the rock a good while later, her report is short and sweet: the Originium Slug nest behind the cave-in has been dealt with, the hole has been collapsed shut, and sure, the standard survey got skipped, but the problem's solved. The village headman's entire response? "What?!"

But Surtr shakes her head. The streets in her memories smelled of earth, not dried grass, and the friends in her memories never chased each other around with ice cream. "Not the neighboring village, and not here either."

When Meteorite says that not finding it today doesn't mean she has nowhere to go home to, Surtr leaves her tongue-tied with a "So you're saying I can rely on you?" Then she turns down the village's hospitality and asks for just one thing. "Could I at least have an ice cream?"
2. The Signatures Are Forged, the Chat Is Genuine

Meanwhile, back on the ship, freshly arrived Sankta **Arene** grumbles as the Doctor explains "weapon reliability certification." He's using his own weapon, and he still needs a workshop inspection plus signatures from two craftsmen? What a pain.

At Repair Workshop No. 3, all five craftsmen are off at a repair contest, leaving only the apprentice **Adnachiel** behind. Arene's pitch — you need two signatures, and hey, there are two of us right here — gets politely turned down, but Adnachiel does agree to inspect the weapon.

blocks.cap: Repair Workshop No. 3 in the morning. The only one left is an apprentice.

blocks.x: Adnachiel figures out that Arene is Infected — something Arene never mentioned — just from his expressions and body language. Meanwhile, Arene quietly uses his Arts to copy two signatures off the craftsmen's handmade badges hanging on the wall.

One of them, written in Lateran, belongs to Gunject, who hates guns so much that he left his in Laterano and never went back. Arene mutters that he'd probably get along with the guy, then asks whether Laterano is really a place worth missing.

Adnachiel's halo has been tilted since birth. Maybe because of that, he failed his firearm qualification and left Laterano with his family, and only caught Oripathy afterwards. But when asked what he has in common with other Sankta, his answer is "Like how I can't wear a hat?" — and Arene finally bursts out laughing.
As Adnachiel's eyes light up talking about John, his old master from the dessert shop, Arene — who was left home alone every year with a giant cake — feels his stomach turn at the very smell.
When even that expression gets read, Arene says: "You're a Laterano Sankta through and through. Even if you can't carry a gun and your halo's tilted."
It's just the city of Laterano I can't go back to, not my home. Your hometown is something you can always reach out for, no matter when.

Just then **Ambriel**, dropping off her gun for maintenance, chimes in. Some people's homesickness only eases once they've smelled the place and touched its earthen walls, she says — but then she laughs it off: there's no rule that Sankta have to spend their whole lives in Laterano.

Ambriel is sick of the Notarial Hall types nagging her about her obligations. When Arene retorts that you just put people like that to work for you, her verdict is: "Whoa, you sound like such a baddie. Nice!"

Arene heads straight back to the Doctor, freely admits to copying the signatures, and asks for another certification form so he can get the real ones once the craftsmen are back. Asked why he's suddenly so conscientious, he answers: "I found some interesting people."
3. A "Boring" Hometown, Brought Up During Festival Prep

Around then, in the operator rest area, **Purestream**, an Ægir from Yan, is getting ready for her hometown's once-a-year festival. **Elysium** takes charge of contacting the operators out in the field, while his old friend from home, **Thorns**, warns that if courting disaster were a talent, this guy would be a prodigy — so don't invite him.

While the two of them bicker over whose fault the deck incident was, **Absinthe** shyly shows up. She asks Thorns to look over the old Ursus-style casting tool her father used, and he says "Very well" the moment he hears it — then tells Elysium "I've already tested it on your weapon," before adding that he's kidding.

blocks.cap: The operator rest area in Cabin No. 2. The festival planning meeting keeps getting sidetracked.

blocks.x: Thinking back to when he first arrived two years ago, Elysium smiles: staying was the right call, and having a place to come back to after the job is done is more than enough for him.

But when Purestream asks whether they miss their hometown of Iberia, Thorns says "Nope," and Elysium just brushes it off as a boring place. Thorns adds that Iberia was never friendly to the Ægir, and that many of them lived near the blockade line dodging the Inquisition until they were hauled away.

Purestream, an Ægir who grew up in Yan where everyone was treated as equals, is lost for words. Still, she says Rhodes Island welcomed her from day one, and Absinthe brings up how Elysium helped her on her last mission and thanks him.

Elysium launches into bragging about the taciturn captain who saved his life, lets slip that one hit from her Arts can make you forget who you are for a while — then hastily covers it up as classified.

As the festival talk wraps up, Thorns asks: a gray city, stifling, pointless — is that really all you remember of the place? Elysium, who says he couldn't spoil the holiday mood in front of a kid who's still a student, adds as if talking to himself:
I don't really want to go back, you know. But I have this feeling that maybe someday... I'll end up going back there.
4. To Bob — A Letter Written in the Foggy Forest

Meanwhile, in Leithanien, **Mudrock** writes a letter to her friend Bob, who has left for Columbia. She passes on news of Chainsmoke, who still wants to beat Bob at arm wrestling, and of Chef, who hasn't forgotten the three coins Bob owes him, and congratulates Bob on getting away from all of it.
But in the forest beyond the letter, Chainsmoke was shouting. Run. Go to Kazdel. And never look back.

Unable to abandon the Infected of Leithanien, Mudrock's group had come to be called the "Mudrock Squad." For eight days in the dense, fog-bound forest, ice, storms and fireballs had rained down on them. They had lost twenty comrades, and still they did not even know who the enemy was.
Taking the rear guard herself, Mudrock asks Chef for one thing. Whatever happens behind them, lead the main group forward and do not look back.

blocks.cap: Fog that never lifts. The pursuers never once show themselves.

blocks.x: In the letter, Mudrock asks whether Columbia's wheat fields are as beautiful as they are in the movies, and whether Bob could someday send her a seedling of the hops she has never seen.

Meanwhile, the Originium crystals inside the Infected began to move on their own. The enemy was using the Infected as tools for casting Arts. One Sarkaz warrior, crystals breaking through his skin, cried out: "I won't let myself be their weapon. Tell the others I died fighting!"

He took his own life. Mudrock cried out that suicide was no end for a warrior, and her golem answered — rising as a colossal statue like a monument to the dead, it charged at the shadows beyond the fog.

In the end, just getting out of the forest cost them half their number. One of the Infected said a few nobles still researched those Arts that toy with Infected lives, and guessed that their pursuers were attendants of "the towers." Mudrock steadied her comrades: as long as they weren't "Knights," it was not yet the worst.
5. Home in Sight, Holding the Bridge
And at last, just over this mountain lies Kazdel. Across the great bridge and 100 km north is a village where outsiders have settled — the place Mudrock once lived.

With her homeland, which she had only ever wanted as a place to rest for a while, right in front of her, Mudrock, who had been using her Arts without pause, was so exhausted she nodded off. When a comrade admits to being afraid, she shares what she has realized: they are experimenting, and to them, Mudrock's people are nothing but material that never runs out, no matter how much is used.
I only want to live on... I only want everyone to live on...

When cooking smoke, wagons and a market at last came into view down in the basin, Mudrock found the bones of a young Sarkaz beside a rusted knife, and buried the child with her own hands rather than her Arts.

blocks.cap: A hill with the home village in sight. And the fog begins to roll in again.

blocks.x: By then, the fog was thickening again. Mudrock told the Infected to go to the village and find new lives, and the Sarkaz warriors stayed at the bridge to see it through. We will not look back, so anyone who wants to leave should go now. We hold this bridge, even to the death.
Mudrock cannot bring herself to look back. A comrade tells her you can tell just by the sound: hardly anyone left. Mudrock thanks them, again and again.

At that same moment, a Rhodes Island team was watching them from within the fog. Its captain, remarking that Leithanien still harbors fools who dig into the Witch King's remnants, declared that Rhodes Island does not permit the desecration of Infected lives, and set out to save the Reunion squad.

With a single touch of the hand, that young Sarkaz subdued Mudrock's colossus, and where the fog cleared, introduced himself: merely an operator of Rhodes Island, and a fellow Sarkaz. His name was **Logos**.

Afterwards, Mudrock asks her new employer to send a second letter. The people she wrote about last time died with honor protecting innocent Infected, and the group turned back with Kazdel right before their eyes.

Having realized she cannot run from fate, she will face it now; saving more of those who need not die is the only way to shoulder her own mistakes. So the letter says, before closing with the hope of meeting Bob in Columbia some far-off day.
6. April's Song (Nostalgia Filter Included)

Meanwhile, **April**, a newcomer just back from a mission, runs into **Ansel** from the Medical Department as he hands a letter to a Messenger in the corridor. Told his uncle is going to ask yet again when he's coming home, Ansel laughs that there are still patients who need him — but once the Messenger leaves, he murmurs, "Sorry, Uncle..."

It turns out they're both from Rim Billiton. April lost her parents in a mine accident, was raised by the company and became one of its hunters. She matter-of-factly explains that she finally quit — withheld pay was par for the course, and catching Oripathy meant the work simply dried up.

blocks.cap: "Wow, guess that's a doctor for you. You sure eat healthy..."

blocks.x: Over lunch, Ansel opens up too. Raised by his uncle, he clashed with him time and again over taking over the company before finally becoming a doctor, and he's hanging in there until the day he can proudly say he's saved a lot of people. Even so, he misses the giant smokestacks, the din of machinery and the shouts of the miners.

April, whose codename comes from a song about spring, digs up memories of a hometown so smoggy it was hard to breathe. Water cutting out mid-shower, the old man upstairs who sent her food, the old lady downstairs who spat at her, supermarket meatballs she's never seen anywhere else — and then she reaches a conclusion. "Oh, I get it, this is that nostalgia filter thing!"
Strictly speaking, I don't think what matters is the hometown itself, but the marks the time we spent there left on us.

April didn't run away, she says — she just had no choice but to leave — so she can't hate Rim Billiton. Then she shares her most unforgettable memory: lying on the roof of her apartment building, hemmed in by taller ones, gazing at a narrow, fenced-in patch of sky and dozing off to "April" in her headphones until her worries drifted away like smoke.

Grumbling that it's all Ansel's fault she now wants to go back, April suddenly seems to think of something, tracks down the Messenger and leaves him a request: when you're in Rim Billiton, go up to the roof of a tall building and take a picture of the view.

"My hometown, my past... turns out I cared more than I thought." Still, finding a nice place to nap is more realistic than going home, so April sets off first in search of Kroos, the undisputed queen of slacking off.
7. When the Curtain Rises, the Phantom Sings
Then one night, the curtain rises on a stage in a dream. "Welcome, all, to the Crimson Troupe!" Under the lights, **Phantom** sings softly, and a voice from the dark presses him for an answer.

blocks.cap: "Who is it? Who calls to me in this dead of night?"

blocks.x: I am the wraith in the dead of night, the apparition behind the curtain, the star upon the stage — just as he is about to answer, three performers who are not in the play appear.

blocks.cap: "I know who you are." From among the empty seats, the past speaks to him.

blocks.x: The performers say: the Devil chose you and taught you music; you followed the Devil, then betrayed and killed it and left; and now you have forgotten even us, who sang beside you. The Phantom in the dream answers that he killed them all — their ways were wrong, and so he had to.
The "brother" who had been as good as family goes on. On the night the candles melted, his blood dripped onto the stage like candle wax. And some are still stuck in that night.

Phantom tries to hold them back, but only coughs break from his throat, and a performer whispers that he should never have been on this stage. When the curtain falls, all that remains is a single line. "...Who am I?"
8. Calais-blason, the Hometown That Doesn't Exist

One rainy morning, an HR staffer brings the Doctor operator Phantom's file, riddled with gaps. Phantom deliberately avoids people and hides himself with his Arts, so no one can find him — and **Mint**, a newcomer who happens to be there, offers to help. The Doctor's solution: at times like this, you ask a lady for her opinion.

That lady — the cat Miss Christine — leads them to a room where Phantom has just woken from his dream. Telling himself over and over that he already killed the ghosts, he recognizes the Doctor by footsteps alone, and says their eyes were only deceiving them — that even memory deceives.

The problem was his birthplace. **Calais-blason**, in northwestern Victoria, as Phantom had written it, was a place where investigators could not find so much as a similar name, however hard they searched.
In that instant, a curtain falls before Phantom's eyes, and blood seeps out. Trampled flowers, a shattering glass, an audience applauding by the roadside. Who is it, laughing?

It isn't a lie, Phantom answers. The person who took him in told him so: a traveling troupe passing through took in children who had lost their village to Catastrophe and war, and he has never gone back since.

He didn't come to Rhodes Island for treatment, either. To be free of the ghosts of the past standing on street corners, at windows, at his side, he must find the true past — and so he is looking for someone who knows what happened.
I heard singing. I followed that voice all the way here. The trail I seek should be in this place.
Then the Doctor points to the clothes hanging on the wardrobe door and asks whether they're an old stage costume. Phantom turns, and his face freezes. "They should not be here—!"

blocks.cap: "There is no one in the seats. No one on the streets."

blocks.x: And in the corridor, as Mint racks her brain over where she's heard the name Calais-blason, a Rhodes Island operator approaches her. Saying they lived there long, long ago, the operator offers to tell her a long story somewhere quiet.
"It's a story about Calais-blason, its people, the families who lost the children they cherished, and a traveling troupe that passed through a small village..."
9. Old Tales on a Festival Night (No Happy Endings, Though)

Meanwhile, on a festival night with a spread of Yan food, **Shamare** and her doll **Morte** are sitting on the canteen sofa. Shamare says she saw people at the party laughing and then crying, and calmly remarks that those feelings, joy and sorrow all mixed together, aren't to Morte's taste.

**Suzuran**, who comes over to spread her tails out on the sofa, can't stop sighing "Haa~ So happy~" over the apple Morte hands her, then tells the Yan myth "Dusk Beauty Flying to the Moon" to **Popukar** and **Mousse**, who drop by next. Dusk Beauty climbed Mount T'ien in search of her missing husband and, with the mountain gods' help, flew up toward the moon — and the day people laid out food every year in her honor became today's festival.

Higashi has a similar tale. Because of a heavenly woman who promised to marry whoever brought her a treasure, the two elder of three hunter brothers found their treasures, only to end up leading armies under rival lords and clashing in the village. The old couple and the brothers all died, and the youngest became a vengeful spirit searching for a way to take revenge on the fairy.

"They're brothers, so why are they fighting each other?!" A fuming Popukar hopes the next story is one where nobody dies, but Mousse's Victorian myth is even worse. Of the twins who set out to find the Divine Originium to save their father, the brother ran off with nothing but the treasure; the king, cured by the Originium, turned into a monster and was slain by knights; the princess was executed as the culprit; and the brother lived out his days in luxury in a foreign land.
Popukar's conclusion is crystal clear. "Myths are like biiig monsters. They always gobble up the good people!"

Shamare, mending Morte, adds a tale from Siracusa: the mother wolf of the seven hills, who rose into the sky to become the moon's shadow when her brood tried to steal her food. She ends it briefly — that city was swallowed up by a bigger family a hundred years ago.

Last up is Popukar's story, which she heard from Orchid. After a mix-up where the "wax figure" gets corrected to a "Forte inventor," the king who stole the inventor's wax bride is swallowed by melted wax, and the inventor, now king himself, sleeps forever without ever managing to make another bride as good. Still, the bride always wanted to go back to her husband someday — and Popukar says she loves warm stories like this.
After everyone leaves, Shamare finishes mending Morte and heads off to return the book to Suzuran. When Morte asks why the stories all end that way, Shamare answers.
Think about what this world looks like. Think about the things you've eaten, and where we used to live. Now you know why the endings turn out that way, don't you?

The village in her memories wasn't that one, Laterano isn't particularly missed, and the road to Kazdel turned back at the bridge. Even so, everyone goes on living, holding the places they left behind in their own way. Maybe we're all just looking for a place to belong.

act10d5.tagline: Students who made it out alive after being trapped in a Chernobog school spend a year on Rhodes Island, each living with a story she has not told even the others. And one person who recognizes that school's uniform.

chars.name: Gummy
chars.desc: A spirited cook in the Rhodes Island canteen who carries a frying pan and a shield wherever she goes.

chars.name: Zima
chars.desc: Leader of the Ursus Student Self-government Group. Loves a fight and rarely listens to the Doctor.

chars.name: Istina
chars.desc: The group's most cautious strategist, and a lover of detective novels.

chars.name: Leto
chars.desc: The group's cheerful fighter, something like its youngest member. Loves playing the guitar.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: The young girl who leads Rhodes Island.

terms.name: Ursus Student Self-government Group
terms.desc: A small group of Ursus students who survived Chernobog and came to Rhodes Island. Only five of them remain.

terms.name: Chernobog
terms.desc: An Ursus city that fell to Reunion's attack.

terms.name: Reunion
terms.desc: An armed organization of the Infected. It took Chernobog and locked students inside a school.

terms.name: Peterheim Middle School
terms.desc: The school where Reunion gathered students from several schools and kept them locked up.

terms.name: Catastrophe
terms.desc: A massive natural disaster that sweeps across the land, scattering Originium.

blocks.x: When Reunion occupied Chernobog, many students were trapped inside one school. A few who made it out were rescued by Rhodes Island and stayed on under the name 'Ursus Student Self-government Group.'
Zima, Istina, Gummy, Leto, Natalya. The five now work aboard the ship. On the surface, they all seem fine.
None of them has forgotten what happened at the school. They just never speak of it.
1. Gummy Has Habits

At 6:30 in the morning, **Gummy**, who cooks in the canteen, waits for Istina to come and wake her. Istina doesn't come, and all that is left in the room is a note from Istina and Zima saying they will be back in the evening.
At lunch, Defender instructor **Dur-nar** points out one of Gummy's habits. When Gummy swings something, she stops at two, a habit that could be fatal on a battlefield.

After training, Dur-nar orders her to keep swinging so they can fix it, and Gummy insists she can't. The third strike comes out at full force before she knows it, and Dur-nar's arm, braced behind a training shield, goes numb.
Dur-nar apologizes for pushing too fast. Gummy has done nothing wrong; she is only upset.
Back in her quarters, without even turning on the light, Gummy stands the small safe door she carries as a 'shield' in the corner and crawls into the gap between the wall and the shield.

blocks.cap: Her quarters, the light left off. Gummy crawls in between the wall and the shield.

blocks.x: Gummy has habits. Wherever she goes, she carries the safe door and the frying pan. She uses toothpaste to the very end, even if she has to suck it out.
Up high, she keeps away from the edge, even with a railing. When she is hungry, she can't hold back and bites whatever is closest. When she stays in the dark too long...
Then Zima opens the door and comes in, asking why the light is off.
That day marks one year since the group came to Rhodes Island, and Zima and Istina have just come back with things they bought for the occasion. When Leto arrives too, the four shout 'Ura!'
Gummy thinks to herself that next time, she wants Rosa there with them too.
That night, the mood lamp Gummy always sleeps with is broken. Istina offers to sleep with her, Zima joins too, and the three lie side by side in Gummy's narrow bed.
The Ursus girls of the Student Self-government Group. Zima and Istina. They are Gummy's habits.
2. I Was Not Late

**Istina** sits down in front of a recording machine borrowed from Closure. The purpose written on the request form is 'self-assessment for post-traumatic stress disorder,' a method the medical department recommended.

Her real name is **Anna Morozova**, the group's strategist and a lover of detective novels. It was her idea to form the group, and Zima who made it happen. There were more members at first, but now only five remain.
She introduces a doll at her side to the camera. This is my friend, **Vika**. Her closest friend before the group, she says, and a member of it.

Back when Chernobog was being occupied, Reunion dragged the students to Zima's school and held them there for more than ten days, and fighting broke out inside. In her memory, someone calls her name. "Anna, pull me up."

blocks.cap: Chernobog under Reunion occupation.

blocks.x: Then a knock cuts the recording short. It is the detective **May**, returning a book, and Natalya, who for once has come on her own.
When May touches the doll, Istina snatches it away. Natalya knows whose doll it is.
Natalya tries to comfort her: it couldn't be helped, it wasn't your fault, you were just a little late.
Istina answers that she is fine. She has always said so, and everyone believed it.
I was only late. No, I wasn't late. ... I had made my choice long before that.
At the end of a talk about detective novels, Istina asks: if a detective uncovers the truth but the law can do nothing about it, should the detective become the judge?

May answers that a detective can reveal the truth but cannot pass sentence. A wrong is a wrong whatever reason it is wrapped in, and what has already happened is never forgotten by those it happened to.
Istina says she is right. What has already happened will never change.
Just then a drone gets caught on the eaves outside the window, and May, climbing onto the windowsill to grab it, slips.
In that moment, Istina sees that day. Her friend calls to her, asking to be pulled up. She could not make a sound, could not speak, could not move.
At her light touch, her friend falls without a sound, leaving only a small mark on her fingertips. "Wait... Anna, what are you doing?!" She only watched her fall.
When she comes back to herself, May has only scraped her hand a little.
The drone carries a note from Silence of the medical department, looking for Natalya. Natalya leaves for a 'test,' saying she may soon have good news for the group.
Left alone, Istina tells Vika that she has never once forgotten her. Someday she will have to face it, but for now, she is still too weak.
3. I Am You
**Zima**'s real name is **Sonya**, 'General Zima,' the brawler every nearby school knew. And that same girl has the same dream, again and again.

The dream begins at an ordinary breakfast table. A father who lost his job. A mother who saved money for her daughter's schooling. But then the porridge in the bowl turns into rice water mixed with dead weeds, the bread into foul-smelling bread, the ham into a bloodstained lump of meat.

blocks.cap: The dream always begins at the breakfast table at home.

blocks.x: Beside the table stands someone with her exact face. **"I am you."** Somehow Sonya knows the bread had been left somewhere bad for days.
The dream moves to the school, where Valeria, the girl with the yellow ribbon whom Sonya saved from bullies, thanks her. Then, a moment later, Sonya picks up that ribbon, torn and stained with blood.
The other Sonya speaks. That girl is already dead, and deep down you know it too, don't you?

The dream goes back over the days at that school. After the first fire burned down one food storehouse, a band of noble students from #4 Secondary School seized the rest and began plundering. The commoner students took food from one another too.
Around then, Anna, wearing another school's uniform, comes to Sonya's classroom leading a group. She is the girl who used to live next door, and Sonya takes them in.
Soon some of that group attacked Sonya, because Anna had recommended Sonya as their new leader. Sonya 'dealt with' all of them, and Anna never knew why the attack happened.

On their third night together, Anna sobs. There was a bullied girl in her class, and she looked away; this time she tried to keep order and could do nothing. Without Sonya, her friends would have killed her.
When Sonya says that, as leader, she will help Anna with the good things she wants to do, Anna chooses the name. 'Ursus Student Self-government Group.' Sonya as leader, Anna as strategist.
The other Sonya speaks. Back then, you thought you were some hero out of a novel. You have neither the courage to ask who was in the wrong, nor the courage to hear the answer.
As their numbers grow, Vika argues for joining the nobles, and Anna gives Sonya's hatred of nobles as the reason not to. Sonya knows. The one who hates nobles is Anna.

Sonya decides to remove the root of the problem, and in the night she jumps alone from a second-floor window and heads for the last storehouse, guarded by the nobles. She does not listen to the other students screaming for help.
She was surrounded, nearly broke through, and then knocked over a candlestick. **The second fire.** The nobles' stronghold burned, and the last of the food with it.
The chaos grew worse than before. Several group members went missing, and Vika did not come back either.
And then one day, Reunion left the school. From the start, all they had done was keep the students locked up.

blocks.cap: "This can't be... can't be... a Catastrophe..."

blocks.x: The very next day, the Catastrophe struck, and outside the school was even worse than inside. Running from refugees and Reunion alike, they were finally rescued by a Rhodes Island operations team.
Even after the rescue, Anna did not blame Sonya. Without the fire, the students would not have ended up like this, she said, and next time, talk to me first. That was all.
And at the end of the dream, voices pour out. You are a sinner. You let me go out of guilt. I hate you.
Zima wakes up screaming. "This dream again. Anna, I..." Leaning on the sink, she looks out the window, where the moonlight is endlessly beautiful.
4. I Thought You Were a Good Person

Zima has been an operator for two months. **Natalya** of the Logistics Support department is a newcomer everyone praises. She talked the rescued refugees round so their escort went smoothly, and last week she passed her review and became a full member.
Zima comes to see her, but when asked what's wrong, says she came to the wrong place and turns to leave. Natalya stops her and takes her to her own room.
They are not friends. They only made it out of that place together. That is exactly why some things can be said.
Zima says only that she has nightmares, and Natalya realizes it is something she cannot tell Anna. Then Natalya tells her own story.
That day, it would have been better if you had killed me.

In Chernobog, she was the eldest daughter of Count Rostov and student council president of #4 Secondary School. Most nobles had already fled by the time Reunion began taking the city. Her family was too late.
On the first day, separated from their parents and sent to the school, the noble students nearly drew each other's blood. Natalya held them together, and some thirty stayed at her side.
Then Pavel proposed that, to uphold the dignity of the nobility, the commoners ought to be made to serve them, and **Natalya agreed to 'plunder the commoners.'** She did it to keep the nobles united.
Zima, who has been listening, knocks her down with her fist. Blood at the corner of her mouth, Natalya smiles.
It was all of you who taught me I wasn't noble, she says, and that was the most hopeless truth of all. So it would have been better if Zima had killed her that day, just as she killed her companions.

She takes out a paper knife and shows it. Over the months, she has thought of cutting her wrist with it twenty-six times and of stabbing her throat fifteen times, and each time she gave up, she ended up sneering at her own weakness, so she cannot forget it.

She cannot believe in her choice to stay and work for the people of Ursus, or in what she has been calling atonement, because she remembers herself smiling at the faces that came back from plundering, waiting to be praised.
In that place where everyone was killing each other, I didn't kill a single person. But the filthiest one there was probably me.
It was Zima, too, who saved her when other students caught her after the fire. Asked why, Zima says she forgot, and that she let her into the group because Anna agreed.
Zima says she doesn't know how to comfort anyone and only says what she thinks. Her parents died in Chernobog, so she won't go back there, or to Ursus. She will go on living as Zima.
Even without you, the nobles wouldn't have been any better, and you weren't the one who started all this. Then she starts to add something, and stops short. Unless it was me.
Zima has nightmares, throws up, barely sleeps. And she tells Natalya that without her, Anna could not have held out alone through the ten-odd days after that.
Still, I think surviving wasn't a bad thing. And saving you wasn't a bad thing either.
Natalya laughs until she cries. You haven't solved a single one of my problems, and I probably can't solve yours, but we survived. Then maybe we can move forward.
She chooses the codename she will use if she becomes an operator. A name that means 'dew' in Ursus: **Rosa**.
5. The Night She Doesn't Remember
**Leto**, who Istina says 'seems to have let go of it, somewhat,' is knocked down again and again by her roommate **Beehunter** in the training room, and keeps coming back.
Leto says quietly that she once had the nerve to take on Reunion, something Beehunter has never heard before.
That evening in their quarters, Leto drinks a honey drink, gets honey-drunk, and starts telling the story of that time.
Her real name is **Rosalind**. She was 'General Leto' at the same school as Sonya, always second to Sonya.

After the school was sealed, every gang tried to recruit her, but she shot back that she'd think about it if they brought Sonya to her themselves. In the end, the one she went to, carrying a few cans of food, was Sonya. There, at least, she could get some proper sleep.

blocks.cap: The snow-covered schoolyard of the sealed school.

blocks.x: In the classroom she opened, there was Sonya, and people lying on the floor. Sonya asked her to take everything lying there outside. She had to protect this place, and those kids.
Rosalind took the job, and said only one thing. "You've changed."
Not long after, Rosalind took down another gang and brought back food, hurting her head along the way, and **Lada**, a former Scout, treated the wound.
Rosalind muttered, "If that cop had met people like you too..." No one answered.

When food and people both ran short, Rosalind went to Reunion alone at night and did not back down, even when a soldier told her to go back if she wasn't Infected. She remembers being scared to death, and yet somehow enjoying it.

Then the one who called from above to send her up was a little kid in white, with a strange expression somewhere between a smile and not. The kid talked with her about this and that, then sent her back.
Whether it was 'the suffering is only beginning' or 'enjoy life,' she doesn't remember. When she woke up, the masked ones were all gone.
What came after was really hard, Leto says. She had thought the time at school was the worst, but once she got out, the school turned out to be only the beginning.
By the time the story ends, Beehunter is already asleep. Leto digs out her guitar, 'Stage,' and falls asleep asking it to hear the rest of the story.
The next morning, remembering nothing, she sees the guitar lying out and decides to play a song for the first time in a while.
6. A Wall Without Form
The document **Amiya** hands the Doctor is a department transfer request from Natalya Rostova. She wants to move from Logistics Support to combat duty.
Amiya was against Zima and the others becoming operators from the start, but accepted it in the end, and this time she asks the Doctor to go and meet Natalya.
On the way to Natalya, **Nearl**, who leads the new recruits' team, says Zima is badly lost over something, but believes her honesty will lead her down the right path.
Next comes **Perfumer**, who says she was worried by something Gummy once said in her sleep in the workshop, yet doesn't say what. Only that what Gummy needs is not comfort, but time.

And at the training ground, Natalya won't let go of a huge weapon she found in Chernobog, and when Leto tells her to use something else, she answers that the weapon means something to her. Leto calls her 'Operator Rosa.'

blocks.cap: The Rhodes Island training ground.

blocks.x: Watching them, instructor **Dobermann** says soldiers like her exist to protect the lives of kids like those. Sending those kids to the battlefield is a dereliction of duty, but she accepted long ago that she cannot help everyone.
All she can do, she says, is teach them how to fight and how to protect themselves. Then she asks the Doctor: what can you do for them?
When the Doctor returns, Amiya opens up. Even in the most ordinary moments, she senses an enormous feeling from them. Not sadness, pain, anger, or despair. If she had to name it, helplessness.
It's as if they're blocked by a wall that has no form.
A wall that is usually neither seen nor felt, yet every time they try to move forward, it stops them and sends them back to where they started.
Protecting them by force might keep them safe, but it cannot heal them. She doesn't believe time heals everything, but she doesn't know another way.
Amiya decides to accept Natalya's request, hoping that someday they will open their hearts, and that Rhodes Island will become their new home.
7. Before Spring Comes
Evil cannot defeat justice. The girl had always taken that for granted.

That winter, **Lovan**, a Chernobog police officer, calms his anxious wife Darya. The police are still in the city, and the army is on the outskirts. Didn't he swear to protect this home and this city?
He promises a spring outing. When the snow melts, they'll pack mead and pancakes and go out dancing. Once their daughter **Zoya** goes back to boarding school, just the two of them.
And then he leaves for the night shift.
That day, the city burst like fireworks before her eyes.

blocks.cap: Chernobog, that day.

blocks.x: And Zoya's school, too, was occupied by Reunion. Looking for a way out, she hides and overhears Reunion soldiers talking. Someone called Mephisto who locked students up in Peterheim Middle School. An order from 'the Captain' not to harm the students.
Zoya seized a chance and climbed over the wall, and Rolena, a Reunion Caster, saw it and did not stop her. Going outside the school was as good as suicide.
Rolena hated everyone in this city, so she wanted that student to see, clearly, everything the city was going through.
The city was collapsing and burning. People with weapons cheered and carved their mark into walls and floors. They called themselves Reunion.
Unable to hear, her fingers broken, Zoya made it close to home, and there she meets **Valery**, a police officer and her father's colleague.
The district where Zoya's home stood was the first to be attacked, and by the time rescuers arrived, an immense heat had already melted everything: grass, brick, rebar.
Valery does not lie. He will not deceive her by saying her mother got out safely; we were too late, he says.
Zoya does not cry. She tells herself she can't cry now, that she will become someone like her dad.
Her father, Valery says, volunteered to go investigate Peterheim Middle School, where the students were held, and hearing they are short-handed, Zoya says she will go.
In the end Valery can't stop her, and hands her a radio to contact the army, along with these words: you are not police, you are someone we are supposed to protect.
"I'll make sure..." Zoya never finished the sentence. In a situation like this, a promise is only comfort traded between the powerless, and they both knew it.
And when she arrived, Peterheim Middle School was too quiet. On the burned floor lay what had once been students.

blocks.cap: Peterheim Middle School. It was too quiet.

blocks.x: The cause of death was not the fire. Blades, blunt objects, and trampling. It did not look like Reunion's work.
On the charred black floor, in that place full of school uniforms, Zoya calls out. "Dad...?"
The promise of a spring outing once the weather warmed. Her father, trying on clothes other than his uniform ahead of a date with her mom.
Because spring always comes, even to this city.
Epilogue. Students of That School
And now, at Rhodes Island's logistics support desk, **Absinthe** finishes her paperwork and receives her new record card.

blocks.cap: Rhodes Island.

blocks.x: Five people pass in front of her. Gummy, showing off a magic trick the Doctor taught her. Rosa, laughing. Istina, telling them to keep their voices down. Leto and Zima, squaring off because neither wants to lose.
Absinthe knows that uniform. They are students of that school.
The five still haven't spoken to one another about those ten days. Gummy needs the light on to sleep, Istina says she is fine, and Zima wakes from the same dream.
Even so, the three lie down together in a narrow bed. Rosa chose a name that means 'dew,' and Leto tells the rest of the story to her guitar.
The formless wall is still there. In front of that wall, they have become each other's habits.
None of them has forgotten what happened at the school. That winter is not over yet. But now, it is not a winter endured alone.

act7d5.tagline: Finding a sitter for some Originium Slugs, rereading an old diary, scolding a thief who won't wash his hands — an afternoon spent hearing, one by one, the stories of people who boarded the same ship for very different reasons. As long as you're headed the same way, you can go together.

chars.name: Vanilla
chars.desc: An intern huntress dispatched from Blacksteel. She dotes on her pets.

chars.name: Steward
chars.desc: A member of Reserve Op Team A4. An operator who looks after others with great care.

chars.name: Melantha
chars.desc: A Guard on Reserve Op Team A4. She rarely lets her true feelings show.

chars.name: Blaze
chars.desc: An operator who says exactly what she thinks. She's sweet with kids.

chars.name: Dora
chars.desc: A young Infected girl from Victoria, receiving treatment at Rhodes Island.

chars.name: Ptilopsis
chars.desc: A Medic from Rhine Lab. She writes in her diary every day.

chars.name: Silence
chars.desc: The Rhine Lab researcher who brought Ptilopsis to Rhodes Island.

chars.name: Ansel
chars.desc: A Medic from Rim Billiton with a gentle personality.

chars.name: Ifrit
chars.desc: A child in Silence's care. She treats Ptilopsis like a big sister.

chars.name: Matterhorn
chars.desc: A shield operator from Kjerag who also mans the ship's kitchen as its cook.

chars.name: Gummy
chars.desc: A cheerful young operator who loves to cook.

chars.name: Ethan
chars.desc: A cheeky operator who uses his special ability to swipe food from the kitchen.

chars.name: SilverAsh
chars.desc: The Kjerag man whom Matterhorn serves as his 'Master.' He has two younger sisters.

chars.name: Ensia
chars.desc: SilverAsh's youngest sister · Operator Cliffheart

chars.name: Enya
chars.desc: SilverAsh's younger sister · Operator Pramanix

chars.name: Vulcan
chars.desc: A blacksmith from Minos who keeps a workshop aboard the ship.

chars.desc: A Medic on the Reserve Op Team. Lava's older sister, with a habit of putting strange ingredients in her food.

chars.name: Lava
chars.desc: A Reserve Op Team operator and Hibiscus's younger sister. Blunt-tongued, but soft-hearted.

chars.name: Ceobe
chars.desc: A wandering girl rescued in Leithanien and brought to Rhodes Island. She calls her weapons her 'treasures.'

chars.name: Orchid
chars.desc: Leader of Team A6. A former civilian with a great sense of style.

chars.name: Popukar
chars.desc: A young operator with tremendous strength. She sticks close to Orchid.

chars.name: Catapult
chars.desc: A Team A6 operator, notorious for stirring up trouble.

chars.name: Midnight

chars.desc: A Reserve Op Team leader, born with true Kuranta speed.

chars.desc: A shield-bearing Reserve Op Team operator who used to serve in a garrison.

chars.name: Kroos
chars.desc: A Reserve Op Team sniper who puts her brains to work finding places to slack off.
