chars.desc: An instructor for the Reserve Op Team. He, too, was trained by Dobermann.

chars.name: Dobermann
chars.desc: The instructor in charge of the Reserve Op Team, infamous for her harsh training.

terms.name: Blacksteel
terms.desc: Officially called Blacksteel Worldwide. A mercenary organization that works in partnership with Rhodes Island.

terms.name: Reserve Op Team
terms.desc: Rhodes Island squads made up of rookie operators, from Infected patients once under treatment to former civilians. Dobermann is in charge of their training.

terms.name: Rhine Lab
terms.desc: A science and technology company that pursues both the treatment of the Infected and research. Its goals align with Rhodes Island's, and the two work in partnership.

terms.name: Originium Slug
terms.desc: A small creature that carries Originium crystals on its back. Said to be common in the Sargon desert.

terms.name: Bolívar
terms.desc: A nation where several entangled factions are locked in an ongoing civil war.

blocks.x: Rhodes Island: a pharmaceutical company that treats the Infected, and a landship that roams the earth. Even this ship has afternoons with no operations and no fighting — and even on those afternoons, everyone aboard manages to keep busy.

An intern huntress in search of a pet-sitter, a Medic opening an old diary, a cook wrestling with a thief who won't wash his hands, a blacksmith saddled with a nameless wanderer, an office worker who became a combatant just to escape the office, and an instructor who keeps a set of old dog tags.
One afternoon, people who came aboard the same ship for different reasons each learn a little more about one another.
1. Pet-Sitter Wanted (Warning: Explodes If You Press the Spikes)

4:22 p.m. one day, in the training grounds. **Vanilla**, an intern huntress on loan from Blacksteel, is gasping for breath after her conditioning drills. In a few days she's heading out on a mission with her seniors — and she has no one to look after the pets she keeps in her room.

When the Doctor asks what kind of pets, Vanilla answers brightly: Puffball, Tiny, and Kuro make up an **Originium Slug** trio, and Stout is a mini Sargon Desert Metal Crab. Then she catches the look in the Doctor's eyes, leaps up insisting that the 'Originium' part is real Originium and they are absolutely not food, and quietly scraps the idea of leaving them with the Doctor.

In the end, at the Doctor's suggestion, she decides to ask whoever walks by next — and the person she identifies by footsteps and scent alone is **Melantha** of Reserve Op Team A4. But Melantha has also been added to this mission so her master Franka can keep teaching her swordsmanship, so her teammate **Steward** agrees to take the pets instead.
As Melantha heads off for her Oripathy checkup, Vanilla invites her to tea afterward — and Steward suddenly thanks Vanilla. Vanilla has no idea what for.
Then **Blaze** shows up with a little patient, **Dora**. Dora dashes off to her paper-flower folding class and, sure enough, trips and falls.

Vanilla remembers that girl. When Vanilla first came aboard, she saw her waiting outside a door with her parents, clutching a tattered doll — a Victorian child who'd been caught up in a street fight and inhaled Originium dust.

Vanilla admits she never expected to see that not-so-well-off family again. Blaze tells her treatment here isn't free either. The only thing they don't ask for is 'money' — filing paperwork, cleaning, washing dishes in the cafeteria, anything that helps the ship is payment enough.
The paper flowers the kids fold will decorate the venue for a mixer. When Steward asks when exactly this mixer was decided, Blaze answers proudly: "Just now. I decided."
Steward sees it a little differently. Some people work here to pay for their treatment, some came because their goals happen to line up, and some have staked everything on Amiya's ideals.
Not everyone needs to share the same will. It's heading in the same direction that lets us walk side by side.

blocks.cap: A corridor aboard the ship. This is where Blaze's mixer was decided "just now."

blocks.x: Then, Vanilla's room. One look at Puffball and the gang in their insulated terrarium, and Steward seriously wonders whether his definition of 'cute' differs from hers. There's only one thing to watch out for, apparently: press the spikes on Kuro's shell and he explodes.

Vanilla's hometown is a remote Sargon village with nothing but sand, where every child grows up to be a hunter. Drawn by the tales of the outside world that traveling merchants told around the campfire, she left home; she had no money, so she became a mercenary, but she says she has no regrets.

Just before they part, Vanilla stops Steward. Next time the Reserve Op Team goes to visit the kids, she asks, please bring her along — she's started to want to fold paper flowers for the mixer together with them.
2. The Database Has Everything — Except What Her Colleagues Like

Meanwhile, **Ptilopsis** returns from a field survey. When **Silence** says she'll handle the next one herself, Ptilopsis replies, "I can go next time too," leaving Silence puzzled — then heads back to her room and opens her diary. It's the one she's kept since following Silence from Rhine Lab to Rhodes Island.

The medical department in her diary is a rowdy place. A newcomer named Aak — once an unlicensed back-alley doctor in Lungmen — openly looked down on the department and even got into a 'contest' with Warfarin. Asked whether those two actually get along, Ptilopsis returns her system search result: 'Birds of a feather flock together.'

There was also the day she talked about the past with fellow Medic **Ansel**. When Ansel said he wished he could see his family more often, Ptilopsis searched her database for her own family and replied, "It seems I had forgotten a little." Her colleagues' stories always felt far away to her, like the parents in her memory.

And then this latest mission. With time to spare while the equipment was being retested, a Guard operator suggested Ptilopsis check out the fair at a nearby Kazimierz nomadic village. Only after digging through her database did she recall that they'd accept local currency only — and the rule that she couldn't go out without an escort was news to her entirely.

blocks.cap: The survey site. The drawn-out equipment testing gives Ptilopsis a chance to go out.

blocks.x: She had forgotten even things she knew, simply from not using them for so long — that was the first problem. The second one found her at a market stall. She wanted to pick out gifts for her colleagues in the medical department, but she had no idea what any of them liked.

blocks.cap: The fair at the Kazimierz nomadic village. When the shopkeeper asks what she's looking for, the answer is "...I don't know."

blocks.x: Back on the ship, she's writing in her diary when **Ifrit** drops by. Swinging a souvenir wooden sword, Ifrit asks, "Don't I look like one of those flippy Kurantas?" Ptilopsis cuts her down in a single stroke: "No."

That day's entry reads like this: ever since Silence worked out her treatment plan, her life has been nothing but research and sleep, and she has known the outside world only through her colleagues' stories and the view out the window. Even while admiring their lives, she had been unconsciously drawing a line, telling herself she didn't belong in those stories.
It isn't a lament. She doesn't dislike research, and she believes it's meaningful. She has simply remembered why she keeps a diary.

When Ifrit asks why she bothers with something as tedious as a diary, Ptilopsis says it's so she won't forget — because she's forgetful. From somewhere deep inside her come the sounds of scraping metal, shouting, and explosions, and sometimes when she wakes up she forgets where she is.

Not long ago, she also saw Silence — who can bury herself in work for days without rest — agonizing over a birthday present for Ifrit. Since she'd decided to take the girl in, Silence said, this was her responsibility. It was a side of Silence that Ptilopsis had never seen before.
When it comes to the important things, just trying not to forget them isn't enough.

She wants to understand the people she cares about better, to do more, and to have no regrets. So when Silence comes to pick up Ifrit, Ptilopsis tells her: she'd like to talk with her about things she never thought about before.
3. The Sandwich Left Behind by a Thief Who Didn't Wash His Hands

Another morning, in the Compartment 2 cafeteria. When Kjerag-born cook **Matterhorn** finishes a plate of North Kjerag-style stir-fried greens, **Gummy** takes a taste and can't stop gushing about how delicious it is — then calls him 'Uncle,' leaving him briefly speechless.

But the plate was already a little emptier before Gummy even touched it. Once Gummy leaves with the stew she's made for the Doctor, Matterhorn turns to the empty kitchen, says "Show yourself," and draws his weapon.

The one hiding is **Ethan**, who uses his special ability to turn invisible and swipe food from the kitchen. When Matterhorn says he 'cares,' Ethan breaks into a cold sweat, thinking he's in real trouble — but what actually has Matterhorn upset is something else entirely: Ethan grabbed the food with his bare hands, without even washing them.

blocks.cap: The Compartment 2 cafeteria. Today's dish: North Kjerag-style stir-fried greens. Today's uninvited guest: Ethan.

blocks.x: Ethan, who's been letting the lecture go in one ear and out the other, suddenly chimes in: Matterhorn sighed more than a few times while cooking. He doesn't have to talk about it if he doesn't want to — but he shouldn't be so hard on himself.

The braised beastmeat simmering on the stove is a Kjerag dish made, by order of his Master **SilverAsh**, for the younger Lady, **Ensia**. SilverAsh had dropped by earlier on his way to see the Doctor, asked after Ensia, and told Matterhorn to bring her a cup of the salted milk tea she loves, too.

When Ethan asks why only the younger sister gets this treatment, Matterhorn shuts him down — family matters — but still whips up some fried beastmeat for Ethan and leaves him with a reminder to wash his hands. Left alone, Ethan grumbles but scrubs his hands with soap for thirty seconds, only for blacksmith **Vulcan** to appear and tell him to dry them before he grabs the bread.

Meanwhile, Lady **Enya** receives her tea, notices the sesame oil in it, and smiles — that's how she often drank it as a child. Matterhorn recalls that it was the Master who loved putting oil in his tea most of all, yet he hasn't once had it that way since returning from Victoria.
And seeing that Lady Ensia has picked out the bell peppers again, he starts to think, 'The Master used to...' — then hastily pretends he never thought it. Far too dangerous a line of thought.

Then, in the corridor, Ethan shoves a sandwich into his hands and vanishes. The bread is burnt and the meat sliced too thick, but Vulcan, following behind, says the kid worked pretty hard on it, and passes along what he said: "For Uncle Matterhorn, some slapdash cooking from us shameless kids these days ought to do as a thank-you." He also made off with every last bit of food in the kitchen.
When Vulcan says he looks pleased, Matterhorn clears his throat — and finally mutters what's really been bothering him: just how old is Ethan, anyway, to be calling him 'Uncle'?
4. The Girl Left in Someone's Care Came Back With a Name

Meanwhile, in Medical Examination Room 6, Medic **Hibiscus** is struggling through a dental checkup on 'Miss Perro.' The girl won't so much as twitch for Hibiscus's homemade biscuits, but snaps right up the honey biscuit her younger sister **Lava** holds out.

'Miss Perro' is a wandering girl they brought back from Leithanien. She'd ambushed twenty-four groups of travelers to steal food, and Lava nearly lost her life to her javelin. They brought her back anyway because the head of the local branch warned that if the police there caught her, the new policy on the Infected meant she'd be dealt with 'humanely.'

Lava may grumble, but Hibiscus knows. It was Lava who spent all her money buying the girl candy, Lava who kept talking to her so they could bring her back without shackles, and Lava who worked hardest baking those biscuits.

But just as the checkup is wrapping up, **Beagle** shouts that they're going to be late for Instructor Dobermann's training. The sisters, who forgot to request the day off, go pale, hand the girl and the honey biscuits off to Vulcan, whom they bump into outside the door, and run — with a parting request not to let her touch her weapons.

At Vulcan's workshop, the girl timidly holds out her axe. Vulcan can't do maintenance on it, but looking can't hurt — and she recognizes it at a glance. Old Minoan craftsmanship, the marks of diligent polishing, and a smithing technique she feels she's seen somewhere before.

A name was carved near the grip in Minoan. The girl had wanted to go to Minos but never made it, and no one she met had been able to read it for her. Working her way through the old Minoan script, Vulcan reads it out: 'Ceobe.'
The girl repeats it over and over. I'm **Ceobe**. Me — I've got a name!
Everyone has two names, Ceobe says, and she wants a short one too. Vulcan, who has only ever named weapons, thinks hard and finally settles on 'Kay.'

Soon, word comes from the Logistics Department: from now on she's free to go about as she pleases. Ceobe wandered from Bolívar all the way to the far eastern borders looking for Minos, but never thought about what she'd do once she got there. So Vulcan asks her again — then what does she want to do now?

Eat until she's full every day, soak in warm water all day long and then crawl under a fluffy blanket, and have a big room to keep all her treasures in. When Vulcan says that in exchange she'd have to use her head and fight bad guys, Ceobe asks back: "Vulcan, ma'am, are you talking about being a hero?"
Vulcan smiles and says yes, then tells the hesitant logistics operator to put her own name down as the sponsor.

The honey biscuit Ceobe shares — Lava's handiwork — isn't crispy and has way too much honey, but it tastes just like the ones back in Minos. Vulcan promises to ask Matterhorn to bake her some fresh ones next time.

When Lava and Hibiscus rush back breathless after training, they're greeted by a girl holding weapons freshly refinished to match the color of her axe. "Don't call me Miss Perro anymore. Call me Ceobe!"

A few weeks later, Ceobe passes despite a disastrous set of test results — but the HR director still has to put in a report why Vulcan got so deeply involved in someone else's decision. Vulcan's answer is a single line.
A girl who likes weapons can't be bad.

Pressed for more, Vulcan adds: the girl didn't know the first thing about whetstones or oils, but the one thing she did know — polishing her weapons — she did well. Minos has no tradition of carving names into weapons, so that name must mean something important. And the technique behind that axe, one Vulcan herself can't forge, is one she's sure she's seen somewhere.

Wanting to solve that mystery together, Vulcan says, is just a blacksmith's selfishness. Once she leaves, the HR director laments: not a single person on this ship has a proper résumé — is this an HR job or detective work?
5. Became a Combatant to Escape the Office — and Still Doing Paperwork

And then, at 9:39 one night, **Orchid**, leader of Team A6, is once again helping the Logistics Department with its paperwork. She's invited to just transfer to logistics outright, and is even told about a clause: if a combat operator of civilian origin can't adapt to the front lines within a year, a transfer to logistics is approved unconditionally.

The truth is, Orchid's reason for choosing combat was simple. She'd signed up here for a change of pace, and didn't want to end up sitting in an office there too. Not a reason she could bring herself to say out loud.

On the way back to the dorms, **Popukar** asks what the 'rat race' is. Orchid explains it's what miserable people live, stuck in offices like mold — and then asks Popukar how she ended up on this ship.

Dr. Kal'tsit and Dr. Ansel 'bought' her, Popukar says — from the lumberyard her parents sent her to work at when she was very small. She's never once seen her mom and dad since, but Dr. Ansel told her that if she's a good girl, Rhodes Island will find them for her.

Orchid hugs Popukar without a word. When she asks how Popukar would feel about a desk job, Popukar answers, "I'm just really strong, that's all" — and Orchid blames herself, saying she never should have asked.

Just then, after getting dragged into **Midnight**'s training and barely escaping, **Catapult** shows up. Hearing for the first time that Midnight spends every mission-free night in the training room, Orchid changes course.

In the training room, Midnight and **Spot** are crossing swords. When Orchid asks why a civilian team would go this far, the host industry's former number one launches, rather unexpectedly, into the secret to his success: never treating clients differently based on who they are.

blocks.cap: The training room at night. When he has no missions, Midnight is always here at this hour.

blocks.x: In his eyes, even the elite operators who head into the most dangerous places are, off the battlefield, just people who drink, tend plants, cry, laugh, get hurt, and sometimes die. And Orchid — the ship's 'fashion guru,' who gives those very elites style advice — ought to know that.
Moving things to the cafeteria, Midnight asks how Orchid got infected, then starts telling his own story.

There was once a junior of his — bright, honest, quick to trust people. Midnight could tell he would surpass him someday. But to that junior, who had grown up poor and clung to money, Midnight was simply too dazzling.

The junior nearly killed him once, and from then on Midnight taught himself the sword. Next, the junior bribed Midnight's manager to secretly infect him with Oripathy — and then showed up, already Infected himself, with his 'friends' in tow.
He fought ready to die and survived, he says, and then, with his own hands, he— That's where Popukar bursts into tears.
Midnight says he's grateful to that guy for showing him how immature he was. Afterward he left the business, registered at the office in Higashi, and took the long way around to end up here.

Seeing a cruel truth doesn't mean you have to accept it, he says, and there's no need to blame yourself for having lived in a greenhouse. Life is the same everywhere: working hard in logistics is just as much effort, and he simply chose combat.
Asked if he isn't afraid of dying, Midnight answers that anyone would be — so she should think properly about how she wants to live on this ship. Orchid quietly thanks him.
On the way back to the dorms, Popukar says it: Orchid hasn't looked happy since they left the Logistics Department, but now she does.

One evening after that, Orchid tells the Logistics Department she'll stay on as a combatant. Too sore to even lift her arms after the fitness training she signed up for herself, she gets dragged off by Catapult to watch Midnight spar with Popukar. Go looking for trouble, and you just might find it.
6. A Lesson You Get a Zero for Repeating

One morning, the Reserve Op Team's mini-tests are underway in the training grounds. **Fang** passes against her instructor, but **Beagle** fails, and **Kroos** is eliminated from a hide-and-seek sniping exercise when her instructor gets behind her.

To the dispirited girls, Instructor **Grace** explains that the tests are there to show them what to work on, and that every instructor learned from the same person: **Dobermann**. The Dobermann they know now, he says, is a hundred times gentler than she once was.
Her tactics and grasp of the battlefield, forged in the Bolívar military, are formidable, Grace adds. She rarely speaks of those days, but back then she was a 'real soldier.'

Before lunch, Fang and Beagle deliver the test results in Grace's place and offer to help Dobermann clean her room. Surprised — she'd thought they were afraid of her — Dobermann accepts. When a military uniform turns up in the wardrobe, she tells them about Bolívar.

A puppet government controlled by Leithanien. An Autonomous Government that split off from parliament. A Resistance of ordinary people worn down by the fighting between the two. Bolívar is divided among these three factions, and Dobermann was a colonel in the Autonomous Government.
As Beagle wipes the top of the wardrobe, metal plates slip from her fingertips. Dog tags. The names Beagle manages to make out are Alan, Juan, and Jose.
"Yes. They're all dead."
In Dobermann's memory, someone speaks. Colonel, your men's deaths were a great help. Thanks to them, my reputation is intact. People don't need the truth. They need an honorable outcome.
She wasn't close to them. She barely exchanged a few words with them. Even so, Dobermann says, they mattered to her.

blocks.cap: Dobermann's room. She says there wasn't much in it when she first arrived.

blocks.x: Then Dobermann asks what they think a soldier's defining trait is. It isn't combat skill, and it isn't weapons; numbers define an army, not a soldier. When Beagle answers 'obeying orders' — something her captain told her back in the garrison — Dobermann says that's right.

There's even a saying that the best soldier is one who doesn't think. When Beagle asks whether that isn't cruel, Dobermann answers that war is crueler. But a soldier is not a machine. A soldier knows better than anyone when they are following a foolish order.

Deceiving such soldiers is folly, so only one path remains: give orders that can be trusted, orders that are correct. She left the Autonomous Government for the Resistance, saw the same thing there, and left again. Rhodes Island, where she arrived after drifting with no real expectations, was the place that did it, Dobermann says.

So cherish this place, she tells them. Even if you don't know why you're fighting, you won't lose anything because of it. The old question — 'Is moving forward enough, and is that direction truly forward?' — has no answer. But if it's the way Rhodes Island shows you, you won't go wrong.
Because this is a utopia that idealists guard with their lives, for the sake of a small hope.

Before long it's 1 p.m. As she sends them off to eat, Dobermann adds one thing: what she just told them may show up on a test — but anyone who answers exactly as she said gets a zero. Fang promises to think it through carefully.
Alone again, Dobermann reflects on how she has somehow grown used to being called 'Instructor.' On this ship she found a new purpose, the one Amiya and Kal'tsit drew for her. But.
Alan. Juan. Jose.
Her roots are still in Bolívar. Someday she'll have to go back and see for herself. ...Someday.

The intern who leaves her Originium Slugs in someone else's care, the Medic rereading her diary, the wanderer who found her name, the instructor who carries old names with her — each came aboard this ship for a different reason. But as long as they're headed the same way, they can go together.

act6d5.tagline: The legendary monster 'Nian' storms Lungmen on New Year's Eve to use the city as her forge, Lava sets off the world's biggest firecracker with a City Defense Cannon, and the final boss gets way too into it. Lungmen's hot peppers, honestly, just aren't spicy enough.

chars.name: Ch'en
chars.desc: A Senior Superintendent of the Lungmen Guard Department, and one of the youngest ever to hold the rank.

chars.name: Snowsant
chars.desc: A rookie intern who also heads Lungmen's Frontier Defense Engineering Department. Her promotions are lightning-fast; her confidence is rock-bottom.

chars.name: Wei Fumizuki
chars.desc: Lungmen's current Chief Executive, and the Chief who commands the Guard Department.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: The leader of Rhodes Island. Young as she is, she has everyone's trust.

chars.name: Lava
chars.desc: An Elite Operator of Rhodes Island. An Arts master and a Catastrophe expert.

chars.name: Nian
chars.desc: A legendary calamity said to descend on Lungmen at the end of every year.

chars.name: Madame Oni
chars.desc: Boss of a Lungmen gang of toughs, with a long-running feud with Ch'en.

chars.name: Swire
chars.desc: A rich girl from Lungmen with an unusual knack for investing.

chars.name: Waai Fu
chars.desc: A martial artist at Lee's Detective Agency. Ghosts, however, scare her.

chars.name: Hung
chars.desc: Full-time security guard at Lee's Detective Agency, and the group's voice of common sense.

chars.name: Closure
chars.desc: A Rhodes Island engineer who keeps the ship's systems running.

terms.name: Terracotta
terms.desc: Enemies of unknown origin that take the form of Reunion members or the dead. They give off no Originium reaction whatsoever.

terms.name: City Defense Cannon
terms.desc: A colossal defensive cannon guarding Lungmen, powered by an Originium drive core.

blocks.x: "Use your spear to strike your shield. Use your shield to block your spear." Someone going around and around in this exchange, head in hands over how it never ends, finally hits on a solution.
**"What if I just set off one massive explosion? Wouldn't that clear everything right up?"**

blocks.cap: An endless exchange of spear and shield. The verdict: blow it up first.

blocks.x: Then it's New Year's Eve at Lungmen's defense command center. Bracing for the 'Nian,' the monster said to strike the city at the end of every year, the Lungmen Guard Department (L.G.D.) has once again put nearly all of its people on emergency duty.

blocks.cap: A single line rises out of the black screen: 'RHODES ISLAND PRESENTS'.

blocks.x: 1. Emergency Duty on New Year's Eve, and a Lost Senior Engineer

The officers at the rooftop post brush off an explosion reading from a warehouse leased by some company called Penguin-something with an "Oh, of course," and joke about the Nian legend: if a hundred-meter giant really showed up, they'd just blast it with the defense cannons. (In Lungmen, that company's name is apparently explanation enough.)

Just then, a woman bursts onto the roof looking for the central control room, scrambles back down in a fluster, and runs smack into her superior in the hallway. "...Snowsant? What are you still doing here?"

**Ch'en**, one of the youngest Senior Superintendents in history, tells the rookie fresh back from Columbia that the Nian is more than an old story: the damage Lungmen has suffered can't be a lie, and neither can the names carved into the headstones. Told to puff out her chest because Chief Wei personally called her back, Snowsant answers: "S-sorry..."
Then, the central control room. When **Wei Fumizuki** points out that the report is late, Ch'en covers for the rookie, blaming the time it took to tidy up the report.

blocks.cap: Wei Fumizuki. Lungmen's current Chief Executive, origins unknown. Rumors of a devoted husband holding down the home front remain unconfirmed.

blocks.x: Snowsant is the senior engineer in charge of the forward defense line's installations. She holds the record for the fastest promotion in history, yet her confidence is so low that when the Chief says she remembers her, the first thing out of her mouth is "D-did I do something wrong?!"

blocks.cap: Snowsant. Rookie intern and head of Lungmen's Frontier Defense Engineering Department. Promotions at top speed, confidence at rock bottom.

blocks.x: Then a docking request comes in from an allied vessel, and the Chief wraps things up: "Tonight, Lungmen's defenses must be stronger than they have ever been."
2. The Superintendent's Year-End Duties: A Drinking Contest with a Gangster

But Ch'en doesn't go home. She heads to Lungmen Park, where gang boss **Madame Oni** is throwing a New Year's drinking party. Ch'en reads out last year's long list of offenses and makes it clear: tonight, nobody is going anywhere.

Madame Oni agrees, on conditions: her crew sets the rules, and if she wins, Ch'en has to tell her what the L.G.D. is hiding behind its 'special circumstances.' The event, naturally, is drinking, and it's Madame Oni who goes down at bottle seventeen. "Since when... can you drink like this?" "The L.G.D. has a lot of get-togethers."

Still, the winner's tongue is just as tangled, and Ch'en spills a lead to Oni's underling: inside a giant crater of unknown origin, they found a melted, abandoned building and massive scorch marks. No trace of Arts, and definitely recent.

Meanwhile, at the next table over, an ordinary citizen named Mr. Wei is playing Go with a retired old man. After some talk about their old days on the force, the old man boasts, "We even beat back the Nian, didn't we?", then gets caught sneaking an extra stone onto the board.

blocks.cap: Lungmen Park on New Year's Eve. Drinks on one side, a Go board on the other.

blocks.x: Out on the street, an honor student who just passed the L.G.D. exam rattles off her rich friend's shady investments one after another and smiles, "We're friends, aren't we? S-w-i-r-e?" **Swire** goes pale. Yet even this honor student shrieks "Eek!" at the bang of a firecracker and hides behind her friend.
And as the night wears on, it gets strangely warmer. The old man at the Go board mutters that the temperature is still climbing long after sunset, and that he has a bad feeling about it.
3. Rhodes Island Arrives, but Lava Is Nowhere to Be Found
Around then, the Rhodes Island ship reaches Lungmen. Amiya, explaining that every record tells the Nian legend differently, has one more question for the Doctor: "Have you seen Lava, by any chance?"

Meanwhile, in an engine room somewhere, someone unidentified is digging through files. "...Re, u, nion?" Then, with an "All right, let's see if I can polish this up a bit...", they start tinkering with something.

At the same time, Snowsant boots up the temperature-check system in her lab and gets the result: 'large number of unresponsive objects within range.' Deciding there's no way anything like an Originium insulator could exist, she concludes it's broken and mourns the wasted electricity bill.

Over at the L.G.D., Amiya casually asks whether an operator can be registered without being present, and the Chief catches on at once. She means **Lava**, the Catastrophe expert who independently researches the Catastrophes of old. But the Chief's "Miss Lava's knowledge of the Nian..." is cut short by an emergency report.

blocks.cap: 'Nian.' A name that has plagued Lungmen for hundreds, even thousands, of years.

blocks.x: "An unidentified group has appeared in downtown Lungmen. ...They're reportedly wearing Reunion insignia."
And in the wilderness outside the city, someone looking down at some kind of traces murmurs: "No matter who they are, I'll stop them all. I won't let the same thing happen again. Never."

blocks.cap: And then the title fills the screen: 'LAVA'S ANCIENT FORGE'.

blocks.x: 4. Reunion Returns (Originium Reaction Not Included)

The 'Reunion' that show up downtown don't say a word. They go down with barely any resistance, yet shed not a drop of blood, and even their bodies vanish, so the L.G.D. decides to call them **Terracotta**.
The problem is their numbers. Nearly every squad has run into Terracotta, and while the temperature keeps soaring, no detector can pick up a heat source.

blocks.cap: Transmissions pour in. The enemy keeps coming, but the heat source is nowhere to be found.

blocks.x: Chief Wei orders the evacuation of downtown civilians as the top priority and declares, "Stand together, and the L.G.D. has nothing to fear." Rhodes Island, having only just arrived, jumps right in to help.

Meanwhile, cutting down Terracotta in the streets, Ch'en grits her teeth. She knows they're only Reunion on the outside, but watching them strut down Lungmen's streets with their heads held high is "...honestly sickening." As Ch'en heads out to set up a cordon, the Chief gives her one short warning: "The L.G.D. can't afford to lose you."

In the park, officers panic when Terracotta turn up disguised as their own colleagues, until a hungover Madame Oni, clutching her head, roars "Get up!" and they reflexively snap, "Y-yes, ma'am!" Her own mind, though, is elsewhere: "Losing a drinking contest to Ch'en... the shame of it."
And things get worse. The Terracotta pick up weapons, start differing in strength from one to the next, and begin fighting as if they were living people.
5. A Reverse-Thinking Gamble Worth Tens of Millions

Around then, Snowsant comes barreling into the command center, crashes into the Doctor, and between a stream of apologies offers an idea: crank every Originium-powered machine up to maximum output, then flip the search around and look for wherever there is no Originium reaction.

Told it could paralyze all of Lungmen and cost tens of millions, Snowsant cries "M-m-maybe we'd better forget I said anything...", but the Chief is firm: if it uncovers even the tip of the iceberg of the Nian's secret, the L.G.D. will accept any loss. "I trust Snowsant's judgment."

Meanwhile, at a barricade, the wisecracking officer freezes in front of a Terracotta wearing the face of someone he knows is long dead. What he gets is a roar from his serious partner: "They're all fakes!" "I just smashed your skull in a minute ago!"
And the reverse-thinking pays off. Thermal imaging locks onto the heat source, and the Chief grants the Doctor the same command authority as Superintendent Ch'en.

blocks.cap: L.G.D. command center. A gamble worth tens of millions catches the heat source by the tail.

blocks.x: Then a sandstorm kicks up where the enemies slipped out of the containment zone. On a special line comes a call from Inspector Lin, a retired hero of the L.G.D. and none other than the old man at the Go board. He's dumped the escapees in a trash bin, he says, and if they'll just give the go-ahead, he and 'the Wei household's number two' will wrap this up in ten minutes.

The Chief is silent for a moment, then smiles. "Heh... That takes me back to when we were young." Even so, the L.G.D. isn't yet so weak that it needs to lean on them, she says, and gives the order: "Now, it's time to fight back."

Back at the Go board in the park, Mr. Wei grumbles about being called by his old nickname in front of people from work, and the old man hits the nail on the head: "So who decides what goes in the dumplings at your house?" "She's the boss, isn't she?"
6. An Ally of Justice, a Back-Alley Doctor, and a Watermelon-Flavored Shot

Around then, the Lee's Detective Agency crew is out on the downtown streets: martial artist **Waai Fu**, full-time security guard **Hung**, and a shady back-alley doctor, debating whether the Terracotta that vanish with a single kick are ghosts or monsters.

The back-alley doctor gives an officer with a broken arm a mystery injection. The pain disappears like magic, but there's a strange fruity smell, and once the officer leaves, the doctor mutters: 'Adrenaline administered to Test Subject No. 3... watermelon scent, origin unknown.'

When Waai Fu backs away, insisting you can't beat ghosts with martial arts, the doctor nudges her: if she beats the Nian, maybe that old man chasing the pinnacle of martial arts will finally come and spar with her. Without a word, Waai Fu walks off toward the containment zone. "...Waai Fu?! Dammit! Hung! Go stop her!"
7. A Washed-Up Star Meets a Fan

And in a corner of that same street, a child looking for their mom walks up to a fully armed 'mister,' and in the moment it takes to yelp "Ow, hot!", the mister is gone. A young woman appears in his place and sends the kid off, telling them the 'battle of the century' is going on here, so they'd better go hide somewhere.

When the woman asks whether a heartwarming scene like that isn't usually the cue to lower your blade, Lava, blade in hand, fires back: "And is one person 'usually' able to run the entire Lungmen Guard Department ragged like this?"
The name Lava calls her: **Nian**. The legendary monster turns out to be a chatty young woman who whines that even that name isn't cool anymore and asks for a new one.

blocks.cap: A downtown street swept by Terracotta. The legend and her researcher face off.

blocks.x: When Lava says she's been studying her all this time, Nian is moved. It's like being a washed-up star meeting a longtime fan, she says. "Sure... if you count someone who wants to kill you as a fan."

But when the talk turns to how the Catastrophe isn't Nian alone, and how things might be different if their 'true form' could be killed, the air changes. Asked why ancient Yan and modern Lungmen alike always met the same end, Nian answers with a smile.
The right amount of destruction and slaughter makes for the best education, you know.

The Terracotta, Nian explains, are made from the enemies people have fought and the fears in their hearts; all she did was froth them up a little. Meanwhile, the top of a building starts to melt away. "Smelt. Cast. Temper. This city makes the perfect forge."

But Lava came prepared too. Amid an ear-splitting din, she recites an old incantation, and for the first time Nian flinches, grinding her teeth: "Damn it, just how much did Dusk teach these humans..." The line Lava had dug out of Yan's old legends was this: "The year ends amid the sound of firecrackers."

Instead, Nian looks delighted. She pulls a sword hilt out of her mouth, slices clean through Lava's spatial Arts, points to the sky, and cries: "Heaven holds a furnace, and the earth yields every metal... Arise!"
8. Three Days Later, the Other Side of the Line Is Lungmen Too

Then, dawn three days later. Chief Wei has given up District 21 and drawn a defensive line at the city's edge, but the other side of that line is Lungmen too. Looking out over the occupied streets, Ch'en says that over there are shops she used to frequent and the homes of her friends.

When Lava returns and apologizes for engaging Nian so rashly, Ch'en snaps back that she should say that to the operators who still haven't gotten back up. What they need right now, Ch'en says, is her knowledge and skill.

blocks.cap: Lava. An Arts master and Catastrophe expert. She leaps past the limits of space as if it were nothing.

blocks.x: Lava brings two pieces of news. The good news: Nian has enough of a personality to hold a conversation. The bad news: that personality is absolutely rotten. To Amiya, who tells her not to go it alone, she answers simply: "My blood alone is enough."

When word comes that Nian is approaching the defensive line, Lava finally reveals the weakness: firecrackers. The legend says Nian 'fears the noise and the flame,' but Lava's hypothesis is that for Nian, a self-styled blacksmith, noise and flame should be part of who she is, or at least part of some being projected onto her body.
The plan: Ch'en and Amiya pin her down while Lava goes for the weak point, with Chief Wei and the Doctor in command.

Meanwhile, Nian knocks on Lungmen's wall, decides she likes it because it's an alloy, says "Once you've drawn your sword, you've gotta cut something, even if it's just a radish," and slices straight through it. If Lava hadn't warned them to watch out for her sword and shield, Ch'en would never in a million years have guessed that thing was a 'sword.'

Having spent the three days studying Reunion some more, Nian sends out new Terracotta, and this time they use Arts. When she says Infected puppets are just one extra step in the process, Amiya's face hardens. "Your attitude toward the Infected... I find it truly offensive!"
Nian just shrugs it off: it's not like you lot spare a thought for Originium slugs either, right?
Ch'en and Amiya finally break Nian's shield, only to hear: "Aww, so sorry~ I just made myself another new one!" As the line collapses, Ch'en orders a full retreat and waits for Lava's plan.
9. The Biggest Firecracker in the World

Around then, Lava goes to Snowsant and asks for the underground blueprints. Her muttering about needing one really loud firecracker drifts over to the City Defense Cannon. Based on Originium processing... propelled by an explosion... in midair... "So it IS a firecracker!" "No! They're completely different! Really!"

When Chief Wei authorizes acting now and filing the paperwork later, Snowsant volunteers to draw the blueprints herself. Being new to the job, she'd memorized every blueprint she could get her hands on, so drawing them from memory is no big deal. Lava is left speechless. "No big deal... she says?"
Meanwhile, when Nian walks into the empty L.G.D. building, it's Lava who greets her. Where they face off is the city's core district.

blocks.cap: Lungmen's core district. The stage Lava chose for the showdown.

blocks.x: Out of nowhere, Nian asks after Lava's older sister, then confesses she's jealous: the two of them get to remember each other normally, without killing each other. Counting herself, there are twelve, she says; Nian and her eleven siblings have been killing one another for longer than anyone could fathom.
It's so stupid. What could ever come of your left hand fighting your right?

Lava's hidden card is the core of a reserve City Defense Cannon. She plans to compress the blast space to trap Nian and to become a source of the explosion herself. Nian warns her she'll die doing that, but Lava doesn't back down. "If I can leave even a scratch on you, that's enough."

Recalling how the siblings, worn out from killing each other, at some point learned a game from humans, something called rock-paper-scissors or whatever, Nian suggests they count down from three together. "Three..."

And then, the explosion. Out of the smoke where reserve City Defense Cannon Core No. 2 vanished, Nian soars up with Lava in her grip. And when told to let go, she really does toss her aside, as a bonus.

Nian says she really hates that sound, yet she ended up saving Lava without even thinking. She's used up all her strength, so she asks to be finished off in one go. Lava says she'll take her back to Rhodes Island, but Nian insists it has to be now, and Ch'en gives the order: "Fire!"
Lava, you said you wanted to know the truth, right? The reason I attacked this city is... because Lungmen's... hot peppers just... really, really... aren't spicy enough...

But her body quietly fades away. It was an illusion made from the energy of the blast. Just as Lava grinds her teeth at having let Nian escape, the city begins to rise. It's the **Dark Devastator**, a monster Nian spent three days forging by refining every bit of matter and energy in the city.

blocks.cap: The city rises, and the Dark Devastator awakens. There's no limit to this final boss's showmanship.

blocks.x: When Nian starts chanting an incantation, Lava cuts in in a panic. "Wait, wait! Why are you suddenly chanting a spell?!" "Then how am I supposed to wrap this up?" "I'm the final boss! I've gotta do at least this much or the audience won't be satisfied!"
10. Cut!
Then, a corridor on Rhodes Island. "...Oh, come ON! And why do all these weird lines keep piling up from the middle onward?"
What Lava is holding is a script. The whole story so far was the script for Rhodes Island's short New Year's film: written and directed by Lava, then rewritten at will by its star, Nian.

Protests that the second half is basically her one-woman show don't faze Nian. "Who cares? I'm the main character." The firecrackers, she says, are because she genuinely hates the sound. Just yesterday, Spot startled her so badly she spilled soda all over herself.

She also pushes to recast the film with people from a file: Blaze, Emperor, and the movie star FEater. But as Lava looks through that file, her face goes white. Mixed in are records accessed with restricted clearance. "My sis... that doctor can never find out about this!"

To change the ending, Nian offers a new scene. Someone in sunset-lit ruins sneers at Nian for losing to a mere firecracker, and plays innocent, claiming all she did was visit Yan long ago and spread one amusing rumor.

blocks.cap: "It's time to snuff out every ember on this earth."

blocks.x: Then a caption appears on screen: ANCIENT FORGE 2, COMING SOON.

blocks.cap: A sequel teaser, complete with a cast list. The director never approved it.

blocks.x: "Wait wait wait wait!!" To Lava, who demands to know why there's a sequel, Nian gushes that as long as you throw in words like 'embers,' 'slaughter,' and 'cycle,' it'll sell like crazy.

"And that's your little sister! Of all the things you could do, you're cashing in on your own sister..." Nian is unbothered. This is the girl who put ice cream in her hot pot and secretly dumped out all her chili sauce, so she has it coming.
When Nian fires back with "So do you like your sister or hate her?", Lava runs off to rewrite her lines.
Epilogue. Based on a True Story?

Once Lava is gone, **Closure** shows up. Scolded that copying restricted-access records went too far, Nian casually changes the subject. Probably only someone like Closure could tell which parts are real and which are made up, she says; old tales and scripts are pretty much the same thing in the end.
When Nian complains that the original title, 'Lungmen Doomwatch,' is way too lame, Closure snaps: "Then why not go all the way and call it 'Ancient Forge'!"

As Nian wonders whether adding 'based on a true story' might throw Lava too much, Closure points out that Lava is a pillar of Rhodes Island now, and Nian agrees. "Just like she wanted, she's become a badass warrior doing badass things."

Asked why she started with Lava of all people, Nian doesn't hesitate. Because she really, really likes Lava. Because she's drawn more to someone growing step by step than to those who are already monstrously strong. That's why she's even been recommending Rhodes Island to those siblings of hers who don't hold much hostility toward humans.
You know it too. For me, 'tomorrow' is a pretty precarious thing. That's why I really like Rhodes Island.
When Closure doesn't know how to react, Nian tells her to just take it as a New Year's greeting, and asks what's for dinner tonight.
By then, the film crew and equipment are all set. Lava looks over the newly revised script, sighs, and says they'll just have to improvise.

blocks.cap: The director, new script in hand, talking to herself.

blocks.x: "...Honestly. Going around in circles like this. What are you even trying to tell me? I can see right through you... If you wanted to leave something behind, you didn't have to make such a scene... I was doing this for you to begin with..."
"'Lungmen's hot peppers aren't spicy enough'... of all things. You still can't bring yourself to be honest, even on your way out."
Heh. Honestly... what a mess of a villain.

The answer to the endless exchange of spear striking shield was a massive explosion after all. But in that explosion, Nian caught hold of Lava, who fought her to the very end, and soared upward with her, hiding what she really wanted to say behind the excuse that 'Lungmen's hot peppers aren't spicy enough.'

blocks.x: On the day Reunion took Chernobog completely, Rhodes Island — which had gone into the city to rescue the Doctor — paid a heavy price. Many operators never made it back.
War leaves behind the names of the side that won and the side that lost. The names of the people who fell, held on, and got back up in between are never written down anywhere.
Around that time, in the ruins of the fallen city, in the forests of Siracusa and on the northern ice fields, and in the corridors of Rhodes Island, small battles of every kind were still going on.
1. Two men who saved the drink for next time

That day, in the ruins of Chernobog, an unnamed Vanguard Operator opens his eyes. He calls out for the boss, then finally swallows his tears — and notices a sheet of Rhodes Island's special paper lying beside him.
It was a note, crammed with rough, hurried handwriting. Don't leave these ruins before the sky goes fully dark, it said. You are completely surrounded by the enemy.

blocks.cap: Chernobog, fallen into Reunion's hands.

blocks.x: Then a familiar voice carries over from close by. **Hellagur**, the old man from the Chernobog clinic, is standing face to face with **Patriot**, leader of Reunion's Northern Tundra Guerrillas.

Hellagur called him by his old name, **Buldrokkas'tee**. Long ago, he was the Ursus soldier who charged a fortress with his shield raised against the blizzard and saved the general and his comrades. Now Oripathy has damaged his vocal cords, and he speaks in broken pieces.
Patriot offered him a drink he had brought from the north, but Hellagur said there was no time and put it off. Next time, they would share a glass with old stories on the side.

When Patriot asked him to join Reunion, Hellagur pointed to a building run through by a mass of Originium. It used to be an ordinary shopping mall, he said, and not long ago the clocktower and the intersection were full of glowing bulbs.
Patriot's answer was short. 'The Infected, had no right, to enjoy those lights.'
You want to light the bulbs again, and I only wish the shopping mall would be rebuilt. That is the difference between us.

To Hellagur, what Reunion was doing wasn't fighting back. It was a war of Ursus people slaughtering Ursus people. Patriot countered that if Ursus had treated the Infected as Ursus too, there would have been no war.
Meanwhile, word came in that Talulah had taken Chernobog completely. Instead of celebrating, Patriot ordered his men to save every civilian.

When Hellagur said he was heading to Rhodes Island, Patriot told him Reunion had just attacked Rhodes Island. A single Sarkaz warrior from Rhodes Island had stood alone against the Sarkaz mercenaries, brought down a great many of their elites, and drawn the enemy away from the ruins behind him.

He lost in the end, but Patriot called him a true warrior and entrusted Hellagur with a keepsake he had found in the ashes. Listening from his hiding place, the Vanguard Operator thinks of one person: **Scout**, Rhodes Island's Sarkaz.
2. Who remembers the names of the pawns?

'Is the war against Ursus just?' Hellagur asked. Patriot answered that it was a righteous war — otherwise, countless sacrifices would lose their meaning. Then he added: don't we all know the true answer already?

Just then, a list arrives of the men who laid hands on civilians. Even when told the Chernobogians had it coming, he only asked again, 'They laid hands on civilians?' — and ordered the ringleaders hanged.

Patriot's son was already gone, while Hellagur was raising the adopted daughter of an enemy commander. When Patriot promised to bring his own daughter next time, Hellagur smiled and said he hoped the girls would get along.
A child's voice weaves in between Hellagur's words. She doesn't want Mama to go off and fight again. When Daddy went with Uncle, he never came back.
We are all but pawns on the chessboard of war. And who cares to know the names of mere pawns?

Asked who would remember the names of the dead filling a dozen-odd cities, Patriot answered that a warrior doesn't care about names. Hellagur's answer was different. Now he only wanted to protect the people around him — and that went for Ursus and the Infected alike.
Patriot didn't blame him. Oripathy would take his life sooner or later, he said, so he would fight to the very end with the time he had left.
You hate war. Please, keep on hating it. If you can, end all of this war, too.
Without saying it aloud, the two make the same vow: whatever happens, they will never become each other's enemy.
As the general turns to leave, Patriot calls after him. 'I hope... I pray... That you find yourself. A true home, for yourself.'
3. Twelve names in a note
After Hellagur leaves, the Vanguard Operator cries out — why go that far for someone like me? — and reads the rest of the note.

In the note, Scout called himself a weak man. Over the past three years he had lost countless brothers and sisters, and while everyone believed a way forward would open once they got the Doctor back, he didn't think so.
When they asked the Doctor to command, he wrote, nothing showed in those eyes but certainty of victory. And the crosses on the photos only kept multiplying.

So he hoped the Doctor would never command another battle — that the Doctor could live a new life, even one with no ties to Rhodes Island. It was a far-fetched wish he had never been able to tell anyone.
Then come three requests. First, tell the Doctor: 'I have never forgotten a single moment of the days I fought by your side.' Second, bear witness to how his squad met their end.
Slink, Pter, Scorpion, Leafa, Milim, Tipsy, Slanna, Mimi, Mary, Thumbtack, Mudflower, and Macron.

The twelve who broke through the enemy line and drove off their reinforcements were all killed. No one will remember their names, he wrote, but if anyone asks, tell them their deaths were dignified, and that they were never afraid to die.
The last request was for the nameless brother himself, the one reading it. Live for your own sake.
That is all, my brother. Treasure your life.

Then Patriot's voice rings out from beyond the ruins. He had known all along that someone was hiding there. Wait for nightfall, avoid the lights, and head south, he said — or go and see the people of Chernobog who need help.
The choice was his. Calling out to the boss, to Scout, and to his brothers, the Vanguard Operator makes a vow: he will see it through.

blocks.cap: The Chernobog street where the nameless operator read the note.

blocks.x: 4. W's recruiting pitch: a 'clearance sale'

Meanwhile, in the wilderness outside Chernobog, **W**, the new leader of the Sarkaz mercenaries under Reunion, gets an annoying report. A squad of mercenaries has deserted, and the pursuit team sent after them has gone silent.
Waiting for W at the scene is an old acquaintance. Greeted by W as the 'wandering swordmaster,' he gives his name as **Flamebringer** and casually cuts down a Reunion swordsman who rushes him.

He was ambushed back in the old civil war and was the only one who walked away. W invites him to join up: there's war, all the blood he could want, and plenty of fellow Sarkaz — everything he's after, at 'clearance sale' prices.

Flamebringer turns her down. There's nothing to gain from mindless destruction. If anything, he'd just like to cross swords with Talulah once; all he's really looking for is the meaning of being alive.
He also says he saw W making a deal with some Sarkaz from outside. W finally comes clean: she asked them to get rid of her boss so she could work more freely.

When he points out she was never going to let those partners walk away, W says she at least left alone the people that guy wanted to protect — her promise to help the Rhodes Island rescue team and killing him are two separate things. As for him wiping out the elites she worked so hard to get, just thinking about it ticks her off.
Before they part, W lets something slip: the one behind the plot that ruined his old mercenary company may be waiting where he's headed. And in the battles to come, he'll probably die.

blocks.cap: "No way out but death. It's been a long time since I felt this excited."

blocks.x: When W asks whether he'd believe her if she said she'd let him live this time, Flamebringer replies, 'Funny, I was going to ask you the same question.'

Later, at Rhodes Island, Flamebringer gets a talking-to from instructor **Dobermann** for clashing head-on with Reunion before officially joining. Dobermann says his past doesn't matter as long as he follows the rules, then takes him to the medical department, where someone wants to see him.
And when he runs into the Doctor in the corridor, Flamebringer mutters to himself: 'So that's how it was. W, you're honest in your own way after all.'
5. Your gun won't betray you, but your senior is clueless

Some time later, in the lower-deck firing range of Rhodes Island, docked at Lungmen Harbor. **Jessica**, a rookie dispatched from Blacksteel, is panting her way through training under her senior, **Liskarm**.

blocks.cap: Aboard Rhodes Island, docked at Lungmen Harbor.

blocks.x: Jessica asked for this training herself, with a scouting mission to the Chernobog ruins coming up. Liskarm tells her that trying to do everything perfectly is exactly what makes her freeze up: focus on your fingertips, and trust the gun in your hand.

Next to them, **Franka** has sat through three straight hours of basic drills and is squirming with boredom. When she suggests Jessica just learn from Laterano's angels instead, Liskarm shakes her head. All they'd say is 'it's as easy as walking.'

When Franka whines about why Blacksteel uses such a pain-in-the-neck pistol, Liskarm earnestly explains everything down to management overhead and portability, and Franka answers with a 'Yeah, yeah, sure~.'

Liskarm had a reason for calling Franka in. She says with a perfectly straight face that no one in Blacksteel controls Originium Arts better than her, and Franka goes bright red and yells, 'Ugh, stop, you're embarrassing me!'

But then Franka points to Jessica's evaluation file, the one Liskarm handed over without ever reading it herself. Jessica doesn't top any category, but her overall numbers aren't behind either of her seniors at all. Liskarm is stunned. She had no idea.
Listen, do me a favor and don't teach Jessica to be a dumbass like you, too.
6. An executor of wills disarms the traps first

Far away in the Siracusan wilds, a stranger follows the sound of singing to a small house in the forest. Its owner was **Vermeil**, a one-armed Vulpo girl, and the moment he said he meant her no harm, she loosed an arrow at him.
The man who caught that arrow bare-handed was **Executor**, of the Laterano Notarial Hall, and Vermeil was the heir named in a will.

He had already disarmed every pit, snare, homemade landmine, and automatic dart trap she had laid throughout the forest. The traps were so basic, he said, that he worried they might injure the person he had come for.

blocks.cap: Vermeil's forest, where anyone who enters is prey.

blocks.x: The testator's name was Dürrenmatt. Vermeil had never heard of him, but she remembered one old man: a Laterano with a halo floating over his head, who found her lying beside a beast after she lost an arm, saved her, and fitted her with an arm made of iron.
Still, when you draw a bowstring with this arm, I'd like you to think, just once. Not about revenge, but about why we're alive.
Executor tells her the man suffered from an incurable disease and died on an operating table, not a peaceful death. Then he points to the Originium that has broken through Vermeil's skin.
Dürrenmatt had sold everything he owned to pay for her treatment and the Notarial Hall's fees, and he had added one clause to the request: 'Let Vermeil live.'
When she cries out, asking why some passerby would go that far, Executor answers that it must be because he believed she deserved to live. Then he asks:
Do you want to live?

In truth, 'died on an operating table' was exactly the example Dürrenmatt gave when he told Executor to make up any excuse he liked. He had spent years fleeing the Notarial Hall and had even shot people dead, but he asked that the girl never learn of his past.
Vermeil agrees to go to Rhodes Island, but insists on saying goodbye to her people first. Executor goes along with her, calculating how much ammunition he'll need if the outlaws come back for her.
While he was alive, Dürrenmatt had asked Executor to pull the girl out of that muddy life — to make sure, at the very least, that she didn't end up like him.
But she is my legacy. And my hope.
7. The homework burned, and so did the corridor
Meanwhile, back on Rhodes Island, **Ifrit** wakes from the same dream again. In that place where no one ever answers, there's always just one question left at the end: 'What... are you?'

blocks.cap: A white, silent, empty dream.

blocks.x: Stuck on homework the Doctor assigned her, she gets so fed up with a problem about finding the area of a shape that she scorches the corner of her desk.
She begs to tag along with **Silence** on tomorrow's mission, and when even the Doctor says no, Ifrit just marks every remaining answer as C.
Then a medic operator comes by for her checkup. The moment Ifrit tries to storm out, sick of the sight of white coats, her homework catches fire, and the nurse runs off to get Nightingale.
Meanwhile, out in the corridor, **Projekt Red**, who's walking along the wall, is asking **Frostleaf** about her homework. She finds talking to Frostleaf easier than talking to the Doctor.
Ifrit butts in, and when Projekt Red smells smoke and points out that her homework got burned, Ifrit's nerves go raw. The temperature around them starts to climb.
With every exchange, a voice echoes in her head: 'Monster.' And when Projekt Red calls her weak, someone who can't control herself, the flames finally erupt.
Then someone quells the fire with water Arts. The person Ifrit calls 'MuMu' says her visit is a secret, and asks Ifrit to be sure to keep their promise.

Violent. Willful. Disobedient. Always destroying things. Ifrit knows those words too. Even so, she's trying, because right now she knows she mustn't burn Rhodes Island, or her homework, or her friends.
In the end, an entire corridor is wrecked, and Ifrit holds out her torn, scorched, waterlogged homework to the Doctor and apologizes. If you're going to yell at me, go ahead.

But what the Doctor presses into her hand isn't a scolding. It's her favorite chili snack: dried peppers. Ifrit mumbles that the white coats still have plenty of problems, but she'll make an exception for you — just barely.

Told she can join the next operation, Ifrit jumps for joy, and when the Doctor tells her to calm down and think it over, she decides to go apologize to the nurse she scared and to Frostleaf. After getting a promise of a trip to the beach, too, she runs off yelling, 'Leave it to me!'
Back in the white place again, Ifrit faces something inside herself. When the voice says there is nothing that cannot be burned, this time she doesn't back down. She fires right back.
I get it. Some things I can burn. Some things I can't!
'Then I wait, little thing.' That was the voice's answer, and Ifrit swears that someday, she'll win.
8. A ghost comes calling at the ice-field outpost

And at Rhine Lab Temporary Research Outpost #420 on the Infy Ice Field in the Northlands, observer **Magallan** is spending day 187 of her survey all by herself. Not that she's gotten used to the sign-in system Mayer rigged up greeting her with 'Hi! How are you, Maggie?'

The blizzard looked set to last at least a week. Remembering a low-temperature test on a new material she'd totally forgotten about, she opens the door to toss the sample outside — and there's a woman standing right there.
Magallan shrieks that she's gorgeous but definitely a ghost, and the woman tells her to touch her face. Her cheek was warm.

blocks.cap: Outpost #420, trapped in the blizzard.

blocks.x: **Simone**, a Sami, says she has come on a request to find someone, and Magallan happily chatters away as she serves hot tea, telling her to help herself to all the stockpiled supplies.
Asked if she doesn't get lonely out here alone, Magallan says she does, but loneliness and happiness are two different things. After all, an explorer's best friend is loneliness.

Simone was Infected, and the crystals had spread all the way to her eye. When she asks if Magallan isn't afraid, Magallan cites Rhine Lab's research showing that Oripathy transmission follows rules, and offers to take her to Rhodes Island for treatment.
'I could be a bad person, you know.' Simone says it, then adds, as if asking herself: '...I wonder. Am I a bad person?'
Then an alarm goes off. A worn-out exterior heating pipe has sprung a leak, and if it's left alone, the outpost will only hold out for about two months.
Simone stops Magallan from heading out into the blizzard. No one has ever come here before, she says. What's the point of being so stubborn?
There is a point, Magallan answers. This outpost is a base camp for explorers, and someday, someone will pass through.
No big deal. An explorer spends her whole life discovering, and her whole life being disappointed.
Then Simone offers to go in her place. She has already found the person she was looking for — she is a Rhodes Island operator sent to bring Magallan back, codename **Santalla**.

In the blizzard, old voices come back to her. Voices that called her 'witch' and shouted that she would live to see this land stained with blood, that she would take the gift of the dead with that one eye of hers.
But the Simone of now wonders why she once believed this land had withered away. As long as there are children like this one, the land will keep struggling, and keep flourishing.
Singing, Simone murmurs that she wants to watch Magallan hold on to her dreams. It's about time this snow stopped.
9. On the way to fix a single light bulb
Back to Rhodes Island, not long after it returned from Chernobog with the Doctor. When chief engineer **Closure** asks if she can go see the Doctor, **Kal'tsit** asks if she's planning another prank.

Kal'tsit tells her not to leave the amnesiac Doctor any more bad impressions, and rattles off Closure's rap sheet: the cabin that auto-played 'Closure's Midnight Video Market' every midnight for three months, and the infamous time the central climate control got set to 36 degrees.

Closure insists it was a power outage in the machine room — until Kal'tsit mentions she has thirteen tissue samples from the console, collected at different times. Closure apologizes without pausing for breath.

blocks.cap: Rhodes Island's engineering office.

blocks.x: Closure begs Kal'tsit to come along because two corridors in Sector 3 have lost power, and Kal'tsit grumbles but follows. In the corridor they run into **Heavyrain**, a new operator who had been tagging along behind Kal'tsit.
One 'Miss Closure' and Closure is head over heels, while Kal'tsit sends Heavyrain, who offers to act as her guard, back ahead of them.

Hearing that she used to be in the Sargon military, Closure sums it up: 'So you picked up another stray, huh?' Heavyrain was also the reason Kal'tsit stayed at the operating table for 72 hours straight last month, but when Closure asks if she's been using reagents on herself again, Kal'tsit refuses to answer.

Then, in the pitch-dark outage zone, Closure steps on a random gachapon machine and her eyes light up at the secret-version prize. Only when Kal'tsit snaps 'Clo-sure!' do the wiring repairs finally get started.
Fiddling with the wires, Closure suddenly asks whether Kal'tsit thinks going to Chernobog to rescue the Doctor was a mistake.
Kal'tsit answers that going into Chernobog at a time like that was foolish. But it was Amiya's choice, made from the heart, and all she could do was support it.
At least we made it through the night. All that's left now is to survive until the sun comes up.

As Closure says you need light to walk at night, the bulb flickers on. When Kal'tsit asks why she's bringing this up today of all days, Closure says what matters isn't what Kal'tsit said, but that she got to hear her say it herself.

Having gotten a promise that Kal'tsit will come again as long as there's a bulb to fix, Closure points at the light and smiles. Kal'tsit says it's reassuring when Closure acts like this, and starts to go on: 'Then, even if I...'
Don't say anything else... For now, let's just enjoy this little light.

In the ruins, Hellagur said Reunion wanted to light the bulbs again. That day is still far off, but in a dark corridor of Rhodes Island, one small bulb came on, and the people whose names are never written down make it through one more night, just like that.

act20mini.tagline: In Nuova Volsinii, a city that promised to be free of famiglie, a judge at the Wine Championship drains a poisoned glass and collapses. When foreign capital pushes the locals aside, it is the old famiglia that stands beside them again.

chars.name: Demetri
chars.desc: Owner of Saluzzo Vino. Mixes his own cocktails in a small bar down a back alley. The operator Bellone.

chars.name: Leontuzzo
chars.desc: Mayor of Nuova Volsinii. Left his famiglia and built a city without famiglie. The operator Vigil.

chars.name: Liesel
chars.desc: A Caprinae who keeps the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra running. Paola's adopted daughter. The operator Ripresa.

chars.name: Lavinia
chars.desc: A judge in Nuova Volsinii. Called 'fair', which is rare in Siracusa. The operator Penance.

chars.name: Paola
chars.desc: Conductor of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra. Came over from Leithanien and took in musicians with nowhere to go, one by one, as family.

chars.name: Czarek
chars.desc: President of Kazimierz's 'Golden Prairie'. Host of the Wine Championship.

chars.name: Tosia
chars.desc: A sales rep at 'Golden Prairie' and Czarek's niece. By her own account, a ruthless top seller.

chars.name: Bettina
chars.desc: A nine-year-old who carries Verdi wine around the streets. Niccolo's granddaughter.

chars.name: Lupina
chars.desc: Third-generation heir to the Verdi Winery. Says herself that she is better at drums than at business.

chars.name: Niccolo
chars.desc: An old hand at the Verdi Winery. Has tended the vines like family.

chars.name: Elio
chars.desc: Handles raw-material purchasing for Saluzzo Vino. A neighbor from Leontuzzo and Demetri's childhood.

chars.name: Eirene
chars.desc: Director of the Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti. Leads the truck drivers and has kept her distance from the famiglie.

chars.name: Sam
chars.desc: A truck driver at the Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti. Won't take a delivery fee when it's for a neighbor.

chars.name: Tommaso
chars.desc: A manager at Saluzzo Vino. Coordinates freight shipments.

chars.name: Timpani
chars.desc: The orchestra's percussionist. Was driving piles at the docks when Paola scouted him.

terms.name: Nuova Volsinii
terms.desc: A nomadic city in Siracusa. Founded to run on law and administration alone, without famiglie.

terms.name: New Urban Management Act
terms.desc: Nuova Volsinii's founding law. Built on the principle of favoring no faction.

terms.name: Bellone Family
terms.desc: One of Siracusa's established famiglie. Lost its strength after its don died and its heir walked away.

terms.name: Golden Prairie
terms.desc: A large Kazimierzian winery. Fills shelves with cheap volume and buys up local wineries.

terms.name: Saluzzo Vino
terms.desc: A local liquor company in Nuova Volsinii. Has more than ten wineries under its banner.

terms.name: Verdi Winery
terms.desc: An old family winery. Its vines are older than its people.

terms.name: Schwarzervorhang Orchestra
terms.desc: An orchestra of people from Leithanien. Paola gathered them one at a time from the streets and the docks.

terms.name: Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti
terms.desc: Nuova Volsinii's municipal transport department, the AST. Formed when the old Truckers' Union came inside the system.

terms.name: General Chamber of Commerce
terms.desc: Kazimierz's merchant body. Czarek's backer.

terms.name: Caprinae
terms.desc: A race with curved, rising horns. Common in Leithanien.

terms.name: Lupo
terms.desc: A wolf-like race. Common in Siracusa.

terms.name: Signora Sicilia
terms.desc: The figure who stands above Siracusa's famiglie. Even Nuova Volsinii's government holds its authority by her leave.

blocks.x: **Nuova Volsinii**, a nomadic city in Siracusa, was founded on a promise: a city without famiglie. Trusting that promise, merchants from Kazimierz, Columbia and Leithanien poured in.
**Golden Prairie**, a large Kazimierzian winery, holds a Wine Championship in the city. On the night of the final, the orchestra conductor serving as judge drinks a glass of wine and collapses.
Around that single glass, the paths of people each trying to protect their own begin to cross.
1. The Third Glass

On the theater stage, Golden Prairie's president **Czarek** taps his wine glass. In Nuova Volsinii, he says smoothly, he never had to worry about famiglie meddling, or about 'hidden meanings' behind a deal.

blocks.cap: The night of the final: the theater under lights that are far too bright.

blocks.x: Mayor **Leontuzzo** answers that any legitimate business that follows the city's rules will meet no barriers. Then **Demetri**, the young owner of the local liquor company Saluzzo Vino, approaches him.
The two spent their childhood together. Seen again after a long time, Demetri wears the face of a respectable businessman, and Leontuzzo cannot tell how much of his courtesy is sincere.
Then keep your eyes on me, Leon. As long as you're watching, I won't make mistakes.

Just before the performance, two guards patrolling the cellar see a hooded Caprinae slip out by the stairs. Soon after, a blonde girl, the daughter of the orchestra's leader, follows with a puzzled look.

When the music ends, the special judge who steps up to the tasting table is the conductor of the **Schwarzervorhang Orchestra**, **Paola**. In a tasting with no labels and no stories, she holds the third wine in her mouth the longest, then chooses it. A wine that flatters no one, she says, and walks its own path to the end.

Czarek picks up the bottle, and for an instant his smile disappears. In place of the Golden Prairie wine that should have been in the final sits a wine from **Saluzzo Vino**, which was never on the list.

Demetri points out the 'beginner's mistake' of a missed registration, and Czarek, still smiling, calls for a toast to the local winery's victory. Demetri introduces the wine to Leontuzzo. It suits the moment, he says, when everything worth saying has been said and you still want a little more time together.
Then a cough comes from a corner of the stage. The glass slips from Paola's hand, and her body tips forward.
By the time a waiter reached her, she had already stopped breathing. Her lips had taken on a strange color, and the blonde girl cried for 'Mama', begging incoherently for help.

Czarek quickly sets the direction of suspicion. A wine that didn't match the registry, a death right after a second drink of it, and a winery owner who is a famiglia don. The reporters' flashes go off faster.

Demetri does not back down. When he says that he is the most obvious suspect right now, and that he will stay where he should be so the police can investigate thoroughly, guards hired by Czarek 'escort' him home.

blocks.cap: Just before he is escorted away, a faint smile has returned to Demetri's face. Leontuzzo cannot read it.

blocks.x: Whether the smile meant 'I won't make trouble for you', 'I trust you to sort this out', or 'I've already taken care of it', Leontuzzo could not tell.

That night, once the escort is done, one of the guards mutters to himself. Maybe Nuova Volsinii is a Siracusan city after all. Maybe the things that never changed have come into this new world and are making something else out of it.
2. Nothing Is Unsellable

Back when preparations for the championship were in full swing, **Bettina**, about to turn ten, goes from shop to shop with wine from the **Verdi Winery**, where her grandfather works, but cannot sell a single bottle.

The one who caught her box on the street was **Tosia**, a Golden Prairie sales rep. Czarek's niece, she had come to this city for a fresh start, afraid of being dragged into a corruption scandal spreading through Kazimierz.

blocks.cap: The midday street where the two first met.

blocks.x: That evening, at a welcome dinner, Czarek produces a shelf display contract. For the term of the contract, retailers may display only Golden Prairie products. The **New Urban Management Act** doesn't forbid it, he says, so there's no problem.

Tosia knows what that contract will bring. The girl she met that afternoon will no longer be able to sell wine anywhere. Even so, when she runs into the girl again that night, she turns down her plea to be taught, saying she can't afford to help a competitor.

She gave in at a bridge railing. She grabbed the girl, thinking she was about to jump, but Bettina was only trying to reach a puppy on the other side of the railing. In the middle of it all, Tosia blurted out that she would teach her, and could not take it back.

But once out on the street, Bettina can't use the lines she's been taught. She can't sell to someone with words she doesn't understand, she said, because her grandfather taught her that you have to be sincere with people for a deal to be a good one, built on trust.
Tosia says flatly that sincerity is worth nothing when there's profit and loss on the line, and ties a ribbon on a bottle to show her how it's done.
The tired-looking man who bought that wine had known 'Verdi' from the start. Long ago he had turned his back on his family and left for Columbia, and now he was on his way back to them.
It was the only wine that ever made it onto a poor family's table, he said. His father never tired of it no matter how much he drank. Surely, for the sake of this wine, they would open the door.
Soon after, a young man planning to open a restaurant in Victoria comes looking for Bettina. Tosia tells her she has graduated. Forget everything I taught you, she says, and do it your own way.

A week later, at a gathering to congratulate her on landing so many display contracts, Tosia shows up with a brown soda called 'Chinotto'. At Bettina's birthday party she had learned of a shop that still sells it. It was the drink her father used to bring back from business trips to Siracusa.
It would be a shame, she says, if 'old things' like this really disappeared, and she clinks the soda bottle lightly against her uncle's wine glass.
3. Verdi 1092

Around that time, **Lupina**, third-generation heir to the Verdi Winery, has decided to sell it to Golden Prairie at a price that was hard to refuse. **Elio**, who buys grapes from her for Saluzzo Vino, picks up on it.
But **Niccolo**, an old hand who has tended the vines all his life, objects. The trees here have lived longer than everyone's ages put together, he says. Caring for vines is like raising a family.

Lupina replies that rather than limp along in disgrace, she would sooner say a graceful goodbye while it is still worth something. This is Nuova Volsinii, she says, and they have to accept the new order.
Late at night, she visits Demetri's small private bar, sits at the drum kit in the corner, and sings a song every Siracusan child knows. The original was too sad, she said, so she rearranged it.
If I should fall in battle, bury me with a single florin. Make my mother's weeping into wine, and pour it on my grave...

She asks whether Saluzzo's wineries could take on the skilled workers she is leaving behind, and Demetri agrees. Looking after one's own family is only natural, he says. And you? Lupina says she is better on the drums than at running a winery, so she will chase her dream of music.

blocks.cap: A small building down an alley: Demetri's private bar.

blocks.x: The next day, just before a Kazimierzian auditor arrives to check the inventory of assets, the handle falls off the press and a crack turns up in the filtration system's cylinder. Lupina pleads that the equipment may be old, but it can be fixed in no time.
The auditor is unmoved. Traditional Siracusan equipment was never part of the valuation, and they don't use handmade oak barrels. What they want is the land.
