The remaining stock had already gone to Golden Prairie last month to cover the workers' wages. Once the auditor leaves, Niccolo confesses. He broke all the equipment himself, and Elio tampered with the water pipes too.

Lupina does not blame them. Her grandfather used to measure her height against that press when she was little, and the lines are still on the hopper. Since it's broken, it won't be sold off, she says. Maybe that's for the better.

blocks.cap: Once bustling, the Verdi Winery now holds only silence.

blocks.x: Niccolo asks her to come to his granddaughter Bettina's tenth birthday. In keeping with Siracusan tradition, with a bottle as old as the child.

Some time later, when Demetri, under house arrest over Paola's case, leaves only a message asking her to stop by the bar, Lupina mixes a cocktail alone in the empty bar and remembers her grandfather drawing.
The big wolf was her grandfather; the little wolf was Lupina. He once said this to his granddaughter as she swung his brush around like a drumstick.
Lupa, I want you to be the heir to the winery, and I want you to be free to become a musician too. A family isn't something that makes you give up your dreams.
"Sorry, Grandpa. I couldn't keep a single bottle from this year."

On the drum stool where she always sat lay a gift box tied with a ribbon. On the label: grapevines, two wolves, one large and one small, and two clumsily drawn drumsticks by the small wolf's ear. Beneath them, **'Verdi 1092'**.
Lupina puts the bottle back in the box and picks up her sticks. The song rings through the bar once more.
4. Kindness With a Hidden Price

Meanwhile, **Eirene**, who brought the Truckers' Union into the city government to form the **Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti** (AST) and became its director, had partnered with foreign merchant houses to steer clear of the famiglie, and the shipping contracts earned the drivers good money.

But as the penalty clauses began to tighten around the drivers, kindness from Saluzzo Vino seeped in through the gap. Wine sent as a housewarming gift for a driver's cousin. A shop handed over. A helping hand from someone who knew troubles no one had spoken of.
Eirene warns them. Even small favors like that are debts, and one day you repay them at a far higher price than you expect. Don't forget what happened two years ago.
The AST's drivers have no need for kindness from outsiders that comes with a hidden price.

blocks.cap: The truck camp where the AST's drivers gather.

blocks.x: Then she goes to the Kazimierzian representative to challenge the unreasonable clauses, and the representative answers that past breach records will be 'put on hold'. Eirene adds up the agency's funds, even her own savings, then tells the drivers they no longer need to worry about penalties.

The night before the championship, **Sam**, a driver just back on his feet after being sick in bed, gets a call from **Tommaso** of Saluzzo Vino. Told that an entry wine was left off the list, Sam readily takes the delivery and gets on his motorbike.

Just short of the venue, Sam comes upon an overturned truck. The driver pinned underneath was his colleague Gianni, and the cargo bed held Golden Prairie's wine for the final. Tommaso was at the scene too.

The next day, the Saluzzo side offers to pay Gianni's medical bills and the cost of the wine. The Kazimierzian chamber of commerce said it would not hold any individual responsible, but it attached a condition: schedules and routes must follow their system.

That night the poisoning happens, and the representative changes his tune. A delivery carrying the suspect's wine ruined Golden Prairie's cargo, so any losses insurance can't cover must be borne by the party responsible.

Faced with damages larger than anything he has seen in his life, Sam turns on Eirene. If she hadn't signed with those foreigners, Gianni wouldn't be lying in a hospital. If she can't fix this, he'll hear out the man the Bellone Family sent.

Eirene meant to say 'No', as she always had, but though her mouth opened, no words came. Meanwhile, one by one, the drivers were gathering around the brochures the Kazimierzian representative was handing out.

At dusk, Eirene drives a truck for the first time in a long while and heads for the courthouse, and with the truck parked in the square out front, she rehearses what she will say to Judge **Lavinia**.
"Lavinia, I'm out of options..." The rest never left her mouth.

blocks.cap: The courthouse square at night, rain drumming on the windshield.

blocks.x: 5. The Tall Horns

Paola's adopted daughter **Liesel** has always handled the orchestra's schedule and day-to-day affairs. Just before the performance that day, she passed a hooded figure in the cellar. She took them for a lost guest.

After the incident, Czarek makes a point of calling Liesel in to tell her the contract won't be renewed. All remaining performances are canceled, and she is shown the clause: if the engagement is halted by force majeure, no balance is paid.

When she returns to the rehearsal room, the members greet her with red eyes. **Timpani**, the percussionist Paola brought in from driving piles at the docks, and Bassoon and Trombone. As Liesel leaves the room, voices follow her out: blame for the Bellone Family for killing Paola, and talk of leaving the city.
Liesel goes into Paola's room. Her mother had forgotten to close the window, leaving the sheet music soaked with rain, and the tears she held back in front of the members finally break loose.

blocks.cap: Paola's room, where a half-altered stage costume and her staff remain.

blocks.x: Trombone, Bassoon, Timpani: each was someone Paola took in as family, one at a time. Asked why she left Leithanien, Paola said she didn't know herself. All she wanted was to play the music she loved. Why wouldn't her own people accept that?
Through her blurred vision, the lights of passing cars slide by. Light bent through a glass. Liesel's hand stops.
That day in the cellar, the figure had been holding a glass, and tall horns rose above the hood. Not a Lupo. A Caprinae.

Apart from a few, every member of the orchestra was a Caprinae. Her mother had taught her that the truth, even when it hurts someone, is warm like a flame. But what if that flame burned this family down?

That night, a call comes: Timpani and Bassoon got caught up in a fight outside the Bellone Family's hotel and are in a holding cell. All the way to the police station, those horns stay in Liesel's head. **Liesel hated herself for doubting her family.**

At the police station, it turns out the two had come to blows trying to stop Columbian merchants who were harassing the hotel staff. Liesel remembers her mother on the day they brought Timpani home from the docks, handing over the whole week's food money.
Liesel bursts out laughing. Everyone in her family is a fool, she says. And she, for doubting them, is the biggest fool in the world.

She asks Timpani to beat out a rhythm and, as her mother used to, straightens her back and smooths her collar. Then she apologizes to the Columbian merchant and makes him an offer. The orchestra will play for free at the opening of the shopping mall he invested in, and she herself will conduct.
I'm my Mama's daughter. I'm Liesel Memminger of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra.

Then, on the stage at the shopping mall's opening, the orchestra wins applause with an untitled quartet Paola left behind. Backstage, Liesel tells the members. She saw the person who killed her mother that day. It wasn't a Lupo. It was a Caprinae.

blocks.cap: The dressing room after the show, full of the members' excited voices.

blocks.x: 6. Case No. 01452

Long ago, when Leontuzzo was heir to the Bellone Family, Demetri taught him something. Their neighbor Elio, who had sold his fruit shop over his daughter's illness and was behind on rent, got breathing room just because Leontuzzo showed his face. Help given at the right moment becomes a debt, Demetri said, and debts come in handy someday.

Leontuzzo pushed back. Wasn't introducing Elio to a doctor simply about wanting to help? Demetri answered that he could only do as much as he was able, and that the oranges at Signor Elio's shop had always been the best.

Now Czarek comes to the mayor and presses him to punish the murderer by the law. The merchants of the **General Chamber of Commerce** chose this city because it had no famiglie, he says. Isn't that what the mayor promised?

After Czarek leaves, Lavinia and Leontuzzo see something else. Exclusive display contracts. Shipping contracts that squeeze drivers with penalties. Encroachment spreading into energy and medicine. Local shops closing, and prices rising.

Lavinia puts forward an amendment to the New Urban Management Act. It would place tariffs on foreign goods and bring in the old famiglia powers to protect key sectors. Leontuzzo hesitates, calling it a step against the times.

Lavinia is calm. This city government's authority rests on **Signora Sicilia**'s temporary permission, she says, and in Siracusa today, only the famiglie can still bind people together. A chance to win people over will come before long.

blocks.cap: Leontuzzo reads the two-page amendment again and again.

blocks.x: That afternoon, the courtroom is packed with spectators. Under questioning, it comes out that at the accident scene, Tommaso put Saluzzo's wine into Golden Prairie's crate and took Golden Prairie's wine out. The forensic pathologist testifies that the poison came not from the wine, but from the glass.

On the witness stand, Liesel describes the person she saw in the cellar. They seemed to be disguised as an orchestra member, and had large Caprinae horns on their head. Then she establishes the members' alibis one by one.
Elio, called next, admits that he wrecked Verdi's equipment together with Niccolo, and damaged the water supply and drainage on his own. No one ordered him to, he said.

Elio testifies that Golden Prairie shut down the wineries it had bought before and left the vineyards abandoned. The labor poured into the vines, the lives and memories held in astringent traditional wine. None of it meant anything to them.

blocks.cap: From longtime locals to foreign merchants, the eyes of the whole city are on the courtroom.

blocks.x: As the gallery stirs, Demetri speaks. Since the offense was committed by his employee, he says, he as the employer will take the penalty in their place, whether a fine or prison.

In the commotion as the verdict is postponed by a few days, Demetri presses his index and middle fingers together, points them at Leontuzzo, then back at himself. It was the signal the two had used since they were kids: let's meet and talk.
Leontuzzo does not respond, and goes to see Elio in detention. Elio says Judge Lavinia gave him the chance to explain himself in court.
And he said the reason he stayed under Demetri is that Demetri still keeps the famiglia's founding creed. Gather the powerless together, so that no one is swallowed by something bigger.
7. The Don's Chair

Meanwhile, Demetri, cleared of the murder charge, receives a visit from Czarek. The proposal, carrying the will of the General Chamber of Commerce, is to let Golden Prairie invest in Saluzzo Vino. Demetri asks him in turn whether he thought he would refuse.
On a night when the rain that fell all day has thinned, Leontuzzo goes to the Bellone estate.

blocks.cap: The chair only the don may sit in. Demetri does not rise to greet him.

blocks.x: As the famiglia's old rules dictate, Demetri sat in that chair, watching him. Leontuzzo realizes it has been a long time since he truly saw Demetri's expression.
Demetri says he has decided to work with Czarek. And that he knows an unsigned amendment is sitting on Leontuzzo's desk.

Just before the championship, he says, a piece of information came into his hands. Someone had been sent from Leithanien to eliminate the exile Paola Memminger. The one called the 'Eternal Grace' will not tolerate any voice that fails to sing their praises, even outside the country.
**"I didn't encourage it. I simply let it happen."** Because of it, there was now a reason to put forward the amendment, and Lavinia, he says, must have prepared the trial with exactly that in mind.

The first famiglie were nothing more than powerless people banding together in a barren Siracusa, Demetri says. After the don died and Leontuzzo left, he took the **Bellone Family** on his shoulders because he could not let its people become people with nowhere to go.
Siracusans take care of their own. That is our tradition, and it is what I have always done.

Leontuzzo asks him to come to City Hall and be his right hand, and Demetri refuses once more. Asked whether he has been to see Signora Sicilia, he says only that she enjoys meeting ambitious young people.
Your rules will be the standard that restrains the famiglie, and my way will be the force that binds Siracusans together. That, Demetri says, is this city's new 'Guns and Order'.
As Leontuzzo gets up to leave, Demetri holds out his hand. The two had once walked arm in arm, laughing and talking. This was the first time they had ever shaken hands formally.
Letting go, Demetri returned to that chair. Like Leontuzzo's father, like every famiglia don in Siracusa, he vanished into the dark.
The rain had stopped.
Epilogue
Then Leontuzzo asks Lavinia whether that amendment doesn't gall her. Both of them had wanted to erase every trace of the famiglie from Siracusa.
I spent more than ten years under the Bellone Family's protection, Leon. Waiting a little longer doesn't bother me.
"...The same goes for me."

blocks.cap: After the rain, the sky was unexpectedly clear and still.

blocks.x: Nuova Volsinii, founded as a city without famiglie, was a Siracusan city after all. The things that had never changed had come into this new world, and were making another kind of order.

act54side.tagline: A Sankta who insists on a funeral full of laughter and a Liberi determined to protect a place for grief prepare one woman's funeral together in Laterano, a city whose god has died. Beside them, young people from another world look up at a full moon that never sets.

chars.name: Makoto Yuki
chars.desc: Leader of S.E.E.S., the Specialized Extracurricular Execution Squad. Says little and decides quickly.

chars.name: Yukari Takeba
chars.desc: A bow-wielding member of S.E.E.S. Frank, and quick to take the lead.

chars.name: Fuuka Yamagishi
chars.desc: S.E.E.S.'s rear support. Senses presences with her Persona, Juno.

chars.name: Ken Amada
chars.desc: The youngest member of S.E.E.S. Calmer than others his age, and a meticulous observer.

chars.name: Aigis
chars.desc: S.E.E.S.'s robot member. Speaks with literal-minded directness.

chars.name: Koromaru
chars.desc: S.E.E.S.'s white dog. Tracks down his friends by scent.

chars.name: Giulio
chars.desc: A Sankta party designer. Laughs easily and talks fast. Back from Columbia.

chars.name: Giada
chars.desc: A Liberi funeral planner. The first Liberi funeral planner in Laterano.

chars.name: Doctor
chars.desc: Homeroom teacher at San Marso Comprehensive School. Always wears a hood.

chars.name: Amiya
chars.desc: Class rep of Makoto's class. Makes a Q&A booklet for transfer students by hand.

chars.name: Vivetta
chars.desc: Giulio's distant aunt. Left a will twenty years ago.

chars.name: Kayla
chars.desc: Steward of the Confectionery Hall. Loves madeleines most of all.

chars.name: Idida
chars.desc: A neighborhood ice cream maker who makes sugar-free ice cream.

chars.name: Rhea
chars.desc: A cleric who keeps guard at the Ecclesia Requietum. Formerly of the Guard.

chars.name: Felice
chars.desc: An elderly Liberi, Vivetta's former lover. He was once an Executor.

terms.name: Laterano
terms.desc: Holy city of the Sankta, and a nomadic city. Long called a miracle upon the earth.

terms.name: Sankta
terms.desc: A race with halos above their heads. The people of Laterano.

terms.name: Liberi
terms.desc: A race with feathered wings. They have lived in Laterano alongside the Sankta since long ago.

terms.name: Empathy
terms.desc: The ability by which the Sankta felt one another's emotions directly. It linked them through their halos.

terms.name: the Law
terms.desc: The god of Laterano. Now called 'the Holy Relic.'

terms.name: the Cataclysm
terms.desc: The great upheaval that struck Laterano last autumn.

terms.name: Fallen
terms.desc: The state of a Sankta who has lost their standing as a Sankta.

terms.name: Guardian Gun
terms.desc: A real gun every Sankta receives at the age of twelve. Carried for the rest of their life.

terms.name: Requietum Funeral Home
terms.desc: Laterano's first cremation facility. Not yet officially open.

terms.name: Ecclesia Requietum
terms.desc: The institution that has handled funerals and cemeteries in each district of Laterano. Centered on burial.

terms.name: Executor
terms.desc: Laterano's law enforcers. They also handle Notarial Hall business.

terms.name: Mobile Confessional
terms.desc: An autonomous Lateran vehicle carrying a confessional booth. It talks.

terms.name: Persona
terms.desc: The 'other self' within one's heart. It can be summoned to fight.

terms.name: Shadow
terms.desc: Monsters that devour the human psyche. They exist in the world of S.E.E.S.

terms.name: Dark Hour
terms.desc: A 'time outside of time' that comes every midnight. Ordinary people don't notice it.

terms.name: Tartarus
terms.desc: The place S.E.E.S. enters to investigate Shadows.

terms.name: Apathy Syndrome
terms.desc: A condition in which people attacked by Shadows become lifeless shells. Mistaken for an illness.

terms.name: S.E.E.S.
terms.desc: The Specialized Extracurricular Execution Squad, which investigates the Dark Hour and Shadows.

blocks.x: On a night when moonlight falls through the window and settles in layers like ice, someone sips a sweet liquor they got for free, and a song lingers in their ears. It is a song about passing through the salt flats of Iberia, the sands of Sargon, and the spring of Ursus, and at last reaching one city.
Nowhere compares to Laterano. Sugar, guns, and faith... I drink Laterano down in one gulp.
Laterano is the holy city of the Sankta. Here, an explosion is a shop's members-only event, and gunfire is part of everyday street life.
And not long ago, this city lost something.
Choosing a Coffin, and a Boy from a Gift Box

Party designer **Giulio** came back to Laterano from Columbia, all but dragged there by a will his distant aunt **Vivetta** had registered twenty years earlier. It asked that a party be held at her funeral, and the Notarial Hall enforced it.
The funeral was in the hands of **Giada**, a Liberi funeral planner. It was the first funeral she had been given to handle alone, and to her, the party was only an addition to the funeral.

The coffins Giulio proposed were a four-wheel-drive car that a twelve-year-old could drive, a life-size Cupcake Kid statue that could be made to dance by remote control, and a transparent airtight container fitted with a cooling module. Giada rejected them one by one and pointed to a coffin shaped like a chocolate cookie, with no features at all.
Just then, the cake-shaped gift box in the corner of the preparation room moved. Giulio had ordered it in advance for the guests' entrance. The lid slid aside, and a hand reached out from inside.

blocks.cap: The preparation room where they were choosing a coffin. A hand reached out of the gift box.

blocks.x: The boy who rose from the box gave his name as **Makoto Yuki**, but all he knew was that this was not 'Tartarus,' and that he could understand a language he had never heard before.

Because foreigners without identification are deported within three days, Giulio registered Makoto at the Notarial Hall as his relative, on the condition that Makoto help him choose the coffin. Then, under the rule that minors must attend school, Makoto enrolled that same day at San Marso Comprehensive School, where Giulio and Giada had both studied.

The Executor handling the registration asked in passing: twenty years ago, when the will was registered, Giulio would have been six, so why had the deceased named him of all people? Giulio answered that he didn't remember.
The Drunk Who Walked Through a Shadow

At the school he entered this way, the homeroom teacher was the hooded **Doctor**, and the class rep was **Amiya**. To buy time to search for his friends, Makoto listed funeral planner, party designer at the funeral home, and salesclerk at the Confectionery Hall, in that order, on his vocational placement form.
That evening, a grey dog ran straight at Makoto from across the street. It was **Koromaru**, who had followed his scent, with the youngest member, **Ken Amada**, panting along behind.

blocks.cap: Koromaru, who found his leader by scent alone.

blocks.x: They were S.E.E.S., the Specialized Extracurricular Execution Squad, which investigates the 'Dark Hour' that arrives every midnight and the monsters called 'Shadows.' Their memories cut off after they approached a door that had suddenly appeared on the first floor of Tartarus, and though they had all gone through the same door, each of them woke in a different place at a different time. The friends still missing were **Yukari Takeba**, **Fuuka Yamagishi**, and **Aigis**.

That night, midnight passed and the clocks did not stop. Laterano had no Dark Hour. Yet Koromaru barked at the window, and when they followed him, they found one section of the streets where the colors were warped, just as in the Dark Hour.

blocks.cap: A warped night street. Yukari was facing a Shadow alone.

blocks.x: Right after they scattered the Shadow that had been after Yukari, a drunk Sankta walked out of an alley, singing. Makoto knocked Yukari's arrow aside, but the man walked straight into the Shadow.

blocks.cap: The drunk who walked through a Shadow. Only the halo above his head grew dark.

blocks.x: As if he saw nothing, the man passed through the Shadow and staggered on, unhurt. But the halo above his head grew steadily darker, and the Shadow seemed to stand still behind him, watching him go.
The song he had been singing went like this: 'Save me, I can't face this life alone.'
The swarming Shadows were cleared only after Fuuka arrived, providing support with her Persona, Juno. On the street, once the anomaly had lifted, the man lay curled up, asleep.
You Have Already Changed

The next day, Yukari and Fuuka joined the same class, and Makoto told the Doctor everything: that they had come from another world, that Shadows had appeared in Laterano, and that they could not simply stand by.

blocks.cap: "Tell me." The Doctor showed no surprise.

blocks.x: The Doctor proposed tracking the Shadows' movements to work backward to where the door was, and came along on that night's investigation in person. That was how they confirmed that the people of Laterano cannot see Shadows.

Around then, Giulio heard from Giada about the funeral of a comic actor she had once handled. When the deceased's colleagues reenacted his best-known routine, the mourners laughed, and his wife ran up onto the stage, crying, and begged them to stop.

When Giada called everyone over to the coffin and asked each of them to choose a dessert and lay it out for the deceased, his wife set down a meringue, and a colleague a raspberry cookie. All she had done, she said, was understand how unbearable it is when no one even knows what they should do.

When Giulio said that Lateran funerals had always been places where people laughed out loud, Giada replied that the Sankta of the past had been 'understood' even when they made a commotion at a funeral, because their feelings reached one another before anything else.
You have already changed. All of us have already changed.
Then she added: Giulio had never been able to feel her heart to begin with, since she was a Liberi, and she could do her job well without either of them 'reading' the other.

The next morning there was a firearms class at school. Makoto's stance was flawless, but at the stage of 'feeling' the Originium circuits inside the gun and its rounds, he could not pull the trigger. That is usually how it goes for anyone who isn't a Sankta, said the teacher, Carla.

blocks.cap: Makoto learning to hold a gun. His stance was flawless, but the gun did not respond.

blocks.x: Carla voiced a different worry: the seventh-graders who had first picked up guns this year were progressing noticeably slower than in past years. As the class was ending, Amiya said that if the gunfire on the streets ever disappeared entirely, that would be more frightening.
Ice Cream Without Sugar

blocks.cap: Aigis striking down a swarm of Shadows from above a smokescreen.

blocks.x: That night, the one driving back a swarm of Shadows at the shooting range was Aigis, the last of their friends. Once she had joined them, she looked at the creatures and trailed off: 'Shadows? No, these are——'

The next day's vocational placement began at the Confectionery Hall, a market that sells nothing but desserts. There, **Idida**, an ice cream maker from next door, was pestering the hall's steward, **Kayla**, for a stall to sell homemade sugar-free ice cream.
When Kayla turned it down, saying sugar holds up the structure of ice cream, Idida shot back:
If Laterano can do without a god, why can't ice cream do without sugar?

Kayla set up a sales contest, with Idida taking the stall's ordinary ice cream and Makoto the sugar-free one. Idida lectured customers on the harms of sugar, while Makoto, asked what was special about his, answered only, 'It's healthy.'

blocks.cap: Idida and Makoto standing side by side at a Confectionery Hall stall.

blocks.x: The sugar-free ice cream was bought up in full by an out-of-town customer who said they wanted to know the Laterano of today, but the regular ice cream sold just as much, and the contest ended in a draw.

Kayla told them about the day she received her Guardian Gun and fired live rounds for the first time, so dizzy she thought she would die, and the madeleine her mother handed her. However great the upheaval, she said, as long as that memory remained, the lives of the Lateran people would not change easily. No one should pretend not to see what people love right now.

Then Makoto held out some ice cream he had set aside, and after one bite, Kayla noticed that, unlike at the earlier tasting, it had the faintest sweetness. It was a sugar-free sweetener Idida had gone to great lengths to bring in from abroad, and Kayla said they should talk about renting out the stall.

That night, following Aigis's words, the group decided to call the creatures 'monsters' to set them apart from Shadows. It seemed that a full moon had hung in the sky over the areas where the monsters appeared every night since the first day of their investigation. And what Koromaru chased down was a monster shaped like a Mobile Confessional, with legs in place of wheels.

blocks.cap: A monster in the shape of a Mobile Confessional. It took the form of something found only in Laterano.

blocks.x: The Death Certificate

On the day of the funeral home placement, Giada began her explanation by saying she would not soften anything for the sake of feelings. This was Laterano's first Requietum Funeral Home, and it would be the first step toward properly spreading cremation in a nomadic city where burial had always been the norm. It would open officially after its first funeral, which was Vivetta's.
Giada added that more and more people had recently been dying without a will, putting a heavy strain on the Ecclesia Requietum's system.
Giulio chimed in about Columbia's culture of cremation, and mentioned that when he came home, his father's urn had been in his luggage. It was the first Giada had heard of it.

Giulio wanted to cut the cremation viewing and bone collection that Giada had scheduled, and put in a karaoke relay instead. When Giada remarked sarcastically that he might as well pack the ashes into a salute cannon and have the guests fire them into the sky, Giulio was genuinely impressed.
Giada asked, her face worn out: why don't you ever get angry?

Meanwhile, Yukari, who had been carrying documents away to leave the two of them alone, stopped in her tracks. The photo on a newly arrived death certificate was of the drunk who had walked through the Shadow on the first night.

That evening, Yukari murmured that even people with Apathy Syndrome don't die this fast, but since no cause of death was written on the certificate, Aigis said they could not conclude it was the monsters' doing. When the Doctor came running, Fuuka confided that during the fights, the monsters had seemed more drawn to the people of Laterano than to them.

The Doctor said that this was a fragile city, and that Laterano was waking from a dream. It had lost its old answers and had yet to find even its new questions, so if they wanted to understand, they should look for the answers among the people of Laterano themselves.
A Ring Made of Blocks
The next morning, when Makoto asked Giada what had happened to Laterano, she handed him a doughnut on the way to buy coffee. It was shaped like a ring of linked blocks.
It was Laterano's god. Its name was 'the Law,' and now it is called 'the Holy Relic.' **The god died last autumn.**

Giada learned of the god's death in the same moment she first learned it existed. Since then, 'Empathy,' which let the Sankta share one another's hearts through their halos, has been cut off, and most Sankta can no longer feel the emotions of the other Sankta beside them.

Giada said the true tradition of the Sankta had never been 'joy.' They had been able to do as their hearts led at funerals only because one person's grief was everyone's grief. The emotion the Sankta had barely known was 'embarrassment,' and now they had lost that good fortune.

Giulio, arriving late, said: I really like you, and I don't want us to keep on like enemies. I can't read your face, so couldn't you just tell me directly? Giada closed her eyes as if she could not bear it, rested a hand on his shoulder for a moment, then took it away.
"That's the kind of person you are."

After Giada went ahead to get ready, Giulio told Makoto about his father. He had studied jokes and magic tricks to make his anxious father laugh, and thanks to Empathy he could feel his father's mood really lift. He guessed his aunt had named him because, as a child, he had been good at making people happy.
We've already lost so much. If on top of that we're crushed under grief and can't climb out, that isn't Laterano.
I'm Lateran Too
That day, Giada brought Vivetta's remains into the preparation room, and Makoto looked at the face of the deceased, whom he had never met. It was not a face that looked asleep.
After two hands have tucked and smoothed it, the look a face settles into once life is gone. That was the look of death.

Giada hesitated over whether to make up the deceased's face. Giulio asked how anyone could go to a party without makeup. Giada answered that the dead do not need makeup; it is the living who need it. Giulio asked for Makoto's opinion, but Makoto did not answer.

That night, Fuuka sensed the presence of a very powerful monster, and they tracked it to the funeral home, where the presence vanished. The only one who came out of the building's shadow was Giada, hastily stubbing out a cigarette.
Giada said she had fought with Giulio again, and this time he had won. She had been using this funeral, she said.

In that argument, Giulio had said she was trying to turn Vivetta's funeral into an experiment, or a declaration. When Giada said no one could speak for the wishes of the deceased, he countered that his aunt's will was exactly the wish she had left in her own words. And he asked whether Giada had ever exchanged even a single word with Vivetta while she was alive.

Giada admitted she had avoided the will not because it was outdated, but because it was inconvenient for her. The Liberi had come to this holy city generations ago to learn the ways of angels, and the holy city had blessed the Liberi all along. But who will bless us from now on, she asked.
If I can change this place too, wouldn't that finally prove that it's my home as well?

blocks.cap: Giada, turning away as if she realized she had said too much. She walked off in the opposite direction from the funeral home.

blocks.x: As Fuuka watched her figure recede, the thought that the two would make up if only they talked things through scattered without a sound. Had they come a little earlier, to the Laterano where hearts still reached each other, would they have met no lonely people here?
Perhaps she already knew the answer.
The Child Outside the Fence

On the day before the funeral, Giada did not come to work, and Giulio asked the kids who came by to tell her, if they saw her, that he was grateful she had finished preparing the deceased, and that he would keep waiting here.

On the day of the Cataclysm, he had been at a party abroad. The moment the halos broke, the children singing along to the birthday song all screamed at once, and after that the work dried up. Vivetta's funeral was the first job he had been given since last autumn.
It isn't true that precious things never come back once they're gone... Don't deny them before you've even tried to hold on.

Later, meeting the kids at the Confectionery Hall, the Doctor explained that when a Sankta's halo darkens, in mild cases it means their mood has sunk, and in serious ones it means becoming 'Fallen,' losing their standing as a Sankta. The Doctor then shared a personal guess about what the monsters had been born from.
Around then, Giada sat at the Ecclesia Requietum with **Rhea**, a cleric who had once served in the Guard, and for the first time told Rhea about her grandmother's funeral.

Long ago, a giant balloon figure printed with a caricature of her grandfather had stood behind her grandmother's coffin, swaying nonstop to dance music. Giada, who had just started middle school, slipped out through a tear in the cemetery fence, but not knowing where to go, she stood leaning against the fence.
A member of the Guard passing by brought her back to the funeral, and the dance music stopped. To the girl shouting that her grandmother was dead and knew nothing, the guard said:
Yes. But you're going to miss your grandmother very much. That's something you'll come to know for yourself.
With an apology, the guard laid her hand on the coffin. The coffin was not as cold as she had thought.

Making sure no one at a funeral ever again wanted to slip out past the fence: that was why she had become a funeral planner. But she had forgotten, Giada said, that she was the only one who crossed the fence that day. She had only ever been doing it for herself.
A Will Made for Fun

On the day of the funeral, on the roof of the funeral home, Giulio met **Felice**, an elderly Liberi said to be Vivetta's former lover. Twenty years earlier, as an Executor, he had been present on the day Vivetta came to register her will, holding little Giulio's hand.

That day, Vivetta had slipped away from a funeral and run into six-year-old Giulio. The boy suffered from an Empathy developmental disorder that made him take in other people's feelings far too strongly, and he said he had been happy, then sad, then wanted to run, and had slipped out because he was exhausted.

When the boy said he liked everyone, Vivetta told him it only meant something if everyone liked him, and that if he made people happy, maybe they would. When he asked what he could do to make her happy, she answered: when I grow old and die, throw a tremendous party at my funeral.
That was how the will was decided: for fun.
In January this year, Felice went to see Vivetta, but she did not open the door. She said she could not understand a single word he was saying, and at the end she asked through the door:
Felice, is this my punishment? Because I was always just testing the waters, and never cherished a thing. Is that why, this time, once I close my eyes, I'll never be able to open them again...?
Felice fell silent, saying he could say no more, for the sake of Vivetta's honor. Just then Giada arrived, and Giulio asked: how did Vivetta die?
Giada answered. **"She took her own life. With her own Guardian Gun."**
Giulio's father's last days came back to him. His father, weaker still after the Cataclysm. A stranger in the hospital garden who traced Sarkaz horns above his own head and sneered.
In their last idle conversation, his father asked where people who had killed their own people go after they die. Then he covered his son's eyes tightly and said, 'Giulio, come with me.'
Not long after, his father died.
No Second Death at This Funeral

Giulio understood why Giada had not told him sooner. It was because she had not wanted to wield that dishonorable fact as a weapon against the person she was arguing with. The one who had never once seen the deceased was not Giada, but himself.
He told Giada she had been right, and asked her to take the kids out. To the kids who offered to help, he made only one last request: don't look at me.

blocks.cap: On the roof of the funeral home, Giulio turns a gun on himself.

blocks.x: He said he wished he had understood Giada's words, 'we have all already changed,' a little sooner. The joy and pride he had felt on returning to Laterano had become pain and shame, and he asked over and over how long we had been deceiving ourselves.
The swindler is always the last to wake from the swindle. Our lives are already over, for good.
A 'full moon' descended on the rooftop in broad daylight. A giant monster bent down, embraced Giulio, and pressed him into its own body. It was a gesture that could almost be called tender.

blocks.cap: The monster embracing Giulio. The 'full moon' above it resembled the halo of a holy statue.

blocks.x: The Doctor's guess proved true: the monsters were psychic forms born from the hearts of the Lateran people, and the cause of death of those they touched was their very essence.
It is nothing more than a wish that has congealed. A will to die, congealed.
This time Giada and the guests could see it too. Makoto asked Giada to keep everyone away, and turned to his friends.
We have to get Giulio out, no matter what... There will be no second death at this funeral.

blocks.cap: S.E.E.S., move out.

blocks.x: Life Doesn't End
At the end of the fight, the monster flung Giulio away and melted into the shade. As Giulio coughed and groped along the floor, Aigis kicked the gun away from beside his hand.
Giulio said he should have gone with his father, but he had been scared. It would always be like this, he said; why wouldn't they let him end it?

Giada said she wanted to throw it back at him: then should every Liberi, everyone who isn't a Sankta, have died long ago? But there was already enough pain here. She kicked off her shoes, sat down beside him, and asked if he wanted to lean on her.

To Giada, ritual was a language: a way of 'translating' what is hard to put into words into something that can be seen, touched, and lived through. For the Sankta, whose hearts were already connected, ritual had been a dance that came afterward. That was why she had disliked his funerals, which repeated the dances of the past by rote.
And if it is communication, its foremost virtue is honesty. He had not lied. He had not ignored grief; he had wanted to leave joy behind because he missed the past so much, Giada said.

People who aren't Sankta have always lived by fumbling for words and making judgments they could not be sure of. Understanding simply has a price: the effort of trying, the risk of getting it wrong, and staking one's pride.
When Giulio said he might fail again, Makoto told him that was no reason to give up. Not because he believed he would surely succeed, but simply because he did not want to give up.
Life doesn't end... That is both its virtue and its flaw, and you have no choice but to accept it.
The anomalous scene dissolved, and the noise that had been interfering with Fuuka's senses all along began to weaken.
Epilogue — The Door Beneath the Apple Blossoms

The report filed afterward was dry. A phenomenon of forgetting was spreading among the witnesses, and the citizen suicide rate, though slightly down from the previous month, remained far higher than before the Cataclysm.
Under the Law, Giulio met every condition for becoming 'Fallen through attempted suicide.' Yet there was no sign that he had become Fallen, and the record was sealed as classified.

Some time later, at the farewell meal, the bankrupt Giulio picked up the bill. He said he had bought a correspondence course in recognizing emotions. When Makoto said Laterano would get better, Giulio answered that if even a hopeless case like him could try, Laterano would surely save itself.
After the kids left to pack their things, Giulio said he would formally apply to work at the funeral home, and Giada told him frankly that she worried the place would be too heavy a burden for him.
Love is... an effort that never ceases. Being willing to do it, and actually doing it.

And the door they finally found was on the school grounds. At the school on a holiday, with the apple trees in bloom, Amiya said quietly that there were still so many places she had wanted to take them.
The Doctor gave the children a blessing: go and do what you believe in, and never forget that you matter a great deal in many people's hearts.

blocks.cap: Beneath the apple blossoms, the Doctor and Amiya see the children off.

blocks.x: When Makoto reached out, a door appeared in the empty air and glowed red at his touch. He sensed, dimly, that once he crossed it, there would be no more exit back to the world he was leaving behind.

blocks.cap: The door that appeared before the boy's fingertips.

blocks.x: As the children passed through the door and walked out of Tartarus, the white city and the school grounds under the apple blossoms faded from their minds like a dream. Only an echo like someone's voice remained, and its words grew more and more unfamiliar. Only the feeling it carried still seemed faintly recognizable.
Sugar, guns, and faith. The city the song drank down in one gulp has lost the god its faith was turned toward. What remains in its place are words, offered haltingly.

act50side.tagline: The leader of A6 and its resident troublemaker set out to round up desert bandits, and one sandstorm later they're 'Monster Hunters,' chasing after a Sovereign with Popukar's face and a prince of thunder. A story about people who carried everything alone learning to lean on one another.

chars.name: Orchid
chars.desc: A6's squad leader. A caster and former costume designer. A worrier with a habit of long lectures. · Operator Violet Mizutsune Orchid

chars.name: Catapult
chars.desc: A6 member. Lived as a hunter for a while after leaving Kazimierz. Her body moves before her head does. · Operator Zinogre S Catapult

chars.name: Midnight
chars.desc: A6 member. Specializes in gathering intel, and gives his squad leader headaches with his woman troubles. The Mirage Kingdom has a general with the same face and the same name.

chars.name: Spot
chars.desc: A6 member. Never without his comics. Does the bare minimum of whatever he's told.

chars.name: Popukar
chars.desc: A6's youngest. Timid and easily swayed. Believes whatever the squad leader says is right.

chars.name: Baowuga
chars.desc: The young Sovereign of the Mirage Kingdom and shrine maiden of the Sacred Wheel. Has the same face as Popukar. Tries to shoulder everything herself.

chars.name: Banmira
chars.desc: The Mirage Kingdom's finest blacksmith. Has the same face as Spot. Obsessed with inventing, and blows things up at the drop of a hat.

chars.name: Masamune
chars.desc: A talking cat. A member of Kamura Village's Meowcenaries, and the Monster Hunter of the previous Trial.

chars.name: Yoshitsune
chars.desc: A wolf-like fanged beast who travels with Masamune. Never says a word, and has plenty of pride.

terms.name: Mirage Kingdom
terms.desc: A land of hunters ringed by bamboo forests. Not a nomadic city.

terms.name: Sacred Wheel
terms.desc: A colossal steel arch standing atop the snowy mountain. The Mirage Kingdom's sacred national treasure.

terms.name: Trial
terms.desc: The event, once every ten years, when a Monster and Monster Hunters descend together from the Sacred Wheel.

terms.name: Monster
terms.desc: An overwhelmingly powerful beast that descends with every Trial.

terms.name: Monster Hunter
terms.desc: The two outsiders the Sacred Wheel sends with every Trial. They hunt the Monster together with the Sovereign.

terms.name: Curse
terms.desc: A black miasma the Monster brings with it. It drives any beast it touches savage. Only the shrine maiden of the Sacred Wheel can lift it.

terms.name: Lord of Thunder
terms.desc: The Monster that appeared in the Mirage Kingdom ten years ago. It commands lightning and has yet to be hunted.

terms.name: Hunting Corps
terms.desc: A samurai organization General Midnight formed by registering the kingdom's hunters.

terms.name: Curse Fiends
terms.desc: A pack of wolves tainted by the Curse. A taboo said to have destroyed the old Mirage Kingdom.

terms.name: Magma Snail
terms.desc: A beast that lives in the lava fields below the snowy mountain. It looks like an Originium Slug. Its shell is made into firebamboo charcoal.

terms.name: Charge Blade
terms.desc: A hunting weapon whose sword and shield combine into a giant axe.

terms.name: Wirebug
terms.desc: A bug that spins tough ironsilk. Kamura Village hunters use it to move and to fight.

terms.name: Thunderbug
terms.desc: A bug that lives in symbiosis with the Lord of Thunder. Its tail gives off a soft glow.

terms.name: Wyvern Riding
terms.desc: A hunting technique that uses Wirebugs to take control of giant beasts.

terms.name: Kamura Village
terms.desc: Masamune and Yoshitsune's home. A village of hunters.

blocks.x: Rhodes Island A6 squad leader **Orchid** is sighing again today. **Spot** never lets go of his comics, **Midnight** gathers his intel at the bar, the youngest, **Popukar**, answers "Yes!" to anything the leader says, and **Catapult** skips meetings to go look at prey. They say time grinds a team into shape, but this bunch of oddballs only gets more set in their ways every year.
This mission: wipe out a bandit gang in the Sargon desert. But just as the fighting starts, Midnight's comms cut out at "Popukar is..." and a massive sandstorm rolls in.
Orchid and Catapult dive toward a beam of light to find their teammates, and when they come to, they're in the middle of a bamboo forest, which has no business being in Sargon.
1. Through the Sandstorm, and Popukar Is a Sovereign
The comms are dead, but Popukar's voice drifts over from beyond the trees. In Higashi, for some reason.

They run over, and it's Popukar all right. Except she's wearing lavish robes, shouting "Stand down!" at her samurai guards, and insisting her name is **Baowuga**. Apparently she's the young Sovereign of the **Mirage Kingdom**, a land of hunters ringed by bamboo forests.

From the pair's strange clothes and speech, Baowuga is certain they're the **Monster Hunters** she has been looking for, and asks for their help against a pack of beasts charging at them, trailing black miasma. That miasma, she says, is the "Curse," and it drives beasts savage.
The fight is a mess. Orchid's Arts Unit, her umbrella, refuses to work, and Spot falls out of the sky along with a man-carrying kite. Naturally, he insists he's the blacksmith **Banmira**.
The new bomb launcher Banmira so proudly shoulders blows up on the spot. He'd loaded the wrong round, a stink bomb, so beasts and people alike back off holding their noses.

With a sinking feeling, Orchid asks whether they happen to know someone named Midnight. The dashing young man in the portrait Baowuga pulls out has Midnight's exact face, and he turns out to be General Midnight of the Mirage Kingdom, said to be serious, strict, and devoted to nothing but his country.
Orchid's scream echoes through the bamboo forest.
2. A Country Where Prey Falls from the Sky Every Ten Years

Here's how Baowuga explains it. Once every ten years, an overwhelming beast, the "Monster," descends from the **Sacred Wheel**, a colossal steel arch atop the snowy mountain, and spreads the Curse. Two outsiders who come through the same gate, the Monster Hunters, then hunt the Monster together with the Sovereign.

The Mirage Kingdom has lived with this for generations and calls it the "Trial." Once the Monster is slain, the Sacred Wheel opens again and the hunters return home. In short: if you want to go home, hunt first.

But the moment they enter the capital, Baowuga announces the two of them as this Trial's Monster Hunters. The crowd cheers and tosses Orchid into the air, and Orchid, who's always wished Popukar would "stand on her own two feet a little more," gets thoroughly outplayed by that very face.

There was a reason. Ten years ago, the previous Sovereign, Baowuga's mother, went after the Monster that descended back then, the "Lord of Thunder," and vanished mid-hunt. General Midnight, who took charge of the country afterward, organized the hunters into the "Hunting Corps," and has been telling her that to challenge the Lord of Thunder she must wait three more Trials. In other words, thirty more years.
This first Trial is Baowuga's chance to prove herself. Claiming the hunters accepted their calling in the end despite their protests, she recites a passage from the histories.

A 'Monster Hunter' is not one whom the 'Sacred Wheel' chooses. It is one who comes to know their own body, hears their own wishes, looks upon their own courage, takes up their own weapon, and at last embraces their own fate.

Then, while Baowuga is off hunting alone, a "Magma Snail" appears before the two of them, and no matter how you look at it, it's a big Originium Slug. They manage to flatten it under a pile of bamboo, but there's no dodging its fire-spitting counterattack.

blocks.cap: A blue beast steps out of the forest. The bamboo falls as if bowing to a king.

blocks.x: At that moment a giant beast with blue scales, wreathed in lightning, walks out of the forest and finishes the Magma Snail in a single blow. It's the Lord of Thunder. Catapult's shots don't leave a scratch, and the pair barely get away thanks to a stink bomb Orchid had quietly pocketed.
3. There Is No Originium in This Country
Orchid still suspects this might be a giant film set built by some bored Sargon pasha. So the two split up to investigate on their own.

The people of the capital say they've never heard of moving cities, Catastrophes, or Oripathy. And when Orchid finds Banmira in his exploded workshop with shrapnel stuck in him, she notices the stone isn't Originium, and lifts up his shirt just to make sure. Where the crystal beside Spot's belly button should be, there's nothing but healthy fur.

Meanwhile, Catapult sneaks into the palace and watches Baowuga dance before the Magma Snail's carcass, the black miasma flowing into her body like dust into a vacuum cleaner. Unable to bear the pain on her face, Catapult leaps in, only to be blocked by **Masamune**, a cat who ends every sentence with "meow." He's the Monster Hunter from the previous Trial.

Out of ammo, Catapult borrows a sword and shield from Banmira's workshop, and with her opponent coaching her the whole way, realizes it's a "Charge Blade" that combines into an axe. Baowuga calls off the fight and rolls up her sleeve: underneath is an arm as clean as jade, without the crystals Popukar should have.

Meanwhile, Orchid sneaks into a storehouse and runs into the Magma Snail carcass, moving again under the Curse's control. With her Arts out of commission, she holds it off with a fallen guard's bow until General Midnight comes to her rescue, and watching him treat her with impeccable courtesy while wearing that face, Orchid tastes an entirely new kind of suffering.
Now even Orchid admits that there really is no Originium here, and that the only way back is the one Baowuga described.

The general asks one favor. Accept the Trial, but if Her Majesty tries to go after the Lord of Thunder, refuse. Only the shrine maiden can lift the Curse, he says, and the Mirage Kingdom cannot lose another Sovereign.
4. One Set of Gear, One Plate of Dango

Then Masamune, now back on his feet, takes them to the workshop of the Mirage Kingdom's finest blacksmith, which, surprisingly, turns out to be Banmira's. He grumbles that it's too much trouble, but the moment he sees Catapult's launcher he does a complete about-face: let him study this weapon, and he'll make them a full set of gear. Orchid, true to her costume-designer roots, revises the blueprints herself.

Masamune hands them Kamura Village's hunting manual and a "Wirebug," a bug whose tail-spun thread flings your body through the air. Catapult gets carried away, takes off, comes crashing down, and Orchid catches her.
Then Masamune comes clean. The Lord of Thunder's real name is "Zinogre," and he and his partner **Yoshitsune** came to this country chasing it while working for Kamura Village's Meowcenaries.

That evening, as Baowuga and Midnight bristle at each other over who gets to equip the hunters, Orchid declares that they'll accept the Trial but refuse to hunt the Lord of Thunder. She makes it clear that it's her own call, not agreement with the general.

Then, without a word, she mends Baowuga's torn clothes. Watching her, Midnight remembers an afternoon ten years ago, in this same workshop, when the previous Sovereign taught little Baowuga how to swing an axe.
Just then, urgent news arrives: the snowy mountain is heating up.
On the day they set out, the new gear Banmira finished overnight fits perfectly, and somehow even makes them stronger. The reward for this urgent quest: "the way home."

blocks.cap: Blueprints revised by Orchid, gear hammered out overnight by Banmira. Ready to head out.

blocks.x: Masamune and Yoshitsune, a wolf-like fanged beast, come along as guides. Catapult hears "a hunter's feast" and expects meat, but what arrives is "Bunny Dango." Still, once she eats, her whole body heats right up.
5. The Snowy Mountain Boils, and the Gate Home Turns Black

As they climb the snowy mountain, the snow underfoot melts away to reveal black volcanic rock. The Monster has been using the Curse's power to turn the mountain into a volcano. When erupting lava splits the party in two, Baowuga tells them to just keep themselves safe and heads off alone toward the Monster.

The two left behind square off against a Magma Snail, while Masamune and Yoshitsune just fold their arms and call it a hunter qualification exam. Catapult blocks its fire breath with her shield, lands her finishing move, the "Super Amped Element Discharge," and promptly collapses.

blocks.cap: Treating wounds by the campfire. "What does hunting even mean to you?"

blocks.x: When Orchid asks while tending her wounds by the fire, even Catapult, who always deflects with a joke, can't answer this time. And Orchid knows something about herself, too. Just as Yoshitsune sensed, she has been unconsciously avoiding close-quarters combat.

Meanwhile, Baowuga brings down the giant Monster, a Magma Snail, all by herself. But something deep underground pulls at her, and the fallen Monster rises again, revealing a shard of torn space beneath its cracked shell.

blocks.cap: Strike the ground with the axe, soar on a Wirebug. The move Catapult fell for at first sight.

blocks.x: Catapult arrives just in time, soars up on her Wirebug, and drives home another Element Discharge, and the Monster finally breathes its last.

When Baowuga draws in the Curse with her dance, a silver-white gate opens in the Sacred Wheel. But in the blink of an eye the gate turns black, and black, wolf-like beasts pour out of it. The "Curse Fiends," the taboo said to have destroyed the old Mirage Kingdom.
Far off on a cliff, the Lord of Thunder looks down on the scene. As Baowuga screams at it to answer her, the alarm bell rings out: a horde of cursed beasts is heading for the capital.

Catapult wants to take out the leader right away, but Orchid stops her. Only Baowuga can lift the Curse, after all. Baowuga turns back toward the capital, gazing at the thing on the cliff for a long time.
6. The Bait Plan, and the Fallen General

Back in the capital, Midnight proposes a bold plan. Use the Monster's carcass as bait to lure the beasts into the eastern bamboo forest, then blow the ground out from under them with Banmira's explosives and drop them into the hollow below. That hollow is the Lord of Thunder's den, which Baowuga has spent ten years searching for.

When Baowuga says she'll lead the bait herself, the general refuses her command for the first time. He would guard even a humiliating peace with everything he has, he says, and all he has done until now was to pave the way for Her Majesty to kill the Lord of Thunder.
In the end, Catapult and Yoshitsune go with the general, and Orchid stays by Baowuga's side. As the general leaves, Baowuga says, "...Come back alive," and he answers, "I will."

Meanwhile, when Orchid and Baowuga visit his workshop, Banmira confides that he lost his master on the previous Sovereign's expedition. He has kept on inventing in the hope that someday someone would bring down the Lord of Thunder with his weapons, and the only one who always believed in him and encouraged him was Midnight.

In the forest, Catapult holds back the beasts and opens a path for the bait unit. The detonation works, and the whole horde drops into the ground. But the collapse spreads wider than expected, and the general, trying to save his samurai, disappears beyond the falling earth.

Around the same time, in the capital, Baowuga finally speaks what she has kept buried. He was the one who taught her to fight and read to her, the one who took on every thankless task. But whenever the Lord of Thunder comes up, his eyes seem to say, "Go ahead and try. When you fail, you will understand," and she cannot bear it.
Orchid answers that maybe what he fears isn't that she will fail, but that she will succeed. When he gets back, she says, let's all eat together and talk it through.

At the same moment, Catapult finds the general lying on the ground, his armor shattered and his sword broken. Beside him, the Lord of Thunder is giving off a white light, drawing the Curse out of the beasts' carcasses. The very same light as when Baowuga dances.
7. If You're Going to Play the Good Guy, See It Through

Baowuga rushes over and, hearing Catapult's account, believes it killed her mother and stole the shrine maiden's power as well. She kneels beside the general and wipes the blood from his face. She does not shed a single tear.
Then she pins down a charging Magma Snail and purifies it on the spot, and walks to the edge of the sinkhole, saying that all she wants is its life.

**"All of you, stop!"** It is Orchid who takes control. She has the general carried to the castle and a group posted to guard the sinkhole. Then she tells Baowuga she won't ask her to let go of her grudge; but if Baowuga goes down there, they are going down with her. And she asks for paper and a brush, and leaves behind a letter.

Unconscious, the general recalls the last time he saw the previous Sovereign. Ever since he failed to stop her from setting out on that expedition, deep in the Curse's grip and coughing up black blood, he has wanted Her Majesty Baowuga to hate him rather than the Lord of Thunder. He believed that was safer.
But was that really right?

Waking in the castle, the general confesses that what he feared was never Her Majesty's failure. It was her success, the kind she would pay for without hesitation, just as the Sovereign before her did. Then Banmira hands him Orchid's letter.
If you're going to play the good guy, see it through, you coward! ...You weren't wrong. But you weren't right, either.
The letter was asking him: if the previous Sovereign and Baowuga both carried everything alone, how is your way any different from theirs? And what can you do for Baowuga?

The general admits he chose to carry it all himself because he did not trust Her Majesty. Banmira adds that in ten years not a single person has left the Hunting Corps, because everyone knew the general was harshest of all on himself.

Meanwhile, the capital gates have held, defended by "Banmira's Custom Dragonator," a bamboo cannon cart Banmira modeled on Catapult's weapon. Before the gathered samurai, the general, struck by a thought, rises, saying there is something he must tell Her Majesty.
8. The Path the Thunderbugs Lit

Meanwhile, the party descends underground and reaches a subterranean bamboo forest made by the Lord of Thunder. Ten years ago, when a path suddenly opened in this misty forest, all Masamune found at its end was a bloodthirsty beast and a single wisp of black smoke scattering away.

Then something glows at Baowuga's chest. Her mother's last keepsake: a Thunderbug in a jar. When she releases the bug, which had barely glowed in ten years, matching points of light rise all over the forest.

blocks.cap: A sea of bamboo, washed clean of darkness. A rain of light falls.

blocks.x: Beside Orchid, who calls it beautiful, Baowuga says it feels strangely sad. These bugs are said to live in symbiosis with the Lord of Thunder. So why can't they stay by its side?

As the lights trace a path through the mist, her mother's voice rings out, as if the forest itself were speaking. Baowuga chases it alone, cuts a path through the corpses of Curse Fiends, and at the end, hearing the voice say "Become stronger than it. Take it back," she leaps down a waterfall.
Only after she jumped did the voice go on. "Do not follow in my footsteps... Use the power of the Lord of Thunder..." Orchid senses that the truth may be something else.

On an altar at the heart of the ruins, Baowuga is resonating her shrine maiden's power with her mother's power, still inside the Lord of Thunder. She meant to die alongside it, and the power draws a pack of Curse Fiends to the altar as well.
Orchid sends Catapult and Masamune to the chokepoint on Yoshitsune's back, and alone, draws her bow at a distant cliff face.

blocks.cap: A bow aimed at the far cliff. At this angle, it isn't too late.

blocks.x: In that brief moment, she thinks. She had taken the three here for better versions of her own people, but they were carbon copies. Without A6, her kids would have gone through life relying on nothing but their own strength, too.
When a person has only one option, it is not a choice.
She had always thought of advising without stopping as a form of respect. But the letter she wrote to Midnight was really written to herself as well.

At the chokepoint, Catapult lets Masamune in on a little A6 secret. The one sentence that comes to every member's mind whenever they're in trouble: **"Orchid always has a way."** At that moment an arrow like a shooting star strikes the cliff, and the collapsing rock blocks the beasts' path.

On the altar, to close the final gap, Baowuga removes her eyepatch to use the shrine maiden's secret art, which unleashes the light of her right eye at the cost of her life. Through her blurring vision she sees two people who should not be here. Orchid grabs her hand and pulls her away, while Catapult, as if it were the most natural thing in the world, steps in front of her.

blocks.cap: The Lord of Thunder rises. The two do not back down.

blocks.x: "That's enough, Baowuga." When Baowuga protests that they should never have come, Orchid answers by rapping her on the head instead, and starts talking about Popukar, the timid, easily swayed girl who is like a little sister to her.
Baowuga is Baowuga, and Popukar is Popukar. But right now, at least, I wish you'd be a little more like her — learn to lean on other people, just a little.
9. The Real Culprit Was Something Else

But the Lord of Thunder turns its fury not on them, but on the Curse Fiends. Just then Midnight arrives, carried on Banmira's cannon cart, and tells them: when the Curse Fiends surrounded him after the blast, it was the Lord of Thunder that saved him.

What Catapult saw was not an attack. It was purification. If the power her mother entrusted to it is what let it devour cursed beasts and endure, then it is not the bringer of disaster but a victim drawn here, Baowuga realizes, piecing it together. The true culprit is the Curse. No, the Sacred Wheel.

Fully activating the Sacred Wheel requires her mother's power inside the Lord of Thunder. Then everyone turns to one person. Catapult calls her "Leader," the Sovereign says her way may be the better one, and the general says the entire Hunting Corps will follow her command.

blocks.cap: "Then I'll assign the operation tasks."

blocks.x: Just as in the Sargon desert, Orchid hands out assignments. The goal is not to hunt, but to help the Lord of Thunder break free of the Curse. Midnight takes the vanguard, Banmira detonates at will, Catapult covers Baowuga, and Baowuga has just one task.
Your task is — to leave nothing you'll regret.
When the leader promises to grill some meat if they succeed, Catapult laughs: this is exactly how A6 should be.

Right before the advance, the general confesses before the Hunting Corps that he never saw far ahead; he was only afraid. And when he says he should have talked with her more long ago, Baowuga answers that when they return, they will speak openly.
10. A Good Day for a Hunt

Approaching the altar, Baowuga realizes it was the Sacred Wheel that had been pulling at her on the snowy mountain. But when she asks to borrow its power, the Lord of Thunder only thrashes, spewing black miasma, and Orchid steels herself to end this before it is swallowed by the Curse.

At that moment, Thunderbugs fly in from the underground forest, form a blue bridge, and envelop the Lord of Thunder. It climbs to a high place and lets out a long howl, and a bolt of lightning pierces the snowy mountain and strikes its body.

blocks.cap: Moonlight pours through the hole the lightning tore. The final transformation.

blocks.x: Wreathed in blue lightning, it has not shaken off the Curse. It has overcome the Curse and made it part of its own power. Even so, Catapult says, their fight must have helped temper it.
When Baowuga tries Wyvern Riding with a Wirebug, the Lord of Thunder knocks the Wirebug down with a single bolt, then looks at her quietly, as if waiting for something.

blocks.cap: Between resentment and guilt, the Sovereign faces the Lord of Thunder.

blocks.x: Baowuga has felt sorry ever since she learned the truth, but she cannot easily let go of her resentment over losing her mother. Orchid answers her.
Brought to a new world, it lives in the new world. Afflicted by the 'Curse,' it overcomes the 'Curse.' ...Life's instinct is simply to live.
In the end, the rest can only be left to the weapons in their hands. The sun rises. It is a good day for a hunt.

Catapult and Yoshitsune take Zinogre's onslaught as if straight out of a textbook. She never managed to answer what hunting means to her, but she knows one thing: right now, she is smiling, and having a wonderful time.

In the wind of claws grazing past her ear, Orchid's lips curl up too before she knows it. The general, who stays out of the hunt, tells his samurai to watch it and carry word back to the capital. It is time, he says, to take up the forgotten meaning of the hunt once more.

blocks.cap: The Lord of Thunder answers the Wyvern Riding. The shrine maiden's light and the lightning meet at the heart of the Sacred Wheel.

blocks.x: At last Baowuga takes control of the Lord of Thunder. The light from her eye and the lightning it calls down meet at the center of the Sacred Wheel; torn space fills the Wheel, and a colorless wave bursts outward, erasing the Curse wherever it reaches.

Then, in the light pouring from the Sacred Wheel, Baowuga hears her mother's voice. Their ancestors came to this land through the Sacred Wheel, and when the Wheel lost its power and began leaking the Curse, two of those ancestors sealed it at the cost of their lives. The Trials may have been nothing more than accidents born of that broken Wheel.

Even so, her mother says, the strong prey on the weak; that is the way of nature, and who would call us wrong, we who have carried our bloodline through the hunt? But deep in the Curse's grip, she knew the next outbreak was not far off, and in the instant between life and death, she stepped before the Lord of Thunder of her own will and entrusted her power to it.

Saying she never taught her daughter how to share a burden, that the girl is truly so much like her, her mother borrows Baowuga's body to recreate the final blow of that day, and leaves one last thought in the mist.
If only I had trusted Masamune and Yoshitsune a little more back then, if only I had shared the burden with Midnight a little more, perhaps it would never have come to this.
Epilogue. Hunters Waking from a Dream

When they come to, they're back in the bamboo forest where they first arrived in this country. The Lord of Thunder's presence is gone, and the sound of a sandstorm drifts in from afar. Goodbyes always come suddenly.
Living is the process of learning that you're not all-powerful. ...Otherwise, I'll come rap you on the head, even with a whole 'Sacred Wheel' between us.
With the Sacred Wheel spent and their way back to Kamura Village closed, Masamune and Yoshitsune join A6 at Catapult's invitation. Baowuga bids them farewell, saying she will remember them forever.

Then, in the Sargon sandstorm, just as a bandit's blade comes down on Spot, an invisible light flashes in Popukar's eyes. The light hits no one, but a shockwave spreads out with a resonance that seems to come from beyond this land, and sends the bandit flying.

When the sand clears, Orchid and Catapult are standing there. They'd been out of contact for barely a minute, yet their leader shows up with a cat and a fanged beast in tow and apologizes for making everyone worry, so the squad is convinced she's possessed by something. In the end, down comes a scolding, along with a mission report to write.

Meanwhile, the Mirage Kingdom decides to raise statues of the heroes, and Baowuga says she wants a statue of the Lord of Thunder too. Not to honor it or to pity it, but simply to remember. When the Sovereign's and the general's eyes meet now, there is no wall between them.

Just then, two hunters who say they come from a faraway land appear at the castle gate. One calm, carrying a longbow; one impatient, with a sword and shield on their back. Their outfits differ a little, but their faces are exactly as Baowuga remembers, and she tries calling out their names.

And Zinogre returns to its own forest and falls asleep on its clifftop throne, washed clean of both the Curse and the shrine maiden's heavy power. It opens its eyes at approaching footsteps to find a hunter with a Long Sword, and in the eyes that meet its own there is neither hatred nor fear. When the strong meet the strong, battle is the highest form of respect.
A6 is as unruly as ever, and Orchid still sighs. But now she knows: a team isn't something time grinds into shape. It comes together only when its members learn to lean on one another.

act53side.tagline: A story about racing from the northern tip of Rim Billiton to its southern end to make up for one misdirected parcel, and, along the way, saying the unspoken words one by one with three friends met on the road. And one letter with no room left even for a signature.

chars.name: Jacinta
chars.desc: Daughter of the Campbells, a mining-magnate family of Rim Billiton. Gave her bodyguards the slip and set out on her own.

chars.name: Amelia
chars.desc: A comms engineer at Meridian Red Earth. Cries easily, but her eyes light up the moment work comes up. · Operator Timeslot

chars.name: Martina
chars.desc: The one who led Angelina onto the Messenger's path one rainy night. Since then, the two have always just missed each other.

chars.name: Inara
chars.desc: Tani's grandmother. The legendary pathfinder who founded Great Springs.

chars.name: Uluru
chars.desc: A podcaster from Redsand. Has a very, very loud voice.

chars.name: Ashton
chars.desc: Department head at Meridian Red Earth. Interviewed and hired Amelia himself.

chars.name: Barnett
chars.desc: Tani's uncle. A Great Springs local who works in the mines. Has a great many kids.

chars.name: Peta
chars.desc: Data analyst at the Rhodes Island office in Great Springs.

chars.name: Hierda
chars.desc: A Cautus revered as a savior by believers in Originium immortalism.
