blocks.cap: A letter she spent a long time deciding whether to send. The addressee: Martina.

blocks.x: "Dear Martina." **Angelina**, a Rhodes Island Messenger, is writing a letter. Martina is the one who led her onto the Messenger's path one rainy night, but whenever Angelina wanted to thank her in person, the two of them just kept missing each other.
To Rhodes Island, to this land, to Messenger Angelina... where on earth is my place?

Around then, she learns that a decryptor parcel she sent never made it to the office in Rim Billiton. Everyone tells her it's a small problem, but Angelina loads up a new decryptor and sets off to deliver it herself.
1. Came to Make Up for a Parcel, Only to Find the Data Cut Off

**Rim Billiton** is a mining nation where Catastrophes strike often. From **Great Springs**, a hot spring town at its northern tip, all the way to **the Far South**, where hardly anyone has ever set foot, an old dirt road called **Route Zero** runs right through the land.
**Barnett**, a miner who helps push her stuck car out in front of town, says there were five Barnetts in his class alone, and pesters her to name his newborn kid as repayment.

blocks.cap: A white hot spring town beneath red rock mountains. "It looks like the most perfect picture of home..."

blocks.x: Meanwhile, **Tani**, a girl at the town switchboard, is gritting her teeth through what she says is her last day as a switchboard operator. She's supposed to put Angelina through to Peta at the office, but connects her to a local troublemaker who just happens to share the name instead.
Only after Tani comes running, exposes their "spicy bottletree powder" as nothing but ground radish and chili, and chases them off does Angelina get to meet the real **Peta**.

But Peta's news is unexpected. Two months ago, "**the Great Disconnect**" cut off all long-range comms along Route Zero, so no data from the Far South has come through at all. If only the parcel had arrived on time, they could have decrypted the data before that happened.

Angelina goes quiet for a moment, then declares: "I'll go to the Far South and bring the data back!" The road is full of sandstorms and high-concentration Originium, but she says it's something she can handle on her own anyway.

In the meantime, Tani brings up a legend she heard from her grandmother: the **pouched musbeast**, a flying creature that steals the words people never quite managed to say. That's why, in Rim Billiton, kids are taught to tell the people they care about whatever they want to say as soon as they can.

Then, as they're about to part ways, Tani starts handing over snacks one by one and begs to be taken along. She turns eighteen today, so she's allowed to leave just like her grandmother did. Her grandmother **Inara** was a legendary **pathfinder** who, at sixty, went all the way to the Far South alone, and came back having lost her Arts Unit, a **pocket watch**.
2. An Eighteenth Birthday Present: A Switchboard Headset

At her birthday party that evening, her parents hand her a present for when she gets promoted soon: a headset with a switchboard attached. When they tell her Grandma's stories are just stories, and then ask her to wait two more years, Tani shouts "I'm done waiting!" and storms out.

According to her father, Tani, whom her grandmother nicknamed "**Thumpy**" because she loved stomping her feet, is the smallest Cautus in town and has no talent for Arts. She's run away from home more than thirty times, only to turn back at the edge of town every single time. Still, Angelina says: "Two years, then two years, then another two years... I completely understand how Tani feels."

Meanwhile, slumped at the edge of the wilderness, Tani remembers when she was little. On a day she'd been teased, she climbed to the top of a bottletree with her grandmother, who picked out a pale pink star and made it Tani's star. Soon, she said, it would catch up with Grandma's star up ahead.
Just then, a group in black surrounds the town gate. Headlights flash in front of a terrified Tani, and after a chase, just as the car plunges into a pit, Angelina grabs her hand tight.

blocks.cap: A night sky without gravity. Floating up: a car, a girl, and a trunk full of hot spring flyers.

blocks.x: Tani had never felt so light. Shaking off the town that had boxed her in, the hurt she felt toward her family, and her small fears, she streaked across the night sky like a single pink star.
3. The "Engineering Director" on the Carrot Rack

The moment they land, there's a "Bleugh!" from inside a supply crate, and out pops **Jacinta**, young lady of the Campbells, a mining-magnate family. The people in black around the town gate? Her bodyguards, who apparently form a human chain around her just to cross the street.
Jacinta's home is down south in **Big Ironton**, the capital. Angelina plans to send both of them back from the next town, but Tani mutters under her breath, "We'll see about that when we get there."

And in the next town, **Artichoke Village**, **Amelia**, an engineer from **Meridian Red Earth**, the company that built the comms network along Route Zero, is clinging to a comms tower that's being used as a carrot-drying rack, and crying. She's afraid of heights, but she refuses to come down until the tower is fixed.

After curing her low blood sugar with dried carrots, Amelia launches a swarm of little flying robots and fixes the tower in no time. Once even the radio comes in, the villagers start calling her "Madam Engineering Director," and Amelia finally puffs out her chest: "That's right, I'm the Engineering Director the company sent!"
It turns out Inara was also the one who found the site for this village. And the keepsake of Grandma's that Tani receives with high hopes? "Clever Arts for Tasty Dishes: 100 Home Recipes."
When Angelina still tells her to go home, Tani answers: if she doesn't set out, she'll forget Grandma's stories one by one. And her anger already faded the moment she left home.
Now a party of four, they gather around a pot of carrot stew and chat about what "unspoken words" really are. Secrets? Lies? Or grudges you can't let go of?

blocks.cap: In a corner of the tent, a tuft of fluff on a little head sways in the breeze.

blocks.x: From a corner of the tent, a small creature was quietly watching that chat.
4. The Sun in the Valley and "Short-Ears Inara"

Next up is **Solar Valley**, a giant mine. In Grandma's stories, this valley held a golden sun, and when a child got trapped digging a tunnel to touch it, Grandma heard the child's stomping and used her Arts to open a path and rescue them.

But the miners tell it differently. According to them, "Short-Ears Inara" was a saboteur hired by one of the two families fighting over the vein, and thanks to the commotion, nobody ended up with the mining rights.
Tani's ears droop, but Angelina tells her it's just the same story read a different way. In that case, all they need to do is find the kid who was rescued back then.
Tani goes down a conduit shaft alone to find that person, but the shaft collapses, comms go dead, and Tani and a technician end up trapped separately in the dark.

Meanwhile, up top, Amelia, who'd been claiming a pouched musbeast ate her repair certification, confesses she left without the company knowing. She says the Great Disconnect was caused by sloppy data from her colleague **Ashton**, but the company pinned it on her. Once Jacinta vouches for her as a shareholder, Amelia dashes to the tower to reestablish contact with the shaft below.
Down in the dark, Tani hears frantic stomping. She doesn't have Arts that can carve a path like Grandma's, but there's one thing she did inherit from her. Her ears.

The tower gets fixed, directions start coming through, and Tani finally finds the technician. "Ah, found you! Miss Technician, who never learned how to stomp out a rescue signal!" Exactly what Grandma was said to have said.
Holding up the frightened technician, Tani tells her stories, just like Grandma did. With stories and company, you can walk any road, no matter how far.

blocks.cap: Out into the sandy wind and sunlight. "We made it out!"

blocks.x: Having done the same thing Grandma did, without a pocket watch, Tani wonders: am I already a quarter as amazing as Grandma?
Later, they learn the technician was that very child. While the two families kept passing the buck and delaying the rescue, Inara had gone in and saved her without asking anyone's permission.

That night, in a valley lit up as bright as the sun, Jacinta and Amelia both volunteer to come along to the Far South. Amelia wants to leave the company and test out a portable comms station; her dream is to connect all of Terra. Angelina finally nods. "Let's all go to the Far South together!"
5. A Funeral While You're Still Alive

Following the next comms tower's signal brings them to **Redsand**, an empty town in the path of a forecast Catastrophe, abandoned by its residents. Yet a broadcast is playing: a voice saying "Follow me," and claiming that what Originium brings isn't death, but happiness and eternal life.

Gathered in the empty town are Infected who believe in "**Originium immortalism**," revere a savior named **Hierda**, and mean to die in the coming Catastrophe. The one they call "the Guide" is **Uluru**, a podcaster from this very town.

Uluru had left town after complaints about her loud voice, and came back to find the Infected listening to her broadcasts like gospel. Neither pleas to leave nor the medicine she offers gets through to them.

That's when Jacinta makes an unexpected suggestion: let them hold their own funerals while they're still alive. And that night, as everyone hesitates in front of coffins carved from hollowed-out bottletrees, the first to lie down in one is Jacinta.

She was infected at five and told she wouldn't last a month. She survived as if by a miracle, but over fifteen years she has received eight critical-condition notices. In a faraway sanatorium she earned dozens of certificates, yet never once got to actually do any of it.
She thought she'd be fine dying in the wilderness, but only lying in the coffin did she realize it. She's afraid of vanishing without a trace, and of a funeral where no one cries for her.
I don't want to die alone.

When Jacinta steps out of the coffin, the Infected begin lining up, one by one, before that small coffin. Some sob openly. One curses a lover who left, then ends up blaming themselves. Another recites a long list of their children's names. Uluru says she can probably lead at least two-thirds of them out.
When Jacinta apologizes for hiding her illness, Amelia throws herself at her and bursts into tears. Why should someone as good as Jacinta have to disappear?
Jacinta laughs. Looks like there's someone who'll cry for her after all, and enough for several people at that.
But the next day, they see that not everyone has turned back. A few lie in the remaining coffins, refusing even water, just staring at the sun.
6. An Old Home Buried in Originium
Angelina, who froze at the sight, says there's somewhere nearby she has to see, and drives off.

blocks.cap: A massive ship surrounded by crystals like thorny brambles. It wasn't a Catastrophe.

blocks.x: This is the wrecked Rhodes Island landship. My old home.

Angelina's memories rewind. When she'd just arrived at Rhodes Island, she used her Arts to help move some cargo, fell into critical condition, and recovered like a miracle thanks to a new drug. The Doctor, who didn't come to the celebration, handed a single candy to every patient in the Medical Department.

blocks.cap: She doesn't remember how the candy tasted. Only that, from that day on, she picked up a habit of folding paper stars.

blocks.x: Later, Rhodes Island also helped her make the trip home she'd put off for so long. After agonizing at a fruit stall, what she picked was a single lime. It was the scent of the last lip balm she'd taken from home, so her parents would know it was her.

blocks.cap: That's me. Mom and Dad will know.

blocks.x: But that happiness ended like waking from a dream. Rhodes Island had a tricky problem to deal with, and Closure ordered her out on field duty for her own safety. All Angelina asked was to be posted as close to the landship as possible.
And when news came that the landship had been destroyed, there was nothing Angelina could do. After that, all she could do was make up for things.

Back outside Redsand, Angelina waits and waits for those who stayed behind to change their minds, but the Infected guarding the gate says anyone who forces their way in will atone with their life. As the car finally pulls away, a single pouched musbeast flies overhead, heading south.
Angelina was grateful to that creature. Because it stole the words she would have said next, she didn't break down sobbing in the car.
7. Big Ironton, and a Promise Turned to Sleep-Talk

After more than ten days on the road, they reach Big Ironton. The danger zone can only be crossed during the few days when Originium concentration is low, so they have to leave within three days. Amelia asks for two days to go get her repair authorization, and Jacinta heads home to tell her parents.

Meanwhile, when Amelia sneaks into the office, Department Head Ashton appears before her. He says the Great Disconnect was caused by the fully automatic Gen-2 system she built, but if she comes back quietly, he'll let her keep her job. People who fail inside the company fail outside it too, he says.

When Amelia doesn't show up on the promised evening, the others go to the company and hear something unexpected: the Engineering Director is a man starting next week, and Amelia is an ordinary employee in a cubicle on the 10th floor.

Jacinta doesn't call out the lie. She asks just one thing: did Amelia mean it when she said they'd go to the Far South together? Amelia keeps her eyes on her terminal as she answers. "All that sleep-talk about going to the Far South... please forget it."
Tani makes one last request: that Amelia think back, even just once, on the promise they made.

Jacinta's day had already fallen apart too. Back home for the first time in three years, her father told her it was enough that she not sully the Campbell name, and if she wanted to live however she pleased, she could do it in her dreams.
That night, Jacinta collapses, gasping for breath, and the Campbell family's medical team, who'd been tailing her the whole time, takes her away.
8. Even a Messenger Who Makes Mistakes

The next day, the day they were supposed to set out, only two of them are left. Angelina looks back on the days behind her. When she left Siracusa, when Rhodes Island was destroyed, in Redsand: every time, she couldn't do a thing.
But Angelina is already a Messenger. **Even a Messenger who makes mistakes still has to deliver people's hearts.**
If people's hearts just reached each other on their own, the job of Messenger wouldn't even exist.
Putting off their departure by a day, the two of them each go to find a friend. "May there be four of us when the time comes."
Around then, in an empty office, Amelia opens a drawer stuffed with resignation letters she's never managed to hand in.

Here's the truth. Ashton had kept projects away from Amelia, but when the competition heated up, he suddenly put her in charge of Gen-2 and pushed her to finish a six-month replacement in two. If anything blew up, there was no better shield than a lowly researcher with no one backing her.

That night, Amelia's name, and only hers, had been wiped from the company system without a trace. Right then, a news flash warns of a two-week sandstorm, but about that road, impassable without the towers' guidance, Ashton only says, "Give it up."
Amelia slams both fists on the desk. "I'm the only one who can pull this off."

Meanwhile, Tani goes to the Campbell mansion. When Mr. Campbell says obedience is how a child repays their parents, Tani fires back that Jacinta only argues because she wants recognition from the people she loves, and gets the door shut in her face.

In the middle of the night, Tani climbs in through the window, and Jacinta admits what really made her angry wasn't the lie. It was Amelia giving up on her dream. Jacinta, whose only driver's license came from a simulator, had envied Amelia for having one.

"Wanna drive?" Gripping a real steering wheel for the first time in her life, Jacinta tears down the night road laughing harder than she ever has, shouting that she's going to drag Amelia out and they're all going to the Far South together.
9. Jump, Amelia

At dawn, Amelia is already up on the Big Ironton comms tower. Ashton rushes over and asks them to coax the scared kid down, but Angelina recognizes that small back. It's the steady back Amelia only shows when she's working.

Suddenly, the arms and legs of Ashton and his security guards grow heavy. "How about getting a feel for what gravity can really do?" At the same time, the security vehicles following behind are being cut off, one after another, by Jacinta's orange off-roader.
Meanwhile, up on the tower, Amelia climbs a ladder with no safety gear, rung by rung, crying, toward the top where the last sensor is.

blocks.cap: Amelia always cries a little longer than everyone else.

blocks.x: At four, she cried alone over a scraped knee. The day she lost her mom, she cried all day. She wanted to be a daughter to be proud of, so she worked overtime, got chewed out, and worked overtime again.

Then Jacinta shouts up from below: if she has something to say, just yell it. So Amelia yells. Thanks to them, she's started to feel like she can do anything, but she still can't even hand in a single resignation letter, and even climbing the tower terrifies her.
"Open your eyes and look! You've already made it to the top of the tower!"
From the top, the Meridian Red Earth logo looks tiny, and her own shadow stretched across the ground looks huge. "I'm quitting the company, and I'm going to the Far South!"

The tower is fixed, but Amelia's legs have given out and she can't move, and security is closing in. Angelina remembers something **Warfarin** once said: when an Infected person makes a mistake, it's their own life that burns away.
Those words planted a seed in Angelina: to one day become someone who burns her life for someone else. "Amelia! Jump! I'll catch you. I'll catch all of you!"

blocks.cap: The carrot crates, the employees running to file reports, the four girls whose hearts had found each other. Everything floated up.

blocks.x: In that small pocket of weightlessness, for the first time, Angelina forgot what she'd lost growing up. The solid weight on her staff from catching her friends was exactly what she wanted to protect.
Back on the ground, Amelia sends the company one last message: "Let's never see each other again, you pieces of garbage who wasted my time."
Then, just before they leave, Jacinta's mother comes to see her off. She saw her daughter's smiling face while she was driving, she says, and Jacinta has never once been a stain on the Campbell name.
Tani watches them enviously, then fights back the urge to pull the terminal out of her backpack.
10. The One Waiting at the End of the Land
As soon as they pass through the gate, a sandstorm blocks their way. Contact with the control tower cuts out and Originium levels skyrocket, but nobody suggests turning back.

blocks.cap: A fast-moving sandstorm standing between them and the Far South.

blocks.x: They let a little pouched musbeast, struggling to fly in the storm, into the car, and Tani names it "**Tuft**" after the fluff on top of its head. Then there's the sound of water under the wheels, and the sandy wind suddenly stops.

Ground like a mirror, water pooled on crystals, tiny flowers blooming in the cracks between them. Just like Grandma said. Tani stomps with all her might and shouts: "Grandma——we made it to the Far South——"
The data from the broken collection station can be taken home hard drive and all, but the pocket watch is nowhere on the flat ground.
Tani remembers the days when Grandma was eating less and less, and all Tani ever did was beg for stories about the pocket watch. Grandma's smile back then had looked a little complicated.

Then, at the end of the crystal plain, the sea appears. Facing a view Grandma never told her about, Tani says: even if she can't find the pocket watch, this place is still beautiful, and she's had a really, really good journey.

At that moment, a swarm of pouched musbeasts descends, snatching car keys, spray cans, anything they can grab, and then the "reinforcements" they called in come walking out. It's **Martina**, the person Angelina has wanted so badly to see.

With Martina translating, it turns out the mother pouched musbeast thought the four of them had kidnapped her baby, Tuft. Once the misunderstanding is cleared up, Tuft presses its pouch to each of their faces in turn. Apparently it means "I like you so much I want to tuck you in here and take you home."

That night in the tent, the truth comes out: the decryptor everyone thought was lost had been mailed to Martina by mistake, along with Angelina's letter. Martina had waited in the Far South, believing Angelina would come to fix her mistake herself.

blocks.cap: "Where would you ever find someone who never makes mistakes?"

blocks.x: When Angelina brings up the question from her letter, Martina answers.
A person's place is decided by what they choose to do.
If you hadn't done anything, she says, Tani, Jacinta, and Amelia would all have gone back to where they started. Could the old you have caught Amelia as she fell from that tower?

And to the worry that she can never say what she wants to say, Martina replies: feelings change if you hide them too long, so bring them out while they can still make you happy. And if it's too awkward face to face, write a letter.
Meanwhile, the mother pouched musbeast sorts the stolen items by scent and returns them to their owners. But mixed into Tani's pile is something she's never seen before.
11. From Somewhere Farther Than the End of the Land
At dawn, the four of them watch the sun rise beyond the sea. From somewhere even farther than the end of the land, the sun came up.
As Tani gets ready to send word home, Angelina hands her a pocket watch. On the lid is the most familiar name in the world: Inara.
When she opens the lid, before the watch face, out comes a photo. A photo of Tani.
Suddenly, Tani is sure of it. Grandma didn't lose the watch. Right here, as the sun rose, Grandma, all alone, must have given it to the pouched musbeasts who'd kept her company, as a thank-you.
And then, making this sunrise the end of her life as a pathfinder, she must have gone home to the people she loved.
"Grandma wasn't just scatterbrained. She was a sulky old grump who couldn't be honest." She'd wanted her family by her side, yet made a point of saying she'd lost it.

Telling herself she mustn't cry, Tani turns on her terminal, and the messages come pouring in. Dad says he came all the way to Artichoke Village, where the comms got fixed, just to send this. Mom reminds her to buy shoes one size up.
And one more line: "About what happened on your birthday... we all owe you an apology. You're an adult, and you should do what you want to do."
The tears she's held back for so long finally burst the dam.

blocks.cap: At the end of the land, a sunrise for four.

blocks.x: Under the early morning sun, the four girls held each other and cried.
Epilogue: A Letter with No Room for a Signature

On the way back, Angelina writes a letter to the Doctor. She'd figured there was no reason to write since she'd be back anyway, but this journey was so much fun that it actually left her a little wistful. Because you weren't there with me.
Meanwhile, in Big Ironton, Mr. Campbell puts on the animal-print tie his daughter had wanted to see before she left for the sanatorium. He's on his way to welcome her home, and to apologize.

And in Great Springs, where Amelia has finally brought the comms back, Uluru's radio sends ripples across the hot springs as Angelina opens a cooler box. Inside is carrot-cone ice cream, a deal Jacinta closed using Artichoke Village carrots.

blocks.cap: Free carrot-cone ice cream under upside-down gravity. The one handing it out isn't all that fond of carrots.

blocks.x: Beside her, Martina tells the rest of the legend. In the distant future, when words can travel a thousand miles in an instant, there will be a pouched musbeast that leaves the Far South in search of a brave Messenger, to deliver the true feelings buried under far too many words.

Martina turns down the invitation to come to Rhodes Island. Showing them a letter with neither a recipient nor a sender, she says she's going to work through a problem of her own that she's left alone for a long time.

After that, Amelia and Jacinta picked Laterano as the starting point for their startup, and Tani found three or four places the townspeople could move to. And Angelina found the answer to the question in that letter.
I'm Angelina, Rhodes Island's Messenger. Whenever you need me, I'll stand by your side without wavering, just like you reached out your hand to me back then.

The letter is so full there's no room left even for a signature. But that's okay. From the moment the things she wanted to say filled the whole page, Angelina would already be running toward the Doctor.

blocks.cap: "Doctor, I'm home!"

blocks.x: As the Messenger introduces her new friends, her face wears a smile brighter than sunshine, one the Doctor has never seen before.

"Where on earth is my place?" The road that began with one misdirected parcel went to the end of the land and back, carrying the answer to that question. A Messenger's place was right beside the feelings she chose to deliver.

act21mini.tagline: On a plantation, a train, a treaty stage and a burning city in Bolívar, a girl stands at the same crossroads again and again under a different name. And each time, she chooses the path that keeps others behind her. A story of a forest with no way back, and of what a life weighs.

chars.desc: A Columbian woman encountered again and again across Bolívar

chars.name: Pedro
chars.desc: A Perro boy of Bolívar. He remembers things from very long ago.

chars.name: Dobermann
chars.desc: Rhodes Island's instructor. She has a past tied to Bolívar's military.

chars.name: Ernesto
chars.desc: Former diplomat of Dossoles. Son of Pancho, a former colonel of the True Bolívarians · Operator Tequila

chars.name: Kroos
chars.desc: Beagle's longtime comrade in Reserve Operator Team A1.

chars.name: Mateo
chars.desc: A Coalition Government officer in charge of the checkpoints.

chars.name: Janco
chars.desc: A general of the True Bolívarians, about to sign a peace treaty.

chars.name: Candela
chars.desc: Mayor of Dossoles.

terms.desc: An armed faction in Bolívar. They vow to drive out foreign powers and return Bolívar to the Bolívarians.

terms.name: Coalition Government
terms.desc: Bolívar's government faction, based in La Unidad. It runs plantations hand in hand with Columbia.

terms.desc: A disease that wears away memory and speech until the body withers. First found in people bitten by hounds. There is almost no cure.

blocks.x: **Beagle** opens her eyes in a golden forest that stretches without end. Someone apologizes to her. This is the last story, the voice says, and she can never leave this place again.

Beagle answers that she does not regret her choice, and, looking out at the forest, she asks: what has trapped her here? Three hundred years of rain on this land, a fever that has lasted twenty years, or a dream that never woke through an entire summer?
Behind that question, many lives in Bolívar unfold one after another. In each life, the protagonist bears a different name.
1. Soil Disease — The Plantation Owner's Offer

**Gillian**, a girl who had collapsed by the roadside, wakes in an unfamiliar mansion. **Lorenz**, its owner, who brought her there, offers the wandering job-seeker work hauling cargo. But Lorenz's estate is a plantation.

Lorenz explains that she is effectively a hostage. Her father, a researcher, was conscripted into a classified Columbian military project, and the plantation was handed to her as his reward. She must run it without bringing trouble on him.

Just then, an officer of the **Coalition Government** arrives for an inspection. He threatens to seize the plantation if output falls below the minimum, and asks why she is so sparing with the 'fertilizer' they supply. There are plenty of unemployed to use up and throw away, he says.
Meanwhile, a worker named Emma collapses in the fields. The officer tells Lorenz to hand her over as valuable material for new drug development. Lorenz refuses.

blocks.cap: Lorenz's plantation. Each season, the Coalition Government takes the harvest.

blocks.x: Emma's illness is **Hound Disease**. It was first found in people bitten by hounds, but now the liquid fertilizer causes the same disease. The fertilizer brings rich harvests from barren soil, but it strips memory and speech from those who tend the crops, withering them into empty shells until they die.

Lorenz has cut back on the fertilizer and made up the shortfall by buying crops from other Bolívarians. If the plantation falls into Coalition hands, the workers will be used up even more cruelly. All of it is 'legal,' and no one is coming to help.
Asked to transport the crops, Gillian hesitates. Right and wrong are easy to speak of, but words alone change nothing. So she decides she has to do it.
2. The Burning Plantation
At that very moment Gillian collapses and remembers something she had forgotten. On her way here she saw people packing explosives to raid the plantation, and she was caught by their hounds.

Soon after, **True Bolívarian** guerrillas storm the plantation. To them, workers who labor under a Columbian are not compatriots but 'false Bolívarians'—traitors. Juan, a fellow worker, weeps as he holds Emma, who has only one arm left.
When the building, tilted by the blast, begins to collapse, Gillian's body moves before she can think. Bracing her shield like a pillar, she holds up the falling roof with everything she has.

blocks.cap: Gillian holds up the collapsing building with nothing but a shield.

blocks.x: To her cry of whether saving people is wrong, a guerrilla answers that leaving even one enemy alive is tightening the noose around your own neck. Lorenz, her legs pinned under the rubble, begs them to spare at least Juan.

The guerrilla orders a recruit to shoot Gillian as an 'initiation test.' Instead, the recruit drags out Juan, who refuses to leave Emma's side. He says killing Bolívarians would give him nightmares, and that no one really cares about true or false anyway.
Pressed to finish off the other two, the recruit answers flatly. The structure cannot hold with one person, and she is already at her limit. Those two are already dead.
3. Degenerative Hound Disease — The Sister Behind the Door
Waking from a dream in which she could not fly, the Perro woman **Yana** finds herself in the treatment center of a Hound Disease quarantine town.
When her attending physician, Lorenz, gives her a 'miracle drug,' a name surfaces: her younger sister, Alba. But no such name is on the patient list.
**Carmelo**, a young man she meets in the park, calls Yana 'Alba.' Alba was his fiancée, and Carmelo is losing the ability to recognize people a little more each day.

At the edge of town, a boy named **Pedro** says he remembers the days before the plantations existed. He tells her the miracle drug only slows the disease and cannot cure it, that the whole town is a lie, and presses his own dose into her hand—adding that the drug is stored somewhere very cold.

That afternoon Yana injects herself to hold on to her memories and enters a building leaking cold air. Carmelo, who followed out of worry, is with her. Inside, drums of black liquid are stacked like ramparts, and coffin-like metal boxes stretch on without end.

blocks.cap: Inside the cold building. Coffin-like metal boxes stretch on without end.

blocks.x: From behind an iron door comes her sister's voice. It is cold and dark, she says. Please open the door.
When they break the door down, beyond it are a yellow butterfly and Alba, just as Yana remembers her. Then dozens of black hounds pour out of the shadows.
For an instant, the hounds stop. It is Lorenz.

Yana entrusts Carmelo to her and makes herself the bait. To Carmelo, who tries to run after her calling 'Alba,' she says: if we get out alive, let's get married, and you'll make me corn flatbread every day on a plantation on the border highlands. Live, Carmelo.

In the headache after the bite, Yana sees what she had forgotten. On the day they fled the plantation together, her sister lost her leg to the hounds, and Yana, trying to save her, lost most of her memories. **Alba had already died that evening, when their escape failed.**
The emergency shutter comes down, and the yellow butterfly leaves Yana's shoulder.

A week later, Carmelo struggles to recall the name of a patient who caused a commotion a few days earlier. He feels he has forgotten someone very important. When Lorenz suggests they go see his younger brother Hilario together, he asks back: "Who's that?"
4. Banana Hemorrhagic Fever — The Train Carrying Bananas
The engineer **Piura** wakes **Valero**, the mercenary riding with her. Valero remembers neither her own name nor what they are carrying.
Piura has only one answer: bananas, to be sold to Columbia. The blade is there to make sure no 'bad bananas' get mixed in.
Looking over the freight car, Valero feels her way along a bunch of rotting bananas. There are only five fruits on it, and that 'banana' speaks. It begs her to save it.
Piura, who drove tourist trains in Dossoles before being tricked and dragged here, says that at least she will not become a banana.

Valero proposes changing the route. The train stops before a junction, and after sending Piura off, she switches the track to the other side, the one no one has ever chosen. They have to go back to their own land, she says.
Over that junction, another voice overlaps. Will you really choose that path, when there is clearly a way to survive? To Lorenz's question, Beagle answers that you can only choose one path.

blocks.cap: The junction where the train stopped. One of the tracks leads to Columbia.

blocks.x: The one who seizes Valero is **Mateo**, the Coalition Government officer in charge of the checkpoints in this area. His soldiers find 'bad bananas' in the freight car, but most have already been torn apart by hounds, and only two remain.

Mateo kills one on the spot and throws a crossbow at the other's feet. Better to end it yourself than be torn apart by hounds. When Valero shouts at the man to aim it at them instead, he thanks her and tells her never to do this again.
Meanwhile, Pedro appears before Piura as she flees the hounds and leads her away. When she asks if he can save Valero too, he shakes his head. She will die, but you will live.

Valero claims to see the future in her dreams, and Mateo loses their wager when Piura is not caught. He tells her to work for him. If others see you as nothing but a banana, he says, your shining heart means nothing, and he is the one who manages the bananas.
...But people aren't bananas.
When he asks what that makes him, Valero answers that she hopes he isn't one either, that she hopes no one is. "Good." Almost as he says it, Mateo cuts her throat.

Mateo orders the body buried rather than fed to the hounds, then has the train driven to **Tecoma**. Even he does not know why corpses and the living dead are shipped there. Soon after, bananas pour from the sky like a downpour, and the train races on, crushing the heaps of rotten bananas covering the tracks.
5. Obligate Parasitism — The Day of the Peace Treaty

On the day the True Bolívarians and the Coalition Government sign a peace treaty, **Sierra**, a young red-haired soldier, asks her platoon leader Pedro whether it is really true that no one will die anymore.

At that same hour, in the room of General **Janco**, his trusted right hand, Colonel **Dobermann**, throws down the treaty. A line not in the previous night's agreement has been added: a clause requiring every demobilized soldier to go labor on plantations across the land.

Meanwhile, when Lorenz—a Columbian secretary of the Coalition Government, out on an inspection—asks whether Sierra will stay on a plantation after the treaty, Sierra trembles at a surfacing memory. 'Become one of us, or become a traitor.' She asks never to hear the word plantation again.

Dobermann presses Janco: a peace bought by selling soldiers is not the peace Bolívar wanted. Janco counters that with a little help from Columbia, Bolívar's farmland and factories can grow. Step by step—so you mean to become the next Coalition Government, Dobermann retorts.
Ending with the words that some people are born to be fertilizer, Janco straightens the medals on his chest before the mirror and tells her that if she wants change, she should kill him.
A sharp dagger pierces the general's back.
Asked whom she has allied with, Dobermann answers. It is only the anger of one Bolívarian soldier who has buried family and friends in the mud, one by one.
My last words... thank you, for everything you won for the Bolívarians.

Standing at the ceremony still stained with blood, Dobermann declares she will not sign unless the clause is struck. The Coalition representative announces to the crowd that this treaty is the general's dying wish, and that whoever signs it will become Bolívar's true leader.

blocks.cap: "So, which of you will sign?"

blocks.x: Warlords, mercenaries and plantation owners scramble over each other toward the signing table.
It feels as if river water is rising over her head, and Dobermann walks against the current back onto land. Outside, she meets Pedro and tells him: we have lost peace once again.
Not long after, a soldier fallen by the riverbank shouts at Sierra to cross the river and run. Arrows fall like rain. Sierra's words—that they would not have to fight anymore—are never finished.
6. The Fever and the City — Dossoles's Hottest Summer

In the hottest summer on record, trees in **Dossoles** keep bursting into flame on their own. **Alba**, a university student home on break from her studies in Columbia, is tracking down the cause in a greenhouse, together with a voice on the other end of the phone.

blocks.cap: Alba's greenhouse. She continues her experiments, cooling the plants' heat with falling drops of water.

blocks.x: The True Bolívarians' 'Grand President' has entered the city. Around then, Mayor **Candela** asks her former subordinate **Ernesto** to personally deliver an invitation to the Grand President, whom no one has ever seen. Ernesto slips into the room next to the lodgings and presses his ear to the wall, but hears only silence.
Meanwhile, Manuel, a childhood friend who comes to see Alba, is wearing a True Bolívarian uniform.

He holds her father in contempt for doing nothing but run with the life a comrade saved at the cost of his own—a waste of Sierra's sacrifice, he says. And he warns her that you can only choose one path.

On the day of the Liberation Festival, gunshots ring out from the Grand President's lodgings. Soldiers block the streets, claiming the Coalition Government has assassinated their leader. As Candela prepares to abandon the city, Ernesto brings up her promise that he could ask for any one thing.

Afterward, Ernesto frees his father, **Pancho**, from prison. Asked what became of Candela, he says only that she is dead, and Pancho just looks at the hand his son hides behind his back. To the son who says he has not decided what lies ahead, Pancho says he has only now remembered that the flower his wife wore the day they first met was a lilac.
If the Dossoles you want is a place where no one forgets even a single flower, how could that be wrong?

Meanwhile, the greenhouse windows shatter, and screams and gunfire from the streets pour in. When Alba says she will just go say goodbye to her departing friends, the voice on the phone says: so you choose that path anyway.

In the street, Alba saves a citizen held at blade-point for giving directions in Columbian. The soldier holding the blade is Manuel. She cannot live treating what happens in her hometown like news on the radio, Alba says—and at the very least, she will not walk his path.
A superior tosses Manuel a pistol. Eliminate the suspicious one, or kill your own weakness—choose.
Manuel murmurs with a smile: I chose the right side.
Around then, a broadcast by Ernesto Salas rings out across the city.
Candela has paid the price in blood, so he will take charge of this city. Those who hate their neighbors rather than the invaders do not hold the ideals of the True Bolívarians. We will be watching.
The search stops, but Alba has already fallen in the street.

Beyond the crowd she sees a pair of green eyes. "I told you, Alba. I told you not to go out." It is the voice from the greenhouse phone. Before she can remember who it was, Alba falls into eternal sleep.
In the greenhouse that has lost its keeper, the plants burst into flame.
7. Pandemic — The Bolívar Great March
In the darkness, someone calls a name, saying this is the last time. Beagle answers. "Yes, I'm here!"

Before her stands Dobermann, Rhodes Island's instructor. On the night they discussed a rescue mission to Bolívar, Dobermann came to tell Beagle and **Kroos** that they had the right to refuse, but Beagle's bags were already packed. She would go in place of the instructor, who could not step forward because of her military past, and she would protect everyone as always, she said with a smile.

On the third day of the Dossoles riots, Columbia cut off supplies to Dossoles and two other nomadic cities. Nearly a million Bolívarians in the north walked south in search of a way to survive. Later, people would call it the **Bolívar Great March**.
In May 1101, beside Beagle as she escorts the column is **Martín**, an old man who says he went from plantation laborer to colonel. He tells her to take her comrade and leave.
The name 'Bolívarian' is a leash. It takes away your freedom, but it also tells you how to live.
To Beagle, who says she fights for ideals, Martín says that if she means to sow seeds in cursed earth, she should not hope for anything.
That night, another Hound Disease patient is found in the camp. On his left arm are needle marks, made as if counting.
Thrown into a fit at the word 'doctor,' the man bites Beagle's arm and howls. Juan, Emma, I got out. Don't take me back to Tecoma.

Around the same time in Tecoma, a Department of Defense investigator urges Lorenz to set out. Only by offering up a plantation, and the corpse of a plantation owner who looked exactly like her as 'the dead Lorenz,' did the Department pull her out from under her homeland's surveillance. The investigator says they hope for results to rival the flash over Trimounts sixteen years ago.

Some time later, True Bolívarian soldiers resolve to go rescue their compatriots imprisoned in Tecoma as soon as day breaks. Beagle's warning that charging in blindly means dying for nothing is drowned out by their roar.
Even Martín takes up a chipped blade. You are still free, he says, but I am already a Bolívarian.

blocks.cap: A sentry by the campfire. He introduces himself by the common name 'Pedro.'

blocks.x: Polishing her shield, Beagle asks Pedro, a young soldier on watch by the campfire: if there are true Bolívarians, who are the false ones? Isn't the only thing truly happening on this land that all of us are getting hurt?
Pedro answers that he joined to survive. For those who are weary of living itself, dying for an identity may be the only way to confirm they are alive.
Deep in the night, the communicator rings. "Have you really made up your mind?" Beagle recognizes the voice.
She knew you would come to stop her, she says, but she cannot step aside. The voice answers that there is no way to stop it. That it is sorry.
8. Tecoma — One Small Shield
In the evening after the rain, Tecoma is a peaceful, even graceful town, its white walls and bell tower dyed by the sunset.

blocks.cap: The streets of Tecoma. Door after door opens as they search for the wounded.

blocks.x: There is hardly any garrison.

When Beagle hands medicine to a captured Coalition soldier who has been bitten by a hound, he confesses. They released patients on purpose to lure the Bolívarians in. He was ordered to stay behind and open the gates.
The moment she shouts to retreat, a black tide surges from holes in the ground, and countless hounds are born from it and come charging out.
It is not only hounds that chase the people. Compatriots swallowed by the black tide, raised whips, heads impaled on plantation fences. Their nightmares have followed them.

Beagle thanks the citizen who called her 'doctor.' But she says she is better suited to protecting everyone with a shield than with medicine and bandages. Then she shouts to the soldier to take the people out and carry the truth to the outside world.
Martín, his leg injured, stays by her side and shouts: you're not a Bolívarian, you should never have stepped into this mire.
Beagle cannot understand. Why must one be a 'True Bolívarian' to have the right to save people? Isn't the reason to raise a shield that there is something behind you that you want to protect?

She swings her shield, and swings it again. The hounds' teeth tear at the shield, and the black tide climbs her body like vines. If raising a shield truly requires an identity, for her it is never that of a 'True Bolívarian.'
A shield makes a sound when it breaks. And then——

blocks.cap: The breaking shield. And then, everything stops.

blocks.x: Everything stops. A warning appears that a debugger has been attached, and Lorenz murmurs.
The protection program has been triggered, she says. The horizon holds its breath, and the sun sets.
9. Dromomania — The Name Left in the Forest

Fleeing Coalition troops, Pedro falls into a swamp in the black forest, from which it is said no one who enters ever leaves. As his body sinks, lightning strikes, and he sees something that should not exist.

blocks.cap: Deep within the Black Flow. A forest from which, once entered, there is no way out.

blocks.x: When he comes to, Pedro is back in that small town. The girl on the swing is a young Lorenz. The dream built to bring Beagle back is over; this is Lorenz's own memory.

The young Lorenz says that in place of her pet, which must have died from a hound's bite, her father brought home a pup that looked exactly the same. She also knew the hounds were what her father and his colleagues used in their research.
I'm going to do better than Father. At the very least, I'll put an emergency brake on dangerous inventions!

Lorenz grew up in Tecoma. Hound Disease spread after a device was activated in the forest more than ten years ago, and this secret town was built for that experiment. Unlike Pedro, who tried and failed to save the patients here back then, Lorenz has never stopped her dangerous research.
Lorenz built a stage from Pedro's memories, and on it she and Beagle played the parts of many different people. Only Pedro was nearly always himself. And now, Beagle has woken.

Lorenz says she could not save Beagle. Her body was completely destroyed, and what is here is only a consciousness salvaged from the black tide and pieced together. This place is neither heaven nor hell but the **Black Flow**—the inside of a being called a **Beast Aristocrat**—and she can never go back.
Beagle first asks whether the people survived.

At the cost of her life, she triggered that weapon's brake, and it swallowed no one else. When Beagle thanks her, Lorenz says she cannot understand that gratitude. She cannot accept that Beagle's sacrifice was logically meaningful.

Afterward, Pedro walks with Beagle to the edge of the forest. The living outside cannot see them. Pedro confides that after an accident some three hundred years ago he never grew up again, and that he has lived under changing identities while his family and friends left him one by one.
When Beagle asks whether her comrades could at least be told she is dead, so they will not wander searching for her, Pedro only says he is sorry.
Then he voices a question he has carried for a long time. Why do people choose sacrifice? So many lives he has seen became, in the end, as light as the wind.
Life doesn't become light because of death. The moment someone decides to step forward, that person is already remarkable.

Asked whether her own life had weight, Beagle bows her head, saying that is not for her to answer, and counts on her fingers. Protecting a child in her days with the security reserves, Rhodes Island's training, the mission in Tkaronto, the patients she helped. The sunset passes through her now-translucent palm and falls to the ground.

The moment Pedro turns back, saying let's go home, Beagle is gone, and a small orange creature sits at his feet. The Beagle they recovered is only a consciousness sleeping deep within that body. Pedro thinks that he was the only one lost in the dream.
He cannot take her back to her friends in this form. Pedro tells her to hold on a little longer, until Lorenz finds another way.
In the distance he sees Tecoma, now an exploration outpost. Inside the Black Flow, a sunset like this cannot be seen.

Three hundred years of rain, a twenty-year fever, a midsummer dream that never wakes. In every dream she stood at the same crossroads and chose the same path, and all Lorenz finally recovered was that one name, which will remain forever in the golden forest.

main_17.tagline: An empire whose Originium veins have run dry stakes its last hope on an ancient device, and feeds that device with the lives of the Infected. And in that fire, one person is given back a life that can only be lived once.

blocks.x: Old Ursine myth tells of a giant who shaped the land with a single gesture. Neither a good god nor an evil one, it was simply so vast that one could only look up at it.
People always call out to something greater than themselves, and look for its shadow in the real world. But when such a thing truly appears before them, every gentle illusion is crushed.
The last great thing that Ursus, an empire whose Originium veins had run dry, held on to was a device left behind by an ancient civilization: the **Sarcophagus**.
1. A Question from Twenty-Five Years Ago

Spring of 1077, the Chernobog laboratory. While its director, Kal'tsit, and her researchers sealed off the Sarcophagus's core, soldiers of the Fourth Army who wanted it as a weapon were closing in, killing the researchers one by one.
The researcher Ilia tells Kal'tsit to take the others and go. He will stay behind, he says, and asks her to take his daughter Lyudmila far away from this country.

Ilia asks which was right: the choice to open the Sarcophagus, or the choice to leave it here now. Kal'tsit answers that Lyudmila, or perhaps her child, will be the one to answer that. Having finished the seal, Ilia stayed behind alone and told the soldiers who burst in that they could take his life now.

blocks.cap: A letter sent to Marquess Boris after that day. Neither a threat nor a plea, but a warning to stop hunting the survivors.

blocks.x: Around the same time, Captain Yakov Petrov, who had joined an army rebellion, is sentenced to death. The letter he sent from prison was blank, and the Petrov family was stripped of its title and exiled to Mine No. 9 in the Northern Tundra.
On the road into exile, the youngest son, Tulin, carried an Infected man who could no longer walk on his back and said:
I think people like you, who have nothing at all, are the true masters of this land.
Then, in 1099, in the same mine, a young miner gathering a bundle of letters left by someone freed in an amnesty for political prisoners is asked for a name by a comrade, and answers: 'Tulin'.
2. An Empire Gone Dark
In the winter of 1102, Ursus's Originium veins fell into an unexplained depletion. The mines dried up, and the night streets of the capital, Deity Grypherburg, were lit by bonfires once again.

The Fourth Army of the north had marched to the gates of the capital in the name of 'suppressing rebellion' and stood in a standoff with the Second Army. Around then, Hellagur, the former general who had become Infected, returned to the capital and met Vice Chairman Vasily of the Council. A soldier burst into the room.

He reported that a new weapon developed by the First Army had succeeded in a test detonation. A weapon that used neither Originium nor any power source known before. A settlement of nomads in the central wastes was reduced to ash without a single evacuation warning.

At that same hour, at the First Army's garrison, Anatoly, only son of Marshal Svetlana, was swinging his blade. Confined to his mother's warship after contracting Oripathy, the boy cut down a soldier who stood in his way, screaming to be let out.

Svetlana brings a girl before her son. **Hierda**, a Cautus girl who leads a band of nomads rumored to cure Oripathy. Even as the blade grazed her neck and drew blood, Hierda stepped closer and held the collapsing boy.

blocks.cap: As the black crystals lose their light, the pain leaves the boy's face. The illness cannot be cured, Hierda said. She can only take away the pain of this world.

blocks.x: 3. Rhodes Island Without Kal'tsit
Rhodes Island had lost Kal'tsit. All that remained were the memories of Kal'tsit that Mon3tr carried, and an experiment to rebuild her body from the blank Originium called 'Oka'.
Closure's simulations had passed 1,860 runs, with zero progress. Everyone thought the same thing, but no one said it aloud: what was missing was whatever makes Kal'tsit Kal'tsit.

blocks.cap: Red error windows flood the screen. Every step, checked countless times, is correct, and still the result is another failure.

blocks.x: Amiya could not sleep either. The King of Sarkaz who dwells within her warns that since Amiya used the Black Crown's power in Ursus, her bond with the crown has been deepening at an unprecedented rate. Amiya asked her not to tell the Doctor yet.
The lead was in Ursus. In a country that had run out of Originium, vast amounts of it were being shipped to one place every day: Zelgrad, a satellite city next to the First Army's garrison.

Eloysius, a lieutenant of the Imperial Guard, arrives bearing an invitation from the emperor. But the one who receives the Doctor and Amiya is Witte, Chairman of the Council. Ursus had reopened the Sarcophagus too, but its research had stalled, and it needed Kal'tsit's knowledge.

Amiya offers to hand over Kal'tsit's data on a terminal that unlocks a little at a time. The price: entry into the Sarcophagus at Zelgrad. Witte asks what Rhodes Island wants, hears that there are still people trying to leave a future for everyone, and writes them an edict of passage.

At that same hour, in another hall, the young emperor Fyodor was hearing the report of a First Army captain. Only a few nomads had died, he was told, and nothing had been cleared but overgrown wasteland. In the hall, thick with the scent of bitter almonds, the emperor staggered as he rose.
4. The Free Folk's Blade

Meanwhile, on the deck of the Fourth Army's flagship, the man dragged out after water torture was **Styopa Razin**, commander of the special tactical unit 'Sechin'. The unit, made up of 'free folk' who are not Ursine, had been secretly smuggling comrades with Oripathy out of the camp.

blocks.cap: A voice over the comms. It belonged to Silka, his aide, whom Styopa believed he had sent far away himself.

blocks.x: Commander-in-chief Evgeny says that when Silka was captured she stabbed herself in the chest, and that he barely managed to save her.
Then he gave his order: take Sechin's ship, the Livonov, to Zelgrad and seize the First Army's new weapon. Refuse, and Silka and every comrade he had smuggled out would 'commit suicide'.

Around then, at the entrance to Zelgrad, stood an Infected Kuranta woman named Silka. She claimed to be a retired soldier; on the rolls, she was a deserter from the Fourth Army. One question filled her mind: how far can I go to return to that ship?

That night, Silka tracks down Yevsey, a Fourth Army spy hiding in an underground tavern. She seals off the area with her sound-erasing Arts, extracts Anatoly's movements from him, and then cuts his throat.
5. The City of Tomorrow

On January 20, the Rhodes Island party reaches Zelgrad's access zone. Lines of the Infected stretched on for three days in the winter wind, and a woman ran out in front of them, shouting: Don't come in. There is a dust no one has seen before. Touch it and you'll be infected.

The woman, dragged off by guards, is Tanya, a laborer. She had been washing the researchers' work clothes, and after she wrapped her youngest sister Nina in them, teal spots began to appear on the child's body. None of her neighbors believed her.
At the checkpoint, Amiya vouches for a group of miners who are about to have their sacks of flour confiscated. Leading them is a small, composed young man whom his comrades call 'Teacher'.

The propaganda broadcasts called this place 'the City of Tomorrow'. The homes given to the Infected still held the belongings of those who had lived there before, yet they were strangely clean, as if something had been wiped away. It was midwinter, but the city was as warm as spring, and nothing could be seen past the massive stone wall.

Raidian, probing the signals beyond the wall, is hit by a powerful counterattack and collapses. That same night, the one who stops Tanya from blowing up the wall is Crownslayer. You can't win alone, she says. Gather evidence first.
And Silka ambushed Anatoly on patrol. Her blade clearly pierced his throat, but what it cut out was not blood. It was a hard, golden substance.

blocks.cap: A single strike on a street with all sound erased. Silka flees without being able to kill him.

blocks.x: Before losing consciousness, Anatoly clung to Hierda and said: Thanks to you, I won't die now. Hierda told him it was not a miracle, but the boy would not listen.
6. The Hand That Erases Pain

Going out into the curfew-bound streets to find medicine for Raidian, Amiya is led by an unknown beast into an alley, where she finds a man. Beneath his bandages, his skin had turned a translucent green and was peeling away like moss.

His name is Kirill. After losing his wife and child, he had taken in 'Mur', a lab animal that had escaped, and locked his door. With a stranger's help, Amiya carries him to the secret clinic of Nadezhda, a doctor who lost her license, and there she comes face to face with Hierda, who was erasing the pain of the Infected with her hands.

blocks.cap: Before the glass wall of the operating room. Hierda recognizes at once the pain that Amiya carries.

blocks.x: Hierda asked: Why does god make people suffer? If we cannot save everyone, does what we do have any meaning?
Amiya answered that if she had been alone, she would have despaired. But she had never been alone, and someone had handed her the ideal that this land could become a home for everyone.
Hardship will not end. But hope will carry on just the same.
After Amiya left, Kirill woke and begged to be killed. When Hierda laid her hand on his chest, orange stone grew wherever his skin had fallen away, and Kirill died with a smile on his face.
The one who witnessed this was the miners' 'Teacher'. When the guards stormed in, Hierda fled with them.
Searching for Hierda, Anatoly raided the Infected residential quarter. The old miner Pakhon took a blade meant for the 'Teacher' and lost his life, and another died after him. Then Hierda returned.
Anatoly threw down his blade and knelt before her. Just don't leave, he begged. Hierda promised to stay by his side if he killed no more innocents, and the survivors were locked in an empty building.
7. The Imperial Guard's Answer

Meanwhile, a different battle was underway in the capital. The emperor had convened the Citizens' Assembly to pass the Emergency Winter Resource Act, a law under which the Council would distribute the Originium left in the country so that no one would freeze to death this winter.

Hellagur declines Eloysius's request that he return to the Imperial Guard. She takes him to watch a preparatory meeting of the Citizens' Assembly and says: The words of those 'workers' representatives' are far too polished. Someone is arranging things behind them.

Then the 'Emperor's Blade' appeared at the Infected shelter in Odoyev. They claimed it was the contact point for the spy who had let assassins into the capital, and declared they would erase the whole building. Hellagur drew the ceremonial sword from Eloysius's waist and cut through the spreading darkness.

blocks.cap: A single ceremonial sword without an edge. With it, the old general cuts away the Blade's darkness.

blocks.x: For everyone in this building that Rhodes Island protects, I will draw my sword like this. A thousand times, ten thousand times, as many times as it takes. Until you withdraw, or until I can no longer stand.
As the Blade withdrew, it spoke to Eloysius: next time, show us which side you will stand on.

The Emperor's Blade also went north to Bresk, to Grand Duchess Elisabeth. When it charged her with aiding the Fourth Army, her attendant Ilyosha declared that he alone would bear all the guilt and stabbed himself in the chest, and the grand duchess called something forth with Sami sorcery.

blocks.cap: Thousands of faces burst out of a void of blood and cold. It was the Yurodstvo, Gavriil.

blocks.x: Just as the Blades moved to cut it down, the grand duchess called out a name. Nastasya.
It took the form of a woman who looked exactly like the late empress and swallowed the Blades as shadows. The Blade cried out: Ursus has no need of a princess who does not even exist.
Around then, beneath the apple trees of the summer palace, Fyodor dreamed of an elder sister who called him 'Fedya'. The emperor woke and murmured: What siblings do I have?
Eloysius pressed her classmate Prado, who had been supplying military goods to the shelter.

Prado confessed with a sneer. Her father Vasily had turned to the war faction and used the shelter as a passage to bring assassins into the capital. All of it had been done to secure an escape route for his daughter.
Eloysius's blade runs Prado through. Then she went to Chairman Witte and denounced her father.
8. The Factory Beyond the Wall

Meanwhile, in Zelgrad's prison, the 'Teacher' kept speaking to the guard Ratkov even under the whip. You are a woodcutter's child, the Teacher said. You are no different from us. That night, the prisoners' door was opened.

At dawn on January 22, Rhodes Island decides to stow away on the tow vehicles that pass through the stone wall every night. Just then, an explosion went off at the base of the wall. It was Tanya's doing.
Tanya, in a protective suit, pushed the Doctor up onto the vehicle when the Doctor could not climb aboard, and fell off herself.
Closure stayed behind to shield Tanya, and the gate closed. Amid a rain of arrows, the one who rescued the two of them was Red of Reunion.

In an underground hideout, the leader of the miners introduces himself as Ivan Tulin. And from behind him, Talulah appeared. She apologized for what happened the day she left Rhodes Island, and said she had come to find out where the Infected of this city were disappearing to.
Talulah said she had once been moved by Tulin's writing.
Tulin held out a rough hand covered in frostbite. We are people who walk together, Tulin said. Talulah took that hand.
Soon Crownslayer joins them with a lead. Talulah called her by her real name, Lyudmila. The place she led them to was a factory in an expansion zone that appeared on no map.

Reunion's flames broke through the guards. Inside stood rows of glass tanks holding severed bodies. Closure read the numbers on the gauges: they were measuring how much Originium the Infected yielded after death.
In a corner, personal belongings were piled up. From that heap Tanya pulled out a red swaddling blanket, its hem faded to white, and buried her face in it. Nina never lived to see that day.

It was Closure who helped Tanya back to her feet, with the story of Kazdel, where only half the children grew up under a roof, yet everyone still called it home. Zelgrad is not that kind of home, Closure told her, but someday she will find a real one.
Tanya rises, saying she will lead everyone out of this city.
9. Aelita's Door

Meanwhile, Rhodes Island, now inside the wall, is caught by guards and released thanks to a lie from Aelita, head of Laboratory No. 6. From records her predecessor left behind, she already knew: Project Zero was 'completely out of control', and the successful test of the new weapon Kuzkina had been a fluke.

Originally from Chernobog, she speaks of her daughter Lada, a daughter of whom she knows nothing except that she survived the Catastrophe five years ago. Amiya tells her that a Lada with the same surname was a Rhodes Island operator and is now studying in the capital.
When soldiers block the way to the high-security zone, Aelita lets Rhodes Island through and closes the safety door from the outside.

blocks.cap: Aelita beyond the closing door. Her last request was that they stop the Sarcophagus, no matter what.

blocks.x: She cried out that what the Sarcophagus was burning now was the lives of the Infected who had been dragged here and taken apart. Having become an accomplice, she said, she no longer had the right to see Lada. Only a bloody handprint remained on the door's controls.
Standing before the Sarcophagus, the Doctor is flooded with unfamiliar memories. Someone's voice, calling the name 'AMa-10'.
Then Mon3tr gave the diagnosis. The Sarcophagus had been completely dismantled.
At the same hour, Styopa realizes it. Sechin was bait. Evgeny's main fleet was following behind it, marching on Zelgrad, and the Second Army holding the front line did not stop them.
10. The People Rise

Then, at noon, in the communal residential quarter. Tulin stood before the people and told them exactly what had been seen beyond the wall. Tanya raised Nina's swaddling blanket above her head, and her neighbor Mark took off his coat to bare a body spread with teal blisters.

blocks.cap: A roar goes up. 'For everyone's tomorrow, let us leave this grave.'

blocks.x: Talulah had seen faces like these long ago, in a square. Faces full of hope, looking at her.
After everyone had dispersed, Lyudmila stayed behind with Talulah. Talulah apologized, and Lyudmila answered that she had resented her once, but that the burden no longer weighed on her.
Instead of the Sarcophagus to which her father had given everything, she chooses to stay with the refugees, leaving Talulah with these words: do what you could not do before.
Meanwhile, Styopa asked Evgeny to let him hear Silka's voice one last time.
When he asked what her last words had been when they parted, the voice could not answer. It had never been Silka. It was a voice mimicked by a War Caster.

Styopa broadcasts to the whole ship. He hands command to his aide Oleg, declares that Sechin no longer belongs to the Fourth Army, and that they will reclaim the true freedom of the free folk. Before the broadcast had even ended, Evgeny's personal guard appeared.

blocks.cap: Evgeny's personal guard, the War Casters. They deliver his final order: if the ship stops before reaching Zelgrad, everyone dies.

blocks.x: 11. Critical Point
Reunion and Closure's swarm of drones broke through the stone wall. Talulah shatters the tanks of another 'fuel factory' and pulls out the Infected who are still breathing.
One of the rescued says that a white-haired Liberi had come first and told them to hold on. It was the same woman who had introduced herself to Tanya as the teacher Koshelna.

Before the Sarcophagus, Mon3tr warns them. The Sarcophagus, barely kept stable by pouring Originium into it, is on the verge of going out of control, and the biological dust leaking from it is the true nature of that strange disease. The First Army began shelling the entire building, and grotesque creatures poured out of the Sarcophagus's core.

blocks.cap: 'Zero Tank', precision annihilation. An algorithm too cruel ever to be used in real combat is used for the first time.

blocks.x: They held out for an hour, but it was too late to stop it through the program.
Mon3tr says that unless they destroy it now, all of Zelgrad will vanish, and that Kal'tsit would have done the same. Kal'tsit's words came to the Doctor's mind: make the choice you believe is right.
Just as the Doctor is about to decide, an independent program awakens deep within the system and begins to slow the Sarcophagus.
Then a voice. I want to fix this too, just like you, it said. AMa-10 holds records that matter to me. It was Priestess.
Closure needed time to trace that program. Going beyond Theresa's instruction to protect herself, Amiya calls upon the Black Crown.

blocks.cap: Amiya, holding down an ancient colossal device alone. On her shoulder, the Doctor feels an endless tide of emotion.

blocks.x: The Sarcophagus falls quiet. The Doctor heard something break, and their consciousness fell into a sea of information.
12. Ten Thousand Years of Memory

There, the Doctor sees Kal'tsit's memories. On the last ark of an ancient civilization facing its end, the scholar whom Priestess called 'Doctor' stored a collection of poems in the memory module of the machine AMa-10, so that the life that came after could see the beauty of the world.
After the civilization was swallowed by darkness, the scholar walked an empty land together with the machine. And at the end of tens of thousands of nights, the scholar saw a meteor split the sky.

blocks.cap: A meteor that fell at the end of ten thousand nights. The scholar runs toward it and collapses.

blocks.x: Lying down in the Sarcophagus, the scholar called the machine Kal'tsit. Find the traces of life, the scholar said. Find the answers on your own. Find yourself.

Kal'tsit walked north. She walked with a bird that had learned to speak, and some two thousand years later, at the northern edge of the land, she found another Sarcophagus. The old bird was buried in the frozen earth beside it.
Later, having seen tribes slaughter one another to seize the Sarcophagus, Kal'tsit buried it in the earth once more.
Time shaped the machine into a person. The Will of Sami, meeting her again after thousands of years, tells her: I have never seen you reach out so desperately for the survival of young lives.
13. Phase Transition
When the Doctor woke, Closure and Mon3tr were pulling a single strand of code out of the sea of information. It was the original code of AMa-10, the code Kal'tsit had possessed at the very beginning.

blocks.cap: A green 'calcite' inside a temporary storage box. Kal'tsit and I were this small once too, Mon3tr murmurs.

blocks.x: With its weaponization module melted down, the Sarcophagus stabilized. And out of it popped a talking 'little house'. It was the very bird that had asked Kal'tsit to bury it outside the Sarcophagus.
Aelita's husband Klim stays behind. He will take charge of channeling the Sarcophagus's energy outward, he says, and asks for one last moment alone with his wife where she died.

Meanwhile, Silka hijacked Anatoly's private line. She let the marshal and her son hear her call with Evgeny to provoke him, and finally, posing as Marshal Andrian's hidden daughter, she called Anatoly 'brother'. As the enraged Anatoly turned all his forces on her, the ship's guns fell silent.

At the city gate, Tulin faced Ratkov once more. The soldier who had heard Tulin's words in the prison handed over a sheet of paper with instructions for operating the gate, then quietly left with his regiment.
Tulin could not read that paper. Lyudmila read it aloud instead, and realized: Ivan Tulin, the author who writes the longest texts in Ursus, could not possibly be unable to read.

blocks.cap: People pour out through the open gate. 'Tulin' watches them go.

blocks.x: The real Ivan Tulin had been captured by a search party three years earlier. The one who took up the name in his place, hoping it would remain a banner for the Northern Tundra, was **Milana**, a farmer's daughter and a miner.
That same evening, aboard the Livonov. Styopa held off the War Casters with a forgotten old short incantation, and in the end they withdrew.
He sends all of his crew off the ship, saying he will send Evgeny a farewell gift.

blocks.cap: The song the crew left their leader as they abandoned ship. A song for one who goes to 'Viy', the monster lying at the end of death.

blocks.x: He walked in our place to where none of us can go. When the sun rises tomorrow, we will still march on, and draw our blades.

Then, a clearing in the forest. Closure assembled a makeshift genesis device from an energy storage block taken from the Sarcophagus, Oka, Kal'tsit's memories, and the original code just recovered. Life is not code at a standstill, but a process that calls itself and keeps repairing itself.
A sentence never seen before appears on the screen. 'Initiate life-phase transition?' Closure presses confirm, and the genesis capsule opens. The Doctor takes that hand once more.
**Welcome back, Kal'tsit.**
Epilogue: A Single Life

The first thing Kal'tsit did on waking was scold the Doctor for a dangerous decision. The Doctor answered that there had been a promise, and asked whether she had found herself. Kal'tsit said she had never forgotten.

Meanwhile, Ursus collapsed and rose again all at once. Svetlana, who had tried to abandon Zelgrad and leave with only the research results, did not deny it when asked whether her son carried the blood of that defeated general, and Anatoly stabbed his mother.

blocks.cap: 'Why can't I just be your son?'

blocks.x: His whole body covered in golden stone, Anatoly begged Hierda to save him just once more. Hierda answered: This time, I will not.
Its course locked, the Livonov accelerated toward the Fourth Army's flagship. Just before jumping, Styopa sings that song through to the end, alone. Viy is nothing much, either.
The Citizens' Assembly in the capital had been filled with nobles. The 'representatives' the emperor had been meeting had already been swapped out for actors, secretaries, and nameless nobles.
Then Eloysius enters with Vetochki, a survivor of the Far North.

Haltingly, Vetochki spoke. She wished that the Infected, too, could have a place to shelter from wind and rain, that everyone could make it safely through this winter. And so she wanted to vote for that law.

blocks.cap: 'I thought the empire's enemies were at its borders. I was wrong. The empire's enemies are here.'

blocks.x: Fyodor proclaims that the Emergency Winter Resource Act has passed by a single vote, and then dissolves the Imperial Council.

But in the north, 'Princess Nastasya' rained bread down upon the starving and preached that they must endure hardship, and in the ruins of Zelgrad, Koshelna cried out that they must grow strong through hardship. Milana, at the refugees' side, said she would not glorify hardship. No one is born to suffer.

blocks.cap: The 'princess', with a face exactly like the late empress's. People press their hands together toward her.

blocks.x: Fyodor had a small, nameless grave in the summer palace cemetery dug up. The coffin was empty, and a single name was carved inside. Nastasya.

Milana took Talulah's hand, saying she would fight alongside her in Reunion's name. Shortly after, First Army shells fell on Reunion's farm, along with a telegram saying that the marshal, recovering from her wounds, welcomed the advance.
Klim buried his wife and left to find his daughter Lada. That night, the lights came on again in Deity Grypherburg. Streetlamps, windows, New Year's decorations.

blocks.cap: A child runs through the capital's night streets, bright once more. Now the snow will not bring the cold.

blocks.x: Kal'tsit left the core code of AMa-10 behind as the Sarcophagus's management program. With it, she said, she was burying the name 'AMa-10'. It meant there would be no next life.
A single lifetime, lived only once, as a true 'person'. Is that, too, not a gift of fate?

blocks.cap: The road home at sunset. Kal'tsit slowly grows used to unfamiliar breathing.

blocks.x: Back at Rhodes Island, Kal'tsit surmised that the code in the Sarcophagus had been planted by the awakened Priestess. Priestess is watching this civilization. There is only one thing to do, Kal'tsit said: prove that the present Terran civilization is worth continuing.

blocks.cap: Kal'tsit, facing the newly built Rhodes Island landship. '...You did it.'

blocks.x: Hierda stayed in Ursus. When she drove an Originium crystal into the heart of a comrade struck by the strange disease, new flesh sprouted from his body, and people fell prostrate, crying out that it was a miracle.
Hierda asked the sky: Is suffering truly the only law of this world?
Beneath the moonlight, Priestess answers. Before long, she will bring her the answer. Her eyes were turned toward the depths of the sea.

blocks.cap: The eyes of Priestess.

blocks.x: And Priestess, having looked into Kal'tsit's ten thousand years, speaks to the Doctor.
Then prove it to me.
People always called out to something greater than themselves. This winter, the Sarcophagus, the empire, and a saint answered that call, and every gentle illusion was crushed.

Even so, Kal'tsit believed that if the Sarcophagus were ever lit again, it would surely be by the hands of good people. The answer to the question Ilia left twenty-five years ago is being written that way, by people's hands.
